passages.text: In March took place the yearly festival of our Lady of the Rosary, which was directed by negroes; and at this period is chosen the King of the Congo nation, if the person who holds this situation has died in the course of the year, has from any cause resigned, or has been displaced by his subjects. The Congo negroes are permitted to elect a king and queen from among the individuals of their own nation; the personages who are fixed upon may either actually be slaves, or they may be manumitted negroes.
passages.zh: 三月舉行了我們玫瑰聖母的年度慶典，由黑人主持；在此期間，若剛果民族的國王於一年之中去世、因任何緣故辭職，或遭其子民罷黜，便會選出新的國王。剛果黑人獲准從自己民族的成員中選出國王與女王；被選定的人物可以是實際的奴隸，也可以是已獲解放的黑人。

passages.text: About eleven o'clock I proceeded to the church with the vicar. We were standing at the door, when there appeared a number of male and female negroes, habited in cotton dresses of colours and of white, with flags flying and drums beating; and as they approached we discovered among them the king and queen, and the secretary of state. Each of the former wore upon their heads a crown, which was partly covered with gilt paper, and painted of various colours. The king was dressed in an old fashioned suit of divers tints, green, red, and yellow; coat, waistcoat, and breeches; his sceptre was in his hand, which was of wood, and finely gilt.
passages.zh: 約十一點時，我與牧師一同前往教堂。我們站在門口，這時出現了一群男女黑人，身穿各色與白色的棉布衣裳，旗幟飄揚，鼓聲咚咚；當他們走近時，我們在他們之中認出了國王、女王與國務大臣。前兩者各在頭上戴著一頂王冠，王冠部分覆以鍍金紙，並塗成各種顏色。國王身穿一套老式服裝，顏色各異，有綠、紅、黃；外套、背心與短褲俱全；他手中握著權杖，權杖為木製，並精細地鍍了金。

title.en: The Sixteen Lands of Ahura Mazda
title.zh: 阿胡拉·馬茲達的十六國土

region.en: Airyanem Vaego (symbolic: Arran, Caucasus)
region.zh: 雅利安維耶迦（象徵位置：高加索阿蘭）

period: Vendidad, Fargard I; Avestan, c. 1000-600 BCE (trans. Darmesteter, 1895)

source.work: Sacred Books of the East, Vol. 4: The Zend-Avesta, Part I, The Vendidad, Fargard I (trans. James Darmesteter)

summary.en: Ahura Mazda enumerates to Zarathustra the sixteen good lands he created, each marred in its turn by the counter-creations of Angra Mainyu, 'who is all death': the first, Airyanem Vaego by the Vanguhi Daitya, receives the serpent in the river and ten months of winter; and in four-cornered Varena was Thraetaona born, who smote the dragon Azi Dahaka.
summary.zh: 阿胡拉·馬茲達向瑣羅亞斯德細數所造十六善土，而「即死亡」的安格拉·曼紐逐一以反造毀之：首土雅利安維耶迦臨達伊提亞河，得河中之蛇與十月寒冬；四角之瓦雷納生了誅龍者特勞塔奧納。

sensitivity.note: Living scriptural tradition of Zoroastrianism. Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text:
Ahura Mazda spake unto Spitama Zarathustra, saying: I have made every land dear (to its people), even though it had no charms whatever in it: had I not made every land dear (to its people), even though it had no charms whatever in it, then the whole living world would have invaded the Airyana Vaego.
The first of the good lands and countries which I, Ahura Mazda, created, was the Airyana Vaego, by the Vanguhi Daitya. Thereupon came Angra Mainyu, who is all death, and he counter-created the serpent in the river and Winter, a work of the Daêvas.
There are ten winter months there, two summer months; and those are cold for the waters, cold for the earth, cold for the trees. Winter falls there, the worst of all plagues.
passages.zh:
阿胡拉·馬茲達對斯皮塔瑪·瑣羅亞斯德說：我使每一片土地（對其人民）都變得可愛，即使它本身毫無魅力：倘若我沒有使每一片土地（對其人民）都變得可愛，即使它本身毫無魅力，那麼整個生靈世界都會湧入艾里亞納·瓦埃戈。
我所創造的第一片善地與善國，便是位於萬古希·戴提亞河畔的艾里亞納·瓦埃戈。隨後，全然是死亡的安格拉·曼紐來了，他反創造了河中的蛇，以及寒冬——一項達埃瓦的作為。
那裡有十個冬季之月，兩個夏季之月；那些月份對水是寒冷的，對大地是寒冷的，對樹木是寒冷的。寒冬降臨那裡，是萬般災禍中最為嚴重者。

passages.text: The fourteenth of the good lands and countries which I, Ahura Mazda, created, was the four-cornered Varena, for which was born Thraetaona, who smote Azi Dahaka. Thereupon came Angra Mainyu, who is all death, and he counter-created abnormal issues in women and barbarian oppression.
passages.zh: 我所創造的第十四片善地與善國，是四角形的瓦雷納，特拉埃陶納為之而生，他擊殺了阿齊·達哈卡。隨後，全然是死亡的安格拉·曼紐來了，他反創造了婦女身上異常的經血，以及蠻族的壓迫。

title.en: Yima and the Vara Against the Deadly Winter
title.zh: 伊瑪與避冬之瓦拉

region.en: Airyanem Vaego (symbolic: Samarkand, Uzbekistan)
region.zh: 雅利安維耶迦（象徵位置：撒馬爾罕）

period: Vendidad, Fargard II; Avestan, c. 1000-600 BCE (trans. Darmesteter, 1895)

source.work: Sacred Books of the East, Vol. 4: The Vendidad, Fargard II (trans. James Darmesteter)

summary.en: The fair Yima, the good shepherd, refuses to preach the Religion but agrees to nourish the world, where for his sway there is 'neither cold wind nor hot wind, neither disease nor death'; warned of deadly winters to come, he builds the Vara and brings into it, two of every kind, the seeds of men, cattle, trees, and fires, to live the happiest life until the earth is renewed.
summary.zh: 美裔牧者伊瑪拒傳其教，卻允養育世界——其治下「無寒風無熱風，無病無死」；得預警毀滅性寒冬將至，遂築地下瓦拉，攜人畜樹火之種各二入內，安居極樂，以候大地更新。

sensitivity.note: Living scriptural tradition of Zoroastrianism. Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Ahura Mazda answered: The fair Yima, the good shepherd, O holy Zarathustra! he was the first mortal, before thee, Zarathustra, with whom I, Ahura Mazda, did converse, whom I taught the Religion of Ahura, the Religion of Zarathustra. Unto him, O Zarathustra, I, Ahura Mazda, spake, saying: 'Well, fair Yima, son of Vivanghat, be thou the preacher and the bearer of my Religion!' And the fair Yima, O Zarathusra, replied unto me, saying: 'I was not born, I was not taught to be the preacher and the bearer of thy Religion.'
passages.zh: 阿胡拉·馬茲達回答：美好的伊瑪，善良的牧者，哦神聖的瑣羅亞斯德！他是在你之前，瑣羅亞斯德啊，與我阿胡拉·馬茲達交談的第一位凡人，我教導了他阿胡拉的宗教，即瑣羅亞斯德的宗教。哦瑣羅亞斯德，我阿胡拉·馬茲達對他說：『美好的伊瑪啊，維萬加特之子，願你成為我宗教的傳道者與承載者！』哦瑣羅亞斯德，美好的伊瑪回答我說：『我未曾被生來，也未曾被教導成為你宗教的傳道者與承載者。』

passages.text: O fair Yima, son of Vivanghat! Upon the material world the evil winters are about to fall, that shall bring the fierce, deadly frost; upon the material world the evil winters are about to fall, that shall make snow-flakes fall thick, even an aredvi deep on the highest tops of mountains. Therefore make thee a Vara, long as a riding-ground on every side of the square, and thither bring the seeds of sheep and oxen, of men, of dogs, of birds, and of red blazing fires.
passages.zh: 哦，善良的伊瑪，維萬加特之子啊！邪惡的寒冬即將降臨於物質世界，帶來猛烈而致命的嚴霜；邪惡的寒冬即將降臨於物質世界，使雪花密密落下，甚至在高山之巔積達一阿雷德維之深。因此，你要為自己造一座瓦拉，四面各長如一片馳馬場，並將羊與牛、人、狗、鳥以及赤紅熾燃之火的種子帶到那裡。

passages.text: Thither thou shalt bring the seeds of men and women, of the greatest, best, and finest on this earth; thither thou shalt bring the seeds of every kind of cattle, of the greatest, best, and finest on this earth. Thither thou shalt bring the seeds of every kind of tree, of the highest of size and sweetest of odour on this earth; thither thou shalt bring the seeds of every kind of fruit, the best of savour and sweetest of odour. All those seeds shalt thou bring, two of every kind, to be kept inexhaustible there, so long as those men shall stay in the Vara.
passages.zh: 你要將男人與女人的種子帶到那裡，即這大地上最偉大、最優秀、最美好者的種子；你要將每一種牲畜的種子帶到那裡，即這大地上最偉大、最優秀、最美好者的種子。你要將每一種樹木的種子帶到那裡，即這大地上最高大、最芬芳者的種子；你要將每一種果實的種子帶到那裡，即滋味最佳、最芬芳者的種子。你要將所有這些種子帶去，每一種各兩份，使它們在那裡取之不盡，只要那些人留在瓦拉之中。

title.en: The Bundahishn: The Covenant of the Two Spirits
title.zh: 邦達希申：二靈之約

region.en: Fars, Persia (symbolic: Pars, Iran)
region.zh: 法爾斯（波斯帕薩，伊朗）

period: Bundahishn, Pahlavi, c. 7th-9th c. CE (trans. West, 1880)

source.work: Sacred Books of the East, Vol. 5: Pahlavi Texts, Part I, The Bundahis, ch. 1 (trans. E. W. West)

summary.en: The Zoroastrian cosmology opens with the two spirits: Auharmazd in endless light, omniscient and good; Aharman in the endlessly dark abyss, 'with backward understanding and desire for destruction.' Foreseeing the end, Auharmazd recites the Ahunavar that confounds the evil spirit, and creates within his confusion the sky, water, earth, plants, animals, and mankind.
summary.zh: 祆教宇宙論開篇即二靈：奧哈爾馬茲達居無盡光明，全知至善；阿哈爾曼居無盡黑暗之淵，「悟性倒錯，志在毀滅」。奧哈爾馬茲達預知終局，誦阿胡納瓦爾咒使惡靈昏亂，並於其昏亂中造天、水、地、植、獸與人。

sensitivity.note: Living scriptural tradition of Zoroastrianism. Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: As revealed by the religion of the Mazdayasnians, so it is declared that Auharmazd is supreme in omniscience and goodness, and unrivalled in splendour; the region of light is the place of Auharmazd, which they call 'endless light,' and the omniscience and goodness of the unrivalled Auharmazd is what they call 'revelation.' Revelation is the explanation of both spirits together; one is he who is independent of unlimited time, because Auharmazd and the region, religion, and time of Auharmazd were and are and ever will be; while Aharman in darkness, with backward understanding and desire for destruction, was in the abyss, and 'it is he who will not be; and the place of that destruction, and also of that darkness, is what they call the 'endlessly dark.' And between them was empty space, that is, what they call 'air,' in which is now their meeting.
passages.zh: 正如馬茲達亞斯納信徒的宗教所啟示的，如此宣稱：奧哈爾馬茲德在全知與善上至高無上，其光輝無與倫比；光明之域是奧哈爾馬茲德的居所，他們稱之為「無盡之光」；而無與倫比的奧哈爾馬茲德的全知與善，就是他們所稱的「啟示」。啟示是對兩位神靈的解釋；其中一位獨立於無盡的時間，因為奧哈爾馬茲德以及奧哈爾馬茲德的領域、宗教與時間過去存在、現在存在、將來也永遠存在；而阿哈爾曼身處黑暗之中，其理解力是倒退的，且渴求毀滅，他曾在深淵之中，而「他就是那將不存在者」；那毀滅之地，也是那黑暗之地，就是他們所稱的「無盡之暗」。在他們之間是空虛的空間，也就是他們所稱的「空氣」，如今他們便在此相遇。

passages.text: Auharmazd also knew this, through omniscience, that within these nine thousand years, for three thousand years everything proceeds by the will of Auharmazd, three thousand years there is an intermingling of the wills of Auharmazd and Aharman, and the last three thousand years the evil spirit is disabled, and they keep the adversary away from the creatures. Afterwards, Auharmazd recited the Ahunavar thus: Yatha ahuv vairy ('as a heavenly lord is to be chosen'), &c. once, and uttered the twenty-one words; He also exhibited to the evil spirit His own triumph in the end, and the impotence of the evil spirit, the annihilation of the demons, and the resurrection and undisturbed future existence of the creatures for ever and everlasting. And the evil spirit, who perceived his own impotence and the annihilation of the demons, became confounded, and fell back to the gloomy darkness.
passages.zh: 奧哈爾馬茲德也憑全知而知曉此事：在這九千年之中，有三千年一切皆依奧哈爾馬茲德的意志而行，有三千年是奧哈爾馬茲德與阿哈爾曼兩種意志的混合，而最後三千年邪靈被制伏，他們使 adversary 遠離造物。此後，奧哈爾馬茲德如此誦出阿胡納瓦爾：Yatha ahuv vairy（「當如一位天界之主被選立」）等等，誦了一次，說出二十一個詞；他又向邪靈展示了自己最終的勝利、邪靈的無能、眾魔的毀滅，以及造物復活並永遠安享不受擾亂的未來存在。而那邪靈既察覺自身的無能與眾魔的毀滅，便惶惑失措，退回幽暗之中。

passages.text: Auharmazd created his creatures in the confusion of Aharman; first he produced Vohuman ('good thought'), by whom the progress of the creatures of Auharmazd was advanced. Of Auharmazd's creatures of the world, the first was the sky; the second, water; the third, earth; the fourth, plants; the fifth, animals; the sixth, mankind.
passages.zh: 奧哈爾馬茲德在阿哈爾曼的混亂之中創造了他的造物；他首先產生了沃胡曼（「善思」），藉著他，奧哈爾馬茲德諸造物的進展得以推進。在奧哈爾馬茲德屬世的造物之中，第一是天空；第二是水；第三是大地；第四是植物；第五是動物；第六是人類。

title.en: The Tao Before Heaven and Earth (Tao Te Ching 25, 42)
title.zh: 道在天地之先（道德經·二十五、四十二章）

region.en: Hangu Pass, Shaanxi (traditional), China
region.zh: 函谷關（陝西，傳統說法）

period: Tao Te Ching, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Legge, 1891)

source.work: The Tao Teh King, trans. James Legge, chs. 25 and 42

summary.en: Two cosmological chapters of the classic of the Way: before Heaven and Earth there was something undefined and complete — the Mother of all things, whose law is simply being what it is; and the Tao produced One, One produced Two, Two produced Three, and Three produced all things, harmonised by the Breath of Vacancy.
summary.zh: 《道德經》兩章：有物混成，先天地生——可以為天下母，其法自然；又道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物，沖氣以為和。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Taoism. Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: There was something undefined and complete, coming into existence before Heaven and Earth. How still it was and formless, standing alone, and undergoing no change, reaching everywhere and in no danger (of being exhausted)! It may be regarded as the Mother of all things. I do not know its name, and I give it the designation of the Tao (the Way or Course). Making an effort (further) to give it a name I call it The Great. Great, it passes on (in constant flow). Passing on, it becomes remote. Having become remote, it returns. Therefore the Tao is great; Heaven is great; Earth is great; and the (sage) king is also great. In the universe there are four that are great, and the (sage) king is one of them. Man takes his law from the Earth; the Earth takes its law from Heaven; Heaven takes its law from the Tao. The law of the Tao is its being what it is.
passages.zh: 有物混成，先天地生。寂兮寥兮，獨立而不改，周行而不殆，可以為天下母。吾不知其名，字之曰道，強為之名曰大。大曰逝，逝曰遠，遠曰反。故道大，天大，地大，王亦大。域中有四大，而王居其一焉。人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然。

passages.text: The Tao produced One; One produced Two; Two produced Three; Three produced All things. All things leave behind them the Obscurity (out of which they have come), and go forward to embrace the Brightness (into which they have emerged), while they are harmonised by the Breath of Vacancy. What men dislike is to be orphans, to have little virtue, to be as carriages without naves; and yet these are the designations which kings and princes use for themselves. So it is that some things are increased by being diminished, and others are diminished by being increased.
passages.zh: 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物。萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和。人之所惡，唯孤、寡、不穀，而王公以為稱。故物或損之而益，或益之而損。

title.en: The Leviathan, the Butterfly, and the Death of Chaos (Zhuangzi)
title.zh: 鯤鵬、蝶夢與混沌之死（莊子）

region.en: Meng, Song state (Anhui/Henan, China)
region.zh: 宋國蒙（今安徽／河南一帶）

period: Zhuangzi, c. 4th-3rd c. BCE (trans. Giles, 1889)

source.work: Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, trans. Herbert A. Giles, chs. 1, 2, 7

summary.en: Zhuangzi's Taoist allegories from the canonised Nanhua zhenjing: the Leviathan of the northern ocean changes into the Rukh bird that mounts a typhoon ninety thousand li towards the southern lake; the sage dreams he is a butterfly and wakes unsure which he is; and the rulers of south and north bore seven holes in primal Chaos — who died on the seventh day.
summary.zh: 莊子寓言（《南華真經》）：北冥鯤魚化為大鵬，乘颶風九萬里而南徙天池；莊周夢蝶，醒後不知人耶蝶耶；南海之帝與北海之帝為中央混沌日鑿一竅——七日而混沌死。

sensitivity.note: Canonical text of the Taoist canon (Nanhua zhenjing, canonised 742 CE). Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: In the northern ocean there is a fish, called the Leviathan, many thousand li in size. This leviathan changes into a bird, called the Rukh, whose back is many thousand li in breadth. With a mighty effort it rises, and its wings obscure the sky like clouds. At the equinox, this bird prepares to start for the southern ocean, the Celestial Lake. And in the Record of Marvels we read that when the rukh flies southwards, the water is smitten for a space of three thousand li around, while the bird itself mounts upon a typhoon to a height of ninety thousand li, for a flight of six months' duration.
passages.zh: 北冥有魚，其名為鯤，鯤之大，不知其幾千里也。化而為鳥，其名為鵬，鵬之背，不知其幾千里也。怒而飛，其翼若垂天之雲。是鳥也，海運則將徙於南冥，南冥者，天池也。《齊諧》者，志怪者也。《諧》之言曰：「鵬之徙於南冥也，水擊三千里，摶扶搖而上者九萬里，去以六月息者也。」

passages.text: Once upon a time, I, Chuang Tzu, dreamt I was a butterfly, fluttering hither and thither, to all intents and purposes a butterfly. I was conscious only of following my fancies as a butterfly, and was unconscious of my individuality as a man. Suddenly, I awaked, and there I lay, myself again. Now I do not know whether I was then a man dreaming I was a butterfly, or whether I am now a butterfly dreaming I am a man. Between a man and a butterfly there is necessarily a barrier. The transition is called Metempsychosis.
passages.zh: 昔者莊周夢為胡蝶，栩栩然胡蝶也，自喻適志與，不知周也。俄然覺，則蘧蘧然周也。不知周之夢為胡蝶與？胡蝶之夢為周與？周與胡蝶，則必有分矣。此之謂物化。

passages.text: The ruler of the southern sea was called Shu. The ruler of the northern sea was called Hu. The ruler of the central zone was called Hun Tun. Shu and Hu often met on Hun Tun's territory, and being always well treated by him, determined to repay his kindness. They said, 'All men have seven holes,--for seeing, hearing, eating, and breathing. Hun Tun alone has none. We will bore some for him.' So every day they bored one hole; but on the seventh day Hun Tun died.
passages.zh: 南海之帝為儵，北海之帝為忽，中央之帝為渾沌。儵與忽時相與遇於渾沌之地，渾沌待之甚善。儵與忽謀報渾沌之德，曰：「人皆有七竅，以視聽食息，此獨無有，嘗試鑿之。」日鑿一竅，七日而渾沌死。

title.en: The Thai-Shang Tractate of Actions and their Retributions
title.zh: 太上感應篇

region.en: The Supreme Empyrean (symbolic: Wudang, Hubei, China)
region.zh: 太上天境（象徵位置：湖北武當山）

period: Thai-Shang Tractate, c. 12th c. CE (trans. Legge, 1891)

source.work: Sacred Books of the East, Vol. 40: The Texts of Taoism, Part II, The Thai-Shang Tractate (trans. James Legge)

summary.en: The Taoist scripture of moral retribution: calamity and happiness have no special doors but come as men call them, the spirits of the Northern Bushel and the three Spirits of the recumbent body record every guilt, and he who would become an Immortal of Heaven must give proof of 1,300 good deeds.
summary.zh: 道教勸善經：禍福無門，惟人自召；善惡之報，如影隨形。北斗星辰與三尸神錄人罪過、奪其紀算；欲求天仙者，當立一千三百善。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Taoism. Included as a comparative text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: The Thai-shang (Tractate) says, 'There are no special doors for calamity and happiness (in men's lives); they come as men themselves call them. Their recompenses follow good and evil as the shadow follows the substance. Accordingly, in heaven and earth there are spirits that take account of men's transgressions, and, according to the lightness or gravity of their offences, take away from their term of life. When that term is curtailed, men become poor and reduced, and meet with many sorrows and afflictions.
passages.zh: 太上曰：「禍福無門，惟人自召；善惡之報，如影隨形。」是以天地有司過之神，依人所犯輕重，以奪人算。算減則貧耗，多逢憂患。

passages.text: There also are the Spirit-rulers in the three pairs of the Thai stars of the Northern Bushel over men's heads, which record their acts of guilt and wickedness, and take away (from their term of life) periods of twelve years or of a hundred days. There also are the three Spirits of the recumbent body which reside within a man's person. As each kang-shan day comes round, they forthwith ascend to the court of Heaven, and report men's deeds of guilt and transgression. On the last day of the moon, the spirit of the Hearth does the same.
passages.zh: 又有三台北斗神君，在人頭上，錄人罪惡，奪其紀算。又有三尸神，在人身中，每到庚申日，輒上詣天曹，言人罪過。月晦之日，灶神亦然。

passages.text: The spiritual Intelligences defend him; what he does is sure to succeed; he may hope to become Immaterial and Immortal. He who would seek to become an Immortal of Heaven ought to give the proof of 1300 good deeds; and he who would seek to become an Immortal of Earth should give the proof of three hundred.
passages.zh: 神靈護衛他；他所行之事必能成功；他可望成為無形無質的仙人。凡欲求成為天仙者，應當行一千三百件善事以為證驗；凡欲求成為地仙者，應當行三百件善事以為證驗。

passages.text: He is sure in the long-run to obtain good fortune:--this is called changing calamity into blessing. Therefore the good man speaks what is good, contemplates what is good, and does what is good; every day he has these three virtues:--at the end of three years Heaven is sure to send down blessing on him. And how is it that men will not exert themselves to do what is good?
passages.zh: 他終究必能獲得福報：這就叫做轉禍為福。因此，善人所言皆善，所思皆善，所行皆善；每日具此三善，三年之後，上天必降福於他。那麼，人們為何不肯努力行善呢？

title.en: Odudua and the Cradle of Humankind at Ife
title.zh: 奧都杜瓦與伊費搖籃

region.en: Ile-Ife, Nigeria
region.zh: 奈及利亞伊費

period: Yoruba oral tradition; recorded 1894 (Ellis)

source.work: A. B. Ellis, The Yoruba-speaking Peoples of the Slave Coast of West Africa (1894), chs. 2-4

summary.en: Ellis records the priests' myths of Odudua the Earth-mother, wed to the sky-god Obatala like two shut calabashes of Heaven and Earth; their first children are Land and Water, and the first human couple, Obalofun (Lord of Speech) and Iya (Mother), come out of the goddess at Ife — the cradle of the human race.
summary.zh: 埃利斯錄祭司神話：地母奧都杜瓦與天神奧巴塔拉如兩合之瓢，天地相扣；所生首子即陸與水；首對人類歐巴洛馮（言之主）與伊雅（母）自女神體中出於伊費——人類搖籃之地。

sensitivity.note: Living religious tradition of the Yoruba. Recorded from an 1894 colonial-era collection; presented as an archival record, not as permission to speak for Orisha worshippers.

passages.text: Odudua is the wife of Obatala, but she was coeval with Olorun, and not made by him, as was her husband. Other natives, however, say that she came from Ife, the holy city, in common with most of the other gods, as described in a myth which we shall come to shortly. Odudua represents the earth, married to the anthropomorphic sky-god. Obatala and Odudua, or Heaven and Earth, resemble, say the priests, two large cut-calabashes, which, when once shut, can never be opened. This is symbolised in the temples by two whitened saucer-shaped calabashes, placed one covering the other; the upper one of which represents the concave firmament stretching over and meeting the earth, the lower one, at the horizon.
passages.zh: 奧杜杜瓦是奧巴塔拉的妻子，但她與奧洛倫同時存在，並非如她丈夫那般由奧洛倫所造。然而，其他本地人則說，她與大多數其他神祇一樣，來自聖城伊費，正如我們稍後將述及的一則神話所描述的那樣。奧杜杜瓦代表大地，與擬人化的天空之神結為夫婦。祭司們說，奧巴塔拉與奧杜杜瓦，即天與地，好比兩個剖開的大葫蘆，一旦合上，便再也無法打開。廟中以兩個漂白的碟形葫蘆象徵此意，一個覆蓋在另一個之上；上面那個代表籠罩於大地之上並與之相接的凹形蒼穹，下面那個則代表地平線。

passages.text: The second story, which cannot be any older than the myth of Yemaja, of which it is a part, is sufficiently precise to give the name of the first couple, that of the man being Obalofun (Lord of Speech), and that of the woman Iya (Mother). After coming out of the goddess at Ife, they settled there, and had a numerous progeny, which increased and multiplied till the whole earth was populated, hence it is that Ife is considered the cradle of the human race.
passages.zh: 第二則故事，其年代不可能早於耶瑪雅神話，因為它本就是該神話的一部分；這則故事足夠精確，道出了第一對夫婦的名字，男子名為奧巴洛豐（言語之主），女子名為伊亞（母親）。他們從伊費的女神體內出來之後，便定居於此，並繁衍了眾多後代，子孫日益增多，直至遍布整個大地，因此伊費被視為人類的搖籃。

title.en: The Destruction of Mankind and the Drunken Hathor
title.zh: 人類之滅與醉酒的哈托爾

region.en: Tomb of Seti I, Thebes, Egypt
region.zh: 埃及底比斯塞提一世陵墓

period: New Kingdom text (tomb of Seti I, c. 1290 BCE); trans. Budge, 1912

source.work: Legends of the Gods, trans. E. A. Wallis Budge, 'The Legend of the Destruction of Mankind'

summary.en: Ra, grown old, learns that men murmur against him and sends his Eye as the goddess Hathor to slay the rebels; she wades in their blood and would destroy all mankind, until Ra has 7,000 vessels of beer mixed with mandrakes and blood poured over the land — she drinks, becomes drunk, and mankind is saved.
summary.zh: 太陽神拉年老，聞世人怨謗，遣其目為哈托爾女神誅叛者；女神涉血而行，欲盡滅人類。拉命以曼德拉草與血和酒七千甕傾於田野——女神飲而醉，人類得免於難。

sensitivity.note: Ancient funerary-religious text of Egypt; presented as a comparative-mythology text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: Let thine Eye go forth and let it destroy for thee those who revile thee with words of evil, for there is no eye whatsoever that can go before it and resist thee and it when it journeyeth in the form of Hathor. Thereupon this goddess went forth and slew the men and the women who were on the mountain (or, desert land). And the Majesty of this god said, "Come, come in peace, O Hathor, for the work is accomplished." Then this goddess said, "Thou hast made me to live, for when I gained the mastery over men and women it was sweet to my heart;" and the Majesty of Ra said, "I myself will be master over them as [their] king, and I will destroy them." And it came to pass that Sekhet of the offerings waded about in the night season in their blood, beginning at Suten-henen.
passages.zh: 讓你的眼睛出去，讓它為你毀滅那些以惡言詆毀你的人，因為當它化為哈托爾的形貌行走時，絕沒有任何眼睛能走在它前面抵擋你與它。於是這位女神便出去，殺戮了山上（或荒漠之地）的男女。這位神的威嚴說道：「來吧，平安地來吧，哈托爾啊，因為事已成。」於是這位女神說道：「你使我得以存活，因為當我制伏男女之時，我心中甚覺甘甜。」拉之威嚴說道：「我必親自作他們的君王，轄制他們，我要毀滅他們。」事情果然如此：供祭之塞赫特女神在夜間於他們的血中涉行，自蘇騰-赫嫩開始。

passages.text: And behold, when the maidservants were bruising the grain for [making] beer, these mandrakes were placed in the vessels which were to hold the beer, and some of the blood of the men and women [who had been slain]. Now they made seven thousand vessels of beer. [...] Then the Majesty of the King of the South and North in the three-fold beauty of the night caused to be poured out these vases of beer which make [men] to lie down (or, sleep), and the meadows of the Four Heavens were filled with beer (or, water) by reason of the Souls of the Majesty of this god. And it came to pass that when this goddess arrived at the dawn of day, she found these [Heavens] flooded [with beer], and she was pleased thereat; and she drank [of the beer and blood], and her heart rejoiced, and she became drunk, and she gave no further attention to men and women.
passages.zh: 看哪，當婢女們為釀造啤酒而碾碎穀物時，這些曼德拉草便被放入盛裝啤酒的器皿之中，連同一些被殺男女的血液。他們共製成了七千罈啤酒。[……]於是，南北之王的威嚴，在那夜之三重美之中，命人傾倒這些使人躺下（或入睡）的啤酒罈，四天之牧場因這位神之威嚴的諸靈而充滿了啤酒（或水）。事情果然如此：當這位女神於黎明時分抵達，她發現這些[天]已被[啤酒]淹沒，心中甚為喜悅；她飲了[那啤酒與血]，心中歡喜，遂醉，便不再理會男女。

title.en: Atrahasis: The Clamor of Men and the Plagues
title.zh: 阿特拉哈西斯：人間喧囂與瘟疫

region.en: Nippur (region of the gods), Iraq
region.zh: 尼普魯（眾神之城，伊拉克）

period: Old Babylonian, c. 18th c. BCE; trans. Rogers, 1912

source.work: Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament, trans. Robert W. Rogers, 'Ea and Atrakhasis'

summary.en: Ellil, troubled by the ceaseless clamor of the teeming men below, holds assembly and sends pestilence to make an end of it; the wise Atrakhasis turns his thought to Ea his lord and pleads for mankind — the Old Babylonian myth that explains why the gods made death and sent the flood.
summary.zh: 眾生滋繁，喧囂不息，恩利爾神擾而集會，降瘟疫以絕其聲；智者阿特拉哈西斯歸念其主埃亞，為人類哀求——此古巴比倫神話釋死亡與洪水之由。

sensitivity.note: Ancient Mesopotamian myth; presented as a comparative-mythology text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: By their clamor he (Ellil) was [troubled] on account of their [...]. [Ellil] held his assembly and said to the gods, his children: "The clamor of men [disturbs me?] Because of their clamor I am troubled." [...] let chill come! [Quickly] let pestilence make an end to their clamor. Like a tempest shall rise against them. Illness, headache, chill, calamity!
passages.zh: 因他們的喧嚷，他（恩利爾）因他們的〔……〕而〔煩擾〕。恩利爾召開他的集會，對眾神、他的子嗣說：「人類的喧嚷〔擾亂了我？〕因他們的喧嚷，我甚煩擾。」〔……〕讓寒氣降臨！〔快快〕讓瘟疫終結他們的喧嚷。如暴風雨一般興起攻擊他們。疾病、頭痛、寒氣、災禍！

passages.text: [Quickly] did the pestilence make an end to their clamor. Like a tempest rose against them, illness, headache, chill, calamity. The wise Atrakhasis, the man, -- to Ea, his lord, is his thought turned, [he] speaks with his god, his [lord] Ea speaks with him. Atrakhasis opened his mouth, [he spoke to] Ea, his lord: "O lord, [Ea] men are in trouble, thy anger consumes the land. [...] thou who hast created us, let the illness, headache, chills, calamity [cease?]."
passages.zh: 〔快快〕瘟疫便終結了他們的喧嚷。如暴風雨一般興起攻擊他們，疾病、頭痛、寒氣、災禍。智慧的阿特拉哈西斯，那個人——他的心思轉向他的主埃阿，他與他的神說話，他的〔主〕埃阿與他說話。阿特拉哈西斯張開口，〔對〕他的主埃阿〔說〕：「哦主，〔埃阿〕人類陷於困苦，你的怒氣吞噬了大地。〔……〕你創造了我們，讓疾病、頭痛、寒氣、災禍〔止息吧？〕。」

title.en: The Bilingual of Creation: Marduk Lays the Reed-Work
title.zh: 雙語創世記：馬爾杜克鋪蘆葦

region.en: Eridu and Nippur, Sumer, Iraq
region.zh: 埃利都與尼普魯（蘇美，伊拉克）

period: Sumerian/Akkadian bilingual text (recorded c. 1000 BCE); trans. Rogers, 1912

source.work: Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament, trans. Robert W. Rogers, 'Another Version of the Creation of the World by Marduk (Bilingual of Creation)'

summary.en: A Sumerian-and-Akkadian creation text: before Eridu, Nippur, or any city was built, all lands were sea; Marduk laid a reed-work on the face of the waters, formed dust upon it, made mankind, the rivers Tigris and Euphrates, the cattle and beasts, and built the holy cities in their place.
summary.zh: 蘇美—阿卡德雙語創世文書：埃利都、尼普魯諸城未建之先，大地皆海；馬爾杜克於水面鋪蘆葦之基，揚塵其上，造人類、底格里斯與幼發拉底二河、牛獸百物，並建眾神聖城。

sensitivity.note: Ancient Sumerian-Babylonian liturgical creation text; presented as a comparative-mythology text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: The holy house, the house of the gods, in the holy place had not yet been made; No reed had sprung up, no tree had been created. No brick had been laid, no mould had been fashioned, No house had been made, no city had been built; No city had been made, no creature had been established. Nippur had not been made, E-kur had not been built; Erech had not been made, E-ana had not been built; The Deep had not been made, Eridu had not been built; [...] All lands were sea. When the middle of the sea was a water basin; In those days Eridu was made, E-sagil was built, E-sagil, where in the midst of the deep the god Lugal-dul-azaga dwelt, Babylon was made, and E-sagil was finished, The gods, the Anunaki, he made at one time; The holy city, the dwelling of the heart's desire, they proclaimed supreme.
passages.zh: 聖殿，眾神之殿，尚未建於聖地之上；蘆葦尚未生出，樹木尚未被造。磚尚未砌，模尚未塑，房屋尚未建成，城邑尚未築起；城邑尚未造成，生靈尚未確立。尼普爾尚未造成，埃庫爾尚未建成；埃雷克尚未造成，埃阿納尚未建成；深淵尚未造成，埃利都尚未建成；〔……〕萬地皆為海。當海之中央尚為水盆；那些日子裡，埃利都被造成，埃薩吉爾被建成，埃薩吉爾，即深淵之中盧加爾杜拉扎加神所居之處，巴比倫被造成，埃薩吉爾得以竣工，眾神，即阿努納基，他一次造成；那聖城，心中所願之居所，他們宣稱為至高。

passages.text: Marduk laid a reed-work upon the face of the waters, He formed dust and poured it out upon the reed-work. To cause the gods to dwell in a habitation of their heart's desire, He formed mankind. The goddess Aruru, with him, created the seed of mankind. The beasts of the field and living things in the field he created. He created the Tigris and the Euphrates, and set them in their place, Their names he did well declare. The grass, the rush of the marsh, the reed, and the forest he created.
passages.zh: 馬爾杜克在水面上鋪設蘆葦之工，他造出塵土，傾倒於蘆葦之工上。為使眾神居住於心中所願之居所，他造了人類。女神阿魯魯與他一同創造了人類的種子。田野的走獸與田野的活物，他創造了。他創造了底格里斯河與幼發拉底河，並安置於其位，它們的名字他宣告得宜。草、沼澤之燈心草、蘆葦與森林，他創造了。

title.en: The Creation of Cattle and Beasts
title.zh: 牛獸之造

region.en: Nippur, Sumer (found in Nineveh library), Iraq
region.zh: 尼普魯（蘇美；見尼尼微圖書館藏板），伊拉克

period: Mesopotamian creation-series fragment (Assyrian library copy); trans. Rogers, 1912

source.work: Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament, trans. Robert W. Rogers, 'The Creation of Cattle and Beasts'

summary.en: A fragment of the Mesopotamian creation-series tradition: when the gods in assembly had made the heavens, formed the firmament and settled the earth, bringing living things of all kinds to life and dividing the wild beasts from the creatures of the city, Nin-igi-azag created two small creatures, one white and one black, in the assembly of the beasts.
summary.zh: 美索不達米亞創世系列殘板：眾神集會造天、成穹、定地，賦萬物以生，分野獸與城居之屬；尼尼吉阿札格於獸群之中造二小獸，一白一黑。

sensitivity.note: Ancient Mesopotamian creation fragment; presented as a comparative-mythology text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: When the gods in their assembly had made the [heavens] Had formed the firmament, and settled the [earth], living things [of all kinds] had brought into life, And had made the cattle of the field, and the beasts of the field, and the moving things of the city [...] [And between the beasts] of the field and the moving things of the city had divided [...] Then arose (?) Nin-igi-azag and [created] two small creatures [In the] assembly of the beasts he made their [form] beautiful [...] one white [and one black...]
passages.zh: 當眾神在其集會中造了〔諸天〕，形成了穹蒼，安定了〔大地〕，將〔各類〕活物帶入生命，並造了田野的牲畜、田野的走獸與城中的爬行之物〔……〕〔並在〕田野的走獸與城中的爬行之物之間劃分〔……〕於是寧伊吉阿扎格興起（？）並〔創造〕了兩個小生靈〔在〕走獸的集會中他使它們的〔形貌〕美麗〔……〕一白〔一黑……〕

title.en: Adapa and the Food of Life
title.zh: 阿達帕與生命之食

region.en: Eridu, Iraq
region.zh: 埃利都（伊拉克）

period: Old Babylonian (Amarna copies, c. 14th c. BCE); trans. Rogers, 1912

source.work: Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament, trans. Robert W. Rogers, 'The Myth of Adapa'

summary.en: Adapa, son of Ea, breaks the wing of the south wind; Ea warns him that food and water of death will be set before him in heaven — but Anu offers food and water of LIFE instead, and Adapa, obeying Ea, refuses them, losing immortality for himself and all mankind.
summary.zh: 埃亞之子阿達帕折斷南風之翼；埃亞預警：天上必奉致死之食水，慎勿受——然安努所奉乃生命之食水，阿達帕遵師言而拒之，遂失永生，人類從此有死。

sensitivity.note: Ancient Babylonian myth; presented as a comparative-mythology text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: O South wind, on the way I shall to thee [...] everything that, thy wing will I break. As he spoke with his mouth, the wing of the South wind was broken, seven days the South wind blew not upon the land. Anu called to his messenger Ilabrat: Why has the South wind not blown upon the land for seven days? His messenger Ilabrat answered him: "My lord, Adapa, the son of Ea, the wing of the South wind has broken."
passages.zh: 哦南風，在路上我將對你〔……〕一切，你的翅膀我將折斷。當他口中說話，南風的翅膀便被折斷，七日之久南風不吹於大地之上。阿努呼喚他的使者伊拉布拉特：為何南風七日之久不吹於大地之上？他的使者伊拉布拉特回答他：「我主，埃阿之子阿達帕，折斷了南風的翅膀。」

passages.text: Be astonished. Good words they will speak to Anu. A good countenance of Anu they will show thee. When thou standest before Anu, food of death they will set before thee, eat not. Water of death they will set before thee, drink not. Garments they will set before thee, put them on. Oil they will set before thee, anoint thyself. The counsel that I have given thee, forget not. The words which I have spoken, hold fast." The messenger of Anu came: "Adapa has broken the wing of the South wind. Bring him before me." The road to Heaven he made him take, and to Heaven he ascended.
passages.zh: 「你要驚異。他們將對阿努說好話。他們將向你展現阿努的善容。當你站在阿努面前時，他們會在你面前擺上死亡之食，不要吃。他們會在你面前擺上死亡之水，不要喝。他們會在你面前擺上衣服，穿上它們。他們會在你面前擺上油，塗抹你自己。我所給你的忠告，不要忘記。我所說的話，要牢牢守住。」阿努的使者來了：「阿達帕折斷了南風的翅膀。把他帶到我面前來。」他使他走上通往天上的路，他便升上了天。

passages.text: "Bring him, that we may eat." Food of life they brought him, but he ate not. Water of life they brought him, but he drank not. Garments they brought him. He clothed himself. Oil they brought him. He anointed himself. Anu looked at him; he wondered at him. "Come, Adapa, why hast thou not eaten, not drunken? (Now) thou shalt not live. [...] Ea, my lord said: 'Eat not, drink not.' Take him and bring him back to his earth."
passages.zh: 「把他帶來，讓我們吃吧。」他們給他帶來了生命之食，但他沒有吃。他們給他帶來了生命之水，但他沒有喝。他們給他帶來了衣服。他穿上了。他們給他帶來了油。他塗抹了自己。阿努看著他；他對他感到驚奇。「來吧，阿達帕，你為什麼沒有吃，沒有喝？（如今）你將不能活了。[……] 我的主埃阿說：『不要吃，不要喝。』把他帶走，送回他的大地。」

title.en: Llew and the Woman Made of Flowers
title.zh: 勒烏與花所造之女

region.en: Mount Snowdon / Dinas Dinlle, Wales
region.zh: 威爾斯斯諾登山／丁勒堡

period: Mabinogion, 'Math son of Mathonwy', 13th c. MS; trans. Lady Charlotte Guest, 1849

source.work: The Mabinogion, trans. Lady Charlotte Guest, 'Math the son of Mathonwy'

summary.en: Arianrod curses her son Llew never to have a wife of any race on earth; so Math and Gwydion form a woman out of the blossoms of the oak, the broom, and the meadow-sweet. When Gronw's poisoned dart fells Llew, he flies up as an eagle, until Gwydion sings him down from the oak and strikes him with his wand.
summary.zh: 阿里安羅德咒其子勒烏永不得世上任何族類之妻；馬斯與格威狄恩遂以橡花、金雀花與繡線菊花合成一女，名曰布洛代薇德。格隆之毒鏢傷勒烏，勒烏化鷹棲橡樹；格威狄恩詠歌三闋召之，以魔杖擊之復其人形。

sensitivity.note: Medieval Welsh mythic literature (Insular Celtic cycle); presented as a comparative-mythology text.

passages.text: They went thereupon unto Math the son of Mathonwy, and complained unto him most bitterly of Arianrod. Gwydion showed him also how he had procured arms for the youth. 'Well,' said Math, 'we will seek, I and thou, by charms and illusion, to form a wife for him out of flowers. He has now come to man's stature, and he is the comeliest youth that was ever beheld.' So they took the blossoms of the oak, and the blossoms of the broom, and the blossoms of the meadow-sweet, and produced from them a maiden, the fairest and most graceful that man ever saw. And they baptized her, and gave her the name of Blodeuwedd.
passages.zh: 於是他們去到馬索努伊之子馬斯那裡，向他極其悲痛地抱怨阿麗安蘿德。圭迪昂也向他展示了他如何為那青年取得武器。「好，」馬斯說，「我和你，將藉由法術與幻術，用花朵為他造一個妻子。他如今已長到成人的身量，是前所未見最俊美的青年。」於是他們取了橡樹的花、金雀花的花，以及繡線菊的花，從中造出了一位少女，是人所見過最美麗、最優雅的。他們為她施洗，給她取名為布洛黛薇德。

passages.text: Thereupon Gronw rose up from the bill which is called Bryn Kyvergyr, and he rested on one knee, and flung the poisoned dart and struck him on the side, so that the shaft started out, but the head of the dart remained in. Then he flew up in the form of an eagle and gave a fearful scream. And thenceforth was he no more seen.
passages.zh: 於是格榮從那名叫布林·基維爾吉爾的山崗上起身，單膝跪地，擲出那支毒鏢，擊中了他的側腹，以致箭桿突出，但鏢頭仍留在裡面。接著他化作鷹的形狀飛起，發出一聲可怕的尖叫。從此以後，就再也見不到他了。

passages.text: And Gwydion came under the tree, and looked what it might be that the sow was feeding on. And he saw that she was eating putrid flesh and vermin. Then looked he up to the top of the tree, and as he looked he beheld on the top of the tree an eagle, and when the eagle shook itself, there fell vermin and putrid flesh from off it, and these the sow devoured. And it seemed to him that the eagle was Llew. [...] And the eagle came down upon Gwydion's knee. And Gwydion struck him with his magic wand, so that he returned to his own form. No one ever saw a more piteous sight, for he was nothing but skin and bone.
passages.zh: 圭迪昂來到樹下，察看那母豬在吃什麼。他看見她正在吃腐肉和蟲子。於是他抬頭望向樹頂，當他望去時，他看見樹頂上有一隻鷹，而當那鷹抖動身子時，蟲子和腐肉便從牠身上落下，母豬把這些都吞吃了。他覺得那隻鷹就是勒烏。[……] 那鷹落到圭迪昂的膝上。圭迪昂用他的魔杖擊打他，使他恢復了自己的形貌。從沒有人見過更可憐的景象，因為他只剩皮包骨。

title.en: Vari, the Very Beginning, and Vatea
title.zh: 瓦里之初與瓦泰亞

region.en: Mangaia, Cook Islands
region.zh: 庫克群島曼加伊亞

period: Hervey Islands oral tradition; recorded 1876 (Gill)

source.work: W. W. Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), 'The Beginning of all Things'

summary.en: In Mangaian chant the universe is the hollow of a vast cocoa-nut shell; at its narrow bottom lives Vari-ma-te-takere, The-very-beginning, who plucked off bits of her own sides to make the first gods — Vatea, half man and half fish, father of gods and men, whose one eye is the sun and the other the moon.
summary.zh: 曼加伊亞創世歌：宇宙如巨大椰殼之腔；其最底處居「太初」瓦里馬特泰克雷，自體側摘片造諸神——首生瓦泰亞，半人半魚，為神人之父；其一目為日，一目為月。

sensitivity.note: Polynesian oral tradition recorded from the last priests of Mangaia; presented as an archival record of a faith no longer practised in its traditional form.

passages.text: In the lowest depth of Avaiki, where the sides of the imaginary shell nearly meet, lives a woman -- a demon, of flesh and blood -- named Vari-ma-te-takere, or The-very-beginning. Such is the narrowness of her territory that her knees and chin touch, no other position being possible. Vari-ma-te-takere was very anxious for progeny. One day she plucked off a bit of her right side, and it became a human being -- the first man Avatea, or Vatea [...] Now Vatea, the father of gods and men, was half man and half fish, the division being like the two halves of the human body. [...] Thus one eye of Vatea was human, the other a fish-eye.
passages.zh: 在阿瓦伊基的最低深處，那想像中的貝殼兩側幾乎相接之處，住著一個女人——一個有血有肉的惡魔——名叫瓦里-馬-特-塔克雷，或稱「太初」。她的領地如此狹窄，以致她的膝蓋和下巴相觸，不可能有其他姿勢。瓦里-馬-特-塔克雷非常渴望有後代。有一天，她從自己右側扯下一小塊，它便成了人——第一個男人阿瓦特亞，或稱瓦特亞[……] 如今，眾神與眾人之父瓦特亞，半人半魚，其分界如同人體的兩半。[……] 因此瓦特亞的一隻眼睛是人的，另一隻是魚眼。

passages.text: On another occasion Vari-ma-te-takere tore off a second bit from that same right side, and it became Tinirau, or In-numerable, who, like his brother, had a second and fishy form. [...] Another day Vari-ma-te-takere took a bit off her left side, and it became Tango, or Support, who went to live at Enua-Kura, or The-land-of-red-parrot-feathers. A fourth child was produced from a bit of the same left side, and was named Tumuteanaoa, or Echo [...] A fifth child originated from a bit of that same left side of the Great Mother, and was designated Raka, or Trouble, who presides, like Aeolus, over the winds.
passages.zh: 另有一次，瓦里-马-特-塔凯雷从同一右侧撕下第二小块，它化作了蒂尼劳，或称「不可胜数者」，他像他的兄弟一样，另有一种鱼类的形态。[……]又一日，瓦里-马-特-塔凯雷从她的左侧取下一小块，它化作了坦戈，或称「支撑」，他前往恩努阿-库拉居住，即「红鹦鹉羽毛之地」。第四个孩子由同一左侧的一小块产生，名为图穆特阿纳奥阿，或称「回声」[……]第五个孩子源自这位伟大母亲同一左侧的一小块，被命名为拉卡，或称「祸患」，他像埃俄罗斯一样，掌管着风。

title.en: Maui Makes the Sun Captive
title.zh: 毛伊縛日（曼加伊亞）

region.en: Mangaia, Cook Islands
region.zh: 庫克群島曼加伊亞

period: Hervey Islands oral tradition; recorded 1876 (Gill)

source.work: W. W. Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), 'The sun made captive'

summary.en: The days are too short for any work or incantation to be finished; so the redoubtable Maui resolves to capture the Sun-god Ra and compel him to obey the dictates of his conqueror — snaring the god by the neck with a rope and forcing him to move more reasonably across the sky.
summary.zh: 白晝苦短，諸業未成日已沒；無畏之毛伊遂謀縛太陽神拉，以繩套神之頸，迫其緩行——自此日月運行有度。

sensitivity.note: Polynesian oral tradition recorded from the last priests of Mangaia; presented as an archival record of a faith no longer practised in its traditional form.

passages.text: Maui had secured fire for the advantage of mortals, had elevated the sky; but there remained one great evil to be remedied -- the sun had a trick of setting every now and then, so that it was impossible to get through any work. Even an oven of food could not be prepared and cooked before the sun had set. Nor could a "karakia," or incantation to the gods, be chanted through ere they were overtaken by darkness. Maui resolved to remove this great evil. Now Ra, or the Sun, is a living creature and divine; in form resembling a man, and possessed of fearful energy. His golden locks are displayed morning and evening to mankind. [...] But the redoubtable Maui was not to be discouraged. He resolved to capture the Sun-god Ra, and compel him to obey the dictates of his conqueror.
passages.zh: 毛伊已为凡人的利益取得了火，已把天空升高；但仍有一大祸患有待补救——太阳惯于不时落下，以致任何工作都无法完成。甚至连一炉食物也来不及在日落之前备好烤熟。也无法把一段「卡拉基亚」，即向诸神吟诵的咒语，完整诵毕而不被黑暗赶上。毛伊决意除去这一大祸患。如今拉，即太阳，是一个有生命的造物，且是神圣的；其形貌类似人，拥有可怖的精力。他的金色鬈发早晚向人类展现。[……]但无畏的毛伊并不因此气馁。他决意擒获太阳神拉，迫使他服从征服者的命令。

title.en: Ina, the Fairy Voyager
title.zh: 伊娜仙航

region.en: Mangaia, Cook Islands
region.zh: 庫克群島曼加伊亞

period: Hervey Islands oral tradition; recorded 1876 (Gill)

source.work: W. W. Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), 'Ina, the fairy voyager'

summary.en: The girl Ina rides a shark across the ocean to the Sacred Isle, piercing her cocoa-nut for water on the creature's erected dorsal fin — and cracking it on its forehead, which is why sharks bear 'Ina's bump' to this day; the shark-king Tekea the Great carries her past her enemies to the long-sought shore.
summary.zh: 少女伊娜乘鯊渡海往聖島；以椰子承鯊立起之背鰭取水，又於鯊額擊破椰殼——故鯊額至今有「伊娜之凸」；鯊王特克亞大神護其過敵鯊之群，達於久覓之岸。

sensitivity.note: Polynesian oral tradition recorded from the last priests of Mangaia; presented as an archival record of a faith no longer practised in its traditional form.

passages.text: At the margin of the ocean a shark came in sight. Addressing the shark in words very like those formerly used, to her great delight the huge fish came to her feet, and Ina mounted triumphantly on its broad back, carrying in her hand two cocoa-nuts to eat. When halfway on the dangerous voyage to the Sacred Isle, Ina felt very thirsty, and told the shark so. The obedient fish immediately erected its dorsal fin, on which Ina pierced the eye of one of her nuts. [...] The shark, smarting from the blow, dived into the depths of the ocean, leaving the girl to float as best she could. From that day there has been a marked protuberance on the forehead of all sharks, called "Ina's bump."
passages.zh: 在海洋的边缘，一条鲨鱼出现了。伊娜用与先前所用极为相似的话语对鲨鱼说话，令她大为欣喜的是，那巨鱼来到她的脚边，伊娜得意洋洋地骑上它宽阔的背，手中拿着两个椰子以备食用。在前往圣岛的险途行至半程时，伊娜感到十分口渴，便告诉了鲨鱼。那顺从的鱼立刻竖起它的背鳍，伊娜便在鳍上刺穿了她一个椰子的眼。[……]鲨鱼因这一刺而疼痛，潜入海洋深处，留下那女孩尽其所能地漂浮。自那天起，所有鲨鱼的额头上都有一处明显的隆起，称为「伊娜之瘤」。

title.en: Qat Makes Things, and Buys the Night
title.zh: 卡特造物與購夜

region.en: Mota, Banks Islands, Vanuatu
region.zh: 萬那杜班克斯群島莫塔島

period: Banks Islands oral tradition; recorded 1891 (Codrington)

source.work: R. H. Codrington, The Melanesians: Studies in their Anthropology and Folk-lore (1891), ch. 10

summary.en: Qat of the Banks Islands begins to make things — men, pigs, trees, rocks — then sails to the foot of the sky to buy the night from Night herself; his brothers see the sun sink for the first time, fear that they shall die, and are taught to sleep till Qat cuts the night open with a piece of red obsidian.
summary.zh: 班克斯群島之神卡特造人、豬、樹、石；復航至天之腳下，向黑夜女神購得夜。弟眾初見日落，驚懼呼死；卡特教其瞑目而眠，至時以赤曜石割開黑夜，曙光復現。

sensitivity.note: Melanesian oral tradition recorded from native teachers of the Banks Islands; presented as an archival record, not as permission to speak for Melanesian communities.

passages.text: There Qat began to make things, men, pigs, trees, rocks, as the fancy took him. But when he had made all sorts of things he still knew not how to make night, and the daytime was always light. [...] Then, seeking what he could do with the daylight, he heard that there was night at Vava, in the Torres Islands; so he took a pig and tied it, and put it into his canoe, and sailed over to Vava, where he bought night, qong, from I Qong, Night, who lived there. [...] Then he let go the night.
passages.zh: 在那里，卡特开始随心所欲地造物：人、猪、树木、岩石。但当他造出各种各样的东西之后，他仍不知如何造出夜晚，白昼总是明亮的。[……]于是，他寻思能用白昼做些什么，他听说在托雷斯群岛的瓦瓦有夜晚；于是他捉了一头猪，把它捆好，放进他的独木舟，航行到瓦瓦，在那里他从住在当地的「夜」——伊·琼——那里买来了夜晚，即「琼」。[……]然后他放出了夜晚。

passages.text: 'What is this coming out of the sea,' they cried, 'and covering the sky?' 'That is night,' said he; 'sit down on both sides of the house, and when you feel something in your eyes, lie down and be quiet.' Presently it was dark, and their eyes began to blink. 'Qat! Qat! what is this? shall we die?' 'Shut your eyes,' said he; 'this is it, go to sleep.' When night had lasted long enough the cock began to crow and the birds to twitter; Qat took a piece of red obsidian and cut the night with it; the light over which the night had spread itself shone forth again, and Qat's brothers awoke.
passages.zh: 「从海里冒出来、遮住天空的这是什么？」他们喊道。「那就是夜晚，」他说；「坐在屋子的两边，当你们感到眼中有异样时，就躺下安静不动。」不久天就黑了，他们的眼睛开始眨动。「卡特！卡特！这是什么？我们会死吗？」「闭上你们的眼睛，」他说；「就是这个，睡吧。」当夜晚持续得够久时，公鸡开始啼叫，鸟儿开始啁啾；卡特取来一块红色黑曜石，用它把夜晚割开；夜晚所覆盖的光明又重新照耀出来，卡特的兄弟们醒了过来。

passages.text: According to the story as told in Mota, Qat made men and pigs at first in the same form, but on his brothers remonstrating with him on the sameness of his creatures, he beat down the pigs to go on all fours and made men walk upright. Man was made of clay, the red clay from the marshy riverside at Vanua Lava.
passages.zh: 根据莫塔所讲述的故事，卡特起初把人和猪造成同样的形态，但他的兄弟们就他造物形态相同一事向他提出异议，于是他把猪打倒，使之四肢着地，并让人直立行走。人是用黏土造成的，那红黏土取自瓦努阿·拉瓦河畔的沼泽地。

title.en: Qat, Marawa the Spider, and the Canoes
title.zh: 卡特、蜘蛛馬拉瓦與獨木舟

region.en: Mota, Banks Islands, Vanuatu
region.zh: 萬那杜班克斯群島莫塔島

period: Banks Islands oral tradition; recorded 1891 (Codrington)

source.work: R. H. Codrington, The Melanesians: Studies in their Anthropology and Folk-lore (1891), ch. 10

summary.en: Qat cuts a great tree for a canoe, but every night his secret work is undone — until he catches the little old man Marawa, the spider, replacing the chips; Marawa promises to finish the canoe with his nails, and the brothers' own canoes, launched in envy, sink one by one.
summary.zh: 卡特伐大樹造舟，然夜夜其功盡毀——樹身復合如初；伏而擒之，乃小老翁蜘蛛馬拉瓦。馬拉瓦諾以指爪為之成舟；弟眾嫉而自造之舟，下水一一沈沒。

sensitivity.note: Melanesian oral tradition recorded from native teachers of the Banks Islands; presented as an archival record, not as permission to speak for Melanesian communities.

passages.text: Qat cut down a large tree well suited for a canoe, and worked secretly every day, but made no progress in his work; every day when he returned to work he found the wood that he had chopped away replaced, and the tree made solid again. [...] Presently he saw a little old man with long white hair creep out of the ground and begin to replace the chips, each in the place from which it had been cut, till the tree trunk was almost whole again. [...] But Marawa, the spider, another very powerful vui, for this was he, entreated Qat, 'Ah, friend, don't kill me, and I will make your canoe all right again;' and he worked at it, and soon finished it with his nails. When all the canoes were finished, Qat bade his brothers launch their own, and as each was launched he lifted his hand, and one by one they sank.
passages.zh: 卡特征得了一棵极适合造独木舟的大树，每日暗中劳作，工作却毫无进展；每天他回去干活时，都发现被砍下的木屑又回到原处，树也重新变得完好如初。[...]不久，他看见一个白发苍苍的小老头从地里钻出来，开始把木屑一片片放回原处，每一片都放回被砍下的地方，直到树干几乎又完整如初。[...]可是马拉瓦——那只蜘蛛，另一位法力强大的vui，因为这就是他——恳求卡特说：『啊，朋友，别杀我，我会把你的独木舟修好的。』于是他动手干起来，很快便用指甲把它修好了。所有独木舟都造好后，卡特吩咐兄弟们各自下水自己的那一只，每当下水一只，他便举起手，那些独木舟便一只接一只地沉了下去。

title.en: How Tagaro Made the Sea
title.zh: 塔加羅造海

region.en: Aurora (Maewo), New Hebrides, Vanuatu
region.zh: 萬那杜新赫布里底群島奧羅拉島

period: New Hebrides oral tradition; recorded 1891 (Codrington)

source.work: R. H. Codrington, The Melanesians: Studies in their Anthropology and Folk-lore (1891), ch. 19 'How Tagaro made the Sea'

summary.en: In old times the sea was only a small pool behind Tagaro's house, walled in with stone; his two sons, forbidden to go there, breach the wall playing at fish — and the water runs out with a roar, spreading into the great sea, while the old woman who tried to stop it turns to stone.
summary.zh: 太古之海，僅塔加羅屋後小池，石牆圍之。其二子犯禁戲魚，推石決牆——水轟然而出，遂成大海；老嫗以身當之，化為石，今猶在焉。

sensitivity.note: Melanesian oral tradition recorded from native teachers of the New Hebrides; presented as an archival record, not as permission to speak for Melanesian communities.

passages.text: They say that he made the sea, and that in old times the sea was quite small, like a common pool upon the beach, and that this pool was at the back of his house, and that there were fish in the pool, and that he had built a stone wall round it. [...] So when he was gone the thought entered into the mind of those two, Why has our father forbidden us to go there? [...] And one of the boys stood on the stones Tagaro had built up, and he sees the fish, and he shoots at one and hits it; and as he runs to catch hold of it he threw down a stone, and then the water ran out. [...] and the sea followed as it flowed. And they think that the old woman turned into a stone, and lies now on the part of Maewo near Raga.
passages.zh: 他们说，是他造了海，而在古时，海很小，就像海滩上寻常的一汪水潭，这水潭就在他屋后，潭里有鱼，他还在它周围砌了一道石墙。[...]于是当他离去后，那两人心中便起了念头：父亲为什么禁止我们去那里呢？[...]其中一个男孩站到塔加罗砌起的石头上，他看见了鱼，便朝一条射去，射中了它；他跑过去要抓住它时，扔下了一块石头，于是水便流了出来。[...]海水随着水流奔涌而出。他们认为那老妇人变成了一块石头，如今就躺在迈沃岛靠近拉加的地方。

title.en: Lumawig Makes the People of the Reeds
title.zh: 盧馬維格造蘆葦人

region.en: Bontoc, Mountain Province, Luzon, Philippines
region.zh: 菲律賓呂宋山省博托克

period: Igorot oral tradition; recorded 1916 (Cole)

source.work: Mabel Cook Cole, Philippine Folk Tales (1916), Igorot: 'The Creation'

summary.en: In the beginning there were no people on the earth; Lumawig the Great Spirit came down from the sky, cut many reeds, and set them in pairs throughout the world — commanding them to speak, and each pair became a man and a woman whose language differed from every other couple's.
summary.zh: 太初大地無人；大神盧馬維格自天而下，刈蘆葦甚多，分置世界各地為偶，命之曰言——蘆葦即化為人，每地一男一女，其語各異。

sensitivity.note: Philippine oral tradition recorded from Igorot narrators; presented as an archival record, not as permission to speak for Igorot communities.

passages.text: In the beginning there were no people on the earth. Lumawig, the Great Spirit, came down from the sky and cut many reeds. He divided these into pairs which he placed in different parts of the world, and then he said to them, "You must speak." Immediately the reeds became people, and in each place was a man and a woman who could talk, but the language of each couple differed from that of the others. Then Lumawig commanded each man and woman to marry, which they did. By and by there were many children, all speaking the same language as their parents. These, in turn, married and had many children. In this way there came to be many people on the earth.
passages.zh: 起初，地上并没有人。伟大的神灵卢马维格从天而降，砍下许多芦苇。他把这些芦苇分成一对一对，安置在世界的不同地方，然后对它们说：『你们必须说话。』芦苇立刻变成了人，每一处都有一男一女会说话，但每一对男女的语言都与其他各对不同。接着卢马维格吩咐每一对男女成婚，他们便照做了。渐渐地，他们有了许多孩子，全都说着与父母相同的语言。这些人又各自成婚，生了许多孩子。就这样，地上便有了许多人。

title.en: Lumawig's Sons and the Flood
title.zh: 盧馬維格之子與洪水

region.en: Pokis, Mountain Province, Luzon, Philippines
region.zh: 菲律賓呂宋山省波基斯

period: Igorot oral tradition; recorded 1916 (Cole)

source.work: Mabel Cook Cole, Philippine Folk Tales (1916), Igorot: 'The Flood Story'

summary.en: Lumawig's sons flood the flat world to raise mountains, drowning all the people but one brother and sister on the peak of Pokis; Lumawig builds a great fire to warm the two survivors, the waters dry away, and the brother and sister marry to re-people the earth.
summary.zh: 盧馬維格二子引水漫淹平坦之世以起群山，世人盡溺，唯波基斯山巔兄妹二人得存；盧馬維格燃巨火暖之，洪水退去，兄妹成婚，人類繁衍復興。

sensitivity.note: Philippine oral tradition recorded from Igorot narrators; presented as an archival record, not as permission to speak for Igorot communities.

passages.text: "Let us cause water to flow over all the world and cover it, and then mountains will rise up." So they caused water to flow over all the earth, and when it was covered they took the head-basket of the town and set it for a trap. [...] Now Lumawig looked down from his place in the sky and saw that his sons had flooded the earth and that in all the world there was just one spot which was not covered. And he saw that all the people in the world had been drowned except one brother and sister who lived in Pokis. [...] As soon as Lumawig reached Pokis he built a big fire which warmed the brother and sister; and the water evaporated so that the world was as it was before, except that now there were mountains. The brother and sister married and had children, and thus there came to be many people on the earth.
passages.zh: 『让我们使水漫过整个世界，把它淹没，然后山便会升起。』于是他们使水漫过整个大地，当大地被淹没时，他们取来镇上的头篮，把它设作陷阱。[...]这时，卢马维格从天上的居所俯视，看见他的儿子们淹没了大地，全世界只剩下一处地方没有被淹没。他又看见世上所有的人都被淹死了，只有住在波基斯的一对兄妹还活着。[...]卢马维格一到波基斯，便燃起一堆大火，温暖了那对兄妹；水蒸发了，世界便恢复如初，只是如今有了山。那对兄妹成了婚，生了孩子，于是地上便有了许多人。

title.en: Melu Makes the Earth and the First People
title.zh: 梅盧造地與初民

region.en: Lake Sebu region, South Cotabato, Mindanao, Philippines
region.zh: 菲律賓民答那峨南哥達巴托省賽布湖

period: Bilaan oral tradition; recorded 1916 (Cole)

source.work: Mabel Cook Cole, Philippine Folk Tales (1916), Bilaan: 'The Story of the Creation'

summary.en: The giant Melu shapes the world out of his own rubbed-off dead skin, then fashions two men from the leftovers; Tau Tana interferes and sets their noses upside down, and Melu, whipping the forms until they moved, later saves their hair and dry skin to make companions — hence the many people of the earth.
summary.zh: 巨人梅盧搓自身蛻下之死皮而成大地，復以餘料塑二人；塔烏塔納從地底來擾，將鼻捏反。梅盧鞭打土偶使其行動，又貯其髮膚，造為新伴——世上人類由是繁盛。

sensitivity.note: Philippine oral tradition recorded from Bilaan narrators; presented as an archival record, not as permission to speak for Bilaan communities.

passages.text: Finally Melu decided to make the earth; so he worked very hard in putting the dead skin into shape, and when it was finished he was so pleased with it that he determined to make two beings like himself, though smaller, to live on it. Taking the remnants of the material left after making the earth he fashioned two men but just as they were all finished except their noses, Tau Tana from below the earth appeared and wanted to help him. Melu did not wish any assistance, and a great argument ensued. Tau Tana finally won his point and made the noses which he placed on the people upside down. When all was finished, Melu and Tau Tana whipped the forms until they moved.
passages.zh: 最后，梅卢决定造大地；于是他非常辛苦地把死皮塑成形，做成之后，他对它十分满意，便决定照自己的样子造两个活物，只是比他自己小些，住在大地上。他取来造大地后剩下的材料碎屑，塑成了两个男人，可就在他们即将完工、只差鼻子的时候，地下的陶·塔纳出现了，想要帮他。梅卢不愿接受任何帮助，于是双方争执起来。陶·塔纳最终占了上风，造出了鼻子，却把它们倒着安在了人脸上。一切完工后，梅卢和陶·塔纳抽打这些形体，直到它们动了起来。

passages.text: The people were very grateful to him, and promised to do anything he should ask of them. Before he left for the sky, they told him that they were very unhappy living on the great earth all alone, so he told them to save all the hair from their heads and the dry skin from their bodies and the next time he came he would make them some companions. And in this way there came to be a great many people on the earth.
passages.zh: 人们对他非常感激，答应凡他所求都愿意去做。在他返回天上之前，他们告诉他，独自住在这片大地上很不快乐，于是他便吩咐他们把所有掉落的头发和身上脱落的干皮都保存起来，等他下次来时，就给他们造一些同伴。就这样，地上便有了许许多多的人。

title.en: Viracocha Creates the World at Tiahuanacu
title.zh: 維拉科查於蒂亞瓦納科創世

region.en: Tiahuanacu, Colla-suyu (Bolivia/Peru)
region.zh: 蒂亞瓦納科（科利亞蘇尤，玻利維亞／秘魯）

period: Inca tradition as given to Sarmiento de Gamboa, 1572; trans. Markham, 1907

source.work: Sarmiento de Gamboa, History of the Incas, chs. 6-7 (Hakluyt Society, trans. Sir Clements Markham)

summary.en: In the beginning Viracocha created a dark world without sun, moon, or stars, and a race of giants; after the flood called uno pachacuti, 'water that overturns the land,' he created the sun, moon, and stars on the island of Titicaca, and at Tiahuanacu sculptured on stone all the nations he meant to create — calling them forth from lakes, caves, trees, and rocks.
summary.zh: 太初維拉科查造暗黑之世，無日月星辰，又造巨人之屬；洪水「翻地之水」過後，遂於的的喀喀島造日月眾星，復於蒂亞瓦納科以石雕萬族之形——呼其名而諸族自湖、泉、洞、樹、石中湧出，遍居大地。

sensitivity.note: Inca tradition recorded under Viceroy Toledo's commission from sworn Inca witnesses; presented as an archival record — a colonial source to be read critically.

passages.text: The natives of this land affirm that in the beginning, and before this world was created, there was a being called Viracocha. He created a dark world without sun, moon or stars. Owing to this creation he was named Viracocha Pachayachachi, which means "Creator of all things." And when he had created the world he formed a race of giants of disproportioned greatness [...] He then created men in his likeness as they are now; and they lived in darkness.
passages.zh: 此地原住民確言，起初、在此世界被創造之前，有一位名為維拉科查（Viracocha）的存在。他創造了一個沒有太陽、月亮與星辰的黑暗世界。由於這番創造，他被稱為維拉科查·帕查亞查奇（Viracocha Pachayachachi），意即「萬物之創造者」。當他創造了世界之後，又造了一個身形比例失調、巨大無比的巨人族〔……〕他隨後照自己的形貌造了如今這般的人類；他們生活在黑暗之中。

passages.text: The flood being passed and the land dry, Viracocha determined to people it a second time, and, to make it more perfect, he decided upon creating luminaries to give it light. With this object he went, with his servants, to a great lake in the Collao, in which there is an island called Titicaca [...] Viracocha went to this island, and presently ordered that the sun, moon, and stars should come forth, and be set in the heavens to give light to the world, and it was so.
passages.zh: 洪水退去、大地乾涸之後，維拉科查決意再次使人居住其上，並且為了使之更為完善，他決定創造發光之體以賜予光明。為此，他帶著僕從前往科利亞奧（Collao）的一座大湖，湖中有一島名為的的喀喀（Titicaca）〔……〕維拉科查來到此島，隨即命太陽、月亮與星辰出現，安置於天上以照耀世界，事便如此成就。

passages.text: He went to a place now called Tiahuanacu in the province of Colla-suyu, and in this place he sculptured and designed on a great piece of stone, all the nations that he intended to create. [...] His servants, obeying the command of Viracocha, set out on their journey and work. [...] At the sound of his voice every place obeyed, and people came forth, some from lakes, others from fountains, valleys, caves, trees, rocks and hills, spreading over the land and multiplying to form the nations which are to-day in Peru.
passages.zh: 他來到如今稱為蒂亞瓦納科（Tiahuanacu）之地，位於科利亞蘇尤（Colla-suyu）省；在此地，他在一塊巨石上雕琢並繪出他打算創造的一切民族。〔……〕他的僕從遵從維拉科查的命令，啟程前往各自的路途與職司。〔……〕一聞其聲，每一處皆順服，人們紛紛而出，有的來自湖泊，有的來自泉眼、山谷、洞穴、樹木、岩石與山丘，遍布大地、繁衍增多，形成了今日秘魯境內的諸民族。

title.en: The Children of the Window of Production
title.zh: 創生之窗的子女

region.en: Paccari-tampu, near Cuzco, Peru
region.zh: 秘魯庫斯科近郊帕卡里坦普

period: Inca tradition as given to Sarmiento de Gamboa, 1572; trans. Markham, 1907

source.work: Sarmiento de Gamboa, History of the Incas, ch. 11 (Hakluyt Society, trans. Sir Clements Markham)

summary.en: Six leagues from Cuzco is the hill Tampu-tocco, 'the house of windows,' where three windows open in the rock; from the rich window Ccapac-tocco came forth four brothers and four sisters, created and sent by Ticci Viracocha to be lords — among them Manco Ccapac and Mama Occlo, the founders of the Inca line.
summary.zh: 庫斯科六里外有山名坦普托科，「窗之屋」，岩上開三窗；四男四女自其中之富窗「卡帕克托科」而出，乃蒂奇維拉科查所造所遣之主——印加王朝之祖曼科卡帕克與瑪瑪奧克洛即在焉。

sensitivity.note: Inca tradition recorded under Viceroy Toledo's commission from sworn Inca witnesses; presented as an archival record — a colonial source to be read critically.

passages.text: All the native Indians of this land relate and affirm that the Incas Ccapac originated in this way. Six leagues S.S.W. of Cuzco by the road which the Incas made, there is a place called Paccari-tampu, which means 'the house of production,' at which there is a hill called Tampu-tocco, meaning 'the house of windows.' It is certain that in this hill there are three windows [...] From the chief window of 'Ccapac-tocco,' came four men and four women, called brethren. These knew no father nor mother, beyond the story they told that they were created and came out of the said window by order of Ticci Viracocha, and they declared that Viracocha created them to be lords. For this reason they took the name of Inca, which is the same as lord.
passages.zh: 此地所有原住印第安人皆講述並確言，印加人卡帕克（Incas Ccapac）便是如此起源的。在庫斯科（Cuzco）南南西六里格處、印加人所築的道路旁，有一地名為帕卡里坦普（Paccari-tampu），意即「產出之屋」，該處有一座名為坦普托科（Tampu-tocco）的山丘，意即「窗之屋」。可以確定的是，此山丘中有三扇窗〔……〕從「卡帕克托科」（Ccapac-tocco）這扇主窗中，走出了四名男子與四名女子，稱為兄弟。他們不知有父亦不知有母，只知他們所講述的故事：他們是奉蒂克西·維拉科查（Ticci Viracocha）之命被創造、並從那扇窗中出來的；他們宣稱維拉科查創造他們是為了讓他們成為領主。因此之故，他們取了「印加」（Inca）之名，其意即為領主。

title.en: The Giants of the First Making
title.zh: 初造之巨人

region.en: Lake Titicaca, Bolivia/Peru
region.zh: 的的喀喀湖（玻利維亞／秘魯）

period: Inca tradition as given to Sarmiento de Gamboa, 1572; trans. Markham, 1907

source.work: Sarmiento de Gamboa, History of the Incas, ch. 7 (Hakluyt Society, trans. Sir Clements Markham)

summary.en: A variant told by the old people: at the Titicaca site Viracocha first formed shapes of large strong men out of proportion, then remade them of his own stature and gave them life; thence they set out to people the land — the memory, in Inca tradition, of the builders of Tiahuanacu.
summary.zh: 古人所傳異說：維拉科查初於的的喀喀之地塑壯偉巨人，以其失度，遂改塑如己身之度而賦以生；諸人由是四出而居——印加傳統以此記蒂亞瓦納科建城古族之由來。

sensitivity.note: Inca tradition recorded under Viceroy Toledo's commission from sworn Inca witnesses; presented as an archival record — a colonial source to be read critically.

passages.text: Others affirm that this creation of Viracocha was made from the Titicaca site where, having originally formed some shapes of large strong men which seemed to him out of proportion, he made them again of his stature which was, as they say, the average height of men, and being made he gave them life. Thence they set out to people the land.
passages.zh: 另有人確言，維拉科查的這番創造是在的的喀喀（Titicaca）之地完成的：他起初先造了一些高大強壯之人的形體，但覺得比例失當，於是又照自己的身量重造了他們——據說他的身量即為常人的中等高度——造好之後便賦予他們生命。他們由此出發，前往各地使人居住。

title.en: Makonaima and the Wondrous Tree
title.zh: 馬科納伊瑪與神樹

region.en: Acawoio country, Essequibo basin, Guyana
region.zh: 蓋亞那埃斯塞基博盆地阿卡瓦奧之地

period: Acawoio oral tradition; recorded 1868 (Brett)

source.work: W. H. Brett, The Indian Tribes of Guiana (1868), ch. 10 'Mythology and Legendary Tales'

summary.en: In the beginning Makonaima, the great spirit whom no man hath seen, created the birds and beasts with the gift of speech, and set his son Sigu to rule them; then, to surprise his creatures, he caused a wondrous tree to spring from the earth bearing every cultivated fruit — the original stock of all the plants of mankind.
summary.zh: 太初，無人得見之大神馬科納伊瑪造飛禽走獸，皆賦以言，命其子西古統之；又使神樹自地湧出，枝結百果，根生木薯玉蜀黍——世間一切栽培植物之源也。

sensitivity.note: Indigenous Amazonian oral tradition recorded by a missionary in 1868; presented as an archival record — a colonial source to be read critically, not as permission to speak for Indigenous communities.

passages.text: In the beginning of this world the birds and beasts were created by Makonaima, -- the great spirit whom no man hath seen. They, at that time, were all endowed with the gift of speech. Sigu, the son of Makonaima, was placed to rule over them. All lived in harmony together and submitted to his gentle dominion. [...] But Makonaima, to surprise his creatures with his bounty, was causing to spring out of the earth an enormous and wonderful tree. Each branch of that great tree produced a different kind of fruit; while from and around its trunk grew bananas, plantains, and cassava; with maize, and corn of all kinds. [...] which (though white men do not know it) is the original stock from whence have sprung all the plants now cultivated among the nations of the earth.
passages.zh: 在此世界之初，鳥獸皆由馬科奈馬（Makonaima）所造——那是無人得見的偉大精靈。當時牠們全都蒙受言語之能。馬科奈馬之子西古（Sigu）被安置以統治牠們。眾生和睦共處，順服於他溫和的治理。〔……〕然而馬科奈馬為以其豐饒使他的造物驚奇，正使一株巨大而奇妙的樹從地中長出。那株大樹的每一枝都結出不同種類的果實；而其樹幹之上與四周則長出香蕉、大蕉與木薯，還有玉米及各種穀物。〔……〕此樹（雖然白人並不知曉）正是如今世上萬民所栽培的一切植物所由出的本源。

passages.text: the Great Spirit, having created the heavens and the earth, seated Himself on a huge silk-cotton tree by a river side, and cut off pieces of its bark or wood, which he cast all around. Those which touched the water became fishes; others flew in the air as birds; while some, as animals of various kinds, and lastly man, moved on the earth.
passages.zh: 偉大的神靈創造了天地之後，便坐在河邊一棵巨大的木棉樹上，切下樹皮或木塊，向四方拋撒。那些落到水裡的變成了魚；其他的飛上空中成了鳥；還有一些則化為各種各樣的動物，最後是人，在大地上行走。

title.en: Aiomun Kondi and the Two Destructions
title.zh: 艾奧蒙孔迪與兩度滅世

region.en: Arawak country, Guyana
region.zh: 蓋亞那阿拉瓦克之地

period: Arawak oral tradition; recorded 1868 (Brett)

source.work: W. H. Brett, The Indian Tribes of Guiana (1868), ch. 10 'Mythology and Legendary Tales'

summary.en: The Arawaks tell that the world has twice been destroyed for the evil doings of men — first by fire, then by flood — each time foretold by Aiomun Kondi, the great Dweller on High; the pious Marerewana saved his family in a canoe tied by a long bush-rope to a tree, and found himself not far from home when the waters fell.
summary.zh: 阿拉瓦克人言：世界因人之惡而兩度遭滅——先以火，後以水，皆艾奧蒙孔迪大神預警；虔智之酋馬雷瓦納以長藤繫舟於樹，攜家避洪，水退而故土不遠。

sensitivity.note: Indigenous Amazonian oral tradition recorded by a missionary in 1868; presented as an archival record — a colonial source to be read critically, not as permission to speak for Indigenous communities.

passages.text: They also believe that, since the Creation, the world has been twice destroyed; first, by a flame of fire sent to sweep over it, and afterwards by a flood of water. Each of those destructions was on account of the evil doings of men, and specially threatened by Aiomun Kondi, the great "Dweller on High." [...] When the great waters were about to be sent, a chief of distinguished piety and wisdom, named Marerewana, was informed of the coming flood, and saved himself and his family in a large canoe. Being desirous not to drift over the ocean, or far from the home of his fathers, he had prepared a cable of 'bush-rope' of great length, and with it he tied his bark to the trunk of a large tree. When the waters subsided, he found himself not far from his former abode.
passages.zh: 他們也相信，自創世以來，世界已被毀滅過兩次：第一次是降下一片烈火橫掃大地，之後又是一場洪水。這兩次毀滅都是因為人類的惡行，尤其是偉大的「居於高處者」艾歐蒙·孔迪所發出的警告。[……]當大洪水將要降下時，一位以虔誠與智慧著稱的酋長，名叫馬雷雷瓦納，得知洪水即將到來，便與家人一同乘上一艘大獨木舟逃生。他不願漂流到海上，或遠離祖先的家園，於是準備了一條極長的「叢林藤索」，用牠把自己的獨木舟綁在一棵大樹的樹幹上。當洪水退去時，他發現自己離原先的居所並不遠。

title.en: The Waraus Descend from Above the Sky
title.zh: 瓦勞人自天而降

region.en: Pomeroon river, Guyana
region.zh: 蓋亞那波默龍河

period: Warau oral tradition; recorded 1868 (Brett)

source.work: W. H. Brett, The Indian Tribes of Guiana (1868), ch. 10 'Mythology and Legendary Tales'

summary.en: The original home of the Waraus was not this lower world but a pleasant region above the sky; the hunter Okonorote found a hole in the heavens, made a rope of cotton, and led his people down to the game-rich earth — but the last, a stout woman, stuck fast in the aperture, closing the way home forever.
summary.zh: 瓦勞人故鄉不在下界，而在天上樂土；獵人奧科諾羅特獵禽而得天窿，搓棉為繩引族人下界狩獵——末行之肥婦困於穴口，歸路遂絕，瓦勞人自此永居人間。

sensitivity.note: Indigenous Amazonian oral tradition recorded by a missionary in 1868; presented as an archival record — a colonial source to be read critically, not as permission to speak for Indigenous communities.

passages.text: the original abode of the Waraus was not on this lower earth at all, but in a pleasant region above the sky. [...] One of these, named Okonorote, having wandered far in pursuit of a choice bird, discharged an arrow at it, which missed its mark and disappeared. While searching for the arrow he found a hole through which it had fallen, and on looking through it he saw this lower world stretched out beneath [...] They accordingly descended by the same means, followed by their children and their wives, all except the last, -- an unfortunate person who, being too stout to squeeze through, remained fixed in the narrow aperture, completely filling it. [...] The Waraus were thus of necessity confined to this earth, without even a glimpse of their former abode!
passages.zh: 瓦勞人最初的居所根本不在這下界的大地上，而是在天空之上一個宜人的地區。[……]其中一人名叫奧科諾羅特，為了追捕一隻珍奇的鳥而遠行，他向那鳥射出一箭，箭未射中目標便消失了。他在尋找那支箭時，發現了一個洞，箭正是從那裡掉下去的；他從洞中望去，看見這下界的世界在下方展開[……]於是他們便循著同樣的途徑下降，子女與妻子隨行其後，只除了最後一人——一個不幸的人，因為身體過於肥胖，無法從那狹窄的洞口擠過去，便卡在那裡，把洞口完全堵住了。[……]瓦勞人因此不得不被局限在這片大地上，甚至連他們昔日居所的一瞥也看不到了！

title.en: Zohak and the Serpents Fed on Men's Brains
title.zh: 佐哈克與食腦之蛇

region.en: Babylon (Zohak's realm) / Mount Alberz, Iran
region.zh: 巴比倫（佐哈克之國）／厄爾布爾士山（伊朗）

period: Shah Nameh of Firdausi, c. 1010 CE; trans. and abridged James Atkinson, 1832

source.work: The Shah Nameh of the Persian Poet Firdausi, trans. James Atkinson (Routledge, 1892), 'Zohak'

summary.en: The evil spirit Iblis, in disguise, begs to kiss the young king Zohak's shoulder — and from the kiss spring two black serpents that can only be kept from devouring him by being fed daily with the brains of men; thus the serpent-king's tyranny over Iran begins, until Feridun rises against him.
summary.zh: 惡靈易卜劣廝喬裝乞吻少王佐哈克之肩——吻處湧出雙黑蛇，日飼人腦方免噬主；蛇王虐政由此始，直至費里敦起而伐之。

sensitivity.note: Persian epic literature (Kayanian and legendary cycle); presented as a comparative-mythology text.

passages.text: Iblis then kissed the part with fiendish glee, And vanished in an instant. From the touch Sprang two black serpents! Then a tumult rose Among the people, searching for Iblis Through all the palace, but they sought in vain. [...] The serpents writhed about as seeking food. And learned men to see the wonder came, And sage magicians tried to charm away That dreadful evil, but no cure was found.
passages.zh: 伊布利斯隨即帶著惡魔般的歡喜親吻了那處，轉瞬便消失了。從那一觸之處，竄出兩條黑蛇！接著人群中一陣騷動，他們搜遍整座宮殿尋找伊布利斯，卻徒勞無功。[……]那兩條蛇扭動著身子，彷彿在尋找食物。博學之士前來觀看這奇異之事，睿智的術士試圖以咒語驅除這可怕的邪祟，卻找不到任何醫治之法。

passages.text: Iblis again roused him by saying, that if the serpents were fed daily with human brains, which would probably kill them, his life might be prolonged, and made easy. If life has any charm for thee, The brain of man their food must be!
passages.zh: 伊布利斯又喚醒了他，說道：倘若每日以人腦餵養那兩條蛇——這大概會使牠們喪命——他的壽命便可延長，日子也能過得安逸。若生命對你尚有半分魅力，人腦便必須成為牠們的食物！

title.en: Zal on Mount Alberz, Nursed by the Simurgh
title.zh: 查爾與神鳥西摩爾格

region.en: Mount Alberz (Alborz), Iran
region.zh: 厄爾布爾士山（伊朗）

period: Shah Nameh of Firdausi, c. 1010 CE; trans. and abridged James Atkinson, 1832

source.work: The Shah Nameh of the Persian Poet Firdausi, trans. James Atkinson (Routledge, 1892), 'The birth of Zal'

summary.en: The infant Zal, born with white hair, is abandoned by his father Sam on mount Alberz — the abode of the Simurgh, the wise wonder-bird, who hears a voice from heaven, takes the crying child up to her nest, and rears him with her young; from his loins, she is told, will spring the champion of the world.
summary.zh: 查爾生而髮白，其父薩姆棄之於厄爾布爾士山——神鳥西摩爾格之居。鳥聞天音，憫而攜啼嬰歸巢，與雛同哺；天音預言其裔將出「世界之雄」。

sensitivity.note: Persian epic literature (Kayanian and legendary cycle); presented as a comparative-mythology text.

passages.text: When Sam was made acquainted with these reproaches and taunts of the people, he determined, though with a sorrowful heart, to take him up to the mountain Alberz, and abandon him there to be destroyed by beasts of prey. Alberz was the abode of the Simurgh or Griffin, and, whilst flying about in search of food for his hungry young ones, that surprising animal discovered the child lying alone upon the hard rock, crying and sucking its fingers. The Simurgh, however, felt no inclination to devour him, but compassionately took him up in the air, and conveyed him to his own habitation. [...] The young ones were also kind and affectionate to the infant, which was thus nourished and protected by the Simurgh for several years.
passages.zh: 當薩姆得知眾人的這些責難與嘲諷後，雖心懷悲傷，仍決意把他帶上阿爾伯茲山，將他棄於該處，任憑猛獸吞噬。阿爾伯茲是西摩格（即獅鷲）的居所；這神奇的生物在為饑餓的雛鳥四處覓食飛翔時，發現那孩子獨自躺在堅硬的岩石上，啼哭著吮吸自己的手指。然而西摩格並無吞食他的念頭，反而心生憐憫，將他帶上空中，送回自己的巢穴。[……]那些雛鳥對這嬰兒也十分友善親切，這孩子便這樣由西摩格哺育保護了好幾年。

passages.text: A voice, not earthly, thus addressed The Simurgh in his mountain nest -- "To thee this mortal I resign, Protected by the power divine; Let him thy fostering kindness share, Nourish him with paternal care; For from his loins, in time, will spring The champion of the world, and bring Honour on earth, and to thy name; The heir of everlasting fame."
passages.zh: 一個非塵世之聲如此對山巢中的西摩格說道——「我將這凡人交託於你，受神力庇護；讓他共享你撫育之恩，以慈父般的關懷哺育他；因為自他的腰間，終有一日將誕生世界的勇士，為大地帶來榮耀，也為你的名號增光；他將是永恆聲名的繼承者。」

title.en: Rustem Slays His Son Sohrab
title.zh: 羅斯坦弒子蘇拉布

region.en: Bukhara frontier (Iran-Turan border)
region.zh: 波斯與突朗邊境（布哈拉一帶）

period: Shah Nameh of Firdausi, c. 1010 CE; trans. and abridged James Atkinson, 1832

source.work: The Shah Nameh of the Persian Poet Firdausi, trans. James Atkinson (Routledge, 1892), 'The story of Sohrab'

summary.en: Father and son meet in single combat, neither knowing the other; Rustem hurls the youthful Sohrab to the ground and gives the deadly thrust — then learns, by the royal bracelet his mother gave him as a token, that he has slain his own son: 'My son, my son is slain.'
summary.zh: 父子相逢於陣前而不相識；羅斯坦擲倒少年蘇拉布，予之以致命一擊——旋見其臂上母贈之御鐲為記，方知所殺乃己子：「吾子！吾子亡矣！」

sensitivity.note: Persian epic literature (Kayanian and legendary cycle); presented as a comparative-mythology text.

passages.text: With rage convulsive Rustem grasps him round; Bends his strong back, and hurls him to the ground; [...] Like lightning quick he gives the deadly thrust, And spurns the Stripling weltering in the dust. [...] An icy horror chills the Champion's heart, His brain whirls round with agonizing smart [...] Believed at length, with frenzied look, he cries: "Prove thou art mine, confirm my doubting eyes! For I am Rustem!" [...] The loosened mail unfolds the bracelet bright, Unhappy gift! to Rustem's wildered sight; Prostrate he falls -- "By my unnatural hand, My son, my son is slain -- and from the land Uprooted."
passages.zh: 魯斯坦姆狂怒痙攣地將他抱住；彎下強健的背脊，把他猛摔在地；[...] 他迅如閃電般刺出致命一擊，將那少年踢倒在塵土中翻滾。[...] 冰冷的恐懼寒透勇士的心，他的頭腦因劇痛而眩暈旋轉 [...] 終於相信了，他帶著瘋狂的神情喊道：「證明你是我的，證實我這滿懷疑慮的雙眼！因為我就是魯斯坦姆！」[...] 鬆開的鎧甲展開那閃亮的手鐲，不幸的贈物啊！映入魯斯坦姆迷亂的眼中；他俯伏倒地——「以我這違逆天性的手，我的兒子，我的兒子被殺了——從此在這片土地上連根拔起。」

passages.text: [...] By my unnatural hand, My son, my son is slain -- and from the land Uprooted. Frantic, in the dust his hair He rends in agony and deep despair. The Champion rose, but ere he reached the throne, Sohrab had breathed the last expiring groan.
passages.zh: [...] 以我這違逆天性的手，我的兒子，我的兒子被殺了——從此在這片土地上連根拔起。他瘋狂地在塵土中撕扯自己的頭髮，滿懷痛苦與深沉的絕望。勇士站起身來，但在他抵達王座之前，索赫拉布已嚥下最後一口氣。

title.en: King Mandhatar, Born from the Crown of the Head
title.zh: 曼陀多王：頂髻而生

region.en: Ladakh / Kah-gyur canon (symbolic: Lhasa, Tibet)
region.zh: 迦濕彌羅經藏所載（象徵位置：拉薩）

period: Tibetan Kah-gyur (Dulva), translated 1882 (Schiefner/Ralston)

source.work: Tibetan Tales derived from Indian Sources, trans. F. Anton von Schiefner, done into English by W. R. S. Ralston (1906), 'King Mandhatar'

summary.en: From the Tibetan Kah-gyur: King Utposhadha's soft crown-tumour breaks open and out comes a golden boy perfect in the thirty-two signs of a Great Being, nursed by eighty thousand queens — Mandhatar, who one day, with his thousand sons and a mighty army, simply rises heavenward and betakes himself to the other continents.
summary.zh: 藏文甘珠爾所傳：鄔波濟瑟吒王頂髻軟瘤既熟而裂，湧出金膚童子，具大人三十二相，八萬后妃乳養之——是為曼陀多王；後一日率千子大軍凌空而起，往赴他洲。

sensitivity.note: Buddhist narrative preserved in the Tibetan canon (Kah-gyur); presented as a mythic corpus text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: In olden days, when the life of man was of unlimited duration, lived King Utposhadha. On the crown of his head grew a very soft tumour, somewhat resembling a cushion of cotton or wool, without doing him any harm. When it had become quite ripe and had broken, there came forth from it a boy, shapely and handsome and gracious, perfect in every limb and joint, with a skin the colour of gold, a head like a canopy, long arms, a broad forehead, interlacing eyebrows, and a body provided with the thirty-two signs of a Mahapurusha. Immediately after his birth he was taken into the apartments of the women; and when King Utposhadha's eighty thousand wives saw him, milk began to flow from their breasts, and each of the women cried out, "Let him suck me! let him suck me!" Wherefore he received the name of Mandhatar.
passages.zh: 在往昔，當人的壽命無有限量之時，住著烏特波沙達王。他的頭頂上長出一個極柔軟的腫瘤，略似棉花或羊毛的墊子，對他毫無傷害。當它完全成熟並破裂時，從中生出一個男孩，身形勻稱、英俊而優雅，四肢與關節無不完美，膚色如金，頭如華蓋，手臂修長，額頭寬闊，眉毛相連，身體具足大丈夫的三十二相。他出生之後立即被抱入婦女們的居室；烏特波沙達王的八萬名妻子見到他時，乳汁便從她們的乳房流出，每個婦人都喊道：「讓他吮吸我！讓他吮吸我！」因此他得名曼達塔。

passages.text: Scarcely had the king entertained this idea when, surrounded by his thousand sons, and accompanied by an army eighteen koti strong, he rose heavenward and betook himself to Purvavidehadvipa, where the four great kings came out to meet him, and the inhabitants of that continent submitted at the mere sight of his host; and when the Asuras afterwards resisted him in battle he conquered them in their own sky-citadel, and lived at ease among the gods.
passages.zh: 國王剛生起這個念頭，便由他的千名兒子圍繞，伴隨一支十八俱胝之眾的軍隊，升向天際，前往東勝身洲，在那裡四大天王出來迎接他，該洲的居民一見他的軍隊便歸順；後來阿修羅在戰鬥中抵抗他時，他在他們自己的天城之中征服了他們，並在眾神之間安樂而居。

passages.text: the seven treasures were revealed, namely, the treasure of the wheel, the treasure of the elephant, the treasure of the horse, the treasure of the gem, the treasure of the wife, the treasure of the householder, and, as the seventh, the treasure of the minister.
passages.zh: 七寶便顯現了，即：輪寶、象寶、馬寶、珠寶、女寶、居士寶，以及第七的臣寶。

title.en: The Magician's Pupil
title.zh: 術師之徒

region.en: Gandhamadana mountain (symbolic: Himalaya)
region.zh: 香醉山（象徵位置：喜馬拉雅）

period: Tibetan Kah-gyur (Dulva), translated 1882 (Schiefner/Ralston)

source.work: Tibetan Tales derived from Indian Sources, trans. F. Anton von Schiefner, done into English by W. R. S. Ralston (1906), 'The Magician's Pupil'

summary.en: A Chandala versed in the Gandhara-Mantra teaches a conceited Brahman youth his spell; the pupil at once soars by magic to the Gandhamadana mountain and plucks out-of-season fruit to amaze the king — and, through his ingratitude, his magic power deserts him.
summary.zh: 旃荼羅術師以乾達婆咒語授傲慢婆羅門少年；其徒旋以術凌空至香醉山，摘非時之果以炫於王——因忘恩負義，術力遂失。

sensitivity.note: Buddhist narrative preserved in the Tibetan canon (Kah-gyur); presented as a mythic corpus text — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: As Brahmans are of a conceited nature, the youth could not restrain himself, but must needs immediately make a trial of his magic art on the spot, and then depart. So he employed his magic power, and soared into the sky. When he came to Gandhamadana, he there plucked fruits and flowers which were out of season on earth, and gave them to the king's purohita, who gave them to King Brahmadatta. The king asked where he had got them [...] But in consequence of the youth's ingratitude his magic power deserted him.
passages.zh: 由於婆羅門天性自負，那少年無法自制，非得當場立即試驗他的法術，然後才離去。於是，他施展法力，騰空而起。當他來到乾陀摩陀那山時，便在那裡採摘了人間不當季的果實與花朵，交給國王的祭司，祭司又轉呈給梵授王。國王問他從何處得來這些東西……然而，由於那少年忘恩負義，他的法力便離他而去。

passages.text: a Chandala of Varanasi, versed in spells and magic lore, who, employing the Gandhara-Mantra, was wont to obtain by spells from the Gandhamadana mountain such fruits and flowers as were not in season, and to present them to king Brahmadatta, who made him presents; and it was with him that the Brahman youth served twelve years, propping the drunk master’s bed with his back all night, before the magic lore was communicated to him.
passages.zh: 一位波羅奈的旃陀羅，精通咒語與法術之學，他施用乾陀羅咒，慣於以咒語從乾陀摩陀那山取得不當季的果實與花朵，獻給梵授王，國王便賞賜他；婆羅門少年正是跟隨他修學十二年，整夜以背撐著醉倒師父的床，之後法術之學才傳授給他。

title.en: The Wishing-Trees of Uttarakuru
title.zh: 北俱盧洲如意樹

region.en: Uttarakuru, the northern continent (mythic)
region.zh: 北俱盧洲（神話北方大陸）

period: Tibetan Kah-gyur (Dulva), translated 1882 (Schiefner/Ralston)

source.work: Tibetan Tales derived from Indian Sources, trans. F. Anton von Schiefner, done into English by W. R. S. Ralston (1906), 'King Mandhatar'
