narrative.en:
The seiðr-mistress file holds Freyja's magic-office. The introduction-clause: at the Aesir-Vanir peace, the hostage-goddess brought the north's magic - 'Freyja? - 'taught? - the? - Aesir? - seiðr? - 'as? - 'it? - 'was? - 'practiced? - among? - the? - Vanir? - (Ynglinga's clause; the record norse-seidr-gullveig-expanded holds the practice-file) - the goddess as the pantheon's magic-teacher: the Aesir's power-set (thunder, law, runes) completed by the Vanir import (prophecy, love-craft, spirit-riding).

Odin's apprenticeship is the file's central paradox: the same chapter documents the god learning the art 'with? - 'the? - 'shame? - 'attached? - (the ergi-cost: seiðr unmanns its male performer - the record's taboo-doctrine), so the chief-god's magic is a licensed transgression: the king of the gods practicing the women's art under the women's stigma. And the flyting's charge completes the hazard-register: Loki's accusation ('thou? - 'didst? - 'ride? - 'in? - witch-shape? - 'and? - 'love? - 'man? - after? - man? - - the seiðr-flight as promiscuity: the goddess's magic and her loves charged in one breath), the social hazard that the practice-file's law-clauses codify.

The late moralization completes the file: Sorla thattr's re-narration (the necklace bought at the dwarfs' price, Odin's war-curse - the record norse-freyja-brisingamen holds the theft-and-duel register) - the converted era's moralization of the magic-goddess: love-craft as war's engine, the seiðr-mistress domesticated into a cautionary tale. The record's cultural functions are the teacher-goddess doctrine (the pantheon's magic imported by a woman hostage - the Vanir culture-transfer as the gods' second education) and the hazard-doctrine (the magic's gender-stigma documented from Odin's apprenticeship to the law-codes' clauses). In the atlas, the record anchors the initiate-goddess family: each a tradition's goddess of magic as teacher; Freyja is distinctive in the ergi-cost her students pay.

For the database, this node complements the seiðr-practice-record, the necklace-record and the Gullveig-record: here the goddess's office runs whole.

The record's institutional reach completes the file: the seiðr-mistress's office documented across the pantheon's history (the Vanir import at the treaty, Odin's apprenticeship, the flyting's charge, the converted era's moralization) - the goddess's magic-office as the corpus's longest-running institution-story. And the ergi-economics completes it: the magic's gender-cost paid by its male students - the teacher's art priced in stigma, the system's gender-grammar visible in every transaction. The record's cat-chariot register completes the file: the goddess's transport documented (the two cats drawing her chariot - the travel-magic beside the seiðr-office) - the seiðr-mistress's mobility and her magic one household-economy, the goddess's daily apparatus listed with her rites.

narrative.en:
The wanderer-god's case-file holds the disguise-episodes whole. The named masks are the file's index: Gangleri (the catechism-visitor at Asgard's illusory hall), Grimnir (the torture-victim freed by a draught - the record norse-poetic-edda-grimnismal), Gagnrad (the head-wagering exam-taker - norse-poetic-edda-vafthrudnismal), Vegtam (the dead-seeress's waker - norse-baldrs-dream), Gestumblindi (the riddle-contestant at Heidrek's hall - norse-heidrek-riddles), Bolverk (the mead-thief under service - norse-kvasir-mead), Hárbarðr (the ferry-mocker - norse-harbard-thor-ferry). Each mask is a method: the catechism, the ordeal, the exam, the necromancy, the riddle, the fraud, the flyting - the god's pedagogy distributed across disguises.

The doctrine is the wanderer's license: the god 'went? - 'under? - 'many? - names? - 'when? - 'he? - 'sought? - knowledge? - (the Hávamál-clause) - inspecting kings and keepers of knowledge under false names, teaching by ordeal, claiming prizes (the mead, the head, the answers), and paying in tricks (the seductions, the broken betrothal, the oath-evasions). The wanderer-names' list (Grimnismal's catalog and Skaldskaparmal's) is the file's name-book: two hundred names and more, 'each? - 'name? - 'a? - door? - 'to? - 'a? - door-keeper's? - story.

The record's cultural functions are the wanderer-license doctrine (the god's right to test mortals in disguise - the xeniá-doctrine's dark twin: hospitality tested by the guest who lies) and the disguise-pedagogy doctrine (each mask a different teaching-method: the corpus's curriculum distributed across personas). And the comparative frame completes it: the Greek Zeus' xenia-visits, the Chinese cloaked immortals, the Islamic dervish-tales - each a tradition's god-in-disguise; Odin is distinctive in the number of masks and the price-list of ordeals. In the atlas, the record anchors the wanderer-god family: each a deity testing mortals under false names; the Norse one keeps a case-file.

For the database, this node indexes the disguise-records already in the corpus: here the wanderer's masks are laid in one register.

The record's price-list completes the file: each disguise-episode's cost itemized (eight nights between fires; the eye pawned; the summer's labor and the seduction; the head wagered) - the wanderer's journeys run on payments, the corpus's knowledge-economy documented mask by mask. And the wanderer's threat completes it: the disguises as the god's auditing-instrument (the kings tested unawares, the knowledge-keepers examined by their own guest) - the hospitality-ethics' dark twin, documented across the corpus. The record's Vegtam-coda completes the file: the wake-the-dead mask's cost (the seeress's unmasking, the mutual loss of dignity) - the wanderer's disguises documented as two-way ordeals: the god examined as well as examining, the case-file's lessons priced in exposure.

The watchman's stray-file holds the profile's beyond-notices. The wave-birth and the foresight: Vafthrudnismal's exam-answers give the nine sisters (the wave-maidens' birth at the world's rim - the record norse-heimdall-profile holds the doctrine) and the attribute-list's signature clause: Heimdall is 'the? - 'foresightest? - of? - the? - gods? - (the exam-answer: he foreknows his own doom, like the Vanir - the watchman's foresight as office: the sentinel who sees the scheduled end and stands his post regardless).

The horn's twin-names and the social paternity: Gjallarhorn ('the? - 'sounding? - horn? - 'heard? - through? - all? - worlds) and the horn-under-the-tree reading (the sibyl hears it from Yggdrasil's crown - the alarm wired to the world-tree); Rigspula's paternity (the estates fathered in the watchman's wanderings - the record norse-rigspula holds the doctrine); and the enmity-clause: Loki's old enemy (the flyting's taunts at the hall-feast; the mutual kill at Ragnarok - the record norse-heimdall-profile holds the appointment). The kenning-register completes the file: the skalds' names for him ('Vindler's? - son? - 'the? - 'the? - 'whitening? - one? - 'Hallinskid? - 'the? - - the court-poets' citations, evidencing the watchman's verse-currency.

The record's cultural functions are the foresight-office doctrine (the sentinel who foreknows and stands post - the corpus's cleanest picture of duty against knowledge) and the stray-notice method (the profile assembled from scattered verses: the watchman as the corpus's most dispersed god, known in fragments). And the kenning-currency completes it: the watchman as a poetic instrument (the guardian invoked for hall-praise: the jarl's watchman likened to Heimdall). In the atlas, the record anchors the stray-notice family: each a profile's fragment-file; the watchman's is distinctive in the foresight-office.

And the vanir-foresight comparison completes the doctrine: the exam-answer that Heimdall foresees 'like? - 'the? - Vanir? - - the foresight credited to the other divine nation: the watchman's office borrowed from the treaty-partners.

The record is the oath-body file: law's price paid in a god's flesh.
summary.zh: 在法律框架中解讀提爾之傷：手為擔保之體（巨狼之契以神的血肉作保）、誓言法的平行制度（以祭血染紅的神廟指環、執環之手浸血——見指環記錄）、傷殘的社會意涵（「不被人稱為和解者」——散文中的辛辣一語：守信者被標記為不宜調停），以及吵罵中的悲傷條款（「狼被縛住，而我淒苦度日」——守誓者的帳簿）。此記錄是誓言身體檔案：法律以神的血肉償付代價。

narrative.en:
The oath-body file holds Týr's wound in its legal frame. The hand as contract (norse-fenrir-gleipnir holds the binding): the wolf's bargain secured by the god's flesh - 'the? - 'pledge? - 'put? - 'in? - 'the? - mouth? - 'as? - 'trust? - 'that? - 'the? - band? - 'was? - no? - trick - the collateral-doctrine in body-form; and the oath-law's parallel institution: the temple-ring reddened in sacrifice-blood, the oath-hand dipped (the record norse-oath-ring-ullr) - the same grammar in the courts: the sworn word bound in blood and held in hand.

The wound's social meaning is the prose's pointed clause: Týr 'is? - one-handed? - 'and? - is? - not? - called? - a? - reconciler? - of? - men? - - the pledge-keeper marked unfit for peacemaking: the hand that binds cannot broker. And the flyting's grief-clause completes the ledger: Loki's taunt ('I? - have? - thy? - hand? - the? - wolf's? - snare) and Týr's reply ('the? - wolf? - 'stays? - bound? - 'and? - I? - 'stay? - wretched? - - the oath-keeper's account: the bargain kept, the cost permanent, the honor intact and the life diminished - the record norse-tyr-profile holds the profile.

The record's cultural functions are the oath-body doctrine (the sworn word secured in flesh - the law's collateral imagined anatomically) and the wound-ledger doctrine (the cost of keeping an oath itemized: the hand, the office, the wife's honor charged at the flyting - the oath-keeper's full account). And the comparative frame completes it: the Roman Fides and the Greek Zeus Horkios - each a deity of the sworn word; Týr is distinctive in paying with body-parts. In the atlas, the record anchors the oath-cost family: each a tradition's sworn-word deity with a price; the Norse one is distinctive in the wound.

For the database, this node complements the profile-record, the binding-record and the oath-ring-record: here the legal frame runs whole.

The record's legal-iconography completes the file: the one-handed god as the oath-figure's body (the missing hand as the contract's receipt, visible at every assembly), and the law-codes' oath-gestures (the hand on the ring, the hand in the blood) as the myth's daily practice - the wound-doctrine documented in court-procedure. And the comparative frame completes it: the Mithraic? - the? - oath-hand traditions - each a sworn-word culture with a hand-sign; the Norse one pays in flesh.

 The record's flyting-silence completes the file: Týr’s second taunt answered with silence (the charge he cannot rebut) - the oath-keeper’s ledger closed in silence, the profile’s cost documented by what the god will not say.

title.en: Sif's Hair and Kin-Symbolism: The Golden Crop

summary.en: Sif's hair read as kin-and-crop symbolism: the episode (Loki's midnight shearing, Thor's rage, the dwarf-gift of real-gold hair that grows like living hair - the record norse-mjolnir-forging holds the forge-scene), the kenning-economy (Sif's hair as a standard gold-kenning - the wife's honor priced in metal), the crop-reading (hair as grain: the golden harvest on the field-wife's head - the fertility-symbolism argued from the kennings), and the household-frame (Sif as Thor's wife, the mother of Ullr and Thrud - the thunderer's household). The record is the kin-symbol file.
summary.zh: 以親族與莊稼象徵解讀西芙之髮：情節（洛基夜半剃髮、索爾之怒、矮人獻上「如真髮般生長」的黃金髮——見鍛造記錄）、隱喻經濟（西芙之髮為標準的黃金隱喻——妻子之榮以金屬計價）、禾穗解讀（髮如穀：田婦頭上的金色收成——由隱喻推證的豐產象徵），以及家庭框架（西芙為索爾之妻、烏勒與斯魯德之母——雷霆者的家宅）。此記錄是親族象徵檔案。

canonical_translation: Brodeur 1916 (public domain); Bellows 1923 (public domain)

narrative.en:
The kin-symbol file holds Sif's hair in its symbolic frames. The episode (norse-mjolnir-forging holds the forge): Loki's midnight shearing of Thor's wife - the trick that opens the treasure-cycle - and the dwarf-gift: hair of real gold that 'grows? - 'like? - 'other? - hair? - - the honor restored in metal. The kenning-economy: 'Sif's? - hair? - is? - a? - standard? - gold-kenning? - (the Skaldskaparmal lists) - the wife's honor priced in metal: the insult measured in gold, the restoration paid in the same coin - the household's economy in verse-diction.

The crop-reading is the file's interpretive register: the scholars' argument that the golden hair is grain - the field's harvest as the earth-wife's hair, the cutting and regrowth as the agricultural year - 'hair? - 'like? - 'the? - corn? - 'cut? - 'and? - 'grown? - again? - (the fertility-reading built from the kenning-lists, where Sif's hair names gold AND the golden crop is named by the same figure). The household-frame completes it: Sif as Thor's wife (the thunderer married to the earth-figure: rain married to field), mother of Ullr (the ski-god, stepson) and Thrud (the strength-daughter) - the thunder-household's roster.

And the flyting's charge: Loki's taunt at the feast ('I? - 'know? - 'one? - who? - shared? - thy? - bed? - 'the? - adultery-charge - the record norse-lokasenna-flyting) - the kin-symbol under moral attack, the honor-theme continued after the hair is restored. The record's cultural functions are the honor-economy doctrine (the wife's hair as the household's visible worth, priced and paid in gold) and the crop-symbolism doctrine (the golden harvest on the field-wife's head - the fertility-reading documented in the kennings). In the atlas, the record anchors the kin-symbol family: each a tradition's household-emblem read symbolically; Sif's is distinctive in the kenning-economy.

For the database, this node complements the forge-record and the flyting-record: here the symbolism runs whole.

The record's iconographic reach completes the file: the golden-haired goddess documented in no surviving image but reconstructed from the kennings - the kin-symbol's evidence entirely poetic, which is itself the datum (Sif's office documented by the verse-economy alone). And the flyting's continuation completes it: the honor-theme running after the restoration - the corpus's longest portrait of a household-insult and its repair, from shearing to hearing? - hearing? - to flyting.

 The record's harvest-parallel completes the file: the kenning-economy’s double entry (gold as Sif’s hair; grain as the field’s gold) - the household’s wealth and the field’s wealth named by one figure, the kin-symbol’s two economies fused in a single diction.

summary.en: The treaty-marriage's ritual grammar expanded: the atonement-frame (the armed arrival, the compensations: husband-choice, laugh-payment, star-setting - each a legal form), the feet-choice's ritual logic (the bride's consent manufactured by ceremony: the choice by proxy), the cohabitation-clause (nine nights alternating - the experimental marriage as contract term), the dissolution and its aftermath (the return to Thrymheim, the ski-goddess's continuing visits: 'she? - 'comes? - 'to? - 'the? - feasts? - still? - the treaty's persistence), and the flyting's scandal-clause (Loki's charge of the goddess's bed-visit to her father's? - the? - incest-insinuation). The record is the treaty-marriage file.

narrative.en:
The treaty-marriage file expands the ritual grammar of Njord and Skaði (norse-njord-skadi holds the core narrative). The compensations as legal forms: the husband-choice by feet (the bride's consent manufactured by proxy - the ceremony choosing for her), the laugh-payment (Loki's goat-trick: the settlement's mirth-clause, legally owed), and the star-setting (the father's eyes as memorial - the compensation's permanent form). Each compensation is a recognized legal instrument (choice, satisfaction, memorial) staged in myth.

The cohabitation-clause and its aftermath: the nine-nights-alternating term ('the? - 'experimental? - 'marriage: 'each? - 'dwelling? - nine? - nights? - 'in? - the? - other's? - home) as a contract's trial-period; the dissolution on evidence (the gull-cries and wolf-howls as the experiment's data); and the treaty's persistence: the divorce does not end the alliance - 'Skaði? - 'comes? - 'to? - 'the? - feasts? - 'still? - (the prose's clause: the ex-wife attending the gods' assemblies, the treaty-hospitality continuing), the winter-goddess keeping her seat in the pantheon after the marriage ends.

And the flyting's scandal-clause: Loki's charge ('thou? - 'didst? - share? - thy? - bed? - 'with? - thy? - brother? - - the incest-insinuation aimed at Skaði's giant-household: the treaty-union defamed by the trickster's charge), the marriage's honor under attack in the same genre that documents it. The record's cultural functions are the marriage-as-treaty doctrine (the divorce as a treaty's normal dissolution, the alliance persisting past the marriage - the north's own politics-of-marriage) and the compensation-grammar doctrine (choice, laugh, memorial as legal instruments staged in myth). In the atlas, the record anchors the treaty-marriage family: each a union resolving a feud; the Norse one is distinctive in the trial-term and the surviving alliance.

For the database, this node complements the core-record and the Skadi-cult-materials: here the ritual grammar runs whole.

The record's ritual-theory completes the file: the compensations' grammar (choice, laugh, memorial) documented as the north's standard settlement-instruments (the same three payments the sagas' feud-settlements use), so the mythic marriage documents the legal marriage's machinery - the treaty-union as the north's own divorce-law in miniature. And the ski-goddess's continuing cult completes it: Skaði's winter-places and snowshoe-place-names - the treaty's residue written into the landscape.

 The record's winter-office completes the file: Skaði's continuing functions after the divorce (the ski-hunts, the mountain-hall)s keeping, the feasts) seat) documented as the treaty)s standing army of rights - the ex-wife)s privileges itemized, the north)s own post-settlement law in mythic dress. And the parallel-settlement register completes it: the sagas) real divorce-and-settlement cases (the property-divisions and the feast-rights negotiated) - the mythic treaty)s grammar documented in the courts) practice.

summary.en: Sigurd's father's own career collected: the apple-sign and the great hall, Signy's forced marriage and the vengeance-plot (the shape-shift into wolves, the wolf-coat years of Sinfjotli), the disguised rescue and the burning of Siggeir's hall, Sigmund's later wars and marriages (the shipwrecked bride, Hjordis and the broken Gram), and Odin's final withdrawal (the spear shattering the sword at the last battle - the god reclaiming his gift). The record is the father-arc: the vengeance-plot that makes Sigurd possible.

narrative.en:
The father-arc holds Sigmund's own episodes (norse-volsunga-saga-full holds the whole saga's arc). The apple-sign and the hall: Volsung's palace built around the apple-tree, the god's token in the queen's lap - the ancestry-miracle that founds the line. Signy's plot: the forced marriage to Siggeir (the bride's loathing at the wedding-feast), the father's death and brothers' enslavement, the vengeance-plan years in the making - and its terrible instrument: the shape-shift into wolves ('the? - 'wolfskins? - 'found? - 'in? - 'the? - wood? - 'the? - 'ten? - nights? - 'the? - wolf-coat? - 'odd? - 'even? - 'the? - - the twins' wolf-years, Sinfjotli growing up in the coat), the disguise as wandering smiths (the boys disguised, the sister's sons unrecognized), the poison-test (Sinfjotli'sProof? - the? - mead-proof? - the? - - 'the? - 'boy? - 'drinks? - 'the? - poisoned? - ale? - 'and? - 'does? - not? - die? - - the viper-mother's? - the? - mother's? - poison-test survived), and the fire: the hall burned with Siggeir's kin inside, Signy entering the flames after her revenge - the plot's completion and its price.

The later episodes: Sigmund's wars (the vengeance-king's campaigns), the shipwrecked bride (the first wife's father drowned by Sigmund's raid - the bride's terror at the shore), and Hjordis (the second marriage: the danish? - the Hunding-raid that kills Sigmund, Odin appearing in the battle 'with? - 'his? - spear? - 'in? - 'the? - host? - 'the? - god's? - intervention: 'the? - spear? - 'shattered? - 'the? - sword? - 'Gram? - 'on? - the? - helm? - - the gift reclaimed, the father dying so the son's story can begin). The record's cultural functions are the vengeance-plot doctrine (the mother's revenge as the son's origin: Sigurd born of a plot) and the god-withdrawal doctrine (Odin reclaiming the gift at the father's death - the divine hand steering the family's biography). In the atlas, the record anchors the father-arc family: each a hero's parent-generation as narrative; the Volsung one is distinctive in the wolf-coat years.

For the database, this node precedes the Sigurd-records: the father's episodes fill the cycle's root.

The record's motif-register completes the file: the wolf-coat episode as the corpus's berserk-origin-document (the shape-shift as the berserk-state's mythic charter), and the god-withdrawal's theology (Odin breaking the sword he gave: the gift's revocation as the father-generation's fate - the corpus's clear statement that divine gifts are loans). And the Signy-register completes it: the sister as the vengeance-plot's author - the corpus's great female plotter, whose death in the fire closes her own design.

narrative.en:
The court-tragedy file holds the Gjúki household's inner destruction. The hall's society: Gunnar the ring-giver (the king whose charisma is gift), Hogni the wise brother (the counselor who speaks truth and is not heeded), Guthorm the instrument (the brother who does the killing because the others' hands are oath-bound), Gudrun the sister (the marriage-piece traded for the hall's security). The queens' quarrel is the file's signature scene: the river-bathing rank-debate (Brynhild insisting she is the greater queen, wading upstream; Gudrun revealing that Sigurd took Gunnar's shape through the fire - so the proud wife's marriage was a proxy's fraud) - 'the? - 'rank? - quarrel? - 'that? - 'unmans? - 'the? - king? - (the saga's clause: Gunnar's kingship destroyed by his wife's humiliation).

Gunnar's broken oath: the oath sworn on the arm-ring by the waterfall ('the? - 'oath? - 'by? - 'the? - water? - 'that? - 'he? - 'would? - not? - wed? - 'her? - - and the evasion by proxy: the oath's letter kept, its meaning destroyed by Sigurd-in-disguise - the record norse-oath-ring-ullr's grammar inverted: the sworn word evaded through ceremony). Brynhild's death-lay (the prophecy-spoken dying: the hall's future foretold as her pyre is lit), and Atli's plot (the marriage-alliance that trades Gudrun for peace, then the lure of the Rhine-gold that kills the brothers - the court's end).

The record's cultural functions are the household-tragedy doctrine (the royal family destroyed not by monsters but by its own oath-evasion and women's war - the corpus's domestic register of doom) and the rank-quarrel doctrine (the queens' humiliation-battle as the state-crisis: status as politics). In the atlas, the record anchors the court-tragedy family: each a royal household's inner destruction; the Gjúki one is distinctive in the oath-evasion by proxy.

For the database, this node holds the court-side records the cycle's battle-records lack: the hall's own destruction-file.

The record's comparative reach completes the file: the Gjúki-court material's German twin (the Nibelungenlied's Kriemhild and Etzel-court: the same household-tragedy in a continental dress), so the tragedy-file documents one story's two literatures - the Rhine-court and the Norse hall as one narrative field. And the queens' quarrel's afterlife completes it: the river-bathing scene as the tradition's most-cited domestic scene - the court-tragedy's engine remembered long after the halls burned.

 The record's counsel-tragedy completes the file: Hogni's wisdom ignored (the brother who warns against the oath’s evasion and the Atli-ride, and is taken anyway) - the court’s counselor as the tragedy’s Cassandra, the household’s end documented through its one clear voice going unheeded.

narrative.en:
The Danish cycle-file holds the Hrólf-material beyond the Bjarki-episode (norse-bodvar-bjarki). The birth-tales: Helgi's elf-woman (the mother Kára? - the valkyrie-shaped lineage), and Böðvar's bear-father (the enchanted Bjorn - the shape-family's origin), the sons' upbringing with the witch-queen Hvit. The hall's society: Hrólf's champions at Lejre - the roster (Böðvar Bjarki foremost; Hjalti the magnanimous; Hrómundr? - the? - twelve? - named? - champions), and the gold-giving: the king's generosity-test ('the? - 'gold? - 'scattered? - 'on? - the? - field? - 'for? - 'the? - fleeing? - - the ring-giver's profile: Hrólf as the north's most open-handed king, 'the? - 'greatest? - 'giver? - 'of? - rings.

The war: Skuld the witch-daughter (Hrólf's half-sister, elf-begotten, raising the ghost-army - 'the? - 'eleven? - hundred? - ghost-warriors? - 'in? - 'boiled? - mail? - 'the? - undead? - host? - - the hall's fall by sorcery: the champions dying against the conjured dead), and the last battle (the Bjarkamal's fragments: the exhortation-scene as the hall falls - 'the? - 'blunted? - 'spear? - 'day? - 'the? - dawn? - 'of? - war? - 'the? - oldest? - battle-verse? - fragments? - 'the? - skaldic? - witness), and the legacy: Hrólf's name as the north's heroic-king standard (the epithet Kraki - 'the? - ladle? - - the nick-name's story: the boy who scattered peas? - 'the? - 'nickname's? - tale). The record's cultural functions are the hero-king-cycle doctrine (the Danish national hero-cycle: the hall, the champions, the fall - the north's own Beowulf-generation, attested in saga, Latin and skaldic verse) and the ghost-army doctrine (the hall destroyed by sorcery: the conjured dead as the final enemy - the undead-register in royal dress). In the atlas, the record anchors the hero-king-cycle family: each a tradition's national hero-hall; the Danish one is distinctive in its Beowulf-twinship.

For the database, this node complements the Bjarki-record: here the cycle runs whole.

The record's cross-corpus attestation completes the file: the Hrólf-material documented in saga, Latin history, skaldic verse-fragments and the rímur-tradition - four media for one cycle, the corpus's best-attested heroic-king material after the Sigurd-cycle. And the nick-name's tale completes it: the epithet Kraki explained by the boy's grain-scattering (the famine-gift trick), the king named by generosity - the cycle's charter in a nickname.

 The record's genealogy completes the file: the Skjöldung-frame’s claim (Hrólf descending from Skjöldr son of Odin) tying the Danish cycle to the founding-record - the hero-king’s charter running into the dynasty-record, the cycle and the ethnogenesis one continuum.

narrative.en:
The North-Sea file holds the Beowulf-Norse cross-references. The named kin: Hrothgar of the poem is the Hróar of the Danish tradition (Hrólf Kraki's uncle-king - the same Healfdene-Hrothgar genealogy the saga knows); the poem's Scyldings are the Skjoldungs (the dynasty-record norse-skjold-dynasty's kin); Ingeld of the poem's feud-episodes is the Ingeld of the Saxo-tradition (the Frisian-war king) - the poem's cast is the Norse kings' cast, documented from the other shore.

The episode-twins are the file's core: Grendel and Glamr (the hall-haunter and the valley-ghost: both night-walkers breaking doors 'with? - 'a? - 'wrench? - 'that? - 'cracks? - 'the? - timber, both wrestled in the dark by the visiting champion, both dying under the grip and leaving a curse-bequest - the record norse-draugr-glamr holds the saga's twin); the dragon's barrow and Grettir's mound (the treasure-guarding dead and the thief-hero entering alone); the fire-drake and the mound's wight (both treasure-wrath narratives); and the swimming-contest with Breca and the saga-world's sea-trials (the boasting-and-testing register both literatures share).

The doctrine-kin completes the file: the hall-joy raided by the outside (Heorot's songs and the moor's envy; Lejre's feast and Skuld's sorcery), the old king and the young champion (Hrothgar sheltering Beowulf; Hrólf harboring Böðvar), and the fate-clauses (the wyrd-doctrine and the ørlög-doctrine: both traditions' doom-grammars). The record's cultural functions are the shared-heroic-world doctrine (the North Sea as one narrative ecology: the poem's Danes are the saga's Danes, the monsters' grammar shared) and the comparative-method doctrine (each tradition reading the other: the saga as the poem's documented twin, the poem as the saga's oldest cousin). In the atlas, the record anchors the cross-reference family: each a tradition's neighbor-file; the North-Sea one is distinctive in the named kin.

For the database, this node links the Norse heroic-records to the English poem: the cross-references as data.

The record's method completes the file: the cross-references work in both directions (the saga illuminating the poem's lost heroic context; the poem's dating anchoring the saga-material's antiquity), so the North-Sea file is a two-way instrument - the myth corpus's comparative method documented in practice. And the monsters' shared grammar completes it: the night-haunter, the barrow-wight and the fire-drake as one ecology of hall-raiders across both literatures.

 The record's shared-verse register completes the file: the measure and diction kin (the alliterative line, the kenning-like compounds, the flyting-form) shared across the North Sea - the two literatures) poetics as one family, the cross-references documented in metre as well as matter. And the Christian-frame contrast completes it: the English poem)s told-by-Christians frame against the Norse corpus)s learned-compilation frame - one heroic world recorded by two different converstion-era editing strategies, the file)s methodological point.

The local-serpent file holds the dragon-motif's minor-key narratives. The record's cultural functions are the dragon-as-local-doctrine (the serpent-motif's minor register: local hoards, local fords, local battles - the dragon mapped onto real geography) and the epithet-origin doctrine (the slaying as the name's proof: Lodbrok's breeches, Frotho's wax, the hero named by the monster's death). narrative.en:
The outlaw-boundary file holds the saga-law's hero-tales. Víga-Glúmr: the fate-cleared killer (the naming-day omen: 'thrice? - 'should? - 'he? - be? - outlawed? - 'and? - 'thrice? - cleared? - 'the? - grandfather's? - prophecy? - - the killer whose outlawries are cleared by settlement, the fate-meter running through the courts), and the land-wight's? - the? - 'the? - eye-motes? - episode (the old man's eye-rubbing that clears Glúmr's sight? - 'the? - 'old? - man? - 'rubbing? - his? - eye? - 'as? - Glúmr? - 'strikes? - - the sympathetic-magic detail the saga preserves), and the saga's verdict: the fate runs through the law.

Grettir and Gísli complete the register: Grettir's long outlawry (the dark-fear as the sentence's instrument - the record norse-grettir-saga), and Gísli's dream-vigil (the outlaw haunted by two dreams - the bright dream-wife and the blood-handed dream-wife - 'the? - 'two? - 'women? - 'who? - 'come? - 'in? - sleep? - 'the? - - the fate's two counselors, and the sister's oath-betrayal (Thórdís revealing the brother-killer at the farm-council - the oath's last breach), the outlaw's end in the single combat against overwhelming odds ('the? - 'last? - 'stand? - 'with? - the? - sword? - 'stuck? - in? - the? - hillside? - - the hero's death-position preserved in verse).

The law's clauses complete the file: the Grágás outlawry-terms (the lesser outlawry: three years and property; the full outlawry: the skógarmaðr - the forest-man, who may be killed by anyone; the fjörbaugsgarðr? - the? - - the foreign-service option: three years overseas as the sentence's alternative), the law's grammar of exile. The record's cultural functions are the law-as-fate doctrine (the courts as the fate's machinery - the record norse-njalssaga's thesis continued) and the heroism-measured-by-law doctrine: the saga-hero's greatness calibrated in outlawry-terms. In the atlas, the record anchors the outlaw-boundary family: each a tradition's hero-versus-law register; the Norse one is distinctive in the fate-cleared killer.

For the database, this node holds the saga-law register: the boundary where heroism and outlawry meet.

The record's genre-boundary completes the file: the family-sagas' outlaw-tales as the myth-motifs' legal laboratory (the fate-prophecies running through the courts, the curses and oaths enforceable in law, the ghosts testifying in disputes) - the myth-tradition's motifs documented inside ordinary litigation, the corpus's social register at its most precise. And the outlaw's afterlife completes it: the skógarmaðr figure's folk-afterlife (the forest-man of later ballads) - the boundary-tales' persistence beyond the law-books.

title.en: The Coming of the Tuatha Dé Danann from the Four Cities
title.zh: 圖阿哈·迪·丹安自四城乘霧而來

region.en: Magh Nia, Connacht, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭康諾特馬格尼亞平原（象徵定位）

period: Recorded in Lebor Gabála Érenn and Cath Maige Tuired traditions, 11th-12th c. manuscripts; Lady Gregory retelling 1904

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book One, Chapter I, eBook #14465

summary.en: The people of the goddess Dana arrive in Ireland from four cities of learning in the north, bearing four treasures — the Stone of Destiny, the sword, the spear of victory and the ever-satisfying cauldron — and come down through the air and the high air in a mist on Beltaine morning, the Firbolgs who hold the island seeing nothing but fog on the hills.
summary.zh: 達娜女神之民自北方四座學藝之城而來，攜四寶——命運之石、劍、勝利之矛、永不空乏之釜——於五月朔日乘霧自空中降臨愛爾蘭；先居之巴格斯人（Bag Men）惟見山間白霧，不見其人。

sensitivity.note: Symbolic pin: the mist-landing site is unlocatable in the narrative; Magh Nia in Connacht is where the Tuatha settled before the First Battle. Living Irish-language and Gaelic communities hold the tradition of the Sídhe; stories are collected from public-domain print, not field consultation.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase of Gods and Fighting Men, Book One ch. 1: It was in a mist the Tuatha Dé Danann, the people of the gods of Dana, came through the air and the high air to Ireland. They came from the north, from four cities where they fought their battle for learning — Falias, Gorias, Finias and Murias — taught by four wise men, and they carried from those cities their four treasures: the Lia Fáil, the Stone of Destiny, from Falias; a sword from Gorias; a spear of victory from Finias; and from Murias the cauldron no company ever went away from unsatisfied. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book One ch. 1; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 《眾神與戰士》第一卷第一章的濃縮意譯：達努神族——達娜諸神的子民——是乘著霧，穿過空氣與高空，來到愛爾蘭的。他們來自北方，來自四座城市，在那裡為求學識而征戰——法利亞斯、戈利亞斯、菲尼亞斯與穆利亞斯——受四位智者教導，並從那些城市帶來他們的四件寶物：來自法利亞斯的命運之石「利亞法爾」；來自戈利亞斯的一把劍；來自菲尼亞斯的勝利之矛；以及來自穆利亞斯的那口大釜，凡離去者無不饜足。非逐字引文。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: Nuada was their king; among the chief men were Ogma who taught writing, Diancecht the healer, Neit god of battle, Credenus the craftsman and Goibniu the smith. Among the women were the battle goddesses Badb and Macha, the Morrígu the Crow of Battle, Eire and Fodla and Banba who gave their names to Ireland, Eadon nurse of poets, and Brigit of poetry and healing, whose face was one side ugly and one side comely. The three things they set above all others were the plough, the sun and the hazel tree. They had a well below the sea where nine hazels of wisdom dropped their blossoms into purple water and five salmon ate the nuts; whoever ate one salmon would know all wisdom and all poetry. They landed on Beltaine, May Day, and the Firbolgs saw only a mist lying on the hills. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book One ch. 1; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 濃縮意譯：努阿達是他們的王；首領之中有傳授文字的奧格瑪、醫者迪安凱特、戰神內特、工匠克雷德努斯與鐵匠戈伊布紐。女子之中有戰鬥女神巴德與瑪哈、戰鴉莫莉根、將名字賜予愛爾蘭的埃里、福德拉與班巴、詩人的乳母埃東，以及司詩歌與醫治的布里吉特，她的臉一面醜陋、一面姣好。他們置於萬物之上的三樣事物是犁、太陽與榛樹。他們在海底有一口井，九株智慧榛樹將花朵落入紫色的水中，五條鮭魚吃下榛果；凡吃下一條鮭魚者，便知曉一切智慧與一切詩歌。他們在貝爾丹節、即五朔節登陸，而菲爾博格人只看見一層霧橫臥於山丘之上。非逐字引文。

canonical_translation: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men, London 1904 (public domain); underlying sources: Cath Maige Tuired (Stokes, Irische Texte, 1891); Lebor Gabála Érenn (Macalister edition 1938-56, copyright)

narrative.en:
The arrival of the Tuatha Dé Danann is Ireland's true myth of creation — not a making of the world out of chaos, but a consecration of an island by a people who are gods, poets, smiths and healers at once.

They did not come by land or sea. The early tales insist it was in a mist, through the air and the high air, from the north. Behind them lay four cities of the far north — Falias the great, Gorias the shining, Finias and Murias the rich — where the young gods had fought their battle for learning, the meaning being that knowledge itself was won like a war. In each city sat one wise teacher: Senias in Murias, Arias the fair-haired poet in Finias, Urias of the noble nature in Gorias, and Morias in Falias. From those cities the newcomers brought four treasures that map their whole theology: from Falias the Lia Fáil, the Stone of Destiny that would cry out under the feet of a lawful king; from Gorias the Sword; from Finias the Spear of Victory; and from Murias the Cauldron that no company ever went away from unsatisfied. Stone, blade, point and vessel — sovereignty, war, victory and abundance.

Nuada was their king. Ogma his brother taught them writing. Diancecht understood healing, Neit was a god of battle, Credenus the craftsman and Goibniu the smith, whose spear-points never missed and whose ale kept age and death away. Among their women were the battle-goddesses Badb, Macha and the Morrígu the Crow of Battle; Eire, Fodla and Banba, three daughters of the Dagda who would each give her name to Ireland; Eadon, nurse of poets; and Brigit — woman of poetry, healing and smith's work, inventor of the whistle for calling through the night — whose one face was ugly and the other beautiful, whose name meant a fiery arrow. Dana herself, the mother of the gods, was beyond them all.

The three things they put above all others were the plough, the sun and the hazel tree — Coll the hazel, Cecht the plough, Grian the sun, in whose three names Ireland was said to be divided. Below the sea lay their well of wisdom, where nine hazels grew and rained their blossoms into purple water; five salmon waiting there ate the falling nuts, and the red spots on their skin carried the color of that knowledge. Whoever ate one of those salmon would know all wisdom and all poetry. Seven streams of inspiration rose from that well and turned back into it again, and all people of many arts have drunk from them — the same well that Cormac would later see at the heart of Manannan's otherworld.

They landed on the first day of Beltaine, May Day, on the northwest coast of Connacht. The Firbolgs who held the island — the Men of the Bag, come earlier from the south — saw nothing at all: a mist lying on the hills. But their king Eochaid son of Erc dreamed a dream, and his druids read it: a strong enemy was coming. The myth thus begins as the old world's nightmare, and the new people of the arts walking out of fog to take the island that the three queens of Ireland, Eire and Fodla and Banba, would make for their own names.
narrative.zh: 圖阿哈·迪·丹安（達娜女神之民）之降臨，乃愛爾蘭真正的創世神話：非由混沌造世界，而是以神與匠師之民將島嶼祝聖。其眾不履陸海，乘霧自北方高空而來；北方四城——大法利亞斯、光戈里亞斯、菲尼亞斯、富繆里亞斯——為學藝而戰之地，四賢者各授其藝。攜四寶而來：法利亞斯之命運之石（Lia Fáil，合法国王踐之則鳴）、戈里亞斯之劍、菲尼亞斯之勝利之矛、繆里亞斯永不使賓客空乏之釜——即主權、戰爭、勝利與豐足之總圖。努阿達為王；歐格瑪授文字，迪安徹特司療，內特司戰，克雷德努斯司工藝，戈伊布尼烏司鍛冶——其矛無虛發，其麥酒令人不老不死。女神輩有戰神巴德布、瑪哈與戰烏摩里古；達格達三女艾雷、福德拉與班巴後各以名予愛爾蘭；詩人之乳母伊頓；與兼詩、療、鍛冶之布里吉特——一面醜一面美，名義為「火之箭」。達娜母神居眾之上。其所最尊者三：犁、日、榛。海底有智慧之泉，九株榛樹落花於紫水；五鮭食堅果，食之者得全知與全詩。至五月朔日（Beltaine）登岸於康諾特西北，巴格斯人惟見山間之霧。其王伊奧凱得夢，德魯伊釋之：強敵將至。神話遂以舊世之噩夢始，以新藝之民自霧中走出、島將以三女神之名命名終。

functions: Creation-by-consecration: the island is claimed by a god-race through arts and treasures, not by chaos-splitting
Charter of the four pagan mysteries — stone (sovereignty), sword, spear, cauldron — later mirrored in the four Treasures of the Sídhe
Aition of Beltaine: the gods land at the fire-feast of May Day
Etiology of Ireland's names through the three queens Eire, Fodla, Banba

title.en: The First Battle of Mag Tuired: Tuath Dé against Fir Bolg
title.zh: 第一次馬格·圖雷德之戰：達娜之民對巴格斯人

period: Recorded in Cath Maige Tuired Cunga traditions and Lebor Gabála; 11th c. manuscripts; Gregory retelling 1904

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book One, Chapter I, eBook #14465

summary.en: The Firbolg champion Sreng and the god-champion Bres meet half-way over their shields and trade spears as proof of one another's peoples; parley fails, and in the first battle on Magh Tuired the gods win, their king Nuada losing his arm, while the defeated Firbolgs are given Connacht to keep.
summary.zh: 巴格斯勇士斯倫格與神族勇士布雷斯隔盾相望、互換長矛以驗其族；談判既破，馬格·圖雷德首戰之中神族雖勝而王努阿達失臂，敗者巴格斯人獲賜康諾特以居。

sensitivity.note: Location verified: the First Battle is traditionally placed at Mag Tuired near Cong, Co. Mayo. The Firbolgs survive in the tale as ancestors of later heroes (Ferdiad, Erc).

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: Sreng son of Erc came out from Teamhair with his strong red-brown shield and two thick-handled spears to look at the strangers; Bres came from the Tuatha Dé to meet him. Each thrust his shield into the ground and looked over the rim; each was in dread of the other's spear — the thin sharp darts of the gods, the heavy blunt Craisech of the Firbolgs whose thrust was death or wounds that never healed. They exchanged spears so each host could see what the other was used to, and Bres brought back his offer: give us half of Ireland in peace, or there will be battle. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book One ch. 1; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 濃縮意譯：埃爾克之子斯倫帶著他那面堅固的紅褐色盾牌與兩支粗柄長矛，從塔拉出來察看那些陌生人；布雷斯從達努神族那邊前來與他相會。兩人各自將盾牌插入地面，越過盾緣觀望；彼此都畏懼對方的矛——諸神那細而銳利的飛鏢，以及菲爾博格人那沉重而鈍拙的克雷塞赫，其刺擊非死即為永不癒合的創傷。他們交換了矛，好讓雙方人馬看清對方慣用何物，布雷斯帶回了他的提議：和平地給我們半個愛爾蘭，否則便只有一戰。非逐字引文。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: The Firbolgs would not yield the half, saying the strangers would soon take the whole. The queens Badb, Macha and the Morrígu covered the Firbolgs' ground with mists, clouds of darkness, showers of fire and blood for three days until the three druids of the Firbolgs broke the enchantment. The battle began on Midsummer day: three nines of hurlers on each side were all killed, the hosts fought four days, the physicians of each side bathed the living in healing herbs each evening. On the fourth day the gods prevailed; King Eochaid, thirst-driven off the field, was overtaken and slain at the strand of Traigh Eothaile, and Sreng was left with the last three hundred of eleven battalions. Nuada offered peace: Sreng chose Connacht, and his people lived there after — of them came Ferdiad, who fought Cuchulainn at the ford, and Erc, who gave him his death. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book One ch. 1; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 濃縮意譯：菲爾博格人不肯讓出那一半，說這些陌生人不久便會奪走全部。女王巴德、瑪哈與莫莉根以霧、黑暗之雲、火與血之雨籠罩菲爾博格人的陣地達三日之久，直到菲爾博格人的三位德魯伊破除了這法術。戰鬥始於仲夏之日：雙方各有三個九人的曲棍球手全數陣亡，兩軍交戰四日，雙方的醫者每晚以療傷藥草為生者沐浴。第四日，諸神得勝；國王埃奧凱德因口渴而離開戰場，在特拉赫·埃奧泰爾的海灘上被追上並殺死，斯倫則率十一營中最後的三百人殘存。努阿達提出和平：斯倫選擇了康諾特，他的族人此後便住在那裡——費爾迪亞德即出自他們之中，他在淺灘與庫胡林交戰；埃爾克亦然，他給了庫胡林致命一擊。非逐字引文。

canonical_translation: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men, London 1904 (public domain); cf. Cath Maige Tuired Cunga in later dindsenchas (Gwynn, Metrical Dindsenchas, copyright)

narrative.en:
Before the gods could be kings of Ireland they had to win it from men — and the tale of the First Battle of Mag Tuired is told not as a slaughter but as a meeting of two armies who discover they are kin.

The Firbolgs, the Men of the Bag, held the island. When word came to their king Eochaid son of Erc at Teamhair that a new race had settled at Magh Rein — whether from the earth, the skies or the wind nobody could say — there was no great wonder on him, for he had dreamed, and his druids had read the dream: a strong enemy was coming. He sent Sreng, a great fighting man, out toward the strangers; and the Tuatha Dé sent Bres to meet him. The two champions walked one toward the other slowly, shields raised, each stopping at talking distance — and then each put his shield before his body and struck it hard into the ground, and looked at one another over the rim.

The first discovery was that they spoke the same tongue: when Sreng heard Irish on Bres's lips he was less uneasy, and they drew near and asked after one another's kindred. The second discovery was mutual respect for weapons. Sreng feared the thin, sharp, hard-pointed spears of the gods; Bres feared the thick-handled Craisech of the Firbolgs, blunt at the side, that broke shields and crushed flesh and bone, whose thrust was death or a wound that never healed. So they exchanged spears, so that the fighters on each side might see what the other was used to — a courteous detail that marks this as a tale told by both peoples' descendants. Bres delivered the offer: half of Ireland in peace, or battle. Sreng advised his king to share the country; Eochaid and his chief men refused: 'if we give the half they will soon take the whole.'

Then the gods showed their other weapons. Three queens — Badb, Macha and the Morrígu — went to Teamhair and by enchantment brought mists, clouds of darkness, showers of fire and of blood over the Firbolgs for three days, until three Firbolg druids, Cesarn, Gnathach and Ingnathach, broke the spell: druid against druid before spear against spear.

The battle itself was contracted like a lawful duel. The gods' hurlers went out first and were killed to a man; Eochaid asked whether the battle would be every day or every second day; Nuada answered every day, but with equal numbers on each side — and Eochaid agreed unhappily, for the Firbolgs were the more numerous. For four days the hosts fought, and each evening the physicians of both sides made a bath of healing herbs so the maimed could rise sound for the next day's fight. On the fourth day the gods got the upper hand. A great thirst came on Eochaid; he went off the field for drink with three fifties protecting him, was pursued to the strand of Traigh Eothaile, and fell there, and a great heap of stones was raised over his grave.

When only three hundred of the eleven battalions were left, and Sreng at their head, Nuada offered peace and a province of their choosing. Sreng took Connacht, and the Firbolgs lived there and their children after them — of whom, the tale insists, came Ferdiad, who held the ford against Cuchulainn, and Erc, who gave Cuchulainn his death. The conquered are not erased but saved for the heroic age to come: an epic's cast of enemies being its oldest friends.
narrative.zh: 神欲為愛爾蘭之王，必先自人族手中得之；首戰之記非屠殺而為兩族相認之會。巴格斯人（Fir Bolg）先居其島。新族至馬格·雷因消息傳至塔拉王伊奧凱時，王無大異——因已得夢兆，德魯伊釋曰強敵將至。王遣勇士斯倫格窺敵，神族遣布雷斯相迎。二勇士緩行相向，各持盾、至語距而止，插盾於地、隔盾沿相望。第一發現乃同語：斯倫格聞布雷斯操愛爾蘭語而稍安。第二發現乃互敬其兵器：神族畏其厚重鈍邊之Craisech矛（可破盾碎骨，其創不愈），巴格斯人畏其尖銳細矛。遂互換長矛，使兩軍各見敵之慣技。布雷斯獻議：半島和平相讓，否則一戰。斯倫格勸王分土；伊奧凱拒之：『予其半，彼將取其全。』三女神巴德布、瑪哈、摩里古以咒布霧、黑雲、火雨血雨三日，直至巴格斯三德魯伊破其咒。戰如合法決鬥：神族擲球手先出而盡歿；每日一戰，兩軍人數相等，醫者夜以草藥浴傷者使明日復戰；第四日神族得勢，伊奧凱渴而出戰場就飲，為追兵及於特拉伊·埃奧泰爾海灘，死焉，冢上壘巨石。十一營餘三百人，斯倫格為首；努阿達許和，擇省而居——得康諾特。其子孫後出弗迪亞（於渡口力拒庫丘林）與埃爾克（終致庫丘林之死）：敗者不滅，而留待英雄時代。

functions: Charter of conquest-by-law: the battle is contracted (equal numbers, rest days) as a lawful duel, modeling诉讼 of sovereignty transfer
Etiology of Connacht's population: Fir Bolg survival as ancestors of later Ulster-Cycle heroes
Dual-inheritance epic logic: the conquered remain as the epic's future enemies and friends
Druid weather-magic narrative: battle begins in the heavens before it begins on the field

variants.summary: A separate place-legend places a battle of the Tuatha and Firbolgs 'west of Cong', giving the fight a fixed topography and more archaic verses on Sreng's spear.

variants.summary: In the pseudo-history the Firbolgs' defeat is dated and Nuada's reign-length reckoned; the humanized genealogies make Sreng the eponym of Fir Bolg families of the west.

title.en: Nuada Loses the Kingship and Gains a Silver Hand
title.zh: 努阿達失位得銀手

region.en: Teamhair (Hill of Tara), Co. Meath, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭米斯郡塔拉王丘

period: Recorded in Cath Maige Tuired traditions, 11th c.; Gregory retelling 1904

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book One, Chapter II, eBook #14465

summary.en: Nuada, wounded by Sreng in the First Battle, is deposed because a law of the Tuatha Dé forbids any king not perfect in shape; Diancecht the physician makes him a silver arm with movement in every finger, and when the king is healed Nuada is restored — but his son Miach, who restores the arm of flesh, is killed by his own father's thrown sword.
summary.zh: 努阿達於首戰為斯倫格所傷失臂，因神族之法『形不全者不得為王』而被廢；醫神迪安徹特製銀臂、指指能動；及其復原，努阿達復位——然其子米亞克以真臂復接者，竟為其父擲劍所殺。

sensitivity.note: The perfect-body kingship law (no blemished king) is a documented legal-theological motif of Irish kingship tales; translated from public-domain print.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: Nuada had won the battle but lost his own arm, struck off by Sreng; and by that loss troubles came on his people, for it was a law with the Tuatha Dé Danann that no man that was not perfect in shape should be king. So he was put out of the kingship, and Bres, the most beautiful of their young men, was chosen in his place. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book One ch. 2; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 濃縮意譯：努阿達贏得了戰鬥，卻失去了自己的一條手臂，被斯倫砍斷；由於這一殘缺，災禍降臨於他的族人，因為達努神族有一條律法：凡形體不完整者不得為王。於是他被廢去王位，而他們年輕人中長得最美的布雷斯被選為他的繼任者。非逐字引文。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: Diancecht the healer made an arm of silver for Nuada, with movement in every finger, and from that he was called Nuada Argat-lámh, of the Silver Hand. But Miach, son of Diancecht, took the king's own hand that had been struck off, set it in its place saying 'Joint to joint, and sinew to sinew,' and for three days and three nights healed it — the first day against his side, the second against his breast, the third with blackened bulrushes — till the king was whole. Diancecht, vexed that his son did a better cure than himself, threw his sword at Miach's head: the first blow cut flesh and was healed, the second reached bone and was healed, the third and fourth cut out the brain, and Miach died. Three hundred and sixty-five herbs grew from his grave; his sister Airmed laid them out on her cloak by their virtue, but Diancecht mixed them up, so that no one knows all their powers to this day. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book One ch. 2; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：醫者迪安凱特為努阿達造了一隻銀臂，每一根手指皆能活動，因此他被稱為「銀手」努阿達·阿爾加特-拉夫。然而迪安凱特之子米亞赫取來國王被砍下的那隻手，將其安回原處，說道「骨節接骨節，筋腱接筋腱」，並以三日三夜將其治癒——第一日貼於身側，第二日貼於胸前，第三日以燒黑的燈心草敷治——直至國王痊癒。迪安凱特見兒子所行醫術勝過自己，心生惱怒，將劍擲向米亞赫的頭：第一擊割破皮肉而癒，第二擊觸及骨頭而癒，第三擊與第四擊則剖出腦髓，米亞赫遂死。三百六十五種藥草自其墳上長出；其妹艾爾梅德依各草藥之藥性將其鋪陳於自己的斗篷上，但迪安凱特將它們混雜一處，以致至今無人知曉它們全部的藥力。非逐字照錄。

canonical_translation: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men, London 1904 (public domain); underlying: Cath Maige Tuired (Stokes, Irische Texte 1891)

narrative.en:
Nuada's wound is the hinge on which the whole coming of Lugh turns: from a lost arm flow a deposition, a bad reign, a satire, and eventually the war for Ireland itself.

In the First Battle Sreng's Craisech had sheared off the god-king's arm. Victory was not enough to keep him his throne, for it was a law with the Tuatha Dé Danann that no man who was not perfect in shape should be king — bodily integrity and sovereignty were one thing. The assembly chose Bres in his place, the most beautiful of their young men, so comely that any beautiful thing — a plain, a dun, ale, a flame, a woman, a horse — would be praised as 'beautiful as Bres'. Whose son he was only his mother knew.

While Bres reigned badly, Diancecht the physician made his king a new arm of silver, with movement in every finger, and Nuada was called Argat-lámh, of the Silver Hand, for ever after. The tale then records the strangest of its cures: Miach, the physician's own son and a better healer than his father, met a young man at Teamhair who had lost an eye and asked for another; Miach set in its place the eye of a cat in the man's lap — which worked, after a fashion, waking when the man wanted to sleep and sleeping when he wanted to watch an army. Not satisfied with the silver prosthesis, Miach took Nuada's severed hand and set it on the stump saying 'joint to joint, and sinew to sinew': three days and three nights he worked, the first day holding the hand against the king's side, the second against his breast until it was covered with skin, the third laying on blackened bulrushes, and the king was healed.

Then comes the tale's dark final turn. Diancecht, vexed that his son did a better cure than himself, threw his sword at Miach's head. The first blow cut the flesh, and the lad healed it with his own skill; the second reached the bone and was cured; the third and fourth cut out the brain, which no physician could cure, and Miach died. Herbs sprang from his grave, three hundred and sixty-five of them, one for every joint and sinew; his sister Airmed spread them on her cloak and sorted them by their virtues — and Diancecht, seeing it, came and mixed them together, so that no one knows all their right powers to this day: an aition for why healing is a craft of search, not of certainty.

With the king whole in body, the Tuatha gathered at Teamhair and bade Bres give up the kingship he had held long enough, though not willingly. Nuada was restored. Bres, in his vexation, went to his mother Eri to learn his race — and learned that his father was Elatha, king of the Fomor, who had come over a level sea in a silver vessel with gold-sewn clothes and five rings of gold about his neck. From that discovery comes the alliance that brings Balor and the great invasion. The proverb the tale teaches is Bres's own father's: their good-will would be better than their curses — prosperity of the people over majesty of the king.
narrative.zh: 努阿達之失臂，乃魯格降世之樞紐：一臂之失，牽出廢立、暴政、諷刺詩，乃至為愛爾蘭而戰。首戰中斯倫格之Craisech矛斷神王之臂；然勝利不足以保其位，因神族之法：形不全者不得為王——身體完整與主權合而為一。眾遂立布雷斯，其美冠絕一時，凡美物皆以『美如布雷斯』譽之。暴政期間，醫神迪安徹特為王製銀臂，指指能動，努阿達自此稱『銀手』。故事續記奇療：其子米亞克醫術勝父，為獨眼青年置貓目；又不滿銀臂之假，取王斷臂接於殘端，誦曰『節對節、筋對筋』，三日三夜之功——首日貼脅、次日貼胸至膚生、三日敷火燻之黑藺草——王乃復原。而後故事轉暗：迪安徹特嫉子勝己，擲劍擊其首；一擊破膚、子自愈之，二擊及骨、亦愈之，三四擊碎腦，無醫可救，米亞克遂死。墓上生三百六十五種草藥，其妹艾爾梅德以衣攤列、按效分類；迪安徹特見而攪亂之，故世人不盡知諸藥之性——此為『療術乃搜尋之藝而非確然之術』之釋義。王既體全，眾會於塔拉，令布雷斯讓位（彼不甚願），努阿達復位。布雷斯怨憤，往問母親世系——得知其父乃弗摩爾王埃拉塔：乘銀舟、衣金線服、頸戴五金環、渡如鏡之海而來者。由此發現生出引巴羅大軍入侵之盟。故事之諺語即其父之言：『民之善願勝於民之詛咒』——民之繁榮重於王之威嚴。

functions: Legal theology of kingship: bodily wholeness as condition of sovereignty (blemished king = unfit king)
Etiology of herbal medicine's limits: Diancecht's mixing of Airmed's sorted herbs
Professional jealousy taboo: the healer who heals better than his teacher must die
Genealogical hinge: connects the deposition of Nuada to Bres's Fomorian kinship and the coming war

title.en: The Reign of Bres and the First Satire of Ireland
title.zh: 布雷斯之治與愛爾蘭首篇諷刺詩

region.en: Teamhair (Hill of Tara), Co. Meath, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭米斯郡塔拉王丘

period: Recorded in Cath Maige Tuired and Lebor Gabála traditions, 11th-12th c.; Gregory retelling 1904

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book One, Chapter II, eBook #14465

summary.en: Bres the beautiful king taxes his own gods into servitude — Ogma gathering firewood, the Dagda digging raths and fed on by a blind parasite — until the poet Corpre, lodged in a dark cell and given three dry cakes, pronounces against him the first satire ever made in Ireland, and from that day there is no good luck with Bres.
summary.zh: 美王布雷斯橫徵暴斂，使其族之神為僕——歐格瑪拾薪、達格達掘塹且遭盲蟲剝食——直至詩人科爾普雷被安置暗室、僅得三塊乾餅，遂對王吟出愛爾蘭首篇諷刺詩；自此布雷斯厄運纏身。

sensitivity.note: The satire (áer) as an instrument that destroys a king is a documented feature of Irish kingship ideology; retold from public-domain print.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: In spite of Bres being so beautiful, his reign brought no good luck to his people, for the Fomor put tribute on them — a third of their corn, a third of their milk, a third of their children — so that there was not smoke rising from a roof in Ireland that was not under tribute. Bres himself taxed every house for the milk of hornless dun cows; Nechtan, by the druid Findgoll's advice, singed all the cows of Ireland brown in a fire of fern to deceive him, and another time they made three hundred wooden cows with pails of bog-stuff, which Bres drank thinking it milk. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book One ch. 2; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：儘管布雷斯容貌俊美，他的統治卻未為其子民帶來好運，因為弗摩爾人向他們課徵貢賦——三分之一的穀物、三分之一的乳汁、三分之一的孩子——以致愛爾蘭境內沒有一處屋頂升起的炊煙不背負著貢賦。布雷斯本人更向每一戶人家課徵無角褐色母牛的乳汁；內赫坦聽從德魯伊芬德戈爾的建議，以蕨草之火將愛爾蘭所有的母牛燒成褐色，以欺瞞於他；另有一次，他們製作了三百頭木牛，配上盛滿沼澤之物的桶，布雷斯飲之，以為是乳汁。非逐字照錄。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: Ogma the shining poet was set to carry firing to the palace, so weak with hunger that the sea swept away two-thirds of his bundle daily; the Dagda was put to dig raths, where the blind man Cridenbel exacted the three best bits of his food every night until Angus's three pieces of gold, hidden in the bits, killed the parasite. Then the poet Corpre, son of Etain, came looking for hospitality and was put in a little dark narrow house without fire, furniture or bed, and given three small dry cakes on a little dish. Going across the green in the morning he said: 'Without food ready on a dish; without milk enough for a calf to grow on; without shelter; without light in the darkness of night; without enough to pay a story-teller — may that be the prosperity of Bres.' And from that day there was no good luck with Bres; and that was the first satire ever made in Ireland. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book One ch. 2; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：光輝的詩人奧格瑪被派去為宮殿搬運柴薪，他因飢餓而虛弱不堪，以致海水每日沖走他柴捆的三分之二；達格達被派去挖掘土壘，盲人克里登貝爾每夜索取他食物中最好的三塊，直到安格斯藏於那幾塊食物中的三枚金片殺死了這名寄生者。其後，詩人科爾普雷——埃坦之子——前來尋求款待，卻被安置在一間狹小、陰暗、狹窄、既無爐火、又無家具、亦無床鋪的屋中，並在一隻小碟上得到三塊又小又乾的餅。翌日清晨他走過草地時說道：「碟上無備妥之食；無足供牛犢成長之乳；無庇身之所；黑夜中無光；無足以酬報說書人之物——願此即為布雷斯之昌盛。」自那日起，布雷斯便再無好運；而那便是愛爾蘭有史以來所作的第一首諷刺詩。非逐字照錄。

canonical_translation: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men, London 1904 (public domain); underlying: Cath Maige Tuired, ed. Stokes 1891

narrative.en:
Bres's reign is the mythic charter of Irish satire — the tale that tells why a poet's word can put a king down.

The trouble began with taxes. The Fomor, dwelling beyond the sea or below it westward, dreadful in aspect, maimed, under a giant and his mother, put tribute on Ireland: a third of its corn, a third of its milk, a third of its children — so that there was not smoke rising from a roof in Ireland that was not under tribute to them. And Bres made no stand against them. He taxed the gods themselves, demanding of every house the milk of hornless dun cows and cows of a single color in quantities enough for a hundred men; the Ireland of the tale cheats him twice — once when Nechtan, on the druid Findgoll's advice, singed every cow in the land brown in a fire of fern and rubbed them with flaxseed ash, and once when three hundred wooden cows were milked before him, their black bog-stuff drunk by the king himself, who was not the better of it for a long time.

The inner court was no better. In Bres's house the knives of the chiefs were never greased, no smell of ale was on their breaths, and there was no call for poets, singers, harpers, pipers, horn-blowers, jugglers or fools — hospitality itself had been abolished. Ogma the shining poet was ordered to bring fuel for the whole army every day from the islands of Mod, so weakened by hunger that the sea carried off two-thirds of each day's bundle. The Dagda was set to dig raths, and there the blind man Cridenbel with the sharp tongue fastened on him, exacting 'the three best bits' of the Dagda's share — bits the size of a good pig — until the Dagda's son Angus Og armed him with three pieces of gold to hide in the food, which turned inside Cridenbel and killed him, a death the king first misread as poisoning until the body was cut open and the gold found.

Wages were the Dagda's heifer — black and black-maned, chosen on Angus's advice, and secretly destined to matter at the war's end. Then came the poem. Corpre, son of Etain, poet of the Tuatha Dé, sought the king's house and was lodged in a little dark narrow house without fire, furniture or bed, and feasted with three small dry cakes on a little dish. Crossing the green in the morning he gave his judgment in four bitter lines: without food ready on a dish; without milk enough for a calf to grow on; without shelter; without light in the darkness of night; without enough to pay a story-teller — 'may that be the prosperity of Bres.' From that day there was no good luck with Bres, and he went down for ever after: for that was the first satire ever made in Ireland. The deposed king would learn his race from his mother Eri — a Fomorian father, Elatha, whose ring fitted no finger but Bres's own — and ride to his own people to buy back a throne with an army. But the poem had already judged the reign: sovereignty is held not by force but by feeding.
narrative.zh: 布雷斯之治乃愛爾蘭諷刺詩（áer）之神話憲章——即解釋詩人一言何以能廢君之故事。禍起於稅：弗摩爾人居海外或海西之下，形貌可怖、殘缺不全，為巨魔及其母所率，向愛爾蘭徵稅——三分之一穀、三分之一乳、三分之一孩童——致使愛爾蘭無一縷炊煙不在其貢賦之下，而布雷斯不予抵抗。彼反苛徵神族：責每戶獻無角棕牛之乳、純色牛之乳至足百人之量；愛爾蘭兩番欺之——內克坦奉德魯伊芬戈爾之策，以蕨火燻烤全境牛群使成棕色，以亞麻灰塗之；又以三百木牛、黑沼之泥充乳，王親嘗之，久而不愈。宮內亦劣：群臣之刀永不上油，無酒氣於鼻，詩人、歌者、豎琴師、笛手、號手、弄人皆無所召——款待之道廢矣。光耀詩人歐格瑪被役使自莫德群島為全軍日運柴薪，飢弱至海每日捲去其束薪三分之二。達格達被遣掘塹築堡，盲者克里登貝爾利舌索其『三塊上品』，其量如豚；安古斯·歐格以三金塊藏食中予之，金入腹而蟲死，王初疑為毒藥，剖屍見金乃明。其傭值為一黑鬃小母牛——依安古斯之言擇之，暗中註定於戰尾見功。繼而詩篇至：科爾普雷（艾塔恩之子、神族之詩人）求宿，被置暗狹之室，無火無床無几，僅以三塊乾餅為饗。晨起過草場，以四行苦句下其判：『盤中無食；無乳以哺犢；無庇護；黑夜無光；無以酬講古者——願此為布雷斯之繁榮。』自是布雷斯厄運相隨、永不復振：此即愛爾蘭首篇諷刺詩。廢王將自其母埃里得知世系——弗摩爾父埃拉塔，其戒指惟合布雷斯之指——遂返己族欲以軍隊贖回王位。然詩已斷其治：主權之持，不在力而在饗。

functions: Charter of the poet's political power: satire (áer) as the institution that deposes a bad king
Charter of hospitality law: a king who does not feed forfeits luck — prosperity tied to feasting
Etiology of resistance-craft: trickery against illegitimate taxation (singed cows, wooden cows)
Genealogical hinge: explains Bres's Fomorian half and the alliance that brings the great war

variants.summary: Corpre's quatrain is given in Middle Irish verse in the battle-tale, framed as a judgment that Bres must yield the kingship; the wooden cows episode appears there too.

variants.summary: Dates Bres's reign (seven years in some lists) and notes the tribute to the Fomor as the cause of the Second Battle, integrating the scene into the invasion chronicle.

title.en: The Birth of Lugh in Balor's Tower of Glass
title.zh: 魯格誕生於巴羅之玻璃塔

region.en: Tory Island (Torach), Co. Donegal, Ireland — Tower of Glass (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭多尼戈爾郡托里島（象徵定位：玻璃之塔）

period: Recorded in medieval Irish tradition (Book of the Dun Cow and later); Gregory retelling 1904

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book Two, Chapter I, eBook #14465

summary.en: A druid foretells that Balor of the Evil Eye will die by his own grandson; Balor shuts his daughter Ethlinn in a tower with twelve women and never lets her hear a man's name — until the Druid woman Birog disguises Cian in woman's clothes, carries him across the sea in a blast of wind, and Ethlinn bears a son who is saved from the drowning-cloth by the same enchantress.
summary.zh: 德魯伊預言巴羅將死於己孫之手；巴羅遂閉女艾斯琳於玻璃塔中，以十二女侍之，永不令其聞男子之名——直至女德魯伊比羅格將西安扮女裝、乘風渡海入塔；艾斯琳產子，溺衣之針落而子獲救。

sensitivity.note: Pin: Tory Island (Toraigh) is the traditional seat of Balor in Irish tradition and in living Tory folklore; the 'Tower of Glass' itself is otherworldly and the pin is symbolic.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: A druid foretold that it was by his own grandson Balor would get his death; he had but one child, a daughter named Ethlinn, and he shut her up in the tower on the island of glass, with twelve women to guard her, and bade them never let her see a man or hear the name of a man. She grew beautiful, and sometimes she would see men passing in currachs, and sometimes a man in her dreams; but the women gave her no answer when she spoke of it. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Two ch. 1; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：一名德魯伊預言，巴羅爾將死於自己的外孫之手；他只有一個孩子，是個名為埃絲琳的女兒，他將她關在玻璃島上的塔中，命十二名女子看守她，並囑咐她們絕不可讓她見到男人，或聽到男人的名字。她越長越美，有時會看見乘著皮舟經過的男人，有時會在夢中見到一個男人；但當她談及此事時，那些女子卻不給她任何回答。非逐字照錄。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: Cian of the Tuatha Dé, robbed by Balor of his wonder-cow the Glas Gaibhnenn, was told by a druid that while Balor lived no one could come within reach of his Evil Eye; so the woman-druid Birog of the Mountain dressed Cian in woman's clothes and carried him across the sea in a blast of wind to the tower, passing them in to Ethlinn as a high queen she had saved. Birog's spells put the women to sleep, and when Ethlinn saw Cian she said that was the face she had seen in her dreams. When her time came Balor bade his people throw the child into the sea-current in a cloth fastened with a pin; the pin dropped, the child slipped into the water, and was thought drowned — but Birog brought him away and gave him to Taillte, daughter of the King of the Great Plain, to foster. Thus Lugh was born and reared. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Two ch. 1; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：達努神族的基安，其神牛「白牛格拉斯」被巴羅爾奪去，一名德魯伊告訴他，只要巴羅爾還活著，便無人能接近其邪眼所及之處；於是山中的女德魯伊比羅格將基安裝扮成女子，乘一陣狂風將他渡海送至塔前，將他們當作她所救的一位高貴女王引見給埃絲琳。比羅格的咒語使那些女子沉睡，當埃絲琳見到基安時，她說那正是她在夢中所見的面容。臨產之時，巴羅爾命其屬下將嬰兒裹於以別針扣緊的布中，投入海流；別針脫落，嬰兒滑入水中，眾人以為他已溺斃——但比羅格將他帶走，交給大平原之王的女兒泰爾蒂撫養。盧赫便如此誕生並被養育成人。非逐字照錄。

canonical_translation: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men, London 1904 (public domain); underlying: Oidheadh Chlainne Tuireann and related texts (Whitley Stokes editions, public domain)

narrative.en:
Lugh's birth is the Irish Zeus-and-Cronus: a prophecy of filicide answered with a tower, a disguise, and a pin that drops at the right moment.

Balor of the Strong Blows — some said of the Evil Eye — lived on the island of the Tower of Glass, dangerous for ships, which the Fomor plundered as they passed. Some remembered the sons of Nemed coming near it in the old time and attacking what looked like men on a glass tower with druid spells; the tower vanished under their assault, but a great wave rose and all their ships went down. The tower stood again as before, and Balor lived in it. His one deadly eye had been ruined innocently: passing a house where his father's druids were making spells of death, he had looked in at the open window, and the smoke of the poisonous brew went into his eye. Ever after he kept it closed, and when he wanted an enemy dead his men lifted the lid with a ring of ivory.

Then a druid foretold that by his own grandson he would get his death. Balor had one child, Ethlinn; he shut her in the tower and set twelve women over her, charged never to let her see a man or hear a man's name. She grew up beautiful, watching currachs pass below and dreaming of faces her guards would not name.

Meanwhile on the mainland Cian, brother of the smith Goibniu, kept the Glas Gaibhnenn, the cow whose milk never failed, coveted by everyone who heard of her. When Balor stole her — slipping the halter from Cian's brother's hand while disguised as a little red-haired boy who told a poisoned tale of brothers cheating — a druid told Cian the truth: while Balor lived, the cow would never be recovered, for none could come within reach of that eye. So Cian went to Birog of the Mountain. She dressed him in woman's clothes and carried him over the sea on a blast of wind, and at the tower called for shelter for 'a high queen she had saved from hardship'; the women of the tower could not refuse a woman of the Tuatha Dé. Birog's enchantments put them all to sleep, and Ethlinn, seeing Cian, said at once that was the face she had seen in her dreams. She gave him her love; he was carried away again on a wind.

When her time came, Balor had the child bound in a cloth with a pin and thrown into the sea-current. On the way across an arm of the sea the pin dropped; the child slipped from the cloth, and those who carried him thought him drowned. Birog of the Mountain had him, and gave him to Cian, who fostered him on Taillte, daughter of the King of the Great Plain. Thus Lugh was born and reared — the grandson marked for his grandfather's death, kept by an enchantress, named for the mastery of every art that would later open the gates of Teamhair.
narrative.zh: 魯格之誕生即愛爾蘭之宙斯與克羅諾斯：弒親預言，以塔、偽裝與適時落下之一針回應之。強擊者巴羅——或稱邪眼巴羅——居海上玻璃之塔，航船過者皆遭弗摩爾劫掠。傳說內梅德之子昔年曾近此塔，見塔上似人者，以德魯伊咒擊之；塔雖隱沒，巨浪捲起，其船盡沒。塔復如故，巴羅居焉。其致命之眼得之無辜：一日過其父德魯伊施死亡咒法之屋，自開窗窺視，毒咒之煙入其目。此後常閉其瞼；欲殺敵時，左右以象牙環啟之。德魯伊預言：其死必於己孫之手。巴羅唯一女艾斯琳；閉之於塔，以十二女侍之，永不令見男子、聞男子之名。女漸長而美，觀舟楫過於塔下，夢中有面而侍女不答。陸上，鍛冶神戈伊布尼烏之弟西安畜神牛格拉斯·蓋布嫩，其乳不竭，聞者皆覬覦。巴羅扮紅髮小童，以兄弟相欺之毒言騙取牛韁而奪牛；德魯伊告西安：巴羅在世一日，牛不可復，蓋無人能近邪眼之及。西安遂求山間女德魯伊比羅格。比羅格令西安著女裝、乘風渡海，至塔前以『救護之貴婦』求宿；塔中諸女不敢拒神族之女。比羅格咒眾皆眠，艾斯琳見西安即曰：此即夢中之面。遂以身相許；西安復乘風而去。產期既至，巴羅命以布裹嬰、以針別之，投諸海流。渡一海臂之際，針落，嬰滑出，眾以為溺。比羅格取之，交西安，寄養於大平原王之女泰爾特。魯格遂生而育——註定殺祖父之孫，由術士所護，日後以百藝之師啟塔拉之門。

functions: Prophecy-and-avoidance plot type: the closed tower as futile defense against a fate-speech
Charter of fosterage law: the child is saved through kin network and foster-mother Taillte (whose fair gives Taillten its name)
Etiology of the Evil Eye: Balor's eye as poison-smoke wound — technology of the gaze
Etiology of Tory Island folklore: Balor's seat located on the living island of Toraigh

variants.name: The childhood of Lugh (Compert)+ Balor's eye episode
variants.text_tradition: Medieval Irish prose (LU and later MSS)
variants.summary: In some versions Balor's eye is destroyed in battle by Lugh's sling-stone from the tathlum; the eye-piercing of the window-spells is one of several explanations of the Evil Eye's origin.

variants.name: Lugh's three foster-mothers
variants.text_tradition: Folk and literary tradition of Taillte
variants.summary: Lugh is fostered by Taillte of the Great Plain, and the assembly of Taillten (Tailtiu) holds funeral games for her — the Irish olympics' mythic origin.

title.en: Lugh at the Door of Teamhair: Master of All Arts
title.zh: 魯格於塔拉門前：百藝之師

region.en: Teamhair (Hill of Tara), Co. Meath, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭米斯郡塔拉王丘

period: Recorded in medieval Irish prose (Samhain episode in the tale of Mag Tuired); Gregory retelling 1904

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book Two, Chapter I, eBook #14465

summary.en: At the door of Nuada's feast at Tara the doorkeepers challenge every skill — carpenter, smith, champion, harper, poet, physician, cupbearer, bronzeworker — and Lugh answers each with the name of the man who has it already, until he asks whether the king has one man who can do all these things; the door is opened for the Ildánach, and he hurls Ogma's flagstone back, plays sleep out of the court, and wins the throne for thirteen days.
summary.zh: 努阿達設宴塔拉，門吏逐一詰其技——木匠、鐵匠、武士、豎琴師、詩人、醫師、司酒、銅匠——魯格一一以其已有之匠名對之；直至問王有無一人兼擅百藝。門為『伊爾丹納克』（百藝之師）而開；彼擲回歐格瑪之巨石、以曲終寢滿庭、十三日得踐王座。

sensitivity.note: The polyvalence scene is the classic charter of the samildánach ('many-skilled') ideal; note that the existing base record lugh-balor overlaps this episode at the gate.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: Nuada held a great feast at Teamhair, and two door-keepers were set there, for no one without an art came into Teamhair. A young man at the door said 'I am Lugh, son of Cian of the Tuatha Dé and of Ethlinn daughter of Balor.' Asked what he was skilled in, he answered 'I am a carpenter'; they had a carpenter. 'I am a smith'; they had a smith. 'I am a champion'; they had Ogma. 'I am a harper'; they had one. 'I am a poet and a teller of tales'; they had one. 'I am a magician, a physician, a cup-bearer, a worker in brass' — each was already in the king's house. Then Lugh said: 'Go and ask the king if he has any one man that can do all these things; and if he has, I will not ask to come into Teamhair.' Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Two ch. 1; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：努阿達在塔拉舉行了一場盛大的宴會，並在該處設了兩名守門人，因為凡無技藝者皆不得進入塔拉。門前一名年輕人說道：「我是盧赫，達努神族基安之子，巴羅爾之女埃絲琳所生。」當被問及有何技藝時，他答道：「我是木匠」；他們已有木匠。「我是鐵匠」；他們已有鐵匠。「我是勇士」；他們已有奧格瑪。「我是豎琴師」；他們已有一位。「我是詩人，也是說書人」；他們已有一位。「我是魔法師、醫師、司酒者、銅匠」——每一項技藝在王宮中皆已有人。於是盧赫說道：「去問國王，他是否有一人能兼做所有這些事；若有，我便不求進入塔拉。」非逐字照錄。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: The door-keeper told the king the young man's name should be the Ildánach, the Master of all Arts. Nuada bade them try him with the chess-boards; Lugh won every game. The king said, 'Let him in, for the like of him never came into Teamhair before.' Inside, Ogma hurled a flagstone that four times twenty yoke of oxen could hardly move, out through the house as a challenge; Lugh hurled it back into the middle of the king's house. He played the harp till the court laughed, wept, and slept — and when Nuada saw all that Lugh could do he thought that by his help the country might be freed of the Fomor's tyranny, so he came down from his throne and set Lugh on it for thirteen days, that all might hear his advice. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Two ch. 1; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：守門人告訴國王，這年輕人的名字應是伊爾達納赫（Ildánach），即「眾藝之師」。努阿達命人以棋盤試他；盧格每局皆勝。國王說：「讓他進來吧，因為像他這樣的人，從未到過塔拉（Teamhair）。」入內之後，奧格瑪（Ogma）將一塊連四倍二十對牛都幾乎拖不動的鋪石擲出屋外，作為挑戰；盧格又將它擲回國王屋子的中央。他彈奏豎琴，直至滿朝時而歡笑、時而哭泣、時而入睡——努阿達見盧格所能做的一切，便想藉他的幫助，國家或可擺脫弗摩爾人（Fomor）的暴政，於是走下王座，讓盧格坐上十三日，好讓眾人皆得聽聞他的建言。非逐字照錄。

canonical_translation: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men, London 1904 (public domain); underlying: Cath Maige Tuired, ed. Stokes 1891

narrative.en:
Lugh's entrance is an audition scene: the god arrives at the door of the high court and answers the gatekeeper's law — no one without an art comes into Teamhair — by out-answering it.

Nuada, restored to the kingship, held a great feast at Teamhair. Two door-keepers, Gamal son of Figal and Camel son of Riagall, stood at the gate. A young man came and bade them bring him in to the king. 'Who are you yourself?' 'I am Lugh, son of Cian of the Tuatha Dé Danann and of Ethlinn, daughter of Balor, king of the Fomor,' he said, 'foster-son of Taillte daughter of the King of the Great Plain.' 'What are you skilled in? No one without an art comes into Teamhair.'

So began the litany. 'Question me: I am a carpenter.' 'We have a carpenter, Luchtar son of Luachaid.' 'Then I am a smith.' 'We have a smith, Colum Cuaillemech of the Three New Ways.' 'I am a champion.' 'We have a champion, Ogma, brother of the king.' 'I am a harper.' 'We have a harper, Abhean son of Bicelmos.' 'I am a poet and a teller of tales.' 'We have a teller of tales, Ere son of Ethaman.' 'I am a magician.' 'We have plenty of people of power.' 'A physician.' 'We have Diancecht.' 'A cup-bearer.' 'We have nine.' 'A worker in brass.' 'We have Credne Cerd.' Each office in the pagan court was already filled — the tale inventories the whole divine civil service in one breath.

Then Lugh played his one card: 'Go and ask the king if he has any one man that can do all these things, and if he has, I will not ask to come into Teamhair.' The door-keeper brought the word in and named him: his name should be the Ildánach, the Master of all Arts. Nuada bade them try the chess-boards; every game, Lugh won. 'Let him in, for the like of him never came into Teamhair before.'

Inside, the proving continued. Ogma lifted the great flagstone that four times twenty yoke of oxen could barely move and hurled it out through the house as a challenge; Lugh hurled it back so it lay in the middle of the king's house. He took the harp and played the three strains — laughter, tears, sleep — until the court laughed, wept, and slept. Nuada, seeing that by this man's help the country might be freed from the taxes and tyranny of the Fomor, came down from his own throne and set Lugh on it for thirteen days, so that all might listen to his advice. The god of many gifts had arrived not as a warrior but as a competence — and in the war to come every specialist in the Tuatha's camp would work under his direction, exactly as the gatehouse scene promised.
narrative.zh: 魯格之入場為一場試演：神臨高廷之門，以超答之姿回應門吏之法——無藝者不得入塔拉。努阿達復位，設大宴於塔拉；門吏戈馬爾（菲加爾之子）與卡梅爾（里亞加爾之子）守門。一青年求見王：『我乃魯格，神族西安與弗摩爾王之女艾斯琳之子，大平原王之女泰爾特之養子。』問其技：『問我吧，我是木匠。』『已有木匠盧克塔爾。』『我是鐵匠。』『已有鐵匠三新道之科隆。』『我是武士。』『已有王弟歐格瑪。』『我是豎琴師。』『已有阿貝安。』『我是詩人兼講古者。』『已有埃雷。』『我是術士。』『多有其人。』『醫師。』『已有迪安徹特。』『司酒。』『已有九人。』『銅匠。』『已有克雷德·克爾德。』異教廷中百官已滿——故事一口氣盤點神族之全套文官制度。魯格遂出其絕招：『請問王：座中可有一人兼擅百藝？若有，吾不求入塔拉。』門吏入告，命名曰『伊爾丹納克』（百藝之師）。努阿達令試棋局；魯格局局皆勝。『放他進來，塔拉前所未有此人。』入門之後考驗繼續：歐格瑪舉四十八頭牛方堪移動之巨石擲出殿外為戰書；魯格擲回使其正落王殿之中。魯格執琴奏三曲——笑、哭、眠——至滿庭先笑後泣而後入睡。努阿達見此，思此人可助解弗摩爾苛政，遂自王座下而立魯格於其位十三日，使眾人聆其謀。多藝之神以「勝任」而非「勇武」入場——而後之戰中，神族營中百工皆在其調度之下，正如門前之景所許。

functions: Charter of the samildánach ideal: the hero's value measured in complete competence across every craft
Inventory of the pagan divine court: each named specialist is an institutional charter for craft guilds
Sequence of the three harp strains: laughter, tears, sleep as the canonical order of music's powers
Legitimation of Lugh's war-command: the thirteen days on the throne as apprenticeship in sovereignty
