title.en: The Sons of Tuireann and the Finest Fine Ever Levied
title.zh: 圖雷恩諸子與最重之罰金

region.en: Beinn Édair (Howth), Co. Dublin, Ireland (symbolic pin for the voyage)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭都柏林郡本·埃代爾山（象徵定位：遠航）

period: Recorded as Oidheadh Chlainne Tuireann, medieval Irish prose (Book of the Dun Cow and later); Gregory retelling 1904

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book Two, Chapter II, eBook #14465

summary.en: The three sons of Tuireann kill Lugh's father Cian in his shape of a pig; Lugh hears it from the earth itself, and levies on them the famous fine of eight wonders — apples of the east, the healing pigskin of Greece, the spear of Persia, the sea-horses and chariot, the self-renewing pigs, the hound, the cooking-spit and three shouts on a forbidden hill — which they gather by trick, war and wound, dying on the last two items.
summary.zh: 圖雷恩三子殺魯格之父西安（時為豬形）；魯格自大地之口得知，遂課其『八件異寶』之罰——東方之蘋果、希臘愈傷豬皮、波斯之矛、海上駿馬與戰車、復生之豬、神獵犬、烹杼與禁丘三聲呼——三子以詭計、戰爭與創傷逐件得之，終死於末二項。

sensitivity.note: The eric-fine (éraic) narrative is a legal-theological myth of blood-price; symbol pin at Beinn Édair/Howth, the brothers' last view of Ireland.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: Cian, traveling north alone, saw the three sons of Tuireann before him — his enemies — and struck himself with a druid rod into the shape of a pig of the herd; Brian saw through the enchantment, struck his brothers into hounds, and the pig was speared at the wood's edge. 'I was a man indeed — I am Cian, son of Cainte; give me your protection.' 'If the life came back seven times to you, I would take it from you every time.' Cian won one request — to die in his own shape, 'for then the blood-fine will be heavier than ever was paid' — and they pelted him with stones till only a broken heap was left; the earth cast up their burial six times, and kept it on the seventh. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Two ch. 2; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：基安（Cian）獨自北行，見圖伊林（Tuireann）三子在前——他的仇敵——便以德魯伊杖擊自身，化為群豬中的一頭豬；布萊恩（Brian）看破這法術，將兩兄弟擊成獵犬，那豬遂在林子邊緣被矛刺中。「我本是人——我乃坎泰之子基安；請賜我庇護。」「縱使你的性命七次回到你身上，我也每次都要取走它。」基安求得一個請求——以自身原形死去，「因為如此一來，血債賠償將比以往所付的更重」——他們便以石擲他，直至只剩一堆殘骸；大地六次吐出他們的埋葬，第七次才留住。非逐字照錄。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: The earth spoke to Lugh: 'in great danger your father was here, and into the shape of a pig he had to go, but in his own shape they killed him.' At Teamhair Lugh asked the assembly what vengeance each would take on his father's killer; all said day-by-day mutilation — 'and there are making that answer the three men that killed my father.' Brian, thinking to keep the fine small, offered to pay; Lugh named three apples from the Garden in the East of the World, the pigskin of Tuis king of Greece that heals all wounds, the deadly spear of the king of Persia, the sea-running horses and chariot of Siogair, the seven pigs of Easal killed each night and alive next morning, the whelp Fail-Inis before whom all wild beasts fall, a cooking-spit of the women of the Island of Fair-Hair, and three shouts on the hill of Miochaoin. The fine was bound under guarantees; a druid spell of forgetfulness later robbed them of the last two items. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Two ch. 2; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：大地對盧格說：「你父親曾在此身陷大險，被迫化為豬的形貌，但他們卻在他本來的形貌下殺了他。」在塔拉，盧格問眾人各將對殺父仇人施以何等報復；眾人皆說逐日殘害——「而作此答的，正是殺我父親的那三人。」布萊恩想使賠償從輕，便提出願付；盧格開出：世界東方花園的三顆蘋果、希臘國王圖伊斯（Tuis）能治一切傷口的豬皮、波斯國王致命的長矛、西奧蓋爾（Siogair）的航海之馬與戰車、埃薩爾（Easal）那七頭每夜被殺而翌晨復活的豬、法爾-伊尼斯（Fail-Inis）之前所有野獸皆伏的幼犬、美髮島婦女的一根烹飪叉，以及米奧海恩（Miochaoin）山上的三聲呼喊。這筆賠償以保證為約束；後來一道遺忘的德魯伊咒語奪去了他們最後兩樣物品。非逐字照錄。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: As hawks they took the apples under a storm of spears; the king's three daughters, as ospreys, scorched them with lightning, and Brian turned them into swans. As poets they won and stole the pigskin and slew Tuis; they killed the king of Persia with one of the apples to win the spear; as hired soldiers they seized the chariot and horses. Easal, king of the Golden Pillars, gave the pigs freely — the only item won without fighting — and helped win the hound at Ioruaidh. A year quartered on the sea bought the cooking-spit from the laughing women. At the hill of Miochaoin they were speared through the body; Brian raised each dying brother with one hand till the three shouts were given, and Tuireann's plea for the healing skin was refused — 'unless I were sure your death would come on you.' Brian lay down between his brothers, and the three lives went out together. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Two ch. 2; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：他們化為鷹，在矛雨之下取得蘋果；國王的三個女兒化為魚鷹，以閃電灼燒他們，布萊恩將她們變成天鵝。他們化為詩人，贏得並竊取了豬皮，殺死圖伊斯；他們以一顆蘋果殺死波斯國王，贏得長矛；他們化為傭兵，奪得戰車與馬匹。金柱之王埃薩爾（Easal）慷慨贈豬——這是唯一未經爭鬥而得的物品——並助他們在伊奧魯艾德（Ioruaidh）贏得獵犬。在海上駐紮一年又四分之一，向那些歡笑的婦女換得烹飪叉。在米奧海恩山上，他們被矛刺穿身體；布萊恩一手扶起每個垂死的兄弟，直至三聲呼喊發出，而圖伊林求取治傷豬皮之請遭拒——「除非我能確定死亡必降臨於你。」布萊恩躺臥於兄弟之間，三條性命一同消逝。非逐字照錄。

canonical_translation: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men, London 1904 (public domain); underlying: Oidheadh Chlainne Tuireann (Book of the Dun Cow recension, ed. Stokes 1877, public domain)

narrative.en:
The tale of the Sons of Tuireann is the Irish saga of a fine — the eric (éraic) — carried to world's end, and Ireland's most sustained study of how vengeance becomes commerce.

The sons of Tuireann — Brian, Iuchar and Iucharba, the best of Teamhair for skill and name — had hatred between their line and the three sons of Cainte. Meeting Cian alone on the Plain of Muirthemne, they caught him changing shape: he struck himself with a druid rod into a pig of the herd. Brian alone understood the enchantment, turned his brothers into hounds, and speared the pig at the wood's edge. 'It is a bad thing you have done, to make a cast at me when you knew me.' Asked for protection, Brian swore he would take the life seven times over. Cian won a single request: to die in his own shape — 'for if you had killed me in the shape of a pig there would be only the blood-money of a pig on me; but in my own shape there never was, and never will be, any person killed for whose sake a heavier fine will be paid than for myself. And the arms I am killed with, it is they will tell the deed to my son.' They stoned him to a broken heap; the earth refused the burial six times and took it on the seventh.

Lugh heard the tale from the earth itself, and buried his father with an ogham stone. At Teamhair he shook the chain of silence and asked the assembly what vengeance they would take on their father's killer: day-by-day mutilation until the end — 'and there are making that answer the three men that killed my father.' Trickery followed: to keep the fine small, Brian answered 'we will pay the fine as if we did kill him.' Lugh then named the eight items with false modesty — three apples from the Garden in the East of the World, golden as burned gold, tasting of honey, that take away wound-pain and sickness and never lessen; the pigskin of Tuis of Greece that heals all wounds and turns streams to wine; the spear of the king of Persia, its head kept under water lest it burn the place; the horses of Dobar that run on sea as on land and their matchless chariot; the seven pigs of Easal, killed every night, found alive at morning, that keep eaters free of sickness; the whelp Fail-Inis before which all the wild beasts of the world fall down; a cooking-spit from the women of Inis Cenn-fhinne; and three shouts on the hill of Miochaoin — where Miochaoin and his sons were under bonds to allow no shout, for they held Lugh's father's learning, and would never forgive.

The gathering of the fine is an odyssey of disguise: hawks under the spears of the garden-guardians, turned to swans by Brian's rod to escape the lightning of the king's three osprey-daughters; poets who win the pigskin of Tuis with a riddling poem and murder the court; a cast of the apple that kills the king of Persia; hired soldiers who seize the chariot at a fair. Only Easal, king of the Golden Pillars, gives freely — the pigs — and then helps at Ioruaidh for the hound, trading battle for peace. A druid spell of forgetfulness, sent by Lugh, makes the brothers come home thinking all is paid; the missing spit and shouts are named publicly, and Tuireann's daughter Ethne laments them back to the sea. A quarter of a year on the ocean wins the spit from the laughing embroiderers. Then the hill of Miochaoin: guardian and sons, mutual spearing, Brian lifting each dying brother with one hand until the three shouts were given at last. Tuireann begged the healing skin of Lugh — 'for we are of the one blood, and let him not give hardness for hardness.' Lugh refused: not for the breadth of the earth in gold, unless he was sure their death would come in satisfaction for the deed. Brian lay down between his brothers, and the three lives went out together; their father died of grief and they were buried in one grave.
narrative.zh: 圖雷恩諸子之故事乃愛爾蘭之『罰金史詩』（éraic），將復仇化為商業之最持久研究。圖雷恩三子——布萊恩、尤哈、尤哈爾巴——技藝與名望冠絕塔拉，與西安三兄弟世代為仇。穆爾西姆尼平原上孤身之西安被擒，以德魯伊杖化為豬形；惟布萊恩識破，化二弟為獵犬，林緣一矛刺中。『知我而射，惡莫大焉。』求庇不得；布萊恩誓取其命七次。西安求得一事：死於人形——『若以豬形殺我，賠償僅如一豬之價；以人形殺我，則世上從無、永無為其人賠償更重之罰金。且所用之器，將向吾子訴此事。』石擊至碎；地六次拒納其屍，第七次乃受。魯格自大地親聞其事，葬父立石、刻歐甘文。於塔拉搖靜默之鏈，問眾人：殺父者當受何報？眾曰日日肢解——『而作此答者，正是殺我父之三子。』布萊恩欲以小額罰金了事，答『如我所殺亦當賠』。魯格遂以假謙列八件：東方世界花園之蘋果三枚（金如鎔金、味如蜜、除創痛與病、永不減少）；希臘王圖伊斯之豬皮（愈百創、化水為酒）；波斯王之矛（矛首浸水以防其焚其所）；西奧蓋爾王之海行雙馬與無雙戰車；埃薩爾王之七豬（夜殺晨生、食者無疾）；伊俄魯伊之犬費爾-伊尼斯（百獸見之皆伏）；妙髮之島婦之烹杼一支；米奧肯禁丘之三聲呼（守丘者與其子誓不許呼，因魯格之父之學藝在其處，永不寬恕）。取寶之旅即偽裝之旅：以鷹形入花園避矛雨、為避王之三魚鷹女之雷電化為天鵝；以詩人形得豬皮而屠其廷；擲蘋果殺波斯王；以傭兵形於市集奪車馬。惟埃薩爾王甘願獻豬——八寶中惟一不戰而得者——繼而助於伊俄魯伊以戰易和取犬。魯格復遣遺忘之咒，使三子誤以為罰已畢；缺失之杼與三呼於眾前點明，圖雷恩之女埃特尼泣別於海。四月之航自繡女之笑聲中得杼。禁丘之上，守者與三子互矛貫體；布萊恩以一手扶起垂死之弟，直到三聲呼畢。圖雷恩求魯格賜愈皮——『我們血脈相連，勿以硬報硬』——魯格拒之：縱以大地之廣之金易之亦不與，除非確信其死足以償其罪。布萊恩臥於二弟之間，三命同盡；父悲而亡，同穴而葬。

functions: Legal theology of the blood-fine (éraic): vengeance converted into a payable, itemized debt
Charter of the geis of truth-telling: a fine once sworn under guarantee cannot be reduced
Odyssey of disguise: transformation and impersonation as the moral currency of the quest
Etiology of the treasures: Lugh's spear, the sword Fragarach and other war-gear enter the Tuatha's arsenal by this fine

title.en: The Coming of the Gael: Amergin's Landing and the Battle of Tailltiu
title.zh: 蓋爾人來臨：阿莫金登岸與塔爾提烏之戰

region.zh: 愛爾蘭科克郡班特里灣因弗·斯凱恩（傳統登陸地）

period: Recorded in Lebor Gabála Érenn, 11th-12th c. manuscripts; Gregory retelling 1904

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book Three, Chapters I-II, eBook #14465

summary.en: The sons of Miled sail from the south to avenge Ith, their kinsman slain at Tara; Amergin stakes the landing on nine waves against the druid winds, five sons drown, and on the quieted shore Amergin speaks the great 'I am' poem — wind, wave, bull, eagle, salmon — before the Gael and the Tuatha Dé settle the island in battle at Tailltiu.
summary.zh: 米勒德諸子為報伊特之仇自南方揚帆；阿莫金以九浪之約與德魯伊風暴相賭，五子溺亡；風浪既平，阿莫金於岸誦『我是』之詩——風、浪、牛、鷹、鮭——蓋爾人與達娜之民遂決戰於塔爾提烏而定島屬。

sensitivity.note: The Milesian conquest is the charter myth of Gaelic Ireland; collected from public-domain print. The landing-place Inver Sceine is identified with Bantry Bay in tradition.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: The druids of the sons of Miled told them there was no country for them to settle in till they came to the island in the west — 'and if you do not get possession of it yourselves, your children will get possession of it.' The Tuatha Dé cast a cloud of enchantment over the island so the fleet saw only a pig-like shape; they rounded the coast and landed at Inver Sceine. On the way to Teamhair they met three queens of the Sídhe one after another — Banba wife of Mac Cuill son of the Hazel, Fodhla wife of Mac Cecht son of the Plough, and Eriu wife of Mac Greine son of the Sun, who was in one moment a wide-eyed beautiful queen and in another a sharp-beaked grey-white crow — and each queen's name would afterward be a name of Ireland. Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Three ch. 1; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：米利德（Miled）眾子的德魯伊告訴他們，除非他們來到西方那座島，否則沒有可供他們定居之地——「而你們若不親自取得它，你們的子孫將會取得它。」圖阿薩·德·達南（Tuatha Dé）在島上施放迷惑之雲，使艦隊只見到一個似豬的形貌；他們繞行海岸，於斯凱內河口（Inver Sceine）登陸。前往塔拉途中，他們先後遇見三位希德（Sídhe）女王——榛樹之子麥克·庫伊爾（Mac Cuill）之妻班巴（Banba）、犁之子麥克·凱赫特（Mac Cecht）之妻福德拉（Fodhla），以及太陽之子麥克·格雷內（Mac Greine）之妻埃里烏（Eriu），她一時是明眸的美麗女王，一時是尖喙的灰白烏鴉——此後每位女王之名都將成為愛爾蘭的一個名字。非逐字照錄。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase: Amergin offered the Tuatha Dé the wager: he would draw his ships out the length of nine waves from the shore; if the Men of Dea could keep them from landing he would sail away for ever, but if the Sons of the Gael landed, the Tuatha Dé should give up the kingship. The Men of Dea raised a druid wind that scattered the fleet and drowned Donn with twenty-four of his people, and Ir, and Colpa of the Sword — five of the sons of Miled destroyed.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Three ch. 1-2; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 精簡改寫：阿梅爾金（Amergin）向圖阿薩·德·達南提出賭約：他將把船隻駛離海岸九個浪的長度；若眾神之人（Men of Dea）能使他們無法登陸，他便永遠揚帆離去，但若蓋爾眾子（Sons of the Gael）登陸，圖阿薩·德·達南便應放棄王權。眾神之人掀起一陣德魯伊之風，吹散艦隊，溺死唐恩（Donn）及其二十四名族人，以及伊爾（Ir）與持劍者科爾帕（Colpa）——米利德眾子中有五人喪命。

passages.text: Donn called it treachery, and Amergin said his incantation over the sea: 'that they that are tossing in the great wide food-giving sea may reach now to the land... let our chief men, let their learned wives, ask that we may come to the noble woman, great Eriu.' The wind went down, and Amergin, first on the shore, said: 'I am the wind on the sea; I am the wave of the sea; I am the bull of seven battles; I am the eagle on the rock; I am a flash from the sun; I am the most beautiful of plants; I am a strong wild boar; I am a salmon in the water; I am a lake in the plain; I am the word of knowledge; I am the head of the spear in battle; I am the god that puts fire in the head.' Not verbatim.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book Three ch. 1-2; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 多恩稱之為背信，阿梅金則對大海誦念他的咒語：「願那些在大海廣闊、賜予食物的波濤中顛簸的人，如今得以抵達陸地……讓我們的領袖，讓他們博學的妻子，祈求我們得以來到那位高貴的女子、偉大的埃里烏面前。」風平息了，阿梅金率先登上岸，說道：「我是海上的風；我是海中的浪；我是七場戰役的公牛；我是岩石上的鷹；我是太陽的一道閃光；我是最美麗的植物；我是強壯的野豬；我是水中的鮭魚；我是平原上的湖泊；我是知識之言；我是戰陣中矛的尖端；我是將火置於頭中的神。」（非逐字引述。）

canonical_translation: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men, London 1904 (public domain); underlying: Lebor Gabála Érenn (Macalister edition, copyright); cf. R. A. Stewart Macalister translations

narrative.en:
The last invasion of Ireland is a lawsuit settled at sea, and its hero is a poet whose only weapon is grammar.

The sons of Miled — the Milesians, the Gael — came from the south under the leadership of the sons of Miled, their druids having told them there was no country for them to settle in until they came to the island in the west: 'and if you do not get possession of it yourselves, your children will get possession of it.' They sailed first to avenge Ith, their kinsman, who had come to the Tuatha's court in an earlier generation and been killed there by treachery. The Men of Dea did not wait for negotiation: they cast such a cloud of enchantment over the island that the fleet could see only a large thing shaped like a pig, and the Gael were hindered from landing until they worked round the coast to Inver Sceine in the west of Munster.

Marching inland, they met the land itself three times. At Slieve Mis a queen with her women and druids came out and gave her name: Banba, wife of Mac Cuill, Son of the Hazel. At Slieve Eibhline: Fodhla, wife of Mac Cecht, Son of the Plough. At Uisnech a woman met them who was in one moment a wide-eyed most beautiful queen, and in another a sharp-beaked, grey-white crow — Eriu, wife of Mac Greine, Son of the Sun. The island kept three names because it had three claimants; in the aftertime the poets would call Ireland by all of them.

At Teamhair the three grandsons of the Dagda held the kingship between them, quarrelling over their father's treasures. Amergin put the case to them and proposed the wager: let the Gael go out the length of nine waves from shore; if the Men of Dea can keep them from landing, the Gael will sail away for ever — but if they land, the Tuatha Dé give up the kingship. The gods took the enchantment side. They raised a druid wind that scattered the fleet and broke the ship of Donn, who was drowned with four-and-twenty men and women; Ir died in the same storm, and Colpa of the Sword at the moment of landing: five of the sons of Miled destroyed by weather.

Donn, before the sea took him, called it treachery, 'our knowledgeable men not putting down this wind.' Amergin answered there was no treachery — and rose before the ships and made his incantation over the winds and the sea: that they that are tossing in the great wide food-giving sea may reach now to the land; that they may find a place upon its plains, its mountains, and its valleys; that there may be a king of their own in Teamhair; that their chief men and their learned wives may ask that they come to the noble woman, great Eriu. The wind went down. Amergin stepped first onto the shore and said the great poem: I am the wind on the sea; I am the wave of the sea; I am the bull of seven battles; I am the eagle on the rock; I am a flash from the sun; I am the most beautiful of plants; I am a strong wild boar; I am a salmon in the water; I am a lake in the plain; I am the word of knowledge; I am the head of the spear in battle; I am the god that puts fire in the head. Who spreads light in the gathering on the hills? Who can tell the ages of the moon? Who can tell the place where the sun rests?

Three days later the first battle was fought at Sliab Mis, where Scota, wife of Miled, fell; the decisive battle of Tailltiu killed the three kings and three queens of the Tuatha Dé, and the surviving gods went under the hills. The poets' settlement of the defeat endures in one sentence: every brave fighting man was of the Sons of the Gael; every skilled man of music and secret enchantment was of the Tuatha Dé Danann — the two peoples of Ireland, army and dream, ranked and named.
narrative.zh: 愛爾蘭最後一次入侵，是一場以詩句為武器、在海上結案之訴訟。米勒德諸子（即蓋爾人）自南方而來，其德魯伊曾告：無他處可居，必至西方之島——『若爾等自不能得之，爾之子孫將得之。』彼等首先為族人伊特復仇——伊特昔年至達娜之民之廷而被謀害。神族不待談判：以咒雲蔽島，使艦隊惟見一豬形巨物；蓋爾人繞岸而至芒斯特西部因弗·斯凱恩登陸。內進途中，三次與土地相會：斯利夫·米斯山遇女王班巴（榛子之子麥克·庫爾之妻）；斯利夫·艾夫林遇福德拉（犁之子麥克·克赫特之妻）；烏斯內克遇一女，頃刻為美目之後，頃刻為灰白銳喙之鴉——艾雷（太陽之子麥克·格賴內之妻）。島有三名，因其有三主；後世詩人遂以三名稱愛爾蘭。塔拉城中，達格達三孫共治而爭產。阿莫金陳案立約：蓋爾人退出九浪之外；若神族能阻其登岸，則永不再來；若登岸，神族讓位。神族以德魯伊風暴應之：艦隊潰散，唐恩與二十四人溺亡，伊爾死於同風暴，劍之科爾帕死於將登之際——米勒德五子皆喪於天氣。唐恩臨沒斥為背信；阿莫金答曰無信——起於舟前向風海誦咒：使飄搖於廣闊賜食之海者今得登陸；使彼等得處其平原、山嶽、溪谷；使塔拉有吾族之王；使吾人之首領與智婦求見偉大之艾雷。風止。阿莫金率先登岸，誦其大詩：我是海上之風；我是海中之浪；我是七戰之牛；我是岩上之鷹；我是日中之一閃；我是至美之草；我是荒野之豬；我是水中之鮭；我是平原之湖；我是知識之言；我是戰中之矛鋒；我是點燃頭腦之火之神。孰於山丘聚會中散布光明？孰能言月亮之齡？孰能言太陽安息之所？三日後斯利夫·米斯首戰，米勒德之妻斯科塔陣亡；塔爾提烏決戰殺神族三王三后，倖存之神入山而居。詩人對敗者之安置存於一句：凡勇戰之士屬蓋爾人之子；凡精於音樂與隱秘咒法者屬達娜之民——愛爾蘭之二族，軍隊與夢，各得其位、各得其名。

functions: Founding charter of Gaelic Ireland: conquest legitimized as a won wager and a paid blood-debt for Ith
Charter of the poet's authority: Amergin's poem as grammar of national identity ('I am' catalog)
Etiology of Ireland's three names (Banba, Fodla, Eriu) from the three queens met on the march
Settlement of the two peoples: fighters of the Gael, craft-and-enchantment people of the Tuatha Dé

variants.summary: The chronicle gives full genealogies of the Milesians from Scota and Goídel Glas and a set of Amergin's invocations (to land, sea, fish) before the landing — the liturgical core of the conquest.

variants.name: Folk remains of Donn
variants.text_tradition: Dindsenchas and later folklore of Tech Duinn
variants.summary: Donn the drowned son becomes lord of the dead: 'to me, to my house, you shall all come after your deaths' — his shipwreck is the mythic origin of the Irish house of the dead.

title.en: The Purusha Sukta: Creation from the Sacrificed Man
title.zh: 原人歌：以犧牲之軀創世

region.en: Punjab plains, Rigveda heartland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 旁遮普平原，梨俱吠陀核心區（象徵性定位）

period: Rigveda, Book 10 (late mandala), c. 1200-1000 BCE (Griffith translation, 1896)

source.work: The Hymns of the Rigveda, trans. Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896), Book 10, Hymn 90 (Purusha Sukta)

summary.en: A thousand-headed cosmic Man, Purusha, is sacrificed by the gods themselves; his body is cut up and becomes the world - sky from his head, earth from his feet, sun from his eye, moon from his mind - while the four castes spring from his mouth, arms, thighs, and feet. The hymn fuses cosmogony with ritual: the world exists because it was once offered.
summary.zh: 千首千眼的宇宙巨人普魯沙為諸神所祭；其身軀被分割而化為世界——頭化天穹、足化大地、眼化太陽、心化月亮；四大種姓則出自其口、臂、腿、足。此頌將創世與祭祀合一：世界之存在，正因其曾為祭品。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition: the Purusha Sukta is recited in Vedic ritual and its caste verses are politically contested in modern India. Classified 'myth' (hymn-myth rather than liturgical prescription); the contested readings are recorded in the variants and sensitivity guidance.

passages.text: Purusha has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet; he covers the earth on every side and extends ten fingers' breadth beyond it. All that is, all that has been and all that shall be, is this Man; he has become immortality and whatever the gods feed upon. Three-quarters of him rose above creation; one-quarter was spread through this world of living things, and from it he pervaded everything that eats and everything that does not eat.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.90 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 原人有千頭、千眼、千足；他遍覆大地於四方，並向外延伸十指之寬。一切存在者、一切曾存在者與一切將存在者，皆是此「人」；他已成為不朽，以及諸神所食的一切。他的四分之三升於造化之上；四分之一散布於這充滿生靈的世界，並由此遍及一切有食者與一切無食者。

passages.text: When the gods spread out the sacrifice, they made of Purusha the victim: spring was the melted butter of the offering, summer the fuel, autumn the oblation. They bound the Man born of old upon the sacrificial grass and sacrificed him with the sacrifice itself; the celestial beings, the seers of old, and the offerings were made one - thus did the gods sacrifice to the sacrifice.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.90 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當諸神鋪開祭祀時，他們以原人為祭品：春是供獻的融酥，夏是燃料，秋是供物。他們將那自古而生的「人」縛於祭祀之草上，並以祭祀本身獻祭他；天上的眾生、古代的先知與供物合而為一——諸神便如此向祭祀獻祭。

passages.text: From that all-encompassing sacrifice the curds and butter were gathered, the victim's parts prepared; the sky came from his head, the atmosphere from his navel, the earth from his feet, the directions of space from his ear. From his mind the moon was born, from his eye the sun, from his mouth Indra and Agni, from his breath the wind; the ridges of the mountains came from him, the seas and streams were made from him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.90 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 從那包羅萬有的祭祀中，凝乳與酥油被聚集起來，祭品的肢體被備妥；天出自他的頭，大氣出自他的臍，地出自他的足，方位出自他的耳。從他的心意生出月亮，從他的眼生出太陽，從他的口生出因陀羅與阿耆尼，從他的氣息生出風；山脈的稜脊從他而來，海洋與河流也從他而成。

passages.text: When they divided the Man, into how many parts did they divide him? His mouth became the Brahmin, his arms the Kshatriya, his thighs the Vaishya, and from his feet the Shudra was born. The sacred word was born from the same sacrifice - the verses, the chants and the ritual formulae - together with the horse, the cow, the goat and the sheep, each from a different portion of the victim; the gods raised him up and made him the oblation.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.90 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他們分割那「人」時，將他分成了多少部分？他的口成為婆羅門，他的臂成為剎帝利，他的腿成為吠舍，而首陀羅則從他的足生出。聖言也從同一祭祀中生出——詩句、頌歌與儀式咒語——連同馬、牛、山羊與綿羊，各自出自祭品的不同部位；諸神將他舉起，使他成為供物。

canonical_translation: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., Benares, 1896 (public domain); critical: Stephanie W. Jamison and Joel P. Brereton, The Rigveda, 3 vols., Oxford University Press, 2014

narrative.en:
The Purusha Sukta is the Rigveda's most concentrated cosmogony and its most debated poem: fifteen verses in an archaic metre, placed at the head of Book 10's creation cluster. It answers the question 'how was the world made?' with a single image - a cosmic human body, offered up and divided.

The hymn opens with the Man himself. Purusha has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet; he envelops the earth and reaches ten fingers' breadth beyond it. He is not one being among others: whatever has been and whatever will be is this Man, and he is himself immortality and the food of the gods. Three-quarters of him rise above creation into the timeless; one-quarter is spread through the world of living things, and from that quarter everything that eats and everything that does not eat is pervaded.

Then comes the act. The gods - 'the celestial beings' and 'those who were seers of old' - bind Purusha, born before time, upon the sacrificial grass, and sacrifice him with the sacrifice itself. Spring supplies the melted butter, summer the fuel, autumn the offering: the ritual calendar is projected back onto the origin of the world, so that every later sacrifice re-enacts the first one. The gods 'sacrificed with the sacrifice to the sacrifice'; from the all-encompassing offering the curds and butter are gathered, and the world's body is distributed.

The dismemberment is the geography. From Purusha's mind comes the moon, from his eye the sun, from his mouth Indra and Agni, from his breath the wind. His head becomes the sky, his navel the atmosphere, his feet the earth, his ear the directions of space; the mountains are his ridges, the sea and the streams his generated waters. Light itself is part of the spent body.

Finally the social order. When they divided the Man, his mouth became the Brahmin, his arms the Kshatriya, his thighs the Vaishya, his feet the Shudra: the four classes of Vedic society are mapped onto the sacrificed body, hierarchy written into creation. The sacred word is born from the same sacrifice - the verses, the chants, the ritual formulae - together with the sacrificial animals, the horse, the cow, the goat, the sheep, each from a different portion of the victim. The gods raise Purusha up and make him the oblation.

Function: the hymn makes sacrifice the engine of the cosmos - the world is not created but offered, and ritual is therefore not man-made devotion but participation in a cosmic event. It grounds the varna system in a creation narrative and gave later thought its model of macrocosm and microcosm: the body and the universe are the same thing at two scales. In later strata, Purusha becomes the Self of the Upanishads (the second bird on the same tree in the Mundaka), and Purusha-Narayana the couch of Vishnu; this late hymn reshaped the whole tradition around itself.

The verses assigning caste have made the hymn politically contested in modern India: Dalit and reformist readings treat the caste verses as a late insertion (linguistic arguments support a late date and possible interpolation), while orthodox commentary reads them as cosmological rather than legislative. The record keeps the hymn whole and records the dispute in its variants.
narrative.zh: 原人歌為梨俱吠陀最集中的創世頌：十五節詩，以一幅圖像回答『世界如何造成』——宇宙之軀被獻祭而分割。普魯沙千首千眼千足，籠蓋大地而超出十指之寬；萬有之過去未來皆此巨人，彼即不死與諸神之食。其四分之三超出造化，四分之一遍於眾生。諸神以祭祀束縛這位太古所生之巨人，以祭祀祭之：春為酥油、夏為薪柴、秋為祭品。祭祀之後，身軀化為世界——心化月亮、眼化太陽、口生因陀羅與阿耆尼、息生風神；首化天穹、臍化空界、足化大地、耳化方位；山是其稜脊，海流由其所生。分割之際，社會秩序亦定：口生婆羅門、臂生剎帝利、腿生吠舍、足生首陀羅；頌詩、歌詠、祭祀口訣皆自同一祭中誕生，馬牛羊亦各出其身之一部。功能：以祭祀為宇宙引擎——世界非被造而是被獻，儀式遂非人為虔敬而為宇宙事件之重演；種姓制度被寫入創世敘事；宏微宇宙相即之模型由此奠定。後世層中，普魯沙化為奧義書之自我（蒙達卡奧義書同樹之雙鳥），普魯沙-那羅延化為毘濕奴之臥榻；此晚期頌歌重塑了整個傳統。種姓諸節在現代印度政治上極具爭議：賤民與改革派讀法視其為晚出插文（語文學論據支持晚期與可能之插入），正統注釋則讀為宇宙論而非立法。本錄保留全頌並於變體欄記錄爭議。

functions: Charter of Vedic sacrifice: every ritual re-enacts the primordial offering of Purusha
Mythic grounding of the four varnas and of macrocosm-microcosm correspondence
Bridge text between Vedic ritualism and Upanishadic interiority (Purusha as Self)
Recited in Agnihotra and major sacrificial rites to this day

variants.name: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad reworking (the Self divides itself)
variants.text_tradition: Brihadaranyaka 1.4, Kuru-Panchala prose, c. 8th-6th c. BCE
variants.summary: Replaces the ritual dismemberment with a Self that alone existed, feared, desired a second and divided itself - the sacrificed body becomes an internalizing meditation on the Self.

variants.name: Narayana-Purusha of the Mahabharata (Shanti Parva)
variants.summary: Epic theology identifies Purusha with Narayana-Vishnu as the universal soul from whose body the worlds proceed; the sacrifice frame softens into avatara doctrine.

variants.name: Mundaka Upanishad's two birds on one tree
variants.summary: Purusha splits into two birds - one eating the tree's sweet fruit (the engaged self), one watching without eating (the witnessing Self) - converting the hymn's cosmology into soteriology.

variants.name: Modern contested readings of the caste verses
variants.summary: Critical philology (e.g. Jamison-Brereton 2014) treats the varna verses as a likely late insertion; Ambedkarite and reform readings reject the hymn's caste grounding, while orthodox commentators read them as cosmological description, not legislation.

title.en: The Hiranyagarbha Hymn: Golden Womb of the Worlds
title.zh: 金胎頌：世界之金卵

region.en: Kurukshetra plains (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 俱盧之野平原（象徵性定位）

period: Rigveda, Book 10 (late mandala), c. 1200-1000 BCE (Griffith translation, 1896)

source.work: The Hymns of the Rigveda, trans. Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896), Book 10, Hymn 121 (Hiranyagarbha Sukta)

summary.en: In the beginning rose the Golden Womb - Hiranyagarbha - born as the one lord of all that is; before heaven and earth were, he held within himself the gods and the worlds. Each verse ends with the refrain 'what deity shall we worship with the oblation?', and the final verse dares to doubt whether even the highest being knows - the Vedic skeptic's creation hymn that later becomes Brahma's cosmic egg.
summary.zh: 太初升起金胎——希任耶加爾波——為萬有唯一之主；天地未分，彼已內含諸神與世界。每節末句重唱『吾人以祭品當敬奉何神？』，末節更敢疑至高者是否自知——此吠陀懷疑論之創世頌，後世演化為梵天之宇宙金卵。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition: recited in worship and meditated upon in Vedanta. Classified 'myth' (hymn-myth).

passages.text: In the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, the Golden Womb, born as the only lord of all created beings. He fixed and held up this earth and heaven. Before heaven and earth had come to be, before the waters moved, that One drew breath, unborn, sustaining all things; whatever breathes and shuts its eyes looked to him alone.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.121 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 太初，金胎希蘭亞加爾巴興起，作為一切受造眾生唯一的君主而生。他固定並撐起這地與天。在天與地尚未形成之前，在水尚未流動之前，那「一」已呼吸，未生而維持萬物；凡有氣息、閉上眼睛者，皆唯獨仰望他。

passages.text: The refrain runs through every verse: what deity shall we adore with the offering? The One by whose command the worlds rose, he in whom the gods found their own seats; he who holds the snow-clad mountains and the sea, the waters that encircle all; he whose are heaven and earth, the sun and the firmament - the one God above the gods.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.121 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這句疊句貫穿每一節詩：我們該以祭品崇敬哪位神祇？那一位，諸世界因祂的命令而升起，眾神在祂之中尋得各自的座位；那一位，執掌積雪的山脈與大海，環繞一切的眾水；那一位，天與地、太陽與蒼穹皆屬於祂——那一位在眾神之上的神。

passages.text: The closing verse turns the hymn on itself: may he not harm us, he who is the procreator of the earth, who established the bright regions of heaven, the golden embryo within the waters that possessed them all - and then, with almost deliberate ambiguity, the poet asks: he who was truly the begetter, the guardian of the gods - whether he himself knows it or not - if he does not know, who among us can know?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.121 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 末節將頌詩轉向自身：願祂不傷害我們，祂是大地之生育者，奠定天上光明之境者，那金胎，在曾擁有它們一切的眾水之中——而後，詩人以近乎刻意的含糊問道：那真正是生育者、眾神的守護者——無論祂自己是否知道——若祂不知，我們之中誰能知道？

canonical_translation: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., Benares, 1896 (public domain); critical: Jamison & Brereton, The Rigveda, Oxford, 2014

narrative.en:
The Hiranyagarbha Sukta (Rigveda 10.121) is the second great creation hymn of Book 10, and the most theological of the Vedic hymns: a chant of ten verses, each ending with the same questioning refrain, addressed to an unnamed supreme origin.

The image: in the beginning there rose from the waters a golden embryo - a cosmic egg, golden like the sun - and it was born as the one lord of all that exists. Before the earth and heaven were made, before even the waters had spread, that One breathed, unborn, sustaining everything that breathes and shuts its eyes. From the Golden Womb the world is not so much manufactured as hatched: the One 'fixed and held up this earth and heaven', gave the gift of breath, of life, of the gods' own thrones. The mountains with their snowy peaks are his; the sea and the encircling waters are his; heaven and earth and the sun's path are his dominion.

The refrain is the hymn's signature: 'what deity shall we worship with the oblation?' - 'he, they say, is that one'. The insistence on the question rather than a name gives the hymn a monotheizing and also a deferring quality: later traditions resolve the ambiguity by naming the One - Prajapati in the Brahmanas, Brahma in the Puranas - but the Vedic poet keeps the divinity unnamed and the worship provisional.

The last verse is the sharpest: the poet prays that the golden one, procreator of the earth, establisher of the bright heavens, may not harm us - and then steps back: he who was the true begetter, the guardian of the gods, whether he himself knows it or not - 'if he does not know, who among us can know?' This is the same skeptical breath that animates the Nasadiya Sukta's closing lines ('perhaps even the highest overseer knows not'). Vedic cosmogony refuses final certainty: creation is affirmed, the creator is doubted.

Function and afterlife: the hymn supplied the tradition with its standing image for cosmic origin - hiranyagarbha, the golden egg - which the Brahmanas elaborate (the waters lay as an egg, heat matured it, Brahma broke through), which the Puranas turn into the immense Brahma-anda surrounding all worlds (see the Vishnu Purana egg record), and which Vedanta takes as a meditation-object. In ritual, 'hiranyagarbha' is also the name of an enormous royal gold-donation sacrifice: a king ceremonially reborn from a golden womb, claiming cosmic kingship by enacting the origin - the myth migrating from cosmology into consecration.
narrative.zh: 金胎頌（梨俱吠陀 10.121）為第十卷第二大創世頌，最具神學性：十節頌歌，每節同以一句疑問重唱作結，向一位未名的至上本源祈唱。意象為：太初自水中升起一金色胎卵——宇宙之卵，金如太陽——彼生而為萬有唯一之主。天地未立、諸水未布之前，此一者已呼吸，未生而養育一切凡呼吸閉目者。世界非被造而是被孵育：『彼奠定、托舉此天與地』，賜予氣息、生命與諸神之座。雪山屬彼，海與環繞之水屬彼，天與地與日行之軌屬其王權。重唱『吾人以祭品當敬奉何神？』——『彼，人言即是』——堅持以問句而非名號，使頌歌帶有獨神化而亦延宕的色彩：後世釋之為生主（梵書）、梵天（往世書），而吠陀詩人始終不名其名。末節最銳利：詩人祈求金胎者勿加害，繼而退問——彼為真正的生者、諸神之守護者，縱彼自身亦未必自知——『彼若不知，吾等誰能知？』此與無有歌結尾之懷疑同調：吠陀創世觀拒絕最終確定性。功能與後續：此頌供給傳統以『金胎』之標準宇宙起源意象——梵書演之、往世書化為梵天之巨卵、吠檀多以之為冥想對象；儀式上『金胎』亦為巨額獻金之王祭：王者自金卵中儀式性重生，以身行創世而宣稱宇宙王權。

functions: Standing Vedic image of cosmic origin (golden embryo/egg) for Brahmana, Purana and Vedanta
Theology of an unnamed supreme lord - prayer without a fixed name
Charter of the hiranyagarbha royal sacrifice (king reborn from a golden womb)
Model of reverent skepticism about final knowledge of origins

variants.name: Shatapatha Brahmana's egg-cosmogony
variants.summary: The waters lay as a cosmic egg; heat (tapas) matured it for a year; Brahma (Prajapati) broke through and created - the hymn's golden womb given narrative procedure and ritual timing.

variants.name: Vishnu Purana's Brahma-anda
variants.text_tradition: Purana corpus, Wilson translation 1840, Book 1, chs. 1-2
variants.summary: The golden egg becomes the immense cosmic egg within which Vishnu sleeps and Brahma creates at each kalpa; the Vedic image is absorbed into Puranic cosmology.

variants.name: Nasadiya Sukta's skeptical parallel
variants.summary: A companion hymn that pushes the doubt further - even the gods are later than creation, and the highest overseer 'knows not'; the two hymns frame the Vedic philosophy of origin.

title.en: Indra Slays Vritra and Frees the Rivers
title.zh: 因陀羅誅弗栗多，釋放眾水

region.en: Indus-Sarasvati river plains (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 印度河-薩拉斯瓦蒂河平原（象徵性定位）

period: Rigveda, Book 1, c. 1500-1200 BCE (Griffith translation, 1896)

source.work: The Hymns of the Rigveda, trans. Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896), Book 1, Hymn 32 (with 1.11, 2.11-12)

summary.en: Vritra, the coverer, coils around the waters and holds the rivers hostage in the mountain's hollow. Indra, made almighty by draughts of Soma, hurls the thunderbolt forged by Tvashtar, splits the serpent, and the pent-up rivers rush down like bellowing chariot-teams - the archetypal storm-god combat that keeps the world's waters moving and rains falling.
summary.zh: 弗栗多（『遮蔽者』）盤踞眾水，將河流挾持於山腹之內。因陀羅飲蘇摩酒而獲全能，擲由特瓦斯特利鍛造之雷霆杵，劈開巨蛇；被囚之河如怒吼的戰車群奔湧而下——此為風暴之神戰鬥的原型，使世界之水常流、雨澤常降。

sensitivity.note: Ancient liturgical-hymn source, still recited in Vedic study. Classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Now let me declare the heroic deeds of Indra, the first that he achieved: he slew the dragon that lay against the mountain. Tvashtar forged the bolt for him; like bellowing cows with flowing milk, the waters rushed down to the ocean. Strong of purpose, he took the Soma, drank its pressed juices, and the worshipper's gift made him mighty.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 1.32 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 現在讓我宣揚因陀羅的英勇事蹟，他所成就的第一樁：他誅殺了橫臥山前的巨龍。陀濕多為他鍛造了金剛杵；眾水如鳴叫的乳牛流著乳汁，奔湧而下注入大海。他意志堅定，取來蘇摩，飲下其壓榨之汁，而崇拜者的獻禮使他強壯。

passages.text: When in his hands he took the thunderbolt, the missile that slays, the lightning made of a hundred joints, he slew the first-born of dragons. Like a tree-trunk felled by the axe, the serpent lay flattened on the ground; the waters, like bellowing chariot-teams, poured over the body as they flowed away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 1.32 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他手中握起那雷霆，那誅殺的投擲之器，那由百節構成的閃電，他誅殺了眾龍之首生者。如被斧頭砍倒的樹幹，那巨蛇癱伏於地；眾水如鳴叫的戰車隊，流過其身而奔湧離去。

passages.text: Vritra had grown insolent with strength; Indra, whose anger grew with the Soma he had drunk, split the serpent's head with the great bolt, and the conquered Vritra sank under his blow. The pent-up mothers of the world - the rivers - flowed on for their lord; they went, the waters, straight to the ocean, forced through the gap Indra had opened.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 1.32 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 弗栗多因力量而變得傲慢；因陀羅的怒火隨他所飲的蘇摩而增長，以巨大的金剛杵劈開巨蛇的頭顱，被征服的弗栗多在他的打擊下沉落。被禁錮的世界之母——眾河流——為它們的主宰繼續流淌；它們前行，那眾水，直趨大海，衝過因陀羅所開的缺口。

canonical_translation: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., Benares, 1896 (public domain); critical: Jamison & Brereton, The Rigveda, Oxford, 2014

narrative.en:
The combat of Indra and Vritra is the epicentre of Vedic mythology - a fight retold, alluded to and re-imagined across dozens of Rigveda hymns, and the single deed by which Indra is king of the gods.

The adversary: Vritra, whose name means 'the coverer' or 'obstructor', a dragon-serpent coiled around the world's waters, gripping the rivers in the hollows of the mountains so that no rain falls and the land lies parched. The Rigveda calls him 'the first-born of dragons', the worst of Vritras; in some hymns he is a three-headed being, in others a vast serpent guarding the foot of the world-mountain, hoarding the cows of light as well as the waters.

The hero: Indra is born for this fight. The later myths tell of his miraculous birth from the side of his mother, of the thunderbolt Tvashtar the divine smith forged for him, of the hundred-jointed missile that no one else could carry. But the immediate engine of victory is Soma: Indra drinks the pressed juice of the Soma plant until his body swells with power - the hymns are candid that the god is intoxicated by the sacrifice, that the drink 'made him mighty', that his rage and his arms grow with each draught. The priests' libations are, quite literally, his ammunition: ritual and myth are one economy.

The fight: when Indra took the bolt in his hands, he slew the first-born of dragons. Vritra is not merely killed but undone - struck in the head, he collapses 'like a tree-trunk felled by the axe', and Indra leaves his vast body lying across the landscape. Then the release: the rivers, pent up like cows whose milk had been withheld, burst through the gap Indra cut and pour down to the ocean 'like bellowing chariot-teams' or 'like bellowing cows with flowing milk', washing over the dead serpent as they go. The sun rises on the freed world; dawns shine again.

Function: this is a rain-and-river myth and a liturgical charter at once. Every monsoon is a repetition of Indra's victory; every drought is Vritra's grip returning; and every Soma offering re-arms the god. The combat also maps cosmic order: Indra's bolt establishes the partition of heaven and earth, and the freed waters establish the flow of life. Comparative mythologists see here the same duel as Marduk-Tiamat (dragon of the waters), Baal-Yam (sea-serpent), and Zeus-Typhon - the storm god slaying the water-dragon to institute order.

The ambiguity: Vritra in several texts is not simply evil - some Brahmana recensions make him a Brahmin slain by Indra, and the god must perform expiation. The verse that makes Vritra 'like a Brahmin among the gods' forced later theology to negotiate: Indra's kingship is stained by the very deed that founds it, a paradox the Upanishadic and Puranic layers will inherit.
narrative.zh: 因陀羅與弗栗多之戰為吠陀神話的震央：數十首頌歌反覆重述、暗示、重構此戰，此功績奠定因陀羅之天帝之位。對手弗栗多，意為『遮蔽者』，蛇龍盤繞世界之水，將河流挾於山腹，使雨澤不降、大地乾涸；吠陀稱其為『龍之長子』、弗栗多中最惡者。英雄因陀羅為此戰而生：特瓦斯特利為其鍛造雷霆杵，百節之彌無人能舉；然勝利之引擎為蘇摩——因陀羅飲榨出的蘇摩汁直至神力充盈，頌詩坦承此神因祭酒而醉、因飲而壯，祭司的澆祭即其彈藥：儀式與神話同屬一種經濟。戰鬥：因陀羅執杵在手，誅龍之長子；弗栗多不僅被殺更被『解散』——擊首而倒，『如斧斫之樹幹』，橫陳大地。隨之釋放：被囚之河如乳汁被扣的母牛，自因陀羅所開之隙衝出，『如怒吼的戰車群』奔流入海，水漫過蛇屍。太陽於解放之世升起，黎明重輝。功能：此為雨河神話亦是禮儀憲章——每場季雨皆因陀羅之勝的重演，每場旱災皆弗栗多之掌握復歸，每次蘇摩祭皆為神再武裝。比較神話學視之與馬爾杜克-提亞馬特、巴力-雅姆、宙斯-提豐同型：風暴神誅水龍以立秩序。曖昧處：若干梵書使弗栗多為婆羅門，因陀羅因而負殺婆羅門之罪，須行贖罪——因陀羅之王權正因其奠基之功而蒙污，此悖論為奧義書與往世書層所承繼。

functions: Aition of rain, rivers and the monsoon - the storm god keeps the waters moving
Liturgical charter of Soma sacrifice (the god's power purchased with libations)
Archetype of the storm-god vs. water-dragon combat across the ancient Near East and Indo-European world
Origin of Indra's kingship - and of the brahminicide-guilt paradox later theology must expiate

variants.name: Ugaritic Baal-Yam combat
variants.text_tradition: Baal Cycle, KTU 1.1-1.2 (c. 14th-13th c. BCE tablets, Ugarit)
variants.summary: The storm god Baal defeats Yam the sea-serpent-prince to claim kingship; the same duel archetype with the waters as adversary, independently fixed in West Semitic epic.

variants.name: Hittite Illuyanka myth
variants.text_tradition: Hittite tablet cycle, KBo (Hattusa, 2nd millennium BCE)
variants.summary: The storm god and the dragon Illuyanka fight in two versions - one won by trickery and a feast; a Near Eastern cousin of the serpent-slaying combat.

variants.name: Shatapatha Brahmana's brahmin-Vritra
variants.summary: Vritra becomes a Brahmin whom Indra must slay; the god hides in guilt and the priests devise expiation, recasting the heroic combat as ritual problem-solving.

title.en: Yama and Yami: The First Mortal and the Forbidden Twin
title.zh: 閻摩與閻蜜：第一位死者和被禁的雙生姊妹

region.en: Yama's realm (symbolic pin at Gaya, city of ancestor rites)
region.zh: 閻摩之國（象徵性定位於伽耶，祖先祭祀之城）

period: Rigveda, Book 10 (late mandala), c. 1200-1000 BCE (Griffith translation, 1896)

source.work: The Hymns of the Rigveda, trans. Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896), Book 10, Hymn 10 (Yama-Yami dialogue; with 10.14 Yama's funeral hymn)

summary.en: Yama, the first mortal to die, finds the road to the pastures of the dead and becomes their king. His twin sister Yami presses him to beget the race with her - 'the makers of mankind made us man and wife in the womb'; Yama refuses: the gods watch the holy law, and no later age will accept what the first age did. The dialogue fixes two foundations at once: death's realm and the incest taboo.
summary.zh: 閻摩為第一位死去之人，尋得通往亡者牧場之路，遂為其王。其雙生姊妹閻蜜懇求與之交合以繁衍族類——『造人者在胎中已以夫妻相成』；閻摩拒絕：諸神守望聖法，後世必不容太初所為。此對話同時奠定兩事：死亡之國與亂倫之禁。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition: Yama worship and ancestor rites (sraddha) continue. Classified 'myth'. The origin-of-death tagging is interpretive (Thompson index is Euro-American) - noted here.

passages.text: Yami speaks to her twin, urgent as a lover: she calls him her husband in the sight of the gods who made them one being in the womb. Even the maker, she says, formed us man and wife; the whole race of gods and mortals comes from such unions - why should Yama alone be restrained? Come to me, my brother; throw your arms about me.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.10 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 閻密對她的孿生兄弟說話，急切如戀人：她在創造他們為一體於胎中的眾神眼前，稱他為她的丈夫。她說，甚至那造物者也把我們造成夫妻；眾神與凡人的整個族類皆出自這樣的結合——為何獨有閻摩應受約束？到我這裡來，我的兄弟；把你的雙臂環抱我。

passages.text: Yama answers with the law: the gods watch with vigilance over their holy ordinances; the speech he speaks does not fit her. The eyes of all beings are upon them; the deeds of the primal ages will not be repeated - later ages will not let what the first ones did stand for them. He cites Tvashtri the maker, who created the pair with separate purposes, and tells her plainly: seek another husband and make him thy partner; join with him and be a mother. Yami retorts that a brother's harshness is pitiable; Yama closes: another husband is found for her - with Yama she shall never lie.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.10 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 閻摩以律法作答：眾神警覺地守護著他們的神聖律令；他所說的這番話並不適合她。一切眾生的目光都落在他們身上；太初時代的作為不會被重演——後來的時代不會讓最初者所行之事為他們立為常例。他援引造物者陀濕多，說他懷著各自不同的目的造了這一對，並直白地告訴她：去另尋一位丈夫，讓他成為你的伴侶；與他結合，為人母。閻彌反駁說，兄弟的嚴酷令人可憐；閻摩作結：另有一位丈夫為她尋得——與閻摩，她將永不共寢。

passages.text: Elsewhere the hymns tell what became of Yama: he chose death and found the path for the many; he was the first to reach the pasture where the ancient herdsmen and their flocks have gone, the first to mark out the meeting-place of the dead. In the house of the fathers his seat is established; he gathers the mortals of old around him, king of the dead, and men still offer to him as they send their fathers ahead by fire.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.14 (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 別處的頌詩講述了閻摩的結局：他選擇了死亡，為眾人尋得了道路；他是第一個抵達那片牧場的人，古老的牧人及其畜群都已前往那裡，也是第一個標劃出亡者聚會之所的人。在父輩的居所中，他的座位已然確立；他將往昔的凡人聚集於自己周圍，身為亡者之王，而人們至今仍向他獻祭，一如他們以火將父輩先行送去。

canonical_translation: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., Benares, 1896 (public domain); critical: Jamison & Brereton, The Rigveda, Oxford, 2014

narrative.en:
Book 10 of the Rigveda contains the tradition's earliest speculation on where death came from, and it does so twice over: in a dialogue about incest, and in funeral hymns about a first traveler. The Yama-Yami dialogue (10.10) is the archetypal origin-of-death-and-kinship-law myth of the Indo-European world.

The situation: Yama and Yami are twins, the first humans born to the creator. Yama, in the Vedic frame, is mortal - the first man to die, the one who chose death and thereby discovered the path to the world of the fathers, where he reigns as king of the pastures where the dead graze like an ancient herd. Yami, his twin, remains alive and unmarried. She speaks first, and her logic is radical: there is no one else. If humanity is to continue, the pair must pair. She reminds him that even the creator formed them 'man and wife in the womb', and that gods and mortals descend from such unions; the first generation cannot be bound by the customs of later ones.

Yama's refusal is the founding argument of the taboo. He invokes surveillance: 'the gods watch with vigilance over their holy law' - the transgression would be seen. He distinguishes epochs: what the first age did, no later age will accept - the taboo is historical, a rule about what may be done 'now that there are later ages'. He appeals to the maker's intent: Tvashtri formed the pair with distinct purposes, not as one flesh. And he offers an exit: another husband exists for her; let her join with him and be a mother. Yami's reply is bitter - she calls his harshness pitiable - and Yama's closing line is absolute: with Yama she shall never lie.

The two halves fit together. The funeral hymns (10.14 and the Yama hymns of Book 10) show Yama as the first to die and the pathfinder of death - he goes first, so that the dead have somewhere to go and a king who receives them. The dialogue with Yami explains why there are no more primeval unions: the first twins did not become the parents of humanity; the race descends instead through ordinary marriage, bounded by the law Yama defended. Death is Yama's own story: to be mortal is to be the species of Yama, who went ahead.

Comparatively, this is the same constellation as the sibling-creator pairs of many cosmogonies - but with a refusal where others have union. The taboo turned into doctrine: Yama's realm (Yamaloka) becomes the intermediate station of the dead in the epics and Puranas, and the Katha Upanishad makes him the teacher who can promise immortality but insists on the law (dharma) as the way.

Function: the dialogue legitimizes exogamy and the incest taboo as divine law with a memory of a first exception; the funeral hymns make Yama the friendly face of necessity - the first traveler who keeps records, receives offerings, and in folk practice is still fed at ancestor rites.
narrative.zh: 梨俱吠陀第十卷含此傳統最早對死亡來源的思辨，分兩次呈現：一場關於亂倫的對話，與數首關於第一位旅人的葬歌。閻摩與閻蜜為雙生，創造者所生之首批人類。吠陀框架中閻摩為有死者——第一位選擇死亡之人，因而發現通往亡者世界之路，在亡者如古牧群般放牧的牧野為王。閻蜜仍活而未嫁，她先開口，邏輯極端：世上再無他人；族類若要延續，雙生必須成偶。她提醒他：連造物者也在胎中以夫妻相成；諸神與凡人皆出自此類結合；太初世代不受後世風俗束縛。閻摩之拒絕是禁忌的立論基礎：他訴諸監視——『諸神以警醒守望其聖法』；訴諸時代——太初所為，後世不容；訴諸造者之意——特瓦斯特利以不同目的造此一對，非使其為一體；並給出出口——另有夫婿存在，可與之成婚為母。閻蜜之答苦澀，斥其嚴苛可憫；閻摩結語絕對：與閻摩同寢，永不。兩半相合：葬歌顯示閻摩為第一位死者、死亡之路的開闢者——他先行，故亡者有可去之處、有收留之王；對話則解釋為何再無太初結合：首對雙生未成人類之父母，族類遂經由閻摩所守之法律界定的平常婚姻而繁衍。功能：對話使外婚制與亂倫禁忌合法化為帶有太初例外記憶的神聖法律；葬歌使閻摩成為必然性之親切面孔——先行旅人、記錄分毫不差、接受祭品，至今仍在祖先祭祀中受饗。

title.en: The Jomsvikings' Founding: Palnatoki's Brotherhood and Its Oath
title.zh: 約姆斯維京的創立：帕爾納托基的兄弟會與其誓言

region.en: Jomsborg on the Baltic (the fortress; symbolic pin at Wolin, Poland)
region.zh: 波羅的海約姆斯堡（象徵性定位於波蘭沃林）

period: Jomsvikinga saga 13th c. (older material); the Jomsviking-lay of Bishop Bjarni (c. 1200); the Battle of Hjorungavag c. 986

source.work: Jomsvikinga saga; the Jomsviking-lay; English: Lee M. Hollander, The Saga of the Jomsvikings, 1955 (paraphrased)

license: Public domain (older editions); Hollander 1955 passages are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The warrior-brotherhood's charter: Palnatoki of Fyn founds the fortress Jomsborg on the Wendish coast and gives the brotherhood its law - no man under eighteen, no kin-feuds inside the walls, no flight from an even fight, no word of fear, all spoils in common; the entry-trials at the founding feast, and the fall at Hjorungavag: the fleet beaten by the jarls' weather-magic, the oath-bound brothers dying on the beach in order. The record is the warrior-constitution file.
summary.zh: 戰士兄弟會的憲章：菲英島的帕爾納托基在文德海岸築起約姆斯堡，並為兄弟會立法——未滿十八歲者不得入會，牆內不得涉血仇，勢均之戰不得退逃，不得言懼，戰利品共享；創立宴上的入會考驗，以及赫約倫加瓦格之敗：艦隊被伯爵們的天氣魔法擊潰，受誓約束縛的兄弟們依序在海灘上受刑而死。此記錄是戰士憲法檔案。

canonical_translation: Lee M. Hollander, The Saga of the Jomsvikings, Austin 1955 (paraphrased); Jomsvikinga saga ed. Islenzk Fornrit IX

narrative.en:
The warrior-constitution file holds the Jomsvikings' founding and fall. The founding: Palnatoki's fortress (the Baltic stronghold raised with captured labor on the Wendish shore - the brotherhood's base, its name Jomsborg), and the law: the constitution-clauses - no man under eighteen; no kin-feuds within the walls; no flight from an even fight; no word of fear however wounded; all spoils in common - the oath-register: a band governed by contract, the corpus's clearest institution-portrait of a professional warrior-state.

The recruitment-feats: the entry-trials at the founding feast (Vagn Akason's boy-oath - the twelve-year-old vowing the exploit that wins his seat), and the brotherhood's roster of champions (Bui the Broad, Sigvaldi the wily, Thorkel the Tall). And the fall at Hjorungavag: the fleet sailing against the jarls of Hladir beaten by weather-magic (the jarls' sorcery binding the winds against the raid), the battle on the beach, and the executions in order (the brothers dying by lot in their armor - the oath's last clause kept: no flight from an even fight, the execution-scene as the constitution's final exam).

The record's cultural functions are the warrior-constitution doctrine (the band as a contract-state: law before blood - a professional brotherhood's charter) and the oath-kept-in-death doctrine: the fall's executions are the constitution's proof. In the atlas, the record anchors the warrior-brotherhood family: each a tradition's professional fighting order; the Norse one is distinctive in the law's precedence over kinship.

For the database, this node complements the founding-records: here the brotherhood's charter-file.

The record's reception completes the file: the Jomsvikings' afterlife in Danish and Scandinavian memory (the brotherhood as the north's professional-warrior ideal, its code quoted by later militia-traditions), and the fortress's archaeology (the Wolin ring-fortress candidate, the harbor-works of the Baltic site) - the charter-document's material residue. And the saga's literary craft completes it: the execution-scene's order (the lots drawn, the armor kept, the jokes exchanged at the block) as the corpus's most disciplined death-scene - the constitution's final exam staged as drama.

 The record's saga-structure completes the file: the founding-told-twice (the saga's two halves: the constitution's golden age and the oath)s fatal test at Hjörungavág) read as one argument - the brotherhood)s law proven only by the death that keeps it, the charter-document)s drama-arc documented. And the brotherhood)s legacy completes it: the Jomsviking-name)s afterlife in Scandinavian memory (the professional-warrior ideal quoted by later companies) - the constitution's reach beyond its fortress. The record's treaty-framing completes it: the brotherhood as Scandinavia's mercenary-contract avant la lettre (the oath)s clauses as employment-terms, the spoils-clause as wage-structure) - the warrior-constitution documented as an employment-charter, the corpus)s most modern-sounding institution.

The oath-register: age, kin-feuds, flight, fear, spoils - five clauses
Oath-kept-in-death doctrine: the beach executions as the constitution's final exam
Weather-magic in war: the jarls' sorcery against the raid-fleet

title.en: Gautrekr's Line: The Founding-Tales of Gautreks saga
title.zh: 高特雷克一門：《高特雷克薩迦》的開基故事

region.en: Vestergotland, Sweden (the Gautar's land)
region.zh: 瑞典西約特蘭（高特人的土地）

period: Gautreks saga 14th century (older legendary material); ed. Fornaldar sogur (Rafn 1829); English: Palsson & Edwards 1970

license: Public domain (Rafn 1829); Palsson & Edwards 1970 passages are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The alternate royal-genealogy file: Gauti's mad northward ride (the king riding his hawk off the cliff-edge - the founding-madness), the cliff-kingdom's law (the elders sent over the rock when the milk ran short - the family's sacrifice-economy), Gautrekr's founding of the Gautar-line, and the frame-tales (Starkadr's youth embedded; Ref the trickster's gift-chain). The record is the alternate-founding file.
summary.zh: 另類王族世系檔案：高蒂的瘋狂北騎（追逐獵鷹衝下懸崖——瘋癲開基）、懸崖王國之法（奶水短缺時以老者獻崖——家族的獻祭經濟）、高特雷克開創高特人一脈，以及框架故事（內嵌斯塔卡德的青年篇章；詭計者雷夫的贈禮鏈）。此記錄是另類開基檔案。

canonical_translation: Palsson & Edwards, Gautrek's Saga, London 1970 (paraphrased); Fornaldar sogur ed. Rafn 1829 (public domain)

narrative.en:
The alternate-founding file holds Gautreks saga's charter-tales (norse-starkadr-gautreks holds the Vikar-chapter). Gauti's madness: the king riding north after his hawk till the cliff-edge - the founding-madness: the kingdom begun by a king lost to the chase, who rode into the unknown. The cliff-kingdom's law: the family-cult of the rock (the elders sent over the cliff when the milk ran short - the sacrifice-law that bought the cows' milk: the household's economy as a cult of the crag, the corpus's blackest founding-institution).

Gautrekr's founding: the son's restoration of the line (the mad king's heir founding the Gautar-dynasty properly - the lineage-record of the West-Gautar kings), and the frame-tales complete the file: Starkadr's youth-tales inside the same Gautar-world, and Ref's gift-economy (the trickster-carpenter whose gifts ascend the chain from king to emperor - the saga's own satire on gift-economics, each gift's profit calculated).

The record's cultural functions are the alternate-genealogy doctrine (the Gautar-line as Sweden's second royal house: the founding told in madness where the Ynglinga told it in migration) and the founding-sacrifice doctrine (the cliff-law as the founding's dark institution: the elders' deaths buying the herd's milk). In the atlas, the record anchors the alternate-founding family: each a tradition's second charter; the Gautar one is distinctive in the madness-frame.

For the database, this node complements the Starkadr-record and the Ynglinga-record: here the alternate charter-file.

The record's genre-completes the doctrine: Gautreks saga's frame-tale structure (the comic-dark founding-tales nested inside the champion's biography) is the fornaldarsaga's anthology-mode - several founding-styles in one document: the madness-charter, the sacrifice-law, the gift-economy satire and the hero-tale, each a different institution's origin told in the same frame. And the saga's reception completes it: the Gautar-line's claim echoed in the Swedish royal genealogies - the alternate charter's reach into the historical dynasties.

 The record's Starkadr-junction completes the file: the champion)s biography embedded in the same saga-frame (the Gautar-world shared), so the alternate-charter document doubles as the great champion)s home-context - the founding-tales and the hero-tale one document. And the saga)s black-humor register completes it: the cliff-law and the madness-ride told without horror - the founding)s institutions narrated in the saga-mode)s deadpan, the corpus)s most ironized charter.

 The record's saga-sequence completes the file: the frame)s nested tales (the madness-charter, the sacrifice-law, the Star-cad youth, Ref)s chain and Gautrekr)s marriage-quest) read in sequence as the fornaldarsaga)s anthology - one document sampling four founding-genres, the corpus)s most composite charter-text. And the Gautar-kingdom)s geography completes it: the West-Gautland sites (the cliff, the farms, the market-ways) carrying the saga)s institutions into the modern landscape - the alternate charter)s geography documented.

Founding-sacrifice doctrine: the cliff-law's elders feeding the rock for milk
Alternate-genealogy doctrine: Sweden's second royal house
The gift-economy satirized: Ref's climbing chain of gifts

title.en: The Jarls' Foundings: Lade, Orkney and the Chieftain-Lines
title.zh: 伯爵們的開基：赫拉迪爾、奧克尼與酋長世系

region.en: Hladir (Trondheim) and Orkney (the jarls' seats)
region.zh: 赫拉迪爾（特隆赫姆）與奧克尼（伯爵根據地）

period: Heimskringla (the Hakonar-jarl material); Orkneyinga saga (13th c.); skaldic jarl-lays

source.work: Snorri, Heimskringla; Orkneyinga saga; English: Laing 1844; Palsson & Edwards, Orkneyinga Saga, 1978

license: Public domain (Laing 1844); Palsson & Edwards 1978 passages are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The chieftain-lines' founding-file: the Lade-jarls (Hakon Grjotgardsson raised by Harald Fairhair to rule Trondelag - the king-made jarl), the Orkney-jarls (Rognvald receiving the islands from Harald; the vengeance-line: Torf-Einar's peat-cutting nickname - the jarl named by fuel), and the jarl-doctrine: the jarls as the kings' delegated sovereignty, with title-deeds in verse (the Háleygjatal and Ynglingatal composed for jarls). The record is the jarl-file.
summary.zh: 酋長世系的開基檔案：赫拉迪爾伯爵（金髮哈拉爾拔擢哈康統治特倫德拉格——「王所冊封之伯爵」）、奧克尼伯爵（羅格恩瓦爾德受哈拉爾賜島；復仇世系：托爾夫-埃納爾以挖泥炭得綽號——「以燃料命名之伯爵」），以及伯爵教義：伯爵乃國王授權之主權者，其憑證即頌詩（《赫萊吉亞塔爾》與《英格林塔爾》皆為伯爵而作）。此記錄是伯爵檔案。

canonical_translation: Laing 1844 (public domain); Palsson & Edwards, Orkneyinga Saga, London 1978 (paraphrased)

narrative.en:
The jarl-file holds the chieftain-lines' foundings. The Lade-jarls: Hakon Grjotgardsson's grant (Harald Fairhair raising the Hladir-house to rule Trondelag - the king-made jarl as the north's second power), and the jarl-house's poetry-commission (the Háleygjatal composed for Hakon jarl - the earls claiming the same god-descent as the kings: the jarls' charter in the kings' genre).

The Orkney-jarls: Rognvald's grant (the islands received from Harald after the raid - the earldom as the king's compensation), the vengeance-line (Rognvald killed by Harald's son, avenged by Torf-Einar with the blood-eagle - the record norse-ivar-blood-eagle), and the nickname's provenance (Torf-Einar named for the peat-cutting his brothers scorned - the fuel-named jarl: the court's scorn converted into the dynasty's name). The jarl-doctrine completes the file: the jarls as delegated sovereignty (the earldoms as land-grants with title-deeds in verse - the corpus's theory of sub-royal power: power's second story, told in the same mythic grammar).

The record's cultural functions are the delegated-sovereignty doctrine (the jarl as the king's tenant-in-chief: power descending by grant, legitimated by the same genealogies) and the nickname-provenance doctrine (the jarls named by their trade: the secondary aristocracy's self-made names). In the atlas, the record anchors the chieftain-line family: each a tradition's sub-royal power-file; the Norse one is distinctive in the verse title-deeds.

For the database, this node complements the king-records and the blood-eagle-record: here power's second story.

The record's charter-method completes the file: the jarls' genealogies composed by the same skalds who sang for kings (the Háleygjatal's god-descent claimed for an earl's line), so the delegated power's legitimacy is documented in the same mythic grammar as the kings' - power's second story told in the first story's language. And the earldoms' archaeology completes it: the Orkney earls' burial-mounds and the Lade-hall's site - the chieftain-lines' material register alongside the verse title-deeds.

 The record's Hladir-palace register completes the file: the Lade-jarl)s hall as the north)s second court (the feasts at which the Yule-blót's crisis played out - the record norse-yule-blot-hakon's stage), so the jarl-file)s power is documented at the feast-table as well as in the grant - the second court)s rituals attested beside its title-deeds.

 The record's dynastic-continuity completes the file: the Orkney-line)s centuries (the earls running from Torf-Einar to the Norse twilight) documented as the grant)s durability - the charter)s title-deeds outlasting the kings who issued them. And the Hlaðir-palace)s archaeology completes it: the Lade-site)s hall-remains beneath Trondheim - the second court)s material seat documented beside its verse.

title.en: Norse Founders in Britain: York, Dublin and the Isles' Origin-Tales
title.zh: 不列顛的北歐開創者：約克、都柏林與群島的起源敘事

region.en: York (Jorvik) and Dublin (the Norse west's capitals)
region.zh: 約克（喬維克）與都柏林（西歐北歐之都）

period: The Norse west's founding-traditions (9th-11th c.); sagas and Irish annals; Thing-sites of the Danelaw

source.work: The Norse-west material: the sagas' England-episodes; Irish annals' Norse founding-notices; the Danelaw's place-lore

license: Public domain (annals and sagas in older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The British-Isles founding-file: Jorvik's Norse kingdom (the Great Army's conquest and the coinage - the Norse kings of York striking their own names in silver), Dublin's Norse founding (the longphort at the black pool - Dublin's name itself the founding-document: Dubh Linn), the Isles' jarldoms (the Hebrides' and Man's Norse lines), and the hybrid origin-tales (Norse-Irish marriages founding dynasties - the mixed genealogies the sagas preserve). The record is the Norse-west file.
summary.zh: 不列顛群島開基檔案：喬維克的北歐王國（大軍征服與鑄幣——約克諸北歐王以自身之名鑄幣）、都柏林的北歐開基（「黑池畔船堡」——都柏林之名本身就是開基文獻：Dubh Linn）、群島伯國（赫布里底與曼島的北歐世系），以及混合起源敘事（諾斯—愛爾蘭聯姻開創王朝——薩迦保存的混血世系）。此記錄是西歐北歐檔案。

language: Old Norse / Old Icelandic; Old Irish (annals)
canonical_translation: Sagas per standard editions; annals per standard translations; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The Norse-west file holds the British founding-tales. Jorvik's kingdom: the Great Army's conquest (the record norse-ivar-blood-eagle's vengeance-campaign becoming settlement - the invasion that founded the Danelaw), and the mint (the coinage of the Norse kings of York - the founding documented in coin, the corpus's rarest register). Dublin's founding: the longphort at the black pool (the Irish annals' notices of the ship-fort - Dublin's name itself the founding-document: Dubh Linn, the black pool, the harbor-fort's name surviving into the modern city).

The Isles' jarldoms: the Hebrides and Man (the Norse lines of the sea-kingdoms - the hybrid dynasties: Norse-Irish marriages founding the island-lines, the mixed genealogies the sagas preserve). The hybrid origin-tales complete the file: the west's dynasties founded across languages (the Norse jarls with Irish mothers, the Irish kings with Norse forebears - the origin-stories told in both tongues), and the Thing-sites of the Danelaw (the assembly-places of the settlers - the record norse-althing-founding's institution exported). The record's cultural functions are the colonial-founding doctrine (the Norse west's capitals founded by conquest and intermarriage - the origin-stories as treaty-documents) and the hybrid-genealogy doctrine: the dynasties' mixed descent as their charter. In the atlas, the record anchors the colonial-founding family: each a tradition's overseas origin-file; the Norse-west one is distinctive in the coinage.

For the database, this node extends the founding-corpus to the British Isles: the origin-stories of the Danelaw and the sea-kingdoms.

The record's source-criticism completes the file: the annals' notices and the sagas' England-episodes do not always agree (the saga-kings' careers inflated against the annals' spare lines), so the founding-file's method is the cross-check - each charter read against its neighbor's witness, the coinage and the place-names as the arbiters. And the Danelaw's persistence completes it: the law-terms and place-names of the Five Boroughs (the 'gate' suffixes, the Danish wapentakes) surviving into English law - the founding-document's longest echo, written in the modern map.

 The record's coinage-cabinet completes the file: the York pennies bearing the Norse kings' names (the raven-mint's output documented in silver), the founding's hardest evidence - the origin-stories) claims checked against the metal they struck. And the place-name register completes it: the Danelaw's Norse suffixes (the -by, -thorpe, -thwaite names numbering in the thousands) as the settlement)s longest document, the founding-tales) claims readable on the modern map.

 The record's assembly-export completes it: the Danelaw)s thing-sites documented (the courts and wapentakes of the Five Boroughs), the Althing-institution)s overseas branch - the founding-tales) institutions as durable as their dynasties, the Norse-west)s charter running in law as well as coin.

title.en: Variants of the Blót: From Household Hearth to High-Feast
title.zh: 布洛特祭的變體：從家灶到高宴

region.en: Farms and temples of Scandinavia (symbolic pin at Gamla Uppsala, Sweden)
region.zh: 斯堪的納維亞的農莊與神廟（象徵性定位於瑞典舊烏普薩拉）

period: Sagas and law-codes 13th-14th c. (older practice); the Grágás and Gulathing-law clauses; Hakonar saga's feast-description

source.work: Hakonar saga goda (the feast-liturgy); Gragas and the Gulathing-law (the blót-clauses); Egils saga and Hrafnkels saga (household-blót episodes)

license: Public domain (Laing 1844); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The blót's practice-variants collected: the scale-register (the household blót at the farm's hall - the farmer's rite with ale and horse-flesh; the district-blót at the hof; the national high-feast at Uppsala), the seasonal-register (the three annual feasts: midwinter, spring sigrblót, autumn), the liturgical register (the hammer-sign over horn and cauldron - the hallowing-gesture documented), and the legal register (the law-codes' clauses: feast obligations and fines for absence - the rite as statute). The record is the sacrifice-practice file.
summary.zh: 布洛特祭的實踐變體全集：規模層級（農家大廳的家祭——以麥酒與馬肉行祭；神廟地區祭；烏普薩拉全國高宴）、季節層級（三大年度祭：仲冬祭、春季勝利祭、秋季祭）、儀軌層級（角杯與鍋上的雷錘之印——有據可查的祝聖手勢），以及法律層級（法典條款：祭宴義務與缺席罰款——祭儀即法令）。此記錄是獻祭實踐檔案。

canonical_translation: Laing 1844 (public domain); Grágás ed. Finsen 1852 (public domain); paraphrase

narrative.en:
The sacrifice-practice file holds the blót's variants. The scale-register: the household-blót (the farmer's own rite - the sagas' farm-sacrifices: ale and horse-flesh at the private hall; the record norse-nine-year-blot's national feast at the scale's top), the district-blót at the hof (the goði's feast for the free farmers - the record norse-thorolf-mostarskegg's district-institution), and the legal register: the law-codes' feast-obligations (the fines for absence from the district-blót - the rite as statute: attendance legally required, the corpus's sacrifice-law).

The seasonal-register: the three annual feasts (Snorri's triad: the midwinter blót for crops and peace, the spring sigrblót for victory, and the autumn-blót for the winter's stores - the calendar-of-sacrifice: the year's rhythm as the rite's structure). The liturgical register: the hallowing-gesture (the hammer-sign over horn and cauldron - the Hakon-chapter's documented gesture: the Christian king's cross mistaken for it, the record norse-yule-blot-hakon), the cup-circles by god, and the meat's distribution (the sacrificial flesh boiled in the cauldrons and eaten by the feasters - the sacrifice as a meal: the communion-structure of the blót).

The record's cultural functions are the practice-variant doctrine (the blót's scales and seasons as one institution's registers - the corpus's fullest ritual-practice documentation) and the sacrifice-as-meal doctrine (the god fed and the people fed in one act: the communion-grammar). In the atlas, the record anchors the sacrifice-practice family: each a tradition's rite documented at multiple scales; the Norse one is distinctive in the legal obligation.

For the database, this node complements the temple-records and the feast-records: here the practice-file runs whole.

The record's legal register completes the file: the law-codes' conversion-era clauses (the Gulathing-law's amended blót-clauses outlawing the private sacrifice, the fines transformed into penalties) document the rite's end as statute - the practice-file's arc running from obligation to prohibition, the blót's life documented from household hearth to banned rite. And the liturgical inventory completes the corpus: the hammer-sign, the cup-circles, the meat-boilers and the sprinkling-twigs - the full equipment-list of the north's sacrifice, documented across saga and law.

 The record's scale-economics completes the file: the three registers' costs documented (the farmer)s own beast at the hearth; the goði)s feast shared by the district; the king)s ninefold offering at Uppsala) - the sacrifice)s burden graded by scale, the rite)s social distribution visible in who paid. And the meal)s theology completes it: the gods) share and the people)s share from the same carcass - the communion-structure that made the blót both worship and dinner, documented in the feast-liturgy)s own clauses.

title.en: Building the Hof: The Temple's Architecture and Its Origin-Tales
title.zh: 建造神廟：廟宇建築及其起源故事

The record is the sacred-architecture file.

narrative.en:
The sacred-architecture file holds the hof's documented layout. The Kjalnesinga temple's plan (the corpus's fullest hof-description): 'a? - 'temple? - 'with? - 'doors? - 'on? - 'three? - sides? - 'the? - 'the? - - the central hall with the idol-platform raised like an altar, the ring (the oath-arm-ring of twenty ounces) on the platform, the bowl for the sacrifice-blood, and the sprinkling-twigs (the blood asperged over walls, idols and the assembled - the liturgy's equipment documented in architecture).

The pillar-doctrine: the high-seat pillars as the temple's core (the gods carved in the shoulder-wood - the record norse-ingolf-iceland's drift-rite depends on the pillar's sanctity: the temple's own furniture as the settler's compass). The site-choice doctrine completes the file: the hofs sited at landings and thing-steads (temple, market and court as one landscape - the record norse-thorolf-mostarskegg's Thorsnes: the headland's temple, assembly and holy ground as one estate), and the archaeology's corroboration (the Hofstadir excavation's hall-and-bowls structure matching the sagas' descriptions - the hof documented in dirt as well as prose).

The record's cultural functions are the temple-architecture doctrine (the hof as hall-plus-altar: the god housed as a chieftain is housed - the domestic-architecture theory of the temple) and the landscape-institution doctrine (temple, court and market as one estate's offices). In the atlas, the record anchors the sacred-architecture family: each a tradition's temple-form documented; the Norse one is distinctive in the blood-liturgy's equipment.

For the database, this node complements the temple-records (Uppsala, Thorsnes, Hrafnkel's A-dale): here the architecture-file.

The record's archaeology completes the doctrine: the Hofstadir excavation's long hall with its door-alignment and the bear-tooth? - the? - ritual deposits, and the Uppakra temple-complex in Skane (the stratified cult-site with the gold? - - the hof's Scandinavian version), each matching the sagas' descriptions closely enough to confirm the architecture-file's reliability. And the landscape-institution completes it: the hofs sited at landings and courts, so the temple's geography is the settlement's own map - the god's house at the center of the district's business.

 The record's orientation-lore completes the file: the hofs) alignments documented (the doorways and the idol-platform)s placement relative to sun and road), the temple-form)s siting-grammar debated from the excavations - the architecture)s cosmology argued from dirt. And the pillar)s afterlife completes it: the high-seat pillars) carving-tradition continuing in the converted halls (the Christian regalia hung where the gods) images stood) - the temple-form)s persistence inside the church.

 The record's household-temple debate completes it: the scholars) question whether the hof was a dedicated temple or a chieftain)s hall used for cult - the architecture-file)s open reading, the evidence (the long-hall plans with cult-furniture) supporting both, the hof)s nature as the corpus)s own architectural question.

title.en: The Sacrificial Animals: Boar, Horse and Stag in Myth and Rite
title.zh: 祭祀動物：神話與儀式中的豬、馬與鹿

region.zh: 北方的神廟與宴席（象徵性定位於瑞典舊烏普薩拉）

summary.en: The sacrificial animals' symbolism-file: the boar (Freyr's Gullinbursti with golden bristles; the Yule-boar's oath-curse 'the? - 'boar? - 'that? - 'carries? - 'the? - 'oath? - - the sonatorrek? - the? - atonement-boar: the oath-animal), the horse (the north's most loaded sacrifice: Adam's horse-heads in the grove; the Hakon-chapter's horse-liver test; the horse-flesh as apostasy's mark in canon law), the stag and the swan (Grimnismal's stag Eikthyrnir and the swan-maidens), and the nine-males doctrine (Adam's clause: nine of every male species - the arithmetic of the altar). The record is the animal-symbolism file.
summary.zh: 祭祀動物象徵檔案：豬（弗雷的金鬃古林伯斯蒂；耶誕祭豬之宣誓——「負誓之豬」：和解的誓願動物）、馬（北方最敏感的祭牲：亞當所載懸於聖林之馬首；哈康篇章的馬肝之試；教會法中食馬肉即叛教之標記）、鹿與天鵝（《格里姆尼爾之歌》的鹿艾克特尼爾與天鵝少女），以及九牲學說（亞當條款：每種雄牲九頭——祭壇的算術）。此記錄是動物象徵檔案。

language: Old Norse / Old Icelandic; Latin (Adam of Bremen)
canonical_translation: Laing 1844; Bellows 1923 (public domain); Adam per Tschan 1959 (paraphrased)

narrative.en:
The animal-symbolism file holds the sacrificial species' offices. The boar: Freyr's own (Gullinbursti with golden bristles lighting the dark - the record norse-mjolnir-forging's forge-gift; the Yule-boar's oath-curse: the atonement-boar 'on? - 'whose? - 'bristles? - 'the? - 'oaths? - 'were? - sworn? - - the oath-animal documented in the sagas' sonatorrek-clauses), the boar as the fertility-god's beast and the feast's oath-bearer.

The horse: the north's most loaded sacrifice (Adam's horse-heads hanging in the sacred grove - the record norse-uppsala-temple's grove-registry; the Hakon-chapter's horse-liver test: the king's negotiated minimum - the record norse-yule-blot-hakon; and the canon-law clause: horse-flesh as apostasy's mark - the meat that unmade Christians), the horse as the chieftain's burial-companion (the horse-graves of the archaeology) and the taboo's center. The stag and the swan: Grimnismal's stag Eikthyrnir (the antlered source of the world's rivers - the cosmological beast on Valhalla's roof) and the swan-maidens (the valkyries' bird-form - the record norse-helgi-hjalmars' swan-brides).

The nine-males doctrine completes the file: Adam's clause (nine of every male species offered, their bodies in the grove - the altar's arithmetic: male animals and men counted in nines, the number's ritual force). The record's cultural functions are the species-symbolism doctrine (each animal an office: the boar for oaths and plenty, the horse for kingship and taboo, the stag for the cosmos) and the meal-sacrifice doctrine (the animals eaten by the worshippers - the communion-structure the record norse-blot-rites-forms documents). In the atlas, the record anchors the sacrificial-animal family: each a tradition's altar-species with meanings; the Norse one is distinctive in the horse-taboo.

For the database, this node contextualizes the sacrifice-records: here the animals' file.

The record's comparative frame completes the file: the altar-species across traditions (the Chinese oxen of the ancestral rites, the Greek hecatombs, the Aztec? - the frame is species-as-office) - and the Norse one is distinctive in the horse: the animal whose sacrifice the converted law banned first, the taboo's survival documented in the Christian-era penalties on horse-eating. And the meal-doctrine completes the rite: the animals were eaten by the worshippers after the gods' portion - the communion-structure documented in the feast-liturgy, the sacrifice as a shared meal rather than a burnt offering.

 The record's feast-grammar completes the file: the sacrificial meals) shared structure (the gods) portion at the altar, the worshippers) portion in the cauldrons) documented across the Uppsala-grove)s exceptions (the bodies hanging rather than eaten - the grove-sacrifice)s different economy, offering without communion). And the nine's symbolism completes it: the number)s ritual force across the corpus (nine nights on the tree, nine mothers of Heimdall, nine worlds) - the altar)s arithmetic matching the cosmology)s own count.
