passages.text: So the kings came out with the best fighters of the Tuatha de Danaan to Tailltin, and the Sons of the Gael, remembering the death of Ith, fell on them in great anger. For a while neither side got the better, but at the last the Gael broke through the army of the Men of Dea and put them to the rout. The three kings and the three queens of Ireland, Eriu and Fodhla and Banba, were killed in the battle, and the Tuatha de Danaan, seeing their leaders dead, fell back in disorder and never brought their army together again, but gave up the country to the Gael. The sons of Miled divided the provinces between them; Heber took Munster, Heremon Leinster and Connacht, and Ulster fell to Eimhir, son of Ir, from whom, after nine hundred years at Emain Macha, came Fergus mac Rogh and Conall Cearnach of the Red Branch.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book III, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是諸王率領達努神族最精銳的戰士來到塔爾廷，蓋爾人之子記起伊斯的死，滿懷怒火向他們撲去。一時之間雙方難分高下，但最後蓋爾人突破了達努神族的軍隊，將他們擊潰。愛爾蘭的三位君王與三位女王——埃里烏、福德拉與班巴——都在這場戰役中喪命，達努神族見首領已死，便潰亂退卻，再也沒能重整軍隊，而是把這片土地讓給了蓋爾人。米爾的兒子們瓜分了各省；希伯取了芒斯特，赫里蒙取了倫斯特與康諾特，阿爾斯特則歸於伊爾之子埃米爾，九百年後在埃文馬哈，出自他這一脈的有紅枝團的弗格斯·麥克羅與康納爾·基爾納赫。

title.en: Bodb Dearg is Elected King of the Sidhe
title.zh: 波德·迪爾格被立為仙族之王

region.en: Sidhe Femen, Slieve Bernagh, Co. Clare, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭克萊爾郡貝爾納赫山仙丘菲曼（象徵定位）

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. I, eBook #14465

summary.en: After their defeat, the Tuatha de Danaan refuse the sway of the sons of Miled; Manannan settles them under hidden walls in the beautiful hills and makes the Feast of Age with Goibniu's ale and pigs that renew themselves. They ask for one king, and Bodb Dearg, eldest son of the Dagda, is chosen — three royal brothers later win wives from Midhir's daughters by fasting on the Sidhe.
summary.zh: 都瑟德那恩敗後不受蓋爾人之統轄，瑪那南遂擇美丘以隱壁居之，並設長生宴——飲哥伊布努之酒，食不盡之豬。族人請立一王，眾推達格達長子波德·迪爾格為王；後三王族兄弟絕食於仙丘，得娶米德之女為妻。

sensitivity.note: Coordinates are a symbolic pin at Sidhe Femen's traditional location near Slieve Bernagh; the settlement of the gods under 'hidden walls' is a hollow-hills (síd) charter myth. The fasting-on-a-people motif (troscud) is an Irish legal remedy for enforcing a claim.

passages.text: When the Tuatha de Danaan were beaten, they would not go under the sway of the sons of Miled, but went away by themselves. Manannan son of Lir, who understood all enchantments, chose out the most beautiful of the hills and valleys of Ireland for them to settle in, and put hidden walls about them that no man could see through, but they themselves could see through them and pass through them. He made the Feast of Age for them, and what they drank at it was the ale of Goibniu the Smith, that kept whoever tasted it from age and from sickness and from death; and for food he gave them his own swine, that though they were killed and eaten one day would be alive again the next.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 達努神族戰敗之後，不願受米爾之子們的統治，便自行離去。通曉一切法術的利爾之子馬納南，為他們在愛爾蘭的丘陵與山谷中挑選了最美的地方供他們定居，並在四周設下隱藏的牆垣，無人能看透，而他們自己卻能看透並穿行其中。他為他們設下「不老之宴」，宴上所飲的是鐵匠戈伊布紐的麥酒，凡嘗過的人都不會衰老、不會生病、不會死亡；至於食物，他把自己養的豬賜給他們，那些豬雖在一日被宰殺吃掉，次日又會復活。

passages.text: After a while they said: "It would be better for us one king to be over us." The men that had the best chance were Bodb Dearg son of the Dagda, Ilbrech of Ess Ruadh, Lir of Sidhe Fionnachaidh, Midhir the Proud of Bri Leith, and Angus Og; but Angus did not covet the kingship. So the chief men agreed to give the kingship to Bodb Dearg, for the sake of his father and because he was the eldest among the children of the Dagda.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 過了一陣子，他們說：「我們頭上有一位國王，對我們會更好。」最有機會的人選是達格達之子博德·德爾格、埃斯魯阿德的伊爾布雷赫、西德·菲奧納海德的利爾、布里萊斯的驕傲的米希爾，以及小安格斯；但安格斯並不貪圖王位。於是首領們同意把王位交給博德·德爾格，一來是看在他們父親的份上，二來因為他是達格達子嗣中年紀最長的。

passages.text: Three sons of Lugaidh Menn, king of Ireland — Eochaid, Fiacha, and Ruide — were refused any land by their father till they would win it for themselves. They went and sat down on the green of Brugh na Boinn and fasted there on the Tuatha de Danaan. Bodb Dearg came out to them, and Midhir of the Yellow Hair gave counsel: "Let us give a wife to every one of these three men, for it is from a wife that good or bad fortune comes." Midhir's three daughters were given to them, and Bodb promised each king's son three times fifty ounces of red gold and suits of clothing of all colours. Gifts followed from all the Sidhe: a horn and a vat of turning wine, three times fifty swords of Lir, a rath with bright sunny houses from Angus Og, a woman-cook whose store filled itself, and a musician whose playing would make men sleep through childbirth and wounding. When their lifetime was over they went back to the Tuatha de Danaan, for they belonged to them through their wives.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 愛爾蘭國王盧蓋德·門恩的三個兒子——埃奧凱德、菲亞哈和魯伊德——被父親拒絕給予任何土地，除非他們自己去贏得。他們前去坐在布魯格納博因的草地上，在那裡對圖哈德·達·達南族絕食。博德·德爾格出來見他們，金髮的米希爾獻策道：「讓我們給這三個人每人一個妻子吧，因為無論好運還是壞運，都是從妻子而來的。」米希爾的三個女兒被許配給了他們，博德還許諾給每位國王之子三倍五十盎司的赤金，以及各色各樣的成套衣物。隨後眾西德都送來了禮物：一隻號角和一桶會轉化的酒、利爾的三倍五十把劍、小安格斯送的一座有著明亮向陽房屋的堡壘、一位倉庫會自行填滿的女廚師，以及一位演奏起來能讓人在分娩和受傷時都睡著的樂師。當他們的壽數盡了，他們便回到圖哈德·達·達南族那裡，因為透過他們的妻子，他們本就屬於那一族。

title.en: Angus Og Wins Brugh na Boinne by a Day and a Night
title.zh: 安古斯·奧格以一日一夜之約奪得博因墓丘

region.en: Brugh na Boinne (Newgrange), Co. Meath, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭米斯郡博因墓丘（紐格蘭治）

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. II, eBook #14465

summary.en: The Dagda keeps his household at Brugh na Boinne with its cooking oven of eighteen wheels and its marvels. Manannan teaches Angus to ask his father for the Brugh for only a day and a night; when the Dagda asks it back, Angus answers that life itself is made of a day and a night following one another, so the Brugh is his for ever, and the Dagda goes away without revenge.
summary.zh: 達格達居博因墓丘，家中藏十八輪奇灶與諸異寶。瑪那南教安古斯向父親只請借墓丘一日一夜；達格達索還時，安古斯答曰：生命本身即由日與夜相續而成，故墓丘永屬於己。達格達不報復，舉家遷離。

sensitivity.note: The day-and-a-night bargain is the classic etiological myth of Newgrange (Brugh na Boinne) as Angus's dwelling; a myth of legalistic word-play transferring divine property. Coordinates are the Newgrange monument.

passages.text: It was at Brugh na Boinne the Dagda, the Red Man of all Knowledge, had his house, and the most noticeable things in it were the Hall of the Morrigu and the Bed of the Dagda; and there was a little hill called the Comb and the Casket of the Dagda's wife, and the Hill of Dabilla, the little hound belonging to Boann, and the Valley of the Mata, the Sea-Turtle that could suck down a man in armour. The Dagda had a cooking oven made by Druimne that lay down with the cinders and rose to the height of the roof with the flame, turning as quick as a stream, with three times nine spits and three times nine pots. He made a great vat for his daughter Ainge that would not lose a drop during the ebb-tide, and Corann the harper, harper to the Dagda's son Diancecht, once called a swine of Debrann with his harping so well that the champions of Connacht chased it through lake and wood; for doing his harping so well the Dagda gave Corann a great tract of land.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 達格達，即無所不知的紅人，他的居所就在布魯格納博因，其中最引人注目的東西是莫里根的廳堂和達格達的床榻；還有一座名叫「梳子」的小丘，以及達格達之妻的「首飾盒」，還有達比拉之丘——那是波安的小獵犬，以及馬塔之谷——那是一隻能將披甲之人吸下去的巨龜。達格達有一座由德魯伊姆內所造的烹飪爐灶，它與炭渣一同伏下，又隨著火焰升到屋頂的高度，轉動得如溪流一般迅速，配有三倍九根烤肉叉和三倍九口鍋。他為女兒安格造了一口大缸，在退潮時也不會漏掉一滴；而豎琴師科蘭——達格達之子迪安凱赫特的豎琴師——曾以他的琴藝如此出色地召喚出德布蘭的一頭豬，以至於康諾特的勇士們追著那頭豬穿湖越林；由於他彈得如此出色，達格達賜給科蘭一大片土地。

passages.text: But however great a house the Dagda had, Angus got it away from him in the end, through the help of Manannan son of Lir. Manannan bade him ask his father for the Brugh for the length of a day and a night, for he by his art would take away the Dagda's power of refusing. So Angus asked for the Brugh, and his father gave it to him for a day and a night. But when the Dagda asked it back again, Angus said it had been given to him for ever, for the whole of life and time is made up of a day and a night, one following after the other. The Dagda went away with his household, for Manannan had put an enchantment on them all, and Angus stopped in Brugh na Boinne — some say he is there to this day, with the hidden walls about him, drinking Goibniu's ale and eating the pigs that never fail.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 然而，無論達格達的宅邸多麼宏大，安格斯最終還是藉助利爾之子馬納南之力把它從他手中奪走了。馬納南吩咐他向父親索要布魯格，為期一日一夜，因為他憑自己的法術能除去達格達拒絕的力量。於是安格斯索要布魯格，他父親便把它給了他，為期一日一夜。但當達格達再要討回時，安格斯說它已被永遠賜給了他，因為整個生命與時間正是由一日一夜、彼此相繼而成的。達格達帶著他的家眷離去了，因為馬納南已對他們全體施了魔法，而安格斯則留在了布魯格納博因——有人說他至今仍在那裡，隱形的牆垣環繞著他，喝著戈伊布紐的麥酒，吃著那永不匱乏的豬。

title.en: The Dagda's Son and the Hill of Sighs
title.zh: 達格達之子之死與嘆息丘

region.en: Shore of Loch Feabhail, Co. Sligo, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭斯利戈郡費巴爾湖畔（象徵定位）

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. II, eBook #14465

summary.en: Corrgenn of Connacht, visiting the Dagda, believes wrongly that his wife has been unfaithful with Aedh, the Dagda's son, and kills the young man before his father's face. The Dagda spares Corrgenn's life but loads him with the body, to carry it until he finds a stone exactly its fit for a grave; when the burial is done Corrgenn drops dead, and the Dagda's builders raise a rath called the Hill of Sighs, watered by the god's tears of blood.
summary.zh: 康諾特人科爾根造訪達格達，疑其妻與達格達之子艾德有私，怒而當父之面殺之。達格達不殺科爾根，卻令其背屍而行，直至尋得長寬恰合之石為墓；葬畢科爾根力竭而亡。達格達命工匠築丘環墓，名為嘆息丘，丘上灑有神之泣血。

sensitivity.note: A justice-myth: the Dagda's judgment weighs guilt rather than blood-revenge, yet the penance kills the offender — an etiology of a cairn ('Hill of Aileac', Hill of Sighs). Pin placed symbolically at the traditional Loch Feabhail (Lough Foyle area); otherworldly legal scene, no historical claim.

passages.text: It chanced one time Corrgenn, a great man of Connacht, came to visit the Dagda, and his wife along with him. While they were there, Corrgenn got it in his mind that there was something not right going on between his wife and Aedh, one of the sons of the Dagda. Great jealousy and anger came on him, and he struck at the young man and killed him before his father's face. Every one thought the Dagda would take Corrgenn's life then and there in revenge for his son. But he would not, for he said that if his son was guilty, there was no blame to be put on Corrgenn for doing what he did.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一次，康諾特的一位大人物科爾根前來拜訪達格達，他的妻子也一同前來。他們在那裡的時候，科爾根心裡起了疑，覺得他的妻子和達格達的一個兒子埃德之間有些不對勁。強烈的嫉妒和憤怒湧上心頭，他朝那年輕人打去，當著他父親的面把他殺死了。人人都以為達格達會當場取科爾根的性命，為兒子報仇。但他沒有這樣做，因為他說，如果他的兒子有罪，那麼科爾根做了他所做的事，就不該受到責備。

passages.text: He spared Corrgenn's life, but the punishment he put on him was to take the dead body of the young man on his back, and never to lay it down till he would find a stone that would be its very fit in length and breadth, to make a gravestone for him. Corrgenn travelled long before he found such a stone at last, on the shore of Loch Feabhail; he raised it, brought it up, dug a grave, and buried the Dagda's son, giving many an Ochone as he put the stone over him — and when he had done that, he was spent and dropped dead there and then. The Dagda brought his two builders, Garbhan and Imheall, and bade them build a rath round the grave, till the work was finished and the top of the house closed with a slab. The place was called the Hill of Aileac, the Hill of Sighs and of a Stone, for it was tears of blood the Dagda shed on account of the death of his son.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他饒了科爾根的性命，但施加於他的懲罰是：把這年輕人的屍體背在背上，永不放下，直到他找到一塊長寬都恰好合宜的石頭，為他做一塊墓碑。科爾根走了很久，最後終於在費巴爾湖的岸邊找到了這樣一塊石頭；他把它撬起，搬了上來，挖了一個墳墓，埋葬了達格達的兒子，在把石頭蓋在他身上時發出了許多聲「奧洪」的哀嘆——做完這件事後，他筋疲力盡，當場倒地而死。達格達帶來了他的兩位工匠加爾班和伊姆赫爾，吩咐他們在墳墓周圍建一座堡壘，直到工程完成，並用一塊石板封住屋頂。這個地方被稱為艾萊阿克之丘，即嘆息與石頭之丘，因為達格達為他兒子的死流下的是血淚。

title.en: Angus Og the Disturber and his Kiss-Birds
title.zh: 擾世者安古斯·奧格與其吻鳥

region.en: Cnoc Aine (Knockainey), Co. Limerick, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭利默里克郡克諾克艾尼山

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. III, eBook #14465

summary.en: Angus Og, son of the Dagda, shows himself on earth in youth and beauty: Cormac sees him with a silver harp and two playing birds; four of his kisses go about as birds crying after young men; plough teams flee in terror before him. He troubles lovers and households — Derbrenn's fosterlings are spelled into swine and hunted to a mound of heads — and at last sets his love on Caer of Connacht.
summary.zh: 達格達之子安古斯·奧格時而下凡顯形：科馬克見其持銀豎琴、上有雙鳥彈奏；其四吻化鳥，繞少年啼喚「來吧」「我去了」；犁隊牲畜見之皆奔逃。德布蓮的六名養子女被咒化豬，遭獵殺而葬於獵丘。安古斯終愛上康諾特之凱爾。

sensitivity.note: Angus Og is the Irish love-god (Midir's counterpart); 'the Frightener/Disturber' is his fixed epithet, and the kiss-birds a love-charm etiology. Coordinates at Cnoc Aine, one of his resorts in the telling.

passages.text: It was a long time after the coming of the Gael that Angus Og was seen by Cormac, King of Teamhair, who told how a very comely young man appeared in his Hall of Judgment, with ornaments of gold on his dress and a silver harp with strings of red gold, the sound of its strings sweeter than all music under the sky; and over the harp two birds that seemed to be playing on it. He sat beside Cormac pleasantly, played his sweet music, and foretold things that put drunkenness on the king's wits. The birds that used to be with Angus were four of his kisses turned into birds, coming about the young men of Ireland and crying after them — "Come, come," two of them would say, and "I go, I go," the other two, and it was hard to get free of them. Even in his youth Angus was called the Frightener, the Disturber, for the plough teams of the world and every sort of cattle used by men would make away in terror before him.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 蓋爾人到來之後過了很久，Teamhair（塔拉）之王科馬克見到了安格斯·奧格（Angus Og）；科馬克講述道，一位非常俊美的年輕人出現在他的審判廳中，衣著上飾有黃金飾物，手持一把銀豎琴，琴弦以赤金製成，其弦聲比天下所有音樂都更甜美；豎琴上方有兩隻鳥，彷彿正在彈奏它。他愉快地坐在科馬克身旁，彈奏甜美的音樂，並預言了一些使國王心神如醉之事。從前伴隨安格斯的那些鳥，是他的四個吻所化成的鳥，它們圍繞愛爾蘭的年輕人飛翔，在他們身後啼叫——其中兩隻會說「來吧，來吧」，另外兩隻則說「我去了，我去了」，而要擺脫它們是很難的。安格斯甚至在年少時就被稱為「驚嚇者」、「擾亂者」，因為世上的犁隊以及人們所使用的各種牲畜，都會在他面前驚恐地逃散。

passages.text: Derbrenn, Eochaid Fedlech's daughter, was loved by Angus, and she had six fosterlings, three boys and three girls; but Dalb Garb the Rough, mother of the boys, made a spell from a gathering of the nuts of Caill Ochuid that turned them into swine. Angus gave them into the care of Buichet the Hospitaller of Leinster, but at the end of a year a longing came on Buichet's wife to eat the flesh of one of them, and she gathered a hundred armed men and a hundred hounds to take them. The pigs made away to Brugh na Boinn and asked Angus's help, but he could give none till they had shaken the Tree of Tarbga and eaten the salmon of Inver Umaill. Maeve gathered the men of Connacht to hunt them, and they all fell but one; their heads were put in a mound, and it got the name of Duma Selga, the Mound of the Hunting. And it was in the time of Maeve that Angus set his love on Caer of the Province of Connacht and brought her away to Brugh na Boinne.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: Eochaid Fedlech 的女兒德爾布倫（Derbrenn）被安格斯所愛，她有六個養子女，三個男孩和三個女孩；但男孩們的母親、粗野的達爾布·加爾布（Dalb Garb the Rough）用從 Caill Ochuid 採集來的堅果施了一道咒語，把他們變成了豬。安格斯把他們交給倫斯特的款待者布伊赫特（Buichet）照料，但一年之後，布伊赫特的妻子生出了想吃其中一隻豬肉的慾望，她聚集了一百名武裝人員和一百隻獵犬去捕捉它們。那些豬逃到 Brugh na Boinn（博因河畔的宮殿），請求安格斯相助，但安格斯無法相助，除非它們搖動 Tarbga 之樹並吃掉 Inver Umaill 的鮭魚。梅芙（Maeve）聚集康諾特的人們去獵捕它們，他們全都倒下了，只有一人倖存；他們的頭被放入一座土丘，這土丘因此得名 Duma Selga，即「狩獵之丘」。正是在梅芙的時代，安格斯愛上了康諾特省的凱爾（Caer），並把她帶到了 Brugh na Boinne。

title.en: The Morrigu and Mechi of the Three Serpent-Hearts
title.zh: 摩里岡與三蛇心之梅奇

region.en: Magh Luathad (Plain of Ashes), Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭灰燼平原（象徵定位）

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. IV, eBook #14465

summary.en: The Morrigu, the Great Queen, kept in Teamhair a cooking-spit holding raw, dressed, and buttered food at once — the pattern of the outlaws' nine-ribbed spit. Her son Mechi, whose three hearts held the shapes of three serpents, is killed by Mac Cecht before the serpents can grow; the hearts are burned to ashes on the Plain of Ashes, and the boiling stream kills every creature in it. Ever after she meddles in Ireland's battles — rousing the boy Cuchulain, taking Odras's cow, and turning Odras into a pool of water.
summary.zh: 大后摩里岡居塔拉時，有一奇妙炙叉，可同時炙生肉、熟肉與奶油。其子梅奇三心中藏三蛇形；若非馬克·克奇特及早殺之，蛇將長成而害愛爾蘭。三心被焚於灰燼平原，灰燼投入溪流，滾水使水中生物盡死。其後摩里岡屢屢干預人間戰事——喚醒少年庫丘林，奪奧德拉斯之牛，並將其化為池水。

sensitivity.note: Morrigan material is mythic; the serpent-hearts episode is a destruction-of-monster etiology tagged 'world-serpent' interpretively. Odras turned to a pool is a place-myth of the river west of Slieve Buane.

passages.text: As to the Morrigu, the Great Queen, the Crow of Battle, she had in Teamhair a great cooking-spit that held three sorts of food at the one time: a piece of raw meat, and a piece of dressed meat, and a piece of butter; and the raw was dressed, and the dressed was not burned, and the butter did not melt. Nine outlaws once asked her for a spit to be made for themselves; it had nine ribs, and every outlaw carried a rib wherever he went till they all met at the close of day, and the spit could be raised to a man's height or set no higher than a fist over the fire without breaking. Mechi, the son the Morrigu had, was killed by Mac Cecht on Magh Mechi; three hearts he had, and they had the shapes of three serpents through them. If Mechi had not met his death, those serpents would have grown, and what they left alive in Ireland would have wasted away.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 至於莫里根（Morrigu），即「偉大的女王」、「戰鬥的烏鴉」，她在 Teamhair 有一根巨大的烹飪叉，一次能盛放三種食物：一塊生肉、一塊熟肉和一塊黃油；而生肉被煮熟了，熟肉沒有燒焦，黃油也沒有融化。有一次，九個亡命之徒請她為他們自己製作一根叉；那叉有九根肋條，每個亡命之徒無論走到哪裡都帶著一根肋條，直到他們在日暮時分全部會合，而那叉可以被舉到一人之高，也可以被架在火上不超過一拳之高，而不會折斷。莫里根所生的兒子梅希（Mechi）在 Magh Mechi 被 Mac Cecht 殺死；他有三顆心，每顆心中都貫穿著一條蛇的形狀。如果梅希沒有喪命，那些蛇就會長大，而它們在愛爾蘭所留下的活物都會被耗盡。

passages.text: Mac Cecht burned the three hearts on Magh Luathad, the Plain of Ashes, and threw the ashes into the stream; and the rushing water of the stream stopped and boiled up, and every creature in it died. The Morrigu used often to be meddling in Ireland in Cuchulain's time, stirring up wars and quarrels. It was she came and roused up Cuchulain one time when he was but a lad, near giving in to some enchantment: "There is not the making of a hero in you," she said, "and you lying there under the feet of shadows" — and Cuchulain rose and struck off the head of a shadow with his hurling stick. One time she brought away a cow from Odras, of the household of the cow-chief of Cormac, going after her husband with cattle; Odras followed her to the Cave of Cruachan till sleep fell on her in the oak-wood of Falga, and the Morrigu awoke her and sang spells over her, and made of her a pool of water that went to the river that flows to the west of Slieve Buane.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: Mac Cecht 在 Magh Luathad，即「灰燼之平原」，燒掉了那三顆心，並把灰燼扔進溪流中；溪流奔騰的水停了下來並沸騰起來，其中的每一個生物都死了。在庫丘林（Cuchulain）的時代，莫里根常常在愛爾蘭插手干預，挑起戰爭和爭鬥。有一次，當庫丘林還只是個少年、幾乎要向某種魔法屈服時，正是她前來喚醒了他：「你身上沒有成為英雄的素質，」她說，「而你卻躺在那裡，在陰影的腳下」——於是庫丘林起身，用他的曲棍球棒砍下了一個陰影的頭。有一次，她從 Odras 那裡帶走了一頭牛，Odras 是科馬克牛群首領的家戶中人，她帶著牛群去追她的丈夫；Odras 追她追到 Cruachan 之洞，直到睡意降臨在 Falga 的橡樹林中，莫里根喚醒了她，對她唱起咒語，並把她變成了一潭水，流入了那條流向 Slieve Buane 西側的河流。

title.en: Aine's Stone of Madness and her Revenge on Oilioll
title.zh: 艾妮之瘋石與其對奧利奧爾的復仇

region.en: Cnoc Aine (Knockainey), Co. Limerick, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭利默里克郡克諾克艾尼山

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. V, eBook #14465

summary.en: Aine, daughter of Manannan — or, some say, the Morrigu herself — keeps a stone called Cathair Aine: who sits on it loses his wits, and mad dogs gather about it and go into the sea. She gives gifts of poetry and music and loves mortal men, but is revengeful: when King Oilioll Oluim kills her brother she makes an enchanted yew-tree with a little harper beside the river, and the quarrel over the harper leads to the battle of Magh Mucruimhe, where Oilioll and his seven sons are killed.
summary.zh: 艾妮或為瑪那南之女，或曰即摩里岡本人。其保有瘋石凱瑟·艾妮：坐之者喪智，瘋犬群集而後入海。她賜詩與樂，屢愛凡人，然報復心極重：愛爾蘭王奧利奧爾殺其兄後，她施法造紫杉樹，樹上小豎琴師引發兄弟爭執，終致馬格·穆克魯伊姆之戰，奧利奧爾與七子皆亡。

sensitivity.note: Aine of Knockainey is a living folkloric figure of Munster (midsummer rituals of torches on her hill are documented into the modern era); recorded here as myth per the project scheme, with no ritual prescription implied. Coordinates are her hill.

passages.text: Aine, that some said was a daughter of Manannan, and some said was the Morrigu herself, had a stone belonging to her that was called Cathair Aine. If any one would sit on that stone he would be in danger of losing his wits, and any one that would sit on it three times would lose them for ever. People whose wits were astray would make their way to it, and mad dogs would come from all parts of the country and flock around it, and then go into the sea to Aine's place there. But those that did cures by herbs said she had power over the whole body; and she used to give gifts of poetry and of music, and she often gave her love to men, and they called her the Leanan Sidhe, the Sweet-heart of the Sidhe.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 艾妮（Aine），有人說她是 Manannan 的女兒，也有人說她就是莫里根本人，她有一塊屬於她的石頭，叫做 Cathair Aine。任何人若坐在那塊石頭上，就有失去理智的危險，而任何人若在它上面坐三次，就會永遠失去理智。理智迷亂的人會走向它，瘋狗會從全國各地趕來，聚集在它周圍，然後進入海中，前往艾妮在那裡的地方。但那些用草藥治病的人說，她對整個身體都有力量；她過去常賜予詩歌和音樂的禮物，也常常把她的愛給予男人，人們稱她為 Leanan Sidhe，即「精靈的甜心」。

passages.text: It was no safe thing to offend Aine, for she was very revengeful. Oilioll Oluim, a king of Ireland, killed her brother one time, and she made a great yew-tree by enchantment beside the river Maigh in Luimnech, and put a little man in it, playing sweet music on a harp. Oilioll's son was passing the river with his step-brother, and they saw the tree and heard the sweet music from it. First they quarrelled as to which of them would have the little harper, then they quarrelled about the tree, and they asked a judgment from Oilioll, and he gave it for his own son. It was the bad feeling about that judgment that led to the battle of Magh Mucruimhe, and Oilioll and his seven sons were killed there, and so Aine got her revenge.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 冒犯艾妮可不是安全的事，因為她非常記仇。愛爾蘭國王 Oilioll Oluim 有一次殺了她的兄弟，她便用魔法在 Luimnech 的 Maigh 河邊造了一棵巨大的紫杉樹，並在樹中放了一個小人，彈奏著甜美的豎琴音樂。Oilioll 的兒子與他的異母兄弟正經過那條河，他們看見了那棵樹，聽到了從樹中傳來的甜美音樂。起初他們爭吵誰該得到那個小豎琴手，接著又為那棵樹爭吵，他們請 Oilioll 作出裁決，而他判給了自己的兒子。正是對那項裁決的不滿導致了 Magh Mucruimhe 之戰，Oilioll 和他的七個兒子都戰死在那裡，艾妮就這樣報了仇。

title.en: Janamejaya's Snake Sacrifice and the Rescue by Astika
title.zh: 闍那彌覺耶的蛇祭與阿悉底迦之救

region.en: Takshashila / Taxila (traditional site of the rite)
region.zh: 怛叉始羅（祭祀傳統聖地）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Astika Upaparva), composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Astika section

summary.en: King Parikshit dies of the serpent-king Takshaka's bite; his son Janamejaya holds a sacrificial fire so powerful that all serpents of the world are dragged into it to burn. The young brahmin Astika, son of a serpent mother, stops the holocaust with a request - and the serpents' race is saved, which is why the Mahabharata itself is being recited at all.
summary.zh: 帕里格希王死於蛇王多剎迦之咬；其子闍那彌覺耶設祭火之力足以將世間一切蛇拖入焚燬。年輕婆羅門阿悉底迦，蛇母之子，以一請求止此浩劫——蛇族得救；這也是《摩訶婆羅多》本身被誦出的緣由。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (naga worship persists); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: King Parikshit, cursed by a seer's son, was told he would die in seven days by the bite of Takshaka the serpent-king; he built a tower, sealed it - and Takshaka came disguised, and the king died as foretold. His son Janamejaya vowed revenge: a snake-sacrifice was raised whose fire drew the serpents of the whole earth into its blaze, kingdom by kingdom, name by name, until even Takshaka was pulled toward the flames.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Astika section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 國王缽羅迦尸（Parikshit）受仙人子之詛咒，被告知將於七日後因蛇王多剎迦（Takshaka）之噬咬而死；他築起高塔，將其封閉——而多剎迦化形而來，國王果如預言般死去。其子闍那梅闍耶（Janamejaya）立誓復仇：舉行了一場蛇祭，其火焰將大地上所有蛇族逐國逐名地吸入烈焰之中，直至連多剎迦也被拉向火中。

passages.text: Then Astika, a boy brahmin of a mixed birth - his father a seer, his mother a serpent-woman - praised the king and begged a boon: let the sacrifice stop while my kinsmen live. The king granted it; the serpents were released, the feud ended - and the story the world now reads was told first at that sacrifice, by its own survivor.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Astika section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 其時，阿斯提迦（Astika）——一位出身混雜的婆羅門少年，其父為仙人，其母為蛇女——讚頌國王並乞求一恩：願在我的親族尚存之時停止祭祀。國王允之；群蛇獲釋，宿怨終結——而世人今日所讀之故事，最初便是在那場祭祀上，由其自身的倖存者所講述。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Garuda Steals the Amrita for His Mother's Freedom
title.zh: 金翅鳥為母贖身而奪甘露

region.en: Ocean of amrita (symbolic pin at Varanasi ghats)
region.zh: 甘露之海（象徵性定位於瓦拉納西河壇）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Astika Upaparva), composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, the birth of Garuda

summary.en: The sisters Vinata and Kadru, wives of Kashyapa, made a fatal wager about the horses of the sun; Kadru's serpent sons enslaved Vinata and her egg-son. The egg hatched into Garuda, of impossible fire and wings; he won his mother's freedom by bringing the gods' amrita from the churning-ocean stronghold - fighting the gods, stealing the nectar, and honoring Vishnu with a covenant: he became the god's own carrier.
summary.zh: 迦葉波之二妻毗娜達與迦德魯就日馬之事立致命之賭；迦德魯的蛇子們奴役了毗娜達及其卵中之子。卵孵化為火翼無雙的金翅鳥；他以從攪乳海要塞奪來的諸神甘露換取母親的自由——戰諸神、竊神露，並與毘濕奴立約：他成為神之座騎。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (Garuda imagery across Asia); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The wager: Kadru said the sun's white horses had black tails; Vinata swore they were pure white. Kadru's serpent-sons made her right by clinging to the tails; the loser became the winner's slave, mother and egg. The egg broke open with fire: Garuda, huge-winged, feathered like flame, heard his mother's condition and flew to the gods' stronghold to fetch the amrita - the price the serpents set for Vinata's freedom.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那場賭約：迦葉波（Kadru）說太陽的白馬有黑色的尾巴；毗那陀（Vinata）發誓牠們是純白的。迦葉波的蛇子們纏附於馬尾之上，使她成為正確的一方；敗者成為勝者的奴隸，母親與蛋皆然。蛋隨著火焰迸裂而開：迦樓羅（Garuda）——巨翼如焰之羽——聽聞母親的處境，便飛往眾神的堡壘去取甘露（amrita）——那正是群蛇為換取毗那陀自由所開出的代價。

passages.text: He scattered the gods with a storm of wings, took the nectar, and Vishnu, impressed, made a covenant: Garuda became his carrier, and his own body immortal without the drink; the amrita was set out as ransom, the serpents licked it from the grass, and their tongues split forever - the covenant that made Garuda the enemy and liberator of serpents both.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他以雙翼的風暴驅散眾神，取走甘露，而毗濕奴（Vishnu）為之折服，與之立約：迦樓羅成為他的坐騎，其自身之軀不飲甘露而得不死；甘露被置於地上作為贖金，群蛇從草間舔食之，其舌遂永遠分裂——此約使迦樓羅既為蛇族之敵，亦為蛇族之解放者。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Ganga's Sons and Bhishma's Eight Births
title.zh: 恆河之子與毗濕摩的八次誕生

region.en: Pratapa of the Ganges at Prayag (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 般耶伽恆河畔（象徵性定位）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Ganga and Shantanu

summary.en: King Shantanu met a beautiful woman who married him on one condition: never ask what she did with their children. Seven sons were born and drowned one by one. The eighth was kept - Devavrata, the future Bhishma - and the river-bride, revealed as Ganga herself, left him with the story of eight gods imprisoned on earth and her task of releasing them.
summary.zh: 王商檀奴遇絕色女子，其嫁他有唯一條件：永不問她如何處置孩子。七子相繼誕生又相繼被溺。第八子被留下——婆德伐羅陀，未來的毗濕摩——而那位河畔新娘，現身為恆河本尊，帶著八位囚於人間之神與她釋放之任的故事離去。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (Ganga worship); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The woman of the river promised herself to Shantanu if he asked no questions: never whatever I do with our children, with or against thy will - and he, enamored, agreed; the sons born of her were drowned at birth, one after another, and the king could not speak.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那河之女自許於娑檀奴（Shantanu），條件是他不得發問：無論我對我們的孩子做什麼，順你之意或逆你之意，皆不得問——而他因愛慕而應允；她所生之子一個接一個於出生時被溺死，國王卻不能出聲。

passages.text: The eighth birth: when Ganga raised the child to drown him, Shantanu cried out at last - and she stopped, gave him the boy Devavrata, and told the secret: the eight Vasus, gods of light, had been cursed into human birth, and she had been their ferry; seven she had released to heaven at once. Devavrata stayed as Shantanu's heir - the one Vasu whose curse ran its longest course - and the hero's later terrible vow of celibacy (bhishana, the 'terrible', hence Bhishma) completes the freight of the river's bargain.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第八次誕生：當恆伽（Ganga）舉起嬰兒欲將其溺死時，娑檀奴終於出聲呼喊——她便停下，將男孩提婆弗羅多（Devavrata）交給他，並道出秘密：八位婆藪（Vasus），即光明之神，曾受詛咒而降生為人，而她正是渡他們之人；其中七位她已即刻釋回天界。提婆弗羅多留為娑檀奴之繼承人——那唯一一位詛咒歷程最為長久的婆藪——而這位英雄日後那可怕的守貞之誓（bhishana，意為「可怕」，故稱毗濕摩 Bhishma）完成了河之契約所承載的全部重負。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Satyavati the Fisher-Girl and Vyasa the Island-Born
title.zh: 漁家女莎蒂亞瓦蒂與生於島上的毗耶娑

region.en: Yamuna ferry-crossing (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 亞穆納河渡口（象徵性定位）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Sambhava section

summary.en: The girl Satyavati, ferrying travelers across the Yamuna smelling of fish, met the seer Parashara; he offered her a boon - she chose that her fish-smell become fragrance, her maidenhood return, and her river-mist conceal their union on an island. Their son was Vyasa, the compiler of the Mahabharata itself - the epic written by its own love-child.
summary.zh: 魚味少女莎蒂亞瓦蒂渡旅人於亞穆納河，遇仙人婆羅沙羅；他允其一恩——她選擇魚味化香、處子復得、河霧蔽於島上的結合。其子即毗耶娑，《摩訶婆羅多》的編纂者——史詩由其自身的愛之子寫成。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The ferry-girl ruled the river-crossing with a will; the seer Parashara, crossing, desired her; she refused him at first, and he offered boons until she bargained: my fish-smell to sweetness, my virginity restored, and a mist to hide us from the two banks.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那渡船女以堅定的意志掌管著渡口；仙人波羅奢羅過河時對她起了欲念；她起初拒絕了他，他便許以恩惠，直到她議定條件：將我的魚腥味換成芬芳，恢復我的童貞，並降下一片迷霧，把我們與兩岸遮蔽起來。

passages.text: On the island in the mist a child was conceived and born within the hour, dark, wise, island-born - Dvaipayana, Vyasa - who went at once to do austerities, promising his mother to come whenever she thought of him. The daughter of the fisher-king rose by that fortune to be the grandmother of both armies - and Vyasa's promise kept: it is he who comes when the dynasty calls, to father its heirs and write its epic.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在霧中的島上，一個孩子受孕，並在一個時辰之內誕生，膚色黝黑、智慧通達、生於島上——即島生者德瓦帕亞那，也就是毗耶娑——他隨即前去修苦行，並向母親許諾：只要她心中念及他，他便前來。那漁王之女因這番際遇而崛起，成為兩支軍隊共同的祖母——而毗耶娑的承諾也得以信守：每當王朝呼喚，前來的正是他，為王朝繁衍後嗣，並寫下它的史詩。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Pandu's Curse in the Deer Forest
title.zh: 般度於鹿林中的詛咒

region.en: Shatasringa hermitage (symbolic pin in Himalayan foothills)
region.zh: 百峰仙人道場（象徵性定位於喜馬拉雅山麓）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Sambhava section

summary.en: King Pandu, on a hunt, shot a stag mid-union with its doe - and the stag was a seer. Dying, he cursed Pandu: union with a woman shall be death for him. Pandu renounced the throne to his blind brother and lived in the forest; his sons - the Pandavas - were born not of him but of the gods his wives invoked: the theology of the five heroes' divine fathers.
summary.zh: 王般度狩獵時射中一頭正與牝鹿交合的雄鹿——而牠是仙人。垂死的詛咒降於般度：與女子交合即死。般度讓位於盲眼的弟弟，居於林中；其子——般度五子——非其親生，而是諸神經由其妻的召喚而生：五英雄神性之父的神學。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Pandu's arrow found the stag in the forest clearing - and the dying creature stood up as a sage and delivered the curse: the same arrow shall find thee in the moment of thy joy; know death in the embrace.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 般度的箭在林中空地上射中了那頭雄鹿——而那垂死的生靈卻站起來，化作一位仙人，降下詛咒：同一支箭將在你歡樂的時刻找到你；在擁抱中領受死亡吧。

passages.text: Pandu gave up the kingdom, the pleasures and the palace, and went to the Himalayan foothills with his two wives; the throne passed to the blind Dhritarashtra and the age's tragedy was set in motion by a hunter's mistake. In the forest the wives were given mantras: Kunti bore three sons of gods she invoked - Yudhishthira of Dharma, Bhima of the Wind, Arjuna of Indra - and Madri two of the Ashvins; the Pandavas are therefore gods' sons on a cursed father's name, the epic's own theology of legitimacy.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 般度捨棄了王國、種種享樂與宮殿，帶著他的兩位妻子前往喜馬拉雅山麓；王位傳給了盲眼的持國，而時代的悲劇便由一名獵人的過失啟動。在林中，兩位妻子獲得了咒語：貢蒂召請神明，生下三子——法神之子堅戰、風神之子怖軍、因陀羅之子阿周那——瑪德麗則生下雙馬童的兩個兒子；因此般度五子是以一位受詛咒的父親之名義而生的神明之子，這正是史詩自身關於正統性的神學。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Amba's Terrible Birth: The Story of Shikhandin
title.zh: 安巴的可怕轉生：希甘丁的故事

region.en: Kashi and Kurukshetra (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 迦屍與俱盧之野（象徵性定位）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Amba Upaparva), composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, the story of Amba

summary.en: At the svayamvara of the three Kashi princesses, Bhishma carried them off for his brother's marriage-bed; Amba, already pledged to another, was returned by the rules of honor - but her bridegroom refused her, ruined. She turned for redress to Bhishma himself, then to Shiva: born again as Shikhandin, she finally faced the old man on the battlefield he had sworn not to fight.
summary.zh: 在迦屍三公主的自擇婚禮上，毗濕摩為其弟之婚床擄走三女；安巴已許他人，依榮譽之規則被送回——但她的新郎因她受辱而拒娶。她轉而向毗濕摩討公道，繼而向濕婆：轉生為希甘丁後，她終於在老人誓不與戰的戰場上與他對面。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; gendered readings contested; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Bhishma, sent to win brides for his brother, took the three princesses of Kashi by force of arms from their svayamvara - a deed of honor in his own code, and an abduction in everyone else's. Amba's plea: she had already chosen a husband. Bhishma honored her word and sent her back - and the bridegroom, hearing she had dwelt in another man's chariot, refused her; ruined twice over, she turned her whole life into a single accusation.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Amba section (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 毗濕摩奉命為他的弟弟奪取新娘，以武力從迦尸三位公主的選婿大典上將她們擄走——在他自己的準則中這是榮耀之舉，在其他人眼中則是劫掠。安巴的懇求是：她早已選定了丈夫。毗濕摩尊重她的話，將她送回——而那新郎聽聞她曾居於另一個男人的戰車之上，便拒絕了她；她遭受了雙重的毀滅，於是將自己的一生化為單一的控訴。

passages.text: Her austerities were answered by Shiva with the promise of rebirth to destroy Bhishma - born again as Shikhandin, a warrior whose past Bhishma knew; on the tenth day of the great war, Arjuna's arrows passed over Shikhandin's body to reach Bhishma, who would not raise his bow against the one he wronged - the debt collected at last.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva and Bhishma Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她的苦行得到了濕婆的回應，應許她轉世以毀滅毗濕摩——她轉生為束髮，一位毗濕摩知曉其前世的戰士；在大戰的第十日，阿周那的箭越過束髮的身軀射中毗濕摩，而毗濕摩不願向他所虧負之人舉弓——這筆債終於討還了。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Bhishma's Terrible Vow at the Fisherman's Ford
title.zh: 毗濕摩於漁人渡口的可怕誓言

region.en: Ganges ford, Kurukshetra region (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 恆河渡口，俱盧之野一帶（象徵性定位）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Bhishma's vow

summary.en: Shantanu loved Satyavati the ferry-girl; her father demanded that her sons inherit. Devavrata, the river's own son and heir, made the vow that bought her: he renounced the throne, and then - for the girl's sons might still fear his descendants - renounced children altogether. The gods rained flowers on a vow so terrible it named him: Bhishma.
summary.zh: 商檀奴愛上渡舟女莎蒂亞瓦蒂；其父要求她之子繼承王位。河神之子、法定繼承人婆德伐羅陀立誓買下她：放棄王位，繼而——因女孩之子或仍懼其後裔——放棄後嗣。諸神對如此可怕的誓言降下花雨，此誓亦為他命名：毗濕摩（『可怕者』）。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The fisherman's price for his daughter was succession: her sons shall reign. Devavrata answered by giving up the throne his birth gave him - and, pressed further, by giving up posterity itself. The vow was spoken at the ford: I shall never marry, never touch a woman, and my life shall end only when the gods appoint - so strong that heaven opened and flowers fell, and the witnesses named him Bhishma, the terrible.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 漁夫為女兒開出的代價是繼承權：她的兒子們將統治。提婆弗羅陀（Devavrata）的回答，是放棄他與生俱來的王位——而在進一步逼迫之下，更放棄了子嗣本身。這誓言是在渡口說出的：我將永不娶妻，永不觸碰女人，我的生命唯有在諸神所定之時才會終結——誓言之強，令天門開啟、花雨飄落，見證者遂為他取名毗濕摩（Bhishma），意即「可怖者」。

passages.text: The whole war is downstream of that vow: the childless Bhishma as regent, the succession crisis of his vow's collateral, and the old man on the arrows-bed at Kurukshetra who taught dharma from the wreck of the kingdom his own word had helped to make.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 整場戰爭皆是那誓言的餘波：無子的毗濕摩攝政，他的誓言所衍生的旁系繼承危機，以及那位在俱盧之野（Kurukshetra）臥於箭床上的老人——他從自己一言所助成的王國廢墟中，宣講達摩（dharma）。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Bhima and Hidimba: The Rakshasa Bride
title.zh: 怖軍與訶底撥：羅剎之妻

region.en: Ekachakra forest (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 一輪森林（象徵性定位）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Hidimva and Ghatotkacha

summary.en: Exiled in the forest, the Pandavas camped where the rakshasa Hidimba and his sister hunted men. The sister, Hidimbi, saw Bhima and chose him; her brother attacked, and Bhima's mace decided it. From the marriage of princess and rakshasa came Ghatotkacha, the pot-born giant, his head shaped like a pot, who would die at Kurukshetra saving Arjuna.
summary.zh: 流亡林中的般度五子在羅剎訶底撥與其妹的獵人之地紮營。妹妹訶底毗見怖軍而屬意之；其兄來攻，怖軍之杵定勝負。公主與羅剎之婚誕生了罐首巨人無底缽迦，他將在俱盧之野為救阿周那而死。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Hidimbi, sent by her man-eating brother to scout the sleepers, found Bhima awake and beautiful - and warned him instead: your brothers and Draupadi are in danger; my brother comes to eat them. The duel that followed was giant against giant: Bhima's strength held through the night, and Hidimba fell; the rakshasa woman, her protector dead, claimed the hero by her brother's own dying law - a marriage of the strong.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 希丁毗（Hidimbi）受食人的兄長所遣，前去窺探沉睡者，卻發現怖軍（Bhima）醒著，且英偉俊美——於是她反倒警告他：你的兄弟們與黑公主（Draupadi）身陷危險；我的兄長正來吞食他們。隨後的決鬥是巨人對巨人：怖軍的力氣撐過了整夜，希丁巴（Hidimba）終於倒下；這羅剎女在其庇護者死後，依兄長臨終所立的律法，將這位英雄據為己有——這是一場強者之婚。

passages.text: Yudhishthira's terms were exile-tight: one son, then they part. Ghatotkacha was born pot-headed, gigantic, devoted to his father's family; he served the Pandavas their whole exile and, at Kurukshetra, flew into Karna's spear - a son spent to save a father's brother.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva and Drona Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 堅戰（Yudhishthira）的條件嚴苛如流放：只許一子，之後便得分別。瓶首（Ghatotkacha）生來便頭如瓶甕、身形巨大，忠於父親的家族；他在整個流放期間服侍般度族（Pandavas），並在俱盧之野撲向迦爾納（Karna）的矛鋒——一個兒子被捨出，以救父親的兄長。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Arjuna and Ulupi, the Naga Princess
title.zh: 阿周那與龍女鄔樓毗

region.en: Ganges, Manipur route (symbolic pin at Haridwar)
region.zh: 恆河，曼尼普爾之路（象徵性定位於赫里德瓦爾）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Arjuna's wanderings

summary.en: Wandering penance-bound after a transgression, Arjuna bathed in the Ganges at night - and was seized by the naga princess Ulupi, who drew him down to the serpent city, married him, and gave him the boon his celibacy needed: victory over every water-being. Their son Iravan would die a hero's death at Kurukshetra.
summary.zh: 因觸戒而流浪贖罪中的阿周那夜浴恆河——被龍女鄔樓毗攫住，帶入蛇城，與之成婚，並賜予其苦行生活所需之恩：戰勝一切水族。其子伊拉萬將於俱盧之野戰死，死如英雄。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (Iravan/Koothandavar cult in Tamil country); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Arjuna's penance-law forbade the bed of any woman; at the night-bath the naga princess Ulupi took him at the wrists and drew him, unresisting, into the river's deep - to the city of the serpents, where she offered her love with the law's own loophole.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿周那（Arjuna）的苦行戒律禁止他與任何女子同床；在夜浴之時，那伽（naga）公主優樓毗（Ulupi）抓住他的手腕，將毫不抵抗的他拖入河水深處——來到蛇族之城，在那裡，她以律法自身的漏洞獻上自己的愛。

passages.text: The loophole: the vow bound him against desire, not against the water's gift - and Ulupi's marriage-bed counted as neither; she bore him Iravan, and gave him the practical blessing that his river-life needed: no water-creature shall overcome thee. He returned by morning to his brothers as if nothing had happened; the son he left behind grew into a self-sacrificing warrior of the war, and in the Tamil south his cult continues in rituals of self-offering to this day.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那漏洞在於：誓言約束他不得起慾念，卻未約束他不得受水之贈禮——而優樓毗的婚床兩者皆不算；她為他生下伊羅婆陀（Iravan），並賜予他河居生活所需的實用祝福：任何水族皆不能勝過你。他於清晨回到兄弟們身邊，彷彿什麼事都未曾發生；他留下的那個兒子成長為戰爭中自我犧牲的戰士，而在泰米爾南方，對他的崇拜至今仍以自我奉獻的儀式延續。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Arjuna and Chitrangada of Manipur
title.zh: 阿周那與曼尼普爾的希甘提耶

region.en: Manipur (symbolic pin, eastern frontier)
region.zh: 曼尼普爾（象徵性定位，東部邊地）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Arjuna's wanderings

summary.en: The third of Arjuna's exile-marriages: at the river-city of Manipur the warrior-princess Chitrangada approached him herself and asked to be his wife. He stayed a season; she bore him Babhruvahana, who as a boy at Kurukshetra would kill his own father - and be forgiven, in the epic's strangest family accounting.
summary.zh: 阿周那流亡中的第三次婚姻：在河城曼尼普爾，女戰士希甘提耶親自來求嫁。他居留一季；她為他生子巴布魯婆訶那，後者在俱盧之野以童子之身親手弒父——並被饒恕，於史詩最奇異的家庭清算之中。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Chitrangada, only daughter of the Manipur king, had been raised as his heir and warrior; hearing of Arjuna's penance-wanderings, she came to the hermitage herself, dressed plainly, and asked - not for a beauty's marriage but a warrior's. Arjuna stayed a season by the river-city; their son Babhruvahana was sent to be raised as his mother's heir, and Manipur passed to the Pandavas' line without a war.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 奇特朗伽達是曼尼普爾王唯一的女兒，自幼被當作繼承人與戰士撫養長大；她聽聞阿周那苦行遊歷之事，便親自來到隱修林，衣著樸素，所求並非美人的婚配，而是戰士的婚配。阿周那在河城旁停留了一季；他們的兒子巴布魯瓦哈納被送去撫養，以承繼母親的嗣位，曼尼普爾遂不經一戰而歸入般度族的世系。

passages.text: The epic's coda: years later at Kurukshetra, the Ashvamedha horse reached Manipur, and the boy-king Babhruvahana fought the rider - his father - and felled him; Ulupi's serpent-charm revived Arjuna, and the son knelt to a father restored - a family puzzle the epic refuses to judge.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 史詩的尾聲：多年之後在俱盧之野，馬祭之馬抵達曼尼普爾，少年國王巴布魯瓦哈納與騎馬者——他的父親——交戰，並將他擊倒；烏露毗的蛇咒使阿周那復活，兒子向復原的父親跪拜——這是史詩拒絕評判的一樁家庭謎題。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Aoibhell and Dubhlaing's Choice at Cluantarbh
title.zh: 艾薇爾與杜夫萊因在克魯安塔之抉擇

region.en: Craig Liath (The Grey Rock), Co. Tipperary, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭蒂珀雷里郡灰岩（象徵定位）

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. VI, eBook #14465

summary.en: Aoibhell, a woman of the Sidhe dwelling in Craig Liath, loves the young Munsterman Dubhlaing ua Artigan. Before the battle of Cluantarbh she tries to hold him back and wraps him in a Druid covering so no one can see him; refusing to fight unseen, he casts it off. She offers him two hundred years of happy life if he will leave the battle, but he will not give up his king or his good name, and both men fall as she foretold.
summary.zh: 仙族女子艾薇爾居灰岩，愛上年輕的芒斯特戰士杜夫萊因。克魯安塔之戰前她欲留他，並施德魯伊隱形罩使其不可見；杜夫萊因拒絕隱身作戰而卸去罩衣。她許諾二百年歡愉歲月勸其離戰，他不願捨君王與名譽；戰場上二人皆亡，如其所言。

sensitivity.note: A fairy-mistress offering otherworld longevity against heroic fame — the Irish inverse of Achilles' choice. Cluantarbh (Slog in an Elum?) battle located symbolically at traditional Craig Liath site.

passages.text: Aoibhell, another woman of the Sidhe, made her dwelling-place in Craig Liath, and at the time of the battle of Cluantarbh she set her love on a young man of Munster, Dubhlaing ua Artigan, that had been sent away in disgrace by the King of Ireland. But before the battle he came back to join with Murchadh, the king's son, and to fight for the Gael. Aoibhell came to stop him; and when he would not stop with her she put a Druid covering about him, so that no one could see him. He went where Murchadh was fighting, and made a great attack on the enemies of Ireland, striking them down on every side. Murchadh looked around him: "It seems to me I hear the sound of the blows of Dubhlaing ua Artigan, but I do not see himself." Then Dubhlaing threw off the Druid covering: "I will not keep this covering upon me when you cannot see me through it."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 艾芙赫爾是另一位希德女子，她以克雷格利亞斯為居所，在克盧安塔夫之戰時，她愛上了芒斯特的一位青年杜布萊恩·烏亞·阿爾蒂根，此人曾被愛爾蘭國王以失寵之身遣走。但在戰前，他回來與國王之子穆爾查德會合，為蓋爾人作戰。艾芙赫爾前來阻止他；當他不肯與她一同留下時，她便在他身上施了德魯伊的遮蔽術，使無人能看見他。他前往穆爾查德作戰之處，對愛爾蘭的敵人發動猛攻，四面擊倒他們。穆爾查德環顧四周：「我似乎聽見杜布萊恩·烏亞·阿爾蒂根的擊打之聲，卻看不見他本人。」於是杜布萊恩拋開德魯伊的遮蔽：「既然你無法透過它看見我，我便不願再把這遮蔽留在我身上。」

passages.text: So they went where Aoibhell was, and she bade them both quit the battle, for they would lose their lives in it. Murchadh said to her: "I will tell you a little true story: that fear for my own body will never make me change my face. And if we fall, the strangers will fall with us." "Stop with me, Dubhlaing," she said, "and you will have two hundred years of happy life with myself." "I will not give up Murchadh," he said, "or my own good name, for silver or gold." There was anger on Aoibhell, and she said: "Murchadh will fall, and you yourself will fall, and your proud blood will be on the plain to-morrow." They went back into the battle, and got their death there.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是他們來到艾芙赫爾所在之處，她吩咐二人退出戰鬥，因為他們會在其中喪命。穆爾查德對她說：「我要告訴你一個真實的小故事：對我自己身體的恐懼，絕不會使我改變面容。倘若我們倒下，那些外來者也將與我們一同倒下。」「與我留下吧，杜布萊恩，」她說，「你將與我共度兩百年幸福的生活。」「我絕不會為了銀子或金子捨棄穆爾查德，」他說，「也不會捨棄我自己的好名聲。」艾芙赫爾動了怒，說道：「穆爾查德將倒下，你自己也將倒下，你高傲的血明日將灑在平原上。」他們重返戰場，並在那裡喪命。

title.en: Manannan of the Many Shapes
title.zh: 化身無數的瑪那南

region.en: Island of Falga / Emain Ablach (Isle of Man, symbolic pin)
region.zh: 法爾加島／埃曼·阿布拉赫（象徵定位於曼島）

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. VIII, eBook #14465

summary.en: Manannan son of Lir, the sea-god and master of enchantments, is said to have died in battle and been buried standing, where a lake burst up under his feet; yet he was long heard of in Ireland. He raised the sons of Usnach's blindness, was perhaps Culain the Smith, and at the Island of Falga Conchobar bound the sea-queen Tiabhal, whose likeness on the smith's shield lessened the strength of enemies in every battle. His hounds that hunted a destroying pig were all destroyed at the lake called after them, Loch Conn.
summary.zh: 海神瑪那南精通幻術，傳說戰死後立而葬之，腳下湧出湖泊；然其後久聞於愛爾蘭。他使烏斯納克諸子盲目互殘，或謂鐵匠庫蘭即其化身。法爾加島上，康恩丘巴縛海后蒂亞巴爾；其像鑄於盾上，使戰陣中敵力消而己力增。瑪那南之獵犬追逐毀田之豬，悉數亡於後稱犬湖之湖。

sensitivity.note: Manannan mac Lir is the euhemerized sea-god; 'buried standing' is a standard divine-grave motif. The Isle of Man (Emain Ablach / Mannanan's isle) is the traditional symbolic pin for the Island of Falga.

passages.text: As to Manannan the Proud, son of Lir, after he had made places for the rest of the Tuatha de Danaan to live in, he went away out of Ireland himself. Some said he was dead, and got his death by Uillenn Faebarderg of the Red Edge, in battle at Magh Cuilenn; that Manannan was buried standing on his feet, and no sooner was he buried than a great lake burst up under his feet in the place that was a red bog till that time, and the lake got the name of Loch Orbson from one of the names of Manannan. And it was said that red Badb was glad and many women were sorry at that battle. Yet he had many places of living and was often heard of in Ireland after; it was he sent a messenger to Etain, mother of Conaire the High King; it was he brought up Deirdre's children in Emhain of the Apple Trees; and it was he taught Cuchulain the use of the Gae Bulg. Some say Culain the Smith, that gave his name to Cuchulain, was Manannan himself, for he had many shapes.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VIII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 至於里爾之子、驕傲的馬南南，在他為達南神族其餘諸神安排好居所之後，他自己便離開了愛爾蘭。有人說他已死，死於紅刃的烏伊倫·法巴德格之手，是在馬格庫倫之戰中；說馬南南被直立著埋葬，剛一埋葬，他腳下便湧出一個大湖，那地方在此之前是一片紅沼澤，這湖便因馬南南諸名之一而得名為奧布森湖。又說那場戰鬥中紅色的巴德布歡欣，而許多婦人悲傷。然而此後他在愛爾蘭仍有許多居處，也常被提及；正是他派遣使者去見至尊王康奈爾之母埃泰恩；正是他在蘋果樹的埃姆海恩撫養了黛爾德蕾的子女；也正是他教會庫丘林使用蓋布爾格矛。有人說，賜名庫丘林的鐵匠庫蘭，就是馬南南本人，因為他有許多形貌。

passages.text: Before Culain came to Ulster he was living in the Island of Falga, one of Manannan's places. Conchubar, advised by a Druid, went to ask the smith there to make arms for him, and while he worked Conchubar walked on the strand and saw a sea-woman asleep on the shore. He put bonds on her in her sleep; when she awoke she asked her freedom: "I am Tiabhal, one of the queens of the sea. Bid Culain that is making your shield to put my likeness on it and my name about it, and whenever you go into battle with that shield the strength of your enemies will lessen, and your own strength will increase." Conchubar let her go, and got the victory wherever he brought that shield. And Manannan had good hounds one time, but they hunted a pig that was making a desert of the whole country, and at a lake it turned on them, and no hound of them escaped alive; the pig made for an island named after it, and the lake got the name of Loch Conn, the Lake of the Hounds.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VIII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 庫蘭在來到阿爾斯特之前，住在法爾加島，那是馬南南的居處之一。康丘巴爾聽從一位德魯伊的建議，前去請那裡的鐵匠為他打造兵器；庫蘭工作之時，康丘巴爾在海灘上行走，看見一名海女在岸上沉睡。他趁她睡時在她身上施了束縛；她醒來後請求自由：「我是蒂亞瓦爾，海中的女王之一。吩咐為你打造盾牌的庫蘭，把我的形貌繪在盾上，把我的名字寫在四周，每當你帶著那面盾上陣，你敵人的力量便會減弱，而你自己的力量便會增強。」康丘巴爾放她離去，此後凡帶那面盾出戰，皆得勝利。馬南南曾有一群好獵犬，但牠們追逐一頭使整個鄉野荒蕪的豬，那豬在一處湖邊反身撲向牠們，牠們之中沒有一隻獵犬生還；那豬奔向一座以牠命名的島，那湖便得名為康湖，即獵犬之湖。

title.en: Tuag and the Sleep-Spell of Fer Ferdiad
title.zh: 圖雅格與費爾·費爾迪亞德之催眠咒

region.en: Inver Glas, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭格拉斯河口（象徵定位）

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. VIII, eBook #14465

summary.en: Tuag, a fosterling of Conaire the High King, is reared in Tara behind a great company of guardians, to be kept for a king's asking. Manannan sends his pupil, the Druid Fer Ferdiad, in the shape of a woman of the household, who sings a sleep-spell over her and carries her away to Inver Glas; while he looks for a boat a flood-tide wave comes over the girl and drowns her, and Manannan kills Fer Ferdiad in his anger. The wave that drowned Tuag is remembered as one of the three great waves of Ireland.
summary.zh: 圖雅格為百戰王康奈爾之養女，於塔拉被重兵環衛撫養，以待君王求婚。瑪那南遣門徒德魯伊費爾·費爾迪亞德化身侍女，以催眠咒攜其至格拉斯河口；彼尋船之際，漲潮之浪沒圖雅格，她溺亡。瑪那南怒殺費爾·費爾迪亞德。沒頂之浪遂成愛爾蘭三大浪之一。

sensitivity.note: The Wave of Tuag (Tonn Tuaithe) is one of the three great waves of Ireland in the dindsenchas tradition; a failed-elopement etiology. Pin symbolic at the Dublin coast where the tradition locates the strand.

passages.text: There was a young girl of the name of Tuag, a fosterling of Conaire the High King, reared in Teamhair, and a great company of the daughters of the kings of Ireland was put about her, so that she would be kept for a king's asking. But Manannan sent Fer Ferdiad, of the Tuatha de Danaan, that was a pupil of his own and a Druid, in the shape of a woman of his own household, and he went where Tuag was, and sang a sleep-spell over her, and brought her away to Inver Glas.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VIII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 從前有個名叫圖阿格的年輕女孩，是至高王科奈爾的養女，在塔拉教養長大，愛爾蘭諸王的女兒們有一大群被安排在她身邊，好將她留著以備某位國王求娶。但馬納南派了圖阿薩·德·達南族的費爾·費爾迪亞德——此人是他的門徒，也是個德魯伊——化作他自家一名女眷的模樣，去到圖阿格所在之處，對她唱了一支催眠咒，將她帶到了因弗爾格拉斯。

passages.text: There he laid her down while he went looking for a boat, that he might bring her away in her sleep to the Land of the Ever-Living Women. But a wave of the flood-tide came over the girl, and she was drowned, and Manannan killed Fer Ferdiad in his anger. It was through Manannan that the wave of Tuag, one of the three great waves of Ireland, got its name.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VIII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他在那裡將她放下，自己則去尋找船隻，好趁她沉睡時將她帶往永恆女子之地。但一道漲潮的浪頭打過那女孩，她便溺死了，馬納南一怒之下殺了費爾·費爾迪亞德。正因馬納南，圖阿格之浪——愛爾蘭三大浪之一——才得了此名。

title.en: O'Donnell's Kern
title.zh: 奧唐奈的流浪樂師

region.en: Bel-atha Senaig (Ballyshannon), Co. Donegal, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭多尼戈爾郡貝利沙納克

period: Late medieval Irish tale tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. IX, eBook #14465

summary.en: At O'Donnell's feast in Ballyshannon a strange clown walks in without passing the gate — old striped clothes, puddle-water splashing in his shoes. He scorns the harpers, plays music sweet enough to sleep women in their pains, refuses clothes and honour, and vanishes in the middle of his music while the watchers strike each other down. Resurrecting them with a herb, he moves from house to house under new names, "one day sweet, another day sour," doing tricks and leaving life restored behind him.
summary.zh: 奧唐奈於貝利沙納克設宴時，一衣衫襤褸之流浪漢不入門而現身，鞋中濺滿泥水。他嘲弄琴師，卻奏出使產婦入睡之美樂；不受衣賞榮銜，樂聲中消失，守衛誤傷彼此倒地。他以草藥救活眾人，四處更名行奇，自言「一日甜，一日酸」，所過之處死而復生。

sensitivity.note: Manannan's wandering-kern cycle is late medieval comedic mythos (the god as beggar-trickster); resurrection tag from the herb that revives the slain. Pin at the feast site named in the tale.

passages.text: Aodh Dubh O'Donnell was holding a feast one time in Bel-atha Senaig, and while they were boasting of the goodness of his house and of his musicians, they saw a clown coming towards them, old striped clothes he had, and puddle water splashing in his shoes, and his sword sticking out naked behind him, and in his hand three spears of hollywood scorched and blackened. When the gate-keeper was brought, he said he had never seen the man before. "Let him off, O'Donnell," said the stranger, "for it was as easy for me to come in as it will be to me to go out again." The musicians began to play their sweetest tunes, but the strange man called out that never was a noise of hammers beating on iron in any bad place so bad to listen to. With that he took a harp and made music that would put women in their pains and wounded men after a battle into a sweet sleep.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IX; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一回，黑奧伊·奧唐奈爾在貝爾阿薩塞奈格設宴，正當眾人誇讚他府邸的豐盛與樂師的技藝時，他們看見一個丑角朝他們走來，他穿著老舊的條紋衣裳，鞋裡濺著泥水，劍赤裸地從身後探出，手裡拿著三支冬青木矛，燒得焦黑。守門人被帶來時，說他從未見過此人。「放他進來吧，奧唐奈爾，」那陌生人說，「因為我進來容易，出去也一樣容易。」樂師們開始奏起最甜美的曲調，但那陌生人喊道，任何壞地方裡鐵鎚敲鐵的聲響，都不曾這般難聽。說著他取過一把豎琴，奏出樂聲，能讓產婦忘卻陣痛，讓戰後的傷兵進入甜美的沉睡。

passages.text: They were afraid he might go from them, and put twenty armed horsemen and twenty men on foot to hold him back; but while they were all listening to his harp, he called out: "Here I am coming, and watch me well now or you will lose me." The watchers lifted their axes in haste and struck at one another till all were stretched in blood. The clown bade the gate-keeper ask twenty cows and a hundred of free land of O'Donnell as a fee, and take an herb and rub it in the mouth of each man, and they would rise up whole and well again. So the gate-keeper did that, and brought all the people to life again. And that is the way Manannan used to be going round Ireland, doing tricks and wonders; if he was put on a gallows itself, he would be found safe in the house after, and some other man on the gallows in his place. But he did no harm, and those that would be put to death by him, he would bring them to life again with a herb out of his bag.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IX; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們怕他會從他們身邊離去，便派了二十名披甲騎兵和二十名步卒攔住他；但正當眾人都在聆聽他的琴聲時，他喊道：「我這就來了，現在好好看著我，否則你們就要失去我了。」看守的人急忙舉起斧頭彼此砍殺，直到全都倒在血泊之中。那丑角吩咐守門人向奧唐奈爾索要二十頭牛和一百畝自由地作為酬勞，再取一株藥草揉進每個人的嘴裡，他們便會完好無恙地重新站起。守門人照做了，使所有人全都復活過來。馬納南便是這樣在愛爾蘭四處遊走，施展戲法與奇蹟；即便把他送上絞架，事後也會發現他安然在家中，而絞架上換成了另一個人的身子。但他從不害人，那些本該被他處死的人，他都會用袋中一株藥草使他們復活。

title.en: The Thread of Silk and the Hunt in the Air
title.zh: 絲線與空中狩獵之戲

region.en: Magh Lorg, Co. Monaghan, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭莫納亨郡馬格·洛格（象徵定位）

period: Late medieval Irish tale tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. IX, eBook #14465

summary.en: Calling himself the Gilla Decair, Manannan comes to Tadg O'Cealaigh and for five marks performs tricks: blowing away a middle rush between two fingers, wagging one ear alone, and — greatest of all — casting a thread of silk that fastens to a cloud, up which run a hare, a hound, a serving-boy, and a beautiful girl. When he draws the thread down, the boy is courting the girl and the hound chewing the hare's bones; he strikes the boy's head off, then restores it — but turned backwards — and at Tadg's word twists it straight again.
summary.zh: 自稱「劣僕」的瑪那南到訪塔格·奧基拉，索五馬克表演戲法：兩指間吹走中間燈芯草、單側動耳，最絕者為擲絲線掛於雲端，兔、犬、小僕、美女相繼攀上。收線時，僕正與女調情，犬正嚼兔骨。他怒斬僕首，又復合之——然面朝後；應塔格之言再扭正之。

sensitivity.note: Continuation of the kern cycle; the cloud-thread hunt is a famous shapeshifting-contest episode (compare the pigkeepers' pursuit in cow-raid tradition). Death-and-restoration of the boy tagged 'resurrection' as a staged trick, not a religious miracle.

passages.text: After that he went to where Tadg O'Cealaigh was, having his old striped clothes and his old shoes as before, and when they asked him what art he had he said: "I am good at tricks. And if you will give me five marks I will show you a trick." With that the stranger put three rushes on the palm of his hand: "I will blow away the middle rush now, and the other two will stop as they are." So it was done. He showed too how he could wag the ear on one side of his head and the other would stay still.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IX; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 此後他來到塔格·奧基利所在之處，仍像先前那樣穿著老舊的條紋衣裳和老舊的鞋子，當他們問他有什麼本領時，他說：「我擅長戲法。你若給我五個馬克，我便給你表演一個戲法。」說著，那陌生人把三根燈心草放在掌心：「我現在要把中間那根吹走，另外兩根會原樣不動。」果然如此。他還表演了如何讓頭一側的耳朵擺動，而另一側保持不動。

passages.text: Then he took from his bag a thread of silk and gave a cast of it up into the air, that it was made fast to a cloud. He took a hare out of the same bag and it ran up the thread; then a little dog after the hare, yelping on its track; then a serving-boy after the hound; and out of another bag a beautiful, well-dressed young woman, bidden to follow them and not let the hare be torn by the dog. It was a delight to Tadg to look at them and listen to the hunt going on in the air.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IX; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 接著他從袋中取出一根絲線，往空中一拋，那線便繫在了一朵雲上。他又從同一隻袋中取出一隻野兔，野兔沿著絲線跑了上去；接著一隻小狗追著野兔，一路吠叫著循跡而上；接著一名僕童追著獵犬；又從另一隻袋中取出一位美麗、衣著講究的年輕女子，吩咐她跟隨他們，別讓獵犬撕咬了野兔。塔格看著他們，聽著空中進行的狩獵，心中甚是歡喜。

passages.text: But the man of tricks said: "I am afraid there is some bad work going on up there. I am thinking the hound might be eating the hare, and the serving-boy courting the girl." He drew in the thread and found it so, and took his sword and struck the head off the boy; then, taking up the head, made a cast of it at the body, and it joined, but the face was turned backwards — and when Tadg said it would be better for him to be dead than living like that, he took hold of the boy and twisted his head straight, and he was as well as before.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IX; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但那耍把戲的人說：「我擔心上頭出了什麼壞事。我想那獵犬或許正在吃那野兔，而那侍童正在向那少女求愛。」他收回絲線，發現果然如此，便拔出劍來，砍下那男孩的頭；隨後，他拾起頭顱，朝那軀體擲去，頭便接了回去，但臉卻轉向了背後——而當塔德格說他死了倒比那樣活著好些時，他便抓住那男孩，把他的頭扭正，於是他便完好如初了。

title.en: Ciabhan and Cliodna's Wave
title.zh: 基亞班與克莉奧德娜之浪

region.en: Tonn Cliodhna (Glandore strand), Co. Cork, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭科克郡格蘭多爾海濱

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. XII, eBook #14465

summary.en: Ciabhan of the Curling Hair, the most beautiful young man of the world, is sent away from the Fianna for jealousy's sake and puts to sea; a rider on a dark grey horse rides under nine waves and rises with the tenth, and carries him to the Land of Promise. There Cliodna of the Fair Hair, who never loved before, gives him her love and sails away with him; but at Teite's Strand treachery plays her asleep with music, a great wave sweeps her off the strand, and the wave that took her bears her name for ever.
summary.zh: 鬈髮之基亞班為世間最美少年，因眾人妒忌而遭芬恩遣離，遂獨舟出海；一騎黑灰馬者潛行九浪、第十浪浮出，引他抵應許之地。彼處從未愛過人的仙姬克莉奧德娜對他一見傾心，隨他乘舟離去；然於泰特海濱，叛者以樂聲使她入睡，巨浪將她捲走。那浪因她得名，永存於世。

sensitivity.note: Tonn Cliodhna at Glandore is one of Ireland's three great waves; the drowning of the fairy bride at the strand is a wave-etiology. Coordinates are the traditional wave site.

passages.text: Ciabhan of the Curling Hair, the king of Ulster's son, was the most beautiful of the young men of the world at that time, but the Fianna grew tired of him because there was not a woman of their women but gave him her love, and Finn had to send him away at the last. He came to the Strand of the Cairn, saw a curragh with a narrow stern of copper, and put out to sea; great white shouting waves rose about him, every one the size of a mountain. Then he saw a rider coming towards him on a dark grey horse having a golden bridle, that would be under the sea for the length of nine waves and would rise with the tenth wave, and no wet on him at all. "What reward would you give to whoever would bring you out of this great danger?" "That you would give your service to whoever would give you his help," said Ciabhan, and he put his hand into the rider's hand, and was drawn on to the horse till they reached the shore of Tir Tairngaire, the Land of Promise.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. XII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 捲髮的基亞班，阿爾斯特國王之子，是當時世上最俊美的青年，但芬尼亞人漸漸厭倦了他，因為他們的女人中沒有一個不把愛慕獻給他的，最後芬恩不得不把他打發走。他來到石塚灘，看見一艘船尾狹窄、以銅製成的皮划艇，便出海而去；巨大的白色呼嘯波濤在他四周湧起，每一道都有山那麼大。接著他看見一名騎手騎著一匹深灰色的馬向他而來，那馬配著金色的韁繩，能在海底待上九道浪的時間，到第十道浪時便升起，而他身上全然不濕。「無論是誰把你從這巨大的危險中帶出來，你會給他什麼報酬？」「你會為任何給你幫助的人效勞，」基亞班說，於是他把手放進那騎手的手中，被拉上了馬，直到他們抵達提爾泰恩蓋爾——應許之地的海岸。

passages.text: There was a feast made ready in Manannan's city, and when a clown had done his trick with nine willow rods, he put the rods in Ciabhan's hand, and Ciabhan stood up and did the feat before them all. Gebann, a chief Druid, had a daughter, Cliodna of the Fair Hair, that had never given her love to any man; but when she saw Ciabhan she gave him her love, and agreed to go away with him on the morrow. They went down to the landing-place and got into a curragh, and went on till they came to Teite's Strand in the south of Ireland.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. XII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 馬納南的城中備好了宴席，當一個丑角用九根柳條表演完他的把戲後，他把柳條放到基亞班手中，基亞班便站起身來，在眾人面前表演了這套技藝。格班，一位首領德魯伊，有一個女兒，名叫金髮的克利奧德娜，她從未把愛獻給任何男子；但當她看見基亞班時，便把愛獻給了他，並同意次日與他一同離去。他們下到登陸處，上了皮划艇，一路前行，直到來到愛爾蘭南部的泰特灘。

passages.text: Ciabhan came on shore and went looking for deer under the thick branches of the wood, and he left the young girl in the boat on the strand. But the people of Manannan's house came after them having forty ships, and Iuchnu, that was in the curragh with Cliodna, did treachery, and played music to her till she lay down in the boat and fell asleep; and then a great wave came up on the strand and swept her away. And the wave got its name from Cliodna of the Fair Hair, that will be long remembered.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. XII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 基亞班上到岸上，在茂密的樹枝下尋找鹿，把那年少的姑娘留在灘上的船裡。但馬納南家中的人帶著四十艘船追了上來，而與克利奧德娜同在皮划艇上的尤赫努行了背叛之事，為她奏樂，直到她躺倒在船中睡去；接著一道巨浪湧上灘頭，把她捲走了。那道浪便因金髮的克利奧德娜而得名，她將長久被人銘記。

title.en: Tadg's Voyage to the Lake Island
title.zh: 塔格之湖島遠航

region.en: Inislocha, western ocean (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西洋湖島（象徵定位）

period: Medieval Irish voyage-tale tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. XIV, eBook #14465

summary.en: Tadg son of Cian sails a forty-oxhide curragh to recover his wife and brothers, carried off by the king of Fresen, and is driven through wonder-islands — rams nine-horned as big as horses, birds whose eggs sprout feathers on the eaters — to Inislocha, the Lake Island. There he meets Cesair, first woman of Ireland, now living for ever; Connla of the Red Hair with his fairy bride; and Cliodna of the Fair Hair, who gives him a cup of wine-from-water and a prophecy of his death by a wild deer's wound in the green valley by the Boyne.
summary.zh: 吉安之子塔格乘四十牛皮大舟出海，尋找被弗雷森王擄走的妻子與兄弟；航經奇異群島——角如駿馬之九角公羊、食蛋生羽之奇鳥——終至湖島伊尼斯拉哈。彼處他遇見永生於此的愛爾蘭首位女子塞塞爾、與仙姬相伴的紅髮康拉、以及仙姬克莉奧德娜；她賜他化水為酒之杯，並預言他將死於博因綠谷野鹿之傷。

sensitivity.note: A full immram grafted onto the historical Tadg genealogy (Cian, father of Brian Boru's line); the island sequence is a Census of wonder-islands in the voyage genre. Cross-tradition parallel: voyage over the sea to islands of undying women.

passages.text: Tadg, son of Cian, was going his next heir's round into the west of Munster when Cathmann, king of the country of Fresen, slipped ashore with nine ships and took away Tadg's wife Liban and his two brothers, and put hardship on them — Eoghan to work a common ferry, Airnelach to cut firing, all their food barley seed and muddy water. Tadg escaped by his courage and the use of his sword, and made orders for a curragh that would be fit for a long voyage, with forty ox-hides of hard red leather soaked in bark, and masts and oars and pitch and everything that was wanting, and they put in every sort of meat and drink and clothes that would last a year.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. XIV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 基安之子塔德格正巡行他的繼承人之地，前往芒斯特西部時，弗雷森之國的國王卡特曼帶著九艘船悄悄登岸，擄走了塔德格的妻子莉班和他的兩個兄弟，並使他們受苦——埃奧甘去划一艘公共渡船，艾爾內拉赫去砍柴，他們的食物盡是大麥種子和泥水。塔德格憑著勇氣和劍術逃脫，並下令造一艘適合遠航的皮划艇，用四十張浸過樹皮的堅硬紅皮革作船身，還有桅杆、槳、瀝青以及一切所需之物，他們又裝上各種足以維持一年的肉食、飲料和衣物。

passages.text: They set out over the stormy heavy flood; on they rowed through twenty days and twenty nights till they got sight of a high land, and found it filled with sheep as big as horses, and one great ram of them all had nine horns, and he charged on Tadg's chief men, and Tadg killed him with a lucky cast of his spear that there was no escape from. On two islands after that were flocks of wonderful birds, and when some of the men began eating their eggs, feathers began to grow out on them on the moment, and dropped off again as quick as they came when they went bathing.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. XIV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們在風暴肆虐、沉重洶湧的洪濤上出發；他們划了二十個晝夜，直到望見一片高地，發現那裡滿是像馬一樣大的羊，其中有一隻巨大的公羊長著九隻角，它向塔德格的首領們衝去，塔德格以一記無可閃避的幸運投矛將牠殺死。此後又經過兩座島嶼，島上有成群的奇異鳥類，當一些人開始吃牠們的蛋時，羽毛立刻在他們身上長了出來，而當他們去洗澡時，羽毛又來得快去得也快，隨即脫落。

passages.text: They came at last to a beautiful inver with green hills about it, and through apple gardens and a plain with a dew of honey over it, with a strong dun on every one of three steep hills. On the nearest hill a white-bodied woman welcomed Tadg: the dun of white marble was the home of the royal line of the kings of Ireland, and this island was Inislocha, the Lake Island. In the middle dun of gold he found Cesair, the first that ever reached Ireland, living for ever since she and the men that were with her came out of that dark unquiet land, and she told him every king and chief man of power in Ireland — Parthalon and Nemed, Firbolgs and Tuatha de Danaan — was in the dun beyond.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. XIV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們終於來到一處美麗的河口，四周環繞著青翠的山丘，穿過蘋果園和一片覆著蜜露的平原，三座陡峭的山丘上各有一座堅固的堡壘。在最近的那座山上，一位肌膚白皙的女子迎接塔德格：那座白色大理石的堡壘是愛爾蘭諸王王族的居所，而這座島便是伊尼斯洛哈，即湖之島。在那座金色的中央堡壘中，他見到了塞薩爾——她是第一個抵達愛爾蘭的人，自她與同行的男子們走出那片黑暗不安之地以來，便一直永生至今；她告訴他，愛爾蘭每一位國王與有權勢的首領——帕薩隆與涅米德、菲爾博格人與達南神族——都在更遠的那座堡壘之中。

passages.text: On the third hill were two comely lovers, a boy and a girl with gold chains about their necks; the boy had a sweet-smelling apple in his hand of which he would eat a third part, and it would never be less, and neither age nor sorrow could touch them that tasted it. "I am son to Conn of the Hundred Battles," he said; "it is Connla I am, and it is this girl of many shapes that brought me here." And Cliodna of the Fair Hair gave Tadg a green cup that turned water to wine, and warned him to keep it from escaping his hand, for at whatever time it escaped him his death would not be far away — a wandering wild deer would wound him in the green valley at the side of the Boinn, and after that strangers would put an end to him.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. XIV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第三座山丘上有一對俊美的戀人，一個男孩和一個女孩，頸上戴著金鍊；男孩手中拿著一顆芬芳的蘋果，他會吃去三分之一，而它永遠不會減少，凡是嘗過它的人，無論衰老或悲傷都無法觸及他們。「我是百戰之康的兒子，」他說；「我就是康拉，是這位多變形貌的姑娘把我帶到這裡來的。」而金髮的克利奧德娜給了塔德格一隻綠杯，能將水化為酒，並警告他要防止它從手中逃脫，因為無論何時它從他手中逃脫，他的死期便不遠了——一頭遊蕩的野鹿會在波因河畔的綠谷中傷他，此後陌生人將終結他的性命。

title.en: Laeghaire Crimthann's Raid into Magh Mell
title.zh: 萊格爾·克里姆坦遠征幸福平原

region.en: Loch na nEan (Lake of Birds), Co. Galway, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭戈爾韋郡鳥湖（象徵定位）

period: Medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. XV, eBook #14465

summary.en: Fiachna of the Sidhe rises from the Lake of Birds to ask mortal help: his wife has been carried off by Goll, king of a people of Magh Mell, the Happy Plain. Laeghaire son of Crimthan Cass goes down into the lake with fifty fighting men, kills Goll in battle, restores the woman to Fiachna, and is rewarded with Fiachna's daughter Deorgreine, a Tear of the Sun, and fifty women for his fifty men — and for a year and a day the Sidhe keep them in the Happy Plain.
summary.zh: 仙族菲亞克納自鳥湖現身，請求凡人相助：其妻被幸福平原之王戈爾擄去。克里姆坦之子萊格爾率五十戰士入湖，陣斬戈爾，將女子歸還菲亞克納，並得菲亞克納之女「太陽之淚」德奧格萊恩為妻，其五十戰士各得一名仙女，眾人在幸福平原留居一年又一日。

sensitivity.note: A mortal raid into the underwater otherworld (descent-underworld by way of a lake); the sithchean (year and a day) elapsed among the Sidhe marks the otherworld-time motif. Lake pin symbolic; Magh Mell has no earthly coordinates.

passages.text: Laeghaire, son of the King of Connacht, Crimthan Cass, was out one day with his father near Loch na-n Ean, the Lake of Birds, and they saw a man coming to them through the mist, with long golden-yellow hair streaming after him, a gold-hilted sword at his belt, two five-barbed darts in his hand, and a five-folded crimson cloak about his shoulders. "I am come to look for the help of fighting men," said the stranger; "my name is Fiachna, son of Betach, of the men of the Sidhe; my wife was taken from my pillow and brought away by Eochaid, son of Sal; I killed him, and now she is gone to a brother's son of his, Goll, son of Dalbh, king of a people of Magh Mell. Seven battles I gave him, but they all went against me, and on this very day there is another to be fought, and I am come to ask help."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. XV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 康諾特國王克林坦·卡斯之子萊格爾，有一天與父親在鳥之湖——洛克納恩湖附近外出，他們看見一個人穿過迷霧向他們走來，金黃色的長髮在身後飄揚，腰間佩著金柄寶劍，手中握著兩支五倒鉤的飛鏢，肩上披著五疊的深紅斗篷。「我來尋求戰士的援助，」那陌生人說；「我名叫菲亞赫納，是貝塔赫之子，屬希德族之人；我的妻子被人從我的枕邊奪走，是薩爾之子埃奧海德所為；我殺了他，如今她已去了他兄弟之子——達爾布之子戈爾那裡，他是瑪格梅爾一族的國王。我與他交戰七次，但全都敗於我手，而就在今日還有一場要打，我特來求助。」

passages.text: Fiachna went down into the lake, for it was out of it he had come, and Laegaire went down into it after him, fifty fighting men along with him. They saw a strong place before them and a company of armed men, and Goll, son of Dalbh, at the head of them. The two fifties attacked one another, and Goll fell, but Laeghaire and his fifty made a great slaughter of their enemies, so that not one of them made his escape. Laeghaire and his men went on to the dun of Magh Mell, and he called out to the men about it: "Your king has got his death, your chief men have fallen, let the woman come out, and I will give you your own lives." They agreed to that, and brought the woman out, and she made a complaint that got the name of "The Lament of the Daughter of Eochaid the Dumb." And that night Fiachna's daughter, Deorgreine, a Tear of the Sun, was given to Laeghaire as his wife, and fifty other women were given to his fifty fighting men, and they stopped with them there to the end of a year.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. XV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 菲亞赫納下到湖中，因為他正是從湖中出來的，萊格爾也隨他下到湖中，帶著五十名戰士同行。他們看見前方有一座堅固的堡壘和一群武裝之人，戈爾——達爾布之子——為其首領。兩隊五十人互相攻擊，戈爾倒下了，但萊格爾和他的五十人對敵人展開了大屠殺，以致無一人逃脫。萊格爾和他的手下繼續前往瑪格梅爾的堡壘，他向周圍的人喊道：「你們的國王已死，你們的首領們已倒下，讓那女子出來，我便饒你們性命。」他們同意了，將那女子帶出，她發出一聲哀訴，因而得了「啞者埃奧海德之女的哀歌」之名。當夜，菲亞赫納的女兒德奧格雷內——意為「太陽之淚」——被許配給萊格爾為妻，另有五十名女子許配給他的五十名戰士，他們便與她們在那裡停留至一年之終。

title.en: Ekalavya's Thumb
title.zh: 以卡拉維亞的拇指

region.en: Nishadha forest (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 尼沙陀森林（象徵性定位）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Ekalavya episode

summary.en: Rejected by Drona because of his forest birth, the Nishada prince Ekalavya built the master's statue in the woods and taught himself archery before it - becoming better than Arjuna. When Drona came demanding his fee, the boy cut off his own thumb and laid it before him: the epic's most-cited, most-contested parable of caste, loyalty and the price of a guru's word.
summary.zh: 因出身林野而被德羅納拒收的尼沙陀王子以卡拉維亞，在林中立師之像，對像自習射術——技藝勝過阿周那。當德羅納索其學資時，少年自斷拇指奉上：史詩中最常被引用、爭論最烈的關於種姓、忠誠與師言之價的寓言。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition and politically contested (caste readings); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Drona refused the forest-born boy as a pupil - the teaching was reserved for princes - and Ekalavya went home, made a clay image of the master in the forest, and practiced before it until his hand was as true as the image's face.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 德羅納拒絕收這名林中出生的男孩為徒——此教導專為王子們保留——於是埃卡拉維亞回到家中，在森林裡用泥土塑成師父的像，在像前練習，直到他的手如那像的面容一般精準。

passages.text: When dogs ran barking through the grove, seven arrows filled their mouths before they could cry; the princes traced the shot to a dark youth with a bow, and Arjuna went to his teacher, wounded in his pride: you promised me the best archer.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當群犬吠叫著奔過樹林時，七支箭在牠們出聲之前便已射滿牠們的口；王子們循著箭跡找到一名手持弓的黝黑少年，阿周那滿懷自尊受創地去找他的老師：你曾許諾我成為最優秀的射手。

passages.text: Drona came and demanded his fee: thy right thumb. Ekalavya, glad to pay a master he had never been allowed to serve, cut it off at a stroke and held it out; his archery was gone in that instant, and the epic left the cost standing on the page for every age to argue.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 德羅納前來，索討他的束脩：你的右手拇指。艾卡拉維亞欣然願付給一位從未獲准侍奉的師父，一刀便將它切下，雙手奉上；他的箭術在那一瞬間便消失了，而史詩讓這代價留在書頁上，供每一個時代爭辯。

canonical_translation: K. M. Ganguli, 1883-96 (public domain)

title.en: Karna's Basket: The Son of the Sun
title.zh: 迦爾納的竹籃：太陽之子

region.en: Ganges bank, Anga kingdom (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 恆河畔，鴦伽王國（象徵性定位）

period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, the birth of Karna

summary.en: The maiden Kunti, testing a boon, called the Sun and bore a child already armored: born with golden ear-rings and a breastplate grown into his skin. Afraid, she set the basket on the river; it floated to the charioteer Adhiratha, who raised the boy as his son - and Karna lived his whole life paying for a birth his mother hid.
summary.zh: 少女恭蒂試驗恩賜，召日神而生下一個已然披甲的孩子：生而戴金環，胸鎧與皮肉同長。她因懼而將竹籃置於河上；竹籃漂至御者阿底羅陀之處，他將男孩養作己子——迦爾納的整個人生都在償付母親隱瞞的那次出生。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The boon was meant for practice; the Sun came as a bridegroom in full glory, and Kunti, unmarried, bore a child already wearing armor and ear-rings of gold - a birth like a dawn. The basket was set on the river at dawn; it floated down past reeds and towns to the charioteer's household, where Radha the childless took the armored boy for her own and named him Karna, the ear-ringed. The armor was his glory and his doom: a prince's courtesy could not outface a charioteer's son - and the sun-son's whole career was a bid to be honored as the person the armor proved he was.
