passages.text: The chariot flew at its rider's thought: Sita seated in state, the monkey commanders in their fur, the sky-road taken south to north over a war's whole geography. Each stop was a rite of return: the bridge of stones, Rishyashringa's hermitage, Bharata's hut outside the capital - the exile's road traveled backward at flying speed. Ayodhya heard the drums and lit every lamp in the city for the midnight entry: fourteen years of darkness ending in a street of fire - the charter of the festival of lights.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 戰車隨馭者心念而飛馳：悉多端坐其中，猴軍統帥們身披毛皮，循天路自南向北，飛越整場戰爭的地理。每一處停留皆是一場歸返之禮：石橋、哩舍舍陵伽的隱修院、婆羅多在都城外的茅舍——流放之路以飛行之速逆向重行。阿逾陀聽聞鼓聲，為這午夜歸來點亮城中每一盞燈：十四年的黑暗終結於一條火光之街——此即燈節之典章。

canonical_translation: R. T. H. Griffith, 1870-74 (public domain)

title.en: Kapila's Fire and the Sons of Sagara
title.zh: 迦毘羅之火與薩伽羅之子

region.en: Ocean depths (symbolic pin at Sagar Island)
region.zh: 海洋深處（象徵性定位於薩伽羅島）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book IV (dynasty of Sagara), c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book IV, the sons of Sagara and Kapila's fire

summary.en: King Sagara's sixty thousand sons dug the ocean in search of a stolen horse and burned everything in their way. The sage Kapila, interrupted in meditation by the horde, opened his eyes and burned all sixty thousand to ash - souls imprisoned in unburnt bones that no water could wash. Many generations later, Bhagiratha's descent of the Ganga (over Shiva's hair) freed them: the ocean is called Sagara for the diggers.
summary.zh: 王薩伽羅的六萬子為尋被竊之馬掘穿大洋，沿途焚燬一切。仙人迦毘羅於禪定中被打擾，睜眼之間，六萬人皆化為灰——其靈魂囚於水洗不去的未化之骨。數代之後，跋吉羅陀引恆河下降（經濕婆之髮）而釋之：大洋至今以掘者之名為名（薩伽羅）。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (Sagar Island rites); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The sacrificial horse was stolen to the underworld sea; Sagara's sixty thousand sons dug after it, turning the earth into the great basin of the ocean in their search. The sage Kapila sat in the depths where their spades arrived; the army's clamor broke his meditation, and one opened eye was a furnace - sixty thousand sons of a king burned to a single ash-heap. The ashes were the debt: no rite could free the souls until the Ganga herself came down to touch them - and the sea the diggers made still carries their king's name.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book IV (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 祭祀之馬被盜至下界之海；薩竭羅的六萬個兒子掘地追尋，在搜尋中將大地挖成了大洋的巨大盆地。仙人迦毗羅端坐於他們鐵鍬所至的深處；軍隊的喧囂擾亂了他的禪定，一隻睜開的眼睛便是一座熔爐——一位國王的六萬個兒子被燒成一堆灰燼。那灰燼便是債：在恆河女神親自降下觸及他們之前，任何儀式都無法解脫這些亡魂——而掘地者所造之海，至今仍載著他們國王的名字。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: Rama and Shambuka: The Ascetic Death
title.zh: 羅摩與首薄迦：苦行者的死亡

region.en: Ayodhya outskirts (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿逾陀城郊（象徵性定位）

period: Ramayana of Valmiki, Uttara Kanda (critical edition appendix), c. 2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE (Griffith translation, 1870-74)

source.work: The Ramayan of Valmiki, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1870-74), Uttara Kanda, Shambuka episode

summary.en: A child of Ayodhya died young; the seers traced the cause to a disorder in the order of castes: a Shudra named Shambuka was practicing austerities reserved for the twice-born, upside-down on a tree-branch. Rama went, confirmed the tale, and struck off the ascetic's head - and the child revived. The episode is the epic's hardest scene: dharma as hierarchy enforced by the ideal king, and the modern argument about it has never closed.
summary.zh: 阿逾陀之一孩童夭折；仙人們究其因於種姓秩序之亂：一名首陀羅名首薄迦者，倒懸於樹枝之上，修習唯再生者可修之苦行。羅摩前往，證實其事，斬下苦行者之頭——孩童於是復活。此幕是史詩最沉重的一幕：正法被理想之王以等級執行；而圍繞它的現代論爭從未閉合。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition and politically contested (caste politics); classified 'myth'. The contested modern readings are recorded here.

passages.text: The diagnosis of the kingdom's grief came from the seers: an ascetic of the wrong caste was heating the world with penance, and a child of the city paid the price. Rama found Shambuka hanging head-down on the branch, emaciated and luminous, and asked him his name and his vow; the answer confirmed the seers' account. The sword fell - and the dead child sat up in Ayodhya as the ascetic's life went out: the episode has made the Uttara Kanda the most argued section of the epic, and modern retellings often refuse it outright.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Ramayana, Uttara Kanda (Griffith 1870-74); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 王國之悲的診斷出自諸位仙人：一名錯種姓的苦行者正以苦行炙烤世界，而城中一名孩童付出了代價。羅摩發現商菩迦倒懸於枝頭，形容枯槁而身放光明，便問其名與其誓願；回答印證了諸仙之言。劍落——阿逾陀城中死去的孩童坐了起來，而苦行者的生命隨之熄滅：此一插曲使《後篇》成為全史詩中最受爭議的部分，現代改編往往逕直棄之不取。

canonical_translation: R. T. H. Griffith, 1870-74 (public domain)

title.en: Arthur of Britain Steals Finn's Hounds
title.zh: 不列顛之亞瑟竊取芬恩獵犬

region.en: Inver Mara Gamiach, coast of Britain
region.zh: 不列顛海岸卡拉馬基河口

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. I, eBook #14465

summary.en: Arthur son of the King of Britain takes service with Finn, then runs off across the sea with the three hounds Bran, Sceolan and Adhnuall. Finn reads the theft in his pale-gold basin of water and sends nine champions after them; Goll spares Arthur's life, and the captive prince bonds with Finn and follows him till he dies. From the bay mare Goll seized on the way descends all the horses of the Fianna; and Finn's hounds had been lost before — to a witch whose enchanted breath shut three times fifty of them in the Mound of the Hounds.
summary.zh: 不列顛王子亞瑟曾投效芬恩，卻攜三犬布蘭、斯克奧蘭、艾德努爾渡海而逃。芬恩於淡金水盆中窺知竊案，遣九位英雄追討；戈爾饒亞瑟一命，被俘王子向芬恩立誓終身相隨。途中戈爾奪得的母馬，其後代即菲亞納全部馬匹；此外芬恩之犬曾被女巫以魔息關入犬冢三次五十隻，永不再出。

sensitivity.note: This Arthur is a Fenian-cycle British prince, not the Arthur of the romances — a useful cross-cycle witness. Scrying in a basin of pale gold parallels Manannan's tokens; the witch's hound-mound (Duma na nCon) is a dindsenchas-style etiology. Pin symbolic on the British coast.

passages.text: Arthur, son of the King of Britain, came one time to take service with Finn, and three times nine men along with him. And while Arthur was there he took notice of three of Finn's hounds, Bran, and Sceolan and Adhnuall, and he made a plan to go away across the sea, himself and his three nines, bringing those three hounds along with him. So he did that, and the place where they landed was Inver Mara Gamiach on the coast of Britain, and they went to the mountain of Lodan, son of Lir, to hunt on it.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 不列顛國王之子亞瑟，有一次前來為芬恩效力，隨他同來的還有三倍九名部眾。亞瑟在那裡期間，注意到了芬恩的三隻獵犬——布蘭、斯克蘭與阿德努爾——便謀劃渡海離去，他本人與他的三個九人，帶著那三隻獵犬同行。他果然如此而行，登陸之地乃是不列顛海岸的因弗馬拉加米亞赫，他們又前往里爾之子洛丹的山上狩獵。

passages.text: As to the Fianna, after their hunting was done they gathered together on the hill, and all Finn's hounds were counted — three hundred full-grown hounds he had and two hundred whelps, and to be counting them was like counting the branches on a tree. On this day Bran and Sceolan and Adhnuall were missing. Then Finn sent for a long-shaped basin of pale gold, and water in it, and he put his face in the water, and his hand over his face, and it was showed him what had happened, and he said: "The King of Britain's son has brought away the hound. And let nine men be chosen out to follow after them."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 至於費尼亞戰團，狩獵結束之後，他們齊聚於山丘之上，清點芬恩所有的獵犬——他有三百隻成犬與兩百隻幼犬，清點牠們猶如清點樹上的枝條。這一日，布蘭、斯克蘭與阿德努爾卻不見了。於是芬恩命人取來一隻淡金色的長形盆，盆中盛水，他將臉俯入水中，以手覆面，所發生之事便向他顯現，他說道：「不列顛國王之子帶走了那獵犬。且選出九人前去追趕他們。」

passages.text: Arthur of Britain and his people were sitting on a hunting mound just at that time, and the nine men of the Fianna made an attack on them and killed all of them but Arthur, that Goll, son of Morna, put his two arms about and saved from death. Then they turned to go back to Ireland, bringing Arthur with them, and the three hounds; and as they were going, Goll saw a dark-grey horse and a bay mare that was not easy to get hold of, and he gave them into Oisin's hand, and he gave them on to Diarmuid. Arthur made bonds with Finn, and was his follower till he died.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 不列顛的亞瑟與其部眾恰在此時正坐在一座狩獵土丘上，費尼亞戰團的九人向他們發動攻擊，將他們盡數殺死，唯有亞瑟倖免——戈爾，莫爾納之子，以雙臂環抱將他救離死地。隨後他們轉身返回愛爾蘭，帶著亞瑟與那三隻獵犬同行；行進途中，戈爾看見一匹深灰色馬與一匹不易制服的棗紅母馬，便將牠們交到奧辛手中，奧辛又轉交給迪爾穆德。亞瑟與芬恩立下盟約，終其一生為其追隨者。

passages.text: And as to the mare, she bred eight times, at every birth eight foals, and it is of that seed came all the horses of the fair Fianna of the Gael, for they had used no horses up to that time. And that was not the only time Finn was robbed of some of his hounds, for a woman-Druid of the Tuatha de Danaan set her love on Finn, and he said, so long as there was another woman to be found in the world, he would not marry a witch; and one time three times fifty of Finn's hounds passed by the hill where she was, and she breathed on the hounds and shut them up in the hill, and they never came out again, and the place got the name of Duma na Conn, the Mound of the Hounds.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 至於那匹母馬，她一共生育了八次，每次生產都生下八匹小馬，而蓋爾人的費奧納勇士團所有駿馬，皆出自這血脈，因為在此之前他們從未使用過馬匹。而那並非芬恩唯一一次被奪去部分獵犬，因為圖阿薩·德·達南的一位女德魯伊愛上了芬恩，而他說，只要世上還找得到別的女人，他就不會娶一個女巫；有一次，芬恩的獵犬三倍五十隻經過她所在的那座山丘，她朝那些獵犬吹了一口氣，便將牠們封閉在山丘之中，牠們再也沒有出來，那地方因此得名杜瑪·納·康，意即「獵犬之丘」。

title.en: The Three Hags and the Hanks of Yarn at Ceiscoran
title.zh: 凱斯克蘭的三巫與紗束

region.en: Cave of Ceiscoran, Slieve League, Co. Donegal, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭多尼戈爾郡凱斯克蘭洞（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. II, eBook #14465

summary.en: To avenge Finn's great hunting, Conaran of the Tuatha de Danaan sends his three hag daughters to the mouth of a cave with enchanted hanks of yarn reeled on crooked holly-sticks. Champion after champion passes the hanks and collapses into weakness, to be bound and dragged into the cave — until Goll of Morna, the Flame of Battle, cuts two hags through with one blow, wrestles the oldest down, and spares her when she puts her body under the protection of his bravery and restores every man of the Fianna.
summary.zh: 為報復芬恩的大狩獵，神族科納蘭派三名巫婆女兒到洞穴口，以彎曲冬青杖上的魔紗束作祟。一個個英雄經過紗束便氣力盡失，被捆入洞中——直到戰火之焰戈爾一劍穿透兩巫，摔倒最年長者；她以身家性命托庇於他的勇武而得赦，將菲亞納眾人全數釋放。

sensitivity.note: The yarn-hank binding spell is a distinct Irish binding-magic motif (compare the binding of battles in Ulster tradition); the hag-battle inverts the fairy-mistress pattern. Pin symbolic at the traditional cave site.

passages.text: Finn called for a great hunt one time on the plains of Magh Chonaill and in the forest parts of Cairbre of the Nuts, and he himself went up to the top of Ceiscoran, and his two dogs Bran and Sceolan with him. Conaran, son of Imidd, of the Tuatha de Danaan, had the sway in Ceiscoran at that time, and when he heard the shouting and the cry of the hounds all around, he bade his three daughters that had a great share of enchantments to do vengeance on Finn for his hunting. The three women went to the opening of a cave that was in the hills, and there they sat down together, and put three strong enchanted hanks of yarn on crooked holly-sticks, and began to reel them off outside the cave.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一次，芬恩在馬格·科奈爾平原與凱爾布雷·納·努特（意即「堅果之凱爾布雷」）的森林地帶召集了一場盛大的狩獵，他親自登上凱斯可蘭山頂，他的兩隻獵犬布蘭與斯凱歐蘭隨行。圖阿薩·德·達南的伊米德之子科納蘭當時統治著凱斯可蘭，當他聽見四周獵犬的吠叫與呼喊聲，便吩咐他那三個深諳魔法妖術的女兒，要為芬恩的狩獵向他報復。那三個女人來到山間一個洞穴的洞口，一同坐下，將三束施了強力魔法的紗線掛在彎曲的冬青枝上，開始在洞外將它們繞解開來。

passages.text: They were not long there till Finn and Conan came towards them, and saw the three ugly old hags at their work, their coarse hair tossed, their eyes red and bleary, their teeth sharp and crooked, their arms very long, their nails like the tips of cows' horns, and the three spindles in their hands. Finn and Conan passed through the hanks of yarn to get a better look at the hags, and no sooner had they done that than a deadly trembling came on them and a weakness, and the bold hags took hold of them and put them in tight bonds.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她們在那裡沒待多久，芬恩與科南便朝她們走來，看見那三個醜陋的老巫婆正在勞作，她們粗亂的頭髮蓬散，雙眼通紅而昏花，牙齒尖銳而歪斜，雙臂極長，指甲如牛角尖端，手中握著三根紡錘。芬恩與科南穿過那些紗線束，想更清楚地看看那些巫婆，他們才一穿過，一陣致命的顫抖與虛弱便襲上他們，那些大膽的巫婆抓住他們，將他們緊緊捆綁起來。

passages.text: Two other men of the Fianna came up then, and the sons of Menhann along with them, and their strength went from them in the same way; and in the end the whole number of them, gentle and simple, were put in bonds by the hags and brought into the cave, while a great outcry of hounds calling for their masters began at the mouth of the cave. Then they saw coming towards them a very tall man that was Goll, son of Morna, the Flame of Battle, and the three hags went to meet him and fought a hard battle with him.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 費奧納勇士團的另外兩名男子隨後趕到，門漢之子們也與他們同行，他們的力氣也同樣離他們而去；最終他們全體，無論高貴或卑微，都被那些巫婆捆綁起來，帶進洞穴之中，而洞口則響起獵犬呼喚主人的巨大吠叫聲。接著他們看見一個非常高大的男子朝他們走來，那便是莫爾納之子戈爾，人稱「戰鬥之焰」，那三個巫婆上前迎戰，與他展開一場艱苦的搏鬥。

passages.text: Great anger came on Goll, and he raised up his sword, and with one blow he cut the two that were nearest him through and through; and the oldest of the three women wound her arms about him, and they wrestled together till Goll gave her a great twist and threw her on the ground, and tied her fast with the straps of a shield. But the hag said: "O champion that was never worsted, I put my body and my life under the protection of your bravery. And it is better for you to get Finn and the Fianna safe and whole than to have my blood." With that Goll set her free, and she took off the fastenings, first from Fergus of the True Lips and the other learned men of the Fianna, and after that from Finn and Oisin and the twenty-nine sons of Morna and all the rest, and Fergus made great praises of Goll for all he had done.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 戈爾勃然大怒，他舉起劍，一擊便將離他最近的兩個巫婆從頭到腳劈成兩半；三個女人中最年長的那個用雙臂纏住他，他們扭打在一起，直到戈爾猛地一扭，將她摔在地上，並用盾牌的皮帶將她牢牢綁住。但那巫婆說道：「啊，從未敗北的勇士，我將我的身體與性命託付於你的英勇之下。你讓芬恩與費奧納勇士團安然無恙、完好無損，總比取我性命要好。」於是戈爾便放了她，她解開了捆綁，先從真言之舌費格斯與費奧納勇士團其他博學之士身上解開，之後再從芬恩、歐辛、莫爾納的二十九個兒子以及其餘所有人身上解開，費格斯對戈爾所做的一切大加讚頌。

title.en: Donn son of Midhir and the Hidden House under the Snow
title.zh: 米德之子東恩與雪下隱宅

region.en: Slieve-nam-Ban (Mountain of the Women), Co. Tipperary, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭蒂珀雷里郡女人山

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. III, eBook #14465

summary.en: A beautiful fawn lures Finn and six men across Ireland to Slieve-nam-Ban and vanishes into the earth as heavy snow falls; Caoilte finds a lighted house of the Sidhe, and Donn son of Midhir tells how he and twenty-eight brothers refused hostages to Bodb Dearg, were threatened with the walling-up of their dwelling, and fight three battles a year with the Men of Dea. Finn and the Fianna stand with them at fall of night and slaughter ten hundred ten score and ten, until Lir of Sidhe Fionnachaidh ends the feud with a wall of fire and a wall of water.
summary.zh: 一頭美麗母鹿引芬恩與六人穿越愛爾蘭至女人山，在大雪中遁入地下。卡爾特尋得燈火通明的仙族宅邸；米德之子東恩講述：因拒絕向波德·迪爾格獻人質，兄弟二十九人遭封居之威脅，每年與神族交戰三次。芬恩與菲亞納於夜幕時分馳援，斬敵一千二百一十，直到利爾以火牆與水牆結束世仇。

sensitivity.note: The hidden house (bruiden) under a fairy hill is a hall-myth of the Fenian-Sidhe interface; hostage-refusal and the walling-up threat mirror the Bodb Dearg kingship records. The fawn-lure repeats the Sadbh pattern — in this cycle deer of the Sidhe are recurrent envoys. Pin is the named Slieve-na-mBan.

passages.text: One time the Fianna were at their hunting at the island of Toraig to the north of Ireland, and they roused a fawn that was very wild and beautiful, and Finn and six of his men followed after it through the whole country, till they came to Slieve-nam-Ban. And there the fawn put down its head and vanished into the earth. A heavy snow began to fall then that bent down the tops of the trees, and the courage and the strength went from the Fianna, and Finn said to Caoilte: "Is there any place we can find shelter to-night?" Caoilte made himself supple and went over the elbow of the hill southward, and he saw a house full of light, with cups and horns and bowls of different sorts in it, and he knew it to be a house of the Sidhe, and he went in. On the one side he saw eight-and-twenty armed men, each of them having a well-shaped woman beside him; and on the other side six nice young girls, yellow-haired; and in the middle a young girl with a harp, playing and singing, and they were all making mirth around her.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一次，費奧納勇士團在愛爾蘭北部的托拉格島狩獵，他們驚起了一隻非常野性而美麗的小鹿，芬恩與他的六名手下跟隨牠穿越了整個鄉野，直到他們來到斯利夫·納姆·班。在那裡，那小鹿低下頭，消失於地中。接著開始下起大雪，將樹梢都壓彎了，勇氣與力氣從費奧納勇士團身上離去，芬恩對凱爾特說：「今晚我們能找到什麼地方棲身嗎？」凱爾特靈活地一躍，越過山丘的肘部向南而去，他看見一座燈火通明的房屋，裡面擺著各式各樣的杯、角杯與碗，他認出那是希德之屋，便走了進去。他一邊看見二十八名武裝男子，每人身旁都有一位姿容姣好的女子；另一邊則是六名黃髮的漂亮少女；而在中央，一名少女手持豎琴，彈奏歌唱，眾人皆圍著她嬉戲作樂。

passages.text: "Those eight-and-twenty armed men," said the tall man, "had the one father and mother with myself; we are the sons of Midhir of the Yellow Hair, and our mother is Fionnchaem, the fair beautiful daughter of the King of the Sidhe of Monaid in the east. At one time the Tuatha de Danaan gave the kingship to Bodb Dearg, son of the Dagda, and he began to ask hostages of myself and of my brothers; but we said that till all the rest of the Men of Dea had given them, we would not give them. Bodb Dearg said then to our father: 'Unless you will put away your sons, we will wall up your dwelling-place on you.' So the eight-and-twenty brothers of us came out to look for a place for ourselves, and we are here ever since, and my own name is Donn, son of Midhir.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「那二十八名披甲之士，」高個子說，「與我同出一父一母；我們是黃髮米迪爾之子，我們的母親是東方莫奈德仙丘之王的女儿、美麗的芬海姆。曾有一時，達努神族將王位授予達格達之子博德·德爾格，他便開始向我和我的兄弟們索取人質；但我們說，除非其餘所有女神之子都已交出人質，我們才肯交出。博德·德爾格於是對我們的父親說：『除非你遣散你的兒子們，否則我們就要把你的居所封砌起來，將你困在其中。』於是我們二十八個兄弟便出來為自己尋覓一處居所，自此便一直在此，而我自己的名字是米迪爾之子唐恩。」

passages.text: The Men of Dea come three times in every year to give battle to us on the green outside." Finn and the Fianna stood with them at the fall of night, for that was the hour the Men of Dea chose to do them the most harm, and from the covering time of evening to the edge of the morning they fought the battle, and the loss of the Tuatha de Danaan was no less a number than ten hundred ten score and ten men. Then Lir of Sidhe Fionnachaidh, the oldest of them, gave his advice: let every one carry away his dead, "and as for us that stop here, let a wall of fire be made about us on the one side, and a wall of water on the other side."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 女神之子每年三次前來，在外面的綠地上與我們交戰。」芬恩與費尼亞眾人在夜幕降臨時與他們並肩而立，因為那正是女神之子選來對他們造成最大傷害的時辰；從傍晚的掩蔽之時直到清晨的邊際，他們一直在交戰，而達努神族的損失不下於一千一百一十人。於是，最年長的希德·芬納凱之李爾獻上他的計策：讓每個人帶走自己的死者，「至於我們這些留在此處的人，就在我們一邊築起一道火牆，另一邊築起一道水牆。」

title.en: Caoilte Carries Off the Physician Luibra
title.zh: 卡爾特擄走醫師盧伊布拉

region.en: Ford of the Slaine, plain of Leinster, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭倫斯特平原斯拉因淺灘

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. III, eBook #14465

summary.en: A year of three battles under the hill leaves Conn son of Midhir dead and two Fianna near death, their wounds held off their bodies with bent hazel sticks. Donn knows only one physician can cure them — the Tuatha de Danaan's own, who gathers healing herbs at dawn while the dew is on them. "Living or dead, I will bring him with me," says Caoilte, and under a Druid mist he and two sons of Midhir carry the physician off; the cure is promised under threat of the head, and within nine days the men are sound again.
summary.zh: 一年三戰令米德之子康恩陣亡，兩名菲亞納戰士瀕死，傷處須以彎榛杖撐開衣物。東恩言唯有神族醫師可治——他每日黎明趁露采藥。「生死不論，我必帶他回來」，卡爾特與米德二子在德魯伊霧中將醫師擄走；以人頭為質索得醫術，九日之內傷者痊癒。

sensitivity.note: The dawn-dew herb gathering and nine-day cure reproduce Asclepieion-style healing logic in the Fenian frame; the forced conscription of the enemy's physician is a raid-law motif (fleet hostage-taking in Irish law). Tagged 'resurrection' for the wound-restoring function as in the Conn Crither record.

passages.text: Conn, son of Midhir, was killed in one of the battles; and as to the Fianna, there were so many wounds on them that the clothing was held off from their bodies with bent hazel sticks, and they lying in their beds, and two of them were like to die. "Good Donn," said Finn, "have you knowledge of any physician that can cure our men?" "I only know one physician could do that," said Donn; "a physician the Tuatha de Danaan have with them. And unless a wounded man has the marrow of his back cut through, he will get relief from that physician, the way he will be sound at the end of nine days." "How can we bring that man here, for those he is with are no good friends to us?" "He goes out every morning at break of day to gather healing herbs while the dew is on them." "Find some one, Donn," said Caoilte, "that will show me that physician, and, living or dead, I will bring him with me."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 米迪爾之子康恩在其中一場戰役中陣亡；至於費尼亞眾人，他們身上傷口如此之多，以致要用彎曲的榛木棍將衣物撐離他們的身體，而他們則躺在床上，其中兩人瀕臨死亡。「好唐恩，」芬恩說，「你可知道有哪位醫師能治好我們的人？」「我只知道有一位醫師能做到，」唐恩說，「那是女神之子身邊的一位醫師。只要傷者的脊背骨髓未被切斷，他就能從那位醫師那裡得到救治，九天之後便可痊癒。」「我們怎能將那人帶到此處，因為他身邊那些人對我們並不友善？」「他每天清晨破曉時分便出去採集藥草，趁露水還在其上之時。」「唐恩，」凱爾特說，「找個人來指給我看那位醫師，無論是死是活，我都要把他帶來。」

passages.text: Then Aedh and Flann, two of the sons of Midhir, rose up and went on before Caoilte to a green lawn with the dew on it, and there they saw a strong young man armed and having a cloak of the wool of the seven sheep of the Land of Promise, full of herbs of healing he was after gathering for the Men of Dea that were wounded in the battle. They ran at him together, and Caoilte took him by the shoulders, and they brought him away with them to the ford of the Slaine in the great plain of Leinster, and a Druid mist rose up about them that they could not be seen.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是米迪爾的兩個兒子艾德與弗蘭起身，先於凱爾特來到一片帶著露水的綠色草坪上，在那裡他們看見一個強壯的年輕人，全副武裝，披著一件用應許之地七隻羊的羊毛製成的斗篷，他剛為在戰役中受傷的女神之子採集了滿滿的療傷藥草。他們一同向他衝去，凱爾特抓住他的肩膀，他們便將他帶走，來到倫斯特大平原上斯萊恩河的淺灘，一層德魯伊迷霧在他們周圍升起，使他們無法被看見。

passages.text: Finn and Donn gave a great welcome to Luibra, the physician, and showed him their two comrades. "Those men can be cured if I get a good reward." "It will take nine days," said Luibra. "It is a good reward you will get, and this is what it is, your own life to be left to you; but if these young men are not healed, it is my own hand will strike off your head." And within nine days the physician had done a cure on them, and they were as well and as sound as before.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 芬恩與唐恩對醫師盧伊布拉致以盛大歡迎，並讓他看他們的兩位同伴。「只要我得到豐厚的報酬，這些人便能治癒。」「需要九天，」盧伊布拉說。「你會得到豐厚的報酬，就是這樣：留你一條性命；但若這些年輕人未能痊癒，便是我親手砍下你的頭顱。」而在九天之內，醫師便治好了他們，他們一如從前般健康完好。

title.en: The Feast of Teamhair: Finn Given Up for Lost
title.zh: 塔拉盛宴：芬恩被認定失踪

region.en: Teamhair (Hill of Tara), Co. Meath, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭米斯郡塔拉王丘

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. III, eBook #14465

summary.en: A year after Finn vanished under the hill, the High King opens the Feast of Teamhair and offers Goll the hunting-rights of Ireland; Goll refuses Finn's place until three years and all hope are gone. Seventeen queens of Finn's household are given safe sunny houses, Berngal keeps the spear and hound's collar Finn left him at their parting, and the Druid Cithruadh — whose every foretelling had come true — announces: before the feast is over you will see the Leader of the Fianna drinking at it.
summary.zh: 芬恩隱入仙丘一年後，至高王設塔拉盛宴，將愛爾蘭獵權許予戈爾；戈爾拒絕頂替——除非三年已過、眾人絕望。芬恩家室十七位夫人各獲安全宅邸；伯恩加爾珍藏分手時芬恩所贈長矛與犬項圈；德魯伊西斯魯——其預言從未落空——宣佈：盛宴未散，你們將見菲亞納之首於此舉杯。

sensitivity.note: The disappearance-and-search assembly is the fixed narrative hinge between Fenian episodes (a year and a quarter being the legal term of absence in Irish tradition). Cithruadh's oracle functions as the tale's plot-charm; retained as divination motif.

passages.text: It was after that time the High King sent a messenger to bring the Fianna to the Feast of Teamhair, and they all gathered to it, men and women, boys and heroes and musicians. Goll, son of Morna, was sitting at the feast beside the king. "It is a great loss you have had, Fianna of Ireland, losing your lord and your leader, Finn, son of Cumhal." "It is a great loss indeed," said Goll. "There has no greater loss fallen on Ireland since the loss of Lugh, son of Ethne. What orders will you give to the Fianna now, king?" "To yourself, Goll, I will give the right of hunting over all Ireland till we know if the loss of Finn is lasting." "I will not take Finn's place," said Goll, "till he has been wanting to us through the length of three years, and till no person in Ireland has any hope of seeing him again."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 正是在那之後，至高王派遣使者召費尼亞眾人前往塔拉之宴，他們全都聚集赴宴，男女老少、英雄與樂師皆在其中。莫爾納之子戈爾坐在國王身旁的宴席上。「你們遭受了巨大的損失，愛爾蘭的費尼亞眾人，失去了你們的君主與領袖、庫馬爾之子芬恩。」「這確實是巨大的損失，」戈爾說。「自埃斯尼之子盧格的損失以來，愛爾蘭再未遭受過比這更大的損失。國王，你現在要對費尼亞眾人下什麼命令？」「戈爾，我要授予你狩獵全愛爾蘭的權利，直到我們確知芬恩的損失是否長久。」「我不會取代芬恩的位置，」戈爾說，「直到他與我們分離滿三年之久，直到愛爾蘭再無一人抱有再見他的希望。」

passages.text: Then the king stood up, a smooth drinking-horn in his hand: "It would be a good thing, men of Ireland, if any one among you could get us news of Finn in hills or in secret places, or in rivers or invers, or in any house of the Sidhe in Ireland or in Alban." With that Berngal, the cow-owner from the borders of Slieve Fuad, said: "The day Finn came out from the north, following after a deer of the Sidhe, he put a sharp spear having a shining head in my hand, and a hound's collar along with it, and he bade me to keep them till he would meet me again in the same place." The High King called then to Cithruadh, the Druid, and he said: "It is much riches and many treasures Finn gave you, and tell us now is he living or is he dead?" "He is living," said Cithruadh; "but as to where he is, I will give no news of that, for he himself would not like me to give news of it." There was great joy among them, for everything Cithruadh had ever foretold had come true.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是國王站起身來，手持一隻光滑的飲酒角杯：「愛爾蘭的眾位男子啊，你們之中若有人能為我們打聽出芬恩的消息——無論他是在山丘間、在隱密之處、在河川中、在河口處，還是在愛爾蘭或阿爾班境內任何一座希德之屋中——那將是件好事。」聽罷，來自斯利夫富阿德邊境的牧牛人貝恩加爾說道：「那日芬恩從北方出來，追隨一頭希德的鹿，他將一柄矛頭閃亮的鋒利長矛交到我手中，連同一副獵犬項圈，並囑咐我保管這些物件，直到他在同一地點與我重逢。」至高王隨即召喚德魯伊基斯魯阿德，對他說道：「芬恩賜予你許多財富與眾多寶物，如今告訴我們，他是生是死？」「他尚活著，」基斯魯阿德說，「但至於他在何處，我不會透露半點消息，因為他本人不願我洩露此事。」眾人聞之大喜，因為基斯魯阿德向來所預言的一切無不應驗。

passages.text: "Tell us when will he come back?" "Before the Feast of Teamhair is over," said the Druid, "you will see the Leader of the Fianna drinking at it." And on the last day of the Feast of Teamhair they came back to their people again, and from that time out the Fianna of Ireland had not more dealings with the people living in houses than they had with the People of the Gods of Dana.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「告訴我們他何時歸來？」「在塔爾瓦節結束之前，」德魯伊說，「你們便會見到他——芬尼亞的領袖——在節上飲酒。」而在塔爾瓦節的最後一日，他們果然回到族人之中；自那時起，愛爾蘭的芬尼亞與居住在屋舍中的人們的往來，並不比他們與達納神族之民更為頻繁。

title.en: The Hospitality of Cuanna's House
title.zh: 庫安納宅邸的款待

region.en: Cairn Feargall, Co. Westmeath, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭西米斯郡費加爾石冢（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish vision-tale tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. IV, eBook #14465

summary.en: A giant with a squealing pig in an iron fork, a girl shoving him on, a man with twelve eyes, an armour-proof ram, and a hag whose grey gown withers men — Finn's five find themselves at a hostelry where the wells give honey-then-gall and bitter healing. When he wakes it is all explained by Cuanna of Innistuil: the giant is Sluggishness pushed by Liveliness, the twelve-eyed man the World, the ram the Desires of Men, the hag Old Age, and the two wells Lying and Truth.
summary.zh: 持鐵叉插尖嘯肥豬的巨人、推他前行的少女、十二眼老人、刀劍不入的公羊、灰袍能使青年衰老的老嫗——芬恩五人宿於一處奇異客邸：兩井之水一甜後苦、一苦而癒。醒來庫安納解釋一切：巨人即怠惰、少女即勤快、十二眼者即世界、公羊即人慾、老嫗即暮年、二井即謊言與真理。

sensitivity.note: A didactic vision-tale (aislinge) grafted onto the Fenian cycle; the allegorical bestiary and twin wells parallel didactic literature across traditions. Coordinates symbolic at the cairn where the vision began.

passages.text: It happened one day Finn and Oisin and Caoilte and Diarmuid and Lugaidh's Son went up on the top of Cairn Feargall, and their five hounds with them. They saw a giant coming towards them, very tall and rough, having an iron fork on his back and a squealing pig between the prongs of the fork, and a beautiful eager young girl behind the giant, shoving him on before her. Before they came to them, a dark Druid mist rose up that hid the road, and when it cleared away they saw a good light-roofed house at the edge of a ford, and before it two wells, on the edge of one a rough iron vessel, on the edge of the other a copper vessel. In the house was a very old white-haired man at the door, the beautiful young girl near him, the great rough giant boiling a pig by the fire, and on the other side an old countryman having dark-grey hair and twelve eyes in his head, and there was a ram in the house with a white belly and a very black head, and dark-blue horns and green feet.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一天，芬恩、奧辛、科爾特、迪爾穆德與盧蓋德之子一同登上卡恩費爾加爾的頂峰，隨行的還有他們的五隻獵犬。他們看見一個巨人朝他們走來，身形極高、相貌粗獷，背上負著一柄鐵叉，叉齒之間夾著一頭尖聲嘶叫的豬，巨人身後跟著一位美麗而熱切的年輕少女，正推著他向前走。他們尚未走近，一陣幽暗的德魯伊迷霧便升騰而起，遮住了道路；待霧散去，他們看見一座屋頂完好的屋舍立於渡口邊，屋前有兩口井，一口井邊放著一隻粗糙的鐵器，另一口井邊放著一隻銅器。屋內，一位白髮蒼蒼的老者立在門口，那位美麗的少女在他身旁，粗壯的巨人正在爐火邊煮著一頭豬，另一側則有一位深灰頭髮、頭上長著十二隻眼睛的老鄉人；屋中還有一隻公羊，白腹、極黑的頭、深藍色的角、綠色的腳。

passages.text: Caoilte brought Finn a drink from the copper vessel, and there was the taste of honey on it while he was drinking and the taste of gall after, so that fierce windy pains and signs of death came on him; and the drink out of the iron vessel was bitter as any battle, but no sooner did he drink it than his own colour and appearance came back to him. The ram seized the quarter of the pig set before the Fianna, and no sword could harm him, for they slipped from his back as from a rock — until the man with the twelve eyes took him by the feet and threw him out from the door. And the hag rose up and threw her pale grey gown over Finn's four comrades, and they turned to four old men, weak and withered; but Finn slept with his head in the man's breast, and the hag took her covering off the four men, and when Finn awoke they were in their own shape again.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 科爾特從銅器中取來飲品遞給芬恩，他飲時其中有蜜的滋味，飲後卻有膽汁的苦味，於是猛烈的絞痛與死亡的徵兆降臨於他；而鐵器中的飲品苦如任何一場戰役，但他剛一飲下，自身的氣色與容貌便恢復如初。那公羊奪走了擺在芬尼亞眾人面前的那份豬肉，任何刀劍都傷不了牠，因為刀劍從牠背上滑落，如同從岩石上滑落一般——直到那長著十二隻眼睛的人抓住牠的腳，將牠從門口扔了出去。那老婦起身，將她那件淡灰色的長袍覆在芬恩的四位同伴身上，他們便化作四個虛弱枯槁的老人；然而芬恩枕著那人的胸膛睡去，老婦又將覆蓋四人的袍子揭去，待芬恩醒來，他們已恢復本來的形貌。

passages.text: "As to the giant you saw first, having the squealing pig in the prongs of his fork, Sluggishness is his name; and the girl shoving him along is Liveliness, for liveliness goes farther in the winking of an eye than the foot can travel in a year. The old man with the twelve bright eyes betokens the World; the ram betokens the Desires of Men; the hag is Old Age, and her gown withered up your four comrades. And the two wells betoken Lying and Truth, for it is sweet to people to be telling a lie, but it is bitter in the end. Cuanna from Innistuil is my name, and I took a very great love for you because of your wisdom, and so I put these things in your way that I might see you. And the hospitality of Cuanna's house to Finn will be the name of this story to the end of the world." And when they awoke in the morning, it is where they were, on the top of Cairn Feargall, and their dogs and their arms beside them.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「至於你最先看見的那個巨人，叉齒間夾著尖聲嘶叫的豬的，他的名字是『遲緩』；推著他前行的少女是『活潑』，因為活潑在一眨眼的工夫裡所行，遠勝雙腳一年所能走的路程。那長著十二隻明亮眼睛的老人象徵『世界』；公羊象徵『人的慾望』；老婦是『老年』，她的長袍使你們四位同伴枯槁。那兩口井則象徵『謊言』與『真實』，因為對人而言，說謊是甜美的，但終究是苦澀的。我名叫庫安娜，來自伊尼斯圖伊爾；我因你的智慧而對你懷有極深的喜愛，故而將這些事物置於你的路途上，好讓我得以見你。而庫安娜之屋對芬恩的款待，將成為這個故事的名字，直到世界終結。」翌日清晨他們醒來時，他們所在之處正是卡恩費爾加爾的頂峰，獵犬與兵器都在他們身旁。

title.en: The Banners and Named Swords of the Fianna
title.zh: 菲亞納的戰旗與名劍

region.en: Magh Leine, Co. Westmeath, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭西米斯郡瑪格·萊恩（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. V, eBook #14465

summary.en: Nine of the Fianna hunting for a pup meet the three armies of the sons of the King of Ruadhleath — Cat-Heads, Dog-Heads, and White-Backs — and destroy them all. In the same telling the cycle assembles its iconography: Finn's banner the Sun-Shape, Oisin's the Dark Deadly One, Conan's a briar; the named swords won from Lon son of Liobhan, a one-footed, one-eyed smith with seven-handed brothers; and Finn's shield that calls out and is heard through all Ireland.
summary.zh: 九名菲亞納為尋一幼犬，遭遇魯拉德王三軍——貓首、犬首、白背——盡數殲滅。同一敘事中並羅列菲亞納圖騰：芬恩之「日形」旗、歐辛之「暗冥」旗、科南之荊棘旗；眾人自獨足獨眼的鐵匠隆之子處贏得名劍；以及一鳴即可傳遍全愛爾蘭的風暴盾。

sensitivity.note: Marvel-races (Cat-Heads, Dog-Heads, White-Backs) are voyage-literature stereotypes; the banner-and-weapon inventory is heraldic charter material of the cycle, best classed as a place/object-myth. Symbolic pin.

passages.text: Nine of the Fianna set out one time looking for a pup they wanted, and they searched through many places before they found it. While they were going from place to place, they saw the three armies of the sons of the King of Ruadhleath coming towards them: cat-headed one army was, and the one alongside of it was dog-headed, and the men of the third army were white-backed. When the Fianna saw them coming, Finn held up his shining spear, and light-hearted Caoilte gave out a great shout that was heard in Almhuin, and in Magh Leine, and in Teamhair, and in Dun Reithlein, and that shout was answered by Goll, son of Morna, and by Faolan, Finn's son that was with him, and by the Stutterers from Burren, and by Cael of the Sharp Sword, that never gave his ear to tale-bearers.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一次，芬尼亞的九名成員出發去尋找他們想要的一隻幼犬，他們搜遍了許多地方才找到。當他們輾轉於各地之間時，他們看見魯阿德萊斯王之諸子的三支軍隊朝他們而來：其中一支軍隊是貓頭，與之並列的一支是狗頭，第三支軍隊的人則是白背。芬尼亞眾人見他們前來，芬恩舉起他那柄閃亮的長矛，性情爽朗的科爾特發出一聲巨吼，這吼聲在阿爾溫、在馬格萊內、在塔爾瓦、在敦雷斯林皆可聽聞；回應這吼聲的有莫爾納之子戈爾、隨行在側的芬恩之子法奧蘭、來自布倫的結巴者們，以及從不聽信搬弄是非之人的利劍之凱爾。

passages.text: It is pleasant the sound was then of the spears and the armies and of the silken banners raised up in the gusty wind of the morning. Finn's banner, the Dealb-Greine, the Sun-Shape, had the likeness of the sun on it; Oisin's banner was the Donn Nimhe, the Dark Deadly One; Caoilte's was the Lamh Dearg, the Red Hand; and merry Diarmuid's banner was the Liath Loinneach, the Shining Grey; and as to Conan, it is a briar he had on his banner, because he was always for quarrels and for trouble — it used to be said of him he never saw a man frown without striking him, or a door left open without going in through it.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那時長矛與軍隊之聲，以及清晨陣風中揚起的絲質旗幟之聲，聽來甚是悅耳。芬恩的旗幟「Dealb-Greine」，意即「日之形」，其上繪有太陽的模樣；奧辛的旗幟是「Donn Nimhe」，意即「幽暗致命者」；凱爾特的旗幟是「Lamh Dearg」，意即「紅手」；而快活的迪爾穆德的旗幟是「Liath Loinneach」，意即「閃耀的灰」；至於科南，他的旗幟上畫的是一株荊棘，因為他總是喜好爭吵與麻煩——人們常說他，從未見人皺眉而不動手打他，也從未見門開著而不走進去。

passages.text: When the Fianna had raised their banners they attacked the three armies, and first of all they killed the whole of the Cat-Heads, and then they took the Dog-Heads in hand and made an end of them, and of the White-Backs along with them. And some of the Fianna had swords that had names to them, Mac an Luin, Son of the Waves, that belonged to Finn; and Ceard-nan Gallan, the Smith of the Branches, that was Oisin's; and Caoilte's Cruadh-Chosgarach, the Hard Destroying One. They got those swords from Lon, son of Liobhan, one of the three smiths of the King of Lochlann, a young man very big and ugly, having but one foot and one eye and a blunt ploughshare turning to red in his hand; they followed him all through Ireland to his smithy, where four smiths with seven hands each were working, and the swords were made before their eyes.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 芬尼亞戰士們舉起旗幟之後，便向那三支軍隊進攻，首先他們殺盡了貓頭族，接著他們著手對付狗頭族，將他們了結，連同白背族也一併消滅。芬尼亞之中有些人的劍是有名號的：屬於芬恩的是「Mac an Luin」，意即「波浪之子」；屬於奧辛的是「Ceard-nan Gallan」，意即「枝條之匠」；凱爾特的則是「Cruadh-Chosgarach」，意即「強力毀滅者」。他們是從洛赫蘭王之三鐵匠之一的利奧班之子隆那兒得到這些劍的，那青年身材魁梧而醜陋，只有一隻腳、一隻眼，手中握著一把轉為赤紅的鈍犁頭；他們跟隨他走遍愛爾蘭，直到他的鐵匠鋪，那裡有四名鐵匠，每人各有七隻手在工作，而那些劍就在他們眼前鑄成。

title.en: Finn's Shield Made from Balor's Hazels
title.zh: 芬恩之巴洛榛木神盾

region.en: Site of Magh Tuireadh, Co. Sligo, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭斯利戈郡莫伊蒂拉戰場（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle linking to the Mythological cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. V, eBook #14465

summary.en: After Lugh struck the head off Balor of the Evil Eye he hung it in the fork of a hazel-tree, which split and shed its leaves under the dripping poison and became for fifty years a dwelling of crows and ravens. When Manannan passing by had it dug up, a mist of poison rose from the roots and killed two nines of his men and blinded the third; and of the wood Luchtaine the Carpenter made a shield for Manannan, that passed to Tadg son of Nuada and so to his grandson Finn, and when Finn's shield called out it could be heard all through Ireland.
summary.zh: 盧格斬下邪眼巴洛之首懸於榛樹杈間，樹身劇裂、葉落於毒滴之下，五十年間為鴉群棲所。瑪那南命人掘樹，根間毒霧升起，兩個九人先後斃命，第三個九人雙目皆盲。木匠魯克坦以樹木為瑪那南製盾；後傳至努阿達之子塔格，再傳其孫芬恩——芬恩之盾一鳴，全愛爾蘭皆聞。

sensitivity.note: This shield-genealogy welds the Fenian cycle to the Second Battle of Magh Tuireadh — the poisoned head and withered hazel parallel the story of Lug's head among the Ulster tales. Object biography from god to mortal hero is a relic-transit motif.

passages.text: At the time of the Great Battle of Magh Tuireadh, Lugh, after he had struck the head off Balor of the Evil Eye, hung it in the fork of a hazel-tree. And the tree split, and the leaves fell from it with the dint of the poison that dropped from the head. And through the length of fifty years that tree was a dwelling-place of crows and of ravens.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在馬格圖伊雷德大戰之時，盧格砍下邪眼巴洛爾的首級之後，將它懸掛在一株榛樹的枝椏間。那樹便裂開了，樹葉因從首級滴落的毒液之力而紛紛墜落。此後五十年間，那棵樹成了烏鴉與渡鴉的棲居之所。

passages.text: And at the end of that time Manannan, son of Lir, was passing by, and he took notice of the tree that it was split and withered, and he bade his men to dig it up. And when they began to dig, a mist of poison rose up from the roots, and nine of the men got their death from it, and another nine after them, and the third nine were blinded. And Luchtaine the Carpenter made a shield of the wood of that hazel for Manannan. And after a while Manannan gave it, and a set of chessmen along with it, to Tadg, son of Nuada; and from him it came to his grandson, Finn, son of Muirne and of Cumhal. And besides his sword, Mac an Luin, Finn had a shield that was called Sgiath Gailbhinn, the Storm Shield; and when it called out it could be heard all through Ireland.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那段時日終了之時，利爾之子馬納南正從旁經過，他注意到那棵樹已裂開枯朽，便吩咐手下將它挖起。他們開始挖掘時，一股毒霧自根部升起，其中九人因此喪命，接著又有九人，第三批九人則雙目失明。木匠盧赫泰恩便用那株榛木為馬納南製了一面盾。過了些時日，馬納南將它連同一副棋子贈予努阿達之子塔德格；由他傳至其孫，即穆爾內與庫瓦爾之子芬恩。除了他的劍「Mac an Luin」之外，芬恩還有一面盾，名為「Sgiath Gailbhinn」，意即「風暴之盾」；當它發出呼號時，全愛爾蘭都能聽見。

title.en: Lomna's Head Speaks the Truth
title.zh: 洛姆納之首吐真言

region.en: Tethra, Luigne of Midhe, Co. Meath, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭米斯郡盧伊涅·梅德地區

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. VI, eBook #14465

summary.en: Lomna the fool of Finn's household sees Coirpre going secretly to Finn's wife and, too faithful to tell, writes the treachery in an ogham riddle on a four-square rod. Finn reads it; the wronged woman has the fool's head struck off and carried to Coirpre's feast, where the head, cheated of its share of fish against the law of the Fianna, speaks a prophecy — and Finn, following his hounds and his divination of rhymes, comes in and makes an end of Coirpre and his men.
summary.zh: 芬恩家中弄臣洛姆納撞見科爾普雷私通芬恩之妻，忠而不言，遂以四方形榛杖上的歐甘謎語記下此樁背叛。芬恩解讀後，被羞辱的婦人命人斬下弄臣之首送往科爾普雷宴席；眾人分魚獨缺其份——違反菲亞納之法——首級遂開口預言。芬恩循獵犬與詩謎占卜而至，誅科爾普雷及其黨羽。

sensitivity.note: The speaking head is a classic Celtic head-cult motif (cf. Bran's head); divination by rhymes (imbas forosnai form) is attested practice in the tradition. The ogham riddle on the rod is legal-poetic shorthand. Pin symbolic in Luigne.

passages.text: Finn took a wife one time of the Luigne of Midhe, and at the same time there was in his household one Lomna, a fool. Finn went into Tethra hunting with the Fianna, but Lomna stopped at the house, and after a while he saw Coirpre, a man of the Luigne, go in secretly to where Finn's wife was. The woman begged and prayed of Lomna to hide it from Finn, and Lomna agreed to that, but it preyed on him to have a hand in doing treachery on Finn. After a while he took a four-square rod and wrote an Ogham on it, and these were the words he wrote: "An alder stake in a paling of silver; deadly night-shade in a bunch of cresses; a husband of a lewd woman; a fool among the well-taught Fianna; heather on bare Ualann of Luigne."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 芬恩有一次娶了米德的盧伊格內族的一名女子為妻，同時他的家中有一個傻子，名叫洛姆納。芬恩帶著芬尼亞戰士到泰斯拉去打獵，但洛姆納留在了屋裡，過了一會兒，他看見盧伊格內族的一名男子科爾普雷悄悄走進芬恩妻子所在之處。那女人懇求洛姆納向芬恩隱瞞此事，洛姆納答應了，但參與對芬恩的背叛令他內心備受煎熬。過了一會兒，他取來一根四方的木條，在上面刻下歐甘文字，他所寫的話是：「銀色籬笆中的一根榿木樁；一束水芹中的致命顛茄；淫婦之夫；飽學的芬尼亞中的一個傻子；盧伊格內光禿的烏阿蘭上的石南。」

passages.text: Finn saw the message, and there was anger on him against the woman; and she knew well it was from Lomna he had heard the story, and she sent a message to Coirpre bidding him come and kill the fool. So Coirpre came and struck his head off, and brought it away with him. When Finn came back in the evening he saw the body without a head, and did the divination of rhymes: "It is the body of Lomna; it is not by a wild boar he was killed; it is by his enemies he died." They let out the hounds on the track of Coirpre, and came to a house where he was cooking fish on a spit, and Lomna's head on a spike beside the fire.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 芬恩看見了這訊息，對那女人心生怒意；她深知他是從洛姆納那兒得知此事的，便送信給科爾普雷，命他來殺了那傻子。於是科爾普雷前來，砍下他的首級，並將其帶走。芬恩傍晚回來時，看見那具無頭的屍身，便行韻文占卜：「這是洛姆納的軀體；他不是被野豬所殺；他是死於仇敵之手。」他們放出獵犬追蹤科爾普雷的足跡，來到一間屋子，他正用鐵叉在火上烤魚，而洛姆納的首級則插在火旁的一根尖樁上。

passages.text: Coirpre divided the fish between his men, but put no bit into the mouth of the head, and that was against the law of the Fianna; and the head spoke: "A speckled white-bellied salmon that grows from a small fish under the sea; you have shared a share that is not right; the Fianna will avenge it upon you, Coirpre." "Put the head outside," said Coirpre, "for that is an evil word for us." Then the head said from outside: "It is in many pieces you will be; it is great fires will be lighted by Finn in Luigne." And as it said that, Finn came in, and he made an end of Coirpre, and of his men.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 科爾普雷把魚分給他的手下，卻沒往那頭的口中放進一點，這違反了費尼亞的律法；那頭便開口說道：「一條從海底小魚長成的斑點白腹鮭魚；你們分了一份不正當的份額；費尼亞必因這事向你科爾普雷報復。」「把那頭放到外面去，」科爾普雷說，「因為那對我們是不祥之言。」於是那頭從外面說道：「你將被剁成許多塊；芬恩將在盧伊涅燃起大火。」話音剛落，芬恩便進來了，他結果了科爾普雷，也結果了他的手下。

title.en: The Bird of Iron Beak and the War of Ilbrec and Lir
title.zh: 鐵喙之鳥與伊爾布雷克、利爾之戰

region.en: Sidhe of Ess Ruadh, Co. Sligo, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭斯利戈郡埃斯·魯阿仙丘

period: Fenian-Sidhe interface tradition, medieval Irish; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. VII, eBook #14465

summary.en: A bird with an iron beak and a tail of fire comes every evening to a golden window of Ilbrec's house in the hill of Ess Ruadh and shakes itself till weapons fall on the heads of the household, and nothing thrown at it will touch it — the doing of Lir of Sidhe Fionnachaidh, with whom Ilbrec is at war. Caoilte casts it down with a copper rod, and next day meets Lir himself hand to hand: the oldest of the Men of Dea falls by the Fianna's best runner, and Derg breaks two backs with one cast of his spear.
summary.zh: 每晚一隻鐵喙火尾之鳥飛至埃斯·魯阿仙丘伊爾布雷克家中的金窗，抖落神威，使兵器紛紛砸向家僕頭頂；擲物擊之而毫髮無傷——此乃與伊爾布雷克交戰的西德·菲奧納凱德之王利爾所為。卡爾特擲銅杖將其擊落；次日與利爾親手相搏——神族中最年長者竟亡於菲亞納最快跑者之手；德格一矛貫穿二人後背。

sensitivity.note: The ruinous bird is the fixed Fenian marvel (compare the geilt bird of Suibhne lore); a feud among two Sidhe-kings witnessed and settled by a mortal champion is a good instance of the mortal-arbiter motif. Pin is the documented hill.

passages.text: One time Caoilte was hunting on Beinn Gulbain, and he went on to Ess Ruadh, and when he came near the hill of the Sidhe that is there, he saw a young man waiting for him, Derg, son of Eoghan of the people of Usnach, his foster-brother, now living among his mother's people the Tuatha de Danaan. "There is nothing wanting to us there of food or of clothing," said the young man, "but for all that I would sooner live the life of the worst treated of the serving-boys of the Fianna than the life I am living in the hill of the Sidhe." And he brought Caoilte into the hill.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一次，凱爾特在貝恩·古爾班山上打獵，一路來到埃斯·魯阿，當他走近那裡的希德之丘時，看見一個年輕人在等他，那是德爾格，烏斯納赫族歐根之子，他的乳兄弟，如今住在母親的族人圖阿薩·德·達南之中。「我們那裡吃的穿的都不缺，」那年輕人說，「可即便如此，我寧願過費尼亞最受苛待的僕役的生活，也不願過我在希德之丘所過的日子。」於是他把凱爾特帶進了丘中。

passages.text: At that time there was great war between Lir of Sidhe Fionnachaidh and Ilbrec of Ess Ruadh. There used a bird with an iron beak and a tail of fire to come every evening to a golden window of Ilbrec's house, and there he would shake himself till he would not leave sword on pillow, or shield on peg, or spear in rack, but they would come down on the heads of the people of the house; and whatever they would throw at the bird, it is on the heads of some of themselves it would fall.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那時，希德·菲奧納海德的利爾與埃斯·魯阿的伊爾布雷克之間正進行著大戰。有一隻長著鐵喙、火尾的鳥，每天傍晚都飛到伊爾布雷克宅邸的一扇金窗上，在那裡抖動身子，直到枕上不留劍、釘上不留盾、架上不留矛，全都落到屋中眾人的頭上；而無論他們向那鳥投擲什麼，落下的總是他們自己人的頭上。

passages.text: Then Caoilte put his hand within the rim of his shield and took out a copper rod, and made a cast of it at the bird that brought it down on the floor of the hall. Ilbrec took down a sharp spear having thirty rivets of gold in it and gave it to Caoilte: "That is the Spear of Fiacha, son of Congha, and it is with that Finn made an end of Aillen, son of Midhna, that used to burn Teamhair." In the morning three brave armies of Lir came all about the hill, and the host of the Sidhe went out to the battle, and the fight went on from the rising of the day till midday.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是凱爾特把手伸進盾牌的邊緣裡，取出一根銅棒，朝那鳥擲去，把它打落在廳堂的地上。伊爾布雷克取下一支鑲有三十顆金鉚釘的鋒利長矛，交給凱爾特：「這是孔加之子菲亞哈的矛，芬恩正是用它結果了那慣於焚燒塔拉城的米德納之子艾倫。」清晨，利爾的三支勇猛大軍圍住了整座山丘，希德的軍隊出戰迎敵，戰鬥從天亮一直持續到正午。

passages.text: And then Caoilte and Lir met with one another, and they made a very fierce fight, and at the last Lir of Sidhe Fionnachaidh fell by the hand of Caoilte. Then the two good champions Dubh and Donn, sons of Eirrge, fought on, Dubh in the front of the whole army and Donn behind all, guarding the rear; but Derg put his finger into the thong of his spear and made a cast at the one that was nearest him, and it broke his back and went on into the body of the other, so that the one cast made an end of the two; and that ended the battle, and all that was left of the great army of Lir went wearing away to the north.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 隨後凱爾特與利爾相遇，二人展開了一場極為兇猛的搏鬥，最後希德·菲奧納海德的利爾死在凱爾特手下。接著，兩位優秀的勇士、埃爾格之子杜布與唐繼續奮戰，杜布在全軍之前，唐在全軍之後，守護後陣；但德爾格把手指伸進長矛的皮帶裡，朝離他最近的那一個擲去，矛打斷了他的脊背，又穿進了另一個人的身體，於是一擲結果了兩人；戰鬥就此結束，利爾那支大軍的殘餘全都向北潰退而去。

title.en: Caoilte's Healing and the Drink of Remembrance
title.zh: 卡爾特療傷與記憶之飲

region.en: Hill of the Sidhe at Ess Ruadh, Co. Sligo, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭斯利戈郡埃斯·魯阿仙丘

period: Fenian-Sidhe interface tradition, medieval Irish; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IV, ch. VII, eBook #14465

summary.en: Poisoned in the thigh by a spear of Mane son of the King of Lochlann, Caoilte rides to Ess Ruadh for Bebind, daughter of Elcmar, keeper of what is left of Goibniu's ale and the Tuatha de Danaan's drink of healing. First the household must be freed of its yearly terrors: Cascorach the musician slays the visiting woman-warrior of Lochlann, Caoilte strikes down the King of Lochlann with the spear called War-Woman, and the three death-screeching ravens that carry off hurling boys are killed with chessmen for casts. Then comes the five-drink cure, the washing of Flann daughter of Flidais, and the parting gifts — the fish-hook that takes fish in any water, and the drink of remembrance that keeps every battle in memory for ever.
summary.zh: 洛赫蘭王之子的毒矛傷了卡爾特大腿，他奔赴埃斯·魯阿，求助於保有哥伊布努殘酒與神族療傷水的艾爾克瑪爾之女貝賓德。先解除仙丘的年 年之災：樂師卡斯卡拉赫誅殺來犯女戰士；卡爾特擲「戰女矛」擊斃洛赫蘭王；三隻叼走擲球少年之烏鴉被以棋子擊殺。而後行五飲之治、弗蕾丹之女弗蘭的洗頭之術；臨別贈禮——無水不獲魚的魚鉤，以及令百戰永誌不忘的記憶之飲。

sensitivity.note: The drink of remembrance is the narrative device that licenses the aged Caoilte's testimony to St Patrick — a metanarrative function of Fenian tales; wound-suction healing and the five-drink cure parallel the Conn Crither well of healing. Tag 'prophetic-vision' omitted in favour of resurrection+voyage.

passages.text: It was in a battle at Beinn Edair in the east that Mane, son of the King of Lochlann, made a cast at Caoilte in the middle of the battle with a deadly spear; it struck into his thigh, and left its poison in it, so that he had to go in search of healing. And it is where he went, to the hill of the Sidhe at Ess Ruadh, to ask help of Bebind, daughter of Elcmar of Brugh na Boinne, that had the drink of healing of the Tuatha de Danaan, and all that was left of the ale of Goibniu.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那是在東方的貝恩·埃達爾的一場戰鬥中，洛赫蘭王之子的馬內在戰陣中央用一支致命的長矛向凱爾特擲去；矛刺進了他的大腿，把毒留在了裡面，於是他不得不去尋求醫治。他去的地方，正是埃斯·魯阿的希德之丘，去向布魯格·納·博因的埃爾克馬爾之女貝賓德求助，她擁有圖阿薩·德·達南的療傷之飲，以及戈布紐之麥酒所剩的全部。

passages.text: Caoilte called to Cascorach the Musician, son of Caincenn, and bade him bring his harp and come along with him; and there was a woman-warrior used to come every year with the ships of the men of Lochlann to make an attack on the Tuatha de Danaan, and there was no precious thing in all the hills of the Sidhe but she had knowledge of it, and would bring it away. It was Cascorach went out against her, and she used high words when she saw so young a man coming to fight with her, but he made an end of her for all her high talk, and left her lying on the strand with the sea foam washing up to her.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 高爾特呼喚凱恩肯之子、樂師卡斯克拉赫，命他帶上豎琴隨行；有一名女戰士慣於每年隨洛克蘭人的船隊前來攻打達努神族，西德諸丘之中凡有珍貴之物，她無不知曉，且必將其奪走。正是卡斯克拉赫出陣迎她；她見來與自己交戰者竟是如此年輕之人，便口出狂言，然而他終究了結了她，任她那些大話也無濟於事，將她棄於海灘之上，任海沫沖刷到她身上。

passages.text: As to Caoilte, he went out in a chariot belonging to Midhir of the Yellow Hair, and a spear was given him that was called Ben-badb, the War-Woman, and he made a cast of it that struck the King of Lochlann, that he fell in the middle of his army, and the life went from him. And there came three flocks of beautiful red birds from Slieve Fuad eating the green grass before the hill, and Caoilte and his comrades drove them away with stones; and there were three ravens come to them every year out of the north, and the time the young lads of the hill are playing their hurling, each one of the ravens carries off a boy of them. On the morrow the whole of the Tuatha de Danaan went out to look at the hurling, and the three ravens from the north came over the sea and pitched on the great tree of power, and gave three gloomy screeches that took the courage out of the whole gathering; and Cascorach took a man of the chessmen and made a cast at one of the ravens that struck his beak and his throat, and Fermaise killed the second, and Caoilte the third.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 至於高爾特，他乘上金髮米希爾的一輛戰車出陣，有人贈他一柄名為「本巴德布」——意即「女戰士」——的長矛，他擲出此矛，正中洛克蘭王，使其倒斃於軍陣之中，魂魄離體。又有三群美麗的紅鳥自斯利夫富阿德飛來，在山丘前啄食青草，高爾特與同伴們以石驅趕；另有三年年自北方飛來三隻渡鴉，每逢山丘上的少年們玩曲棍球時，每隻渡鴉便各擄走一名少年。翌日，達努神族全族出外觀看曲棍球賽，那三隻北方渡鴉越海而來，棲於那棵象徵權力的大樹之上，發出三聲陰沉的嘶鳴，令全場眾人盡失勇氣；卡斯克拉赫取來一枚棋子，擲向其中一隻渡鴉，擊中其喙與喉，費爾邁斯殺死第二隻，高爾特殺死第三隻。

passages.text: Then Elcmar's daughter made a bed of healing for Caoilte, and a bowl of pale gold was brought to her full of water, and she bruised herbs into it, and he took five drinks of it that made him cast up the poison of the spear; and the washing of Flann, daughter of Flidais, was done for his head, that will never be troubled with pain, or baldness, or weakness of sight. And the people of the hill gave good gifts to Caoilte — a fish-hook that was called Aicil mac Mogha, that could not be set in any river or inver but it would take fish, and along with that a drink of remembrance, and after that drink there would be no place he ever saw, or no battle or fight he ever was in, but it would stay in his memory.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IV, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 隨後，埃爾克馬爾之女為高爾特鋪設療傷之床，有人為她送來一隻盛滿水的淡金碗，她將藥草搗碎浸入水中，他飲了五口，遂將矛毒嘔出；又為他的頭施行弗利戴斯之女芙蘭的洗滌之法，此後他的頭永不受疼痛、禿髮或目力衰弱之苦。山丘之民又贈高爾特以佳禮——一枚名為「艾基爾·麥克·莫加」的魚鉤，無論置於何河何口，皆能釣得魚；此外還有一杯憶念之飲，飲過此杯之後，凡他曾見之地、凡他曾身歷之戰或爭鬥，無不長存於其記憶之中。

title.en: Dhruva Wins the Pole Star
title.zh: 達魯婆贏得北極星

region.en: Madhuvana forest (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 摩陀森林（象徵性定位）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book I, chs. 12-13, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book I, the story of Dhruva

summary.en: Five-year-old Dhruva climbed his father's knee and was pushed off by his stepmother: no seat for the son of a rival wife, and none but the king's own. His mother's advice - seek the one whose seat never shakes - sent the boy into the forest; he stood on one leg in tapas until Vishnu came, touched his cheek, and set him above the turning sky: the pole star is a child who was denied a lap.
summary.zh: 五歲的達魯婆爬上父親之膝，被繼母推下：妃嬪之子的座位不屬於他，唯有王座除外。母親的忠告——去找那位座位永不動搖者——將男孩送入森林；他一足而立行苦行，直到毘濕奴前來，觸其面頰，將他安置於旋轉的天空之上：北極星即那位未被允許坐膝的孩童。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (Dhruva recited in devotional instruction); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The boy climbed the king's knee as kings' sons do, and the senior queen pulled him off with the sentence that made a saint of him: only my son sits the lap; go to thy mother, and ask her for a seat elsewhere.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那男孩像王子們那樣爬上國王的膝頭，年長的王后卻將他拽了下來，那句話使他成了聖者：只有我的兒子才能坐這膝頭；去找你母親，向她另討一個座位吧。

passages.text: His mother told him plainly: she had no seat to give but the one that cannot be given by a king - seek the Lord whose seat never falls; and the boy walked into the forest at five. The tapas is a child's enormity: one leg, breath stopped, the forest burning around a fixed point - until Vishnu's hand came down and offered him a seat in the sky's own pivot, the star that does not set.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他的母親直截了當地告訴他：她沒有座位可給，唯有那國王給不了的座位——去尋求那位寶座永不傾覆的主；於是那男孩五歲便走進了森林。苦行是孩童的極端之舉：單足而立，屏息不動，森林圍繞著一個定點燃燒——直到毗濕奴的手降下，賜他一個座位，就在天穹自身的樞軸之上，那顆永不沉落的星辰。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: Prithu Milks the Earth
title.zh: 缽哩陀擠乳於大地

region.en: Sarasvati plains (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 薩拉斯瓦蒂平原（象徵性定位）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book I, ch. 13, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book I, Prithu and the Earth

summary.en: When a wicked king starved the earth, the seers churned the dead king's arm and produced Prithu, the first consecrated king - and the earth, made woman, fled from his bow like a cow from the brand. She consented to be milked instead: Prithu levelled her fields, and from her every creature then milked its own food - the first agriculture, and the charter of kingship as a covenant, not a conquest.
summary.zh: 惡王使大地饑饉之際，仙人們攪動亡王之臂而生出缽哩陀——首位受冕之王——而化為女子的大地如母牛見烙印般逃避其弓。她轉而允許被擠乳：缽哩陀平整其田，自此萬物皆自她擠得各自之食——最早的農耕，以及王權作為盟約而非征服的憲章。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The kingless earth grew wild and thin; from the right arm of the slain tyrant the seers kneaded out Prithu, and the rites made him the first of consecrated kings. The Earth fled him in a woman's shape, and he chased her with a bow across the worlds until she stopped - 'slay me and who will feed thy subjects?' - and offered the cow's bargain instead.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 無王的大地變得荒蕪而貧瘠；先知們從那被弒暴君的右臂中揉捏出普利圖，種種儀式使他成為首位受祝聖的國王。大地化作女子之形逃避他，他持弓追逐她，跨越諸界，直到她停下腳步——「殺了我，誰來養活你的臣民？」——並提出以母牛之約代替。

passages.text: So the king levelled her fields and became her herdsman: every creature milked its own food from her - herbs to the brahmin, grain to the merchant, grass to the deer - and kingship was defined as the keeping of a covenant with the ground.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是國王平整了她的田地，成為她的牧人：每一種生靈都從她身上擠取屬於自己的食物——藥草歸婆羅門，穀物歸商人，青草歸鹿——而王權的定義，便是與大地恪守盟約。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: Putana, the Poison Nurse
title.zh: 普塔那：毒乳之乳母

region.en: Gokula (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 戈庫拉（象徵性定位）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, Putana

summary.en: Kamsa sent a shape-changing demoness to nurse the infants of Vraja - she was beautiful, and her breast was poison. The baby Krishna drank, and the drink was fatal to the nurse: she grew to her true giantess size, blackened the landscape with her fall, and the poison she meant for the child was counted by the village as his first miracle.
summary.zh: 甘薩遣一變形羅剎女為牧區之嬰兒授乳——她貌美，其乳即毒。嬰孩克里希那飲之，而毒反噬其乳母：她現出真身巨妖之形，墜落之體黑遍大地；村人將那本欲毒死嬰兒的毒計數為他的第一件奇蹟。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The demoness walked into the herdsmen's village as a lovely stranger, offering to nurse the most darling baby of the season - the one born at midnight to Nanda's house. The child drank what was meant to kill him, and held on: the nurse's body swelled to her true size, a giantess blackening the horizon as she fell - the poison drawn into the poisoner. The village counted its miracle and its funeral in one breath; Yashoda found her baby laughing in the dust - the first proof, in the village's eyes, of what the mother did not yet know she had adopted.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那女妖化作一位可愛的陌生女子，走進牧人的村落，自願哺育這一季最惹人疼愛的嬰兒——那個午夜降生於難陀家中的孩子。孩子飲下了本欲取他性命的乳汁，卻牢牢不放：乳母的身軀脹回她真實的體量，一個使地平線為之昏暗的女巨人就此倒下——毒藥被吸入了下毒者體內。村人一口氣之間既數算奇蹟，又數算葬禮；耶輸陀在塵土中發現自己的孩子正笑著——在村人眼中，這是第一道明證，印證了那位母親尚不知自己已收養了什麼。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: Krishna Dances on Kaliya's Heads
title.zh: 克里希那舞於迦利耶百首之上

region.en: Yamuna at Kalindi (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 迦林蒂河亞穆納段（象徵性定位）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, Kaliya

summary.en: The hundred-headed serpent Kaliya poisoned the Yamuna: birds fell from the branches, the water smoked. Krishna leapt from a kadamba tree into the pool and danced - on the serpent's heads, each coil pinned under a child's foot, until the great snake's wives rose from the water to beg for his life. Krishna spared him on one condition: go, and never come back to my river.
summary.zh: 百首蛇王迦利耶毒化了亞穆納河：禽鳥自枝頭墜落，水面冒煙。克里希那自瞻蔔樹躍入池中，在蛇王之首上舞蹈——每一盤曲都被孩童之足釘住——直到巨蛇的妻妾自水中升起為其求命。克里希那以一條件饒之：去吧，永不回到我的河中。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (Kaliya-damana imagery); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The river had become a poison: cattle refused its banks, birds fell into the water unburned by any fire, and the village learned which pool to fear. Krishna dived in without armor and came up in the coils - then stood, and danced, a child's bare feet keeping time on a hundred heads until the serpent's strength was the tune's. The wives' pleading saved the dancer's prisoner: he was sent to the far sea with his lives intact - the dance's mercy as famous as the dance's stamping; the Yamuna ran sweet from that hour.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那河流已化為毒：牛群不肯靠近河岸，鳥兒墜入水中，卻非被任何火焰灼傷，村人於是得知該畏懼哪一汪水潭。黑天不披甲冑便躍入其中，浮出時已陷於蛇軀盤繞之中——隨即立起，起舞，一雙孩童的赤足在百個蛇首上踏著節拍，直到巨蛇的氣力盡化為那曲調。眾蛇妻的懇求救了舞者的囚徒：他被遣往遠海，性命完好無損——這舞蹈的慈悲與舞蹈的踐踏同樣著名；自那一刻起，亞穆納河便流淌甘甜。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: Krishna Kills Kamsa in the Arena
title.zh: 克里希那於鬥技場誅甘薩

region.en: Mathura arena (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 馬圖拉鬥技場（象徵性定位）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, Kamsa's death

summary.en: Invited to Mathura for a festival and a wrestling match, Krishna walked into the arena where the tyrant had raised the bow of Shiva as bait. He bent and broke the bow; the wrestlers Chanura and Mushtika were sent at the cowherd boys and were broken instead; and Krishna, seizing his uncle by the hair on the dais itself, ended the prophecy in front of the whole city - the child of the massacre decree killing the man who wrote it.
summary.zh: 受邀赴馬圖拉慶典與角力賽的克里希那，走入暴君以濕婆神弓為餌設下的鬥技場。他彎折並折斷神弓；奉命對付牧童的摔角手迦奴羅與穆什底迦反被折斷；克里希那在高臺上抓住舅舅的頭髮，當著全城終結預言——屠嬰令所針對的孩子親手誅殺了下令者。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The arena was a trap with decoration: the bow of Shiva set in the center to be admired - and the herdsman boy bent it with one hand, and broke it with the sound of an omen. Chanura, the champion, was assigned the child by the king's smile; the wrestler went into the dust and did not leave it - the cowherd's arms were his father the Wind's. The prophecy's author died at the hands of its subject: Krishna took his uncle by the hair where the whole city could watch, and the tyrant who had counted his wife's children found his own counted at last.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 競技場是一座裝飾過的陷阱：濕婆之弓置於中央供人瞻仰——而那牧童單手便將它彎折，又一聲如凶兆般的聲響將它折斷。國王含笑將那孩子指派給力士闍努羅；那力士倒進塵土，再未離開——牧牛人的雙臂，其父乃風神。預言的作者死於預言對象之手：黑天當著全城可觀之處揪住舅父的頭髮，那曾數算妻子諸子的暴君，終於發覺自己的命數也被數到了盡頭。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: The Abduction of Rukmini
title.zh: 魯克彌尼的被劫成婚

region.en: Kundina and Vidarbha (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 恭提那與維陀爾薄（象徵性定位）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, Rukmini

summary.en: Rukmini, princess of Vidarbha, loved Krishna and was promised to Shishupala; the day before the wedding she sent him a letter with her plan: come at dawn with a chariot and take me from the temple before the bridegroom's procession arrives. Krishna came, lifted her into the chariot in front of the assembled kings - and fought his way out against the wedding armies.
summary.zh: 維陀爾薄公主魯克彌尼愛克里希那，卻被許給尸市場沙巴拉；婚禮前一日，她送信告知計劃：拂曉攜車而來，於迎親行列到達前從神廟將我帶走。克里希那到來，當著會集諸王將她抱上戰車——並衝破送親軍陣殺出。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The letter was her own elopement-plan written in full: come before the wedding sun, take me at the temple, and let no king's procession finish its arrival - a bride engineering her own abduction. He came at dawn, swept her up from the shrine where she was said to be praying to the rival bridegroom's patron, and the wedding's shock troops found an empty temple and a chariot already past the gates. The running battle that followed cleared the road behind the flying chariot - and the marriage it produced became the model of Krishna's queenship in Dvaraka; the letter is the tradition's first love-letter with tactics.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那封信便是她親筆寫就的私奔全盤計畫：在婚禮的太陽升起之前前來，於神廟中將我帶走，別讓任何國王的儀仗完成它的抵達——一位新娘親自策劃了自己的劫奪。他於黎明而至，從她據說正向情敵新郎的守護神祈禱的神殿中將她席捲而去，婚禮的突擊隊只尋得一座空廟，以及一輛早已駛過城門的戰車。隨之而來的奔逃之戰掃清了飛馳戰車身後的道路——而由此締結的婚姻，成為黑天在德瓦拉卡王后之尊的典範；那封信，是傳統中第一封帶有戰術的的情書。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: The Curse at Dvaraka: The Yadavas' Last Feast
title.zh: 達瓦迦之咒：耶度族的最後宴席

region.en: Prabhasa, the shore pilgrimage (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 般羅婆沙海岸聖地（象徵性定位）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, chs. 35-38; Mausala tradition, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, the end of the Yadavas

summary.en: At a pilgrimage-feast the Yadavas drank, quarreled, and turned their hands to grass that became iron reeds, slaughtering each other to the last man on the beach - the fulfillment of a seer's curse and Gandhari's. Krishna sat apart under a tree; a hunter's arrow took him for a sleeping deer and struck the one mortal spot - the sole unarmored place the Lord had left himself.
summary.zh: 朝聖宴上，耶度族人飲酒、口角、以手握草化為鐵蘆而互相屠殺，於海灘上戰至最後一人——應驗仙人之咒與甘陀利之詛。克里希那獨坐樹下；獵人之箭誤其為睡鹿，射中主為自己留下的唯一不設防之處。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The seer's curse had named the instruments: grass shall be your iron. The drunk warriors pulled reeds from the ground and found each one a blade - and the beach at Prabhasa did the arithmetic. By evening the race of Yadu was a field of the fallen; Krishna walked the shore of his own people's ruin, and the women of Dvaraka began the wailing that Gandhari had promised them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 仙人的詛咒已點明了工具：草將成為你們的鐵。醉酒的戰士們從地上拔起蘆葦，發覺每一根都是利刃——而婆羅婆沙海灘替他們算清了這筆帳。到了傍晚，雅度族已成一片伏屍之野；黑天行走於自己族人覆滅的岸邊，德瓦拉卡的女人們開始了甘陀利曾向她們預言的那場哀號。

passages.text: The hunter's arrow found the heel-mark of the god's own choice: the Lord of the universe kept one mortal spot for himself, and left the world there - the sky filled with the leaving, and the age of heroes ended on a beach.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 獵人的箭找到了神明自己所選的腳跟印記：宇宙之主為自己保留了一處凡人之處，就在那裡離開了世界——天空滿是離去之勢，英雄時代終結於一片海灘之上。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: Garuda and the Amrita of the Gods
title.zh: 金翅鳥與諸神的甘露

region.en: Cosmic ocean and Indra's heaven (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 宇宙之海與因陀羅天界（象徵性定位）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book I, chs. 29-31, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book I, Garuda and the amrita

summary.en: The Purana's Garuda version is a covenant-story: sent to steal the amrita as his mother's ransom, the great bird quenched a forest-fire by drinking a river, outwitted the gods' guards, took the nectar in his claws - and Vishnu appeared, not to fight but to bargain: the bird shall be immortal without drinking, and the god's own carrier forever. Indra's thunderbolt was returned with the ransom paid and the amrita taken back.
summary.zh: 往世書的金翅鳥版本是一則盟約故事：為贖其母而奉命竊取甘露，巨鳥飲盡一條河以撲滅森林之火，以智勝過諸神的守衛，以爪取走神露——毘濕奴現身，非為交戰而為交易：鳥不飲而得不死，並成為神之座騎直到永遠。因陀羅的雷霆杵隨贖金之付與神露之取回而物歸原主。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The ransom the serpents demanded was the one thing the gods hoarded: the amrita - and Garuda's wings measured the distance between a mother's slavery and heaven's strong-room. The obstacles fell to scale and wit: a forest-fire quenched with a river swallowed, the guards of the nectar outflown - and the great bird left the theft without drinking a drop. Vishnu's offer changed the story's species: immortality without the theft, wings under the god forever - the bird kept his bargain and Indra's bolt retrieved the jar; the ransom was paid in honor rather than in nectar.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 眾蛇所索取的贖金，正是眾神所囤積的唯一之物：甘露——而迦樓羅的雙翼丈量了母親的奴役與天國寶庫之間的距離。障礙皆因衡量與機智而倒下：一場林火被吞下的河流所熄滅，甘露的守衛被飛越而過——而那隻巨鳥完成了竊取，卻一滴未飲。毗濕奴的提議改變了這個故事的物種：無需竊取便得永生，雙翼永遠歸於神明之下——那隻鳥守住了他的約定，因陀羅的雷霆取回了那罈甘露；贖金以榮譽而非甘露償付。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: Prahlada in the Furnace of His Father's Anger
title.zh: 布羅赫拉達於父怒之火爐中

region.en: Hiranyakashipu's capital (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 金輪王之都（象徵性定位）

period: Vishnu Purana, Book I, chs. 15-17, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book I, the persecution of Prahlada

summary.en: The persecution chapters of the Narasimha cycle are a catalogue of failed murders: poison that the boy blessed, fire that cooled around him, elephants that knelt, the fall from a palace balcony caught by the earth. Prahlada's defense in every scene was a sentence his father could not counter - He is in me as He is in the pillar - and each failure made the boy's theology more public.
summary.zh: 獅面人循環中的迫害章節是一份失敗謀殺的目錄：被孩童祝禱的毒、圍繞他轉涼的火、跪下的巨象、被大地接住的宮殿墜落。布羅赫拉達在每一幕中的辯護都是一句父親無法反駁的話——祂在我中，如祂在柱中——而每一次失敗都使孩童的神學更為公開。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The poison was served in the boy's own cup and blessed before drinking; the fire was built to burn him and cooled around the one child inside it; the elephant that was to trample him knelt. The balcony, the ocean, the serpents: the catalogue of a father's methods - and the son's reply never varied: He is in the pillar as He is in me; the whole world is His pillar. Each public failure made the theology public: the boy who would not die for saying Vishnu's name became the court's teacher, and the father's rage had nowhere left to hide from the sentence its own child kept repeating.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 毒藥被斟入那男孩自己的杯中，並在飲前祝禱；火被堆起要燒死他，卻在身處其中的那唯一孩童周圍冷卻；本要踐踏他的大象跪了下來。陽台、海洋、眾蛇：一位父親種種手段的目錄——而兒子的回答從未改變：祂在柱中，正如祂在我中；整個世界都是祂的柱子。每一次公開的失敗都使這神學公開：那不肯因稱念毗濕奴之名而死的男孩成了朝廷的教師，而父親的怒火已無處可躲，躲不開自己孩子反覆念誦的那句判詞。

canonical_translation: H. H. Wilson, 1840 (public domain)

title.en: The King and the Vetala: Twenty-Five Tales on a Corpse's Shoulders
title.zh: 王與毘舍遮：負屍肩上的二十五個故事

region.en: Cremation ground of Dhurandhara (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 陀羅陀羅火葬地（象徵性定位）

period: Kathasaritsagara of Somadeva, c. 1070 CE, Vetala-Panchavimshati cycle (Tawney translation, 1880-84)

source.work: The Katha Sarit Sagara, trans. C. H. Tawney (1880-84), the Vetala tales

summary.en: A king was asked by a mendicant to fetch a corpse from a burning ground for a rite - and the corpse was a vetala, a spirit who told stories. Twenty-five times the king carried it on his shoulders and twenty-five times a riddle at the end of the tale tempted an answer; twenty-five times the vetala flew back to the tree. The frame is the tradition's great logic-exam: answer correctly and be caught, or keep silence and be called a coward.
summary.zh: 一位苦行者請王赴火葬地取一具屍體以行其祭——而屍體乃一毘舍遮（起屍鬼），講故事的精靈。二十五次王以肩負屍，二十五次故事末尾的謎題誘其作答；二十五次毘舍遮飛返樹上。此框架是傳統的邏輯大考：答對則被擒，沉默則被斥為懦夫。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (tale-telling); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The mendicant's request sounded simple: a corpse from the burning ground on the fourteenth night - and the king, a man of his word, went alone to the dark to keep it. The corpse spoke as it was lifted: stories to pass the road, riddles to break the bargain - and the rule was understood at once: speak the answer, and I fly back to the tree; keep silent, and be shamed as a coward. Twenty-five riddles later the king out-tricked the trickster - one question he answered with a truth so bare that the spirit stayed to be caught: the frame story is India's logic-classroom, and its diploma is a captured ghost.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kathasaritsagara, Vetala cycle (Tawney 1880-84); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 苦行僧的請求聽來簡單：在第十四夜的焚屍場取一具屍體——而國王，一個言而有信之人，獨自走入黑暗去取它。屍體在被舉起時開口說話：故事用以打發路途，謎題用以破壞約定——而那規則立刻被領會：說出答案，我便飛回樹上；保持沉默，便以懦夫之名受辱。二十五道謎題之後，國王智勝了那作弄者——有一問他以如此赤裸的真相作答，以致那精靈留下來被擒：這框架故事是印度的邏輯課堂，而其文憑是一隻被擒的鬼魂。

canonical_translation: C. H. Tawney, 1880-84 (public domain)

title.en: Three Suitors and the Girl Made of Bones, Ashes and Charms
title.zh: 三位求偶者與骨、灰、咒所成之女

region.en: Burning ground of Ujjain (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 鄔闍衍那火葬地（象徵性定位）

period: Kathasaritsagara, Vetala-Panchavimshati tale, c. 1070 CE (Tawney translation, 1880-84)

source.work: The Katha Sarit Sagara, trans. C. H. Tawney (1880-84), Vetala tale of the restored maiden

summary.en: A maiden died and three suitors worked her three resurrections: one gathered her bones, one collected the ashes, one found the charm that restored her - and the restored girl was claimed by all three. The vetala asks the king: whose wife is she? The answer taught in the tale: the bones made the body she wears, but the one who knew the charm of life is the one who gave her back herself.
summary.zh: 少女已死，三位求婚者各完成其一部分的復活：一個收其骨，一個收其灰，一個尋得復原之咒——復生的少女被三者同時索求。毘舍遮問王：誰是她的丈夫？故事所教：骨成其所穿的身，而知生命之咒者才是把她還給她自己的人。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The maiden was dead, and three men loved the fact back to life: the bones gathered, the ashes collected, the charm found - a resurrection in three trades. The girl stood restored and was claimed three times - by the builder of her body, the keeper of her dust, the caster of her life; the vetala's riddle is which claim is marriage. The king's answer - the one who gave her back to herself - sent the vetala flying, and the tale's logic stands: a body is not a wife; the self is what the charm restored.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kathasaritsagara, Vetala tales (Tawney 1880-84); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 少女已死，而三個男人以愛將這事實重新喚回生命：骨骸被收攏，骨灰被聚集，咒語被尋得——一場由三種技藝完成的復活。女孩復原而立，被三度主張——由她身體的建造者、她骨灰的保存者、她生命的施咒者；毗陀羅的謎題是：哪一項主張才是婚姻。國王的答案——那將她還給她自己的人——使毗陀羅飛走，而故事的邏輯成立：身體不是妻子；自我才是咒語所復原之物。

canonical_translation: C. H. Tawney, 1880-84 (public domain)

title.en: The Bride Tested by the Serpent's Bite
title.zh: 以蛇咬試探的新娘

region.en: City of a merchant-king (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 商王之城（象徵性定位）

period: Kathasaritsagara, Vetala-Panchavimshati tale, c. 1070 CE (Tawney translation, 1880-84)

source.work: The Katha Sarit Sagara, trans. C. H. Tawney (1880-84), Vetala tale of the serpent-bite

summary.en: A bridegroom died of a serpent's bite on his wedding night; his bride, refused permission to burn with him, kept his body, caught the serpent as it returned to its hole, and held its head over her own neck - 'bite me or bring him back'. The serpent, out-bargained by a widow, restored the prince with its gift; the vetala's riddle asks who loved whom more - the wife who died for the husband, or the one who made death return him.
summary.zh: 新郎於婚夜死於蛇咬；其妻未獲准同焚，守其屍身，待蛇歸穴時將其擒住，以蛇首置於自己頸項——『咬死我，或使他復生』。蛇被寡婦逼出更好的交易，以其贈禮使王子復原；毘舍遮的謎題問誰愛得更深——為夫而死的新娘，還是令死亡歸還丈夫的那一位。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The prince died on his wedding night, and the widow's petition to burn with him was refused - so she took the law of grief into her own hands. She caught the serpent at its hole and gave it her own neck as its next bite: bring him back, or take me instead - the bargain a snake could not refuse.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kathasaritsagara, Vetala tales (Tawney 1880-84); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 王子在新婚之夜死去，而寡婦請求與他一同火葬被拒——於是她將悲傷的法則握入自己手中。她在蛇洞口捉住那條蛇，將自己的頸項獻作它的下一口咬：把他還回來，否則帶走我——這是蛇無法拒絕的交易。

passages.text: The prince woke in her arms; the vetala asked the king to weigh two loves - the one who lay down under the fangs, the one who lay down under the law - and the answer was neither: the serpent's gift was the marriage.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kathasaritsagara, Vetala tales (Tawney 1880-84); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 王子在她的懷中醒來；毘陀羅請國王權衡兩種愛——那躺臥於毒牙之下者，與那躺臥於律法之下者——而答案是兩者皆非：蛇的贈禮便是這樁婚姻。

canonical_translation: C. H. Tawney, 1880-84 (public domain)

title.en: The Sage and the Brazen门 Gate of Heaven's Gift
title.zh: 仙人與天賜銅門

region.en: Forest hermitage (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 森林仙居（象徵性定位）

period: Kathasaritsagara, c. 1070 CE (Tawney translation, 1880-84)

source.work: The Katha Sarit Sagara, trans. C. H. Tawney (1880-84), the sage and the heavenly gift

summary.en: A seer's hospitality was rewarded by heaven with a golden gate that gave whatever was asked at it - and the seer's city grew rich on the gift while his wife grew suspicious of the crowd. When the king of the city coveted the gate, the seer asked the gate to take itself away: prosperity that invites greed is a gift that must be declined. The vetala-style moral: the best gifts are the ones that can leave.
summary.zh: 仙人殷勤待客，上天以一扇金門為報——凡於門前所求皆得——而其城因禮而富，其妻卻因人潮生疑。當城王覬覦此門，仙人求門自去：招引貪婪的繁榮必須謝絕。毘舍遮式的道德：最好的禮物是能夠離開的。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Heaven's reward for the seer's open door was a gate with an open hand: ask and it is given - and the poor of the district arrived before the rumor did. The king heard of it as a treasury and came with soldiers; the seer heard of it as a test and came with a sentence - a gift that breeds robbery is a curse wearing a crown. He asked the gate to leave, and it folded itself out of the world: the tale's arithmetic is bhakti's - abundance is only dharma when it can be closed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Kathasaritsagara (Tawney 1880-84); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 上天對仙人敞開之門的賞賜，是一扇敞著手的門：求便得賜——而本地的窮人比傳聞先一步抵達。國王聽聞此事，視之為一座寶庫，便帶著兵士前來；仙人聽聞此事，視之為一場試煉，便帶著一句判詞前來——滋生搶劫的贈禮，是戴著王冠的詛咒。他命那扇門離去，門便自行摺疊，脫出這世界：此故事的算術是虔信（bhakti）的算術——豐盛唯有能夠關閉時，方為正法。

canonical_translation: C. H. Tawney, 1880-84 (public domain)

title.en: Naravahanadatta and the Quest for the Vidyadhara Crown
title.zh: 那羅婆訶那達陀與飛天王冠之探索

region.en: Vindhya and Himalaya, Vidyadhara realms (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 溫迪亞與喜馬拉雅，飛天境域（象徵性定位）

period: Kathasaritsagara of Somadeva, c. 1070 CE (Tawney translation, 1880-84)

source.work: The Katha Sarit Sagara, trans. C. H. Tawney (1880-84), the Naravahanadatta cycle

summary.en: The Ocean of Story's great frame: a prince told at birth that he will wear the crown of the Vidyadharas - the wizard-kings of the air - spends his whole youth on a quest up the mountains: sorcerers, flying cities, wife-captures, magic battles and loves, each one a story that contains another. The crown is less an object than the tale's own way of never ending.
