Diarmuid rolls a tun of wine down the hill with men crushed beneath it, lights on the point of Manannan's upturned spear like a bird, and walks thrice along the edge of Angus's sword; each feat is copied to death, fifty in the wine alone.
summary.zh: 芬恩遣「穆爾納赫特綠衣勇士」——兩千戰士與三隻火不能焚、水不能溺的魔犬——追捕逃亡者；他們遇上一名自稱昨日見過迪爾穆德的戰士。迪爾穆德滾酒桶下山、壓斃模仿者，如飛鳥般立於瑪那南倒插長矛之尖，並在安古斯之劍刃上三度行走——每一次技戲皆被依樣模仿而死，僅酒桶一項已斃五十人。

sensitivity.note: The lethal-feat mimicry (hostiles die copying the hero's tricks) is a fixed chase-tale device of the Diarmuid pursuit; the weapons named — Crann Buidhe of Manannan, Mor-alltach of Angus, Gae Buidhe/Gae Dearg — are Diarmuid's charter arms from his god-fosterers. Symbolic pin.

passages.text: Diarmuid went up on a hill that was near, and saw a great fleet of ships coming from the west, and when they were come to land, nine times nine of the chief men came on shore. "Three kings we are of the Green Champions of Muir-na-locht, and Finn, son of Cumhal, sent looking for us by cause of a thief of the woods, and an enemy of his own that has gone hiding from him. We are twenty hundred good fighting men, and every one of us is a match for a hundred, and we have three deadly hounds with us; fire will not burn them, and water will not drown them, and arms will not redden on them." "I saw him yesterday," said Diarmuid, "and I myself am but a fighting man. And by my word, you will know Diarmuid's hand when you will meet it."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 迪爾穆德登上附近的一座山丘，望見一支龐大的船隊自西方而來；當他們靠岸登陸時，九乘九的首領們上了岸。「我們是繆爾納洛克特綠衣勇士的三位國王，庫馬爾之子芬恩因林中一名盜賊、以及一個躲藏起來與他為敵的人，派人來尋我們。我們是兩千名善戰的精兵，我們每一個人都抵得上一百人，我們還帶著三隻致命的獵犬；火燒不傷牠們，水淹不死牠們，兵器也不會在牠們身上染紅。」「我昨日見過他，」迪爾穆德說，「而我自己不過是一名戰士。我以我的話擔保，當你們遇上迪爾穆德之手時，你們就會認得它。」

passages.text: "Is there wine in your ships? If you have a mind to bring out a tun of wine, I will do a trick for you." Diarmuid took the tun between his two hands and drank a drink out of it, and brought it to the top of the hill, and went up himself on the tun, and let it go down the steep of the hill till it was at the bottom; and he did that trick three times before the strangers. But they said he was a man had never seen a good trick when he called that a trick; and with that a man of them went up on the tun, but Diarmuid gave a stroke of his foot at it and the young man fell from it before it began to move, and it rolled over him and crushed him, that he died. Another man went on it, and another after him again, till fifty of them were killed trying to do Diarmuid's trick.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「你們船上可有酒？若你們有意搬出一桶酒來，我便為你們耍一個把戲。」迪爾穆德雙手捧起那桶酒，從中飲了一口，又把它帶到山頂，自己登上酒桶，任它沿著陡坡滾下，直到桶底；他在那些陌生人面前把這把戲耍了三次。但他們說，他把這稱作把戲，可見他是個從未見過好把戲的人；於是他們中有一人登上酒桶，但迪爾穆德一腳踢去，那青年便在桶開始滾動之前從桶上跌落，桶滾過他身上將他壓死。另一人又登上去，接著又一人，直到他們中有五十人因試圖耍迪爾穆德的把戲而死。

passages.text: And the next day he put off his arms, all but the shirt next his skin, and struck the Crann Buidhe, the spear of Manannan, into the earth with the point upwards, and rose with a leap and lit on the point of the spear as light as a bird, and came down off it again without a wound on him — and a young man of the Green Champions came down heavily on the point, and it went through his heart. And the third day he put the sword of Angus Og, the Mor-alltach, between two forked poles on its edge, and walked on the sword three times from the hilt to the point, and came down and asked was there a man of them could do that feat; and a man rose up to walk on the sword, but came down heavily on it the way he was cut in two halves.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 次日，他卸下鎧甲，只留下貼身的襯衣，將摩納南之矛「克蘭布伊」尖端朝上插入土中，縱身一躍，輕如飛鳥般落在矛尖上，又從矛尖上下來，身上毫無傷痕——而綠衣勇士中一名青年重重落在矛尖上，矛尖穿透了他的心臟。第三日，他將安格斯·奧格的寶劍「莫爾阿爾塔赫」以其鋒刃架在兩根叉狀木桿之間，沿劍從柄走到尖，來回走了三次，然後下來，問他們中可有誰能耍這般本領；於是一人起身去走那劍，卻重重落在劍上，被劈成兩半。

title.en: Three Kings Die in Diarmuid's Bonds
title.zh: 三王死於迪爾穆德之縛

region.en: Slieve Luachra, Co. Kerry, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭克里郡盧赫拉山

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VII, ch. III, eBook #14465

summary.en: After the Green Champions fall, Diarmuid binds their three kings and leaves them alive, knowing only four men — Oisin, Osgar, Lugaidh's Son and Conan — can loosen bonds he tied. Muadhan's belt-whelp leaps into the first hound's throat; the Red Spear brings out the second's bowels; the third Diarmuid dashes its brains on the flagstone of Dubhan, then casts down the troop with the Gae Dearg. Finn's woman-messenger of the Black Mountain reports it all, and the three kings die under the hardness of the bonds.
summary.zh: 綠衣勇士潰滅後，迪爾穆德生擒並縛其三王——他知道僅有奧辛、奧斯加、盧蓋德之子、科南四人能解他所縛之縛。穆阿丹腰帶中的幼犬躍入第一隻魔犬咽喉；紅矛穿出第二隻內臟；第三隻被他在杜班石上撞破頭顱，繼而紅矛連誅三將。芬恩的「黑山信使」回報一切，三王竟死於堅不可解的束縛之中。

sensitivity.note: The unloosenable bonds (only four named looser-men) are a legalistic chain-of-bonds device characteristic of the cycle's geis logic; Muadhan's belt-whelp parallels Bran's whelp-rearing. The messenger-woman (fast as a weasel) repeats the cycle's shape-shifting courier pattern.

passages.text: Diarmuid drew his sword the Mor-alltach out of its sheath, and he made a fierce blow at the head nearest him that put it in two halves. Then he made an attack on the whole host of the Green Champions, and began to destroy them, cutting through the beautiful shining armour of the men of Muir-na-locht till there was hardly a man that could go back to give news of the fight, but only the three kings and a few of their people. He put his battle clothes on him, that no weapon could go through, and took the sword of Angus, that left no leavings after it, at his left side, and his two thick-handled spears, the Gae Buidhe and the Gae Dearg, the Yellow and the Red, that gave wounds there was no healing for; and he bound the three kings fast and firm: "There is no man of the heroes of Ireland can loosen those bonds but four only, Oisin, son of Finn, and Osgar, son of Oisin, and Lugaidh's Son of the Strong Hand, and Conan, son of Morna; and I know well none of those four will do it."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 迪爾穆德從鞘中拔出寶劍「莫爾阿爾塔赫」，朝離他最近的那顆頭顱猛力一擊，將其劈成兩半。隨後他向綠衣勇士的整支軍隊發起攻擊，開始殲滅他們，砍穿繆爾納洛克特人華美閃亮的鎧甲，直到幾乎無人能回去報信，只剩下三位國王和少數部下。他穿上戰衣，任何兵器都無法穿透，又將安格斯的寶劍——那劍過處不留殘餘——佩在左側，並帶上他那兩支粗柄長矛「蓋布伊」與「蓋德爾格」，即黃矛與紅矛，它們造成的傷口無藥可治；他將三位國王牢牢緊緊地縛住：「愛爾蘭的眾英雄中，只有四人能解開這捆綁，即芬恩之子奧辛、奧辛之子奧斯加、強手之子盧蓋德的兒子，以及莫爾納之子科南；我深知這四人中無一人會去解它。」

passages.text: They brought their three hounds out of the ship and laid them on Diarmuid's track, and when he saw them coming like that he was filled with great hatred of them. Then Muadhan turned back, and took a whelp out of his belt, and put it on the flat of his hand; and when the whelp saw the hound rushing towards him, and its jaws open, he rose up and made a leap from Muadhan's hand into the throat of the hound, and came out of its side, bringing the heart with it, and left the hound dead after him. Another hound was loosened after them, and Diarmuid said: "I often heard there is nothing can stand against weapons of Druid wounding," and he made a cast at the hound, and the spear went through its body and brought out its bowels.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們把三隻獵犬從船上帶出來，放牠們去追迪爾穆德的蹤跡；當他看見牠們這樣追來時，心中對牠們充滿了極大的憎恨。於是穆阿丹轉過身來，從腰帶中取出一隻幼犬，放在自己的手掌心上；那幼犬見獵犬張著大口朝牠衝來，便躍起，從穆阿丹手中跳進獵犬的喉嚨，又從牠的側腹鑽出，帶出了心臟，留下那獵犬死在他身後。另一隻獵犬被放出來追他們，迪爾穆德說：「我常聽說沒有什麼能抵擋德魯伊致傷的兵器。」他朝那獵犬擲出一擊，長矛穿透牠的身體，帶出了牠的腸子。

passages.text: The third hound overtook them at Lic Dhubhain, the flag-stone of Dubhan, on Slieve Luachra; Diarmuid took him by the two hind legs, and struck a blow of his carcase against the side of the rock till he had let out his brains through the openings of his head and of his ears. Then he made a good cast at the young man of the green cloak that was at the head of the troop, and killed him, and the second man, and the third man in the same way. And when Finn heard of the Kings of the Green Champions that were bound by Diarmuid, neither Oisin nor Osgar nor Conan nor Lugaidh's Son would loosen them; and they were not long talking about it till the three kings died under the hardness of the bonds that were on them. Then Finn made three wide-sodded graves for them, and a flag-stone was put over them, and another stone raised over that again, and their names were written in branching Ogham.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第三隻獵犬在斯利夫盧阿克拉的杜班石板（Lic Dhubhain）處追上了他們；迪爾穆德抓住牠的兩條後腿，將牠的身軀朝岩壁猛力一擊，直到從牠頭部和耳朵的孔洞中打出了牠的腦子。隨後他朝那領隊、身穿綠斗篷的青年奮力一擲，將他殺死，又以同樣的方式殺死了第二人和第三人。當芬恩聽說綠衣勇士的國王們被迪爾穆德縛住時，奧辛、奧斯加、科南和盧蓋德的兒子都不肯去解開他們；他們沒商議多久，三位國王便在捆綁的堅硬之下死去。於是芬恩為他們掘了三座寬闊的草皮墳墓，墳上立了一塊石板，石板上又立了一塊石頭，並用枝狀歐甘文刻下了他們的名字。

title.en: The Rowan of Dubhros and the Hurling-Match of the Gods
title.zh: 杜布羅斯的花楸與神族擲球賽

region.en: Wood of Dubhros, Ui Fiachrach, Co. Mayo, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭梅奧郡杜布羅斯林地

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VII, ch. IV, eBook #14465

summary.en: Two daughters of Manannan quarrel over whose man is the better hurler, and the match between the Men of Dea and the Fianna runs three days and nights without a goal. Passing homeward through Ui Fiachrach, the gods drop a rowan berry of the Land of the Ever-Living Living Ones, and a tree springs up whose berries banish sickness, make the hundred-year-old young again, and turn any girl into a flower of beauty — a tree the Tuatha de Danaan must guard with the Surly One of Lochlann, a giant with one eye and a prophecy that he will not die till three strokes of his own iron club fall on himself.
summary.zh: 瑪那南的兩位女兒為誰的情人更善擲球而爭執，神族與菲亞納之賽遂歷時三日三夜不分勝負。神族歸途經過伊·菲赫拉赫時失落一顆「永生者之國」的花楸果，樹從果中生——食其果者百病不侵，百歲老人可返少年，少女可成絕色。神族不得不以獨眼巨人格瓦恩看守此樹——預言曰：唯有親受自己鐵棒三擊者方能殺他。

sensitivity.note: The rejuvenating rowan is the Fenian apple-of-immortality (Berries of the Land of Promise) — compare Goibniu's ale and Idunn's apples cross-traditionally; the hurling-match of gods and men is a distinctive Irish divine-game motif. Coordinates at the traditional Dubhros (Doo Lough) country.

passages.text: There rose a dispute one time between two women of the Tuatha de Danaan, Aine and Aoife, daughters of Manannan, son of Lir, for Aoife had given her love to Lugaidh's Son, and Aine had given her love to a man of her own race, and each of them said her own man was a better hurler than the other. It came from that dispute that there was a great hurling match settled between the Men of Dea and the Fianna of Ireland, on a beautiful plain near Loch Lein. The highest men and the most daring of the Tuatha de Danaan were there — the three Garbhs of Slieve Mis, and the three Mases of Slieve Luachra, and the three yellow-haired Murchadhs, and Bodb Dearg, son of the Dagda, and Manannan, son of Lir; and they themselves and the Fianna were playing the match through the length of three days and three nights, and neither of them winning a goal.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一次，達南神族（Tuatha de Danaan）的兩個女子之間起了爭執，她們是里爾（Lir）之子馬納南（Manannan）的女兒愛妮（Aine）與愛芙（Aoife）；因為愛芙已將她的愛給了魯蓋德之子（Lugaidh's Son），而愛妮則將她的愛給了自己族中的一名男子，兩人各自都說自己的男人比對方的男人更善於擲球。這場爭執促成了一場盛大的擲球比賽，由迪亞族（Men of Dea）與愛爾蘭的費安納戰團（Fianna）在利恩湖（Loch Lein）附近一片美麗的平原上較量。達南神族中最高貴、最勇猛的人都到了那裡——斯利夫米斯（Slieve Mis）的三位加爾布（Garbhs）、斯利夫盧阿克臘（Slieve Luachra）的三位馬斯（Mases）、三位金髮的穆爾哈德（Murchadhs）、達格達（Dagda）之子博德·德爾格（Bodb Dearg），以及里爾之子馬納南；他們與費安納戰團一連較量了三天三夜，雙方都未能攻進一球。

passages.text: Now the provision the Men of Dea had brought with them from the Land of Promise was crimson nuts, and apples, and sweet-smelling rowan berries. And as they were passing through the district of Ui Fiachrach by the Muaidh, a berry of the rowan berries fell from them, and a tree grew up from it. And there was virtue in its berries, and no sickness or disease would ever come on any person that would eat them, and those that would eat them would feel the liveliness of wine and the satisfaction of mead in them, and any old person of a hundred years that would eat them would go back to be young again, and any young girl that would eat them would grow to be a flower of beauty.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 迪亞族從應許之地帶來的儲糧，是深紅色的堅果、蘋果和芳香的紅果（rowan berries）。當他們經過穆艾德河（Muaidh）畔的烏伊·菲亞赫拉赫（Ui Fiachrach）地區時，一顆紅果從他們手中掉落，從中長出了一棵樹。它的果實具有靈力，凡吃過它的人永遠不會染上任何疾病；吃過它的人會感到如葡萄酒般的活力與如蜂蜜酒般的滿足；任何百歲的老人吃了它，都會重返青春；任何年輕女子吃了它，都會長成如花般的美人。

passages.text: And it is what they agreed, to send a young man of them in search of a man of Lochlann that would guard the tree by day and sleep in it by night; and his name was the Searbhan Lochlannach, the Surly One of Lochlann. Very black and ugly he was, having crooked teeth, and one eye only in the middle of his forehead. And he had a thick collar of iron around his body, and it was in the prophecy that he would never die till there would be three strokes of the iron club he had, struck upon himself.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們商定，派他們中的一個年輕人去找一位洛克蘭（Lochlann）人，讓他白天看守這棵樹，夜裡睡在樹上；他的名字叫塞爾班·洛克蘭納赫（Searbhan Lochlannach），即「洛克蘭的乖戾者」。他非常黑，非常醜，長著歪斜的牙齒，額頭正中只有一隻眼睛。他身上圍著一圈粗厚的鐵項圈，而預言說，除非他自己那根鐵棒在他身上打三下，他永遠不會死。

title.en: The Surly One of Lochlann Dies by His Own Club
title.zh: 洛赫蘭悍翁死於己棒

region.en: Wood of Dubhros, Ui Fiachrach, Co. Mayo, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭梅奧郡杜布羅斯林地

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VII, ch. IV, eBook #14465

summary.en: Finn sets two sons of Morna, children of his father's killers, the price of peace: Diarmuid's head or a fistful of the quicken berries of Dubhros. Oisin warns them of both; they choose to fight for Diarmuid's berries instead, and are bound by him. Grania will not live without the berries, so Diarmuid wakes the Surly One, takes his three blows on the shield, then seizes the iron club and strikes three great blows on the giant — putting his brains out through his head, fulfilling the prophecy.
summary.zh: 芬恩向弒父仇人莫爾納之子索和，開價：迪爾穆德之頭，或一把杜布羅斯花楸果。歐辛警告二者皆不可得；他們選擇為迪爾穆德求果，反遭其縛。格拉尼亞誓言無果不活，迪爾穆德遂喚醒悍翁，先受其三擊於盾上，繼而奪其鐵棒，反擊三棒——巨漿迸腦而出，預言應驗。

sensitivity.note: Self-inflicted fatal blows fulfilling a prophecy is the classic paradoxical-death motif (cf. Balor's eye under Lug, Rhiannon's birds); the 'fine of peace' demanded of orphans of old enemies is a legal-fiction of Irish feud-settlement. Same pin as the rowan record.

passages.text: Finn and his people were not long at Almhuin till they saw fifty armed men coming towards them: "We are enemies of your own, and our fathers were at the killing of your father, and they themselves died for that deed. And it is to ask peace we are come now to you." "I must put a fine on you first in satisfaction for my father's death. I am asking but the head of a champion, or the full of a fist of the berries of the quicken-tree at Dubhros." "I will give you a good advice, children of Morna, to go back to the place you were reared, and not to ask peace of Finn through the length of your lives. For do you know whose head he is asking you to bring him? The head of Diarmuid, grandson of Duibhne; and if you were twenty hundred men in their full strength, Diarmuid would not let you take that head."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 芬恩（Finn）和他的部眾在阿爾穆因（Almhuin）沒待多久，就看見五十名武裝男子朝他們走來：「我們是你們的仇人，我們的父輩參與了殺害你們父親之事，他們自己也為那件事喪了命。我們如今來，是向你們求和的。」「我必須先向你們索取賠償，以抵償我父親之死。我所求的，不過是一名勇士的首級，或者滿滿一拳杜布羅斯（Dubhros）那棵花楸樹（quicken-tree）的果實。」「我給你們一個好忠告，莫爾納（Morna）的子孫們，回到你們被養育長大的地方去吧，終你們一生都不要向芬恩求和。因為你們可知道他要求你們帶給他的是誰的首級？是杜布涅（Duibhne）之孫迪爾穆德（Diarmuid）的首級；就算你們有兩千名處於全盛之力的男子，迪爾穆德也不會讓你們取走那顆首級。」

passages.text: "Although the children of Morna do not go looking for those berries, I will not lie in a bed for ever till I get a share of them," said Grania, "and I will not live if I do not get them." Then Diarmuid went to the Surly One, and gave him a stroke of his foot, and said: "It is Grania, daughter of the High King, has a desire to taste those berries, and it is to ask a handful of them I am come." "If she is to die for it, she will never taste a berry of those berries." "Willing or unwilling, I will take those berries from you." When the Surly One heard that, he rose up on his feet and lifted his club and struck three great blows on Diarmuid, that gave him some little hurt in spite of his shield.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「雖然莫爾納的子孫不去尋那些果實，但在我分得一份之前，我是不會永遠躺在床上的，」格拉尼亞（Grania）說，「若得不到它們，我也活不下去。」於是迪爾穆德走到那乖戾者面前，用腳踢了他一下，說道：「是至尊王之女格拉尼亞想嘗嘗那些果實，我來是求取一把的。」「就算她因此而死，她也永遠嘗不到那些果實中的一顆。」「不管你願不願意，我都要從你手中取走那些果實。」乖戾者聽了這話，便站起身來，舉起他的鐵棒，朝迪爾穆德猛擊三下，儘管有盾牌護身，仍使他受了些許小傷。

passages.text: But when Diarmuid saw him not minding himself, he threw down his weapons, and made a great leap and took hold of the club with his two hands. And when he had a hold of the club he struck three great blows on him that put his brains out through his head. And when they saw the Surly One was killed, Diarmuid plucked the berries for Grania and for the children of Morna, and they ate their fill of them, and the two young men went back to where Finn was with the load Diarmuid plucked for them.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. IV; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但迪爾穆德見他疏於防備，便拋下武器，縱身一躍，雙手抓住了那根鐵棒。他抓住鐵棒之後，便朝他猛擊三下，把他的腦漿從頭顱中打了出來。眾人見那乖戾者已被殺死，迪爾穆德便為格拉尼亞和莫爾納的子孫們採摘果實，他們盡情吃了個飽，那兩名年輕人便帶著迪爾穆德為他們採摘的果實，回到芬恩所在之處。

title.en: The Fomor's Stake at Chess and the Broken Bread
title.zh: 弗莫爾的棋局賭注與碎麵包

region.en: Cave by the western sea, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭西海岩洞（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VII, ch. V, eBook #14465

summary.en: Storm-bound in a sea cave, Diarmuid and Grania host Ciach the Fierce One of the Fomor; at chess Diarmuid wins, and the Fomor stakes Grania for his winnings. Grania, jealous of the touch, stabs Diarmuid's thigh — and he makes an end of the Fomor and will not speak to her. From the Quarrel come the famous farewell-laments of Diarmuid and Grania, and the sign to Finn of broken faith: henceforth broken bread, not whole, is left behind.
summary.zh: 風暴困於海洞，迪爾穆德與格拉尼亞款待弗莫爾悍者基亞赫；棋局迪爾穆德得勝，弗莫爾竟以格拉尼亞作為賭注索取。格拉尼亞妒火中燒，刺傷迪爾穆德大腿——他誅殺弗莫爾後拒與她言語。由此衍生迪爾穆德與格拉尼亞著名的離別哀歌，以及向芬恩示忠的標記——此後留下的不再是整塊麵包，而是碎屑。

sensitivity.note: Chess as a binding game with persons as stake is the fixed otherworld-gamble motif (cf. Midir and Etain, Finn and the chessboard oracles); Diarmuid's leaving bread as a fidelity-sign to Finn is the tracking device of the pursuit narrative. Symbolic pin.

passages.text: One night while they were there a great storm came on, so that they went into the far part of the cave. But bad as the night was, a man of the Fomor, Ciach, the Fierce One, his name was, came over the western ocean in a currach, with two oars, and he drew it into the cave for shelter. And Diarmuid bade him welcome, and they sat down to play chess together. And he got the best of the game, and what he asked as his winnings was Grania to be his wife, and he put his arms about her as if to bring her away. And Grania said: "I am this long time going with the third best man of the Fianna, and he never came as near as that to me." And Diarmuid took his sword to kill Ciach, and there was anger on Grania when she saw that, and she had a knife in her hand and she struck it into Diarmuid's thigh. And Diarmuid made an end of the Fomor, and he said no word to Grania, but ran out and away through the storm.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們在那裏的一夜，一場大風暴襲來，他們便躲進洞穴深處。那夜雖然惡劣，卻有一個弗摩爾族人渡過西海而來——他名叫基亞赫，綽號「兇猛者」，划著一張雙槳皮舟，把舟拖進洞裏避風。迪爾穆德歡迎了他，兩人便坐下一起下棋。迪爾穆德棋局佔了上風，他索要的彩注竟是要葛蘭妮為妻，還伸手攬住她，像要把她帶走。葛蘭妮說：「我與芬尼亞的第三好漢同行這麼久，他從不曾這樣靠近過我。」迪爾穆德拔劍要殺基亞赫，葛蘭妮見了動了怒，手中正握著一把小刀，便刺進了迪爾穆德的大腿。迪爾穆德結果了那個弗摩爾人，對葛蘭妮一言不發，便冒著風暴奔出洞去。

passages.text: At the break of day she overtook him, and after a while they heard the cry of a heron: "Tell me that, Grandson of Duibhne, to whom I gave my love." "O Grania, daughter of the High King, woman who never took a step aright, it is because she was frozen to the rocks she gave that cry. O Grania of the beautiful hair, though you are more beautiful than the green tree under blossom, your love passes away as quickly as the cold cloud at break of day... I lost my people by you, and my lord, and my large bright ships on every sea; I lost my treasure and my gold; it is hunger you gave me through your love." And Grania said: "O Diarmuid of the face like snow, the sound of your voice was dearer to me than all the riches of the leader of the Fianna. The love-spot on your forehead is better to me than honey in streams...
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 天剛破曉她便追上了他。走了一陣，他們聽見一隻蒼鷺的叫聲：「告訴我吧，杜布涅的孫兒，我曾把愛情託付給你的那個人。」「哦，葛蘭妮，高王的的女兒，從不曾走對一步路的女人，那聲啼叫，是因為她被凍在岩石上了。哦，秀髮的葛蘭妮，你雖比開花的綠樹更美，你的愛卻像破曉的寒雲一樣轉瞬即逝……我為你失去了我的族人，我的君主，我在四海的大船；我失去了財寶和黃金；你的愛帶給我的只有飢餓。」葛蘭妮答道：「哦，面如雪的迪爾穆德，你的聲音對我來說，比芬尼亞首領的一切財富都可貴。你額上的愛斑，於我勝過流淌的蜜……

passages.text: O Diarmuid of the beautiful hands, take me now the same as before; it was with me the fault was entirely; give me your promise not to leave me." But Diarmuid said: "How can I take you again, you are a woman too fond of words; one day you give up the Head of the Fianna, and the next day myself, and no lie in it." They came then to a place where there was a cave, and water running by it, and they stopped to rest; and Grania said: "Have you a mind to eat bread and meat now, Diarmuid? Give me a knife, so, till I cut it." "Look for the knife in the sheath where you put it yourself." She saw then that the knife was in his thigh where she had struck it, for he would not draw it out himself; so she drew it out then, and that was the greatest shame that ever came upon her.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. V; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「哦，有美手的迪爾穆德，如今再如從前那樣要我吧；錯全在我；答應我不要離開我。」但迪爾穆德說：「我怎能再要你？你這女人太愛多言；今日捨棄芬尼亞的首領，明日又捨棄我，這話沒有半句虛假。」他們來到一處洞穴，洞旁有流水，便停下歇息。葛蘭妮說：「迪爾穆德，你現在想吃麵包和肉嗎？把刀給我，好讓我切。」「到你親手放刀的鞘裏去找吧。」她這才看見刀仍插在他大腿上，正是她刺進去的那把——他一直不肯自己拔出來。於是她拔出刀來，這是她一生所受最大的羞辱。

passages.text: They stopped then in the cave. And the next day when they went on again, Diarmuid did not leave unbroken bread like he had left every other day as a sign to Finn that he had kept his faith with him, but it was broken bread he left after him. And they went on wandering after that, all through Ireland, hiding from Finn in every place, sleeping under the cromlechs, or with no shelter at all, and wherever they went Finn would follow them, for he knew by his divination where they went; but one time he made out they were on a mountain, for he saw them with heather under them, and it was beside the sea they were, asleep on heather that Diarmuid had brought down from the hills for their bed; and so he went searching the hills and did not find them.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. V-VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們便在洞中歇下。次日再啟程時，迪爾穆德不再像往日那樣留下未掰開的麵包作為對芬恩守義的信號，而是留下了掰碎的麵包。此後他們輾轉流浪，走遍愛爾蘭，處處躲避芬恩，睡在巨石墓下，或全然露宿。無論他們去哪裏，芬恩總是追隨而至，因為他能以占卜知曉他們的去向。有一次他推算他們在一座山上，因為望見他們身下有石楠——其實他們在海邊，睡在迪爾穆德從山上採來鋪床的石楠上；於是他搜遍山嶺，終究沒有找到他們。

title.en: Grania's Sleep-Songs over the Wandering Bed
title.zh: 格拉尼亞的搖籃曲與流浪之床

region.en: Beinn Edair (Howth), Co. Dublin, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭都柏林郡埃達山（霍斯）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VII, ch. VI, eBook #14465

summary.en: Watched over by the sleep of Diarmuid, Grania sings her songs of the sleep in the South and the North and the West and the East — then rouses him: the stag is not asleep, the hornless doe cries after her fawn, the bog lark is not sleeping between the streams. In a cave of Beinn Edair an old woman dips her cloak in the sea and lies of frost and rivers to hold them for Finn; Grania tastes salt on the cloak and Diarmuid arms — and Angus Og's boat carries them away in the nick of night.
summary.zh: 守著迪爾穆德的酣眠，格拉尼亞唱起南、北、西、東四方名人酣睡之歌——隨即喚醒他：雄鹿未眠，無角母鹿啼喚花斑幼鹿，雲雀仍在溪澗間守望。埃達山洞中，老嫗以海水蘸濕斗篷、謊稱嚴寒冰封以拖住二人等芬恩到來；格拉尼亞舌試斗篷嚐出鹹味，迪爾穆德披掛而起——安古斯·奧格之舟恰於深夜接應他們脫險。

sensitivity.note: Grania's sleep-song and rousing-song are quoted whole through the cycle and are among the most anthologised Fenian lyrics; the wet-cloak betrayal test (tasting salt) is a countersign motif. Pin at Beinn Edair cave tradition.

passages.text: And Grania would be watching over Diarmuid while he slept, and she would make a sleepy song for him: "Sleep a little, a little little, for there is nothing at all to fear, Diarmuid, grandson of Duibhne; sleep here soundly, soundly, Diarmuid, to whom I have given my love. It is I will keep watch for you, grandchild of shapely Duibhne; sleep a little, a blessing on you, beside the well of the strong field; my lamb from above the lake, from the banks of the strong streams. Let your sleep be like the sleep in the South, of Dedidach of the high poets, the time he took away old Morann's daughter, for all Conall could do against him. Let your sleep be like the sleep in the North, of fair comely Fionnchadh of Ess Ruadh, the time he took Slaine with bravery as we think, in spite of Failbhe of the Hard Head. Let your sleep be like the sleep in the West, of Aine, daughter of Gailian, the time she went on a journey in the night with Dubhthach from Doirinis, by the light of torches. Let your sleep be like the sleep in the East, of Deaghadh the proud, the brave fighter, the time he took Coincheann, daughter of Binn, in spite of fierce Decheall of Duibhreann."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 迪爾穆德睡時，葛蘭妮總守在他身旁，為他唱一支安眠的歌：「睡一會兒，一小會兒，什麼都不必怕，杜布涅的孫兒迪爾穆德；安穩地睡吧，睡吧，我把愛情給了你的迪爾穆德。我來為你守夜，秀美的杜布涅的孫兒；睡一會兒，願祝福降在你身上，在堅實田野的泉邊；我那湖那頭來的羊羔，從湍急河岸來的羊羔。願你的睡眠像南方的睡眠，像大詩人德迪達赫的睡眠，那時他帶走了老莫蘭的女兒，任康納爾如何追迫也奈何不了他。願你的睡眠像北方的睡眠，像埃斯魯阿的美少年芬克哈的睡眠，那時他勇敢地帶走了斯萊妮，我們都這樣想，硬腦袋的法爾維也攔他不住。願你的睡眠像西方的睡眠，像加利安的女兒安妮的睡眠，那時她夜裏與多布赫塔赫舉著火把從多伊里尼斯啟程遠行。願你的睡眠像東方的睡眠，像驕傲而勇武的迪加赫的睡眠，那時他帶走了賓恩的女兒科因基恩，杜伊弗里恩的兇猛的德希爾也攔他不住。」

passages.text: And then to rouse him she would make another song: "Caoinche will be loosed on your track; it is not slow the running of Caoilte will be; do not let death reach to you, do not give yourself to sleep for ever. The stag to the east is not asleep, he does not cease from bellowing; the hornless doe is not asleep, crying after her speckled fawn; she is going over the bushes, she does not sleep in her home. The cuckoo is not asleep, the thrush is not asleep, the tops of the trees are a noisy place; the duck is not asleep, she is made ready for good swimming; the bog lark is not asleep to-night on the high stormy bogs; the sound of her clear voice is sweet; she is not sleeping between the streams."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 然後為喚醒他，她又唱另一支歌：「奎恩切要循你的蹤跡而至；奎爾特奔跑決不遲緩；莫讓死亡追上你，莫把你自己永遠交給睡眠。東方的雄鹿不曾睡，他的吼叫不曾停；無角的母鹿不曾睡，哭喚她斑點的小鹿；她躍過灌木叢，不曾在家安眠。杜鵑不曾睡，鶇鳥不曾睡，樹梢是一片喧鬧之地；鴨子不曾睡，已為暢游做好準備；今夜沼澤雲雀也不睡，在高曠多風的沼地上；她清亮的歌聲甜美，她不曾睡在溪流之間。」

passages.text: One time they were in a cave of Beinn Edair, and there was an old woman befriending them and helping them to keep a watch; and one day she chanced to go up to the top of Beinn Edair, and saw an armed man coming towards her, and did not know him to be Finn: "It is looking for a woman I am come, and for a woman's love. And will you do all I will ask you?" "I will do that," she said, for she thought it was her own love he was asking; and she told him where Diarmuid was hiding. She dipped her cloak in the sea-water before she went into the cave, and made a complaint against the cold: "Cold, cold, cold to-night is the wide plain of Lurg; the snow is higher than the mountains, the deer cannot get at their share of food...
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一次他們在貝恩埃達爾的一處洞穴裡，有一位老婦人與他們交好，幫他們守夜；有一天她偶然登上貝恩埃達爾的山頂，看見一個帶武器的人朝她走來，卻不知那人就是芬恩：「我來是為尋一個女人，為尋一個女人的愛。你願意做我要求你的一切嗎？」「我願意，」她說，因為她以為他所求的是她自己的愛人；她便告訴他迪爾穆德藏身何處。她進洞之前把斗篷浸在海水中，然後抱怨天冷：「今夜寒冷、寒冷、寒冷的是遼闊的勒爾格平原；雪比山還高，鹿兒吃不到自己那份食物……」

passages.text: Ice is heaped up in every ford; it is for that I am saying and ever saying 'Cold.'" And when she was gone, Grania took hold of the cloak she had left there and put her tongue to it, and found the taste of salt water on it: "My grief, Diarmuid, the old woman has betrayed us. And rise up now, and put your fighting suit upon you." And no sooner were they outside than they saw Finn and the Fianna of Ireland coming towards them; then Diarmuid saw a little boat at hand in the shelter of the harbour, and they knew it was Angus was in it, that had come again to help them to escape from Finn, and they went back with him for a while to Brugh na Boinne.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. VI; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 每一處淺灘都堆滿了冰；正因如此我才說、且一直說『冷』。」她走後，格拉尼亞拿起她留在此處的斗篷，把舌頭貼上去，發覺上面有海水的鹹味：「我的悲痛啊，迪爾穆德，那老婦人把我們出賣了。現在起來，把你的戰衣穿上。」他們剛走出洞外，就看見芬恩和愛爾蘭的費尼亞人朝他們而來；這時迪爾穆德看見港灣掩蔽處近旁有一隻小船，他們知道船裡是安格斯，他又來幫他們逃離芬恩，於是他們隨他回到博因河畔的布魯赫住了一段時日。

title.en: Finn's Nurse and the Spearing through the Drowned Leaf
title.zh: 芬恩的奶母與洞穿枯葉之矛

region.en: Land of Promise, western ocean (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 應許之地，西海（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VII, ch. VII, eBook #14465

summary.en: Beaten in Alban, Finn sails to the Land of Promise for his nurse, for it is not possible to put Diarmuid down by any strength of an army unless enchantment would put him down. Under a Druid mist she rises on a blast of Druid wind over the hunting Diarmuid with a drowned leaf, pierced like a mill-quern, and aims deadly spears through the hole — until Diarmuid, lying on his back, casts the Red Spear through the hole itself and the hag falls dead on the spot.
summary.zh: 阿爾巴受挫，芬恩遠航應許之地求助於奶母——「非魔力不能制服迪爾穆德」。她以德魯伊霧隱身，乘魔風升至打獵的迪爾穆德頭頂，持一片葉孔如磨盤的枯葉，穿孔擲出致命之矛——迪爾穆德仰臥舉紅矛，一擲洞穿葉孔，巫嫗當場斃命。

sensitivity.note: The nurse-enchantress of the Land of Promise is Finn's female counter-gift from the Sidhe (paralleling Manannan's fostering of Diarmuid); the millstone-holed leaf is one of the cycle's signature marvel-weapons. Symbolic pin.

passages.text: And after that, Finn went out again on the sea, and his people with him, and there is no word of them till they came to the Land of Promise where Finn's nurse was. And when she saw Finn coming she was very joyful before him. And Finn told her the whole story from beginning to end, and the cause of his quarrel with Diarmuid; and he said it was to ask an advice from her he was come, and that it was not possible to put him down by any strength of an army, unless enchantment would put him down. "I will go with you, and I will do enchantment on him."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 此後，芬恩又出海去了，他的部眾隨他同去，直到他們來到芬恩的乳母所在的應許之地，其間再無他們的音訊。她看見芬恩前來，在他面前十分歡喜。芬恩把事情的始末從頭到尾告訴了她，也說了他與迪爾穆德結怨的緣由；他說他來是為向她求一個計策，又說單憑軍隊的任何力量都不可能將他壓倒，除非用魔法將他壓倒。「我將與你同去，我要對他施魔法。」

passages.text: And when they came to Brugh na Boinne, the nurse put a Druid mist around Finn and the Fianna, the way no one could know they were there. Now the day before that, Osgar had parted from Diarmuid, and Diarmuid was out hunting by himself. That was shown to the hag, and she took a drowned leaf having a hole in it, like the quern of a mill, and she rose with that by her enchantments on a blast of Druid wind over Diarmuid, and began to aim at him through the hole with deadly spears, till she had done him great harm, for all his arms and his clothing, and he could not make away he was so hard pressed.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們來到博因河畔的布魯赫時，那乳母在芬恩和費尼亞人周圍布下一重德魯伊迷霧，使人無法察覺他們在那裡。而在此前一天，奧斯加已與迪爾穆德分別，迪爾穆德獨自外出打獵。此事被那老妖婆得知，她取來一片中間有洞的枯葉，那洞像磨坊的石磨一般，她藉魔法乘一陣德魯伊之風升到迪爾穆德上方，開始透過那洞瞄準他投擲致命的長矛，終於使他受了重傷，儘管他有鎧甲和衣物護身，卻因被逼得太緊而無法脫身。

passages.text: And every danger he was ever in was little beside that danger. And it is what he thought, that unless he could strike the old woman through the hole that was in the leaf, she would give him his death there and then. And he lay down on his back, and the Gae Dearg, the Red Spear, in his hand, and he made a great cast of the spear, that it went through the hole, and the hag fell dead on the spot. And he struck off her head and brought it back with him to Angus Og.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他以往所遭遇的一切危險，與那危險相比都微不足道。他心想，除非他能透過葉上的洞擊中那老婦人，否則她就會當場要了他的命。他仰面躺下，手持紅色長矛蓋德爾格，奮力一擲，長矛穿過那洞，老妖婆當場倒地而死。他砍下她的頭，帶回去交給小安格斯。

title.en: Peace with Finn and the Settling of Rath Grania
title.zh: 與芬恩議和與格拉尼亞堡的安定

region.en: Rath Grania, Ceis Corainn, Co. Kerry, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭克里郡格拉尼亞堡（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VII, ch. VII, eBook #14465

summary.en: With Finn's nurse dead, Angus Og goes mediator: to Finn, to the High King, and home to Diarmuid, who will make peace only on conditions — his father's district of Ui Duibhne free of Finn's hunting and the King's tribute, Dumhais in Leinster, and Ceis Corainn as a marriage portion with the King's daughter. The terms are granted, sixteen years of hiding are forgiven, and at Rath Grania Grania bears him four sons and a daughter, richer in gold and cattle than any man living.
summary.zh: 巫嫗既死，安古斯·奧格充當調停人：先見芬恩，再見至高王，最後回到迪爾穆德處。後者僅在特定條件下方肯議和——父親封地伊·迪夫涅免於芬恩狩獵與王室貢賦、倫斯特之杜馬伊斯、以及隨王室之女作嫁妝的凱斯·科雷恩。條件獲准，十六年藏匿既往不咎；格拉尼亞在堡中為他誕下四子一女，金銀牛羊之富冠絕當世。

sensitivity.note: The peace-conditions are a land-grant legal episode (éiric and marriage-portion vocabulary); the sixteen-year term of hiding is the cycle's fixed chronology before the Boar of Beinn Gulbain. Pin symbolic at traditional Rath Grania.

passages.text: And the next morning early, Angus rose up, and he went where Finn was, and he asked would he make peace with Diarmuid, and Finn said he would. And then he went to the King of Ireland to ask peace for Diarmuid, and he said he would agree to it. And then he went back to where Diarmuid and Grania were, and asked him would he make peace with the High King and with Finn. "I am willing, if they will give the conditions I will ask. The district my father had, that is, the district of Ui Duibhne, without right of hunting to Finn, and without rent or tribute to the King of Ireland; and with that the district of Dumhais in Leinster, for they are the best in Ireland, and the district of Ceis Corainn from the King of Ireland as a marriage portion with his daughter; and those are the conditions on which I will make peace with them."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 次日清晨，安格斯起身，去到芬恩那裡，問他是否願意與迪爾穆德講和，芬恩說願意。然後他去見愛爾蘭國王，為迪爾穆德請求和平，國王說他願意應允。接著他回到迪爾穆德和格拉尼亞所在之處，問他是否願意與至高王及芬恩講和。「我願意，只要他們答應我所要求的條件。我父親曾有的領地，即烏伊杜布涅的領地，芬恩不得在其中享有狩獵之權，也不必向愛爾蘭國王繳納租金或貢賦；此外還有倫斯特的杜姆海斯領地，因為那是愛爾蘭最好的地方，以及愛爾蘭國王作為他女兒嫁妝而給的凱斯科蘭領地；這些就是我願與他們講和的條件。」

passages.text: Then Angus went with that news to where the King of Ireland was with Finn, and they gave him all those conditions, and they forgave him all he had done through the whole of the time he had been in his hiding, that was sixteen years. And the place Diarmuid and Grania settled in was Rath Grania, in the district of Ceis Corainn, far away from Finn and from Teamhair; and Grania bore him children there, four sons and one daughter. And they lived there in peace, and the people used to be saying there was not a man living at the same time was richer as to gold and to silver, as to cattle and to sheep, than Diarmuid.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VII, ch. VII; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是安格斯帶著這個消息，前往愛爾蘭國王與芬恩所在之處，他們向他提出了所有這些條件，並赦免了他躲藏期間所做的一切，那已是十六年之久。狄爾米德與格拉尼婭安頓下來的地方是拉斯格拉尼婭，位於凱斯柯蘭地區，遠離芬恩與塔拉；格拉尼婭在那裡為他生下了孩子，四子一女。他們在那裡安居樂業，人們常說，當時在世之人中，沒有誰在金銀、牛羊方面比狄爾米德更為富足。

title.en: Tailc son of Treon and the Woman of the World's Three Walks
title.zh: 特雷昂之子塔爾克與三繞世界之女

region.en: Hill of the Fianna's gathering, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭菲亞納集結之丘（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VIII, ch. I, eBook #14465

summary.en: Dark clouds of blood hang over the Fianna's feats, and Finn's dream shows Aodh Beag headless and Goll fighting a very strong man. A beautiful woman with a crimson cloak comes asking protection from her husband Tailc son of Treon — skin of coal, the head and tail of a cat — and Finn gives it against the seven battalions. Thousands fall in their thousands; Osgar fights Tailc five days and nights without food or sleep and strikes his head off — and the woman, seeing all the slaughter done on account of her, falls dead of shame.
summary.zh: 菲亞納演武之際，血雲密佈，芬恩夢見無首的艾德·貝格與強人搏鬥的戈爾。一紅衣美婦前來求庇護，躲避其夫特雷昂之子塔爾克——他膚如煤炭、首尾若貓。芬恩以七營之力相保；千人千人的部隊潰滅；奧斯加與塔爾克晝夜五日無食無眠地血戰，終斬其首——而那女子見因己身而致的大屠殺，羞慚倒地而亡。

sensitivity.note: The blood-cloud omen and dream-oracle open the Book of the Fianna's wearing-away; the cat-headed marvel-man repeats the marvel-race repertoire (compare the Cat-Heads king slain by Abarthach). The heroine dying of shame at the rescue echoes Credhe's death for Cael — inversion of the grief-death. Symbolic pin.

passages.text: One time the Fianna were all gathered together doing feats and casting stones, and the Druid of Teamhair that was with them said: "I am in dread, Finn of the Fianna, that there is some trouble near at hand; look now at those dark clouds of blood that are threatening us side by side overhead, and there is fear on me that there is some destruction coming on the Fianna." Finn lay down to sleep, and it was not long till he saw through his sleep Aodh Beag his son, and he without his head; and after that he saw Goll fighting with a very strong man. And then he heard a great shout, and saw Conan running, and the hounds after him; and when he came, Osgar asked him where was Aodh Beag. "Nothing troubles me but myself," said Conan; and Osgar found Aodh Beag with no fear or trouble on him at all, stopping there till he would hear the noise of the shields.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一次，費尼亞全體聚在一起較量武藝、投擲石塊，隨行的塔拉德魯伊說道：「費尼亞的芬恩，我心中恐懼，近處恐有禍患；且看那些血色的暗雲，並肩在我們頭頂上威脅著我們，我擔心有某種毀滅正降臨到費尼亞身上。」芬恩躺下入睡，不久便在睡夢中看見他的兒子奧德貝格，且是無頭的；此後他又看見戈爾與一個非常強壯的人搏鬥。接著他聽到一聲巨響，看見科南奔跑，獵犬在後追趕；當他來到時，奧斯加問他奧德貝格在哪裡。「除了我自己，沒有什麼困擾我，」科南說；奧斯加發現奧德貝格毫無畏懼或困擾，只是待在那裡，直到他聽見盾牌的聲響。

passages.text: They saw a great army coming as if in search of them, and a beautiful woman, having a crimson cloak, came to them over the plain, and her voice was as sweet as music: "I am the daughter of Garraidh, son of Dolar Dian, the Fierce; and my curse upon the King of Greece that bound me to the man that is following after me, and that I am going from, Tailc, son of Treon. For he has no good appearance, and his skin is of the colour of coal, and he has the head and the tail of a cat.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們看見一支大軍前來，彷彿在搜尋他們，一位美麗的女子身披深紅斗篷，越過平原向他們走來，她的聲音甜美如樂：「我是加雷之子、凶猛者多拉爾迪安之女；我詛咒希臘國王，他將我許配給那個跟在我身後、而我正逃離的人——特雷翁之子塔爾克。因為他相貌不佳，膚色如煤，且長著貓的頭和貓的尾巴。」

passages.text: And I have walked the world three times, and I did not leave a king or a great man without asking help from him, and I never got it yet." "I will give you protection, or the seven battalions of the Fianna will fall for your sake." A thousand of the Fianna went out to meet him and his men, and they all fell, and not one of them came back again; and another thousand of the best men of the Fianna, having blue and green shields, went out under Caoilte, son of Ronan, and they were worsted by Tailc and his people. Then Osgar asked leave of Finn to go out and fight the big man, and he himself and Tailc, son of Treon, were fighting through the length of five days and five nights without food or drink or sleep; and at the end of that time, Osgar made an end of Tailc, and struck his head off. And as to the young woman, when she saw all the slaughter that had been done on account of her, shame reddened her face, and she fell dead there and then.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「我已走遍世界三遍，未曾放過任何一位國王或大人物而不向其求助，卻從未得到過。」「我願給你庇護，否則費尼亞的七個營隊將為你而倒下。」費尼亞的一千人出去迎戰他和他的部下，他們全都倒下，無一人歸還；費尼亞另一千名精銳，持藍綠盾牌，在羅南之子科爾特率領下出戰，卻被塔爾克及其部眾擊敗。於是奧斯加向芬恩請求出去與那大漢搏鬥，他本人與特雷翁之子塔爾克激戰了五天五夜，不食不飲不眠；在那段時間結束時，奧斯加結果了塔爾克，砍下了他的頭。至於那年輕女子，當她看到因她而造成的這一切殺戮時，羞愧染紅了她的臉，她當場倒地而死。

title.en: Meargach of the Green Spears
title.zh: 綠矛之梅爾加赫

region.en: Hill of the Fianna's gathering, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭菲亞納集結之丘（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VIII, ch. II, eBook #14465

summary.en: On the heels of Tailc's fall comes Meargach of the Green Spears, whose body no arms were ever reddened on, to avenge the queen-woman's death; Osgar fights him three days and at the last strikes off his head. Goll puts down Ciardan the Swift, and Conan — to Faolan's shame — takes Liagan the Nimble's head before the fight is begun: "If I could make an end of the whole army by one blow, I would do it, and I would not be ashamed."
summary.zh: 塔爾克既亡，梅爾加赫——「身經百戰而未嘗見血」的綠矛戰士——為王后之死而來復仇；奧斯加與其苦戰三日，終斬其首。戈爾誅「迅捷之基爾丹」；科南——令法奧蘭蒙羞——在交手之前便閃電般取下「敏捷之利亞根」首級：「若能一擊滅其全軍，我必為之而不以為恥。」

sensitivity.note: The honour-duel code (fair fight vs Conan's pragmatism) is debated in-text — a rare moment of the cycle commenting on its own ethics. Continuation record of the Tailc sequence; same symbolic pin.

passages.text: While the Fianna were gathered yet on the hill where Tailc, son of Treon, had been put down, they saw a very great champion coming towards them, having an army behind him; and he asked in a very rough voice where was Finn, the Head of the Fianna. "Meargach of the Green Spears is my name, and arms were never reddened yet on my body, and no one ever boasted of driving me backwards. Was it you, Finn, put down Tailc, son of Treon?" "It was not by me he fell, but by Osgar of the strong hand. And if it is satisfaction for her death or the death of Tailc you want, you can get it from a man of the Fianna, or you can go quietly from this place."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當費尼亞仍聚集在特雷翁之子塔爾克被擊倒的那座山上時，他們看見一位非常魁梧的勇士向他們走來，身後帶著一支軍隊；他用非常粗魯的聲音問費尼亞的首領芬恩在哪裡。「我是綠矛的梅爾加赫，我的身體從未染紅過兵器，也從無人誇口能將我逼退。芬恩，是你擊倒了特雷翁之子塔爾克嗎？」「他並非死於我手，而是死於強手奧斯加。如果你要為她的死或塔爾克之死尋求補償，你可以從費尼亞的某個人那裡得到，或者你可以安靜地離開此地。」

passages.text: It was Osgar stood up against him, and they fought a very hard fight through the length of three days, and at one time the Fianna thought it was Osgar was worsted, and they gave a great sorrowful shout. But in the end Osgar put down Meargach and struck his head off, and the army of Meargach keened him very sorrowfully. And after that, the two sons of Meargach, Ciardan the Swift and Liagan the Nimble, came up and asked who would come against them, hand to hand, that they might get satisfaction for their father.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 是奧斯加站出來對抗他，他們激戰了整整三天，有一次費尼亞以為是奧斯加被擊敗了，便發出極其悲痛的呼喊。但最終奧斯加擊倒了梅爾加赫，砍下了他的頭，梅爾加赫的軍隊為他悲痛哀悼。此後，梅爾加赫的兩個兒子，迅捷的基爾丹與靈巧的利亞甘，上前詢問誰願與他們交手，以便他們為父親尋求補償。

passages.text: And it was Goll stood up against Ciardan, and it was not long till he put him down; and Conan came out against Liagan, and Liagan mocked at him: "It is foolishness your coming is, bald man!" But Conan made a quick blow and struck his head off before the fight was begun at all. And Faolan said that was a shameful thing to do, not to stand his ground and make a fair fight. But Conan said: "If I could make an end of the whole army by one blow, I would do it, and I would not be ashamed, and the whole of the Fianna could not shelter them from me."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 而站出來對抗夏爾丹的是戈爾，沒過多久他便將他擊倒；接著康安出陣迎戰利亞甘，利亞甘嘲笑他：「禿頭漢，你來得真是愚蠢！」但康安迅速一擊，戰鬥尚未開始便已砍下他的頭。福蘭說這般行徑是可恥的，不站穩腳跟堂堂正正地決鬥。但康安說：「若我能一擊了結整支軍隊，我便會這麼做，且毫不羞愧，整個費尼亞也護不住他們。」

title.en: Ailne of the Bright Face and her Keening of Omens
title.zh: 明顏之艾妮與兆象哀歌

region.en: Cnoc-an-Air (Hill of Slaughter), west of Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭西部屠戮之丘（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VIII, ch. II, eBook #14465

summary.en: The battle stops on both sides for the coming of the golden-haired queen Ailne, who keens her husband Meargach and her two sons — and reads their deaths back through every omen: the host of the Sidhe fighting in the valleys of the air, tears of blood on their cheeks, the battle-crow, the stream turning to blood, the eagle over the dun, the withered tree, the vision of a lake of blood. Grania defends Finn against her; Ailne will have no food of the Fianna, and up to thirty against thirty and then all, until she is worsted and the hill keeps the name Cnoc-an-Air, the Hill of Slaughter.
summary.zh: 雙方陣前停下——金髮王后艾妮到來，哀悼亡夫梅爾加赫與兩子，並將其死兆一一追述：空中溪谷間的仙族大軍互戰、他們頰上的泣血、戰鴉之聲、化為血流的溪水、堡上盤旋的巨鷹、枯萎的樹、夢中之血湖。格拉尼亞為芬恩辯護；艾妮拒食菲亞納之食，索戰自三十對三十直至全軍——最終潰敗，該丘得名「屠戮之丘」。

sensitivity.note: Ailne's lament is the most extended omen-catalogue (filidecht prophecy-list) in the Fenian corpus — tears of blood, battle-crow, withering tree are standard Irish death-omens; the keening is ritual-adjacent material embedded in battle narrative. 'Resurrection' tag retained for the lament-rite function as in Credhe's lament.

passages.text: Then the two armies came towards each other, and they were making ready for the attack. And they saw a beautiful golden-haired woman coming towards them, and she crying and ever crying, and the battle was given up on both sides, waiting for her to come; and the army of Meargach knew it was their queen, Ailne of the Bright Face. And she went to the place where her husband and her two sons were lying, and stood over their bodies, and her golden hair hanging, and she keened them there: "O Meargach of the sharp green spears, it is many a fight and many a heavy battle your hard hand fought in the gathering of the armies or alone... My grief! my three Candles of Valour...
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 接著兩軍相向而行，正準備發動攻擊。他們看見一名美麗的金髮女子朝他們走來，她哭著，哭個不停，雙方於是都停止了戰鬥，等她前來；米爾加赫的軍隊認出那是他們的女王，明顏的艾爾妮。她走到丈夫和兩個兒子躺臥之處，站在他們的遺體旁，金髮垂落，在那裡為他們哀哭：「噢，持銳利綠矛的米爾加赫，你那堅硬的手在軍隊集結之時或獨自一人時，打過多少場仗、多少場沉重的戰役……我的悲痛啊！我的三支勇武之燭……」

passages.text: I knew by the great host of the Sidhe that were fighting over the dun, giving battle to one another in the valleys of the air, that destruction would put down my three. I knew at the beginning of the day when my three good men went from me, when I saw tears of blood on their cheeks, that they would not come back to me as winners. I knew by the voice of the battle-crow over your dun every evening, that misfortune and grief were at hand. I knew, Candles of Valour, by the stream near the dun turning to blood when you set out, that there would be treachery in Finn. I knew by the withering of the tree before the dun, that you would never come back as conquerors from the treachery of Finn, son of Cumhal."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我從那些在堡壘上空爭戰、在空氣的溪谷中彼此交戰的眾多希德大軍，便知道毀滅將要擊倒我的三人。那天清晨，當我的三個好男兒離我而去，當我看見他們臉頰上的血淚，我便知道他們不會以勝利者的身分回到我身邊。每天傍晚，我從你那堡壘上空戰鬥烏鴉的叫聲，便知道不幸與悲傷近在眼前。勇武之燭啊，當你們出發時，我從堡壘旁化為血水的溪流，便知道芬恩那裡必有背叛。我從堡壘前那棵樹的枯萎，便知道你們絕不會以征服者的身分，從庫馬爾之子芬恩的背叛中歸來。」

passages.text: When Grania heard what the woman was saying there was anger on her: "Do not be speaking against Finn or the Fianna, Queen, for it was not by any treachery or any deceit your three men were brought to their end." But Ailne gave no heed to her, and went on with her complaint, crying and ever crying. "I knew by the sorrowful vision that showed myself in danger, my head and my hands cut off, that it was yourselves were without sway. I knew when I saw in a vision a lake of blood in the place of the dun, that my three were put down by the deceit that was always with Finn." "Well, Ailne, I know it is a far journey you have come.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 格蘭妮聽見那女子所說的話，便動了怒：「女王，不要說芬恩或費尼亞的壞話，因為你的三個男兒並非因任何背叛或任何欺詐而喪命。」但艾爾妮毫不理會她，繼續她的哀訴，哭著，哭個不停。「我從那向我顯示自身身陷險境的悲傷異象，從我的頭和雙手被砍下，便知道是你們自己失了勢。當我在異象中看見堡壘所在之處成了一片血湖，我便知道我的三人是被那始終伴隨芬恩的欺詐所擊倒。」「好吧，艾爾妮，我知道你走了很遠的路而來。

passages.text: And come now and eat and drink with myself and with the Fianna." But Ailne would not do that, but said it would not be fitting for her to take food from people that did such deeds, and what she wanted was satisfaction for the death of her husband and her two sons. First it was settled for two men of each side to go out against one another, and then thirty men on each side, and then she said she would not be satisfied to go back to her own country till she brought the head of Finn with her, or till the last of his men had fallen. And there was a great battle fought in the end, and it is seldom the Fianna fought so hard a battle as that; but in the end Ailne of the Bright Face was worsted, and the hill in the west those battles were fought on got the name of Cnoc-an-Air, the Hill of Slaughter.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 現在來與我和費尼亞一同吃喝吧。」但艾爾妮不肯，說她從做出這等行徑的人手中取食並不合宜，她要的是為丈夫和兩個兒子的死討回公道。起初議定雙方各派兩人出陣對決，接著各派三十人，然後她說，除非她帶著芬恩的首級回去，或直到他最後一名部眾倒下，她都不會甘心回到自己的國土。最終爆發了一場大戰，費尼亞鮮少打過如此艱難的一仗；但最後明顏的艾爾妮敗下陣來，那些戰役所在的西方山丘便得了「屠殺之丘」之名。

title.en: Ailne's Revenge: The Prison under the Sea and Conan's Cup
title.zh: 艾妮的復仇：海底囚牢與科南之杯

region.en: Blue sea-house of Ailne's brother (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 艾妮其兄的海上藍屋（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book VIII, ch. III, eBook #14465

summary.en: A Druid mist draws Finn and the harper Daire to a lighted house in a stormy sea, Ailne's prison for revenge. Daire is forced to play — grief-strings, shouts of lamentation — to earn spells weakened by instalments, while the whole Fianna sleeps into the dun under sorcery. Beheadings sit them frozen on their benches until Conan leaps, loses his skin to the seat, and begs a sheepskin that grows to his body for life; with the enchanted cup he secretly revives Finn, Osgar and the host, Osgar kills the Grey Man, Ailne drops dead, and the dun vanishes to bare grass.
summary.zh: 德魯伊迷霧將芬恩與豎琴手戴爾引入風暴大海中燈火通明的屋宇——艾妮的復仇囚牢。戴爾被迫奏樂——悲弦與哀嚎之聲——以分段換取法術之緩；全菲亞納在巫術下睡入牢中。斬首之刑使眾人僵坐凳上，直到科南躍起、皮膚黏於凳面，討得一件終身長於己身的羊皮；他以魔杯暗中復甦芬恩、奧斯加與全軍，奧斯加誅灰衣人，艾妮倒地而亡，華屋化為荒草。

sensitivity.note: The spells-weakened-by-music instalment and the sitting-enchantment (no rising from seats) are fixed hostel-horror devices; Conan's sheepskin is the origin joke of his byname Conan Maol (the Bald) grown to a new level. The cup of the Sidhe restoring strength parallels Bebind's bowl in the corpus.

passages.text: One day Finn and his people were hunting on Slieve Fuad, and Finn and Daire of the Songs went astray and lost the rest of their people; a Druid mist came about them, and after a while they met with a young woman, comely and pleasant: "Glanluadh is my name, and my husband is Lobharan; and we heard the cry of hounds, and he left me and went after the hunt." They came to a hill and heard sleepy music of the Sidhe beside them, and heavy sleep came on Finn and Daire; and when they awoke they saw a very large lighted house before them, and a stormy blue sea around it. Then they saw a very big grey man coming through the waves, and he took hold of Finn and of Daire, and brought them across the waves and into the house, and shut the door with iron hooks: "My welcome to you, Finn of the great name; it is long we are waiting here for you." And the woman of the house they knew to be Ailne, wife of Meargach: "It is long I am looking for you, Finn, to get satisfaction for the treachery you did on Meargach and on my two comely young sons, and on Tailc, son of Treon."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一天，芬恩和他的部眾在福阿德山上狩獵，芬恩與歌謠之達雷走散了，與其餘部眾失散；一陣德魯伊迷霧籠罩了他們，過了一會兒，他們遇見一名年輕女子，容貌秀美、性情可親：「我叫格蘭盧阿德，我的丈夫是洛瓦蘭；我們聽見獵犬的吠聲，他便離開我，追獵去了。」他們來到一座山丘，聽見身旁希德的慵懶樂聲，沉重的睡意便降臨在芬恩與達雷身上；當他們醒來，看見眼前有一座非常巨大、燈火通明的屋宇，四周環繞著波濤洶湧的藍色大海。接著他們看見一個非常高大的灰衣人穿過波浪而來，他抓住芬恩和達雷，帶他們越過波浪進入屋中，並用鐵鉤關上了門：「歡迎你，大名鼎鼎的芬恩；我們在此等你已久了。」而屋中的女子他們認出是艾爾妮，米爾加赫之妻：「芬恩，我尋你已久，要為你對米爾加赫、對我兩個俊美的年輕兒子，以及對特雷翁之子塔爾克所行的背叛討回公道。」

passages.text: The Grey Man heard them talking of the Fianna, and that Daire had a great name for the sweetness of his music: "I will take my spells off you for so long as you play for me." "I could never make music seeing Finn in bonds the way he is." "I will take the power of my spells off Finn till you play for me." And Daire played first the strings of sweetness, and of the noise of shouting, and then he sang his own grief and the grief of all the Fianna. Now as to the Fianna, when they came to this place they could hear Daire's sweet music, and they made an attack on Ailne's dun to release them; but the Grey Man heard their shouts, and put the full power of his spells again on Finn and on Daire, and when they heard the noise like the loud roaring of waves, there was not one of them but fell into a sleep and clouds of death, and the Grey Man and Ailne brought the whole of the men of the Fianna into the dun, and put hard bonds on them.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 灰衣人聽見他們談論費安納，又聽說達雷以樂聲甜美而享有盛名：「只要你為我奏樂，我便在這段期間內解除對你施的咒術。」「眼看芬恩這般受縛，我實在無法奏樂。」「只要你為我奏樂，我便解除對芬恩所施的咒術之力。」於是達雷先彈奏甜美之弦，繼而奏出呼喊喧鬧之聲，然後唱出自己的悲傷，以及全體費安納的悲傷。至於費安納眾人，當他們來到此地，聽見達雷甜美的樂聲，便攻打艾爾妮的堡壘，欲救出他們；然而灰衣人聽見他們的呼喊，便再度對芬恩與達雷施以咒術的全部力量，當他們聽見那如波濤大聲咆哮般的聲響時，無一人不陷入沉睡與死亡之雲，灰衣人與艾爾妮遂將費安納全體男子帶入堡壘，並以堅固的鎖鏈縛住他們。

passages.text: They were kept a long time in that prison, and sometimes Ailne's brother would come in and strike the heads off some of them, for none of them could rise up from the seats they were sitting on through his enchantments. But one time he was going to strike the bald head off Conan, and Conan made a great leap from the seat; but if he did, he left strips of his skin hanging to it, that his back was left bare. And then he came round the Grey Man with his pitiful words: "Stop your hand now, for that is enough for this time; and do not send me to my death yet awhile, and heal me of my wounds first." And the reason he said that was because he knew Ailne to have an enchanted cup in the dun that had cured Glanluadh. And the Grey Man took pity on his case, and Ailne brought a sheepskin and put it on Conan's back, and it fitted and grew to him, and covered his wounds.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們被囚禁於那座牢中許久，有時艾爾妮的兄弟會進來，砍下其中幾人的頭顱，因為憑他的魔法，他們無人能從所坐的座位上起身。但有一次，他正要砍下科南的禿頭，科南便從座位上猛然一躍；然而他雖躍起，卻留下片片皮肉黏在座位上，以致他的背脊裸露無遺。接著他便以哀懇之言向灰衣人求道：「現在請住手吧，這回已經夠了；暫且別送我去死，先醫好我的傷。」他這麼說，是因為他知道艾爾妮的堡壘中有一只曾治好格蘭盧阿德的魔法杯。灰衣人憐憫他的處境，艾爾妮便取來一張羊皮，覆在科南背上，羊皮便貼合在他身上，與他一同生長，並遮蓋了他的傷口。

passages.text: And with that he brought Conan to where the enchanted cup was, and put it in his hand; and no sooner was the Grey Man gone than Conan took out the cup that he had hidden, and gave a drink from it to Finn and to Osgar and to the rest of the Fianna, and they that were withered and shaking got back their own appearance and their strength again on the moment. And when the Grey Man came back and saw what had happened, Osgar attacked him, and it was not long till he made him acquainted with death; and when Ailne saw that, with the grief and the dread that came on her, she fell dead then and there. But as to Conan, the sheepskin never left him; and the wool used to grow on it every year, the same as it would on any other skin.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book VIII, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是灰衣人帶科南到魔法杯所在之處，將杯放在他手中；灰衣人一走，科南便取出他先前藏起的杯子，讓芬恩、奧斯加以及其餘費安納眾人各飲一口，那些枯萎顫抖的人當下便恢復了本來的容貌與力氣。灰衣人回來見狀，奧斯加便向他進攻，不久便讓他嘗到了死亡的滋味；艾爾妮見此，悲痛與恐懼齊湧心頭，當場倒地而死。至於科南，那張羊皮始終沒有離開他；羊毛每年都會在上面生長，就像在任何其他皮上生長一樣。

title.en: The Quarrel at Almhuin and the Slain of Berach Brec
title.zh: 艾倫山之爭與貝拉赫之死

region.en: Almhuin (Hill of Allen), Co. Kildare, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭基爾代爾郡艾倫山

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IX, ch. I, eBook #14465

summary.en: At Finn's feast in Almhuin, Goll's hand-tribute from the men of Lochlann stirs the old quarrel with the sons of Morna; blows begin between Cairell and Conan and spread through the whole hall until the poets' songs put the weapons on the floor and bonds of peace on Finn and Goll. The feud breaks out again at the dividing of a pig of Manannan's: Berach Brec, the yellow-haired queen Finn loved, is speared by Art son of Morna on the strand; the hound Conbeg is drowned; and nine women of the Tuatha de Danaan are slain on their way to meet nine men of the Fianna.
summary.zh: 艾倫山宴上，戈爾自洛赫蘭人收取的「手貢」重燃與莫爾納諸子的宿怨；凱瑞爾與科南鬥毆擴及全廳，詩人之歌使兵刃落地，芬恩與戈爾立誓暫和。然曼南之豬分配爭執再啟戰端：芬恩所愛的金髮王后貝拉赫·布里克遭莫爾納之子阿特矛殺於海灘；忠犬康貝格被溺斃；九位神族女子赴會途中亦遭殺害。

sensitivity.note: The poets-as-peacemakers scene is the fixed image of filid authority (bonding kings and champions); the killing of Berach and the women en route to meet the Fianna are transgression-motifs marking the feud's guilt-load before Goll's death. Pin is Almhuin.

passages.text: It was not long after that Finn gave a feast at Almhuin for all his chief men, and Fergus of the True Lips rose up and sang before Finn the songs and the good poems of his forefathers; and then he went on to Goll, son of Morna, and told the fights and the destructions and the courtings of his fathers, and it is well-pleased and high-minded the sons of Morna were, listening to that. And Goll said then: "Where is my woman-messenger?" and with that she laid on the floor of the hall before Goll a load of pure gold, the size of a good pig.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 此後不久，芬恩在阿爾穆因為他所有的首領設宴，真唇費格斯起身，在芬恩面前歌唱他祖先的歌謠與佳詩；接著他又轉向莫爾納之子戈爾，講述他父輩的戰役、毀滅與求愛之事，莫爾納的眾子聽得十分滿意，意氣高昂。戈爾隨即說道：「我的女使者在哪裡？」說著，她便在大廳地板上、戈爾面前放下一堆純金，大小如同一頭肥豬。

passages.text: "How long is it, Goll, you have this rent on the men of Lochlann, and my own rent being on them always with it?" And Goll saw there was anger on Finn, and told how Cumhal had banished the sons of Morna and put him out of country after country, till he came back and fought a battle against Finn's father, and he fell by him there. "By your own hand, if you were to give me the same treatment your father gave me, I would pay you the same way as I paid him."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「戈爾，你向洛克蘭人索取這筆貢賦有多久了？而我自己的貢賦也一直與此並存向他們索取。」戈爾看出芬恩面有怒色，便講述庫瓦爾如何放逐莫爾納的眾子，將他逐出一國又一國，直到他歸來，與芬恩之父交戰，並在那裡被他擊倒。「若你以你父親對待我的方式對待我，我便會以我對待他的方式回報你。」

passages.text: Then Cairell of the White Skin, son of Finn, gave a furious blow of his fist to Conan, and Conan gave him back a blow in his teeth, and it was not long till many of the chief men of the Fianna were fighting on the side of Finn or on the side of the sons of Morna. But then Fergus of the True Lips rose up, and the rest of the poets of the Fianna along with him, and they sang their songs and their poems to check and to quiet them; and they left off their fighting at the sound of the poets' songs, and let their weapons fall on the floor, and the poets took them up, and put bonds on Finn and on Goll to keep the peace for a while. But it broke out again, one time there was a falling out between Finn and Goll as to the dividing of a pig of the pigs of Manannan, and fifteen of the sons of Morna were killed at Daire Tardha.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是芬恩之子、白膚凱雷爾揮拳猛擊科南，科南也回擊他的牙齒，不久費安納的許多首領便分作兩方，或助芬恩，或助莫爾納的眾子而打了起來。但真唇費格斯隨即起身，費安納其餘的詩人也隨他而起，他們唱起歌謠與詩篇，以制止並安撫他們；眾人聞詩人之歌便停止爭鬥，將武器丟落地上，詩人們拾起武器，並令芬恩與戈爾立約，暫且維持和平。但爭端又再度爆發，有一次芬恩與戈爾因分配瑪納南的豬群中一頭豬而起爭執，莫爾納的眾子中有十五人在達雷塔爾哈被殺。

passages.text: They kept to their word and spared no one: there was a yellow-haired queen that Finn loved, Berach Brec her name was, that had her house full of treasures and never refused the asking of any; and the sons of Morna bade her give up Finn, and she said she would not give up her kind lover to please them, and Art, son of Morna, made a cast of his spear that went through her body, that she died. And Goll took a little hound that Finn thought a great deal of, Conbeg its name was, and he drowned it in the sea; and about that time, nine women of the Tuatha de Danaan came to meet with nine men of the Fianna, and the sons of Morna saw them coming and made an end of them.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們信守諾言，一個也不放過：有一位芬恩所愛的黃髮王后，名叫貝拉赫·布雷克，她的宅邸滿是財寶，從不拒絕任何人的請求；莫納之子們命她交出芬恩，她說她不願為討好他們而拋棄自己仁慈的愛人，於是莫納之子阿特擲出長矛，穿透她的身體，她便死了。戈爾又捉住一隻芬恩極為珍視的小獵犬，名叫康貝格，將牠溺死在海中；大約就在那時，九名達努神族的女子前來與九名費尼亞的戰士相會，莫納之子們見她們到來，便將她們盡數殺害。

title.en: The Death of Goll on the Sea Rocks
title.zh: 海岩上的戈爾之死

region.en: Sea-cave point, west coast of Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭西海岸海岬岩洞（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IX, ch. II, eBook #14465

summary.en: Goll kills Cairell son of Finn in the sea at the strand and withdraws to a cave in a point of rock. Finn watches every path and gap; Osgar comes as a friend and Goll's cast crushes his shield, hardening Finn's anger. Goll's wife calls him over the water — she will nurse him from her own breast — but he refuses: he never took the advice of a woman east or west, bids her remember her seven hounds and her former lover, and lies down on the rocks, dying at the end of twelve days.
summary.zh: 戈爾於海灘誅芬恩之子凱瑞爾，退隱海岬岩洞。芬恩遣人封鎖每條通路；奧斯加前來示好，戈爾一矛擊碎其盾，更激芬恩之怒。其妻隔水相喚——願以自己的乳哺他——他卻拒絕：「我東西四海從不聽女子之言」，囑她記起七隻獵犬與舊情人，臥於岩石之上，十二日後死去。

sensitivity.note: Goll's refusal of rescue through pride ('I never took the advice of a woman') is the fixed heroic-death-by-decline motif; the wife's breast-nursing offer inverts the mother-goddess pattern. Symbolic pin at the cave-point tradition.

passages.text: And at last it chanced that Goll and Cairell, son of Finn, met with one another, and said sharp words, and they fought in the sea near the strand, and Cairell got his death by Goll. And there was great anger and great grief on Finn, seeing his son, that was so strong and comely, lying dead and grey, like a blighted branch. As to Goll, he went away to a cave that was in a point stretching out into the sea, and Osgar knew where he was, and he went to see him, that had been his comrade in so many battles; but Goll thought it was as an enemy he came, and he made a cast of his spear at him that struck his shield and crushed it. And Finn bade his men watch every path and every gap that led to the cave the way they would make an end of him; and Goll stopped where he was, without food, without drink, blinded with the sand that was blowing into his eyes.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 最後，戈爾與芬恩之子凱雷爾偶然相遇，彼此說了幾句刻薄的話，便在岸邊的海中交戰，凱雷爾被戈爾所殺。芬恩見自己的兒子——如此強壯俊美——如今灰白地躺著死去，如同一根枯萎的樹枝，心中充滿了極大的憤怒與悲痛。至於戈爾，他離去，躲進一處伸入海中的岬角上的洞穴；奧斯加知道他所在之處，便前去見他——此人曾與他並肩作戰於無數戰役；但戈爾以為他是以敵人的身分前來，便向他擲出長矛，擊中他的盾牌，將盾牌擊碎。芬恩命手下把守通往那洞穴的每一條路徑與每一處缺口，好將他置於死地；戈爾便留在原地，無食無飲，被吹進眼中的沙子弄得雙目失明。

passages.text: His wife came to a rock where she could speak with him: "Come over to me, and it is a pity you to be blinded where you are, on the rocks of the waste sea, with no drink but the salt water, a man that was first in every fight. And in place of the hard sea-water I will nourish you from my own breast, and it is I will do your healing. And the gold of your hair is my desire for ever." But Goll would not leave the spot where he was for all she could say: "It is best as it is, and I never took the advice of a woman east or west, and I never will take it.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他的妻子來到一塊能與他說話的岩石上：「到我這邊來吧，你這樣雙目失明地待在那裡，實在可憐，在荒涼大海的岩石上，除了鹹水別無可飲，而你曾是每一場戰鬥中的第一人。我願以自己的乳汁代替那苦澀的海水哺育你，我願為你療傷。你那金髮，是我永遠的渴望。」但無論她怎麼說，戈爾都不肯離開他所在的地方：「這樣最好，我從未聽過東方或西方任何女人的勸告，今後也絕不會聽。

passages.text: And remember now your silver and your gold, and your silks and stuffs, and remember the seven hounds I gave you at Cruadh Ceirrge; and do not be crying tears after me, but remember your constant lover, Aodh, the son of the best woman of the world, that came out from Spain asking for you, and go to him now, for it is bad when a woman is in want of a good man." And he lay down on the rocks, and at the end of twelve days he died. And his wife keened him there, and made a great lamentation for her husband that had such a great name, and that was the second best of the Fianna of Ireland.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 如今請記住你的金銀，記住你的絲綢與布匹，記住我在克魯阿德·凱爾格給你的那七隻獵犬；不要為我流淚，而要記住你那忠貞的愛人奧德——世間最優秀女子的兒子，他從西班牙前來尋你，如今去投奔他吧，因為一個女人若缺少一個好男人，那是不好的。」於是他躺在岩石上，過了十二天，他便死了。他的妻子在那裡為他哀哭，為她那聲名顯赫的丈夫、愛爾蘭費尼亞中第二出色的英雄，舉行了盛大的哀悼。

title.en: The Battle of Gabhra and the Death of Osgar
title.zh: 加布拉之戰與奧斯加之死

region.en: Hill of Gabhra, Co. Dublin, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭都柏林郡加布拉丘（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book IX, ch. III, eBook #14465

summary.en: The High King turns against the Fianna, and Osgar rides to his feast with three hundred men; a woman of the Sidhe washing blood-red clothes foretells nine hundred falling by him and the king's death-wound. The demand for Osgar's spear of nine spells breaks the peace, and at Gabhra — twenty men against one — Osgar kills his hundreds, sends the spear of seven spells through his own body, and answers it with his spear into the meeting of the king's hair and beard. He falls like a king; the whole rath at Gabhra is his grave, and Finn never shed a tear in all his lifetime but for Osgar and for Bran.
summary.zh: 至高王倒向敵視菲亞納，奧斯加率三百人赴宴；河邊浣洗血衣的仙姝預言：九百人將亡於其手，王亦受其致命傷。索劍之爭破裂，加布拉丘上——二十敵一——奧斯加連誅數百，身中七咒之矛，反手將九咒之矛送入王者鬚髮之間。如王者般倒下；加布拉全丘盡為其墓——芬恩一生只為奧斯加與布蘭流過淚。

sensitivity.note: Gabhra is the Fenian eschaton — the wearing-away of the Fianna before the coming of the saints; the washing-woman omen parallels the washing-bean-sidhe omen-complex of later folklore. Finn's two tears (Osgar, Bran) is a famous character-note. Pin symbolic at the traditional site.

passages.text: The High King of Ireland had got to be someway bitter against Finn and the Fianna, and he spoke out to his people: "I would sooner die fighting the Fianna, if I could bring them down along with me, than live with Ireland under them the way it is now." And when all was ready he sent and bade Osgar to come to a feast he was making at Teamhair. And Osgar set out for Teamhair, and three hundred of his men with him; and on the way they saw a woman of the Sidhe washing clothes at a river, and there was the colour of blood on the water where she was washing them. "There is red on the clothes you are washing; and it is for the dead you are washing them." "It is not long till the ravens will be croaking over your own head after the battle. There will nine hundred fall by yourself, and the High King himself will get his death-wound from you."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 愛爾蘭的最高國王不知怎地對芬恩與費尼亞心懷怨恨，他向自己的人們說道：「我寧願與費尼亞作戰而死，只要能拉他們與我同歸於盡，也不願像現在這樣，讓愛爾蘭活在他們的統治之下。」一切準備妥當後，他派人召奧斯加前來他於塔拉所設的宴會。奧斯加便啟程前往塔拉，隨行三百名部下；途中他們看見一名希德族的女子在河邊洗衣，她洗衣處的水上泛著血一般的顏色。「你洗的衣服上有紅色；你是在為死者洗衣。」「不久之後，烏鴉便會在你戰後的頭頂上呱呱叫了。將有九百人死於你手，而最高國王本人也將被你重創致死。」

passages.text: On the last day of the drinking the High King called out with a loud voice, and asked Osgar would he make an exchange of spears with him. "It is not right for you to ask my spear." "I will put my spear of the seven spells out through your body." "And I give my word against that, I will put my spear of the nine spells between the meeting of your hair and your beard." It was at the hill of Gabhra the two armies met, and there were twenty men with the King of Ireland for every man that was with Finn. As to Osgar, he killed five score of the Sons of the Gael, and five score fighting men from the Country of Snow, and seven score of the Men of Green Swords, and four hundred from the Country of the Lion, and five score of the sons of kings.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 飲宴的最後一天，最高國王高聲呼喊，問奧斯加是否願意與他交換長矛。「你向我索要長矛，是不對的。」「我要將我那支有七重法力的長矛刺穿你的身體。」「我以我的諾言擔保，我要將我那支有九重法力的長矛，刺進你頭髮與鬍鬚交界之處。」兩軍在加夫拉山崗相遇，愛爾蘭國王那邊每一名隨芬恩的戰士，便有二十名士兵。至於奧斯加，他殺死了一百名蓋爾之子、一百名來自雪之國的戰士、一百二十名綠劍之人、四百名來自獅之國的人，以及一百名君王之子。

passages.text: But when he saw the High King near him, he made for him like a wave breaking on the strand; and the king made a cast of his greedy spear, and it went through his body and brought him down on his right knee; but Osgar made a cast of his spear of the nine spells that went into the High King at the meeting of the hair and the beard, and gave him his death. And Osgar lifted a thin bit of a slab-stone and made a cast of it that broke the king's helmet where it was hung on a pillar, and then he himself fell like a king.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但當他看到至尊王就在近旁，便如浪濤拍岸般朝他撲去；國王擲出他那貪婪的長矛，矛穿透了他的身體，將他擊得單膝跪地；然而奧斯卡也擲出他那帶有九道咒術的長矛，那矛正中至尊王髮與鬚相接之處，給了他致命一擊。奧斯卡又拾起一塊薄薄的石板碎片擲了出去，擊碎了懸掛在石柱上的國王頭盔，隨後他自己也如一位君王般倒下。

passages.text: Oisin went looking for Osgar, and it is the way he found him, lying stretched, resting on his left arm and his broken shield beside him, and his sword in his hand yet. "It is glad I am to see you safe, my father." And Caoilte searched the wound, and when he saw how the spear had torn its way through to the back he cried out: "O Osgar, you are parted from the Fianna, and they themselves must be parted from battle from this out, and they must pay their tribute to the King of Ireland." When Osgar saw Finn coming he saluted him and said: "I have got my desire in death, Finn of the sharp arms." "Child of my child, calf of my calf, white and slender, it is a pity the way you are. And my heart is starting like a deer, and I am weak after you and after the Fianna of Ireland. And farewell now to battles and to a great name, and farewell to taking tributes; for every good thing I ever had is gone from me now." And when Osgar heard those words he stretched out his hands, and his eyelids closed. And Finn turned away from the rest, and he cried tears down; and he never shed a tear through the whole length of his lifetime but only for Osgar and for Bran. And the whole length of the rath at Gabhra, from end to end, it is that was the grave of Osgar, son of Oisin, son of Finn.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book IX, ch. III; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 奧伊辛前去尋找奧斯卡，他找到他時，他便是這般模樣：直挺挺地躺著，倚著左臂，破損的盾牌擱在身旁，手中仍握著劍。「見你安然無恙，我很高興，我的父親。」凱爾特查看了傷口，當他看到長矛如何一路撕裂穿至背後時，他喊道：「噢，奧斯卡，你已與費尼亞人分離，而他們從今往後也必將與戰鬥分離，他們必得向愛爾蘭之王繳納貢賦。」奧斯卡見芬恩走來，便向他行禮說道：「我已在死亡中得償所願，銳臂的芬恩。」「我孩子的孩子，我犢的犢，白皙而修長，你這般模樣真是可惜。我的心像鹿一樣躍動，在你之後、在愛爾蘭的費尼亞人之後，我已虛弱不堪。如今告別戰鬥與盛名，告別收取貢賦；因為我曾擁有的一切美好，如今都已離我而去。」奧斯卡聽到這番話，便伸出雙手，眼瞼闔上。芬恩轉身離開眾人，淚水滾落而下；他一生漫長歲月中從未落過一滴淚，唯有為奧斯卡和為布蘭。加夫拉的整座環堡，從一端到另一端，便是奧斯卡——奧伊辛之子、芬恩之孫——的墳墓。

title.en: The Fawn That Passed under Finn's Knees
title.zh: 自芬恩膝下穿過的母鹿

region.en: Almhuin hunting-ground, Co. Kildare, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭基爾代爾郡艾倫山獵場

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book X, ch. I, eBook #14465

summary.en: Hunting one day, Finn and Bran follow a fawn that speaks: if she goes into the sea she will never come back, but no air will save her from Bran, who could overtake the wild geese. "Go out through my legs," says Finn — and as Bran goes under him he squeezes his two knees on her, and she dies on the moment. Some say the fawn was Oisin's mother; Finn grieves as he did for Osgar, and some say Bran and Sceolan are still seen to start at night out of the thicket on the hill of Almhuin.
summary.zh: 獵之日，芬恩與布蘭追趕一頭能言的母鹿：「若入海我永不回返；然上天亦難逃布蘭——她連野雁也能追上。」「從我腿間穿過吧。」布蘭掠過芬恩膝下之際，他雙膝一夾，母鹿當場斃命。有人說那母鹿正是歐辛之母；芬恩哀慟如失奧斯加——而人們說，至今夜裡仍見布蘭與斯克奧蘭自艾倫山樹叢間驚躍而出。

sensitivity.note: The speaking fawn and the knee-death repeat the Donn-Steward killing pattern (birth chapter of Diarmuid), closing the circle of knee-killings in the cycle; the apparition of the hounds is an attested modern folk-belief at the Hill of Allen. Pin Almhuin.

passages.text: One day Finn was hunting, and Bran went following after a fawn. And they were coming towards Finn, and the fawn called out, and it said: "If I go into the sea below I will never come back again; and if I go up into the air above me, it will not save me from Bran." For Bran would overtake the wild geese, she was that swift. "Go out through my legs," said Finn then. So the fawn did that, and Bran followed her; and as Bran went under him, Finn squeezed his two knees on her, that she died on the moment.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book X, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有一天芬恩正在打獵，布蘭跟在一隻小鹿後面追去。牠們正朝芬恩這邊奔來，那小鹿便開口叫道：「我若鑽進下方的海裡，便再也回不來了；我若升上頭頂的天空，也逃不過布蘭。」因為布蘭連野雁都追得上，她就是這般迅捷。「從我兩腿之間穿過去吧。」芬恩於是說道。那小鹿便照做了，布蘭緊隨其後；當布蘭從他身下經過時，芬恩用雙膝一夾，她便當場死去。

passages.text: And there was great grief on him after that, and he cried tears down the same as he did when Osgar died. And some said it was Finn's mother the fawn was, and that it was to save his mother he killed Bran; but that is not likely, for his mother was beautiful Muirne, daughter of Tadg, son of Nuada of the Tuatha de Danaan, and it was never heard that she was changed into a fawn; it is more likely it was Oisin's mother was in it. But some say Bran and Sceolan are still seen to start at night out of the thicket on the hill of Almhuin.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book X, ch. I; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 此後他悲痛萬分，淚水滾落，一如奧斯卡死時那般。有人說那小鹿是芬恩的母親，他殺死布蘭是為了救自己的母親；但那不大可能，因為他的母親是美麗的繆爾恩，她是達格之子、達南神族努阿達之女，從未聽聞她曾變作小鹿；更可能的是，那裡面是奧伊辛的母親。但也有人說，至今仍能看見布蘭與斯克蘭在夜裡從阿爾溫山上的灌木叢中驚起奔出。

title.en: Niamh of the Golden Head Calls Oisin
title.zh: 金髮妮芙召喚歐辛

region.en: Borders of Loch Lein, Co. Kerry, Ireland
region.zh: 愛爾蘭克里郡利恩湖畔

period: Fenian cycle, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book X, ch. II, eBook #14465

summary.en: After the wearing-away of the Fianna, a queen rides out of the west on a white horse shod with gold and crowned with silver: Niamh of the Golden Head, daughter of the King of the Country of the Young, who has given her love to Oisin for his great name. She puts the bonds of a true hero on him and sings her promise — a hundred swords, a hundred hounds, the crown of the King of the Young, feasts and youth without wasting — and Oisin kisses Finn farewell; at the strand the horse shakes itself and neighs three times and makes for the sea, and Finn says he is without hope ever to see him coming back.
summary.zh: 菲亞納凋零之後，一位王后自西方乘金蹄白馬而來——青春國王之女、金髮妮芙，因歐辛的大名而屬意於他。她以英雄之誓縛他同行，唱出許諾——百劍百犬、青春國王之王冠、盛宴與不老之身——歐辛吻別父親；海灘上白馬三度長嘶，徑直入海。芬恩言：自此再無相見之望。

sensitivity.note: The fairy-bride calling at Loch Lein is the frame of the Oisin cycle (existing record celtic-oisin-tir-na-nog covers the return; this is the call). The white horse that never touches ground is the otherworld-vehicle rule later enforced at the stone trough. Pin at Loch Lein borders.

passages.text: One misty morning, what were left of the Fianna were gathered together to Finn, and they went hunting near the borders of Loch Lein, where the bushes were in blossom and the birds were singing. And it was not long till they saw coming towards them from the west a beautiful young woman, riding on a very fast slender white horse: a queen's crown she had on her head, and a dark cloak of silk down to the ground, having stars of red gold on it; and her eyes were blue and as clear as the dew on the grass, and her lips as sweet as honey that is mixed through red wine; and as to the horse, he had a silver crown on the back of his head, and he was shod with shining gold.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book X, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 一個霧濛濛的早晨，費尼亞人的殘部聚集到芬恩身邊，他們到萊恩湖邊界附近打獵，那裡灌木開花，鳥兒歌唱。沒過多久，他們便看見一位美麗的年輕女子從西邊朝他們走來，騎著一匹非常迅捷的細長白馬：她頭戴一頂王后的冠冕，身披一件垂至地面的深色絲綢斗篷，上面綴著赤金的星辰；她的眼睛是藍色的，清澈如草上的露珠，她的嘴唇甜美如摻入紅酒的蜂蜜；至於那匹馬，牠後腦上戴著一頂銀冠，蹄上釘著閃亮的黃金蹄鐵。

passages.text: "Niamh of the Golden Head is my name, and I am the daughter of the King of the Country of the Young. My husband is not gone from me, for I never went yet to any man. But O King of the Fianna, I have given my love and my affection to your own son, Oisin of the strong hands." When Oisin heard what she was saying, there was not a limb of his body that was not in love with beautiful Niamh.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book X, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「金髮的尼婭芙是我的名字，我是青春之國國王的女兒。我的丈夫並未離我而去，因為我從未嫁與任何男子。但費尼亞人的王啊，我已將我的愛與我的情意獻給了您自己的兒子，強手的奧伊辛。」奧伊辛聽到她這番話，他全身上下沒有一處不愛上了美麗的尼婭芙。

passages.text: "I put on you the bonds of a true hero, you to come away with me now to the Country of the Young: it is the country is most delightful of all that are under the sun; the trees are stooping down with fruit and with leaves and with blossom; honey and wine are plentiful there, and no wasting will come on you with the wasting away of time; you will never see death or lessening... you will get the royal crown of the King of the Young that he never gave to any one under the sun." And Oisin kissed Finn his father and bade him farewell, and went up on the horse with Niamh; and when the horse came to the strand he shook himself and he neighed three times, and then he made for the sea. "It is my grief to see you going from me; and I am without a hope ever to see you coming back to me again."
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Gregory 1904, Book X, ch. II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「我以真正英雄的束縛加於你身，要你如今隨我同往青春之國：那是普天之下一切國度中最令人歡喜之地；樹木因著果實、綠葉與花朵而低垂；那裡蜂蜜與美酒豐盛充足，而你不會因時光流逝而衰敗；你永遠不會見到死亡或衰弱……你將得到青春之王的王冠，那是他從未賜予天下任何人的。」奧辛親吻了他的父親芬恩，向他道別，便與尼婭芙一同上了馬；當馬來到海灘時，牠抖了抖身子，嘶鳴了三聲，然後便向大海奔去。「看著你離我而去，令我悲傷；我再也沒有希望見你回到我身邊了。」

title.en: The Sleeping Fianna and the Dord Fiann
title.zh: 沉睡的菲亞納與菲亞納號角

region.en: Hidden cave, Ireland (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛爾蘭隱秘山洞（象徵定位）

period: Fenian cycle eschatology, medieval Irish tradition; Lady Augusta Gregory retelling (1904)

source.work: Lady Augusta Gregory, Gods and Fighting Men (1904), Book X, ch. III, eBook #14465
