summary.zh: 底比斯陷落後，阿爾克邁翁得知其母厄里菲勒亦受賄賣己，怒火更盛；依阿波羅神諭弒母。弒母之復仇女神使其瘋狂：他流亡至阿卡迪亞的俄伊克勒斯、普索菲斯的費革俄斯（娶其女阿爾斐西波亞，以和諧女神之項鍊為聘禮），然狂疾隨行；德爾菲諭曰：唯「母血未染之地」可避。他在阿克洛俄斯河淤積的新陸定居，娶河之女卡利羅厄，生二子。宙斯應卡利羅厄之請，使二子一夜成人；他們誅費革俄斯父子，依阿克洛俄斯之命將項鍊與嫁衣獻於德爾菲，開拓阿卡納尼亞。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: After the capture of Thebes, when Alcmaeon learned that his mother Eriphyle had been bribed to his undoing also, he was more incensed than ever; and, in accordance with an oracle given to him by Apollo, he killed his mother. Some say that he killed her in conjunction with his brother Amphilochus, others that he did it alone.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 3.7.5 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 底比斯被攻陷之後，阿爾克邁翁得知母親厄里菲勒也因受賄而害了他，愈發憤怒；於是遵照阿波羅給他的神諭，殺死了母親。有人說他與兄弟安菲洛科斯一同殺了她，也有人說是他獨自所為。

passages.text: But Alcmaeon was visited by the Fury of his mother's murder; and going mad, he first repaired to Oicles in Arcadia, and thence to Phegeus at Psophis. And having been purified there, he married Alphesiboea, the daughter of Phegeus, and gave her the famous necklace and robe of Harmonia as bride-gifts.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 3.7.5 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 然而阿爾克邁翁遭到弒母之罪復仇女神的糾纏；他發了瘋，先投奔阿卡迪亞的俄伊克勒斯，又從那裡前往普索菲斯的斐勾斯。他在那裡獲得潔淨之後，娶了斐勾斯的女兒阿爾斐西玻亞，並把著名的項鍊與哈耳摩尼亞的長袍作為聘禮送給她。

passages.text: But as while he dwelt in Arcadia his madness became no better, he consulted the oracle at Delphi, and the Pythian priestess informed him that the Avenger of his mother Eriphyle would follow him to every place except to a spot which was most recent, and made by the action of the sea since he had stained himself with his mother's blood. And he found such a place: the Achelous had silted it up, and there he dwelt, and married Callirrhoe, the daughter of Achelous, according to the tradition of the Acarnanians, and had by her two sons, Acarnan and Amphoterus.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 3.7.5-3.7.6 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但他在阿卡迪亞居住期間，瘋病並未好轉，於是去德爾斐求問神諭，皮提亞女祭司告訴他：他母親厄里菲勒的復仇者會追隨他到任何地方，唯有在他以母親之血玷污自己之後，因海水作用而最新形成的一處地方除外。他找到了這樣一處地方：阿刻羅俄斯河已將其淤積成陸，他便住在那裡，並依阿卡納尼亞人的傳說，娶了阿刻羅俄斯的女兒卡利洛厄，與她生下兩個兒子，阿卡耳南與安福忒洛斯。

passages.text: Being apprized of Alcmaeon's untimely end, and courted by Zeus, Callirrhoe requested that the sons she had by Alcmaeon might be full grown in order to avenge their father's murder. And being suddenly full-grown, the sons went forth to right their father's wrong: they killed Phegeus and his sons, pursued the men who carried the necklace, and dedicated the necklace and robe at Delphi according to the injunction of Achelous; then they journeyed to Epirus, collected settlers, and colonized Acarnania, which took its name from the elder of the two.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 3.7.6-3.7.7 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 卡利洛厄得知阿爾克邁翁橫死，又受宙斯求愛，便請求讓她與阿爾克邁翁所生的兒子們快快長大成人，以便為父親之死報仇。兒子們果然突然長大，便前去為父親伸冤：他們殺死了斐勾斯及其諸子，追擊那些攜帶項鍊的人，並遵照阿刻羅俄斯的吩咐，把項鍊與長袍獻於德爾斐；隨後他們前往伊庇魯斯，招集移民，開拓了阿卡納尼亞，此地之名即取自兩人中年長的那一位。

title.en: The Golden Lamb: Atreus and Thyestes
title.zh: 金羔羊：阿特柔斯與堤厄斯忒斯

region.en: Mycenae (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 邁錫尼（象徵性定位）

period: Composed from the lost epics (c. 7th century BCE; summary in Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), Epitome e.2.10-e.2.14

summary.en: Atreus once vowed to sacrifice to Artemis the finest of his flocks; but when a golden lamb appeared, they say, he neglected the vow, choked the lamb and kept it in a box; and his wife Aerope gave it secretly to Thyestes, by whom she had been debauched. The Mycenaeans, having received an oracle that they should choose a king of the line of Pelops, sent for Atreus and Thyestes; and Zeus sent Hermes to Atreus with the stipulation that he should be king if the sun went backward. Thyestes agreed to the test, and the sun set in the east: so Atreus got the kingdom and banished his brother. Later, learning of the adultery, Atreus lured Thyestes back under a pretence of friendship, slaughtered his three sons — Aglaus, Callileon and Orchomenus — on the altar of Zeus as suppliants, boiled them limb from limb and served them up to their father; and when Thyestes had eaten heartily, Atreus showed him the extremities, and cast him out of the country. Thyestes then asked the oracle how to pay Atreus out, and was told to beget a son by his own daughter; and the son, Aegisthus, when grown, killed Atreus and restored the kingdom to Thyestes — the last link in the curse that ends with Agamemnon.
summary.zh: 阿特柔斯曾誓祭阿爾忒彌斯己群中最美之羊；金羔羊出現時卻毀誓，勒死羔羊藏於箱中；其妻厄洛珀暗將其交予情人堤厄斯忒斯。邁錫尼人得神諭「立珀羅普斯之裔為王」，召二兄弟；宙斯遣赫爾墨斯告阿特柔斯：若日反行則為王。堤厄斯忒斯同意，日竟自東而落；阿特柔斯得王位，放逐其弟。後阿特柔斯察其通姦，假意和解誘其歸，在其三子（阿格勞斯、卡利勒翁、俄爾科墨諾斯）於宙斯祭壇避難時殺之，肢解煮熟端上餐桌；待父食畢示其手足，再放逐之。堤厄斯忒斯問神諭如何復仇，神諭令其與親女交合生子；其子埃癸斯托斯成年後殺阿特柔斯、復其父位——此詛咒終至阿伽門農。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; violence presented as historical material without endorsement.

passages.text: Now the wife of Atreus was Aerope, daughter of Catreus, and she loved Thyestes. And Atreus once vowed to sacrifice to Artemis the finest of his flocks; but when a golden lamb appeared, they say that he neglected to perform his vow, and having choked the lamb, he deposited it in a box and kept it there; and Aerope gave it to Thyestes, by whom she had been debauched.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.2.10-e.2.11 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿特柔斯之妻是卡特柔斯的女兒埃洛珀，她愛上了堤厄斯忒斯。阿特柔斯曾立誓要把羊群中最美的一隻獻祭給阿耳忒彌斯；但據說當一隻金毛羔羊出現時，他卻疏於履行誓言，把羔羊勒死，藏入箱中保存；而埃洛珀把它交給了堤厄斯忒斯，她已被他誘姦。

passages.text: For the Mycenaeans had received an oracle which bade them choose a Pelopid for their king; so they sent for Atreus and Thyestes. And Zeus sent Hermes to Atreus, telling him to stipulate with Thyestes that Atreus should be king if the sun should go backward; and when Thyestes agreed, the sun set in the east. Hence the deity, having plainly attested the usurpation of Thyestes, Atreus got the kingdom and banished Thyestes.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.2.12 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 因為邁錫尼人曾得到神諭，命他們從珀羅普斯的後裔中選立國王；於是他們召來阿特柔斯與堤厄斯忒斯。宙斯派赫耳墨斯到阿特柔斯那裡，叫他與堤厄斯忒斯約定：若太陽倒退而行，王位便歸阿特柔斯；堤厄斯忒斯同意之後，太陽竟從東方落下。因此，神明既已明白昭示堤厄斯忒斯的篡奪，阿特柔斯便取得了王國，並放逐了堤厄斯忒斯。

passages.text: But afterwards, being apprized of the adultery, he sent a herald to Thyestes with a proposal of accommodation; and when he had lured Thyestes by a pretence of friendship, he slaughtered the sons, Aglaus, Callileon and Orchomenus, whom Thyestes had by a Naiad nymph, though they had sat down as suppliants on the altar of Zeus. And having cut them limb from limb and boiled them, he served them up to Thyestes without the extremities; and when Thyestes had eaten heartily of them, he showed him the extremities, and cast him out of the country.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.2.13 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但後來，他得知了這樁姦情，便派了一名傳令官去見堤厄斯忒斯，提出和解的建議；當他以友誼的假象誘騙了堤厄斯忒斯之後，便殺害了堤厄斯忒斯與一位水澤仙女所生的兒子阿格勞斯、卡利勒翁與俄耳科墨諾斯，儘管他們已作為懇求者坐上了宙斯的祭壇。他將他們肢解並煮熟，把他們端給堤厄斯忒斯，卻不給他們的手足；當堤厄斯忒斯盡情吃了他們之後，他便把手足拿給他看，並將他逐出國境。

passages.text: But seeking by all means to pay Atreus out, Thyestes inquired of the oracle on the subject, and received an answer that it could be done if he were to beget a son by intercourse with his own daughter. He did so accordingly, and begat Aegisthus by his daughter. And Aegisthus, when he was grown to manhood and had learned that he was a son of Thyestes, killed Atreus and restored the kingdom to Thyestes.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.2.14 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但堤厄斯忒斯千方百計想要報復阿特柔斯，便就此事求問神諭，得到回答說，只要他與自己的女兒交合生下一子，便可辦到。他於是照辦，與女兒生下了埃癸斯托斯。埃癸斯托斯長大成人、得知自己是堤厄斯忒斯之子後，便殺死了阿特柔斯，將王國歸還給堤厄斯忒斯。

title.en: The Centaurs at the Wedding of Pirithous
title.zh: 半人馬婚宴之亂

region.en: Thessaly (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 色薩利（象徵性定位）

period: Composed from the lost epics (c. 7th century BCE; summary in Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), Epitome e.1.21-e.1.22

summary.en: Theseus allied himself with Pirithous, when he engaged in war against the centaurs; for when Pirithous wooed Hippodamia, he feasted the centaurs because they were her kinsmen. But being unaccustomed to wine, they made themselves drunk by swilling it greedily, and when the bride was brought in, they attempted to violate her. Pirithous, fully armed, with Theseus, joined battle with them, and Theseus killed many of them. And Caeneus, who had once been a woman, asked of Poseidon to become an invulnerable man after the god had intercourse with her; and in the battle with the centaurs he thought scorn of wounds and killed many of them; but the rest of them surrounded him, and by striking him with fir-trees buried him in the earth.
summary.zh: 忒修斯與珀里托俄斯結盟，共戰半人馬；後者娶希波達彌亞時宴請其親族半人馬。眾馬人不慣飲酒，狂飲而醉，新娘入席時竟欲施暴。珀里托俄斯與忒修斯全副武裝與之戰，忒修斯殺其多數。卡紐斯原為女子，與波塞冬交合後求變為不可傷之男身；戰中不懼傷害、連誅馬人，終被其餘以松樹幹活埋入土。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: And Theseus allied himself with Pirithous, when he engaged in war against the centaurs; for when Pirithous wooed Hippodamia, he feasted the centaurs because they were her kinsmen. But being unaccustomed to wine, they made themselves drunk by swilling it greedily; and when the bride was brought in, they attempted to violate her. But Pirithous, fully armed, with Theseus, joined battle with them, and Theseus killed many of them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.1.21 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 忒修斯在與半人馬作戰時，與庇里托俄斯結為盟友；因為庇里托俄斯向希波達彌亞求婚時，宴請了半人馬，因為他們是她的親族。但他們不慣飲酒，貪婪地痛飲而醉；當新娘被帶進來時，他們企圖侵犯她。庇里托俄斯全副武裝，與忒修斯一同與他們交戰，忒修斯殺死了他們中的許多人。

passages.text: And Caeneus was formerly a woman; but after that Poseidon had intercourse with her, she asked to become an invulnerable man. Wherefore in the battle with the centaurs he thought scorn of wounds and killed many of the centaurs; but the rest of them surrounded him, and by striking him with fir-trees buried him in the earth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.1.22 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 刻涅斯從前是個女人；但波塞冬與她交合之後，她請求變成一個刀槍不入的男人。因此在與半人馬的戰鬥中，他蔑視傷痛，殺死了許多半人馬；但其餘的半人馬將他團團圍住，用冷杉樹擊打他，把他埋入土中。

title.en: The Chair of Forgetfulness
title.zh: 遺忘之椅

region.en: Hades (mythic geography)
region.zh: 冥府（神話地理）

period: Composed from the lost epics (c. 7th century BCE; summary in Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), Epitome e.1.23-e.1.24

summary.en: Having made a compact with Pirithous that they would marry daughters of Zeus, Theseus, with the help of Pirithous, carried off Helen from Sparta for himself, when she was twelve years old; and in the endeavour to win Persephone as a bride for Pirithous he went down to Hades. And the Dioscuri, with the Lacedaemonians and Arcadians, captured Athens, carried away Helen, and with her Aethra, daughter of Pittheus, into captivity. But when Theseus arrived with Pirithous in Hades, he was beguiled; for, on the pretence that they were about to partake of good cheer, Hades bade them first be seated on the Chair of Forgetfulness, to which they grew and were held fast by coils of serpents. Pirithous therefore remained bound for ever; but Heracles brought Theseus up and sent him to Athens. Thence he was driven by Menestheus and went to Lycomedes, who threw him down an abyss and killed him.
summary.zh: 忒修斯與珀里托俄斯立約共娶宙斯之女：忒修斯藉珀里托俄斯之力自斯巴達擄走年僅十二歲的海倫；又為珀里托俄斯下冥府欲奪珀耳塞福涅。此時狄俄斯库里率斯巴達與阿卡迪亞人攻陷雅典，救出海倫並擄忒修斯之母埃特拉。二人在冥府受哈得斯所騙，先坐「遺忘之椅」，被蛇纏身不能起；珀里托俄斯永縛，忒修斯則由赫拉克勒斯救出送回雅典。後被墨涅斯透斯逐出，亡於呂科墨德斯所擲深淵。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Having made a compact with Pirithous that they would marry daughters of Zeus, Theseus, with the help of Pirithous, carried off Helen from Sparta for himself, when she was twelve years old; and in the endeavour to win Persephone as a bride for Pirithous he went down to Hades.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.1.23 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 忒修斯與庇里托俄斯約定要娶宙斯的女兒為妻，於是在庇里托俄斯的幫助下，為自己從斯巴達劫走了海倫，當時她年方十二歲；而在為庇里托俄斯娶珀耳塞福涅為妻的圖謀中，他下到了哈得斯。

passages.text: And the Dioscuri, with the Lacedaemonians and Arcadians, captured Athens and carried away Helen, and with her Aethra, daughter of Pittheus, into captivity; but Demophon and Acamas fled. And the Dioscuri also brought back Menestheus from exile, and gave him the sovereignty of Athens.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.1.23 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 狄俄斯庫里兄弟與拉刻代蒙人及阿卡狄亞人一同攻佔了雅典，擄走了海倫，並將庇透斯之女埃特拉與她一同擄為俘虜；但得摩豐與阿卡瑪斯逃走了。狄俄斯庫里兄弟還將墨涅斯透斯從流放中召回，並把雅典的統治權交給他。

passages.text: But when Theseus arrived with Pirithous in Hades, he was beguiled; for, on the pretence that they were about to partake of good cheer, Hades bade them first be seated on the Chair of Forgetfulness, to which they grew and were held fast by coils of serpents. Pirithous, therefore, remained bound for ever; but Heracles brought Theseus up and sent him to Athens. Thence he was driven by Menestheus and went to Lycomedes, who threw him down an abyss and killed him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.1.24 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但當忒修斯與庇里托俄斯抵達哈得斯時，他受了騙；因為哈得斯假稱他們即將享用盛宴，命他們先坐上「遺忘之椅」，他們便與椅子黏合，被蛇的盤繞緊緊纏住。因此，庇里托俄斯永遠被束縛；但赫拉克勒斯把忒修斯帶了上来，送他回雅典。他從那裡被墨涅斯透斯驅逐，前往呂科墨得斯處，呂科墨得斯將他推下深淵殺死。

title.en: The Cretan Bull
title.zh: 克里特公牛

region.en: Crete (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 克里特島（象徵性定位）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), § 2.5.7

summary.en: The seventh labour was to bring the Cretan bull. Acusilaus says this was the bull that ferried Europa across for Zeus; but some say it was the bull that Poseidon sent up from the sea when Minos promised to sacrifice to Poseidon whatever should appear. Minos, seeing the beauty of the animal, sent it to his herds and sacrificed another to the god; at which Poseidon, angry, made the bull savage. Heracles came to Crete; and when Minos, in reply to his request for aid, told him to catch it for himself, Heracles caught the bull and brought it to Eurystheus, and afterwards let it go free. The bull roamed to Sparta and all Arcadia, and, crossing the Isthmus, arrived at Marathon — where it would be known, in later tellings, as the Marathonian bull of Theseus.
summary.zh: 第七項勞役：捉克里特公牛。阿庫西勞斯言此即載歐羅巴渡海之牛；另有說為波塞冬應米諾斯許諾之祭而自海中送上之牛。米諾斯見其俊美，棄入牛群、另祭他牛；神怒而使其狂暴。赫拉克勒斯至克里特，米諾斯令其自捕；英雄擒牛獻於歐里斯透斯，而後釋之。牛逃至斯巴達、阿卡迪亞，越地峽而至馬拉松——後世所謂「馬拉松牛」，忒修斯將馴服之。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: The seventh labour he enjoined on him was to bring the Cretan bull. Acusilaus says that this was the bull that ferried across Europa for Zeus; but some say it was the bull that Poseidon sent up from the sea when Minos promised to sacrifice to Poseidon what should appear out of the sea.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.7 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他命令他完成的第七項勞役，是帶回克里特公牛。阿庫西拉俄斯說，這就是載歐羅巴渡海給宙斯的那頭公牛；但有人說，這是波塞冬從海中送上来的一頭公牛，當時彌諾斯承諾要將從海中出現之物獻祭給波塞冬。

passages.text: And they say that when he saw the beauty of the bull he sent it away to the herds and sacrificed another to Poseidon; at which the god was angry and made the bull savage. To attack this bull Heracles came to Crete, and when, in reply to his request for aid, Minos told him to fight and catch the bull for himself, he caught it and brought it to Eurystheus; and having shown it to him he let it afterwards go free. But the bull roamed to Sparta and all Arcadia, and, traversing the Isthmus, arrived at Marathon in Attica, harrying the inhabitants like a plague.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.7 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們說，當他看見這頭公牛的美麗時，便把它送到牛群中，另獻一頭給波塞冬；波塞冬因此發怒，使這頭公牛變得兇暴。赫拉克勒斯來到克里特攻擊這頭公牛，當彌諾斯回應他求援的請求，叫他自行與公牛搏鬥並捕獲牠時，他捕獲了牠，帶到歐律斯透斯處；給他看過之後，便將牠放走。但這頭公牛漫遊到斯巴達和整個阿卡迪亞，又穿越地峽，抵達阿提卡的馬拉松，如瘟疫般蹂躪居民。

title.en: The Burial of the Dead and the Sons of the Seven
title.zh: 安葬亡者與七雄之子

region.en: Thebes & Athens (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 底比斯與雅典（象徵性定位）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), §§ 3.7.1-3.7.4

summary.en: Creon, having succeeded to the kingdom of Thebes, cast out the Argive dead unburied and set watchmen over them; but Antigone, daughter of Oedipus, stole the body of Polynices and buried it in secret, and, detected by Creon, was interred alive in the grave. Adrastus fled to Athens and laid the suppliant's bough on the altar of Mercy, praying that the dead might be buried; the Athenians marched with Theseus, took Thebes, and gave the dead to their kinsfolk to bury. Evadne, wife of Capaneus, threw herself on his pyre and was burned with him. Ten years later the sons of the fallen — the Epigoni — marched again on Thebes, took it, and pulled down its walls.
summary.zh: 克瑞翁繼底比斯王位，將阿爾戈斯亡者曝屍不得葬、並設哨看守。安提戈涅（俄狄浦斯之女）偷取波呂尼刻斯遺體祕葬，被克瑞翁發現，活埋於墓中。阿德拉斯托斯奔雅典，在「慈悲祭壇」置請願枝求葬亡者；雅典人與忒修斯出征底比斯，取城並歸還遺體。卡帕紐斯之妻厄瓦德涅投身夫之火葬堆殉死。十年後，七雄之子（後裔英雄）再征底比斯，取城毀牆。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Having succeeded to the kingdom of Thebes, Creon cast out the Argive dead unburied, issued a proclamation that none should bury them, and set watchmen. But Antigone, one of the daughters of Oedipus, stole the body of Polynices and secretly buried it; and, having been detected by Creon himself, she was interred alive in the grave.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 3.7.1 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 克瑞翁繼承了忒拜的王位後，將阿爾戈斯陣亡者棄置不葬，頒布公告禁止任何人埋葬他們，並設置了守衛。但俄狄浦斯的女兒之一安提戈涅偷走了波呂尼刻斯的屍體，秘密埋葬了它；她被克瑞翁本人發現後，被活埋於墓中。

passages.text: Adrastus fled to Athens and took refuge at the altar of Mercy, and, laying on it the suppliant's bough, prayed that they would bury the dead. And the Athenians marched with Theseus, captured Thebes, and gave the dead to their kinsfolk to bury. And when the pyre of Capaneus was burning, his wife Evadne, the daughter of Iphis, threw herself on the pyre and was burned with him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 3.7.1 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿德剌斯托斯逃往雅典，在慈悲之神的祭壇尋求庇護，將懇求者的樹枝放在壇上，祈求他們埋葬死者。雅典人與忒修斯一同進軍，攻下忒拜，將死者交給其親屬埋葬。當卡帕紐斯的火葬堆燃燒時，他的妻子、伊菲斯的女兒厄瓦德涅撲向火葬堆，與他一同焚燒。

passages.text: Ten years afterwards the sons of the fallen, called the Epigoni, purposed to march against Thebes to avenge their fathers; and the Argives, having learned of the flight of the Thebans, entered the city, collected the booty, and pulled down the walls. And they sent a portion of the booty to Apollo at Delphi, and with it Manto, daughter of Tiresias; for they had vowed that, if they took Thebes, they would dedicate to him the fairest of the spoils.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 3.7.2-3.7.4 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 十年之後，陣亡者的兒子們，被稱為「後繼者」，打算進軍忒拜為父親們報仇；阿爾戈斯人得知忒拜人逃亡後，進入城中，收集戰利品，並拆毀城牆。他們將一部分戰利品送往德爾斐獻給阿波羅，連同提瑞西阿斯的女兒曼托；因為他們曾立誓，若攻下忒拜，便將戰利品中最美之物獻給他。

title.en: The Tunic of Nessus and the Pyre on Oeta
title.zh: 涅索斯之毒衣與厄塔火葬

region.en: River Evenus to Mount Oeta (mythic geography)
region.zh: 厄維努斯河至厄塔山（神話地理）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), §§ 2.7.6-2.7.8

summary.en: Taking Deianira with him, Heracles came to the river Evenus, where the centaur Nessus ferried passengers for hire, alleging that he had received the ferry from the gods for his righteousness. Heracles crossed himself, but entrusted Deianira to Nessus, who in ferrying her attempted to violate her; and Heracles shot him through the heart. Dying, Nessus told Deianira that his seed mingled with the blood from the barb would make a love-charm for Heracles, and she kept the mixture. Years later, jealous of Iole, she smeared a tunic with it and sent it to the altar of Cenaean Zeus; the poison of the hydra burned into the hero's flesh, and he tore the garment off with the skin. Deianira hanged herself on the news; Heracles, charging his son Hyllus to marry Iole, made a pyre on Mount Oeta, and Poeas, passing by with his flocks, set it alight. A cloud passed under him and, with a peal of thunder, wafted him up to heaven; reconciled with Hera, he married her daughter Hebe.
summary.zh: 赫拉克勒斯攜得伊阿涅拉渡厄維努斯河，船夫乃半人馬涅索斯。涅索斯欲對伊阿涅拉無禮，赫拉克勒斯一箭穿心；臨終涅索斯言其精液混箭毒可為愛情魔藥，伊阿涅拉收藏之。多年後，因嫉妒伊奧勒，伊阿涅拉以之浸衣送至赫拉克勒斯祭壇；許德拉之毒燃及肌骨，英雄撕衣連皮同剝。伊阿涅拉聞訊自縊；赫拉克勒斯命子許勒斯娶伊奧勒，於厄塔山自焚，帕阿斯牧羊時點燃柴堆；雲至、雷鳴，升天成神；與赫拉和解，娶其女赫柏。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Taking Deianira with him, he came to the river Evenus, at which the centaur Nessus sat and ferried passengers across for hire, alleging that he had received the ferry from the gods for his righteousness. So Heracles crossed the river by himself, but, on being asked to pay the fare, he entrusted Deianira to Nessus to carry over. But he, in ferrying her across, attempted to violate her.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.7.6 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他帶著得伊阿尼拉一同前行，來到厄維諾斯河，半人馬涅索斯坐在那裏，以收費載人渡河為業，聲稱他因正直而從諸神那裏得到這渡河之職。於是赫拉克勒斯獨自渡過了河，但當被要求付渡資時，他便把得伊阿尼拉託付給涅索斯載她過河。然而涅索斯在載她渡河時，竟企圖侵犯她。

passages.text: She cried out; Heracles heard her and shot Nessus to the heart when he emerged from the river. And Nessus, at the point of death, called Deianira to him and said that, if she would have a love-charm to operate on Heracles, she should mix the seed he had dropped on the ground with the blood that flowed from the wound inflicted by the barb. She did so and kept it by her.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.7.6 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她大聲呼喊；赫拉克勒斯聽見了，當涅索斯從河中出來時，便一箭射中他的心臟。涅索斯在臨死之際，把得伊阿尼拉喚到跟前，說若她想要一種能對赫拉克勒斯起作用的愛情符咒，就該把他落在地上的精液，與從那箭鏃所造成的傷口流出的血混合起來。她照做了，並把它留在身邊。

passages.text: Heracles mustered an army and attacked Oechalia, wishing to punish Eurytus, and took the city, leading Iole captive. At Cenaeum, a headland of Euboea, he built an altar of Cenaean Zeus, and, intending to offer sacrifice, sent the herald Lichas to Trachis to fetch fine raiment. From him Deianira learned about Iole, and, fearing that Heracles might love that damsel more than herself, she supposed that the spilt blood of Nessus was in truth a love-charm, and with it she smeared the tunic.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.7.7 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 赫拉克勒斯召集了一支軍隊，攻打俄卡利亞，想要懲罰歐律托斯，攻下了那座城，並擄走伊俄勒為俘虜。在歐玻亞的海角刻奈翁，他築了一座刻奈翁宙斯的祭壇，本打算獻祭，便派遣傳令官利卡斯前往特拉基斯取來華美的衣袍。得伊阿尼拉從他口中得知了伊俄勒的事，因害怕赫拉克勒斯會愛那少女勝過自己，便以為涅索斯灑下的血當真是一種愛情符咒，就用它塗抹了那件長袍。

passages.text: So Heracles put it on and proceeded to offer sacrifice. But no sooner was the tunic warmed than the poison of the hydra began to corrode his skin; and on that he lifted Lichas by the feet, hurled him down from the headland, and tore off the tunic, which clung to his body, so that his flesh was torn away with it. In such a sad plight he was carried on shipboard to Trachis; and Deianira, on learning what had happened, hanged herself.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.7.7 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是赫拉克勒斯穿上它，前去獻祭。可是那長袍一經受熱，九頭蛇的毒便開始腐蝕他的皮膚；他隨即抓住利卡斯的雙腳，把他從海角上拋下去，又撕扯那緊貼在他身上的長袍，以致連他的皮肉也隨之被撕去。他就在這般悲慘的境況中被載上船，送往特拉基斯；而得伊阿尼拉得知所發生的事後，便自縊而死。

passages.text: But Heracles, after charging Hyllus, his elder son by Deianira, to marry Iole when he came of age, proceeded to Mount Oeta, in the Trachinian territory, and there constructed a pyre, mounted it, and gave orders to kindle it. When no one would do so, Poeas, passing by to look for his flocks, set a light to it, and on him Heracles bestowed his bow. While the pyre was burning, it is said that a cloud passed under Heracles and, with a peal of thunder, wafted him up to heaven. Thereafter he obtained immortality, and, being reconciled to Hera, he married her daughter Hebe.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.7.8 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 赫拉克勒斯囑咐他與得伊阿尼拉所生的長子許洛斯，待他成年後娶伊俄勒為妻，隨後便前往特拉基斯境內的俄塔山，在那裏築起一座火葬堆，登上其上，下令點燃。當無人肯點時，波阿斯正經過那裏尋找他的羊群，便點燃了火葬堆，赫拉克勒斯於是把自己的弓贈給了他。據說火葬堆燃燒之際，一朵雲從赫拉克勒斯身下經過，伴著一聲雷鳴，把他送上了天。此後他獲得了不死之身，並與赫拉和解，娶了她的女兒赫柏。

title.en: The Madness of Heracles: Megara's Children
title.zh: 赫拉克勒斯之瘋狂：墨伽拉諸子

region.en: Thebes (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 底比斯（象徵性定位）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), § 2.4.12

summary.en: After the battle with the Minyans, Heracles was driven mad through the jealousy of Hera, and flung his own children — those he had by Megara — and two children of Iphicles into the fire. Condemning himself to exile, he was purified by Thespius; and at Delphi the Pythian priestess first called him Heracles — until then he was Alcides — and told him to dwell in Tiryns, serving Eurystheus for twelve years and performing the ten labours he would impose, after which, she said, he would become immortal.
summary.zh: 密尼亞人之戰後，赫拉克勒斯因赫拉嫉妒而發瘋，將墨伽拉所生子女與伊菲克勒斯之二子擲入火中。他自判流放，由忒斯庇俄斯淨禮；在德爾菲，皮提亞女祭司初次稱其「赫拉克勒斯」（此前名阿爾喀德斯），命其居提林斯、事歐里斯透斯十二年、行十項勞役，功成則得永生。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; violence presented as historical material without endorsement.

passages.text: Now it came to pass that, after the battle with the Minyans, Heracles was driven mad through the jealousy of Hera, and flung his own children, whom he had by Megara, and two children of Iphicles into the fire. Wherefore he condemned himself to exile, and was purified by Thespius; and, repairing to Delphi, he inquired of the god where he should dwell.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.4.12 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 且說在與米尼安人交戰之後，赫拉克勒斯因赫拉的嫉妒而發了瘋，把他與墨伽拉所生的親生兒女，以及伊菲克勒斯的兩個孩子，都扔進了火裏。因此他自判流放，並由忒斯庇俄斯為他淨罪；他前往德爾斐，向神請示自己該在何處居住。

passages.text: The Pythian priestess then first called him Heracles, for hitherto he was called Alcides. And she told him to dwell in Tiryns, serving Eurystheus for twelve years, and to perform the ten labours imposed on him; and so, she said, when the tasks were accomplished, he would be immortal.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.4.12 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 皮提亞的女祭司於是首先稱他為赫拉克勒斯，因為在此之前他名叫阿爾喀得斯。她吩咐他居住在提林斯，為歐律斯透斯服役十二年，並完成加諸於他的十項勞役；她說，如此一來，當這些任務完成之後，他便會成為不朽。

title.en: Heracles Among the Cercopes: Slavery to Omphale
title.zh: 赫拉克勒斯為呂底亞女王所役

region.en: Lydia (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 呂底亞（象徵性定位）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), § 2.6.3

summary.en: After the oracle at Delphi, Hermes sold Heracles, and Omphale, daughter of Iardanes, queen of Lydia, bought him: she had received the government of her husband Tmolus at his death. In her service Heracles seized and bound the Cercopes — the two knavish brothers of Ephesus — at Ephesus; he killed Syleus of Aulis, who forced passers-by to dig in his vineyards, and burned the vines to the root; and on the island of Doliche he saw the body of Icarus washed ashore, buried it, and renamed the island Icaria. It was during this servitude, says the tradition, that the voyage of the Argonauts, the hunt of the Calydonian boar and Theseus' clearing of the Isthmus road took place.
summary.zh: 德爾菲神諭之後，赫爾墨斯將赫拉克勒斯賣予呂底亞女王翁法勒（伊阿爾達涅斯之女，承繼亡夫特摩洛斯之王位）。為奴期間，他在以弗所縛住狡詐兄弟科爾科佩斯；殺害強迫路人掘地的奧利斯人敘琉斯並焚其葡萄園；在多利刻島見伊卡羅斯屍身漂流至岸，將其安葬，島遂名伊卡里亞。據傳阿爾戈遠航、卡呂冬狩獵與忒修斯清道皆在此奴役期間。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: After the delivery of the oracle, Hermes sold Heracles, and he was bought by Omphale, daughter of Iardanes, queen of Lydia, to whom at her husband Tmolus' death the government had been bequeathed. Eurytus did not accept the compensation when it was presented to him; but Heracles served Omphale as a slave. And in the course of his servitude he seized and bound the Cercopes at Ephesus.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.6.3 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 神諭下達之後，赫耳墨斯將赫拉克勒斯賣出，他被伊阿耳達涅斯之女、呂底亞女王翁法勒買下；其夫特摩羅斯死後，政權便遺贈給了翁法勒。歐律托斯在補償金呈上時並未接受；但赫拉克勒斯仍以奴隸身分服侍翁法勒。在他服役期間，他在以弗所捉住並捆綁了刻耳科珀斯。

passages.text: And as for Syleus in Aulis, who compelled passing strangers to dig, Heracles killed him with his daughter Xenodoce, after burning the vines with the roots. And having put in to the island of Doliche, he saw the body of Icarus washed ashore and buried it, and called the island Icaria instead of Doliche.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.6.3 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 至於奧利斯的那個西勒烏斯，他強迫過路的陌生人為他掘土，赫拉克勒斯便將他連同其女色諾多刻一同殺死，並將葡萄藤連根燒毀。他又駛入多利刻島，看見伊卡洛斯的屍體被沖上岸，便將他埋葬，並將該島由多利刻改稱為伊卡里亞。

passages.text: And in return Daedalus made a portrait-statue of Heracles at Pisa, which Heracles, mistaking it at night for a living man, struck with a stone. And it is said that during the time of his servitude with Omphale the voyage to Colchis, the hunt of the Calydonian boar, and Theseus' clearing of the Isthmus road all took place.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.6.3 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 作為回報，代達羅斯在庇薩為赫拉克勒斯製作了一尊肖像雕像，赫拉克勒斯在夜間誤以為它是活人，便用石頭擊打它。據說，在他服侍翁法勒的期間，前往科爾基斯的航行、獵捕卡呂冬野豬，以及忒修斯清剿地峽道路之事，全都發生了。

title.en: The Cerynitian Hind and the Erymanthian Boar
title.zh: 刻律涅特赤鹿與厄律曼托斯野豬

region.en: Arcadia (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿卡迪亞（象徵性定位）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), §§ 2.5.3-2.5.4

summary.en: Third, Eurystheus ordered him to bring the Cerynitian hind alive: golden-horned, sacred to Artemis, unwilling to be hurt. Heracles hunted it a whole year, shot it on the bank of the Ladon just as it was about to cross, and carried it away on his shoulders; and Artemis and Apollo met him and would have wrested the hind from him, till, pleading necessity and blaming Eurystheus, he appeased the goddess's anger. Fourth, the Erymanthian boar, alive: Heracles, on the way, was entertained by the centaur Pholus, whose wine-jar, opened, brought the other centaurs up the mountain with rocks and firs; in the melée Heracles' arrow, passing through the arm of Elatus, stuck in the knee of Chiron, who could not die — for he was immortal — until Prometheus offered himself to Zeus to be immortal in his stead. Heracles then chased the boar into deep snow, trapped it, and carried it alive to Mycenae.
summary.zh: 第三項勞役：活捉刻律涅特金角赤鹿——乃阿爾忒彌斯之聖獸，不可傷害。赫拉克勒斯追獵整年，於拉冬河畔趁其渡水一箭射之，扛於肩上而歸；途中遇阿爾忒彌斯與阿波羅欲奪鹿，英雄以「奉歐里斯透斯之命」之辭平息女神之怒。第四項勞役：活捉厄律曼托斯野豬——途中宿於半人馬福羅斯家，啟酒引來眾半人馬，混戰中一箭穿厄拉托斯臂而中喀戎膝；喀戎不死（因其為神）直至普羅米修斯自請代其不死。英雄追豬至深雪中，活捉而返。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: As a third labour he ordered him to bring the Cerynitian hind alive to Mycenae. Now the hind was at Oenoe; it had golden horns and was sacred to Artemis; so wishing neither to kill nor wound it, Heracles hunted it a whole year.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.3 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 作為第三項勞役，他命令他將刻律涅亞的牝鹿活著帶到邁錫尼。那牝鹿當時在俄諾厄；牠有金色的角，是阿耳忒彌斯的聖獸；因此赫拉克勒斯既不願殺牠，也不願傷牠，便追獵了整整一年。

passages.text: But when, weary with the chase, the beast took refuge on the mountain called Artemisium, and thence passed to the river Ladon, Heracles shot it just as it was about to cross the stream, and catching it, put it on his shoulders and hastened through Arcadia. But Artemis with Apollo met him and would have wrested the hind from him, rebuking him for attempting to kill her sacred animal; howbeit, by pleading necessity and laying the blame on Eurystheus, he appeased the anger of the goddess and carried the beast alive to Mycenae.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.3 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但當那野獸因追逐而疲憊，逃到一座名叫阿耳忒彌西翁的山上避難，又從那裡轉往拉冬河時，赫拉克勒斯趁牠正要渡河之際射中了牠，捉住牠，扛在肩上，匆匆穿過阿耳卡狄亞。然而阿耳忒彌斯與阿波羅遇見了他，想要從他手中奪走牝鹿，責備他竟企圖殺害她的聖獸；不過，他藉口出於不得已，並將過錯歸咎於歐律斯透斯，平息了女神的怒氣，將那野獸活著帶到了邁錫尼。

passages.text: As a fourth labour he ordered him to bring the Erymanthian boar alive; now that animal ravaged Psophis, sallying from a mountain which they call Erymanthus. So passing through Pholoe he was entertained by the centaur Pholus, a son of Silenus by a Melian nymph. He set roast meat before Heracles, while he himself ate his meat raw. When Heracles called for wine, he said he feared to open the jar which belonged to the centaurs in common; but Heracles, bidding him be of good courage, opened it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.4 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 作為第四項勞役，他命他去活捉厄律曼托斯野豬；這隻野獸當時肆虐普索菲斯，從一座他們稱為厄律曼托斯的山中竄出。於是他途經福洛厄，受到半人馬福洛斯——西勒諾斯與一位墨利亞寧芙所生之子——的款待。福洛斯在赫拉克勒斯面前擺上烤肉，自己則吃生肉。當赫拉克勒斯要酒時，福洛斯說他不敢打開那屬於半人馬共有的酒罈；但赫拉克勒斯叫他放心大膽，便打開了它。

passages.text: Not long afterwards, scenting the smell, the centaurs arrived at the cave of Pholus armed with rocks and firs; the first who dared to enter, Anchius and Agrius, were repelled with a shower of brands, and the rest Heracles shot and pursued as far as Malea. Thence they took refuge with Chiron, who, driven by the Lapiths from Mount Pelion, took up his abode at Malea. As the centaurs cowered about Chiron, Heracles shot an arrow at them which, passing through the arm of Elatus, stuck in the knee of Chiron. Distressed at this, Heracles ran up to him, drew out the shaft, and applied a medicine which Chiron gave him; but the hurt proving incurable, Chiron retired to the cave and wished to die, but he could not, for he was immortal. However, Prometheus offered himself to Zeus to be immortal in his stead, and so Chiron died. And when Heracles had chased the boar with shouts from a certain thicket, he drove the exhausted animal into deep snow, trapped it, and brought it to Mycenae.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.4 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 不久之後，半人馬聞到氣味，帶著石塊和冷杉木來到福洛斯的洞穴；最先膽敢進入的安喀俄斯與阿格里俄斯被一陣火把擊退，其餘的則被赫拉克勒斯射擊，並被追趕至馬勒亞。他們從那裡逃到喀戎處避難，喀戎被拉庇泰人逐出珀利翁山，便在馬勒亞定居。當半人馬蜷縮在喀戎周圍時，赫拉克勒斯向他們射出一箭，那箭穿過厄拉托斯的手臂，扎進喀戎的膝蓋。赫拉克勒斯為此十分苦惱，跑上前去，拔出箭桿，敷上喀戎給他的藥；但傷勢無法醫治，喀戎退入洞穴，想要死去，卻不能如願，因為他是不死的。然而，普羅米修斯向宙斯自願代替他成為不死者，於是喀戎死去。赫拉克勒斯從某處灌木叢中吶喊著追趕野豬，將這隻筋疲力盡的野獸趕入深雪之中，設陷捕獲，帶到了邁錫尼。

title.en: Phaedra and Hippolytus
title.zh: 菲德拉與希波呂托斯

region.en: Athens & Troezen (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 雅典與特洛真（象徵性定位）

period: Composed from the lost epics (c. 7th century BCE; summary in Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), Epitome e.1.17-e.1.19

summary.en: Theseus afterwards received from Deucalion in marriage Phaedra, daughter of Minos. At the wedding the Amazon who had before been married to him appeared in arms with her Amazons and threatened to kill the assembled guests; the doors were hastily closed and she was killed. Phaedra bore Theseus two children, Acamas and Demophon; then she fell in love with the son he had by the Amazon — Hippolytus — and besought him to lie with her. He fled her embraces, because he hated all women. Phaedra, fearing that he might accuse her to his father, cleft open the doors of her bedchamber, rent her garments, and falsely charged Hippolytus with an assault. Theseus believed her and prayed to Poseidon that Hippolytus might perish: when the boy was riding his chariot beside the sea, Poseidon sent up a bull from the surf; the horses were frightened, the chariot dashed in pieces, and Hippolytus, entangled in the reins, was dragged to death. When her passion was made public, Phaedra hanged herself.
summary.zh: 忒修斯後娶米諾斯之女菲德拉。婚宴上，先前與忒修斯成婚的亞馬遜女王率眾持械闖入欲殺賓客，門扉緊閉而亡。菲德拉生二子（阿卡馬斯與得摩豐）後，愛上忒修斯與亞馬遜女王所生之子希波呂托斯，求其同寢；他因憎惡所有女子而逃。菲德拉懼其告發，破寢室門、撕裂衣衫，誣告希波呂托斯非禮。忒修斯信之，向波塞冬祈其子死；少年驅車海濱，波塞冬自浪中送出公牛，馬驚車碎，希波呂托斯纏於韁繩拖死。菲德拉事洩後自縊。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Theseus afterwards received from Deucalion in marriage Phaedra, daughter of Minos; and when her marriage was being celebrated, the Amazon that had before been married to him appeared in arms with her Amazons, and threatened to kill the assembled guests. But they hastily closed the doors and killed her. However, some say that she was slain in battle by Theseus.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.1.17 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 後來，忒修斯從丟卡利翁那裡娶了彌諾斯的女兒淮德拉為妻；當她的婚禮正在慶祝時，先前曾與他成婚的亞馬遜女子帶著她的亞馬遜人全副武裝出現，威脅要殺死聚集的賓客。但他們急忙關上門，將她殺死。然而，有人說她是在戰鬥中被忒修斯殺死的。

passages.text: And Phaedra, after she had borne two children, Acamas and Demophon, to Theseus, fell in love with the son he had by the Amazon, to wit, Hippolytus, and besought him to lie with her. Howbeit, he fled from her embraces, because he hated all women.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.1.18 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 淮德拉為忒修斯生下兩個孩子阿卡瑪斯和得摩豐之後，愛上了他與亞馬遜女子所生的兒子，即希波呂托斯，並懇求他與她同寢。然而，他因憎恨所有女人而逃離她的擁抱。

passages.text: But Phaedra, fearing that he might accuse her to his father, cleft open the doors of her bedchamber, rent her garments, and falsely charged Hippolytus with an assault. Theseus believed her and prayed to Poseidon that Hippolytus might perish. So, when Hippolytus was riding in his chariot and driving beside the sea, Poseidon sent up a bull from the surf; and the horses were frightened, the chariot dashed in pieces, and Hippolytus, entangled in the reins, was dragged to death. And when her passion was made public, Phaedra hanged herself.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.1.18 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.1.19 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但淮德拉害怕他會向她父親控告她，便劈開臥室的門，撕破自己的衣裳，誣告希波呂托斯施暴。忒修斯相信了她，向波塞冬祈禱讓希波呂托斯滅亡。於是，當希波呂托斯乘著戰車沿海邊行進時，波塞冬從浪中送出一頭公牛；馬匹受驚，戰車撞得粉碎，希波呂托斯被韁繩纏住，被拖拽而死。當她的情慾公之於眾後，淮德拉自縊身亡。

title.en: The Red Kine of Geryon
title.zh: 革律翁的紅牛群

region.en: Erythia, far west (mythic geography)
region.zh: 遠西厄里提亞島（神話地理）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), § 2.5.10

summary.en: As a tenth labour Heracles was ordered to fetch the kine of Geryon from Erythia, an island near the ocean, now called Gadira. Geryon, son of Chrysaor by Callirrhoe, daughter of Ocean, had the body of three men grown together and joined in one at the waist, parted in three from the flanks and thighs. His red kine were tended by Eurytion, with the two-headed hound Orthus, begotten by Typhon on Echidna, as watchdog. Journeying through Europe Heracles destroyed many wild beasts, set foot in Libya, and at Tartessus erected two pillars over against each other at the boundaries of Europe and Libya — the Pillars of Heracles. Heated by the Sun on his journey, he bent his bow at the god, who, in admiration of his hardihood, gave him a golden goblet in which he crossed the ocean. The hound rushed at him and was clubbed; Eurytion came to its help and was killed; Menoetes, herdsman of the kine of Hades, reported it to Geryon, who met Heracles beside the river Anthemus and was shot dead. Heracles put the kine in the goblet, gave it back to the Sun, and drove the herd home through Liguria and Tyrrhenia; at Rome a bull broke away and fled, and Heracles chased it to Sicily, where Eryx, son of Poseidon, mingled it with his own herds and offered to surrender it if Heracles beat him in a wrestling bout — and Heracles beat him thrice and killed him in the wrestling.
summary.zh: 第十項勞役：取遠西厄里提亞島（今加迪拉）革律翁之紅牛。革律翁乃克律薩俄耳與大洋之女卡利羅厄之子，三身一腰、腰以下三分。其牛由歐律提翁牧養、雙頭犬俄耳托斯看守（堤豐與厄喀德那所生）。英雄歐洲、利比亞一路誅獸，至塔爾特索斯於歐非交界豎雙柱（即「赫拉克勒斯之柱」）；旅途受烈日炙烤，向日神張弓，日神嘆其勇而賜金盃渡洋。英雄擊犬、殺牧人；哈得斯之牛倌墨諾忒斯報信，革律翁於安忒穆斯河畔迎戰，被射死。英雄以金盃渡牛、還盃於日神，經利古里亞、第勒尼亞而歸；一牛逃至西西里，王厄律克斯攙入己群、欲與英雄角力而失敗被殺，牛群遂驅回。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: As a tenth labour he was ordered to fetch the kine of Geryon from Erythia. Now Erythia was an island near the ocean; it is now called Gadira. This island was inhabited by Geryon, son of Chrysaor by Callirrhoe, daughter of Ocean. He had the body of three men grown together and joined in one at the waist, but parted in three from the flanks and thighs.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.10 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 作為第十項勞役，他奉命從厄律忒亞取回革律翁的牛群。厄律忒亞是靠近大洋的一座島嶼；它現在稱為伽得拉。這座島上住著革律翁，他是克律薩俄耳與俄刻阿諾斯之女卡利洛厄所生之子。他有三個人的身體，在腰部合而為一，但從脅腹和大腿處分為三人。

passages.text: He owned red kine, of which Eurytion was the herdsman and Orthus, the two-headed hound, begotten by Typhon on Echidna, was the watchdog. So journeying through Europe to fetch the kine of Geryon he destroyed many wild beasts and set foot in Libya; and, proceeding to Tartessus, he erected as tokens of his journey two pillars over against each other at the boundaries of Europe and Libya.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.10 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他擁有一群紅色的母牛，由歐律提翁擔任牧人，而堤豐與厄喀德那所生的雙頭獵犬俄耳托斯則負責看守。因此，赫拉克勒斯為取得革律翁的牛群而穿越歐羅巴，沿途消滅了許多野獸，並踏上利比亞的土地；他繼續前行至塔爾忒索斯，在歐羅巴與利比亞的邊界上，相對而立地豎起兩根石柱，作為他此行的標記。

passages.text: But being heated by the Sun on his journey, he bent his bow at the god, who, in admiration of his hardihood, gave him a golden goblet in which he crossed the ocean. And having reached Erythia he lodged on Mount Abas. However the dog, perceiving him, rushed at him; but he smote it with his club, and when the herdsman Eurytion came to the help of the dog, Heracles killed him also.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.10 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 然而他在旅途中被太陽神曬得酷熱難當，便張弓搭箭射向那位神祇；太陽神欽佩他的剛勇，便贈他一隻金杯，他乘坐此杯渡過了大洋。抵達厄律提亞之後，他投宿於阿巴斯山。那獵犬一見到他便撲了上來；他卻以棍棒將其擊斃，而當牧人歐律提翁前來救助獵犬時，赫拉克勒斯也把他一併殺死。

passages.text: But Menoetes, who was there pasturing the kine of Hades, reported to Geryon what had occurred; and he, coming up with Heracles beside the river Anthemus as he was driving away the kine, joined battle with him and was shot dead. And Heracles, embarking the kine in the goblet and sailing across to Tartessus, gave back the goblet to the Sun.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.10 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 然而當時正在那裡放牧哈得斯牛群的墨諾忒斯，將所發生之事稟報了革律翁；革律翁在安忒穆斯河畔追上正趕著牛群離去的赫拉克勒斯，與之交戰，卻被射死。赫拉克勒斯將牛群裝上金杯，渡海航至塔爾忒索斯，然後把金杯歸還給太陽神。

passages.text: At Rhegium a bull broke away from the herd and plunged into the sea, swam across to Sicily, and came to the plain of Eryx, who reigned over the Elymi and mingled the bull with his own herds. Heracles entrusted the kine to Hephaestus and hurried away in search of the bull; and when the king refused to surrender it unless Heracles should beat him in a wrestling bout, Heracles beat him thrice, killed him in the wrestling, and, taking the bull, drove it with the rest of the herd to the Ionian Sea. But Hera afflicted the cows with a gadfly, and they dispersed among the skirts of the mountains of Thrace; Heracles caught some, drove them to the Hellespont, and the remainder were thenceforth wild. He blamed the river Strymon, and made it unnavigable by filling it with rocks; and he conveyed the kine and gave them to Eurystheus, who sacrificed them to Hera.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.10-2.5.11 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在瑞癸翁，一頭公牛脫離牛群，躍入海中，游過海峽抵達西西里，來到厄律克斯的平原；厄律克斯統治著厄律米人，將這頭公牛混入自己的牛群之中。赫拉克勒斯把牛群託付給赫淮斯托斯，急忙前去尋找那頭公牛；國王拒絕交出公牛，除非赫拉克勒斯能在角力中勝過他，於是赫拉克勒斯三次將他摔倒，在角力中將他殺死，然後帶走公牛，與其餘牛群一同趕往伊奧尼亞海。但赫拉使牛群遭受牛虻的侵擾，牠們便四散於色雷斯山麓之間；赫拉克勒斯捉回了一些，趕往赫勒斯滂，其餘的從此便成了野牛。他歸咎於斯特律蒙河，用石塊將河道填塞，使其無法通航；他運送牛群，交給歐律斯透斯，歐律斯透斯便將牠們獻祭給赫拉。

title.en: The Women of Lemnos
title.zh: 利姆諾斯的女人们

region.en: Lemnos, Aegean (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛琴海利姆諾斯島（象徵性定位）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), § 1.9.17

summary.en: These with Jason as admiral put to sea and touched at Lemnos, which happened to be bereft of men and ruled over by a queen, Hypsipyle, daughter of Thoas. The Lemnian women did not honour Aphrodite, and she visited them with a noisome smell; therefore their husbands took captive women from the neighbouring country of Thrace and bedded with them. Dishonoured, the Lemnian women murdered their fathers and husbands — Hypsipyle alone saved her father Thoas by hiding him. The Argonauts had intercourse with the women, and Hypsipyle bore Jason two sons, Euneus and Nebrophonus.
summary.zh: 阿爾戈英雄以伊阿宋為首航行至利姆諾斯島，島上男子皆亡，由托阿斯之女許普西皮勒為后。利姆諾斯婦女不敬阿芙洛狄忒，被神賜以惡臭之體；其夫遂擄色雷斯女子為妾。受辱的妻子們遂殺父戮夫——唯許普西皮勒藏匿其父托阿斯得以保全。阿爾戈英雄與島上女子結合；許普西皮勒為伊阿宋生二子。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: These with Jason as admiral put to sea and touched at Lemnos. At that time it chanced that Lemnos was bereft of men and ruled over by a queen, Hypsipyle, daughter of Thoas. The reason of this was as follows. The Lemnian women did not honour Aphrodite, and she visited them with a noisome smell; therefore their spouses took captive women from the neighbouring country of Thrace and bedded with them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 1.9.17 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這些人推舉伊阿宋為統帥，揚帆出海，抵達了利姆諾斯。當時恰逢利姆諾斯島上男子盡失，由女王許普西皮勒——托阿斯的女儿——統治。箇中緣由如下。利姆諾斯的婦女不敬奉阿佛洛狄忒，女神便使她們身上散發惡臭；因此她們的丈夫便從鄰近的色雷斯擄來婦女，與之同寢。

passages.text: Thus dishonoured, the Lemnian women murdered their fathers and husbands; but Hypsipyle alone saved her father Thoas by hiding him. So, having put in to Lemnos, at that time ruled by women, the Argonauts had intercourse with the women; and Hypsipyle bedded with Jason and bore sons, Euneus and Nebrophonus.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 1.9.17 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 利姆諾斯的婦女既受此羞辱，便殺害了自己的父親與丈夫；唯有許普西皮勒將父親托阿斯藏匿起來，救了他一命。於是，阿爾戈英雄們駛入當時由婦女統治的利姆諾斯，與那些婦女交合；許普西皮勒與伊阿宋同寢，生下兒子歐紐斯與涅布羅福諾斯。

title.en: The Nemean Lion and the Hydra of Lerna
title.zh: 尼米亞獅與勒拿九頭蛇

region.en: Nemea & Lerna (mythic geography)
region.zh: 尼米亞與勒拿（神話地理）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), §§ 2.5.1-2.5.2

summary.en: First Eurystheus ordered him to bring the skin of the Nemean lion, an invulnerable beast begotten by Typhon. Heracles lodged with a day-labourer, Molorchus, and told him to wait thirty days: if the hero returned safe, Molorchus was to sacrifice to Saviour Zeus; if he were dead, to sacrifice to Heracles as to a hero. At Nemea he shot the lion, found the beast invulnerable, heaved up his club, chased it into a cave with two mouths, built up one entrance, came in through the other, and strangled it. Second, the Hydra of Lerna: nine heads, eight mortal and the middle one immortal; as each head was cut off two grew in its place, and a crab sent by Hera bit the hero's foot. He burned out the necks and buried the immortal head under a heavy rock on the road from Lerna to Elaeus, dipping his arrows in the hydra's gall so that any wound they gave became incurable.
summary.zh: 首項勞役取尼米亞獅之皮：獅乃提豐所生、刀槍不入。赫拉克勒斯宿於雇工墨羅爾科斯家，囑其候三十日：若歸則祭「救主宙斯」，若死則祭己為英雄。在尼米亞，箭無效，遂以棒擊之，追入雙口洞穴，封其一端自他口入而扼斃之。第二項勞役為勒拿九頭蛇：九首之中中間者不死，每斬一首即生二首，赫拉又遣巨蟹噬其足。英雄以火烙頸、以巨石鎮其不死之首；並以蛇之膽汁塗箭，使傷者不得痊。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: First, Eurystheus ordered him to bring the skin of the Nemean lion; now that was an invulnerable beast begotten by Typhon. On his way to attack the lion he came to Cleonae and lodged at the house of a day-labourer, Molorchus; and when his host would have offered a victim in sacrifice, Heracles told him to wait for thirty days, and then, if he had returned safe from the hunt, to sacrifice to Saviour Zeus; but if he were dead, to sacrifice to him as to a hero.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.1 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 首先，歐律斯透斯命令他去取涅墨亞獅子的皮；那是一頭由堤豐所生、刀槍不入的野獸。他在前往攻擊獅子的途中來到克勒俄奈，寄宿在日工摩羅耳科斯的家中；當主人想要獻上一頭犧牲作為祭品時，赫拉克勒斯告訴他等三十天，然後，如果他從狩獵中平安歸來，就向救主宙斯獻祭；但如果他死了，就把他當作英雄來獻祭。

passages.text: And having come to Nemea and tracked the lion, he first shot an arrow at him; but when he perceived that the beast was invulnerable, he heaved up his club and made after him. And when the lion took refuge in a cave with two mouths, Heracles built up the one entrance and came in upon the beast through the other, and, putting his arm round its neck, held it tight till he had choked it; then, laying it on his shoulders, he carried it to Cleonae. Amazed at his manhood, Eurystheus forbade him thenceforth to enter the city, but ordered him to exhibit the fruits of his labours before the gates.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.1 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他來到涅墨亞，追蹤那頭獅子，先向它射了一箭；但當他發覺那野獸刀槍不入時，便舉起棍棒追了上去。當獅子躲進一個有兩個入口的洞穴時，赫拉克勒斯堵住了其中一個入口，從另一個入口進去迎上那野獸，用胳膊摟住它的脖子，緊緊勒住直到把它掐死；然後，把它扛在肩上，帶到了克勒俄奈。歐律斯透斯對他的勇猛感到驚異，從此禁止他進入城內，但命令他在城門前展示他勞動的成果。

passages.text: As a second labour he ordered him to kill the Lernaean hydra. That creature, bred in the swamp of Lerna, used to go forth into the plain and ravage both the cattle and the country. Now the hydra had a huge body, with nine heads, eight mortal, but the middle one immortal. So mounting his chariot, Heracles drove to Lerna, and by the help of Iphicles held back the crabs that came to the hydra's help: he burned out the root of each head with a firebrand and stopped the necks, and the immortal head he buried under a heavy rock on the road between Lerna and Elaeus.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.2 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 作為第二項勞動，他命令他去殺死勒耳那的九頭蛇。那生物在勒耳那的沼澤中長大，常常來到平原上，蹂躪牲畜和鄉野。那九頭蛇身軀巨大，有九個頭，八個是會死的，但中間那個是不死的。於是赫拉克勒斯登上戰車，驅車前往勒耳那，在伊菲克勒斯的幫助下，擋住了前來援助九頭蛇的螃蟹：他用火把燒掉每個頭的根部，封住脖子，而那個不死的頭，他把它埋在了勒耳那與埃萊俄斯之間路上的 一塊重石之下。

passages.text: But Eurystheus said that this labour ought not to be reckoned, because it was done with the help of Iolaus; and so Heracles had to perform two more labours for the same number. And he dipped his arrows in the gall of the hydra, so that any wound they gave became incurable — a device that would cost the centaur Chiron his life, and would one day kill the hero himself.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.2 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但歐律斯透斯說這項勞動不應計算在內，因為它是在伊俄拉俄斯的幫助下完成的；因此赫拉克勒斯不得不為同樣的數目再完成兩項勞動。他把箭浸在九頭蛇的膽汁中，這樣它們造成的任何傷口都變得無法醫治——這一計謀將使半人馬喀戎喪命，並有朝一日殺死英雄本人。

title.en: The Man-Eating Mares of Diomedes
title.zh: 食人馬：狄俄墨得斯的母馬

region.en: Thrace (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 色雷斯（象徵性定位）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), § 2.5.8

summary.en: The eighth labour was to bring the mares of Diomedes the Thracian to Mycenae. Diomedes, son of Ares and Cyrene, was king of the Bistones, a very warlike Thracian people, and he owned man-eating mares. Heracles sailed with a band of volunteers, overpowered the grooms in charge of the mangers, and drove the mares to the sea. When the Bistones came to the rescue, he committed the mares to the guardianship of Abderus, a son of Hermes from Opus in Locris, a minion of his own; but the mares killed him by dragging him after them. Heracles fought the Bistones, slew Diomedes, and put the rest to flight; and he founded a city, Abdera, beside the grave of the friend who had been done to death, and brought the mares to Eurystheus, who let them go — they came to Mount Olympus, as it is called, and there they were destroyed by the wild beasts.
summary.zh: 第八項勞役：將色雷斯狄俄墨得斯之食人母馬帶回邁錫尼。狄俄墨得斯乃阿瑞斯與庫瑞涅之子，比斯托涅人之王，養食人母馬。赫拉克勒斯率義勇出海，制服馬夫，驅馬至海邊；比斯托涅人來救時，託阿布德羅斯（赫爾墨斯之子、洛克里人、英雄之侍從）看守，馬群拖死此人。英雄擊潰比斯托涅人、殺狄俄墨得斯，並於亡友墓旁建城阿布德拉；母馬獻予歐里斯透斯後被釋，逃至奧林波斯山，為野獸所食。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: The eighth labour he enjoined on him was to bring the mares of Diomedes the Thracian to Mycenae. Now this Diomedes was a son of Ares and Cyrene, and he was king of the Bistones, a very warlike Thracian people, and he owned man-eating mares.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.8 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他吩咐他做的第八項勞動，是把色雷斯的狄俄墨得斯的母馬帶到邁錫尼。這個狄俄墨得斯是阿瑞斯與庫瑞涅的兒子，他是比斯托涅斯人的國王，那是一個非常好戰的色雷斯民族，他擁有吃人的母馬。

passages.text: So Heracles sailed with a band of volunteers, and having overpowered the grooms who were in charge of the mangers, he drove the mares to the sea. When the Bistones in arms came to the rescue, he committed the mares to the guardianship of Abderus, who was a son of Hermes, a native of Opus in Locris, and a minion of Heracles; but the mares killed him by dragging him after them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.8 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是赫拉克勒斯帶著一隊志願者航行而去，制伏了看守馬槽的馬夫後，把母馬趕到海邊。當比斯托涅斯人武裝起來前來救援時，他把母馬交給阿布得羅斯看守，那人是赫爾墨斯的兒子，洛克里斯的俄波斯的本地人，也是赫拉克勒斯的寵兒；但母馬把他拖在後面，將他殺死了。

passages.text: But Heracles fought against the Bistones, slew Diomedes and compelled the rest to flee. And he founded a city Abdera beside the grave of Abderus who had been done to death, and bringing the mares he gave them to Eurystheus. But Eurystheus let them go, and they came to Mount Olympus, as it is called, and there they were destroyed by the wild beasts.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.8 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 但赫拉克勒斯與比斯托涅斯人交戰，殺死狄俄墨得斯，並迫使其餘的人逃走。他在被殺害的阿布德羅斯墓旁建立了一座城，名為阿布德拉，然後把那些牝馬帶去交給歐律斯透斯。但歐律斯透斯放走了牠們，牠們便來到所謂的奧林帕斯山，在那裡被野獸所毀。

title.en: Pelops and the Chariot Race of Oenomaus
title.zh: 珀羅普斯與俄諾瑪俄斯的賽車

region.en: Pisa, Elis (Olympia) (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 厄利斯皮薩（奧林匹亞，象徵性定位）

period: Composed from the lost epics (c. 7th century BCE; summary in Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), Epitome e.2.3-e.2.9

summary.en: Pelops, after being slaughtered and boiled at the banquet of the gods, was fairer than ever when he came to life again, and on account of his surpassing beauty he became the beloved of Poseidon, who gave him a winged chariot such that even when it ran through the sea the axles were not wet. Oenomaus, king of Pisa, had a daughter Hippodamia, and, whether he loved her himself or was warned by an oracle that he must die by the man who married her, he put every suitor to death: armed with horses from Ares, he offered her hand as the prize of a race to the Isthmus of Corinth, and slew the losers — some say twelve — and nailed their heads to his house. Pelops came a-wooing; Hippodamia, seeing his beauty, fell in love and persuaded Myrtilus, her father's charioteer and a son of Hermes, to help him; Myrtilus, in love with her himself, did not insert the linchpins in the boxes of the wheels, and Oenomaus, losing the race, was entangled in the reins and dragged to death. Pelops got Hippodamia; and, on the journey home, when Myrtilus tried to violate her, Pelops threw him into the sea — the Myrtoan — at Cape Geraestus; and Myrtilus, as he was being thrown, uttered curses against the house of Pelops. Cleansed by Hephaestus on his return to the Ocean, Pelops went back to Pisa, succeeded to the kingdom of Oenomaus, and subjugated what was formerly called Apia and Pelasgiotis, calling it Peloponnesus after himself — the founder, in the Greek telling, of the chariot races at Olympia.
summary.zh: 珀羅普斯被父坦塔羅斯剁碎煮於神宴，復活後愈見俊美，成為波塞冬之愛人，得賜「飛車過海而輪軸不濕」。厄利斯皮薩王俄諾瑪俄斯有女希波達彌亞，或因自愛、或因神諭（「必死於其婿之手」）而誅殺所有求婚者——戰車由阿瑞斯所賜，追逐敗者至科任托斯地峽，殺十二人，將其首釘於屋牆。珀羅普斯求婚；希波達彌亞見其美貌生情，說服御者墨耳提爾斯（赫爾墨斯之子）相助；御者亦戀她，便不加輪軸銷釘，俄諾瑪俄斯賽敗纏於韁繩拖死。歸途中墨耳提爾斯欲玷希波達彌亞，被珀羅普斯投海（該海因得名墨耳托安），臨死咒珀羅普斯家族。珀羅普斯經赫菲斯托斯淨禮，得皮薩王位，並將「阿庇亞／珀拉斯戈提斯」改名「珀羅奔尼撒」——奧林匹亞賽車之起源神話。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Pelops, after being slaughtered and boiled at the banquet of the gods, was fairer than ever when he came to life again, and on account of his surpassing beauty he became the beloved of Poseidon, who gave him a winged chariot, such that even when it ran through the sea the axles were not wet.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.2.3 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 珀羅普斯在眾神的宴席上被宰殺並烹煮之後，當他重獲生命時，比以往更加俊美；由於他出眾的美貌，他成了波塞頓的愛人，波塞頓賜給他一輛有翼的戰車，即使它奔馳於海上，車軸也不會沾濕。

passages.text: Now Oenomaus, the king of Pisa, had a daughter Hippodamia; and whether it was that he loved her, as some say, or that he was warned by an oracle that he must die by the man that married her, no man got her to wife; for her father could not persuade her to cohabit with him, and her suitors were put by him to death. For he had arms and horses given him by Ares, and he offered as a prize to the suitors the hand of his daughter; and each suitor was bound to take up Hippodamia on his own chariot and flee as far as the Isthmus of Corinth, and Oenomaus straightway pursued him in full armour, and if he overtook him he slew him. In this way he slew many suitors, some say twelve, and he cut off the heads of the suitors and nailed them to his house.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.2.4-e.2.5 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 皮薩的國王俄諾瑪俄斯有一個女兒希波達彌亞；有人說他愛上了她，也有人說他受到神諭警告，說他必死於娶她為妻的人之手，因此無人能娶她為妻；因為她的父親無法說服她與他同床，而她的求婚者都被他處死。因為他從阿瑞斯那裡得到了武器和馬匹，他便以女兒的婚事作為獎賞提供給求婚者；每個求婚者都必須讓希波達彌亞登上自己的戰車，逃到科林斯地峽；俄諾瑪俄斯隨即全副武裝追趕他，若追上了便將他殺死。他就這樣殺死了許多求婚者，有人說有十二個，他砍下求婚者的頭顱，釘在自己的屋上。

passages.text: So Pelops also came a-wooing; and when Hippodamia saw his beauty, she conceived a passion for him and persuaded Myrtilus, son of Hermes, to help him; for Myrtilus was charioteer to Oenomaus. Accordingly Myrtilus, being in love with her and wishing to gratify her, did not insert the linchpins in the boxes of the wheels, and thus caused Oenomaus to lose the race and to be entangled in the reins and dragged to death.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.2.6-e.2.7 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是珀羅普斯也前來求婚；當希波達彌亞看見他的美貌時，便對他產生了愛慕之情，並說服赫耳墨斯之子密耳提羅斯幫助他；因為密耳提羅斯是俄諾瑪俄斯的馭者。於是密耳提羅斯因愛慕她，又想討她歡心，便沒有把輪軸銷插入車輪的軸箱中，因而使俄諾瑪俄斯輸了比賽，被韁繩纏住，拖拽而死。

passages.text: Pelops, therefore, got Hippodamia; and on his journey, in which he was accompanied by Myrtilus, he came to a certain place and withdrew a little to fetch water for his wife, who was athirst; and in the meantime Myrtilus tried to rape her. But when Pelops learned that from her, he threw Myrtilus into the sea, called after him the Myrtoan Sea, at Cape Geraestus; and Myrtilus, as he was being thrown, uttered curses against the house of Pelops.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.2.8 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 因此，珀羅普斯得到了希波達彌亞；在他由密耳提羅斯陪同的旅途中，他來到某個地方，稍稍離開去為口渴的妻子取水；在此期間，密耳提羅斯企圖強暴她。但當珀羅普斯從她口中得知此事後，便在革賴斯圖斯海角把密耳提羅斯拋入海中，那片海便以他命名為密耳托斯海；密耳提羅斯在被拋下時，對珀羅普斯的家族發出了詛咒。

passages.text: When Pelops had reached the Ocean and been cleansed by Hephaestus, he returned to Pisa in Elis and succeeded to the kingdom of Oenomaus — but not till he had subjugated what was formerly called Apia and Pelasgiotis, which he called Peloponnesus after himself.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.2.9 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當珀羅普斯到達大洋並被赫費斯托斯潔淨之後，他回到厄利斯的皮薩，繼承了俄諾瑪俄斯的王國——但這是在他征服了從前稱為阿皮亞和佩拉斯吉奧提斯的地方之後，他用自己的名字將其命名為伯羅奔尼撒。

title.en: Salmoneus the False Zeus
title.zh: 偽宙斯薩爾摩紐斯

region.en: Elis, Peloponnese (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伯羅奔尼撒厄利斯（象徵性定位）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), § 1.9.7

summary.en: Salmoneus, one of the many sons of Aeolus, came from Thessaly to Elis and founded a city there. Wishing to put himself on an equality with Zeus, he took away the sacrifices of the god and ordered them offered to himself, and dragged dried hides with bronze kettles behind his chariot, saying that he thundered, and flung lighted torches at the sky, saying that he lightened. Zeus struck him with a thunderbolt and wiped out the city he had founded, with all its inhabitants.
summary.zh: 埃俄羅斯之子薩爾摩紐斯自色薩利來至厄利斯建城，自比宙斯：奪神之祭、命祭己身，以乾皮青銅鍋拖曳於戰車之後而自稱「雷霆」，向天投擲火把而自稱「閃電」。宙斯以雷殛之，滅其城邑，全城無一倖免。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Salmoneus at first dwelt in Thessaly, but afterwards he came to Elis and there founded a city. And being arrogant and wishful to put himself on an equality with Zeus, he was punished for his impiety. For he said that he was himself Zeus, and he took away the sacrifices of the god and ordered them to be offered to himself; and by dragging dried hides, with bronze kettles, at his chariot, he said that he thundered; and by flinging lighted torches at the sky he said that he lightened. But Zeus struck him with a thunderbolt, and wiped out the city he had founded with all its inhabitants — a story told for the Greek who might mistake clever theatricals for divinity.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 1.9.7 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 薩爾摩紐斯起初住在色薩利，後來他來到厄利斯，並在那裡建立了一座城。他為人傲慢，又妄圖使自己與宙斯平起平坐，因而為自己的不敬神而受到懲罰。因為他自稱他就是宙斯，又奪走獻給那位神的祭品，下令把它們獻給自己；他還把乾獸皮連同青銅壺拖在戰車後面，說自己是在打雷；又把點燃的火把拋向天空，說自己是在閃電。但宙斯以雷霆擊中了他，並把他所建立的那座城連同全體居民一併抹去——這個故事是講給那些可能把巧妙的戲劇表演誤當作神性的希臘人聽的。

title.en: The Stables of Augeas and the Birds of Stymphalus
title.zh: 奧革阿斯牛廄與斯廷法利斯湖怪鳥

region.en: Elis & Stymphalus, Arcadia (mythic geography)
region.zh: 厄利斯與阿卡迪亞斯廷法利斯湖（神話地理）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), §§ 2.5.5-2.5.6

summary.en: The fifth labour was to carry out the dung of the cattle of Augeas, king of Elis, in a single day. Heracles did not reveal the command of Eurystheus, but offered the task for a tenth of the cattle; Augeas promised, with his son Phyleus as witness. Heracles made a breach in the foundations of the yard, diverted the courses of the Alpheus and Peneus into it, and made an outlet for the water on the other side. When Augeas learned the work had been done at Eurystheus' command, he refused the reward and denied the bargain; and the arbitrators, hearing Phyleus witness against his own father, saw Augeas order both the witness and Heracles out of Elis before the voting. The sixth labour was to chase away the Stymphalian birds: countless birds had flocked to the lake of Stymphalus in Arcadia, fearing the wolves; Athena gave Heracles brazen castanets made by Hephaestus, and by clashing them on a mountain that overhung the lake he scared the birds into the air, where he shot them.
summary.zh: 第五項勞役：一日之內清空厄利斯王奧革阿斯之牛廄。赫拉克勒斯未言明是歐里斯透斯之命，只求得牛群十分之一為酬；奧革阿斯許諾，以其子菲琉斯為證。赫拉克勒斯鑿開牛欄地基，引阿爾甫斯與珀紐斯二河之水灌入，另鑿出水口。當奧革阿斯得知此乃奉命而為，竟拒不付酬、矢口否認承諾；仲裁時，菲琉斯出庭指證其父，奧革阿斯怒而在投票前將二人逐出厄利斯。第六項勞役：驅逐斯廷法利斯湖之怪鳥。雅典娜賜赫拉克勒斯赫菲斯托斯所鑄之銅響板；英雄在湖邊山上擊之，鳥群驚起，遂以箭射殺。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: The fifth labour he laid on him was to carry out the dung of the cattle of Augeas in a single day. Now Augeas was king of Elis — some say a son of the Sun, others of Poseidon, and others of Phorbas — and he had many herds of cattle. Heracles accosted him, and without revealing the command of Eurystheus, said that he would carry out the dung in one day if Augeas would give him the tithe of the cattle. Augeas was incredulous, but promised.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.5 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他加給他的第五項勞役，是在一日之內把奧革阿斯的牛群的糞便清運出去。奧革阿斯是厄利斯的國王——有人說他是太陽之子，有人說是波塞冬之子，還有人說是福爾巴斯之子——他擁有許多群牛。赫拉克勒斯上前與他搭話，並未透露歐律斯透斯的命令，只說若奧革阿斯肯把牛群的十分之一給他，他便能在一天之內把糞便清運出去。奧革阿斯不肯相信，但還是答應了。

passages.text: Having taken Augeas' son Phyleus to witness, Heracles made a breach in the foundations of the cattle-yard, and then, diverting the courses of the Alpheus and Peneus, which flowed near each other, he turned them into the yard, having first made an outlet for the water through another opening.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.5 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 赫拉克勒斯請奧革阿斯之子菲琉斯作證，在牛欄的地基上開了一個缺口，然後把彼此相近而流的阿爾甫斯河與珀涅俄斯河的河道改道，將它們引入牛欄之中，事先又另開一個出口讓水流出。

passages.text: When Augeas learned that this had been accomplished at the command of Eurystheus, he would not pay the reward; nay more, he denied that he had promised to pay it, and on that point he professed himself ready to submit to arbitration. The arbitrators having taken their seats, Phyleus was called by Heracles and bore witness against his father, affirming that he had agreed to give a reward. In a rage Augeas, before the voting took place, ordered both Phyleus and Heracles to pack out of Elis.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.5 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當奧革阿斯得知此事是奉歐律斯透斯之命而完成時，他不肯支付報酬；不僅如此，他還否認自己曾答應支付，並且聲稱在這一點上他願意接受仲裁。仲裁者就座之後，菲琉斯被赫拉克勒斯傳喚，作了不利於自己父親的證詞，確認他曾同意給予報酬。奧革阿斯勃然大怒，在投票舉行之前，便下令把菲琉斯和赫拉克勒斯二人一起趕出厄利斯。

passages.text: The sixth labour he enjoined on him was to chase away the Stymphalian birds. Now at the city of Stymphalus in Arcadia was the lake called Stymphalian, embosomed in a deep wood. To it countless birds had flocked for refuge, fearing to be preyed upon by the wolves. So when Heracles was at a loss how to drive the birds from the wood, Athena gave him brazen castanets which she had received from Hephaestus. By clashing these on a certain mountain that overhung the lake, he scared the birds; they could not abide the sound, but fluttered up in a fright, and in that way Heracles shot them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 2.5.6 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他吩咐給他的第六項勞役，是趕走斯廷法利斯湖的鳥。在阿卡迪亞的斯廷法利斯城，有一個名叫斯廷法利斯的湖，四周環繞著茂密的森林。無數的鳥兒聚集到那裡避難，因為牠們害怕被狼捕食。因此，當赫拉克勒斯不知如何把鳥兒從林中趕走時，雅典娜給了他一副她從赫菲斯托斯那裡得到的青銅響板。他在俯瞰該湖的某座山上敲響這些響板，把鳥兒嚇住了；牠們受不了那聲音，驚慌地撲騰飛起，赫拉克勒斯就這樣把牠們射了下來。

title.en: Tyro, the River, and the Twins
title.zh: 提洛、河神與雙生子

region.en: Thessaly (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 色薩利（象徵性定位）

period: Compiled c. 1st-2nd century CE (attrib. Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), § 1.9.8

summary.en: Tyro, daughter of Salmoneus, was brought up by Cretheus her uncle, and fell in love with the river Enipeus, going often to its running waters to pour out her heart to them. Poseidon, taking the river's own shape, lay with her, and she bore twin sons in secret and exposed them. A mare of some passing horse-herdsmen kicked one of the babies and left a livid mark on its face; the horse-herdsman took up both children and reared them, calling the marked one Pelias and the other Neleus. Grown, the twins found their mother and killed her stepmother Sidero, who had mistreated her; and Pelias cut her down on the very altars of Hera, and ever after treated the goddess with contempt.
summary.zh: 薩爾摩紐斯之女提洛由伯父克瑞透斯撫養，愛上河神厄尼珀斯，常赴其流水之畔傾訴。波塞冬化作河神之形與之結合；她祕誕雙子而棄之。路過牧馬者的母馬踢傷一嬰留於面部青痕；牧馬人收養二子，稱青痕者珀利阿斯、另一為涅琉斯。雙子長成尋母，誅其繼母西得羅——珀利阿斯竟於赫拉祭壇前將其殺害，此後亦常輕慢女神。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Now Tyro, daughter of Salmoneus and Alcidice, was brought up by Cretheus, brother of Salmoneus, and conceived a passion for the river Enipeus, and often would she hie to its running waters and utter her plaint to them. But Poseidon in the likeness of Enipeus lay with her, and she secretly gave birth to twin sons, whom she exposed. As the babes lay forlorn, a mare belonging to some passing horse-herdsmen kicked with its hoof one of the two infants and left a livid mark on its face.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 1.9.8 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 薩爾摩紐斯與阿爾喀狄刻之女堤洛，由薩爾摩紐斯之兄克瑞透斯撫養長大，她對厄尼剖斯河產生了愛慕之情，常常趕到那奔流的河水邊，向它們傾訴自己的哀怨。但波塞冬化作厄尼剖斯的模樣與她同寢，她秘密地生下了一對雙生子，並把他們拋棄了。當這兩個嬰兒孤零零地躺著時，一些過路的牧馬人的一匹母馬用蹄子踢了兩個嬰兒中的一個，在他的臉上留下了一塊青紫的傷痕。

passages.text: The horse-herdsman took up both the children and reared them; and the one with the livid mark he called Pelias, and the other Neleus. When they were grown up, they discovered their mother and killed their stepmother Sidero: for knowing that their mother was ill-used by her, they attacked her; but before they could catch her she had taken refuge in the precinct of Hera. However, Pelias cut her down on the very altars, and ever after he continued to treat Hera with contempt.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library 1.9.8 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那牧馬人抱起兩個孩子撫養長大；他把身上有青紫印記的那個叫作珀利阿斯，另一個叫作涅琉斯。他們長大以後，尋回了母親，並殺死了繼母西得羅：因為他們得知母親受她虐待，便去攻擊她；但還沒等他們捉住她，她就已逃入赫拉的神域避難。然而珀利阿斯就在祭壇上把她砍倒，此後他始終對赫拉心存輕蔑。

title.en: The Locrian Maidens at Troy
title.zh: 洛克里少女赴特洛伊

region.en: Ilium (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 特洛伊（象徵性定位）

period: Composed from the lost epics (c. 7th century BCE; summary in Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), Epitome e.6.20-e.6.22

summary.en: The Locrians regained their own country with difficulty, and three years afterwards, when Locris was visited by a plague, they received an oracle bidding them to propitiate Athena at Ilium and to send two maidens as suppliants for a thousand years. The lot first fell on Periboea and Cleopatra. When they came to Troy they were chased by the natives and took refuge in the sanctuary; and they did not approach the goddess, but swept and sprinkled the sanctuary; and they did not go out of the temple, and their hair was cropped, and they wore single garments and no shoes. And when the first maidens died, they sent others; and they entered into the city by night, lest, being seen outside the precinct, they should be put to the sword; but afterwards they sent babes with their nurses. And when the thousand years were passed, after the Phocian war, they ceased to send suppliants.
summary.zh: 洛克里人艱難還鄉；三年後瘟疫襲境，神諭命其「在特洛伊向雅典娜贖罪、送兩名少女為乞援者，以繼千年」。初籤落於珀里玻亞與克勒俄帕特拉。二女至特洛伊被土人追逐、避入圣所；不入神前，只掃灑圣所；不出廟門、剃髮、單衣赤足。首批少女亡後續送他人；夜間入城以免被殺；其後改送嬰兒由乳母攜往。千年期滿（福基斯戰爭之後），方停止派遣。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: The Locrians regained their own country with difficulty, and three years afterwards, when Locris was visited by a plague, they received an oracle bidding them to propitiate Athena at Ilium and to send two maidens as suppliants for a thousand years. The lot first fell on Periboea and Cleopatra.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.6.20 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 洛克里斯人好不容易才收復了自己的國土，三年之後，洛克里斯遭遇瘟疫，他們得到神諭，命他們到伊利昂去安撫雅典娜，並派遣兩名少女作為祈求者，為期一千年。抽籤首先落在珀里玻亞和克勒俄帕特拉身上。

passages.text: And when they came to Troy they were chased by the natives and took refuge in the sanctuary. And they did not approach the goddess, but swept and sprinkled the sanctuary; and they did not go out of the temple, and their hair was cropped, and they wore single garments and no shoes.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.6.21 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她們來到特洛伊後，遭到當地人追逐，便躲進聖所避難。她們不接近女神，只是清掃並灑掃聖所；她們不走出神廟，頭髮剃短，身穿單衣，不穿鞋。

passages.text: And when the first maidens died, they sent others; and they entered into the city by night, lest, being seen outside the precinct, they should be put to the sword; but afterwards they sent babes with their nurses. And when the thousand years were passed, after the Phocian war, they ceased to send suppliants.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.6.22 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第一批少女死後，他們又派去別的少女；她們在夜間入城，以免在聖域之外被人看見而遭殺害；後來他們改派嬰兒，由乳母陪同。一千年過去之後，即在福基斯戰爭之後，他們便不再派遣祈求者了。

title.en: Tenes and the Founding of Tenedos
title.zh: 特涅斯與特涅多斯島之建立

region.en: Tenedos, Aegean (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 愛琴海特涅多斯島（象徵性定位）

period: Composed from the lost epics (c. 7th century BCE; summary in Apollodorus; Frazer translation 1921)

source.work: Apollodorus, Library, trans. J. G. Frazer (1921), Epitome e.3.23-e.3.26

summary.en: After putting to sea from Aulis they touched at Tenedos, which was ruled by Tenes, son of Cycnus and Proclia — though according to some he was a son of Apollo. For Cycnus had a son Tenes and a daughter Hemithea by Proclia, daughter of Laomedon; but he afterwards married Philonome, daughter of Tragasus, and she fell in love with Tenes, and, failing to seduce him, falsely accused him to Cycnus of attempting to debauch her, producing in witness of it a flute-player, Eumolpus. Cycnus believed her, and, putting Tenes and his sister in a chest, set them adrift on the sea; the chest was washed up on the island of Leucophrys, and Tenes landed and settled in the island, calling it Tenedos after himself. Cycnus afterwards learning the truth, stoned the flute-player to death and buried his wife alive in the earth. So when the Greeks were standing in for Tenedos, Tenes saw them and tried to keep them off by throwing stones, but was killed by Achilles with a sword-cut in the breast — though Thetis had forewarned Achilles not to kill Tenes, because he himself would die by the hand of Apollo if he slew Tenes.
summary.zh: 希臘艦隊自奧利斯出海，先抵特涅多斯島——島主特涅斯乃庫克諾斯與普羅克莉亞之子（另有說為阿波羅之子）。庫克諾斯續娶特拉伽索斯之女菲洛諾墨；繼母戀特涅斯不遂，誣其非禮，並以笛師歐墨爾甫斯為偽證。庫克諾斯信之，將特涅斯與其妹赫彌忒亞裝箱漂流；箱漂至琉科佛里斯島，特涅斯登陸建城，以其名命名「特涅多斯」。庫克諾斯後知真相，以石擊斃笛師、活埋其妻。希臘艦隊抵島時，特涅斯投石阻之，為阿基琉斯劍穿胸而死——忒提斯曾預警：若殺特涅斯，阿基琉斯必將死於阿波羅之手。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: After putting to sea from Aulis they touched at Tenedos. It was ruled by Tenes, son of Cycnus and Proclia, but according to some, he was a son of Apollo. He dwelt there because he had been banished by his father.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.3.23 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們從奧利斯出海後，停泊於忒涅多斯。該地由忒涅斯統治，他是庫克諾斯與普洛克利亞之子，但有人說他是阿波羅之子。他住在那裡，是因為被父親放逐。

passages.text: For Cycnus had a son Tenes and a daughter Hemithea by Proclia, daughter of Laomedon; but he afterwards married Philonome, daughter of Tragasus; and she fell in love with Tenes, and, failing to seduce him, falsely accused him to Cycnus of attempting to debauch her, and in witness of it she produced a flute-player, by name Eumolpus.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.3.24 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 因為庫克諾斯與拉俄墨冬之女普洛克利亞生有一子忒涅斯和一女赫彌忒亞；但他後來又娶了特拉加索斯之女菲洛諾墨；她愛上了忒涅斯，引誘不成，便向庫克諾斯誣告他企圖誘姦自己，並找來一名吹笛人作證，此人名叫歐摩爾波斯。

passages.text: Cycnus believed her, and putting him and his sister in a chest he set them adrift on the sea. The chest was washed up on the island of Leucophrys, and Tenes landed and settled in the island, and called it Tenedos after himself. But Cycnus afterwards learning the truth, stoned the flute-player to death and buried his wife alive in the earth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.3.25 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 庫克諾斯相信了她，便把他和他妹妹裝進一隻箱子，讓他們在海上漂流。箱子被沖上琉科弗律斯島，忒涅斯登陸後在島上定居，並以自己的名字將該島命名為忒涅多斯。但庫克諾斯後來得知真相，便用石頭砸死了那名吹笛人，並將妻子活埋於土中。

passages.text: So when the Greeks were standing in for Tenedos, Tenes saw them and tried to keep them off by throwing stones, but was killed by Achilles with a sword-cut in the breast, though Thetis had forewarned Achilles not to kill Tenes, because he himself would die by the hand of Apollo if he slew Tenes.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Apollodorus, Library, Epitome e.3.26 (Frazer 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 因此，當希臘人駛近忒涅多斯時，忒涅斯看見了他們，便投擲石塊試圖阻止他們登岸，卻被阿基里斯一劍砍中胸膛而死，儘管忒提斯曾事先警告阿基里斯不要殺死忒涅斯，因為他若殺了忒涅斯，自己便會死於阿波羅之手。

title.en: The Birth of Pan
title.zh: 潘神的誕生

region.en: Arcadia, Cyllene (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿卡迪亞庫勒涅山（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 7th-6th century BCE (Lang translation 1899)

source.work: Homeric Hymns XIX (To Pan), trans. Andrew Lang (1899)

summary.en: Tell me, Muse, concerning the dear son of Hermes, the goat-footed, the twy-horned, the lover of the din of revel, who haunts the wooded dells with dancing nymphs that tread the crests of the steep cliffs, calling upon Pan the pastoral god of the long wild hair. Lord is he of every snowy crest and mountain peak and rocky path; he ranges over the high white hills and chases the wild beasts with keen eye, and at evening returns piping from the chase. The mountain nymphs go wandering with him by the dark water of the well, while the echo moans along the mountain crest; on his back he wears the tawny hide of a lynx. They sing of the blessed gods and of high Olympus, and above all of boon Hermes: how he came to many-fountained Arcadia, the mother of sheep, where his Cyllenian demesne is, and there, god as he was, he shepherded the fleecy sheep, the thrall of a mortal man; for soft desire had come upon him to wed the fair-haired daughter of Dryops, and the glad nuptials he accomplished, and to Hermes in the hall she bore a dear son. From his birth he was a marvel to behold: goat-footed, twy-horned, a loud speaker, a sweet laugher. Then the nurse leaped up and fled when she saw his wild face and bearded chin. But him did boon Hermes straightway take in his hands and bear, and gladly did he rejoice at heart. Swiftly to the dwellings of the gods went he, bearing the babe hidden in the thick skins of mountain hares; there he sat down by Zeus and the other immortals, and showed his child, and all the immortals were glad at heart, and chiefly the Bacchic Dionysus. Pan they called the babe to name, because he had made glad the hearts of all of them.
summary.zh: 繆斯啊，請歌頌赫爾墨斯之愛子：羊足雙角、喜好狂歡之聲的潘神，與舞於崖頂之仙女們漫遊林谷；他為雪峰、山巔與巉岩之主，日逐野獸，暮攜蘆笛而歸；仙女們伴其於幽泉旁歌唱，回聲在山脊嗚咽；背披猞猁皮。歌中頌諸神與奧林波斯，尤頌赫爾墨斯：他至多泉的阿卡迪亞（羊之母）、其庫勒涅領地，化身凡人為人牧羊；因戀德律俄普斯之金髮女兒而結良緣，生下一子。此子生而奇異：羊足、雙角、聲宏、愛笑。乳母見其野面與鬍鬚驚逃；赫爾墨斯抱起嬰兒、以野兔厚皮裹之，攜至奧林波斯示於宙斯與眾神，眾神皆喜，尤以酒神狄俄尼索斯為甚；因其使眾心皆悅，遂名之曰潘（Pan）。

sensitivity.note: Ancient literary source; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Tell me, Muse, concerning the dear son of Hermes, the goat-footed, the twy-horned, the lover of the din of revel, who haunts the wooded dells with dancing nymphs that tread the crests of the steep cliffs, calling upon Pan the pastoral god of the long wild hair. Lord is he of every snowy crest and mountain peak and rocky path.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Homeric Hymns XIX, To Pan (Lang 1899); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 繆斯啊，請向我講述赫爾墨斯那親愛的兒子，那山羊腳的、雙角的、喜愛歡宴喧鬧的，他與踏著陡峭崖頂起舞的寧芙們一同出沒於林木繁茂的山谷，呼喚著那長著蓬亂長髮的牧神潘。他是每一座積雪的山脊、每一座山峰和每一條岩石小徑的主宰。

passages.text: Hither and thither he goes through the thick copses, sometimes being drawn to the still waters, and sometimes faring through the lofty crags he climbs the highest peak whence the flocks are seen below; ever he ranges over the high white hills, and ever among the knolls he chases and slays the wild beasts, the god with keen eye, and at evening returns piping from the chase, breathing sweet strains on the reeds. In song that bird cannot excel him which, among the leaves of the blossoming springtide, pours forth her plaint and her honey-sweet song.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Homeric Hymns XIX, To Pan (Lang 1899); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他往來穿梭於茂密的灌木叢中，時而被引向靜止的水邊，時而穿越高聳的岩崖，攀上最高的峰頂，從那裡可以望見下方的羊群；他總是漫遊於高聳潔白的山丘之間，又總是在圓丘之間追逐並殺死野獸——那目光銳利的神；到了傍晚，他從狩獵中歸來，吹著蘆笛，吹出甜美的曲調。在歌聲上，那隻在繁花盛開的春日枝葉間傾吐哀怨與蜜般甜美之歌的鳥兒也無法勝過他。

passages.text: With him then the mountain nymphs, the shrill singers, go wandering with light feet, and sing at the side of the dark water of the well, while the echo moans along the mountain crest, and the god leaps hither and thither, and goes into the midst, with many a step of the dance. On his back he wears the tawny hide of a lynx, and his heart rejoices with shrill songs in the soft meadow where crocus and fragrant hyacinth bloom all mingled amidst the grass.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Homeric Hymns XIX, To Pan (Lang 1899); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是，那些聲音尖銳的山中寧芙們與他一同輕盈地漫遊，在井邊幽暗的水旁歌唱，而回聲沿著山脊哀鳴，那神則跳來跳去，步入她們中間，舞步翩翩。他背上披著一隻猞猁的黃褐色皮，在柔軟的草地上，番紅花與芬芳的風信子混雜盛開於青草之間，他的心隨著尖銳的歌聲而歡欣。

passages.text: They sing of the blessed gods and of high Olympus, and above all do they sing of boon Hermes, how he is the fleet herald of all the gods, and how he came to many-fountained Arcadia, the mother of sheep, where is his Cyllenian demesne, and there he, god as he was, shepherded the fleecy sheep, the thrall of a mortal man; for soft desire had come upon him to wed the fair-haired daughter of Dryops, and the glad nuptials he accomplished, and to Hermes in the hall she bare a dear son.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Homeric Hymns XIX, To Pan (Lang 1899); not verbatim.
