She avoided the feathers till she reached a spot where the wind had blown them away, and then the trouble began. Her very motherhood proved her salvation, because her unborn babe began talking and told her which path to follow.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §33; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 太陽亞爾告訴妻子，他打算往西邊遠行，但既然她如今有孕在身，最好從容而行：他先出發，她必須循著他的足跡，始終走右邊的路，因為他會在左邊撒下羽毛，好讓她不會走錯。她避開羽毛，直到抵達一處風把羽毛吹走的地方，麻煩便開始了。她的母性反倒成了她的救星，因為她腹中的胎兒開始說話，告訴她該走哪條路。

passages.text: The child told her to pluck the pretty flowers bobbing over the roadway; she had picked some when a marabunta wasp stung her below the waist, and in trying to kill it she missed and struck herself. The unborn baby, misinterpreting her action as a smack, became vexed and refused any longer to show her the direction. Hopelessly astray, more dead than alive, she found herself before a very large house whose only occupant was Nanyobo, a very old and very big frog-woman. She was told to clean her hostess's head, 'but mind, do not put the insects into your mouth, because they will poison you.' Overcome with fatigue and anxiety, she forgot the injunction, picked out a louse, placed it between her teeth as is customary — and fell dead.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §33; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 孩子叫她摘下路邊搖曳的漂亮花朵；她摘了一些，卻被一隻馬拉本塔黃蜂螫了腰下，她試圖打死牠時失手打中了自己。腹中胎兒誤以為她這一動作是摑打，便惱怒起來，再也不肯為她指路。她徹底迷了路，半死不活，發現自己來到一棟非常大的房子前，屋裡唯一的居民是娜尼約博，一個非常年老、非常巨大的蛙女。她奉命為女主人清理頭髮，「但記住，別把蟲子放進嘴裡，因為牠們會毒死你。」她因疲憊與焦慮而忘卻了告誡，揀出一隻蝨子，照慣例把它放在齒間——隨即倒地而死。

title.en: The Twins Discover Fire: Makunaima and Pia Kill the Old Frog
title.zh: 雙子識火：馬庫納伊瑪與皮亞誅老蛙

region.en: Pomeroon River, Guyana (Warrau)
region.zh: 蓋亞那波默龍河瓦勞之地

period: Warrau oral tradition; recorded 1915 (Roth)

source.work: Walter E. Roth, An Inquiry into the Animism and Folk-lore of the Guiana Indians (33rd Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1915), ch. II 'Tribal Heroes', §§34

summary.en: Old Nanyobo slashed open the dead mother and extracted not one child but two — the beautiful boys Makunaima and Pia — and minded them well. She always sent them to dry their fish in the sun, never over a fire, yet fed them cooked fish: she vomited fire from her mouth, cooked, and licked the fire up again. One brother changed himself into a lizard and watched from the roof, seeing her also scratch her neck for balata-milk to make starch. 'What old woman do, no good. Kill old woman.' They tied her to a tree and burned her; the fire passed from her body into the fagots of hima-heru wood — from which we still get fire by rubbing two sticks together.
summary.zh: 老蛙婦剖亡母而取出雙子：馬庫納伊瑪與皮亞。彼令曝魚於日，不許就火，然魚皆已炊熟——原來其口中吐火，炊畢舔滅。其一化蜥登屋窺之，見其搔頸取乳為粉。『老婦所為不善，殺之。』縛於樹而焚；火自其身入柴，此柴即取火之木。

sensitivity.note: Warrau oral tradition recorded 1915 (Roth); archival record, read critically.

passages.text: Old Nanyobo thereupon slashed open the mother, and extracted not one child but two — a pair of beautiful boys, Makunaima and Pia. Nanyobo proved a kind foster-mother and minded them well. As the babies grew they commenced shooting birds, then fish and game. On each occasion she would say, 'You must dry your fish in the sun, and never over a fire' — yet by the time they returned with the firewood she had sent for, the fish would be all nicely cooked and ready. As a matter of fact she would vomit fire out of her mouth, do her cooking, and lick the fire up again before the lads' return; she apparently never let them see fire burning.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §34; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 老娜尼約博於是剖開母親的肚子，取出的不是一個孩子，而是兩個——一對漂亮的男孩，馬庫奈馬與皮亞。娜尼約博證明是個慈愛的養母，把他們照料得很好。孩子們長大後開始射鳥，接著是魚與獵物。每次她都會說：「你們必須把魚曬在太陽下，絕不可放在火上烤」——然而等他們帶著她打發去取的柴火回來時，魚早已烹調妥當、準備就緒。事實上，她會從嘴裡吐出火來做飯，再在小伙子們回來之前把火舔回去；她顯然從不讓他們看見火在燃燒。

passages.text: Day after day made the boys suspicious, and they determined to find out how the old lady made her fire. When next despatched for firewood, one of them changed himself into a lizard, ran back up into the roof, and watched: he saw the old woman vomit out fire, use it, and lick it up again, and also scratch her neck, whence flowed something like balata milk, out of which she prepared starch. Their deliberations were summarized tersely: 'What old woman do, no good. Kill old woman.' They tied her to a fine tree in the middle of a large cleared field and burned her; as she was consumed the fire within her passed into the surrounding fagots of hima-heru wood — the timber from which we still get fire by rubbing two sticks together.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §34; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 日復一日，男孩們起了疑心，決心查明老婦人是如何生火的。下一次被派去取柴時，其中一人變成一隻蜥蜴，爬回屋頂上窺看：他看見老婦人吐出火來，使用它，又把它舔回去，還抓撓自己的脖子，從那裡流出某種像巴拉塔乳汁的東西，她用它製成澱粉。他們的商議簡潔地總結為：「老婦人所做，不是好事。殺掉老婦人。」他們把她綁在一片大開墾地中央的一棵好樹上，將她燒死；當她被燒盡時，她體內的火傳入了周圍的希馬赫魯木柴堆——我們至今仍靠摩擦兩根木棍取火的木材。

title.en: Tiger's Mother and the Powis Bird's Revelation
title.zh: 虎母與鳳冠鳥之啟示

region.en: Pomeroon district, Guyana (Carib)
region.zh: 蓋亞那波默龍加勒比之地

period: Carib oral tradition; recorded 1915 (Roth)

source.work: Walter E. Roth, An Inquiry into the Animism and Folk-lore of the Guiana Indians (33rd Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1915), ch. II 'Tribal Heroes', §§35-36

summary.en: A woman pregnant by the Sun with twins Pia and Makunaima lost her way after quarrelling with her unborn children and arrived at the house of Tiger's mother, the Rain-frog. The frog hid her in the big cassiri jar, but Tiger smelled her out and killed her, extracting the unborn twins, whom his mother ordered him to cherish in a cotton bundle. They grew to man's size in a month; a Powis bird told them it was Tiger who had killed their mother; they shot him from a staging and slaughtered the old woman too.
summary.zh: 孕於日神之婦與未生雙子失和而迷路，至虎母雨蛙之屋。蛙婦匿之於酒甕，虎聞而殺之，取出雙子；蛙母命以棉束育之。一月而成人形；鳳冠鳥告以其母乃虎所殺；遂於高臺射虎，並誅老婦。

sensitivity.note: Carib oral tradition recorded 1915 (Roth); archival record, read critically.

passages.text: A long time ago there was a woman who had become pregnant by the Sun, with twin children, Pia and Makunaima. When she stumbled and hurt herself on the road she blamed her two unborn children as the cause; they became vexed and refused to tell her which road to follow, and thus it was that she took the wrong direction and arrived, foot-sore and weary, at a curious house belonging to Tiger's mother, Kono(bo)-aru, the Rain-frog. The house-mistress took pity on her and hid her in the big cassiri jar, popping on the cover; but Tiger, sniffing up and down, peeped into the jar and discovered the frightened creature.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §35; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 很久以前，有一個女人因太陽而懷孕，懷了雙胞胎孩子，皮亞與馬庫奈馬。當她在路上絆倒受傷時，她責怪腹中兩個未出生的孩子是禍首；他們因此惱怒，不肯告訴她該走哪條路，於是她就走錯了方向，最後腳痛疲憊地來到一間奇特的屋子，那是老虎的母親、雨蛙科諾（波）阿魯的家。女主人憐憫她，把她藏進大卡西里罐裡，蓋上蓋子；但老虎上下嗅聞，往罐裡一瞧，發現了這個驚恐的婦人。

passages.text: On killing the poor woman, Tiger found the two as-yet-unborn children, and his mother said he must now mind and cherish them; so he put them in a bundle of cotton to keep them warm, and they crept next day, grew fast, and reached man's size in about a month. Tiger's mother told them to go and shoot the Powis because it was this bird which had killed their own mother. Day after day they shot Powis, until the last bird told them it was none of his tribe but Tiger himself who had killed their mother. The boys went home empty-handed on the excuse that the Powis had taken their arrows — they had hidden the arrows to make new and stronger weapons — built a staging against a tree, shot and killed Tiger as he passed below, and reached home to slaughter his mother also.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §36; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 老虎殺了那可憐的婦人後，發現了兩個尚未出生的孩子，他的母親說他現在必須照料並愛護他們；於是他把他們放進一團棉花裡保暖，他們第二天便爬了出來，長得很快，大約一個月就長到了成人的體型。老虎的母親叫他們去射波維斯鳥，因為正是這種鳥殺了他們的親生母親。他們日復一日地射波維斯鳥，直到最後一隻鳥告訴他們，殺死他們母親的不是牠的族類，而是老虎本人。男孩們空手回家，藉口說波維斯鳥拿走了他們的箭——他們其實把箭藏了起來，要製作更新更強的武器——他們在一棵樹旁搭起高台，趁老虎從下方經過時射死了牠，然後回到家裡，把牠的母親也一併殺了。

title.en: The Frog's Cassava Shoulder and the Wrinkled Skin
title.zh: 蛙婦之肩粉與皺皮

region.en: Pomeroon district, Guyana (Carib)
region.zh: 蓋亞那波默龍加勒比之地

period: Carib oral tradition; recorded 1915 (Roth)

source.work: Walter E. Roth, An Inquiry into the Animism and Folk-lore of the Guiana Indians (33rd Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1915), ch. II 'Tribal Heroes', §§37

summary.en: Travelling on to meet their father the Sun, the twins lodged with a very old woman who was really a frog, in a house among cotton-trees. She always had cassava ready though no field was anywhere about; hiding behind a tree, the boys saw her bend down and pick at a white spot on her shoulders, and observed the cassava-starch fall. They teased out cotton as a soft bed for her; as soon as she sat upon it they set fire to it, scorching her skin so dreadfully as to give it the wrinkled and rough appearance it bears to this day.
summary.zh: 雙子途中宿於棉林間老婦之屋——實蛙也。其無田而常有薯餅；伏樹窺之，見其俯身肩上白斑，薯粉自落。二人採棉為褥，老婦喜而坐之；即縱火焚之，灼其皮，皺縮之狀至今猶然。

sensitivity.note: Carib oral tradition recorded 1915 (Roth); archival record, read critically.

passages.text: Pia and Makunaima proceeded on their way and arrived at last at a clump of cotton-trees in the center of which was a house occupied by a very old woman, really a frog, with whom they took up their quarters. They went out hunting each day and on their return invariably found some cassava their hostess had baked. 'That's very strange,' remarked Pia to his brother, 'there is no field anywhere about, and yet look at the quantity of cassava. We must watch her.' Next morning they hid themselves behind a tree whence they could see everything that took place at the house.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §37; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 皮亞與馬庫奈馬繼續趕路，最後來到一叢木棉樹，樹叢中央有一間屋子，住著一個非常老的女人，她其實是一隻青蛙，他們便在她那裡住下。他們每天外出打獵，回來時總會發現女主人烤好了些木薯。皮亞對弟弟說：「這太奇怪了，附近根本沒有田地，可你看看這木薯的數量。我們得留意她。」第二天早晨，他們躲在樹後，從那裡可以看見屋裡發生的一切。

passages.text: They noticed that the old frog had a white spot on her shoulders; they saw her bend down and pick at this spot, and observed the cassava-starch fall. On their return home they refused to eat the usual cake, having now discovered its source. Next morning they picked cotton from the neighboring trees and teased it out on the floor, telling her it was something nice and soft for her to lie upon. Much pleased, she promptly sat upon it — and no sooner had she done so than the two lads set fire to it, scorching her skin so dreadfully as to give it the wrinkled and rough appearance it bears to this day.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §37; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們注意到老青蛙肩上有一個白點；他們看見她彎下腰去摳這個白點，並觀察到木薯澱粉掉落下來。他們回家後拒絕吃平常的餅，因為此時已發現了它的來源。第二天早晨，他們從鄰近的樹上採來棉花，在地上把它揉鬆，告訴她這是又好又柔軟的東西，可以讓她躺臥。她大為高興，立刻坐了上去——她剛一坐下，兩個少年便點火燒它，把她的皮膚灼傷得極其嚴重，從此她的皮膚便成了如今這般滿是皺紋、粗糙的模樣。

title.en: The Tapir, the Severed Leg, and the Stars
title.zh: 貘、斷腿與眾星

region.en: Pomeroon district, Guyana (Carib)
region.zh: 蓋亞那波默龍加勒比之地

period: Carib oral tradition; recorded 1915 (Roth)

source.work: Walter E. Roth, An Inquiry into the Animism and Folk-lore of the Guiana Indians (33rd Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1915), ch. II 'Tribal Heroes', §38

summary.en: On their way to meet their father the twins spent three days with a Maipuri (tapir) woman, sleek and fat when she returned each evening. Following her tracks to a plum-tree, they shook it so violently that all the fruit, ripe and unripe, fell and lay wasted; the furious tapir beat both boys and fled into the bush. They pursued her for many a long day; Pia told Makunaima to wheel in front and drive her back, but as she passed the harpoon-arrow flew and the rope cut his leg off. On a clear night you can still see them among the clouds: Maipuri the Hyades, Makunaima the Pleiades, and below, his severed leg — Orion's Belt.
summary.zh: 雙子宿貘婦之家三日，見其晚歲肥潤；尋跡至李樹，搖之使果盡落，貘怒而遁。追之累日；皮亞令馬庫納伊瑪迎頭驅之，魚叉疾發，繩索斷其腿。晴夜猶見雲間：貘乃畢宿、雙子乃昴宿、斷腿乃獵戶帶。

sensitivity.note: Carib oral tradition recorded 1915 (Roth); archival record, read critically.

passages.text: Pia and Makunaima next continued their travels to meet their father, and soon arrived at the house of a Maipuri (tapir), where they spent three days. On the third evening Maipuri returned, looking very sleek and fat. Wanting to know what she had been feeding on, the boys followed her tracks to a plum-tree; this they shook and shook so violently as to make all the fruit, both ripe and unripe, fall to the ground, where it lay wasted. When Maipuri went to feed next morning she was disgusted to see her food thus destroyed, and in a very angry mood quickly returned home, beat both boys, and cleared out into the bush.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §38; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 皮亞與馬庫奈馬接著繼續旅行，去見他們的父親，不久便來到一隻邁普里（貘）的家，在那裡待了三天。第三天傍晚，邁普里回來了，看上去油光水滑、肥肥胖胖。男孩們想知道她吃了什麼，便循著她的足跡來到一棵李子樹；他們使勁搖啊搖，把樹上所有果實，無論熟的還是未熟的，都搖落到地上，任其糟蹋。第二天早晨邁普里前去進食時，看到自己的食物被這樣毀掉，十分厭惡，怒氣沖沖地迅速回家，打了兩個男孩一頓，然後衝進灌木叢裡去了。

passages.text: The boys started in pursuit, tracked her for many a long day, and at last caught up with her. Pia told Makunaima to wheel round in front and drive the creature back to him, and as she passed he let fly a harpoon-arrow; the rope, however, got in the way of Makunaima as he passed in front, and cut his leg off. On a clear night you can still see them up among the clouds: there is Maipuri (Hyades), there Makunaima (Pleiades), and below is his severed leg (Orion's Belt).
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §38; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 男孩們開始追趕，循著她的蹤跡追了許多漫長的日子，最後終於追上了她。皮亞叫馬庫奈馬繞到前面，把那隻獵物趕回他這邊來，當她經過時，他放出一支魚叉箭；然而繩子卻在馬庫奈馬經過前方時纏住了他，把他的腿割斷了。在晴朗的夜晚，你仍能看見他們高懸在雲間：那是邁普里（畢宿星團），那是馬庫奈馬（昴宿星團），下方則是他被割斷的腿（獵戶座腰帶）。

title.en: Alligator's Carved Daughter and the Woodpecker
title.zh: 鱷之雕女與啄木鳥

region.en: Roraima savanna (Makusi)
region.zh: 羅賴馬草原馬庫希之地

period: Makusi oral tradition; recorded 1915 (Roth, after Dance)

source.work: Walter E. Roth, An Inquiry into the Animism and Folk-lore of the Guiana Indians (33rd Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1915), ch. II 'Tribal Heroes', §39

summary.en: The Sun's fish-ponds were constantly robbed; Yamimi the water-lizard failed as watchman, and Alligator — the real thief — was detected and slashed with a cutlass, every cut forming a scale. To propitiate the Sun he offered a beautiful daughter he did not have, so he sculptured her from a wild plum tree and exposed her to the Sun's influence; fearing detection he hid in the water peering up, which he has done ever since. The woman was imperfectly formed, but a woodpecker pecked her body into perfection. The Sun deserted her, and grieving, she set out to seek him.
summary.zh: 日神魚池屢遭竊；水蜥守而不力，鱷乃真賊，被斬，每創成鱗。求贖，謂有美女——實無；遂刻李木為女，曝於日光。畏露而行藏於水，昂首窺日，至今如此。其體未完，啄木鳥啄之乃成。日神棄之；婦悲而尋夫。

sensitivity.note: Makusi oral tradition recorded 1915 (Roth); archival record, read critically.

passages.text: The Sun, finding his fish-ponds too frequently robbed, set Yamimi, the water-lizard, to watch them. Yamuru was not sufficiently vigilant, so Alligator was appointed watchman. Alligator, the depredator, continued his old trade while employed as a watchman, and at last was detected by the Sun, who slashed him with a cutlass within an inch of his life, every cut forming a scale. Alligator begged piteously for his life, and to propitiate the Sun offered him his beautiful daughter in marriage. But he had no daughter.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §39; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 太陽發現自己的魚池屢遭偷竊，便派水蜥蜴亞米米前去看守。亞米米不夠警覺，於是鱷魚被指派為看守者。鱷魚本是偷魚的賊，擔任看守時仍舊重操舊業，最後被太陽察覺；太陽用彎刀砍他，砍得他只剩一口氣，每一道刀痕都化成一片鱗甲。鱷魚苦苦哀求饒命，為了討好太陽，便獻上自己美麗的女兒與他成婚。但他根本沒有女兒。

passages.text: He therefore sculptured the form of a woman from a wild plum tree, exposed her to the Sun's influence, and — fearing ultimate detection of the fraud — hid himself in the water, peering at the Sun; and this habit Alligator has continued to the present time. The woman was imperfectly formed, but a woodpecker, in quest of food, pecked at her body and prepared her. The Sun left her, and she, grieving for his desertion, said that she would seek him — and so came at last to old Mother Toad's house, where she died from the poisonous head-lice, leaving the two unborn children who were to become the twin Heroes.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §39; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是，他用一棵野李樹雕出一個女子的形貌，將她置於太陽的影響之下；又怕這騙局終究會被識破，便躲進水裡，窺視著太陽——鱷魚至今仍保持著這個習性。那女子形貌並不完整，一隻啄木鳥尋食時啄了她的身體，將她修整成形。太陽離棄了她，她因他的拋棄而悲傷，說要去尋他——於是終於來到老蟾蜍婆婆的家，卻因頭蝨的毒而死，留下兩個尚未出生的孩子，他們後來成為那對雙生英雄。

title.en: Crane and the Making of Fire; the First Canoe
title.zh: 鶴教取火與首舟

region.en: Roraima savanna (Makusi)
region.zh: 羅賴馬草原馬庫希之地

period: Makusi oral tradition; recorded 1915 (Roth, after Dance)

source.work: Walter E. Roth, An Inquiry into the Animism and Folk-lore of the Guiana Indians (33rd Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1915), ch. II 'Tribal Heroes', §40

summary.en: Pia slew Tiger and took from the carcass the parts of his mother's body, and she became whole and alive. But Makunaima ate live coals, and the toad remonstrated in anger. Makunaima dug a great canal and made a corial — the first of its kind — persuading his mother and Pia to travel with him. From Crane, who struck his bill against a flint so that the friction produced fire, the brothers learned the art of fire-making. They placed huge rocks in all the rivers to detain the fishes — and these rocks caused the great waterfalls. When Crane quarrelled with Pia and flew off with Makunaima to Spanish Guiana, the family was divided forever.
summary.zh: 皮亞誅虎，自其屍取母體之部，母復活。馬庫納伊瑪好吞火炭，蟾母勸之而怒。乃鑿巨渠，造首舟，攜母與兄同行。兄弟自鶴學取火：鶴喙擊石生火。置巨石於諸河以留魚——瀑布由此而生。鶴與皮亞爭，攜馬庫納伊瑪飛往西班牙圭亞那，一家遂散。

sensitivity.note: Makusi oral tradition recorded 1915 (Roth); archival record, read critically.

passages.text: Pia's first work was to slay Tiger and take out of his carcass the parts of the body of his mother, who became whole and alive. But Makunaima had an appetite for fire-eating, and invariably devoured the live coals. The toad remonstrated, and Makunaima in anger prepared to leave and to travel throughout the land. To attain his purpose he dug a large canal, into which flowed water; and having made a corial — the first of its kind — he persuaded his mother and Pia to go with him.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §40; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 皮亞的第一件功業，是殺死老虎，從牠的屍體中取出他母親身體的各個部分，使她得以完整並復活。但馬庫奈馬嗜食火焰，總是把燒紅的炭吞下肚。蟾蜍出言勸阻，馬庫奈馬一怒之下準備離去，遊歷全境。為達成目的，他挖了一條大運河，河水流入其中；又造了一艘獨木舟——此類舟船的第一艘——並說服母親與皮亞隨他同行。

passages.text: It was from Crane that the brothers learned the art of fire-making, when he struck his bill against a flint and the friction produced fire. The brothers placed huge rocks in all the rivers to detain the fishes: the rocks thus placed caused the great waterfalls. Crane was at first accustomed to catch his own fish, but finding Pia and Makunaima more successful fishermen after the rivers had been dammed, kept near to them and took away their fish. Pia consequently quarrelled with Crane, who, becoming angry, took up Makunaima — who had taken part with him against his brother — and flew away with him to Spanish Guiana.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §40; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 兩兄弟正是從鶴那裡學會了取火之術：鶴將喙擊向燧石，摩擦便生出火來。兩兄弟在各條河裡放置巨石以攔住魚群：這些巨石便造成了巨大的瀑布。鶴起初慣於自行捕魚，但見河流被攔截之後，皮亞與馬庫奈馬捕魚更為豐收，便緊隨他們，把他們的魚奪走。皮亞因此與鶴爭吵，鶴一怒之下，帶上曾站在他這邊與兄長作對的馬庫奈馬，一同飛往西屬圭亞那。

title.en: Pia on Roraima: the Mother's Tears Become Streams
title.zh: 皮亞居羅賴馬：母淚成川

region.en: Mount Roraima, Guyana-Brazil-Venezuela border (Makusi)
region.zh: 圭亞那-巴西-委內瑞拉交界羅賴馬山（馬庫希）

period: Makusi oral tradition; recorded 1915 (Roth, after Dance)

source.work: Walter E. Roth, An Inquiry into the Animism and Folk-lore of the Guiana Indians (33rd Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1915), ch. II 'Tribal Heroes', §§41-42

summary.en: Deserted with his mother, Pia abandoned the hunt and traveled from place to place teaching the Indians many useful and good things — by him and his teachings we have the piai men. He bore his weary mother to the heights of Roraima to be her abiding place of rest. When his time of departure arrived he told her that whatever of good she desired she would obtain if she bowed her head and covered her face with her hands while expressing her wish. Whenever the mother of the twin heroes is sorrowful, a storm rises on the mountain, and it is her tears that run down in streams from the heights of Roraima.
summary.zh: 皮亞與母被棄，乃棄獵而遍行教人善事——醫師之職由之而起。攜疲母登羅賴馬山而安之。臨別囑其俯首掩面而祈，所願必得。雙子之母每悲，山即起風暴；羅賴馬之川，皆其淚也。

sensitivity.note: Makusi oral tradition recorded 1915 (Roth); archival record, read critically.

passages.text: Pia and his mother, thus deserted, continued their daily employment of traveling together, fishing, and seeking fruits. At last one day the mother complained of weariness, and Pia conveyed her to the heights of Roraima, these to be her abiding place of rest. Then came a change of occupation for Pia: he abandoned the hunt as the principal occupation of his life, and traveled from place to place, teaching the Indians many useful and good things. By him and his teachings we have the piai men.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §41; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 皮亞與母親就這樣被遺棄，仍繼續每日結伴同行、捕魚、尋覓果實。終於有一天，母親抱怨疲憊，皮亞便將她送到羅賴馬山的高處，那裡成了她安歇的居所。此後皮亞的職分有了轉變：他不再以狩獵為畢生主要之事，而是四處遊歷，教導印第安人許多有益而美好的事物。多虧他與他的教誨，我們才有了皮艾伊祭司。

passages.text: When his time of departure from her had arrived, he told her that whatever of good she desired she would obtain if she would bow her head and cover her face with her hands while she expressed her wish. This she does in her need to the present hour. Whenever the mother of these two heroes of our race is sorrowful, there arises a storm on the mountain, and it is her tears that run down in streams from the heights of Roraima. On Mount Zabang, the Olympus of the Makusis, dwells their great Spirit Makunaima.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §41-42; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他離她而去的時刻到來，他告訴她：只要她低頭以雙手掩面，同時說出自己的願望，無論她想要什麼好處，都能如願。她至今每逢需要，仍如此行事。我們這民族這兩位英雄的母親，每當悲傷，山上便興起風暴，正是她的淚水從羅賴馬山的高處奔流而下。在馬庫西人的奧林帕斯——扎邦山上，居住著他們偉大的神靈馬庫奈馬。

title.en: Amalivaca and Vochi Carve the Orinoco
title.zh: 阿馬利瓦卡與沃希鑿奧里諾科

region.en: Orinoco cataracts region, Venezuela (Tamanac/Carib)
region.zh: 委內瑞拉奧里諾科灘區塔馬納克之地

period: Tamanac tradition recorded by Humboldt; summarized 1915 (Roth)

source.work: Walter E. Roth, An Inquiry into the Animism and Folk-lore of the Guiana Indians (33rd Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1915), ch. II 'Tribal Heroes', §43

summary.en: Amalivaca, venerated by the Caribs and especially the Tamanacs, arrived in a bark during the subsidence of the great waters, and carved the sculptures still seen high on the perpendicular rock faces that border the great rivers. With his brother Vochi he created the world, and while making the Orinoco the two held a long consultation about making the stream flow up and down at one and the same time, to ease the paddlers. Fond of gadding, his daughters were condemned by him to sedentary life — their legs broken to force them to people the land of the Tamanacs. His stone house may still be seen on the plains of Maita, with a great stone beside it said to be 'the drum of Amalivaca'.
summary.zh: 阿馬利瓦卡於大水退時乘舟而至，鑿巨石為紋，至今猶存。與弟沃希共造世界；鑿奧里諾科河時，欲使水上下同流以利舟人。其女好遊，遂折其足使居塔馬納克之地而繁衍。邁塔平原猶見其石屋，旁有大石，號『阿馬利瓦卡之鼓』。

sensitivity.note: Tamanac tradition recorded by Humboldt and summarized in Roth 1915; archival record, read critically.

passages.text: Amalivaca, venerated by the Caribs and more especially by the Tamanacs, is said to have arrived in a bark during the subsidence of the great waters, and to have carved the sculptures now seen high on the perpendicular faces of the rocks which border the great rivers. He has a brother, Vochi; together they created the world. While making the Orinoco they had a long consultation about causing the stream to flow up and down at one and the same time, so as to ease the paddlers as much as possible.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §43 (from Humboldt); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 據說，阿馬利瓦卡（Amalivaca）深受加勒比人敬奉，尤其是塔馬納克人；相傳他在大洪水退落之時乘一葉樹皮舟抵達，並雕刻了如今可見於大河兩岸陡直岩壁高處的種種石雕。他有一位兄弟沃奇（Vochi）；二人一同創造了世界。在造奧里諾科河時，他們曾長久商議，欲使河水同時向上與向下流動，以便盡可能減輕划槳者的辛勞。

passages.text: Amalivaca had daughters who were very fond of gadding about, so he broke their legs to render them sedentary and force them to people the land of the Tamanacs. He also made the earth sufficiently level for people to dwell on, and he seems to have known music. His house, consisting of blocks of stone piled one on another and forming a sort of cavern, may still be seen on the plains of Maita; and near it is a large stone which the Indians say was an instrument of music — 'the drum of Amalivaca'.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Roth 1915, §43 (from Humboldt); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿馬利瓦卡有幾個女兒，她們極愛四處遊蕩，於是他打斷了她們的腿，使她們安坐不動，並迫使她們繁衍塔馬納克人之地。他又把大地弄得足夠平坦，以供人居住，而且他似乎還通曉音樂。他的居所由一塊塊石頭堆疊而成，形成一種洞穴，至今仍可在邁塔平原上見到；居所附近有一塊大石，印第安人說那是件樂器——「阿馬利瓦卡的鼓」。

title.en: The Earth Itself Danced: Huathiacuri Wins Every Contest
title.zh: 大地也隨之起舞:瓜提亞庫里連勝諸賽

region.en: Anchicocha (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 安奇科查(象徵性標記)

period: Huarochiri manuscript collected by Francisco de Avila, 1608; publ. Markham 1873

source.work: Francisco de Avila, 'A Narrative of the Errors, False Gods and other Superstitions... of Huarochiri, Mama and Chaclla', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: The rich brother-in-law, angry that the girl had been given to the ragged Huathiacuri, challenged him to contests. For drinking and dancing, Pariacaca turned himself into a dead huanacu on the road: a fox with its vixen came playing a flute of many pipes and carrying a jar of chicha, put down their burden to eat the huanacu, and fled when it revived with a great cry - so Huathiacuri carried off the jug, the drum and the flute. Entering the feast with his wife, at the first sound of her drum the whole earth began to shake as if keeping time to the music: 'not only the people but the earth itself danced'. He drank all they gave him without a sign of satiety, then poured round after round from the fox's jug, from which the chicha never failed, each drinker falling drunk in turn. For the next challenge Pariacaca dressed him in a shirt of snow; for the lion-skin contest he found a red lion-skin at a fountain, with a rainbow round the lion's head; and for the house-building contest, while the rich man's vassals laboured, in perfect silence an infinite number of birds, snakes and lizards completed Huathiacuri's house in the night. Next day, when llamas brought straw for the rival's roof, Huathiacuri stationed an oscollo (a wild cat) that shrieked so as to terrify the llamas into shaking off their loads.
summary.zh: 闊綽的內兄見妹子竟許配給衣衫襤褸的瓜提亞庫里,怒而設賽。先賽飲與舞:帕里亞卡卡化作道旁死駝馬;一對狐狸攜奇恰酒罐、吹多管竹笛而來,見死駝馬便放下酒罐鼓笛大嚼;駝馬忽醒,大吼一聲,狐狸倉皇逃竄——瓜提亞庫里遂得酒罐、鼓與笛。他攜妻赴宴,其妻鼓聲一響,大地竟隨節拍震動:「不但人們在跳舞,連大地也在跳舞。」闊佬灌他多少,他便喝多少,面不改色;再以狐罐斟酒回敬,罐中之酒永不見底,接連醉倒一片。次賽盛裝:其父帕里亞卡卡賜他一件「雪織之衫」。三賽獅皮:泉邊得赤色獅皮,獅首環繞彩虹。四賽築屋:闊佬奴僕雲集,一日將成;而瓜提亞庫里夜間得無數飛鳥、蛇、蜥蜴悄然協力,天亮屋成,觀者莫不驚異。翌日駝馬為對手馱草蓋頂,他遣一隻尖嘯的「奧斯科略」(野貓)埋伏途中,駝馬驚得拋棄草束,功虧一簣。

sensitivity.note: Contest cycle between the poor son of Pariacaca and the rich pretender; the dancing-earth and never-failing jug are classic trickster wonders.

passages.text: So Huathiacuri accepted the challenge, and posted off to his father Pariacaca, who told him to go to a neighbouring mountain, where he would turn into a dead huanacu. Next morning a fox with its vixen would come to the place, bringing a jar of chicha on her back, while the fox would have a flute of many pipes called astara... when they should see the dead huanacu on the road, they would not wish to lose the opportunity of filling their stomachs; and that they would put down the chicha, the drum, and the flute, and would begin to eat; that then he would come to himself and return to his own shape, and begin to cry aloud, at which the foxes would take to flight... and that he would then take the things they had left behind, and might be sure of victory in the challenge with his brother-in-law.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 5 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是瓦蒂亞庫里（Huathiacuri）接受了挑戰，急忙趕去見他的父親帕里亞卡卡（Pariacaca）；父親叫他前往鄰近的一座山，他會在那裡變成一頭死去的羊駝。翌日清晨，一隻公狐帶著母狐會來到該處，母狐背上馱著一罐奇恰酒，公狐則帶著一支名為阿斯塔拉（astara）的多管笛……當牠們看見路上的死羊駝時，便不願錯過填飽肚子的機會；牠們會放下奇恰酒、鼓和笛子，開始進食；這時他便會恢復知覺，變回原形，並開始大聲呼喊，狐狸們聞聲便會逃之夭夭……然後他便會取走牠們留下的東西，如此一來，他與妻兄的這場較量必能穩操勝券。

passages.text: While this was going on Huathiacuri entered with his wife, dancing with her, and she charging his cup and playing on a drum. At the first sound of her drum the whole earth began to shake, as if it was keeping time to the music, so that they had the advantage of the rich man, for not only the people but the earth itself danced. Then he rose and began to drink to those who were seated, his wife filling the cups with chicha from the fox's jug. They laughed, because they thought that before he had given cups to two of them the jug would be empty; but the chicha never failed, and each man that drank fell down in a state of intoxication.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 5 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 正當這一切進行之際，瓦蒂亞庫里帶著妻子進來，與她一同起舞，她為他斟滿酒杯，並敲擊鼓。她的鼓聲一響，整個大地便開始震動，彷彿隨著音樂打拍子，於是他們比那富人佔了上風，因為不僅是人們，連大地本身也起舞了。接著他起身，開始向在座的人敬酒，他的妻子則從狐狸的酒罐裡斟出奇恰酒注滿酒杯。眾人笑了，因為他們以為他還沒向其中兩人敬完酒，酒罐便會空了；然而奇恰酒始終不竭，每個飲酒的人都酩酊大醉，倒地不起。

passages.text: Huathiacuri accepted this challenge also, and went for help to his father Pariacaca, who dressed him in a shirt of snow, and so he vanquished his brother-in-law once more. Then the brother-in-law challenged him once more, saying that people should now see who could enter the public square with the best lion-skin on his shoulders, for dancing. Huathiacuri went again to his father Pariacaca, who sent him to a fountain, where he said he would find a red lion-skin; and when he entered the square, men saw that there was a rainbow round the lion's head; so Huathiacuri again obtained a victory.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 5 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 瓦蒂亞庫里也接受了這項挑戰，前去向他的父親帕里亞卡卡求助；父親給他穿上一件雪做的襯衫，於是他再一次戰勝了妻兄。接著妻兄又向他挑戰，說現在該讓大家看看，誰能披著最好的獅皮進入公共廣場跳舞。瓦蒂亞庫里又去見他的父親帕里亞卡卡，父親派他前往一處泉水，說他會在那裡找到一張紅色的獅皮；當他進入廣場時，眾人看見那獅子頭上環繞著一道彩虹；於是瓦蒂亞庫里再度獲勝。

passages.text: The rich man at once began to collect his numerous vassals, and in one day he had nearly finished the walls, while Huathiacuri, with only his wife to help him, had scarcely begun the foundations. During the night the work of the rich man was stopped, but not that of Huathiacuri: for, in perfect silence, an infinite number of birds, snakes, and lizards completed the work, so that in the morning the house was finished, and the rich man was vanquished, to the great wonder of all beholders. Then a great multitude of huanacus and vicuñas came next day laden with straw for the roof... But Huathiacuri ordered an animal that shrieks loudly, called oscollo, to station itself at a certain point; and it suddenly began to scream in such a way as to terrify the llamas, which shook off their loads, and all the straw was lost.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 5 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那富人立刻開始召集他眾多的臣屬，一天之內便幾乎築好了牆，而瓦蒂亞庫里只有妻子相助，連地基都幾乎還沒開始。夜間，富人的工程停了下來，瓦蒂亞庫里的工程卻沒有停：因為在完全的寂靜中，無數的鳥、蛇和蜥蜴完成了這項工程，所以到了早晨，房屋已然建成，富人就此敗北，令所有旁觀者大為驚嘆。接著，翌日一大群羊駝和駱馬馱著蓋屋頂用的茅草而來……但瓦蒂亞庫里命令一隻名叫奧斯科約（oscollo）、叫聲響亮的動物駐守在某處；牠突然尖叫起來，把駱馬嚇得甩掉了背上的貨物，所有的茅草都丟失了。

language: Spanish record of a Quechua tradition
canonical_translation: C. R. Markham, Narrative of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas (Hakluyt Society, 1873)

title.en: The Stag That Ate People and the Stone with Her Feet in the Air
title.zh: 食人之鹿與頭足倒置之石

region.en: Anchicocha (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 安奇科查(象徵性標記)

period: Huarochiri manuscript collected by Francisco de Avila, 1608; publ. Markham 1873

source.work: Francisco de Avila, 'A Narrative of the Errors, False Gods and other Superstitions... of Huarochiri, Mama and Chaclla', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: At the end of the competition Huathiacuri proposed a last challenge: who danced best in a blue shirt with a white cotton huara round the loins. The rich man appeared first in the proposed dress; then Huathiacuri, with a sudden shout, ran into the place where the other was dancing, and he, alarmed at the cry and the sudden rush, began to run - to give him more speed he turned, or was turned by Huathiacuri, into a deer. In this form he came to Anchicocha, where, when his wife saw it, she also rose up saying, 'Why do I remain here? I must go after my husband and die with him.' So she began to run after him, and Huathiacuri after both. At last Huathiacuri overtook the wife in Anchicocha, and said to her: 'Traitress! it is by your advice that your husband has challenged me to so many proofs... Now I will pay you for this by turning you into a stone, with your head on the ground and your feet in the air.' This happened as he said, and the stone is there to this day; the Indians go there to worship and to offer coca. Thus the woman was stopped; but the deer ran on and disappeared, and it maintained itself by eating people; but after some time the deer began to be eaten by men, and not men by deer.
summary.zh: 賽事之末,瓜提亞庫里提議最後一比:著藍衫、繫白棉腰布,看誰舞得最好。闊佬先著此服登場;瓜提亞庫里忽發一聲大喊,直衝其舞處。闊佬驚駭奔逃——為求其速,他自己、或說被瓜提亞庫里——化作一隻鹿。鹿逃至安奇科查,其妻望見,也起身說:「我留在此地作甚?我要追隨丈夫,與他同死!」拔腿便追,瓜提亞庫里隨後緊趕。終於在安奇科查追上其妻,喝道:「叛婦!是你唆使丈夫屢屢向我挑戰,百般試我耐性。今日便叫你變作一塊石頭:頭朝下,腳朝天!」言畢果然如此,那石至今猶在;印第安人常往拜祭,獻上古柯。婦人就此止步;而鹿繼續奔逃,從此絕跡,據說它曾以人為食;但不久之後,鹿反為人所獵,人不再是鹿的食物。

sensitivity.note: Punishment-transformations closing the contest cycle; the head-down stone is a named huaca of Anchicocha.

passages.text: He said to the rich man, 'Brother, now you have seen that I have agreed to everything that you have proposed. It is reasonable, therefore, that you should now do the same; and I propose that we should both see who dances best, in a blue shirt with a white cotton huara round the loins.' The rich man accepted the challenge, and, as usual, was the first to appear in the public square, in the proposed dress. Presently Huathiacuri also appeared, and, with a sudden shout, he ran into the place where the other was dancing; and he, alarmed at the cry and the sudden rush, began to run, insomuch as, to give him more speed, he turned, or was turned by Huathiacuri, into a deer.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 5 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他對那富人說：「兄弟，如今你已看見，凡你所提議的，我都一一應允了。因此，如今你也理當照樣而行；我提議我們二人比試一番，看誰舞得最好，身穿藍色襯衫，腰間圍著白色棉製的瓦拉。」那富人接受了這挑戰，並且一如往常，頭一個穿著所議定的服飾出現在公共廣場上。不久，瓦蒂亞庫里也出現了，他忽然大喊一聲，衝進那人正在跳舞的地方；那人被這喊聲與突如其來的衝撞所驚，便開始奔逃，為了讓他跑得更快，他竟變成了一頭鹿，或說是被瓦蒂亞庫里變成了一頭鹿。

passages.text: In this form he came to Anchicocha, where, when his wife saw it, she also rose up saying, 'Why do I remain here? I must go after my husband and die with him.' So she began to run after him, and Huathiacuri after both. At last Huathiacuri overtook the wife in Anchicocha, and said to her, 'Traitress! it is by your advice that your husband has challenged me to so many proofs, and has tried my patience in so many ways. Now I will pay you for this by turning you into a stone, with your head on the ground and your feet in the air.' This happened as he said, and the stone is there to this day; and the Indians go there to worship and to offer coca... Thus the woman was stopped; but the deer ran on and disappeared, and it maintained itself by eating people; but after some time the deer began to be eaten by men, and not men by deer.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 5 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他以此形態來到安奇科查，他的妻子見了，也起身說道：「我為何還留在這裡？我必須去追我的丈夫，與他同死。」於是她也開始追趕他，瓦蒂亞庫里則在二人之後追趕。最後，瓦蒂亞庫里在安奇科查追上了那妻子，對她說：「你這叛徒！正是聽了你的主意，你的丈夫才向我提出這麼多考驗，用種種方法試探我的耐性。如今我要報應你，把你變成一塊石頭，頭朝地，腳朝天。」事情果然如他所說發生了，那石頭至今仍在那裡；印第安人常到那裡禮拜並獻上古柯……那婦人就此被攔住了；但那鹿卻繼續奔逃，消失無蹤，牠靠吃人維生；但過了些時候，那鹿反倒開始被人吃，而不是人吃鹿了。

language: Spanish record of a Quechua tradition
canonical_translation: C. R. Markham, Narrative of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas (Hakluyt Society, 1873)

title.en: Five Falcons, and the Flood That Took the False God to the Sea
title.zh: 五隼與洪水:假神葬身大海

region.en: Between Vicocha and Llantapa, river of Pachacamac (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 維科查與蘭塔帕之間、帕查卡馬克河畔(象徵性標記)

period: Huarochiri manuscript collected by Francisco de Avila, 1608; publ. Markham 1873

source.work: Francisco de Avila, 'A Narrative of the Errors, False Gods and other Superstitions... of Huarochiri, Mama and Chaclla', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: The five eggs in Condorcoto opened, and five falcons issued from them, who were presently turned into five men, who went about performing wonderful miracles. One was that the rich Indian who had pretended to be God perished: Pariacaca and the others raised a great storm and a flood which carried him and his house and wife and family away into the sea. The site of this man's house is between two very lofty mountains, the one called Vicocha, near the parish of Chorrillo, and the other Llantapa, in the parish of San Damian; and between them flows the river of Pachacamac. There was a sort of bridge, consisting of a great tree called pullao, forming a most beautiful arch from one hill to the other, where a great variety of parrots and other birds passed to and fro. All this was swept away by the flood.
summary.zh: 孔多爾科托的五枚蛋裂開,五隻隼破殼而出,頃刻化作五位男子,遍行世間,顯大神蹟。其一,便是那自稱為神的富人遭到了報應:帕里亞卡卡與諸兄弟興起狂風暴雨與洪水,把那富人連人帶宅、攜妻攜子,一併衝入大海。其宅舊址在兩座極高的山之間:一曰維科查,近喬里略教區;一曰蘭塔帕,在聖達米安教區;二山之間流著帕查卡馬克河。兩山之間曾橫著一株巨樹構成的「普利亞奧」天然拱橋,美不勝收,各色鸚鵡與飛鳥穿行其上。這一切都隨洪水而去。

sensitivity.note: The deluge that ends the false creator's reign; tagged flood for the deluge cluster.

passages.text: They say that those five eggs in Condorcoto, one of which contained Pariacaca, opened, and five falcons issued from them, who were presently turned into five men, who went about performing wonderful miracles; and one was that the rich Indian, whom we have mentioned as having pretended to be God, perished, because Pariacaca and the others raised a great storm and a flood which carried him and his house and wife and family away into the sea.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 5 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們說，孔多爾科托的那五顆蛋——其中一顆孕育著帕里亞卡卡——裂開了，從中飛出五隻隼，隨即化為五個人，四處施行奇蹟；其中一件便是：我們曾提到的那個自稱是神的富有印第安人滅亡了，因為帕里亞卡卡與其餘幾人掀起了一場大風暴與洪水，把他連同他的房屋、妻子和家人一併沖入海中。

passages.text: The site of this man's house is between two very lofty mountains, the one called Vicocha, near the parish of Chorrillo, and the other Llantapa, in the parish of San Damian, and between them flows the river of Pachacamac. There was a sort of bridge, consisting of a great tree called pullao, forming a most beautiful arch from one hill to the other, where a great variety of parrots and other birds passed to and fro. All this was swept away by the flood.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 5 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這人房屋的舊址位於兩座極高的山之間，一座名叫維科查，靠近喬里略教區，另一座名叫良塔帕，位於聖達米安教區，兩山之間流淌著帕查卡馬克河。那裡曾有一座橋，由一棵名叫普堯的大樹構成，從一座山到另一座山形成一道極美的拱形，各種鸚鵡和其他鳥兒往來其間。這一切都被洪水沖走了。

language: Spanish record of a Quechua tradition
canonical_translation: C. R. Markham, Narrative of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas (Hakluyt Society, 1873)

title.en: The Cup That Saved a Village: Rain, Hail and White Stones on Huarochiri
title.zh: 一觴之恩:瓦羅奇里的雨雹飛石之災

region.en: Matro-coto peak above Huarochiri (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 瓦羅奇里上方馬特羅-科托峰(象徵性標記)

period: Huarochiri manuscript collected by Francisco de Avila, 1608; publ. Markham 1873

source.work: Francisco de Avila, 'A Narrative of the Errors, False Gods and other Superstitions... of Huarochiri, Mama and Chaclla', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: On his way from Condorcoto to the residence of Caruyuchu Huayallo, Pariacaca came to the village of Huagaihusa, at the bottom of the ravine where the river flows, where they were celebrating a great festival. He entered in the dress of a poor man and sat down at the end of all, as is the custom with those who are not invited; but no man drank to him nor gave him drink during the whole day. Seeing this, a girl was moved with pity, saying: 'How is it that no one gives a drink to this poor man?' and she put a good draught of chicha into one of those large white calabashes called putu, and took it to Pariacaca, who received it with thanks and told her she had gained his friendship. 'This is worth to you the same as your life, for at the end of five days wonderful things will happen in this place, and none of the inhabitants shall remain alive, for their neglect has enraged me. You must put yourself in safety on that day, with your children... but if you reveal this secret to any other inhabitant of the village, your death is also inevitable.' On the fifth day she went far away with her children, brothers and relations; the rest were still drinking and feasting when the enraged Pariacaca ascended the high mountain called Matro-coto which overhangs the village, below which there is another peak called Puipu-Huana. Then an enormous quantity of rain began to fall, with hail and yellow and white stones, which carried the village away into the sea, so that no man escaped. This flood is still a tradition among the people of Huarochiri, and some high banks were left which may be seen before arriving at the village.
summary.zh: 帕里亞卡卡自孔多爾科托前往卡魯尤丘-瓦亞約住地途中,來到溝底瓦加伊瓦薩村——其時村民正大設酒宴。他作窮人裝束入村,按不速之客之禮坐於末席;然而終日無人向他敬酒。一位姑娘心生憐憫:「怎麼沒人給這窮人斟酒?」便取白色大葫蘆「普圖」盛滿奇恰酒奉上。帕里亞卡卡受而謝之,說她已贏得他的友誼:「這一觴抵得上你的性命。五日之後,此地將有大變,居民無一得活——他們的怠慢激怒了我。到那天,你要帶著孩子自尋生路……但若將此秘洩與村中任何人,你的死期也一樣難逃。」第五日,她攜子女兄弟親戚遠走他鄉;村中其餘人仍沉酣宴飲。盛怒的帕里亞卡卡登上俯臨村莊的高峰馬特羅-科托(其下另有一峰名普伊普-瓜納),霎時大雨傾盆,冰雹與黃白飛石俱下,將全村捲入大海,無一人得免。此災至今仍是瓦羅奇里人的傳說;村前尚餘幾道高岸,即當年洪水之遺。

sensitivity.note: Hospitality-reward flood tale; the single cup motif parallels Sodom-type visitor tests.

passages.text: On his way from Condorcoto to the residence of Caruyuchu, he came to the place where now stands the village of Santa Maria de Jesus de Huarochiri... Here there was a village called Huagaihusa, where they were celebrating a great festival. Pariacaca entered the place, where all the people were drinking, in the dress of a poor man, and he sat down with the others, but at the end of all, as is the custom with those who are not invited. But no man drank to him nor gave him to drink during the whole day.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 6 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他從孔多爾科托前往卡魯尤丘的居所途中，來到了如今聖瑪利亞·德·赫蘇斯·德·瓦羅奇里村所在的地方……這裡曾有一個名叫瓦蓋烏薩的村子，人們正在那裡慶祝一個盛大的節日。帕里亞卡卡以窮人的裝扮進入那地方，那裡的人都在飲酒，他便與眾人一同坐下，但坐在最末的位置，正如那些未受邀請者的習俗一般。然而整整一天，沒有人向他敬酒，也沒有人給他酒喝。

passages.text: Seeing this, a girl was moved with pity and compassion, and she said, 'How is it that no one gives a drink to this poor man or takes any notice of him?' and she put a good draught of chicha into one of those large white calabashes called by the Indians putu, and took it to Pariacaca, who received it with thanks, and told her she had done a very good deed, and had gained his friendship. 'This is worth to you the same as your life, for at the end of five days wonderful things will happen in this place, and none of the inhabitants shall remain alive, for their neglect has enraged me. You must put yourself in safety on that day, with your children... but if you reveal this secret to any other inhabitant of the village, your death is also inevitable.'
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 6 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 一個女孩見了，心生憐憫與同情，說道：「怎麼沒有人給這窮人一杯酒喝，也沒有人理會他呢？」她便把一大口奇恰酒倒進一個印第安人稱作普圖的大白葫蘆裡，拿去給帕里亞卡卡，他道謝著接過，告訴她她做了一件大好事，贏得了他的友誼。「這對你來說，價值等同於你的性命，因為五天之後，這地方將發生奇事，居民無一能存活，因為他們的怠慢激怒了我。那日你必須帶著你的孩子躲到安全之處……但如果你把這秘密洩露給村中任何其他居民，你的死也在所難免。」

passages.text: On the fifth day she took good care to go far away from the village with her children, brothers, and relations; leaving the rest of the inhabitants off their guard, and still engaged in drinking and feasting. But the enraged Pariacaca had ascended a high mountain called Matro-coto, which overhangs the village of Huarochiri. Then an enormous quantity of rain began to fall, with hail and yellow and white stones, which carried the village away into the sea, so that no man escaped. This flood is still a tradition among the people of Huarochiri, and some high banks were left, which may be seen before arriving at the village.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 6 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 到了第五天，她小心翼翼地帶著子女、兄弟與親族遠離村莊；讓其餘居民毫無防備，仍舊沉溺於飲酒作樂。然而，滿懷怒火的帕里亞卡卡已登上了一座名為馬特羅科托的高山，此山高懸於瓦羅奇里村之上。接著，天降巨量暴雨，夾雜著冰雹與黃石、白石，將整座村莊沖入海中，無一人得以逃脫。這場洪水至今仍是瓦羅奇里人的傳說，當地還留下了一些高岸，在抵達村莊之前便可見到。

language: Spanish record of a Quechua tradition
canonical_translation: C. R. Markham, Narrative of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas (Hakluyt Society, 1873)

title.en: Choque Suso at the Head of the Canal: Love, Water and a Fox Engineer
title.zh: 渠首的喬克-蘇索:愛、水與狐工程師

region.en: Ayllu Copara lands, above San Lorenzo de Quinti (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 聖洛倫索-德-金蒂上方科帕拉世系之地(象徵性標記)

period: Huarochiri manuscript collected by Francisco de Avila, 1608; publ. Markham 1873

source.work: Francisco de Avila, 'A Narrative of the Errors, False Gods and other Superstitions... of Huarochiri, Mama and Chaclla', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: Having crossed the river, Pariacaca travelled over the fields of the Ayllu Copara, which were in great want of water for irrigation. A very beautiful girl of that ayllu, seeing that the maize crop was drying up, began to weep at the small supply that came from the dam she had opened. Pariacaca, captivated by her charms, took off his yacolla or cloak and used it to stop up the drain she had made, then asked her in loving words why she wept. 'My father, I weep because this crop of maize will be lost for lack of water.' He replied that she had gained what he had lost - his love - and would make the dam yield more than enough. Choque-suso told him first to produce the water, and afterwards she would yield to his wishes: he opened the channel, such a quantity of water flowed out that it sufficed for the thirsty fields. He promised to conduct a channel from the river to irrigate all the farms, and ordered all the birds of the hills and trees to assemble, together with snakes, lizards, bears, lions and other animals, to remove the obstruction and widen the channel. The fox managed, by his cunning, to get the post of engineer, and carried the line of the canal to the spot just above the church of San Lorenzo; but a partridge came flying making a noise like Pich-pich, and the unconscious fox let the water flow off down the hill. The labourers were enraged, and ordered the snake to take the fox's place; but he did not perform the work so well, and the people to this day deplore that the fox should have been superseded - the broken course just above the church is the place where the fox let the water flow off, never since repaired. Having brought the water, Pariacaca besought the damsel to keep her promise; they went to the summit of rocks called Yanacaca, where he obtained his desires, and she was well repaid when she knew who he was. She would never let him go anywhere alone, and he took her to the head-works of the channel he had constructed for her love; there she felt a strong wish to remain, and she was converted into a stone, while Pariacaca went up the mountains. Thus Choque Suso was turned into a stone at the head of the channel, which is called Cocochalla. Above this channel there is another called Vim-lompa, where there is another stone, into which they say Coniraya was turned.
summary.zh: 帕里亞卡卡渡河之後,行經科帕拉世系的田畝——其時缺水甚急。田中有一極美的少女,眼見玉米將因缺水枯萎,對著自己開閘引來的涓涓細流哭泣。帕里亞卡卡為其姿色所動,脫下斗篷「亞科利亞」塞住她掘開的排水口,然後柔聲相問:「姑娘為何啼哭?」「父親,我哭這片玉米要旱死了。」他答道:「你已得到我失去的東西——我的愛。我必使閘中水足灌你的田。」喬克-蘇索卻道:先引水來,後允所請。他開閘放水,滔滔而下,旱田得潤。他又允諾開鑿一條大河渠道,灌溉全部田莊:召來山上林間所有的鳥,以及蛇、蜥蜴、熊、獅諸獸,移開阻水之壩,拓寬水道。狡狐以巧計謀得工程師之職,將渠線測至聖洛倫索教堂上方;不料一隻鷓鴣飛來,「畢!畢!」連聲啼叫,懵懂的狐狸竟讓水順坡流失。眾役大怒,改命蛇接替狐狸,但蛇做工程遠不如狐——至今人們猶為狐狸被撤而惋惜;教堂上方斷裂的渠線,便是狐狸放水的所在,從此無人修復。渠成之後,帕里亞卡卡求她履行前約;二人登上名為「亞納卡卡」(黑岩)的巖頂,他遂其所願,她亦知情後甘願相從。她寸步不離,他帶她到自己為愛而築的渠首;她便執意要留在此處——於是化作一塊石頭,帕里亞卡卡獨自上山而去。喬克-蘇索就此化為渠首之石,其地名「科科查利亞」。此渠之上另有一渠名「維姆-隆帕」,渠畔亦有一石,相傳是庫尼拉亞所化。

sensitivity.note: Irrigation-canal love myth; Choque Suso as canal-guardian stone matches the named huacas of the channel system still in use.

passages.text: Having crossed the river, Pariacaca travelled over the fields which now belong to the Ayllu Copara, and which then were in great want of water for irrigation. In those days there was a very beautiful girl belonging to the Ayllu Copara, who, seeing one day that the maize crop was drying up for want of water, began to weep at the small supply that came from one of the smaller dams she had opened. Pariacaca happened to be passing by, and, seeing her, he was captivated by her charms. He went to the dam, and taking off his yacolla or cloak, he used it to stop up the drain that the girl had made... and she, without knowing who he was, thus answered: 'My father, I weep because this crop of maize will be lost and is drying up for lack of water.'
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 7 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 渡過河後，帕里亞卡卡行經如今屬於科帕拉氏族（Ayllu Copara）的田野，當時這些田地極度缺乏灌溉用水。那時，科帕拉氏族中有一位非常美麗的少女，某天她見玉米作物因缺水而枯萎，又見她所開啟的一座較小水壩流出的水量稀少，便開始哭泣。帕里亞卡卡恰好路過，見到了她，被她的美貌所傾倒。他走到水壩旁，脫下他的亞科利亞（yacolla，即斗篷），用它堵住了少女所開的排水口……而她並不知他是何人，便如此答道：「父親啊，我哭泣是因為這片玉米作物將要毀於缺水而枯萎。」

passages.text: He replied that she might console herself, for that she had gained what he had lost, namely, his love; and that he would make the dam yield more than enough water to irrigate her crop. Choque-suso told him first to produce the water in abundance, and that afterwards she promised willingly to yield to his wishes. Then he went up to the dam, and, on opening the channel, such a quantity of water flowed out, that it sufficed to irrigate the thirsty fields... He examined the country, to see whence he could draw the water; and observed that above the site of the present village of San Lorenzo a very small rill came from the ravine of Cocachalla... By opening this dam and leading the water onwards, it appeared to Pariacaca that it would reach the farms of the Ayllu Copara.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 7 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他回答說，她可以寬心，因為她已得到了他所失去的，即他的愛；又說他會讓水壩流出遠超灌溉她作物所需的水量。喬克蘇索（Choque-suso）先要他讓水大量湧出，之後她承諾願意順從他的意願。於是他登上水壩，打開渠道，水量之大足以灌溉乾渴的田野……他察看地勢，尋找可引水之處；發現現今聖洛倫索村所在地之上方，有一條極小的溪流從科卡查利亞（Cocachalla）山谷流來……帕里亞卡卡認為，若打開這座水壩並將水引向前方，便可到達科帕拉氏族的農田。

passages.text: So he ordered all the birds in those hills and trees to assemble, together with all the snakes, lizards, bears, lions, and other animals; and to remove the obstruction. This they did; and he then caused them to widen the channel and to make new channels until the water reached the farms. There was a discussion as to who should make the line for the channel... But the fox managed, by his cunning, to get the post of engineer; and he carried the line of the canal to the spot just above the present site of the church of San Lorenzo. Then a partridge came flying and making a noise like Pich-pich, and the unconscious fox let the water flow off down the hill. So the other labourers were enraged, and ordered the snake to take the fox's place... but the people to this day deplore that the fox should have been superseded, saying that the channel would have been higher up and better if this had not taken place.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 7 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是，他命令那些山丘與樹木間的所有鳥類齊聚一堂，連同所有的蛇、蜥蜴、熊、獅子及其他動物；要牠們清除障礙。牠們照做了；接著他讓牠們拓寬渠道並開鑿新渠道，直到水流抵達農田。眾人爭論該由誰來勘定渠道的路線……但狐狸憑其狡詐，謀得了工程師之職；牠將運河的路線引至現今聖洛倫索教堂所在地正上方的位置。接著一隻鷓鴣飛來，發出「皮奇—皮奇」般的聲響，那隻毫無警覺的狐狸便讓水順著山坡流走了。於是其他勞工大為憤怒，命令蛇取代狐狸的位置……但人們至今仍惋惜狐狸竟被取代，說道：若非如此，渠道本會位於更高處，且更為完善。

passages.text: Having brought the water to irrigate the farms in the way that is still working, Pariacaca besought the damsel to keep her promise, and she consented with a good grace, but proposed that they should go to the summit of some rocks called Yanacaca. This they did, and there Pariacaca obtained his desires, and she was well repaid for her love when she knew who he was. She would never let him go anywhere alone... There she felt a strong wish to remain, and he again consented, so she was converted into a stone, while Pariacaca went up the mountains. Thus Choque Suso was turned into a stone at the head of the channel, which is called Cocochalla. Above this channel there is another called Vim-lompa, where there is another stone, into which they say Coniraya was turned.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Avila, Narrative of the Errors of Huarochiri, ch. 7 (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 帕里亞卡卡以至今仍運作的方式引水灌溉農田之後，便懇求那少女履行承諾，她欣然應允，但提議他們一同前往一處名為亞納卡卡（Yanacaca）的岩石之巔。他們照做了，帕里亞卡卡在那裡得償所願；而當她得知他是何人後，也深感自己的愛得到了豐厚的回報。她再也不肯讓他獨自去任何地方……她在那裡強烈地想要留下，他又一次應允，於是她化為一塊石頭，而帕里亞卡卡則登上群山。就這樣，喬克蘇索在渠道的源頭化為一塊石頭，該處名為科科查利亞（Cocochalla）。此渠道上方另有一條名為維姆隆帕（Vim-lompa）的渠道，那裡還有一塊石頭，據說科尼拉亞（Coniraya）便化作了那塊石頭。

language: Spanish record of a Quechua tradition
canonical_translation: C. R. Markham, Narrative of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas (Hakluyt Society, 1873)

title.en: Faridun Divides the World Among His Sons
title.zh: 法里東分天下於三子

region.en: Thrones of Rum, Turan, Iran (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 羅姆、圖蘭、伊朗三王座（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun sec. 7

summary.en: Faridun divides the earth into three realms: Rum and the West to Salm; Turan and the land of Chin to Tur; and to Iraj, the youngest, he selects all Iran with Arabia and the throne of majesty, perceiving that Iraj deserved to rule. All the princes acceded to their thrones in peace and mirth — until envy ripened in the elder brothers' hearts.
summary.zh: 法里東三分天下：羅姆與西方歸薩爾姆；圖蘭與秦地歸圖爾；而將整個伊朗連同阿拉伯與至尊王座擇予幼子伊朗支，認為其德配其位。三王子起初相安於位——直到嫉妒在兩位兄長心中成熟。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source. The division is an etiology of Rum/Turan/Iran peoples; tagged as founding legend. No living community restriction.

passages.text: These secrets known, the Shah divided earth and made three realms: he joined Rum with the West, Turan with Chin, Arabia with Iran. He first took thought for Salm and gave him Rum and all the West, commanding him to lead an army thither; so Salm took the throne, and all the West saluted him as lord.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這些秘密既已明瞭，沙阿便劃分大地，立下三個疆域：他將魯姆（Rum）與西方相連，將圖蘭（Turan）與秦（Chin）相連，將阿拉伯與伊朗相連。他首先為薩爾姆（Salm）著想，將魯姆與整個西方賜予他，命他率軍前往該地；於是薩爾姆登上王位，整個西方都尊他為主。

passages.text: Next Faridun assigned Turan to Tur to rule the Turkmans and the land of Chin, providing troops; Tur arrived, assumed the seat of sovereignty, and all Turan hailed him as king. Iraj came last: the sire selected all Iran for him, this with Arabia and the throne of majesty and crown of chiefs he gave, perceiving that Iraj deserved to rule. How all the princes, prudent, wise, and shrewd, all-hailed him as the master of Iran!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 接著，法里頓將圖蘭分給圖爾，命他統治突厥人與秦地，並供給兵馬；圖爾抵達後，登上王位，全圖蘭皆尊他為王。伊拉吉最後到來：父王為他選定了整個伊朗，連同阿拉伯、威嚴的寶座與首領的冠冕一併賜予他，因為他看出伊拉吉理當治國。眾王子——審慎、明智而精明——無不尊他為伊朗之主！

title.en: Salm and Tur Conspire Against Their Father's Favour
title.zh: 薩爾姆與圖爾合謀怨父

region.en: West and Chin (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西方與秦地（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun secs. 8-10

summary.en: Salm, immersed in greed, sends to Tur: the youngest hath the chiefest place, and I cannot brook this settlement. Tur answers like a savage lion: this is a tree our father's hands have set; the fruit is blood. Together they send a priest as envoy to Faridun demanding Iraj be discrowned, else they will bring the cavaliers of Rum and Chin in vengeance on Iran. The aged Shah answers with warning: the crop that ye have sown that shall ye reap.
summary.zh: 薩爾姆因貪而遣使圖爾：「最幼者居首，我難以忍受此安排。」圖爾如猛獅回應：「此乃我父親手所植之樹，其果實是血。」二人遂遣使向父索要伊朗支之王冠，否則將率羅姆與秦地騎兵伐伊朗。老王答以箴言：「種何穀，收何穀。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Much time rolled on till wise Shah Faridun was worn with age. Then gloom began to gather in the state; immersed in greed Salm changed in heart and mind, for he much misliked his sire's apportionment, which gave Iraj the throne of gold. He hurried off a camel-post, an envoy, to the king of Chin: three sons were we who graced our father's throne, and now the youngest hath the chiefest place! The youngest hath Iran; I cannot brook this settlement.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 歲月流轉，直到睿智的沙阿法里頓為年歲所困。於是國中開始籠罩陰霾；薩爾姆沉溺於貪欲，心性大變，因為他極不滿父王的分配，那分配將黃金寶座給了伊拉吉。他急忙派出駱駝驛使、一名使者，前往秦地之王處：我們本是三子，曾共榮耀父王之座，如今最小的卻佔了最高的位置！最小的得了伊朗；我無法容忍這樣的安排。

passages.text: The message filled Tur's brainless head with wind, and savage as a lion he replied: this is a tree which his own hands have set; the fruit is blood, the leafage colocynth; so let us meet and parley, fix on our course of action and raise troops. Poison being mixed with honey thus, they met together to deliberate the matter both in council and in state.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這訊息灌滿了圖爾那無腦的頭顱，他如獅子般兇暴地回答：這是一棵他親手栽下的樹；果實是血，枝葉是苦瓜；所以讓我們相會商議，定下行動之策，並徵集兵馬。毒藥就這樣摻入蜂蜜之中，他們相聚商議此事，既在議會中，也在國事上。

passages.text: Their envoy to Faridun demanded: if his worthless head shall be discrowned and earth rescued from his sway, well; else will we bring the Turkman cavaliers and eager warriors of Rum and Chin in vengeance on Iran and on Iraj. The Shah's brain seethed with anger: tell mine unholy and abandoned sons, this pair of Ahrimans with dregs of brains: the crop that ye have sown that shall ye reap; I fear that in that Dragon's clutch your bodies and souls will part.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun secs. 9-10 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們派往法里頓的使者要求：倘若他那無用的頭顱能被摘去王冠，大地能從他的統治中解脫，那便罷了；否則我們將率領突厥騎士與羅馬及秦地急切的戰士，向伊朗與伊拉吉復仇。沙阿怒火中燒：告訴我那兩個不敬神、放蕩的兒子，這兩個腦中盡是渣滓的阿赫里曼：你們所播下的莊稼，必由你們收割；我擔心在那巨龍的爪中，你們的身與魂將要分離。

title.en: The Murder of Iraj
title.zh: 伊朗支遇弑

region.en: Tur borders (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 圖蘭邊境（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun secs. 11-12

summary.en: Against his father's warning, Iraj goes unattended to his brothers to make peace: I do not want the royal crown or throne; my faith is naught without humanity. Tur hears and answers with a dagger from his boot; he robes Iraj in blood, entrenches the royal breast, cuts off the young king's head, and the brothers fill the head with musk and ambergris and send it to the aged world-divider: look upon thy darling's head.
summary.zh: 伊朗支不顧父親警告，輕裝前往兄長處謀和：「王冠寶座我皆不要；無仁愛則無信仰。」圖爾置若罔聞，自靴中拔出匕首，染其血、刺其胸，割下幼王之頭。二人以麝香龍涎填入頭顱，送呈年邁的分天下者：「請看您愛子之頭。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; fratricide as ethnogenesis of Iran-Turan enmity. No living community restriction.

passages.text: The great Shah wrote a letter to the lord of all the West and to the king of Chin, and Iraj set forth with such attendants only as were imperative. Tur said to him: since thou art youngest born why shouldst thou take the crown of power? Thine eldest brother chafeth in the West while thou art crowned. Iraj made answer in a holier strain: seek peace if thou wouldst have thy heart at ease. I do not want the royal crown or throne; I do not want Iran, the West, or Chin; although thou ridest on the heaven above, a brick will be thy pillow in the end.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun secs. 11-12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 偉大的沙阿寫了一封信給整個西方之主與秦地之王，伊拉吉便帶著僅屬必要的隨從出發。圖爾對他說：既然你是最小的，為何要奪取權力的冠冕？你的長兄在西方焦躁不安，而你卻加冕了。伊拉吉以更為神聖的語氣回答：若你想心安，就尋求和平。我不要王冠或寶座；我不要伊朗、西方或秦地；儘管你如今騎行於九天之上，最終一塊磚將是你的枕頭。

passages.text: Tur heard the words and little heeded them, but, angry that Iraj should speak, rose up with a cry and, grasping the massive seat of gold, smote Iraj, who pleaded for his life: hast thou no fear of God, nor any reverence for thy sire? Oh, hurt not e'en the poor grain-dragging ant, for it hath life, and sweet life is a joy. Tur drew a dagger from his boot, he robed Iraj in blood, and with the keen bright blade entrenched the royal breast. The lofty Cypress fell, the imperial girdlestead was broken, and thus the young illustrious monarch died.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 圖爾聽了這些話，卻毫不在意，但對伊拉吉竟敢開口而憤怒，他起身大叫，抓住那巨大的黃金座椅，猛擊伊拉吉，伊拉吉則為自己的性命哀求：你難道不畏懼上帝，也不敬重你的父王嗎？哦，連那拖曳穀粒的螞蟻也不要傷害，因為它有生命，而甜美的生命是一種喜悅。圖爾從靴中抽出匕首，讓伊拉吉浴於血中，以鋒利明亮的刀刃刺入那王者的胸膛。高聳的柏樹倒下了，帝王的腰帶斷裂了，年輕而顯赫的君主就這樣死去。

passages.text: Tur with his dagger cut the prince's head from the elephantine form and all was over. They filled the head with musk and ambergris and sent it to the aged world-divider with these words: look upon thy darling's head, the inheritor of our forefathers' crown, and give it crown or throne as pleaseth thee. The royal and far-shadowing Tree had fallen, and those two miscreants went their way in spleen, one unto Rum, the other unto Chin.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 圖爾以匕首將王子的頭從那如象般的身軀上割下，一切就此終結。他們將那頭顱填滿麝香與龍涎香，送交那位年邁的分疆之主，並附上這樣的話語：看看你愛子的頭顱吧，那繼承我們祖先王冠之人，要賜他王冠或王座，悉聽尊意。那株尊貴而遠蔭四方的樹已然傾倒，那兩個惡徒滿懷怨毒地離去，一個前往魯姆，另一個前往秦。

title.en: Faridun's Mourning and His Prayer for an Avenger
title.zh: 法里東之慟與復仇者之祈

region.en: Garden of Iraj (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊朗支之園（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun sec. 13

summary.en: A dromedary brings the golden casket with Iraj's head wrapped in painted silk; Faridun falls from his steed, the troops rend their clothes, and the welcome turns to wailing. The Shah enters the garden of Iraj, fires the house his son dwelt in, burns the cypresses, and prays head turned Godward: grant me so long a respite from the day of death that I may see descended from Iraj one born to fame, girded to avenge.
summary.zh: 單峰駝送來金匣，內裹彩絲包著伊朗支的頭顱；法里東墜馬，軍民裂衣痛哭。老王步入愛子之園，焚其居所，燒柏樹，面向真主祈禱：「賜我壽數，使我得見伊朗支後嗣中出成名之子，束帶復仇。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: The eyes of Faridun were on the road; he had prepared the prince a turquoise throne and added jewels to his crown, and the people were all in readiness to welcome him with wine and song. While the Shah and troops were busied thus a cloud of dust appeared, and from its midst a dromedary ridden by one in grief who uttered bitter cries: he bore a golden casket, and therein the prince's head enwrapped in painted silk.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法里東的目光望向道路；他已為王子備好一張綠松石王座，又為他的王冠添上珠寶，而眾人皆已準備妥當，要以美酒與歌聲迎接他。正當沙阿與軍隊如此忙碌之際，一片塵雲出現，塵中走出一頭單峰駝，騎者滿懷悲傷，發出痛苦的呼喊：他捧著一只金匣，匣中以彩繪絲綢裹著王子的頭顱。

passages.text: Down from his steed fell Faridun, the troops all rent their clothes, their eyes blanched with their horror. The troops that went to meet him thus returned, their banners rent, their kettledrums reversed, the warriors' cheeks like ebony. The Shah, with cries of Alas! went toward the garden of Iraj, entered bearing his son's head, fired the house wherein Iraj had dwelt, destroyed the rose-beds, burnt the cypress-trees, and closed up once for all the eye of joy.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法里東從坐騎上跌落，全軍撕裂衣裳，雙眼因驚駭而發白。前去迎接他的軍隊就這樣歸來，旗幟撕裂，銅鼓倒轉，戰士們的面頰黑如烏木。沙阿高呼「哀哉！」走向伊拉吉的花園，捧著兒子的頭顱進入，放火焚燒伊拉吉曾居住的屋舍，毀壞玫瑰園，燒盡柏樹，就此永遠闔上了歡樂之眼。

passages.text: He placed the prince's head upon his breast and said with head turned Godward: righteous Judge, look down upon this murdered innocent. Do Thou so burn up those two miscreants' hearts that they may never see a bright day more. Oh grant me, Thou that judgest righteously, so long a respite from the day of death that I may see descended from Iraj one born to fame, and girded to avenge: let him behead those two injurious men as they beheaded him who wronged them not. He wept thus many days and bitterly; his pillow was the dust, his bed the ground, until the herbage grew about his breast.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他將王子的頭顱置於胸前，轉首向神說道：公正的審判者啊，請俯視這被殺害的無辜者。願祢如此燒盡那兩個惡徒的心，使他們再也見不到明亮的白日。哦，祢以正義審判，請賜我如此長久的緩期，延緩死亡之日，使我得以見到從伊拉吉所出、生而享有盛名、束腰以復仇的子嗣：讓他將那兩個害人者斬首，正如他們斬殺那未曾傷害他們之人。他如此痛哭多日，悲切至極；他的枕是塵土，他的床是地面，直到青草在他胸前生長。

title.en: The Birth of Minuchihr, Son of Iraj's Daughter
title.zh: 米努奇赫爾誕生

region.en: Court of Faridun (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 法里東王庭（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun secs. 14-16

summary.en: In Iraj's bower Faridun finds Mah Afrid, the slave the prince had loved, with child; she bears a daughter, who grows up tulip-cheeked like Iraj himself and is wed to Pashang, a descendant of Jamshid. When nine months elapse Pashang's wife brings forth a son fit for crown and throne. Behold Iraj! cries the bearer, and Faridun prays so earnestly for his sight again that God vouchsafes it: be this day blest and our foes' hearts plucked out.
summary.zh: 法里東於伊朗支閨閣中發現其所愛的婢女瑪赫·阿弗莉德已有身孕；她誕下一女，容顏如伊朗支重生，及笄嫁與賈姆希德後裔帕尚格。九月期滿，誕下合乎王冠寶座之男嬰。「看，伊朗支回來了！」法里東懇求復明，神允其願：「此日當受祝福，敵人之心當被剜出！」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: A while passed and the Shah went in to view Iraj's bower and marked the moon-faced beauties who resided there. He saw a slave of lovely countenance whose name was Mah Afrid; Iraj had loved her, and fate decreed that she should bear him fruit. The Shah rejoiced because she was with child, but when her time was come she bore a daughter, and hope deferred hung heavy on the Shah. He nursed the babe with joy and tenderness; thou wouldst have said to her the tulip-cheeked: thou art Iraj himself from head to foot.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 過了些時日，沙阿前去察看伊拉吉的居所，留意居住其中的那些月貌美人。他見到一名容顏秀美的女奴，名叫瑪赫·阿弗里德；伊拉吉曾愛過她，而命運註定她當為他結出果實。沙阿因她懷有身孕而歡喜，然而待她產期到來，卻生下一個女兒，延宕的希望沉沉壓在沙阿心頭。他滿懷喜悅與柔情地撫育這嬰孩；你定會對那鬱金香般面頰的她說：你從頭到腳就是伊拉吉本人。

passages.text: When she was old enough to wed her grandsire chose Pashang to be her spouse: Pashang was brother's son to Faridun, descended from a noble ancestry, a hero of the seed of Shah Jamshid. Mark what a wonder yon blue vault revealed when nine months had elapsed: that virtuous dame brought forth a son fit for the crown and throne, who from his tender mother's womb was brought without delay before the mighty Shah.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 待她到了可婚配之年，她的祖父選定帕尚為她的夫婿：帕尚是法里東的姪兒，出身高貴的世系，是沙阿賈姆希德血脈中的英雄。且看那蒼穹在九個月過去之後揭示了何等奇蹟：那位賢德的女子產下一名配得王冠與王座的兒子，他從溫柔母親的腹中一出，便即刻被帶到強大的沙阿面前。

passages.text: Let all thy heart be joy: behold Iraj! said the bearer. The world-divider's lips were full of smiles; he clasped the noble child and prayed the Almighty: oh, would that I might have mine eyes again. He prayed so earnestly that God vouchsafed to give his sight back; when with open eyes he gazed on that new-comer's face he cried: be this day blest and our foes' hearts plucked out! He called that babe of open visage Minuchihr and reared the babe so tenderly that not a breath passed o'er him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「願你滿心歡喜：看哪，伊拉吉！」抱持者說道。那位劃分世界者的唇上滿是笑容；他緊抱這高貴的孩子，向全能者祈禱：噢，但願我能重見光明。他祈禱得如此懇切，以致上帝恩准歸還他的視力；當他睜開雙眼凝視那新生兒的面容時，他喊道：願這一日蒙福，願我們敵人的心被剜出！他為這面容開朗的嬰孩取名米努奇赫爾，並如此溫柔地撫養這嬰孩，連一絲氣息都不曾掠過他。

title.en: The Ghost of Wahaula Temple
title.zh: 瓦豪拉神廟之魂

region.en: Wahaula (red-mouth) temple, Puna, Hawaii Island
region.zh: 夏威夷島普納瓦豪拉神廟

period: Hawaiian oral tradition; retold 1915 (Westervelt)

source.work: W. D. Westervelt, Legends of Gods and Ghosts (Hawaiian Mythology), ch. 1 (New York 1915)

summary.en: The heiau Wahaula carried a burning tabu: even its smoke falling on a man was cause for death. The young chief Kahele, journeying around Hawaii, forgets the danger; a wisp of temple smoke touches his cheek, and the temple's body-catcher fells him for the altar. His bones, hidden for dishonorable incantation use, haunt the temple until his ghost flies home to Kau, warns his father in dreams, and guides him through the night to the loose stone behind which the folded bones lie - so the spirit passes to the Under-world in honour.
summary.zh: 瓦豪拉神廟禁忌如焚：連其炊煙落在人身上也是死罪。環遊夏威夷島的青年酋長卡赫勒忘卻此忌，一縷廟煙拂面，廟中『捕人者』揮棒擊倒，獻於祭壇。其骨被折疊收藏、備作邪術之用；幽魂不堪其辱，飛回考烏托夢告其父。父親循跡千里，夜探神廟，移開幽魂所指之石，取回骨束——亡魂遂得尊榮歸入幽冥。

sensitivity.note: Temple-sacrifice legend; paraphrase, no ritual text reproduced.

passages.text: Wahaula was a tabu temple of the very highest rank. The native chants said, concerning this heiau is the burning tabu. The heiau was so thoroughly tabu that the smoke of its fires falling upon any of the people or even upon any one of the chiefs was sufficient cause for punishment by death, with the body as a sacrifice to the gods of the temple. Certain days were tabu to Lono; other days belonged to Ku; at other times Kane was held supreme, then again Kanaloa had his days especially set apart for sacrifice and chant. The Mu, or body-catcher, of this heiau with his assistants seems to have been continually on the watch for human victims, and no one dared rescue a man from his hands, for then the wrath of all the gods would follow him all the days of his life.
passages.note: Paraphrase of W. D. Westervelt, Legends of Gods and Ghosts, ch. 1 (1915); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 瓦豪拉是一座等級極高的禁忌神廟。當地的吟唱如此說道：與這座神廟相關的，是那焚燒的禁忌。這座神廟的禁忌如此森嚴，以致其火焰的煙霧若落在任何平民身上，甚至落在任何一位首領身上，便足以構成處死的理由，其屍體則作為獻給神廟諸神的祭品。某些日子對羅諾而言是禁忌；另一些日子則屬於庫；又在其他時候，卡內被奉為至尊，接著卡納洛阿又有其特別劃定用於獻祭與吟唱的日子。這座神廟的穆，即捕屍者，連同他的助手，似乎不斷守候著活人祭品，無人敢從他手中救走一人，因為如此一來，諸神的憤怒將在他一生所有的日子裡追隨他。

passages.text: Many ages ago a young chief named Kahele determined to make a journey around the island visiting all the noted and sacred places. He passed from place to place, riding the surf, gambling, racing the sled, and visiting the most noted of the heiaus. In time he came to Puna, the district in which was located the temple Wahaula. But in the midst of the many stories of the past and the pleasures he had enjoyed, Kahele forgot the peculiar power of the tabu of the smoke of Wahaula. The fierce winds of the south were blowing; he saw the sacred grove and hastened toward the temple. The perilous moment came: the warm breath of one of the fires touched the young chief's cheek, and soon a blow from the club of the Mu laid him senseless on the rough stones. Quickly the body was dismembered and offered as a sacrifice.
passages.note: Paraphrase of W. D. Westervelt, Legends of Gods and Ghosts, ch. 1 (1915); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 許多世代以前，一位名叫卡赫萊的年輕首領決意環島旅行，遍訪所有著名與神聖之地。他從一地到另一地，衝浪、賭博、賽雪橇，並造訪最著名的神廟。終於他來到普納，即瓦豪拉神廟所在的區域。然而，在種種往昔的故事與他所享受的歡樂之中，卡赫萊忘記了瓦豪拉煙霧禁忌那獨特的力量。南方的烈風正吹著；他看見那片神聖的樹林，便急忙朝神廟走去。危急的時刻來臨了：其中一處火焰的溫熱氣息觸及了這位年輕首領的臉頰，不久，穆的棍棒一擊便將他打得不省人事，倒在粗石之上。屍體隨即被肢解，作為祭品獻上。

passages.text: For some reason the priests, after the flesh had decayed, set apart the bones for some special purpose - it may have been that the bones were folded together in the shape known as unihipili, or grasshopper bones, folded and laid away for purposes of incantation, until a new spirit dwelt in the bundle and gave the possessor peculiar power in witchcraft. The spirit of Kahele rebelled against this disposition of all that remained of his body; he wanted to be back in his native district. At last the spirit fled by night from this place of torment to the home he had left. Kahele's father, the high chief of Kau, had a strange dream in which the ghost revealed that he had been put to death and his bones were in danger of dishonorable treatment. The father journeyed secretly around the island, guided by dream-warnings, until he lay down to rest in the lava fields of Wahaula.
passages.note: Paraphrase of W. D. Westervelt, Legends of Gods and Ghosts, ch. 1 (1915); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 由於某種緣故，祭司們在血肉腐爛之後，將骨骸留作某種特殊用途——或許是將骨骸摺疊成稱為烏尼希皮利，即蚱蜢骨，的形狀，摺疊並存放以備施咒之用，直到一個新的神靈住進這捆骨骸之中，賦予持有者在巫術上的奇特力量。卡赫萊的神靈對其遺骸遭受如此處置感到憤慨；他想回到自己的故鄉。終於，這神靈趁夜從這折磨之地逃回他所離開的家。卡赫萊的父親，即考的高級首領，做了一個奇異的夢，夢中鬼魂透露他已被處死，其骨骸有遭受不光彩對待的危險。父親在夢中警示的引導下，秘密環島而行，直到他在瓦豪拉的熔岩地裡躺下歇息。

passages.text: Walking along carelessly to avoid suspicion, he drew near the temple lands and was attacked by an Olohe, a beardless man of a lawless robber clan. Almost all day the battle raged over the lava beds; the chief's well-oiled body was hard to grasp, and at last he forced the Olohe into a narrow place, seized him, broke his bones and killed him. For several days the chief hid himself near the temple, uttering the prayers and incantations needed for the protection of his family gods. One night of very great darkness, when deep sleep rested on all the temple-dwellers, the ghost of Kahele aroused his father for the dangerous task. Step by step he felt his way along the temple walls until the ghost stood near a great rock pointing at a part of the wall. The father seized a stone which very easily was removed from the wall; behind it was a hollow place in which lay a bundle of folded bones. He carried them to Kau and placed them in his own secret family burial cave, and the ghost of Wahaula went down to the spirit world in great joy.
passages.note: Paraphrase of W. D. Westervelt, Legends of Gods and Ghosts, ch. 1 (1915); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他漫不經心地走著以避人疑心，漸近神廟的土地，卻遭到一名奧洛赫的攻擊，那是無法無天的盜匪氏族中一名無鬚的男子。戰鬥在熔岩地上幾乎持續了一整天；首領塗滿油脂的身體難以抓握，最後他將那奧洛赫逼入一處狹窄之地，抓住他，折斷他的骨頭，將他殺死。首領在神廟附近躲藏了數日，念誦保護其家族神祇所需的禱詞與咒語。在一個極其黑暗的夜晚，當沉睡降臨所有住在神廟的人身上時，卡赫萊的鬼魂喚醒他的父親去執行這危險的任務。他一步一步沿著神廟的牆壁摸索前行，直到鬼魂站在一塊大岩石旁，指著牆上的一處。父親取下一塊很容易便從牆上移開的石頭；其後是一個凹洞，裡面放著一捆摺疊的骨骸。他將它們帶到考，安置在自己秘密的家族墓葬洞穴中，而瓦豪拉的鬼魂便滿心歡喜地降入神靈世界。

title.en: Maluae Descends for the Ghost of His Boy
title.zh: 馬魯埃下冥界尋子魂

region.en: Manoa Valley, Oahu, and the breadfruit-tree Lei-walo (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 瓦胡島馬諾阿谷與幽冥麵包樹（象徵性定位）

period: Hawaiian oral tradition; retold 1915 (Westervelt)

source.work: W. D. Westervelt, Legends of Gods and Ghosts (Hawaiian Mythology), ch. 2 (New York 1915)

summary.en: The boy Kaa-lii robs the altars of Kane and Kanaloa; in anger the gods kill him and thrust his ghost into the Under-world. His father Maluae lies refusing food, determined to die with his son; shamed by their own deed, the gods give him a ghost body, a hollow cane of food, weapons and burning lava, and send him down through the ghost-breadfruit-tree of Lei-walo. Battles fought, he finds the boy 'down in the papa-ku' choking on ghost-bananas, and pours the lava-fire of the gods into the floor of Po to drive back the spirits and carry the child's ghost home to its body.
summary.zh: 男孩卡阿利利偷食卡內與卡納洛亞祭壇上的香蕉，二神怒而殺之，將其魂擲入幽冥。父親馬魯埃絕食待死，神自愧過甚，遂授其魂體、內藏食物兵刃與熔岩之火的中空竹杖，令其循幽冥麵包樹萊伊瓦羅而下。父親一路斬鬼開路，終在冥土根基之處尋得噎食鬼蕉的孩童；又傾出神火熔岩，驅散群魂，攜子之魂重返軀體。父子從此終身供奉。

sensitivity.note: Descent-to-underworld cluster: father quests into Po for a child's spirit.

passages.text: In the upper end of Manoa Valley, at the foot of the highest mountains of Oahu, lived Maluae, a farmer, who cultivated bananas and taro and sweet potatoes. Whenever he gathered any food he brought a part to his family temple and placed it on an altar before the gods Kane and Kanaloa. He had a boy whom he dearly loved, Kaa-lii, a careless, rollicking child. One day the boy was tired and hungry; he passed by the temple, saw bananas ripe and sweet on the little platform before the gods, took them and ate them all. The gods looked down expecting food and found nothing; they were very angry, ran out after the boy, caught him eating the bananas and killed him. They left the body under the trees, and taking out his ghost threw it into the Under-world.
passages.note: Paraphrase of W. D. Westervelt, Legends of Gods and Ghosts, ch. 2 (1915); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在馬諾阿山谷的上端，即瓦胡島最高山脈的山腳下，住著一位名叫馬盧阿埃的農夫，他種植香蕉、芋頭和番薯。每當他收穫任何食物，便帶一部分到他的家族神廟，放在卡內與卡納洛阿兩位神祇面前的祭壇上。他有一個他深愛的男孩，名叫卡阿利伊，是個漫不經心、歡鬧嬉戲的孩子。有一天，這男孩又累又餓；他經過神廟，看見神祇面前的小平台上放著成熟甜美的香蕉，便拿起來全部吃光。神祇俯視著，期待著供品，卻一無所獲；他們非常憤怒，跑出去追那男孩，抓住正在吃香蕉的他，將他殺死。他們把屍體留在樹下，取出他的鬼魂，將其投入下界。

passages.text: The father searched for the body and found it, partly eaten bananas filling the mouth set in death. He wrapped the body in kapa cloth, laid it on the sleeping-mat, refused all food, and planned to die with his boy. The gods talked together, and Kane said: Maluae eats no food, he prepares no awa to drink; he is near the door of the Under-world; if he should die, we would be to blame. Kanaloa said: He has been a good man; we have called him morning and evening in his worship; he has provided fish and fruits and vegetables for our altars; we have not paid him well for his care. So they decided to go and give life to the father, and permit him to take his ghost body and go down into Po, the dark land, to bring back the ghost of the boy.
passages.note: Paraphrase of W. D. Westervelt, Legends of Gods and Ghosts, ch. 2 (1915); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 父親尋找兒子的遺體，找到了，部分被吃過的香蕉塞在死後僵硬的嘴裡。他用卡帕布裹住遺體，放在睡席上，拒絕一切食物，打算與兒子一同死去。眾神商議，凱恩說：馬盧阿埃不進食，也不調製阿瓦酒飲用；他已臨近冥界之門；若他死去，我們難辭其咎。卡納洛阿說：他一直是個好人；我們早晚在他的祭祀中呼喚他；他為我們的祭壇供上魚、果實與蔬菜；我們對他的照料回報不周。於是他們決定前去賜予父親生命，並允許他帶著幽靈之身下到黑暗之地波，帶回男孩的幽靈。

passages.text: The gods gave him a ghost body and prepared a hollow stick like bamboo, in which they put food, battle-weapons, and a piece of burning lava for fire. Near the seacoast of Moanalua was a ghostly breadfruit-tree named Lei-walo, perhaps the eighth wreath - the last wreath of leaves from the land of the living which would meet the eyes of the dying. Ghosts would leap or fly or climb into its branches trying to find a rotten branch on which they could sit until it broke and threw them into the dark sea below. Maluae climbed up; his weight broke the branch at once and down they all fell into the land of Po. He tasted the food in his hollow cane for new life and strength, and went from place to place, finding the boy at last 'down in the papa-ku', the established foundation of Po, choking from the bananas of ghost-land which he was compelled to force into his mouth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of W. D. Westervelt, Legends of Gods and Ghosts, ch. 2 (1915); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 眾神賜予他幽靈之身，並準備了一根如竹子般中空的棍子，在其中放入食物、戰鬥武器，以及一塊燃燒的熔岩作火種。在莫阿納盧阿海岸附近，有一棵幽靈麵包樹，名叫雷伊瓦洛，或許意為「第八個花環」——那是生者之地最後一個葉環，將映入垂死者的眼簾。幽靈們會跳躍、飛翔或攀爬進它的枝椏，試圖找到一根腐爛的樹枝棲身，直到樹枝斷裂，把它們拋入下方黑暗的海中。馬盧阿埃爬了上去；他的重量立刻壓斷了樹枝，他們全都墜入波之地。他品嘗了空心杖中的食物，獲得新的生命與力量，然後四處行走，終於在「帕帕庫」——波之穩固根基——之下找到了男孩，男孩正被幽靈之地的香蕉噎住，被迫將香蕉塞入口中。

passages.text: The father caught the spirit of the boy and started back toward the Upper-world, but the ghosts surrounded him, trying to take the spirit away. Once more he partook of the food of the gods and wielded his war-club, but the hosts of enemies were too great, multitudes crushing him by overwhelming numbers. At last he raised his magic hollow cane and poured out the portion of burning lava which the gods had placed inside.
