passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古爾金為自己的利益與名聲，在那青年的路上張開了他的羅網，說道：哦，勇士啊，戰鬥之心、智慧之魂！不遠處有一處遊樂之地，距土蘭僅兩日路程，你將在那裡看見一片紅黃相間的平原。阿弗拉西亞布之女瑪尼扎會把那座花園照耀得如同太陽一般，並帶著一百名侍女——皆是土庫曼人的女兒，個個容貌完美如畫——在那片草地上搭起她的帳篷。如今若我們前往那處遊樂之地，一日之內趕完路程，便可擄走幾名那些仙女般的少女，並贏得霍斯勞的讚許。

passages.text: In this wise spake Gurgin. Bizhan was young, and all the paladin was stirred in him; he was a youth and followed youthful fashion, some whiles pursuing fame and some whiles passion. When the fair one saw the visage of the chieftain from her tent she yearned for love of him, who came in quest of love, and sent her nurse as envoy: can it be Siyawush returned to life, or else a fairy? He answered: I am not Siyawush or fairy-born, sweet-spoken messenger! But from Iran, the country of the free. Bizhan am I, the son of Giv.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha secs. 4-5 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古爾金如此說道。比詹年輕，他心中的勇士之氣全被激起；他是個少年，追隨少年的習性，時而追求名聲，時而追逐情慾。那美人從帳篷中看見這位首領的容貌，便對這前來尋愛之人燃起了愛慕，派她的乳母為使者：莫非是西亞武什復生，抑或是仙女？他答道：我既非西亞武什，也非仙女生養，甜言蜜語的使者啊！我來自伊朗，自由之邦。我乃比詹，吉夫之子。

passages.text: Bizhan proceeded hastily afoot toward Manizha's tent and entered it. Manizha came and clasped him to her breast. They bathed his feet in musk and pure rose-water, then hasted to set meat, and held high revelry with wine and harp, excluding every stranger from the tent; old wine in crystal cups gave to Bizhan new strength, but, when three days and nights had passed in pleasure, sleep and drink prevailed at last.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 6 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 比詹匆匆徒步走向瑪尼扎的帳篷，走了進去。瑪尼扎前來，將他摟在胸前。她們用麝香與純淨的玫瑰水為他洗腳，隨即急忙擺上酒食，以美酒與豎琴大肆歡宴，將一切外人屏於帳外；水晶杯中的陳年美酒給了比詹新的氣力，然而，當三日三夜在歡樂中度過之後，睡意與酒力終於占了上風。

passages.text: Manizha, when her time for going home arrived, still longed to gaze upon Bizhan, and, since his face was gloomy, called her handmaids and bade them mingle with a grateful draught a drug that maketh senseless. This they gave him, and he, bemused already, swallowed it; his head sank down and he was lost to sense. On coming near the city she veiled the sleeper in a woman's wrapper, and, entering the palace privily by night, preserved her secret. He woke and found that jasmine-bosomed beauty in his arms, and in the palace of Afrasiyab!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 瑪尼扎到了該回家的時候，仍渴望凝望比詹，又見他面色陰沉，便召來侍女，吩咐她們在一杯可口的飲料中摻入令人失去知覺的藥。她們把這飲料給他，他本已昏沉，便吞了下去；他的頭垂了下來，失去了知覺。接近城時，她用女子的罩袍遮住這沉睡之人，並在夜裡悄悄進入宮殿，守住了她的秘密。他醒來，發現那茉莉般胸脯的美人就在他懷中，而自己竟在阿弗拉西亞布的宮殿裡！

title.en: Bizhan in the Pit under the Boulder of Akwan
title.zh: 比讚困於阿克萬巨岩之穴

region.en: Pit of Afrasiyab (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿弗拉西亞卜之囚穴（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Bizhan and Manizha secs. 9-11

summary.en: Afrasiyab commands: prepare a gloomy pit and weighty bonds, secure with chains Bizhan's hands to a yoke, then throw him in the pit head first — no more of sun and moon for him! Fetch the boulder of the div Akwan, which covereth the dungeon of Arzhang, and cover Bizhan's, then leave him to go mad with anguish. Manizha is stripped of her fortune and dragged naked to the pit: behold thy house and home; henceforth thou art to be this prisoner's drudge. Then when a day and night had passed she came with lamentations and made a passage large enough to pass one hand, and thereafter gathered food at every door by day-long wanderings and passed it through the crevice to Bizhan.
summary.zh: 阿弗拉西亞卜下令：掘暗穴、縛鐵鏈，將比讚頭朝下擲入穴中——「永不得見日月！」再搬來阿克萬巨岩封住穴口（那原是阿爾章地牢之蓋），讓他瘋癲於苦痛。瑪尼札被剝奪財富、赤足拖至穴邊：「這就是你的家！從今為囚徒做僕役。」一夜一日之後，她哭至穴旁鑿開一掌寬的小縫，從此日日沿門乞討，把食物遞進石縫。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Afrasiyab commanded Garsiwaz: prepare a gloomy pit and weighty bonds, secure with chains Bizhan's hands to a yoke, then throw him in the pit head first — no more of sun and moon for him! Take elephants, and fetch the boulder of the div Akwan, which God raised from the ocean-depth; convey this stone, which covereth the dungeon of Arzhang, upon high-crested elephants, and cover Bizhan's, then leave him to go mad with anguish.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 10 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿弗拉西亞布命令加爾西瓦茲：備好一個陰暗的深坑與沉重的鐐銬，用鎖鏈把比詹的雙手鎖在軛上，然後將他頭朝下扔進坑裡——再無日月屬於他了！帶上大象，去取來妖魔阿夸恩的那塊巨石，那是神從海底舉起的；用高冠大象把這塊石頭——它覆蓋著阿爾尚的地牢——運來，蓋住比詹的坑，然後任他在痛苦中發狂。

passages.text: They carried out the monarch's evil purpose; they haled the son of Giv back from the gallows, and bore him to the pit's mouth in his bonds, there fettered him from head to foot in iron, while smiths with steel and hammers made secure the massive rivetings, and then they flung him head-foremost down the pit and set the stone upon it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 10 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們執行了君王的邪惡意圖；他們把吉夫之子從絞架上拖了回來，將他帶著鐐銬抬到坑口，在那裡用鐵從頭到腳把他鎖住，同時鐵匠們用鋼鐵和鐵鎚把巨大的鉚釘固定牢靠，然後他們把他頭朝下扔進坑裡，並把石頭蓋在上面。

passages.text: Garsiwaz thence led his troop to where the daughter of Afrasiyab dwelt, gave up all her treasury to spoil. Manizha was reduced to naked feet, bare head, and single wrap. Behold thy house and home! he said; henceforth thou art to be this prisoner's drudge. He turned back, and Manizha, the spouse of woe, roamed wailing o'er the plain. Now when a day and night had passed she came with lamentations to the pit, and made a passage large enough to pass one hand; thereafter she used to gather food at every door by day-long wanderings and pass it through the crevice to Bizhan, and weep.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha secs. 10-11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 加爾西瓦茲從那裡率領他的隊伍前往阿夫拉西亞布之女所居之處，將她所有的財寶盡數掠奪。瑪尼扎被弄得赤足、光頭，只裹著一件單衣。他說：看看你的房屋和家園吧！從今以後你要做這個囚徒的苦役。他轉身回去了，而瑪尼扎，這個苦難的妻子，在平原上徘徊哀號。如今一日一夜過去之後，她帶著悲泣來到坑邊，挖出一個足以伸進一隻手的通道；此後她白天四處遊走，挨家挨戶乞討食物，從縫隙中遞給比詹，然後哭泣。

title.en: Giv Brings Gurgin Before Khusrau
title.zh: 吉夫押古爾金見王

region.en: Court of Kai Khusrau (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 卡伊霍斯勞王庭（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 12

summary.en: Gurgin returns to Iran without Bizhan, leading the riderless steed, and lies about a fabled onager that was the White Div. Giv, rushing to the street with cheeks all tears, cries: Bizhan returneth not! He marks the confused account, the eyes that could not look him in the face, and ascertaining that the whole account was fraudulent restrains his hand — what shall I gain by slaying him? — and brings Gurgin before Khusrau: he hath come back with an idle tongue, with guilty soul, and evil news of him.
summary.zh: 古爾金獨自返伊，牽著空鞍的戰馬，編造「化作白魔的野驢」之謊。吉夫聞訊衝上街頭、淚流滿面：「比讚沒有回來！」他識破那支離的謊言、不敢對視的目光，按住怒火——殺他何益？——遂押古爾金上殿：「他空言而歸，心懷鬼胎，還帶來我兒的噩耗。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: When one week passed, and still Bizhan returned not, Gurgin began to search on every side in haste and bathed his face in tears of blood. He spied in the distance on the river-bank, with bridle broken and with saddle dragging, his comrade's steed, and knew: Bizhan is sped! By gibbet or by prison or by bonds ill hath befallen him from Afrasiyab.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 一週過去，比詹仍未歸來，古爾金便急忙四處搜尋，以血淚洗面。他望見遠處河岸上，有一匹韁繩斷裂、馬鞍拖地的馬，正是他同伴的坐騎，便知道：比詹已遭不測！或因絞架，或因牢獄，或因鐐銬，阿夫拉西亞布已使他遭逢不幸。

passages.text: Giv heard of his brave son's loss, rushed to the street, pierced to the heart with anguish and with cheeks all tears, and cried: Bizhan returneth not! He marked Gurgin's confused account, those eyes that could not look him in the face, those cheeks grown wan with terror of the Shah, that body a-tremble, and that conscience-stricken heart, and ascertaining that the whole account was fraudulent. What shall I gain by slaying him save pleasing malignant Ahriman? he said; let us tarry till his guilt is clear before the Shah.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 吉夫聽聞他勇敢的兒子失蹤，便衝到街上，心中悲痛如刺，雙頰滿是淚水，喊道：比詹沒有回來！他察覺到古爾金那慌亂的敘述，那雙不敢正視他臉的眼睛，那因畏懼沙阿而變得蒼白的雙頰，那顫抖的身體，以及那受良心譴責的心，於是斷定整番說辭盡是虛假。他說：我殺了他除了取悅邪惡的阿里曼之外還能得到什麼？讓我們暫且等待，直到他的罪責在沙阿面前清楚明白。

passages.text: With bloodshot eyes and vengeance in his heart Giv went before the Shah: I had one son, a youth who was my care both night and day; and now Gurgin hath come back with an idle tongue, with guilty soul, and evil news of him. Gurgin hath brought a steed in disarray, but not another token of Bizhan! If now my lord will carefully consider my case he will do justice for me on Gurgin, the man that put this dust upon my head.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 吉夫雙眼充血，心中懷著復仇之念，來到沙阿面前：我只有一個兒子，一個我日夜操心的少年；如今古爾金卻帶著空口白舌、有罪的心靈和他那邪惡的消息回來了。古爾金帶回了一匹凌亂的坐騎，卻沒有比詹的其他任何蹤跡！倘若我主現在仔細審察我的案情，他就會為我向古爾金這個把塵土撒在我頭上的人主持公道。

title.en: Farud Beholds the Army of Iran
title.zh: 法魯德遠望伊朗大軍

region.en: Mount Sapad (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 薩帕德山（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Farud secs. 11-12

summary.en: Farud, the unrecognized son of Siyawush, hears that a host marcheth from Iran against Turan for vengeance. Jarira counsels him: thy brother is the new Shah of Iran; thou shouldst be foremost in the race for vengeance — go with Tukhar and look for the blazons of Bahram and Zanga, for he and these twain were never separable. From the summit of a lofty mountain the two view the Iranian host defiling between two mountains: what with golden helm and golden shield thou wouldst have said no gold is left unmined, a cloud hath risen and rained jewelry.
summary.zh: 西亞瓦什不為人知的兒子法魯德聽聞伊朗大軍為復仇而來。母親賈里拉勸道：「你的兄長正是伊朗新王；你當率先復仇！」並囑他隨圖卡爾上山，尋找巴赫拉姆與贊加的旗徽——他們與其父形影不離。二人立於高山之巔俯瞰：金盔金盾、金斧金戈，彷彿「天下之金已盡採，雲中降下寶石之雨」。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Farud is killed by his brother's army through Tus' haste — a tragedy of mistaken kinship. No living community restriction.

passages.text: News reached Farud: the bright sun's face is darkened by dust raised by the feet of elephants and camels; a host marcheth from Iran against Turan for vengeance, purposing to take the road that leadeth to Kalat. The inexperienced youth on hearing this grew very sore of heart and dark of soul. He came down from the hold, unbarred the gate, and going forth surveyed the lofty mountain.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 消息傳到法魯德耳中：明亮的太陽之面被大象和駱駝腳下揚起的塵土所遮蔽；一支大軍正從伊朗向圖蘭進發復仇，打算取道通往卡拉特之路。這個缺乏經驗的少年聽聞此事，心中大為痛苦，靈魂陰鬱。他從要塞上下來，打開城門，走出去察看那高聳的山嶺。

passages.text: Jarira said to him: thy brother is the new Shah of Iran; a world-lord shrewd is Kai Khusrau, and he well knoweth both thy name and native worth. One father's blood and bone are in you both, and Siyawush was peerless in the world. Now, since thy brother seeketh to avenge the soul of Siyawush, thou shouldst be foremost in the race for vengeance. In the dust afar raised by the host look for two cavaliers, Bahram and Zanga son of Shawaran; he and these twain were never separable, they were his lords, he was their over-lord.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 賈里拉對他說：你的兄長乃是伊朗的新沙阿；睿智的世界之主乃是凱霍斯魯，他深知你的名字與你本有的價值。你們二人身上流著同一位父親的血與骨，而西亞武什在世間無人能及。如今，既然你的兄長尋求為西亞武什的靈魂復仇，你便應當在復仇的競逐中居於首位。在遠方由大軍揚起的塵土中，尋覓兩位騎士，巴赫拉姆與沙瓦蘭之子贊加；他與這二人從不可分離，他們是他的領主，他是他們的至尊之主。

passages.text: They chose the summit of a lofty mountain, commanding all the army of Iran, and marvelled at the troops and their equipment. The Iranian host defiled between two mountains, and what with golden helm and golden shield, with golden ax and golden partisan, thou wouldst have said: no gold is left unmined, a cloud hath risen and rained jewelry! The roar of kettledrums along the pass affrayed the vultures as they flew o'erhead, while thirty thousand sword and buckler men marched bravely on in all points dight for war.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們選了一座高山的山頂，俯瞰伊朗全軍，並驚嘆於這些軍隊及其裝備。伊朗大軍在兩山之間魚貫而行，金盔與金盾、金斧與金矛，你定會說：再無黃金留存於礦中，一片雲已升起並降下了珠寶！隘口沿途的銅鼓轟鳴，驚擾了飛翔於頭頂的禿鷲，而三萬名持劍執盾之士英勇前行，各方面皆已裝備齊整，準備作戰。

title.en: The Death of Farud and of Jarira
title.zh: 法魯德之死與賈里拉自刎

region.en: Hold of Mount Sapad (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 薩帕德山堡（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Farud secs. 20-21

summary.en: Jarira dreams that from the lofty castle a flame rose in front of Farud, burning all the castle and the women-slaves, and wakes to see the mountain filled with mail and spears. Farud fights alone till Ruhham strikes his shoulder and Bizhan houghs his steed; dying, he bids the slaves fling themselves from the battlements that none may be the portion of Bizhan, and the beloved Farud plucked out their lives. Jarira kindles a pyre, burns the treasures, hamstrings the steeds, presses her cheeks upon his face, rips up herself and dies upon his breast, and Tus, with beard like camphor, sheds a stream of tears of blood.
summary.zh: 賈里拉夢見城堡起火焚盡侍女，驚醒見滿山甲兵。法魯德孤身力戰，被魯哈姆斫傷肩臂、比讚砍斷馬足；彌留之際他命侍女跳下城牆「免遭比讚之辱」，隨即嚥氣。賈里拉點火焚財、刺廢戰馬，將面頰貼上兒子的臉，自刎於其胸。圖斯鬚如樟腦，泣血如注。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the tragedy of Farud is a canonical Shahnama lament. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Now when the shining sun had disappeared, and dark night led its host across the sky, the daughter of Piran approached her son Farud with anxious mind and aching heart. She dreamed that from the lofty castle rose a flame in front of him she loved so well, illuming Mount Sapad and burning all the castle and the women-slaves. She woke in pain and went out upon the wall, and looking round saw all the mountain filled with mail and spears.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 20 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 如今，當燦爛的太陽已然消失，黑夜率其大軍橫越天空，皮蘭之女懷著焦慮的心與疼痛的心，走近她的兒子法魯德。她夢見從那高聳的城堡中，在他所深愛之人面前升起一團火焰，照亮了薩帕德山，並燒毀了整座城堡與那些女奴。她在痛苦中醒來，走上城牆，環顧四周，看見整座山滿是鎧甲與長矛。

passages.text: Farud descended from the castle-ramparts with all his gallant Turkmans, but of the Turkmans no cavalier remained with him; he fought alone. Ruhham sought with Bizhan to intercept him: Bizhan was staggered by the young man's stroke and lost both sense and power; Ruhham behind struck the lion-man upon the shoulder, and his hand fell useless. Wounded he cried out, and Bizhan came up and houghed his steed as he neared the hold.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 20 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法魯德帶著他所有英勇的突厥人從城堡的城垛上下來，但突厥人中已無一名騎士留在他身邊；他獨自奮戰。魯赫哈姆與比詹一同尋求攔截他：比詹被這年輕人的一擊震得搖晃，失去了知覺與力量；魯赫哈姆從背後擊中這獅般之人的肩膀，他的手便廢了。他受傷呼喊，比詹上前，在他接近堡壘時砍斷了他的坐騎的腿筋。

passages.text: It is no marvel that ye pluck your hair, said dying Farud; the Iranians will come with girded loins to sack the hold and make my slave-girls captive. Let all whose hearts and cheeks burn for my life go fling themselves down from the battlements that none may be the portion of Bizhan. His mother and the female slaves plucked out the scented tresses of their musky hair, while the beloved Farud plucked out their lives: the throne was strewn with hair, the house all sorrow.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 20 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 垂死的法魯德說：你們拔扯自己的頭髮，這並不奇怪；伊朗人將束緊腰帶來洗劫這座堡壘，並將我的女奴擄為俘虜。凡心與頰為我的性命而灼燒者，都讓他們從城垛上縱身跳下，好使無人成為比詹的戰利品。他的母親與女奴們拔下她們那麝香般頭髮中芬芳的髮辮，而心愛的法魯德則拔去了她們的性命：王座上鋪滿了頭髮，屋中盡是悲傷。

passages.text: Now when in failure thus had passed away Farud, the hapless son of Siyawush, the slave-girls scaled the roof and dashed them to the ground. Jarira kindled a pyre and burned the treasures; sword in hand she locked the stable of the Arab steeds, hamstrung, and ripped them up. All blood and sweat she sought the couch of glorious Farud, and, having pressed her cheeks upon his face, ripped up herself and died upon his breast. They built upon the mountain-top a royal charnel wherein they placed a throne of gold, and set him there; beside the prince they set Rivniz and great Zarasp, while Tus, with beard like camphor, shed a stream of tears of blood.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 21 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 如今，當法魯德——西亞武什那不幸的兒子——如此在失敗中逝去，女奴們攀上屋頂，縱身躍向地面。賈里拉點燃了一座火葬堆，燒毀了財寶；她手持寶劍，鎖上了阿拉伯駿馬的馬廄，砍斷牠們的腿筋，並剖開牠們的腹部。她滿身血與汗，尋向光榮的法魯德的靈床，將雙頰貼上他的臉後，剖開自身，死在他的胸膛上。他們在山頂上建了一座王家的墓室，在其中放置一張黃金寶座，將他安放於此；在王子身旁，他們安放了里夫尼茲與偉大的扎拉斯普，而鬍鬚如樟腦般白的圖斯，則流下了一股血淚之流。

title.en: The Snowstorm on the Kasa Rud
title.zh: 卡薩魯德風雪之災

region.en: Kasa Rud (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 卡薩魯德河（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Farud secs. 23-24

summary.en: On the Iranian side a tempest rose: a dense cloud came like flying dust, their lips congealed with cold, the tents and camp-enclosures were turned to ice, snow carpeted the mountains, and for a sennight's space earth disappeared. They slew and ate their horses; multitudes of men and cattle perished, and none at last possessed a charger. To pass the barricade of faggots on the river, old Giv girds up his loins — I can burn a flinty mountain with my breath — kindles the pile with a javelin-point, and after three weeks of conflagration, wind, and smoke the army went across the river, for the fire was spent.
summary.zh: 伊朗軍營驟起風暴：黑雲挾塵、唇凝於寒、帳幕成冰、積雪封山，七日之間大地無蹤。士卒宰馬而食，人畜死傷無數，最後竟無一馬可騎。為通過河上柴薪障壘，老將吉夫束腰請命：「我一口氣能燒穿燧石之山！」以鏢尖引火焚壘；烈焰、狂風與濃煙封路三週，第四週柴盡火熄，大軍方渡。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: A tempest rose and none took thought of fight; a dense cloud came like flying dust, their lips congealed with cold, the tents and camp-enclosures were turned to ice, snow carpeted the mountains, and for a sennight's space earth disappeared. There was but little food or rest or sleep: thou wouldst have said earth's face is turned to stone. They slew and ate their horses; multitudes of men and cattle perished. When the eighth day came the sun prevailed, the earth was like a sea, the troops were mustered, and Tus spake of fight.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 23 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 暴風驟起，無人再思征戰；密雲如飛塵般湧來，眾人之唇為寒氣所凍結，帳幕與營柵盡化為冰，積雪覆蓋山嶺，七日之間大地隱沒無蹤。糧食、安歇與睡眠皆極匱乏：人幾可說大地之面已化為石。他們殺馬而食；人畜死者無數。至第八日，太陽得勝，大地宛如一片汪洋，軍隊集結，圖斯乃言征戰之事。

passages.text: Giv said: this will not be a toil, or, if it be, a toil not unrequited. Bizhan was grieved: I cannot give consent to this; thou rearedst me in stress and hardihood; it must not be that I a youth sit still while thou an old man girdest up thy loins. Giv said: my son, I took this enterprise upon my shoulders; 'tis the time for arms, not for indulgence and decrepitude; be not in dudgeon at my going, I can burn a flinty mountain with my breath.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 23 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 吉夫說道：此事不會是徒勞，縱然是勞苦，也非無所回報。比讓心中悲傷：我不能同意此事；你於艱難困苦中將我撫育成人；絕不可讓我這少年安坐不動，而你這老者卻束腰備戰。吉夫說道：我兒，我已將此重任擔於肩上；如今是披甲上陣之時，而非縱情逸樂與衰朽之年；勿因我前去而心懷慍怒，我一口氣便能燒盡一座堅如燧石之山。

passages.text: He passed the Kasa rud albeit with stress, the world for warp and woof had ice and snow, and when he reached the barricade of faggots its length and breadth were more than he could tell; he used a javelin-point to kindle fire, threw it upon the mass and burned the pile. For three weeks conflagration, wind, and smoke allowed no passage through the burning mass, but when the fourth week came the army went across the river, for the fire was spent.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 23 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他雖歷經艱難，終究渡過了卡薩河，天地之間盡是冰與雪；當他抵達那柴束所築的柵壘時，其長寬之廣已非他所能言說；他以標槍之尖引火，擲於柴堆之上，將那柴堆焚毀。三週之間，烈焰、狂風與濃煙使人無法穿越那燃燒之物，然至第四週來臨，火焰已熄，大軍遂渡河而過。

title.en: Piran's Night-Attack on the Drunken Host
title.zh: 皮蘭夜襲醉營

region.en: Plain of Turan (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 圖蘭平原（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Farud sec. 27

summary.en: Out of that noble host Piran made choice of thirty thousand horse who marched at dead of night; no tymbal sounded, no trumpet blared, none raised the battle-cry. The Turkmans marched upon the Iranian host, all drunken and disposed in groups unarmed, and Giv, that fight-engrosser, was astound. Arraying his body in the mail of Siyawush, raging like a leopard at himself in shame for his own indolence, Up! Up! the enemy hath come while we, the warriors of the Shah, are sleeping! The flags were rent, the kettledrums over-turned, for sires had lost their sons and sons their sires, and that great host was utterly overthrown.
summary.zh: 皮蘭自大軍中精選三萬騎，深夜潛行——無鼓、無號、無喊殺。突厥人撲向沉醉的伊朗軍營；吉夫驚醒，披上西亞瓦什的鎧甲，羞憤自斥：「起來！起來！敵人來了，王的戰士還在酣睡！」旗裂鼓翻，父失其子、子失其父，大軍潰不成軍。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Out of that noble host Piran made choice of thirty thousand horse with scimitars, who marched at dead of night; no tymbal sounded, no trumpet blared, none raised the battle-cry. Thence like a murky cloud the Turkmans marched upon the Iranian host, all drunken and disposed in groups unarmed; howbeit Giv was in his tent alert, Gudarz the chieftain sober. Then arose the war-cry with the crash of battle-axes.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 27 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 皮蘭自那高貴的軍中挑選了三萬持彎刀的騎兵，於深夜行軍；不聞銅鼓之聲，不聞號角之鳴，無人高呼戰號。圖蘭人遂如陰雲一般向伊朗大軍進發，彼等皆醉，散作一群群、未著甲冑；然而吉夫於帳中警覺，族長古達爾茲亦清醒。隨即戰號與戰斧之擊聲齊起。

passages.text: The gallant hero lion-like arrayed his body in the mail of Siyawush, and, raging like a leopard at himself in shame for his own indolence and sloth: Up! Up! How is it that to-night my brain is filled with fumes instead of war? The enemy hath come while we, the warriors of the Shah, are sleeping! The Iranians were hemmed in; soft pillows were beneath the drunkards' heads, above were sword, hot mace, and scimitar.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 27 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那英勇的雄獅般的武士將西亞瓦什的鎧甲披於身上，如豹般暴怒，為自身的怠惰與疏懶而羞慚：起來！起來！何以今夜我腦中充滿醉意而非戰意？敵人已至，而我等沙阿的武士卻在沉睡！伊朗人被團團圍困；醉漢們頭下是柔軟的枕頭，頭上卻是利劍、灼熱的狼牙棒與彎刀。

passages.text: Now when dawn showed forth from the Sign of Leo, and gallant Giv surveyed the host, he saw the waste all covered with Iranian slain. The flags were rent, the kettledrums over-turned, and the survivors' cheeks like ebony, for sires had lost their sons and sons their sires, and that great host was utterly overthrown. Unable to resist they turned their backs, abandoning their camp in their confusion, and on this wise fared they toward the Kasa rud, a strengthless mob.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Farud sec. 27 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 及至黎明自獅子座顯現，英勇的吉夫巡視大軍，只見荒野之上盡是伊朗陣亡將士。旗幟撕裂，銅鼓傾覆，生還者面如烏木，因父失其子、子失其父，那龐大的軍隊徹底潰敗。他們無力抵抗，轉身而逃，於混亂中棄營而去，如此這般向卡薩河而去，成了一群毫無氣力的烏合之眾。

title.en: Rustam Hurls the Boulder and Frees Bizhan
title.zh: 魯斯塔姆搬岩救比讚

region.en: Pit of Afrasiyab (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿弗拉西亞卜之囚穴（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Bizhan and Manizha secs. 13-24

summary.en: On New Year's Day Khusrau takes up Jamshid's cup, sees the seven climes, and beholds Bizhan fast fettered in the pit with the daughter of Afrasiyab attending him: none save deft Rustam can liberate Bizhan. Rustam draws up the seven warriors, and when their hands gall in vain on the boulder he himself grasps, raises, and hurls it back to the forest of the land of Chin; earth shook thereat. He draws up Bizhan with fettered feet, snaps the chains, and that night breaks bolt and bar into the palace of Afrasiyab: for thy bed thou hadst a throne, Bizhan had but a pit — let no one thus maltreat a son-in-law!
summary.zh: 新年之日，霍斯勞舉起賈姆希德的寶杯，望見七洲之中比讚被縛於穴、瑪尼札相伴——「唯巧捷的魯斯塔姆能救他！」七勇士合力搬不動巨岩，英雄束甲請力於神，獨力舉起擲回秦地森林，大地為之震動。他垂索救出比讚、捏斷鎖鏈；當夜破門闖入阿弗拉西亞卜王宮：「你睡的是寶座，比讚睡的是土穴——休得如此虐待女婿！」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Jamshid's cup pairs with the Jamshid records. No living community restriction.

passages.text: When jocund New Year's Day arrived Giv yearned for consultation with that glorious cup. Thence returning to his throne Khusrau assumed the Kaian crown, took up the cup, and gazed: he saw the seven climes reflected there, and every act and presage of high heaven; in that cup the wizard-king was wont to see futurity. He scanned the seven climes for traces of Bizhan, and, when he reached the Kargasars, beheld him by God's decree fast fettered in the pit, and praying in his misery for death, with one, the daughter of a royal race, attending him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當歡樂的新年來到，吉夫渴望向那光輝的酒杯求問。庫斯勞由此回到王座，戴上凱揚王冠，拿起酒杯凝視：他看見七域映照其中，以及高天的每一舉動與徵兆；那巫王慣於在那杯中窺見未來。他遍覽七域，尋找比讓的蹤跡，當他來到卡爾加薩爾時，依上帝旨意看見他被緊緊鎖在坑中，在苦難中祈求死亡，身旁有一位王族出身的女子照料著他。

passages.text: Bizhan is yet alive; be of good cheer, said the Shah: he is now a prisoner in Turan, attended by a maid of noble birth. Who will come forward to rescue him? Who is there that will brave the Dragon's breath? None save deft Rustam, he who from the deep will drag the crocodile. Then matchless Rustam led them toward the fire; when he approached the boulder of Akwan, that pit of sorrow, smart, and anguish, he told the seven warriors to strive to clear the pit's mouth of the stone; they strove in vain and sorely galled their hands.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha secs. 13-24 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「比讓還活著；振作起來吧，」沙阿說道：「他如今是圖蘭的囚徒，有一位高貴出身的侍女相伴。誰願挺身前去救他？有誰敢直面巨龍的氣息？除了靈巧的魯斯塔姆，無人能從深處拖出鱷魚。」於是無與倫比的魯斯塔姆領他們向火前行；當他接近阿夸恩的巨石，那悲傷、痛苦與苦惱之坑時，他吩咐七位勇士奮力清除坑口的石頭；他們徒勞地使勁，雙手被磨得傷痕累累。

passages.text: Now while their sweat ran, for the stone stood still, the lion-chief alighted, hitched his skirt of mail beneath his belt and, asking strength from God its source, grasped, raised, and hurled the boulder back to the forest of the land of Chin: earth shook thereat. Then Rustam let his lasso down the pit and drew up thus Bizhan with fettered feet; now Rustam cried aloud when he beheld Bizhan with body hidden by the iron, and putting forth his hands he snapped the chains and bonds, and freed Bizhan from ring and fetter.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 24 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 正當他們汗流浹背，石頭卻紋絲不動，那獅中之首下馬，將鎖子甲的衣裾掖在腰帶下，向上帝——力量之源——祈求力量，抓住、舉起，將巨石拋回秦地之林：大地為之震動。隨後魯斯塔姆將套索垂入坑中，就這樣把雙腳被鎖的比讓拉了上來；當魯斯塔姆看見比讓的身體被鐵器遮蔽，便大聲呼喊，伸出雙手扭斷鎖鏈與鐐銬，將比讓從鐵環與腳鐐中解脫。

passages.text: The seven warriors set forth with Rustam; while all slept within he reached the court-gate of Afrasiyab, and, breaking with his hands both bolt and bar, fierce as a lion flung himself inside. May sweet sleep distaste thee! cried Rustam in the porch; for thy bed thou hadst a throne, Bizhan had but a pit. I am Rustam of Zabul, the son of Zal; I have burst through thy prison, door and bar; Bizhan is free both head and foot from bonds: let no one thus maltreat a son-in-law!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bizhan and Manizha sec. 25 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 七位勇士隨魯斯塔姆出發；當眾人在內沉睡時，他來到阿弗拉西亞布的宮門，用雙手打斷門閂與門槓，如獅子般兇猛，縱身躍入。 「願甜美的睡眠令你厭惡！」魯斯塔姆在門廊喊道：「你的床是王座，比讓卻只有一坑。我是扎爾之子、扎布爾的魯斯塔姆；我已衝破你的牢獄、門與閂；比讓的頭與腳都已脫離束縛：誰也不該如此虐待女婿！」

title.en: Bizhan Slays Human on the Waterless Waste
title.zh: 比讚荒漠誅胡曼

region.en: Desert spot near Kanabad (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 卡納巴德附近荒漠（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. IV, Twelve Rukhs secs. 14-15

summary.en: Human challenges Bizhan and names the scene: wilt thou contend with me upon Mount Kanabad, or make the scene Raibad, and far from aid on either side? They agreed: whichever shall survive shall spare the fallen man's interpreter to bear his king the news. They fought from morning till the shadows lengthened with bows, spears, swords, maces, and wrestling, till by consent they hastened to a pool, and Bizhan prayed: if thou perceivest justice in my cause, the strength which I possess take not away. Though Human was mightier, all prowess is but defect in him whose sun is set: Bizhan bent that mighty Camel, raised him aloft, flung him to the ground, drew forth a dagger, swift as wind beheaded him, and donned instead the armour of Human.
summary.zh: 胡曼向比讚叫陣：「在卡納巴德山，還是去兩軍莫及的荒漠決戰？」二人約定：倖存者須放走敗者的通譯以報信。自晨戰至日斜——弓、矛、劍、錘、角力——同赴泉邊；比讚祈禱：「若我師出有名，請勿奪我之力。」胡曼雖勇，然「其日已落，勇武皆成缺陷」——比讚如豹出爪，彎折駱駝般的巨軀、高舉過頂、擲落於地，拔匕首如風斬其首，然後披上胡曼的鎧甲。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the duel echoes the Rustam-Sohrab wrestling. No living community restriction.

passages.text: When morning breathed above the mountain-tops Human equipped himself, and told Piran: I challenged Bizhan, the son of Giv, and spent the night preparing. Human replied: to-day Giv's heart shall break for his bold son. Wilt thou contend with me upon Mount Kanabad, or make the scene Raibad, and far from aid on either side? They left Mount Kanabad, rode toward the waste, and reached a desert-spot where they beheld no footprints left by man, where vultures flew not, and lions trod not, far from host and help. There they agreed: whichever shall survive shall spare the fallen man's interpreter to bear his king the news of what befell.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當晨光在山巔之上吹拂，胡曼整裝完畢，對皮蘭說道：「我向吉夫之子比讓挑戰，整夜都在準備。」胡曼答道：「今日吉夫的心將為他勇敢的兒子而碎。你願在卡納巴德山上與我交手，還是將戰場設在賴巴德，雙方皆遠離援助？」他們離開卡納巴德山，向荒野馳去，來到一處荒漠之地，在那裡看不見人留下的足跡，禿鷲不飛，獅子不踏，遠離軍隊與援助。他們在那裡約定：無論誰倖存，都要饒過倒下之人的譯者，讓他將所發生之事報知國王。

passages.text: They strained their bows until the notches touched, discharged their poplar arrows tipped with steel, then took their spears, and wheeled to left and right; they took their maces, having done with swords, and passed all measure in their combating; thereafter they essayed each other's strength, and neither of them had the mastery. Bizhan, when he had drunk, arose in anguish, all shaking like a willow in a gale, and, in his heart despairing of sweet life, called upon God: if thou perceivest justice in my cause, both in my challenge and my purposes, the strength which I possess take not away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們拉弓直至弓弦觸及弓梢，射出鋼尖的楊木箭，然後拿起長矛，左右盤旋；他們放下刀劍，拿起釘頭鎚，在交戰中超越了一切限度；此後他們互試氣力，誰也未能取勝。比讓飲酒之後，在痛苦中起身，渾身顫抖如狂風中的柳樹，心中對甜美生命感到絕望，向上帝呼求：若你在我這事業中——無論是我的挑戰還是我的意圖——看見正義，請不要奪去我所擁有的力量。

passages.text: Human, distressed and raven-black with pain, advanced. All wounded as they were both came like pards to fight again, and first one, then the other, touched the ground. For, though Human was mightier, all prowess is but defect in him whose sun is set. Bizhan put forth his hands like leopard's claws: his left hand gripped his foeman's neck, the right his foeman's thigh, he bent that mighty Camel, raised him aloft, and flung him to the ground; then holding down Human, and drawing forth a dagger, swift as wind beheaded him, and flung away his carcase like a dragon's.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那「人」滿懷痛苦、憂傷，面如鴉黑，向前進逼。兩人皆已負傷，卻仍如豹一般再度交戰，先是這一個、後是那一個，都曾仆倒在地。因為「人」雖更為強悍，然而對於那太陽已落之人，一切勇武也不過是缺陷。比詹伸出雙手，如豹爪一般：左手扼住敵人的脖頸，右手抓住敵人的大腿，他將那雄偉的「駱駝」彎折，高高舉起，擲於地上；隨後按住「人」，拔出匕首，迅疾如風，斬下他的頭顱，並將他的屍身如巨龍般拋棄。

passages.text: Bizhan surveyed that elephantine form, fall'n like a stately cypress in a meadow, with great amazement, turned away, looked up to Him who ruleth o'er the world and said: I have no portion in this doughty deed, not having pluck to fight an elephant, yet have cut off Human's head in revenge for Siyawush, and my sire's seventy brothers. Fearing lest the Turkman multitude should come forth to battle while he was not prepared to fight alone, he put from him the mail of Siyawush and donned instead the armour of Human, then mounted on the elephantine steed and took in hand the banner of that prince.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 比詹凝視那如象般龐大的身軀，它已如草原上挺拔的柏樹般倒下，他大為驚愕，轉過身去，仰望那統御世界的主，說道：這樁勇武之功，我並無半分功勞，我本無膽量與一頭象搏鬥，卻已斬下「人」的首級，為西亞武什報仇，也為我父的七十位兄弟報仇。他唯恐那突厥大軍會在他尚未準備好獨自應戰之時殺出交鋒，便脫下西亞武什的鎧甲，改穿「人」的甲冑，隨後跨上那如象般的駿馬，執起那位王子的旗幟。

title.en: Gudarz Shoots Piran's Steed; the Wise Man Falls
title.zh: 古達爾茲射殺皮蘭坐騎

region.en: Field of the Eleven Rukhs (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 十一勇士戰場（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. IV, Twelve Rukhs secs. 29-39

summary.en: Gudarz and Piran arrange a battle of Eleven Rukhs; the paired champions fight one by one, and when the ninth hour of the day had passed there was no Turkman left on that broad plain. Disaster came upon Piran from God; against that will he had no remedy, for the will that made his steed fail under him. Gudarz chose out a poplar arrow that would pierce iron, shot it mightily, and pierced the armour of his foeman's steed, which shivered, gasped, and fell; Piran fell under, his right hand was broken, and he fled from Gudarz toward the hill: born was I in the world for death. Gudarz wept bitterly and shouted: ask quarter for thy life that I may bear thee still living to the Shah — and Piran answers: God forbid! To beg my life were heaviness indeed.
summary.zh: 古達爾茲與皮蘭約定「十一勇士之戰」，兩軍名將逐一配對搏殺；日過九時，圖蘭無一騎存留。天災降於皮蘭——「使他的坐騎失蹄的正是天意」——古達爾茲選一支能穿鐵的白楊箭，大力射出，穿透敵騎甲胄；馬嘶而斃，皮蘭墜地，右手折斷，蹣跚奔向山丘：「人生在世本為一死。」老將含淚高呼：「求饒吧，我帶你去見王！」答曰：「神明在上——乞命之辱，我寧死不受！」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Piran, Turan's wise elder, dies a soldier's death. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Whenas the ninth hour of the day had passed there was no Turkman left on that broad plain: their lives had been dissevered by the sword. Thou wouldst have said: the world is pitiless! Whenas the Turkmans in those luckless combats had struggled fruitlessly Piran descried none of his champions left upon the field; the leaders of Iran and of Turan advanced together for their grim revenge, grief in their hearts and vengeance in their heads.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs secs. 26-39 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當白晝的第九個時辰過去，那廣闊的平原上已不剩一個突厥人：他們的性命已被刀劍斬斷。你定會說：這世界真是無情！當突厥人在那些不幸的戰役中徒勞掙扎之後，皮蘭已望不見麾下還有一位勇士留在戰場上；伊朗與圖蘭的將領們一同向前推進，懷著冷酷的復仇之心，心中悲痛，腦中滿是報復。

passages.text: Those cavaliers tried every kind of sleight with sword and brand, with lasso and with mace, but Heaven's purposes were brought to pass; disaster came upon Piran from God; against that will he had no remedy, the will that made his steed fail under him. Piran saw well enough how matters stood, and knew that God had caused that change of fortune, yet he acquitted him right manfully, and strove against the purposes of fate.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 39 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那些騎士以刀劍、以套索、以狼牙棒使盡各種巧計，然而上天的旨意終究成就；災禍因神而降於皮蘭身上；面對那旨意他無可補救，那旨意使他的坐騎在他腳下失足。皮蘭已十分清楚局勢如何，也明白是神造成了這番命運的轉變，然而他仍堂堂正正地為自己奮戰，與命運的旨意相抗。

passages.text: The two chiefs of the host, those shrewd old men, then took their bows and arrows in their hands. Gudarz chose out a poplar arrow, one that would pierce iron, shot it mightily, and pierced the armour of his foeman's steed, which shivered, gasped, and fell. Piran fell under; his steed rolled o'er him; his right hand was broken. He struggled out and rose upon his feet. Though knowing well that his last hour had come, and that he could not scape from that dark day, yet fled he from Gudarz toward the hill.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 39 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 兩軍的兩位首領，那兩位精明的老者，隨即拿起弓與箭。古達爾茲挑選了一支楊木箭，那箭能穿透鐵甲，他奮力射出，射穿了敵將坐騎的鎧甲，那馬顫抖、喘息，頹然倒地。皮蘭也隨之倒下；他的坐騎在他身上翻滾；他的右手折斷了。他掙扎著爬出，站了起來。儘管他深知自己的最後時刻已至，明白自己無法逃脫這黑暗之日，卻仍從古達爾茲面前逃向山丘。

passages.text: O famous paladin! what aileth thee that thou dost foot it thus like game before me? shouted Gudarz, weeping bitterly; ask quarter for thy life that I may bear thee still living to the Shah; that conquering one will pardon thee because, like me, thou art a hoary paladin. Now God forbid! Piran replied: God grant that no such ill befall my latter end and I survive. To beg my life were heaviness indeed! Born was I in the world for death, and I thus fighting put my neck within thy power.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 39 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「啊，著名的勇士！你怎麼了，竟像獵物一般在我面前徒步奔逃？」古達爾茲痛哭著喊道，「為你的性命求饒吧，好讓我將你活著帶到沙阿面前；那位常勝之君會赦免你，因為你和我一樣，都是白髮蒼蒼的勇士。」「如今但願神不許！」皮蘭答道，「願神不讓這般禍患降臨我的末路，讓我得以存活。乞求活命實是沉重之事！我生於世間本為赴死，而我如今這般奮戰，已將自己的脖頸送入你的掌中。」

title.en: Khusrau Builds Piran a Charnel and Executes Gurwi
title.zh: 霍斯勞葬皮蘭而誅吉爾維

region.en: Mountain of the charnel (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 陵墓之山（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. IV, Twelve Rukhs sec. 47

summary.en: The Shah surveyed the slain and, when he saw the Turkman general, shed tears of sorrow, remembering Piran's good offices: thou hast been troubled for me all my life; this man deplored the blood of Siyawush, and in that matter gave offence to none; but Ahriman seduced his heart and turned his rede to other ends. The mountain was Piran's grave, and Khusrau in his affection had a charnel built, and raised its summit to the turning sky; within it there were set up princes' thrones, and they placed the Turkman paladins thereon with belted waists and crowns upon their heads. Then Khusrau looked upon Gurwi, the son of Zira, cursing him as he deserved, and bade disjoint Gurwi with cords and fling into a stream, first cutting off the head.
summary.zh: 王巡視屍場，見圖蘭主帥而落淚，追念皮蘭平生的恩義：「他一生為我憂勞；他憐惜西亞瓦什之血，未曾開罪於人；只是阿赫里曼蠱惑其心。」皮蘭葬於山中，霍斯勞因情築陵，陵頂直指蒼穹，內設君王寶座，讓圖蘭勇士束腰戴冠端坐其上。隨後王直面弑西亞瓦什的兇手吉爾維，咒其罪愆，先斬其首，再以繩拆解其身投入河中。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; royal mourning and justice. No living community restriction.

passages.text: The Shah then surveyed the slain and, when he saw the Turkman general, shed tears of sorrow, remembering Piran's good offices; his heart burned so that thou hadst said: it flameth! Ill fortune is a Dragon grim and snareth great lions with its breath, he made oration o'er that chieftain's death: thou hast been troubled for me all my life, and hast for my sake laboured strenuously. This man deplored the blood of Siyawush, and in that matter gave offence to none; but Ahriman seduced his heart and turned his rede to other ends.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 47 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 國王隨後檢視陣亡者，當他看見那位突厥將領時，不禁流下悲傷的眼淚，憶起皮蘭的種種恩義；他心中如焚，令人要說：它燃燒起來了！惡運是一條猙獰的巨龍，以氣息羅陷雄獅，他為那位首領之死而致辭：你一生為我憂勞，為我竭力奔走。此人痛惜西亞武什之血，於此事上未曾開罪於人；但阿赫里曼蠱惑了他的心，將他的謀劃引向別處。

passages.text: He ordered that the body should be washed with musk, pure camphor, and rose-water mixed with spices, and embalmed with musk and camphor, and clad it stainless with brocade of Rum. The mountain was Piran's grave, and Khusrau in his affection had a charnel built, and raised its summit to the turning sky. Within it there were set up princes' thrones, such as befitted men of high degree, and they placed the Turkman paladins thereon with belted waists and crowns upon their heads.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 47 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他下令以麝香、純樟腦與玫瑰水調和香料洗淨遺體，再以麝香與樟腦防腐，並為它穿上潔淨的羅馬錦緞。那座山便是皮蘭的墳墓，霍斯魯因眷愛之情而建了一座骨塔，將其頂端高聳至旋轉的天穹。塔內設有君王們的寶座，正合高貴之人的身分，他們將那些腰束寶帶、頭戴冠冕的突厥勇士安置其上。

passages.text: Khusrau then looked upon Gurwi, the son of Zira, cursing him as he deserved, looked on that loathly face wherefrom the hair hung down like divs', and said: O God! Thou knowest the manifest and hidden. Of a truth Kaus had done amiss and grieved the Maker in that He raised up such a div as this 'gainst Siyawush. I wot not why Gurwi should hate that faultless one, but by His might who ruleth all and giveth good, I will have vengeance on Afrasiyab for Siyawush and soon. He bade disjoint Gurwi with cords and fling into a stream, first cutting off, as 'twere a sheep's, the head: so must I treat Afrasiyab, he said.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Twelve Rukhs sec. 47 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 霍斯魯隨後望向齊拉之子古爾維，按他所應得地詛咒他，望著那張可憎的臉——其上毛髮如妖魔般垂落——說道：啊，神啊！你洞悉顯明與隱微之事。考斯確曾行惡，觸怒造物主，因祂興起這樣一個妖魔來對付西亞武什。我不知古爾維為何要憎恨那無瑕之人，但憑那統御萬物、賜予美善者的權能，我必為西亞武什向阿弗拉西亞布復仇，且為時不遠。他下令以繩索將古爾維肢解，投入河中，先如宰羊般斬下其首：他說，我必如此對待阿弗拉西亞布。

title.en: Kai Khusrau Walks into the Mountain and Vanishes
title.zh: 卡伊霍斯勞登山隱逝

region.en: Mountains beyond Iran (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊朗境外群山（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. IV, Kai Khusrau secs. 62-63

summary.en: Khusrau, his vengeance wrought, makes Luhrasp Shah and leads seven chiefs toward the mountains: my day hath passed. A hundred thousand Iranians follow weeping; three turn back at his command — Zal, Rustam, and old Gudarz — but Tus, Giv, Fariburz, Bizhan, and Gustaham press on. At a spring by night the Shah bathes and recites the Zandavasta: farewell for ever! when the sky shall bring the sun again ye shall not look on me henceforth save in your dreams. When the sun rose the Shah had disappeared; then there came up storm and cloud, the sky became as 'twere a lion's hide, and when the snow had hoisted sail upon the earth the lances of the nobles disappeared — under it they struggled for a while, and at the last strength failed them and they yielded up sweet life.
summary.zh: 大仇已報，霍斯勞立盧赫拉斯普為王，攜七位名將入山：「我的日子已滿。」十萬伊朗人含淚相隨；扎勒、魯斯塔姆、古達爾茲三人奉命折返，圖斯、吉夫、法里布爾茲、比讚與古斯塔哈姆執意前行。泉畔之夜，王沐浴誦經：「永別了！明日太陽重升，你們只能在夢中見我。」日出之時，王已無蹤；隨即風雪驟起、天幕如獅皮，長矛沉入雪海——五壮士掙扎片刻，氣絕於雪底。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the vanished-king motif (cf. Arthur in Celtic tradition). No living community restriction.

passages.text: Khusrau commanded that Luhrasp should come, and said to him: my day hath passed. Go thou, maintain the usage of the royal throne, and in the world sow but the seed of good. From Iran went chieftains with the Shah, great, shrewd, and valiant, as Zal and Rustam, as Gudarz and Giv, the brave Bizhan and gallant Gustaham; the seventh was Fariburz, son of Kaus, the eighth famed Tus. The host marched troop on troop till from the waste they reached a mountain-top, while every archimage said privily: none in the world e'er told of such a case!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Khusrau sec. 62 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 霍斯魯命魯赫拉斯普前來，對他說：我的時日已盡。你去吧，維護王座的舊制，在世間只播撒善的種子。首領們隨國王自伊朗出發，皆偉岸、睿智而英勇，如扎爾與魯斯塔姆，如古達爾茲與吉夫，勇敢的比詹與豪邁的古斯塔哈姆；第七位是考斯之子法里布爾茲，第八位是著名的圖斯。大軍一隊接一隊行進，直至離開荒野抵達一座山頂，而每位大祭司都私下說道：世上從未有人講述過這樣的事！

passages.text: A multitude collected from all parts, and five score thousand of the Iranians, both men and women, went before the Shah in grief; the mount was full of wails and cries, and e'en the flints were moved. Quit not Iran nor give this ancient world a youthful Shah, the people said. Yon desert none may pass who hath not Grace and lofty stature, answered the king; three proud warriors attended to the bidding and turned back — Zal, Rustam, and the old Gudarz — but Tus and Giv and Fariburz, Bizhan, and gallant Gustaham would not return.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Khusrau sec. 62 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 四方之人聚集而來，十萬伊朗男女滿懷悲傷地走在國王之前；山上充滿哀號與哭喊，連燧石也為之動容。眾人說道：不要離開伊朗，不要給這古老的世界一位年輕的國王。國王答道：那荒漠，若無靈光與高大身軀者，無人能過。三位高傲的勇士遵從命令而折返——扎爾、魯斯塔姆與年邁的古達爾茲——但圖斯、吉夫與法里布爾茲、比詹與豪邁的古斯塔哈姆都不願回去。

passages.text: At length a spring was seen upon the way, and thither went the aspiring Kai Khusrau. Here let us make our sojourn for the night, said the Shah, and talk at large together of the past, for henceforth nobody will see me more. What time the radiant sun shall raise its flag, then is the time when I shall pass away, and haply with Suriish for company. As night advanced the famous Kaian went before his God, bathed, head and body, in the limpid stream, reciting to himself the Zandavasta, and thus addressed those famous men of lore: farewell for ever! when the sky shall bring the sun again ye shall not look on me henceforth save in your dreams.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Khusrau sec. 62 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 終於，途中見到一處泉水，志存高遠的凱·霍斯魯便往那裡去。國王說：今夜我們就在此停留，一同暢談往事，因為從今以後再無人能見到我。當光輝的太陽升起旗幟之時，便是我離去之刻，或許有蘇魯什相伴。夜色漸深，著名的凱揚族人在他的神面前，將頭與身浸入清澈的溪流中沐浴，獨自誦念《贊德阿維斯塔》，並如此對那些著名的博學之士說道：永別了！當天空再度帶來太陽時，你們從今以後只能在夢中見到我。

passages.text: The chieftains' heads were heavy at the news, and when the sun rose o'er the hills the Shah had disappeared. They roamed thence seeking him and saw no trace of Kai Khusrau; meanwhile there came up storm and cloud, the sky became as 'twere a lion's hide, and when the snow had hoisted sail upon the earth the lances of the nobles disappeared! They tarried in the snow, and under it they struggled for a while, and made a hollow space, but at the last strength failed them and they yielded up sweet life. Gudarz, son of Kishwad, shed tears, plucked out his hair, and tore his cheeks: none e'er saw such ills as come upon me from the offspring of Kaus!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Khusrau sec. 63 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 首領們聞訊後心情沉重，當太陽從山巒升起時，沙阿已經消失了。他們從那裡四處尋覓他，卻不見凱·霍斯魯的任何蹤跡；同時風暴與雲層湧起，天空變得宛如獅皮，當大雪在地面上揚帆而行時，貴族們的長矛也消失了！他們在雪中逗留，在雪下掙扎了一陣，挖出一個空穴，但最終力竭，交出了甜美的生命。基什瓦德之子古達爾茲流淚、扯髮、抓破雙頰：從未有誰見過像我這般因考斯後裔而遭受的災禍！

title.en: Zarduhst Appears with Fire from Paradise
title.zh: 扎爾杜什特持天堂之火顯現

region.en: Palace of Gushtasp at Balkh (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 巴爾赫古什塔斯普王宮（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Gushtasp secs. 2-4

summary.en: A Tree appeared on earth within the palace of Gushtasp and grew up to the roof, a Tree whose roots spread far and wide, whose leafage was precept and its fruitage wisdom, a Tree right fortunate and named Zarduhst, the slayer of malignant Ahriman. I am a prophet and thy guide to God, said he, and brought a censer filled with fire: this have I brought with me from Paradise; the Maker said take thou this, and look upon the heaven and the earth, because I made them not of dust and water. When the good Shah had heard of that good Faith, his valiant brother Zarir and all the mighty chiefs assumed the cincture and received the Faith; he set up Fanes of Fire and first established the Fire of Mihr Barzin, and Zarduhst planted the noble cypress of Kishmar before the portal.
summary.zh: 一棵神樹在古什塔斯普宮中生長至屋頂——其根深廣、其葉為訓、其果為智——此樹名扎爾杜什特，「誅滅惡神阿赫里曼者」。「我是先知，是你通神的引路人。」他捧著盛火香爐：「此火我自天堂攜來；造物主說：『天地非由塵水所造——看這火焰便知我的創造。』」賢王與弟扎里爾及群臣繫上聖帶、皈依真教；王遍設火廟，首立米赫爾·巴爾津聖火，先知於火廟前植下基什馬爾神柏。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the coming of Zoroaster in the Shahnama. Prophet-vision cluster; handle as literature. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Thus passed a while, and then a Tree appeared on earth within the palace of Gushtasp, and grew up to the roof, a Tree whose roots spread far and wide, a Tree with many branches, its leafage precept and its fruitage wisdom: how shall one die who eateth of such fruit? A Tree right fortunate and named Zarduhst, the slayer of malignant Ahriman. Thus said he to the monarch of the world: I am a prophet and thy guide to God.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 如此過了一段時日，隨後一棵樹出現在古什塔斯普宮殿內的地上，長及屋頂，這棵樹根鬚廣佈四方，枝葉繁茂，其葉為訓誡，其果為智慧：食此果者怎會死去？這是一棵極為幸運的樹，名為扎爾杜什特，即邪惡阿里曼的誅殺者。他對世界之王如此說道：我是先知，是你通往神的引導者。

passages.text: He brought a censer, filled with fire, and said: this have I brought with me from Paradise. The Maker of the world said: take thou this, and look upon the heaven and the earth, because I made them not of dust and water: behold herein how I created them. See now if any one could do this thing, save I that am the Ruler of the world? If thou acknowledgest My handiwork thou must acknowledge Me to be the Lord. Receive His good religion from the speaker, and learn from him His usage and the way; see that thou do as he directeth thee, choose wisdom, recognise this world as vile, and learn the system of the good religion, for kingship is not well when Faith is lacking.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他帶來一隻香爐，盛滿火焰，說道：這是我從天堂帶來的。世界的創造者說：取此物，觀看天與地，因為我並非以塵土與水造它們：在此觀看我如何創造了它們。現在看看，除我這世界之主外，可有任何人能行此事？你若承認我的手工，就必須承認我是主。從說話者那裡接受祂美好的宗教，從他那裡學習祂的習俗與道路；務必照他所指示你的去做，選擇智慧，認識到此世為卑劣，學習善宗教的體系，因為缺乏信仰時，王權便不完善。

passages.text: When that good Shah had heard of that good Faith, and had accepted it and its good customs, his valiant brother, glorious Zarir, who used to vanquish mighty elephants; the Shah, his father, now grown old at Balkh; the mighty chiefs from all the provinces, the wise physicians and the men of war, all gathered to the monarch of the earth, assumed the cincture and received the Faith. Then was the Grace of God made manifest, for evil left the hearts of evil men. Then mounting to his throne high-born Gushtasp dispatched his troops throughout the provinces, distributed archmages through the world, and set up Fanes of Fire: he first established the Fire of Mihr Barzin. Zarduhst then planted him a noble cypress before the portal of the Fane of Fire, and wrote upon that noble, straight-stemmed tree: Gushtasp is convert to the good religion.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當那位善良的沙阿聽聞了那善良的信仰，並接受了它及其良好習俗後，他英勇的兄弟、光榮的扎里爾——曾慣於征服巨象——；沙阿的父親，如今在巴爾赫已年老；來自各省的強大首領，智慧的醫師與戰士，全都聚集到大地之君面前，繫上腰帶，接受了信仰。於是神的恩典顯現了，因為邪惡離開了惡人的心。隨後，高貴出身的古什塔斯普登上王座，派遣軍隊遍佈各省，將大祭司分派到世界各地，並設立了火壇：他首先建立了米赫爾·巴爾津之火。扎爾杜什特隨後在火壇門前為他種下一棵高貴的柏樹，並在那棵高貴挺拔的樹上寫道：古什塔斯普已皈依善宗教。

title.en: Zarir Falls to Bidirafsh's Treacherous Dart
title.zh: 扎里爾中暗鏢而歿

region.en: Battlefield of Ayas (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿亞斯戰場（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Gushtasp sec. 14

summary.en: Zarir, brother of Gushtasp, rides into the enemy camp like blazing fire and wind amid the grass, and none that beheld withstood him. Arjasp, astound, offers his daughter's hand and the conduct of his host to whoever will throw the maddened Elephant from his steed, and at last the lusty Bidirafsh advances, that foul dog, that warlock, that old wolf. Adventuring not to face him openly, the enchanter skirmished round him stealthily and hurled unseen at him the double-headed dart: his royal mail was pierced, his kingly form bedrenched with blood, and he tumbled from his steed. Woe for that youthful, royal cavalier!
summary.zh: 古什塔斯普之弟扎里爾如烈火疾風般衝入敵營，所向披靡。阿爾賈斯普驚惶許諾：誰能將那頭狂象掀下馬，便以公主相許、授予兵權！最終那「惡犬、術士、老狼」比迪拉弗什應聲而出——不敢正面交鋒，卻繞行偷襲，暗中擲出雙頭鏢：王甲洞穿、君軀浴血，英雄墜馬。哀哉，那年輕的王族騎士！

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the war of religion cycle (Ayas = Khwarazm). No living community restriction.

passages.text: Then brave Zarir advanced before the host, bestriding his huge chestnut, threw himself upon the encampment of the enemy, like blazing fire and wind amid the grass, slew, and dispatched them to their last repose: none that beheld withstood him. Then Arjasp, perceiving that the prince had slaughtered many of name, cried loudly to his warriors: the warriors of Shah Gushtasp have slain full many a man of name among our troops, and now Zarir is in the midst of you, as 'twere a fierce wolf or a rending lion.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 隨後，勇敢的扎里爾挺進於大軍之前，跨騎著他巨大的栗色戰馬，如熾烈的火焰與草間之風般撲向敵營，誅殺並送他們歸於最後的安息：見到他的人無一能抵擋。阿爾賈斯普見王子已屠殺許多有名之士，便向他的戰士們高聲喊道：古什塔斯普沙阿的戰士們已誅殺了我們軍中眾多有名之人，如今扎里爾就在你們中間，宛如一頭兇猛的狼或一頭撕裂獵物的獅子。

passages.text: We must devise a remedy for this, or trudge back to Turan, said Arjasp; what man of you in quest of fame will go forth man-like, alone, and compass world-renown? I will bestow on him my daughter's hand, and give to him the conduct of my host. The soldiers answered not a word, for all feared that Wild Boar. At last the lusty Bidirafsh advanced, the foul, that dog, that warlock, that old wolf, and spake thus to Arjasp: O mighty Sun! I will confront yon raging Elephant; if I shall seize and fling him to the dust before the king, let me be leader of this countless host.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿爾賈斯普說：我們必須為此想出對策，否則就得跋涉回圖蘭；你們中有誰為求名聲，願像個男子漢般獨自出戰，贏得舉世聞名？我將把女兒許配給他，並將我軍的統帥權交給他。士兵們一言不發，因為所有人都懼怕那頭野豬。最後，強壯的比迪拉夫什上前——那污穢者、那狗、那巫師、那老狼——對阿爾賈斯普如此說道：哦，強大的太陽！我願迎戰那頭狂暴的象；若我能在國王面前將他擒住並摔落塵埃，就讓我做這支無數大軍的統帥。

passages.text: That foul enchanter with the loathly form went toward Zarir, the leader of the folk, but seeing from afar his fearsome fury, his beard besoiled, his eyes fulfilled with dust, a mace like Sam the hero's in his hand, and slain before him heaped up like a mountain, adventured not to face him openly, but skirmished round him stealthily and hurled unseen at him the double-headed dart. His royal mail was pierced, his kingly form bedrenched with blood. He tumbled from his steed. Woe for that youthful, royal cavalier! Foul Bidirafsh alighted, stripped the prince, and bare off to the king the horse and girdle, the standard and the goodly, jewelled crown.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那形貌可憎的邪惡巫師走向部族首領扎里爾，但從遠處望見他可怕的怒容、沾滿污穢的鬍鬚、滿是塵土的眼睛、手中握著如英雄薩姆般的狼牙棒，以及在他面前堆積如山的屍首，便不敢公然與他對陣，只在他周圍偷偷游鬥，暗中向他擲出雙頭飛鏢。他的王族鎧甲被刺穿，王者之軀浸滿鮮血。他從坐騎上翻落。哀哉，那年輕的王族騎士！邪惡的比迪拉夫什下馬，剝去王子的衣甲，帶著馬匹與腰帶、旗幟與華美鑲寶的冠冕，奔回國王那裡。

title.en: Nastur and Asfandiyar Slay Bidirafsh
title.zh: 納斯圖爾與阿斯凡迪亞爾誅比迪拉弗什

region.en: Battlefield of Ayas (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿亞斯戰場（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Gushtasp sec. 17

summary.en: Nastur, the slaughtered prince's son, rides forth on his father's Bihzad: Nastur am I, the offspring of Zarir; where is that warlock Bidirafsh who holdeth the flag of Kawa? Bidirafsh comes on wearing Zarir's mail and wielding the selfsame sword wherewith he had overthrown Zarir; seeing Asfandiyar advance, he hurled his baneful weapon at the prince to darken that radiant face: it missed the prince, who caught it in his hand and pierced, a hero's stroke, his foeman's liver, so that the point came out the other side. Thus Bidirafsh fell from his steed and perished, and Asfandiyar, stripping off the armour of Zarir from that ancient warlock, severed the head and brought back to the Shah the prince's dun steed.
summary.zh: 扎里爾之子納斯圖爾騎父親的比赫扎德出陣：「吾乃扎里爾之子！那竊取卡瓦戰旗的術士何在？」比迪拉弗什披著扎里爾的鎧甲、持那把弑主的寶劍而來；見阿斯凡迪亞爾逼近，擲出毒鏢欲遮其光輝容顏——王子接鏢在手，一擊貫穿其肝！術士墜馬而亡；阿斯凡迪亞爾剝其甲、斬其首，牽回父王的坐騎與戰旗。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; blood-vengeance episode. No living community restriction.

passages.text: The Shah then gave his steed Bihzad, his helm of steel, and sable breastplate to Nastur, the slaughtered prince's son who, armed and mounted, rode forth between the opposing hosts and, halting before the battle of the enemy, heaved from his breast a deep, cold sigh, and cried: Nastur am I, the offspring of Zarir: the lion dareth not encounter me. Where is that warlock Bidirafsh who holdeth the flag of Kawa?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 17 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是沙阿將他的坐騎比赫扎德、他的鋼盔與黑色胸甲賜給納斯圖爾，即那位被殺王子的兒子。他披甲上馬，騎行於兩軍之間，在敵陣之前勒住韁繩，從胸中吐出深沉而冰冷的嘆息，喊道：我乃納斯圖爾，扎里爾的子嗣：獅子也不敢與我交鋒。那手持卡瓦旗幟的巫師比迪拉夫什何在？

passages.text: Then Bidirafsh went forth at once, he bare the violet flag, was mounted on the charger of prince Zarir, and wore the prince's mail, advancing in his pride toward Nastur. Men told the glorious Asfandiyar, the Shah's son, of their combating, who made all haste to go to them. Now when that chief of sorcerers beheld this, and perceived what man now was advancing to assail him, he urged his charger from amid the fray, and hurled his baneful weapon at the prince to darken if he might that radiant face.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 17 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是比迪拉夫什立刻出陣，他持著紫色旗幟，騎著扎里爾王子的戰馬，穿著王子的鎧甲，傲然向納斯圖爾推進。有人將他們交戰之事稟報沙阿之子、榮耀的阿斯凡迪亞爾，他急忙趕往他們那裡。那巫師之首見此情景，察覺如今是何人前來攻擊他，便從混戰中催馬而出，向王子擲出他那致命的武器，若能便使那光輝的面容黯淡。

passages.text: It missed the prince, who caught it in his hand and pierced, a hero's stroke, his foeman's liver, so that the point came out the other side. Thus Bidirafsh fell from his steed and perished, experiencing the might of Kaian birth. Asfandiyar dismounted from his steed, and stripping off the armour of Zarir from that ancient warlock, whose head he severed from its trunk withal, he carried off the prince's glossy charger, the flag, and head of worthless Bidirafsh. The Kaian army raised a shout: the prince hath triumphed, hath overthrown the foe, gone forth, and brought the dun steed back!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 17 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 武器未中王子，王子以手接住，英雄般的一擊刺穿敵人的肝臟，以致尖端從另一側穿出。比迪拉夫什就此從坐騎上墜落身亡，親身體驗了凱揚血脈的威力。阿斯凡迪亞爾下馬，從那老巫師身上剝下扎里爾的鎧甲，並將他的頭顱從軀幹上斬下，帶走了王子的光澤戰馬、旗幟與卑劣的比迪拉夫什的首級。凱揚軍中爆出吶喊：王子得勝了，擊倒了敵人，出陣歸來，帶回了那匹褐色駿馬！

title.en: Asfandiyar and the Dragon in the Sword-Box
title.zh: 阿斯凡迪亞爾劍匣鬥龍

region.en: Stages on the road to the Brazen Hold (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 通往銅堡的路上（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Seven Stages sec. 4

summary.en: Gurgsar warns the prince of an awesome dragon whose breath doth draw forth from the deep the fish, a flame of fire proceeding from its maw, its body a mountain made of flint. Asfandiyar has carpenters build a wooden carriage all set about with swords and a box, harnessed two noble steeds, and drives at the dragon; the horses strove to 'scape its mischief, but it sucked them in, them and the break, and in his box dismayed the warrior: in the dragon's gullet stuck the sword-blades, and blood poured forth like a sea. Tortured by the points and chariot the dragon by degrees grew weak, and the gallant warrior, arising from the box, hacked the dragon's brains till fumes of venom overpowered him and he tumbled mountain-like and swooned away.
summary.zh: 古爾格薩爾示警：前方有巨龍，「呼氣可自深海引出遊魚，口吐烈焰，軀如燧石之山」。王子命木匠造一輛四面插劍的木車、附一座劍匣，親坐其中，驅雙駿直衝巨龍；駿馬欲逃卻被連車吸入口中——龍喉被劍刃卡住，鮮血如海湧出；魔龍受刺與車磨，漸漸力竭；王子自匣躍出，如獅狂斫其腦，直至毒煙熏得他如山傾倒、昏厥於地。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the Seven Stages of Asfandiyar (Haft Khan counterpart of Rustam's). No living community restriction.

passages.text: Gurgsar returned reply: gone hast thou into battle like a fire, and made a shift to over-pass these bales, but know'st not what will come on thee tomorrow; there will encounter thee an awesome dragon, whose breath doth draw forth from the deep the fish; a flame of fire proceedeth from its maw; its body is a mountain made of flint. Asfandiyar replied: thou evil one! I mean to drag thee in thy chains with me to be a witness that this sharp-clawed dragon escapeth not my trenchant scimitar.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古爾格薩爾回答說：你如烈火般投入戰鬥，設法越過了這些災厄，卻不知明日將有何事臨到你身上；將有一條可怕的巨龍與你相遇，牠的氣息能從深淵中吸出魚來；火焰從牠的喉嚨噴出；牠的身軀是一座由燧石構成的山。阿斯凡迪亞爾回答：你這惡徒！我打算用你的鎖鏈把你拖在身邊，作為見證，證明這利爪巨龍逃不過我鋒利的彎刀。

passages.text: At his command some carpenters were fetched, and therewithal some long and heavy beams. He had a goodly wooden carriage built all set about with swords and with a box, and harnessed to the break two noble steeds. Afar the dragon heard the rumble and beheld the prancing of the battle-steeds; it came like some black mountain, and thou wouldst have said: the sun and moon are darkened. Its two eyes seemed fountains bright with blood, while from its gullet fire issued, and like some dark cavern gaped its jaws.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他下令召來一些木匠，並備好一些又長又重的橫樑。他造了一輛精良的木製戰車，四周遍插刀劍，並設有一個箱籠，又將兩匹駿馬套在車前。巨龍在遠處聽見隆隆聲響，望見戰馬騰躍；牠如黑色山巒般而來，你會說：日月都黯淡了。牠的雙眼宛如鮮血映照的泉眼，火從牠的咽喉噴出，牠的巨口如黑暗的洞穴般張開。

passages.text: It bellowed at Asfandiyar, who, seeing the monster, drew his breath and turned to God for help. The horses strove to 'scape the dragon's mischief, but it sucked them in, them and the break, and in his box dismayed the warrior. In the dragon's gullet stuck the sword-blades, and blood poured forth like a sea; it could not free its gullet, for the swords were sheathed within it. Tortured by the points and chariot the dragon by degrees grew weak, and then the gallant warrior, arising from the box, clutched his keen glaive with lion-grip and hacked the dragon's brains till fumes of venom rising from the dust overpowered him; he tumbled mountain-like, and swooned away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 牠向阿斯凡迪亞爾咆哮，阿斯凡迪亞爾見了這怪物，便屏住氣息，轉向上帝求助。眾馬奮力想逃離巨龍的禍害，牠卻將牠們連同戰車一併吸入，令那勇士在廂中驚惶失措。劍刃卡在巨龍的咽喉裡，鮮血如海般湧出；牠無法鬆脫咽喉，因為劍已深插其中。巨龍受劍尖與戰車折磨，漸漸衰弱，於是那英勇的勇士從廂中起身，以獅爪般的勁力抓住鋒利的刀劍，猛砍巨龍的頭顱，直到從塵土中升起的毒煙將他壓倒；牠如山崩般倒下，他也昏厥過去。

title.en: Asfandiyar Slays the Simurgh
title.zh: 阿斯凡迪亞爾誅西摩爾格

region.en: Mountain of the Simurgh (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西摩爾格之山（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Seven Stages sec. 6

summary.en: Gurgsar warns of a bird imperious, one like a flying mountain, called Simurgh by merchants: with its claws it beareth off the elephant at sight, the pard on land, the crocodile from water; upon its mountain-home it hath two young, and when it flieth the earth is impotent, the sun is put to shame. The hero laughs — I will sew up its shoulders with mine arrows — and drives at the peak: the Simurgh, swooping down like some dark cloud obscuring sun and moon, essayed to seize the chariot with its talons, but transfixed its legs and pinions with the swords; it beat awhile with claws and beak while strength remained, and then was still. Its young flew off with screams and weeping tears of blood, and Asfandiyar hewed to pieces with his sword that bird now mastered, once so masterful.
summary.zh: 古爾格薩爾又報：「有一飛山般的神鳥——商人稱之西摩爾格；一爪便能擄象、擒豹、拔鱷；山巢之中還有兩隻雛鳥；其翔時大地失色、太陽蒙羞。」王子大笑：「我以神箭縫其羽翼！」驅車至山巔；神鳥如蔽日黑雲俯衝欲攫戰車，卻被劍陣刺穿腿與翼；掙扎片刻便寂然不動。雛鳥泣血哀鳴而去；王子出匣揮劍，將這不可一世的巨鳥碎屍於地。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; pairs with Rustam's Simurgh fosterage (zal-simurgh). No living community restriction.

passages.text: He answered: O Elephant of war in battle-time! Upon this stage thou hast a harder task: be more than ever cautious and alert, thou wilt behold a mount, with head in air, and thereupon a bird imperious, one like a flying mountain, combative, and called Simurgh by merchants. With its claws it beareth off the elephant at sight, the pard on land, the crocodile from water, and feeleth not the effort. Upon its mountain-home it hath two young, and when it flieth the earth is impotent, the sun is put to shame.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 6 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他答道：啊，征戰之時的戰象！在此階段你有一項更艱難的任務：務必比以往更加謹慎警覺，你將見到一座山峰，其首高聳入雲，其上有一隻威猛的鳥，狀如飛行之山，好鬥，商人稱之為西摩格。牠一見大象便以爪攫走，陸上的豹、水中的鱷魚亦然，且毫不費力。在牠山中的巢穴裡有兩隻幼鳥，當牠飛翔時，大地無能為力，太陽也為之失色。

passages.text: The hero laughed: a wonder! I will sew up its shoulders with mine arrows, cleave its breast with Indian scimitar, and bring its head from height to dust. He spying in air a peak stayed in its shadow break and steed, absorbed in contemplation. The Simurgh marked from the mount the box, the troops behind it, and all their trumpeting, and, swooping down like some dark cloud obscuring sun and moon, essayed to seize the chariot with its talons, as leopard seizeth quarry, but transfixed its legs and pinions with the swords, and all its might and glory passed away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 6 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那英雄笑道：真是奇事！我要用箭縫住牠的雙肩，以印度彎刀劈開牠的胸膛，將牠的頭從高處打落塵埃。他望見空中一座山峰，便停在它的陰影下，讓戰車與戰馬歇息，凝神沉思。西摩格從山上望見那廂、其後的軍隊以及他們所有的號角聲，便如遮蔽日月的一片烏雲般俯衝而下，試圖以利爪抓住戰車，如同豹攫取獵物，卻被劍刺穿了雙腿與雙翼，牠所有的力量與榮耀就此消逝。

passages.text: It beat awhile with claws and beak while strength remained, and then was still. On seeing this its young flew off with screams and weeping tears of blood down from the eyry, blurring every eye beneath their shade. When the Simurgh thus sank with all its wounds and bathed steeds, box, and break in blood, Asfandiyar, all armed and shouting, emerged and hewed to pieces with his sword that bird now mastered, once so masterful; then prayed thus to the Maker who had given such mastery to him in good and ill: O righteous Judge! Thou hast bestowed upon me wisdom, puissance, and prowess, hast driven out the sorcerers and been my Guide to every good.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 6 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 牠以爪與喙搏擊了一會兒，直到力氣耗盡，然後便靜止不動。見此情景，牠的幼鳥尖叫著飛走，從巢中灑下血淚，其陰影使下方每一隻眼睛都為之模糊。當西摩格帶著滿身傷痕如此墜落，並將戰馬、廂與戰車都浸於血中時，阿斯凡迪亞爾全副武裝、高聲呼喊著現身，以劍將那隻如今已被制伏、昔日卻如此威猛的鳥砍成碎片；隨後他向那位在順境與逆境中都賜予他如此制勝之力的造物主祈禱：啊，公正的審判者！你已賜予我智慧、權能與英勇，驅逐了巫師，並引導我走向一切善。

title.en: The Simurgh Draws the Arrows from Rustam
title.zh: 西摩爾格為魯斯塔姆拔箭

region.en: Heights of Sistan (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 錫斯坦高地（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Rustam and Asfandiyar secs. 23-25

summary.en: Zal, the well-beloved, goes to a lofty height with three censers and burns a plume of the Simurgh; whenas the first watch of the night had passed, gazing from the eminence Zal saw the air filled with the fluttering plumes of the Simurgh. The body of the lion-hearted Rustam hath been bewounded, says Zal; the bird surveyed and sought to heal the wounds, sucked them and, drawing forth eight arrow-heads, stroked with her feathers on the wounded parts, and Rustam was restored to might and Grace. She in like manner having called for Rakhsh employed her beak on him to make him whole, and drew out from his neck six arrow-heads.
summary.zh: 扎勒攜三座香爐登上高地，焚燒西摩爾格的一根羽毛；初更過後，天空中滿是神鳥的翎羽——神鳥臨凡。扎勒泣訴：「獅心之子魯斯塔姆傷重垂危！」神鳥診視傷處，吮淨膿血，拔出八支箭簇，以神羽輕撫傷口——英雄重獲神力與榮光。她又以喙為拉赫什治病，自其頸間取出六支箭簇；駿馬嘶鳴，英雄喜極而笑。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the Simurgh's plume is the healing token of the Zal cycle. No living community restriction.

passages.text: When both were set on this bold project Zal, the well-beloved, went to a lofty height, and carried from the palace censers three containing fire. With him went three brave sages. Now when the wizard reached the top he drew forth from brocade a plume of the Simurgh and, having raised a flame within a censer, consumed therein a portion of the feather. Whenas the first watch of the night had passed thou wouldst have said: the face of air is darkened! And gazing from the eminence Zal saw it filled with the fluttering plumes of the Simurgh.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 25 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當兩人決意進行這一大膽計劃時，深受愛戴的扎爾登上高處，從宮中取來三個盛火的香爐。三位勇敢的智者隨他同行。當那術士到達頂端時，他從錦緞中取出一根西摩格的羽毛，在香爐中燃起火燄，於其中燒去羽毛的一部分。當夜的第一更過去時，你定會說：天空的面容已暗了下來！扎爾從高處望去，見空中滿是西摩格拍動的羽毛。

passages.text: Just then the bird, surveying from the air and seeing fire ablaze with Zal before it, set seared and sad, swooped down upon the dust. What was't, O king! that made thee need these fumes? said the Simurgh. Zal answered: may the ills that miscreants have brought upon me fall upon my foes. The body of the lion-hearted Rustam hath been bewounded, and my care for him hath fettered me; his injuries raise fears about his life; Asfandiyar hath come against our land and knocketh only upon the door of war.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 25 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 就在那時，那鳥從空中俯瞰，見火燄熊熊燃燒，扎爾立於其前，便滿懷傷痛與悲傷，俯衝向地面。西摩格說道：啊，國王！是什麼使你需用這些煙霧？扎爾答道：願惡人加諸我身的災禍降臨到我的敵人身上。獅心魯斯塔姆的身體受了傷，我對他的憂慮使我不得自由；他的傷勢令我擔憂他的性命；阿斯凡迪亞爾已來犯我境，只敲響戰爭之門。

passages.text: The bird surveyed and sought to heal the wounds, sucked them and, drawing forth eight arrow-heads, stroked with her feathers on the wounded parts, and Rustam was restored to might and Grace. She said: bind up thy hurts and for a week shun danger, moisten one of these my feathers with milk and stroke therewith inside the wounds. She in like manner having called for Rakhsh employed her beak on him to make him whole, and drew out from his neck six arrow-heads, all that there were. Rakhsh neighed. The crown-bestower laughed for delight.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 25 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那鳥審視傷口，設法治療，吮吸傷處，取出八枚箭頭，並以羽毛撫拂傷處，魯斯塔姆遂恢復力量與神恩。她說：包紮你的傷口，七日之內避開危險，取我一根羽毛以乳汁浸濕，塗抹於傷口之內。她同樣召來拉赫什，以喙為他療治使其痊癒，從他頸中取出六枚箭頭，盡數拔出。拉赫什嘶鳴。賜冠者欣喜而笑。

title.en: The Tamarisk Shaft That Blinded Asfandiyar
title.zh: 白楊箭射盲阿斯凡迪亞爾

region.en: Field of Zabul (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 扎布勒戰場（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 27

summary.en: When Rustam knew that humbleness availed not before Asfandiyar he strung his bow and set therein the shaft of tamarisk, the arrow as the Simurgh had bidden, and prayed: thou seest my mind pure in intent; thou knowest that his contention is unjust; so visit not my crime with retribution, O Maker of the moon and Mercury. Asfandiyar perceived him tarrying long from strife: now thou shalt behold the arrows of Gushtasp. Then Rustam quickly fitted to his bow the tamarisk-shaft: he struck Asfandiyar full in the eyes, and all the world grew dark before that chief; the straight-stemmed Cypress bent, intelligence and Grace abandoned him, and the pious prince fell prone.
summary.zh: 魯斯塔姆知卑辭無用，便如神鳥所囑搭上白楊毒箭，向造物主祈禱：「我心純正，其戰不義；願祢勿因我罪降罰。」阿斯凡迪亞爾見他遲遲不戰，喝道：「且看古什塔斯普的神箭！」話音未落，白楊箭已正中雙目——光明之邦頓成黑暗，挺秀如柏的王子彎折倒下，智與恩棄他而去。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the great tragedy of Rustam's career. No living community restriction.

passages.text: When Rustam knew that humbleness availed not before Asfandiyar he strung his bow, and set therein the shaft of tamarisk with baneful points, and said: O Lord of sun and moon, who makest knowledge, Grace, and strength to wax! Thou seest my mind pure in intent, my soul, and self control, for much I toil to turn Asfandiyar from strife. Thou knowest that his contention is unjust, and how his traffic with me is all fight and prowess; so visit not my crime with retribution, O Maker of the moon and Mercury!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 27 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當魯斯塔姆得知在阿斯凡迪亞爾面前謙卑無用，便張弓搭上檉柳之箭，箭鏃塗有劇毒，說道：啊，日月之主，使知識、神恩與力量增長者！你見我心意純正、靈魂與自制，因我竭力使阿斯凡迪亞爾放棄爭鬥。你知他的爭執不義，知他與我交往盡是戰鬥與武力；故勿以懲罰加於我的罪過，啊，月與水星之創造者！

passages.text: Asfandiyar perceived him tarrying long from strife, and said to him: O famous Rustam! Thy soul is satiate of fight, but now thou shalt behold the arrows of Gushtasp, Luhrasp's own arrow-heads and lion-heart. Then Rustam quickly fitted to his bow the tamarisk-shaft as the Simurgh had bidden; he struck Asfandiyar full in the eyes, and all the world grew dark before that chief; the straight-stemmed Cypress bent, intelligence and Grace abandoned him. The pious prince fell prone, his bow of Chach dropped from his hands; the battlefield was reddened with his blood.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 27 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿斯凡迪亞爾見他久不交戰，便對他說：啊，著名的魯斯塔姆！你的靈魂已厭倦戰鬥，但如今你將見識古什塔斯普的箭，盧赫拉斯普親手所製的箭鏃與獅子之心。於是魯斯塔姆迅速依西摩格所囑，將檉柳之箭搭上弓；他正射中阿斯凡迪亞爾的雙眼，那位首領眼前頓時一片黑暗；筆直的柏樹彎折，智慧與神恩離他而去。那位虔誠的王子俯伏倒地，他的查奇弓從手中跌落；戰場被他的鮮血染紅。

passages.text: Said Rustam: thou hast brought this evil seed to fruit! Thou art the man who saidst: my form is brazen, and I dash high heaven to earth. Yet through one arrow hast thou turned from strife, and fallen swooning on thy noble charger. Meanwhile the famous prince had tumbled headlong down from his black steed's back and lay awhile till he recovered consciousness, sat up amid the dust, then seized the arrow by its end and drew it out, drew it out soaked in blood from point to feather.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 27 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 魯斯塔姆說：你已使這惡種結出果實！你就是那曾說：我的身軀是青銅所鑄，我能將高天擊落於地的人。然而僅憑一箭，你便退出了爭鬥，昏倒在你高貴的戰馬之上。其時那位著名的王子已從黑色駿馬背上頭朝下翻落，躺臥片刻直至恢復知覺，在塵土中坐起，然後抓住箭的末端拔出，拔出那浸透鮮血、從箭鏃到箭羽皆染血之箭。

title.en: Asfandiyar's Last Wishes to Rustam
title.zh: 阿斯凡迪亞爾臨終託孤

region.en: Field of Zabul (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 扎布勒戰場（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 28

summary.en: The son of Zal hath slain me not by prowess, says the dying prince: mark what I have in my hand — a shaft of tamarisk! Not Rustam or Simurgh or bow and arrow have robbed my body of its life in battle, for that hath been the doing of Gushtasp. He said to me: go and burn up Sistan; and now do thou with loving heart receive from me the charge of this my noble son, Bahman, wise, watchful, and my minister; keep him in gladness in Zabulistan, make a great man of him both in deed and word. Rustam lays his right hand on his breast: e'en if I die I will not fail herein, but will set Bahman upon the famous ivory throne.
summary.zh: 垂死的王子道：「殺我的非魯斯塔姆的勇力——看，我手中只握著一支白楊箭！奪去我性命的不是神鳥、弓箭，而是古什塔斯普。他曾命我焚燒錫斯坦……請以愛心接納我那賢明審慎的兒子巴赫曼，養於扎布勒，教他武藝禮樂，使他成為偉人。」魯斯塔姆右手撫胸：「縱我一死，也必不負所託；我將親立巴赫曼於象牙寶座之上。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: In this world have I toiled exceedingly in public and in private to establish the way of God and wisdom as the guide thereto, but when through me the enterprise had grown illustrious, and when the hands of Ahriman were barred from wickedness, fate stretched its lion's claws and brought me down as though an onager! And now my hope is that in Paradise my heart and soul may reap what they have sown. The son of Zal hath slain me not by prowess. Mark what I have in my hand: a shaft of tamarisk! That wood hath closed my lifetime by the practice of the Simurgh and of resourceful Rustam.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 28 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在此世間，我於公開與私下皆竭力辛勞，以確立上帝之道與智慧為其指引，但當事業因我而顯赫，當阿赫里曼之手被阻於邪惡之外，命運卻伸出獅爪，將我擊倒如同野驢！如今我的希望是，在樂園中我的心與靈魂能收穫他們所播種的。扎爾之子並非以勇力殺我。看我手中之物：一根檉柳之箭！那木頭藉西摩格與足智多謀的魯斯塔姆之術，終結了我的壽命。

passages.text: Then thus to Rustam spake Asfandiyar: my time is at an end. Avoid me not, arise and come to me, since all our schemes are changed, that thou mayst hear my last requests upon my son's behalf, my chiefest Pearl. Not Rustam or Simurgh or bow and arrow have robbed my body of its life in battle, for that hath been the doing of Gushtasp. He said to me: go and burn up Sistan; from this time forth I would have no Nimruz.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 28 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 然後阿斯凡迪亞爾如此對魯斯塔姆說：我的時辰已盡。勿避開我，起來到我這裡來，因我們的一切謀劃皆已改變，好讓你聽我為我兒子——我最珍貴的珍珠——所作的最後請求。並非魯斯塔姆、西摩格或弓箭在戰鬥中奪去我身體的生命，因那是古什塔斯普所為。他對我說：去燒毀錫斯坦；從今往後，我不要尼姆魯茲。

passages.text: And now do thou with loving heart receive from me the charge of this my noble son, Bahman, wise, watchful, and my minister; keep him in gladness in Zabulistan, remembering what evil men may say; instruct him to array the host and order the chase, the combat, and the festival; make a great man of him both in deed and word. The matchless Rustam, hearing, stood and laid his right hand on his breast in acquiescence: e'en if I die I will not fail herein, he said, but bring thy words to pass, will set Bahman upon the famous ivory throne, and crown him with the heart-illuming crown.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Asfandiyar sec. 28 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 如今請你以慈愛之心，從我這裡接下對我这高貴之子巴赫曼的託付；他睿智、警醒，是我的大臣。請讓他在扎布利斯坦安享歡樂，記住惡人可能說些什麼；教導他整頓軍隊、安排狩獵、戰鬥與慶典；使他在言行兩方面都成為偉大之人。無與倫比的魯斯塔姆聽罷，起身將右手按在胸前以示應允：他說，縱然我死去，也絕不在此事上有負所託，必將你的話付諸實行，讓巴赫曼登上著名的象牙寶座，為他戴上那照亮心靈的王冠。

title.en: Dara Stabbed by His Own Ministers
title.zh: 大流士遭近臣刺殺

region.en: Flight toward Kirman (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 逃往克爾曼途中（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VI, Dara sec. 8

summary.en: Dara marches a third time against Sikandar with an army no longer bent on strife but broken-hearted and grown sick of war; the Iranians closed not with the Rumans hand to hand: they were the fox, the Rumans were the lion, and all the chiefs asked quarter. Dara turns away and flees lamenting with three hundred cavaliers and two ministers of high degree, Mahiyar and Janusiyar. Seeing the star so lofty thus set, they hold talk: Sikandar will give to us a province — and night gloomed, a storm arose, Janusiyar laid hand upon a dagger, stabbed the king upon the breast, that famed head reached its fall, and the troops deserted, one and all.
summary.zh: 大流士三度迎戰亞歷山大，然伊朗軍心已散——「他們是狐，羅馬人是獅」——眾將求饒。王泣而退走，身邊僅三百騎與兩位重臣馬希亞爾與賈努西亞爾。二人見王星已落，密議：「亞歷山大必封我等為省督！」夜黑風起，賈努西亞爾拔匕首刺入王胸，名王頭顱就此墜落，部眾作鳥獸散。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Alexander's Persianised biography (Sikandar). No living community restriction.

passages.text: When Dara led forth his troops, no army bent on strife, but broken-hearted and grown sick of war, the fortune of the Iranians drooped its head. They closed not with the Rumans hand to hand; they were the fox, the Rumans were the lion, and all the chiefs asked quarter, having come down from their pride to deep humility. Dara saw, turned away, and fled lamenting. With him there went three hundred cavaliers, the noblest of Iran.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Dara sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當達拉率軍出征時，那已不是一支一心求戰的軍隊，而是心懷悲傷、厭倦戰爭之眾，伊朗人的命運垂下了頭。他們沒有與羅馬人短兵相接；他們是狐狸，羅馬人是獅子，所有首領都請求寬恕，從驕傲跌入深深的謙卑。達拉見狀，轉身悲嘆而逃。隨他而去的還有三百名騎兵，皆是伊朗最尊貴之人。

passages.text: He had withal two ministers of high degree, who used to comrade him in fight. The name of one, an archimage, was Mahiyar, the other was called Janusiyar. These twain, on seeing their efforts fruitless and the star erewhile so lofty, and the glory of Dara thus set, held talk and said: this luckless man henceforth will see not crown and throne again; we needs must poniard him upon the breast, or smite his head with Indian sword. Sikandar will give to us a province. We shall be a crown upon the kingdom.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Dara sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他還有兩位地位崇高的臣子，常在戰事中與他為伴。其中一人是術士，名叫馬希亞爾，另一人名叫賈努西亞爾。這兩人見自己的努力徒勞無功，那顆不久前還如此高懸的星辰，以及達拉的榮耀竟如此隕落，便商議道：這個不幸之人從今往後再也見不到王冠與寶座了；我們必須以匕首刺其胸膛，或以印度之劍擊其頭顱。西坎達爾會賜我們一個行省。我們將成為王國頭上的冠冕。

passages.text: Both of them, one minister, the other treasurer, went with the Shah; Janusiyar, the chief, upon the left hand, Mahiyar to right. Night gloomed, a storm arose, Janusiyar laid hand upon a dagger, stabbed the king upon the breast, that famed head reached its fall, and then the troops deserted, one and all.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Dara sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們二人，一位大臣，一位司庫，隨沙阿同行；首領賈努西亞爾在左，馬希亞爾在右。夜幕降臨，風暴驟起，賈努西亞爾伸手握住匕首，刺入國王胸膛，那著名的頭顱就此倒下，隨後軍隊盡皆散去，一個不剩。

title.en: Dara's Last Wishes to Sikandar
title.zh: 大流士臨終遺言

region.en: Field of Dara's fall (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 大流士隕落之地（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)
