source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VI, Dara sec. 9

summary.en: The ministers come to Sikandar saying they have slain his enemy, and the Ruman's heart and soul are filled with rage and grief: on drawing nigh he gazed upon Dara and saw his breast all blood. He takes on his lap the wounded monarch's head, removes the royal crown, unclasps the warrior's mail, and says: I will resign to thee the realm and throne; but these that thus have wronged thee will I hang head-downward from two gibbets presently. Dara, on hearing this, began to speak: death is much nearer to me than the throne; beware of saying I by mine own might prevailed o'er this famed people; know that good and ill are both of God, and while thou livest give Him the praise.
summary.zh: 二臣來報「已誅敵王」；亞歷山大聞言悲憤交加，趨近見大流士胸前皆血。他將垂死之王攬於膝上，摘其冠、解其甲，泣曰：「我願讓還江山王座；至於這二賊，我必倒懸其身於絞架！」大流士留言：「死比王座更近；切勿自誇『憑己力勝此名族』——善惡皆出於神，生時當頌揚祂。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: The ministers came to Sikandar, saying: O Shah victorious and endowed with knowledge! we have surprised and slain thine enemy; the crown and throne of chiefs are his no more. Sikandar, having heard Janusiyar, said thus to Mahiyar: where is the foe whom thou hast overthrown? Show me the way. The two led on. The Ruman's heart and soul were filled with rage and grief. On drawing nigh he gazed upon Dara and saw his breast all blood, his countenance like fenugreek.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Dara sec. 9 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 兩位大臣來到西坎達爾面前，說道：啊，勝利而富有智慧的沙阿！我們已突襲並殺死了你的敵人；首領們的王冠與寶座不再屬於他了。西坎達爾聽罷賈努西亞爾的話，便對馬希亞爾說：你所推翻的敵人在哪裡？給我指路。二人引路前行。這羅馬人的心與靈魂充滿了憤怒與悲傷。走近時，他凝視達拉，見他胸膛滿是鮮血，面容如葫蘆巴般枯黃。

passages.text: He gave orders to alight and set a guard o'er those two ministers, and then, dismounting as swift as wind himself, took on his lap the wounded monarch's head, and, tarrying until the stricken should begin to speak, chafed with his hands the visage of Dara, removing from the head the royal crown, unclasping from the breast the warrior's mail, while showering tears on him because no leech was then at hand: I will resign to thee the realm and throne; but these that thus have wronged thee will I hang head-downward from two gibbets presently.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Dara sec. 9 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他下令下馬，並派人看守那兩位大臣，然後自己迅疾如風地下馬，將受傷君主的頭攬在膝上，等待那受創之人開口說話，同時用雙手揉搓達拉的面龐，從他頭上取下王冠，解開他胸前的戰甲，淚水灑落在他身上，因為當時身邊沒有醫生：我將把國土與王座讓給你；但這些如此加害於你的人，我即刻要將他們頭朝下吊死在兩座絞架上。

passages.text: Dara, on hearing this, began to speak, and said: may wisdom alway be thy mate. Sure am I that thou wilt be recompensed by God, the all-holy Judge, for these thy words; but as for what thou saidst — Iran is thine — death is much nearer to me than the throne; high heaven so willeth, whose joy is travail and whose profit loss. Beware of saying: I by mine own might prevailed o'er this famed people. Know that good and ill are both of God, and while thou livest give Him the praise.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Dara sec. 9 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 達拉聞此言，乃開口說道：願智慧永為汝之伴侶。我確信，全聖之審判者上帝必因汝此語而報償汝；然至於汝所言——伊朗歸汝——死亡之於我，較王座近之遠矣；高天如此意欲，其樂在勞苦，其利在損失。慎勿言：我以己力勝此著名之民。當知善與惡皆出於上帝，汝在世之日，當讚美祂。

title.en: Sikandar in the Gloom: Israfil and the Stones
title.zh: 亞歷山大入幽暗：伊斯拉菲爾與寶石之訓

region.en: The Gloom beyond the western dark (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 極西幽暗之地（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VI, Sikandar sec. 29

summary.en: Sikandar goes unattended toward the Fount of Life and prays: He will not die who nurtureth thus his soul; he takes two signets that shine like suns on water, one for his guide Khisr, who slips away to the Fount of Life, bathes, drinks, and returns apace. Sikandar finds a mountain with four aloewood columns, on each a huge green bird speaking in the Ruman tongue, and at the top beholds Israfil, with trump in hand and head uplifted, standing at his post, wind on his lips and moisture in his eye, till God shall bid him blow: O thou slave of greed! toil not so much, because some day a Call will reach thine ears. Then in the Gloom a voice cries: he that shall take a stone up from the road will grieve for what he beareth; and if he taketh none he will repent — and, emerging from the Gloom, each perceived the trick: their pockets were full of jewels.
summary.zh: 亞歷山大隻身尋訪「生命之泉」，攜兩枚遇水如日之印：一枚交引路人希茲爾——他卻悄然尋得聖泉、沐浴暢飲而歸。亞歷山大見山巔四根沉香柱、棲四隻操羅馬語的巨鳥；峰頂佇立著天使伊斯拉菲爾——號在唇邊、目含淚水，靜待神命：貪婪的僕人啊！莫要過勞，因為末日之號總會吹響。幽暗中又有聲音告誡：拾石者悔、不拾者亦悔——出得幽暗，才知囊中皆是寶石。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the Gihon/Water-of-Life quest fused with the angel of the Trumpet. No living community restriction.

passages.text: He tarried there until the sun, grown pale, sank in that fount of lapis-lazuli; he saw the wonder wrought by holy God, the Bright One's disappearance from the world. He chose the most enduring of his troops, took with him food for forty days and more, and sought and found a guide. Khisr, who was chief among the nobles of that folk, advised him, and Sikandar said: if we shall obtain the Water of Life then we will pass much time in prayer. He will not die who nurtureth thus his soul, and in his wisdom refugeth with God. I have two signets that in sight of water shine out at night like suns. Take one, lead on; the other one shall light me on my way.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 29 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他停留於彼，直至太陽轉為蒼白，沉入那青金石之泉；他見聖潔上帝所行之奇蹟，即那光明者之消失於世間。他從其軍中選取最為耐久者，攜四十日有餘之糧，尋得並找到一位嚮導。希茲爾，乃彼族貴族中之首領，為他獻策，西坎達爾說道：若我們得獲生命之水，則將以多時祈禱。如此滋養其靈魂、並以其智慧歸託於上帝者，必不死。我有兩枚印戒，於水前之夜間如太陽般閃耀。取其一，引路前行；另一則照我於途。

passages.text: Khisr left that station and all food behind him, and fared thus for two days and nights while none bestirred his lips to eat. Upon the third two ways showed mid the Darkness, and the Shah lost trace of Khisr. What while the prophet went toward the Fount of Life, exalting thus his living head to Saturn, bathed his body and head in that bright Water, sought no guard save God, drank, rested, and returned apace.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 29 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 希茲爾離開彼處，棄其所有食物於身後，如此行兩晝夜，其間無人動唇進食。至第三日，黑暗中現出兩條道路，沙赫遂失希茲爾之蹤。先知往赴生命之泉，如此將其活首高舉至土星，以那明淨之水沐浴其身與首，除上帝外不求守護，飲之，歇息，旋即返回。

passages.text: Sikandar reached the light and saw a mountain both high and bright, and on its top four columns of aloe-wood uplifted to the clouds; on every column was a mighty nest, and in each nest there sat a huge, green bird, which, speaking loudly in the Ruman tongue, hailed the victorious master of the world. He then descended and there saw Israfil, with trump in hand and head uplifted, standing at his post, wind on his lips and moisture in his eye, till God shall bid him blow. On seeing Sikandar he roared like thunder: O thou slave of greed! toil not so much, because some day a Call will reach thine ears.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 29 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 西坎達爾抵達光明處，見一山既高且明，其頂有四根沉香木柱高聳入雲；每柱之上有一巨巢，每巢之中坐一巨大綠鳥，以羅馬語高聲鳴叫，向那勝利之世界之主致敬。他遂下降，於彼見伊斯拉菲爾，手持號角，昂首而立於其崗位，風在其唇，濕在其目，直至上帝命其吹響。見西坎達爾，乃如雷鳴般吼道：汝貪婪之奴！勿如此勞苦，因有朝一日，一聲召喚將達汝耳。

passages.text: A cry ascended from the darksome heights: he that shall take a stone up from the road will grieve for what he beareth in his hand, and if he taketh none he will repent. The soldiers all gave ear; one man took of the stones; another left them; a third through indolence took little ones. When they reached the plain, emerging from the Gloom, each sought the truth and then perceived the trick: one had his bosom full of jewels cut, another his with jewels in the rough, and both regretted that they had so few; but sorrier still was he that picked up none.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 29 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 一聲呼喊自幽暗高處升起：凡從路上拾石者，將為其手中所持而悔；若一無所取，亦將懊悔。眾兵皆傾耳；一人取石；另一人棄之；第三人因怠惰而取小石。當他們出幽暗而抵平原，各人尋求真相，遂悟其中之詭：一人懷中滿是琢磨之寶石，另一人懷中滿是未琢之寶石，兩者皆悔其取之太少；然最為懊悔者，乃一無所取之人。

title.en: Sikandar Bars Yajuj and Majuj Behind Iron and Naphtha
title.zh: 亞歷山大築鐵障禦雅朱者與馬朱者

region.en: Cloud-capt mountain range of the east (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 東方插雲山脈（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VI, Sikandar sec. 30

summary.en: Marching eastward Sikandar finds a noble city whose people bewail their fortune: by reason of this cloud-capt mountain-range our hearts are full of anguish, for Yajuj there and Majuj give us no sleep; their faces all resemble those of beasts, their tongues are black, their eyes like blood. The Shah builds the Barrier: the iron and molten naphtha poured between the mountain-walls shut the wild tribes out of the world, and God keepeth it till the Day of Doom, when the hosts of Yajuj and Majuj shall break forth upon the earth.
summary.zh: 亞歷山大東行至一富城，百姓泣訴：因這座插雲山脈，雅朱者與馬朱者使我們不得安眠——他們面如獸、舌黑、目如血。王乃於兩山之間築起鐵障，灌以熔化的石腦油，將野族封於世界之外；神守護此障至審判之日，屆時雅朱者與馬朱者的大軍將破障而出。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the Gog-Magog wall shared with Qur'anic and Syriac traditions. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Two weeks he tarried and, when rested, marched. He set forth eastward, having seen the west; his purpose in the world was wayfaring. Now as he went he saw a noble city: no wind or dust passed o'er it, thou wouldst say. Whenas the drums beat on the elephants the chiefs came out two miles to welcome him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 30 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他停留兩週，待歇息既畢，乃行軍。他已見西方，遂啟程東行；其於世間之目的，乃在遠行。行進之間，見一宏偉之城：可謂無風無塵越過其上。當象上鼓聲響起，首領們出城兩哩以迎之。

passages.text: They loosed their tongues and thus bewailed their fortune: a very grievous case confronteth us, and we will tell it to the conquering Shah. By reason of this cloud-capt mountain-range our hearts are full of anguish, toil, and grief. Since for resistance we are powerless Yajuj there and Majuj give us no sleep, for when a portion of them reach our city our portion is all misery and travail. Their faces all resemble those of beasts, their tongues are black, their eyes like blood.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 30 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們放開喉舌，如此悲嘆自己的命運：一樁極其悲痛的事臨到我們身上，我們要把它稟告給征服者沙阿。因著這道高聳入雲的山脈，我們心中滿是痛苦、勞苦與憂傷。我們無力抵抗，那裡的雅朱者和馬朱者使我們不得安眠，因為當他們中有一部分人來到我們的城邑，我們這一份便盡是苦難與勞頓。他們的臉面全都像野獸的臉，他們的舌頭是黑的，他們的眼睛像血一般。

passages.text: The Shah bade smelt the iron and pour the molten naphtha between the mountain-walls, and built the Barrier which God keepeth till the Day of Doom, when the hosts of Yajuj and Majuj shall break forth upon the earth. So he made the world secure behind iron, and marched on, leaving the tribes to rage beyond the wall.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 30 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 沙阿下令熔煉鐵，並將熔化的石腦油澆灌在山壁之間，築起了那道屏障，真主一直守護它直到末日，那時雅朱者和馬朱者的眾軍將衝破而出，臨於大地。於是他以鐵使世界得保安寧，繼續前行，任那些部族在牆外咆哮。

title.en: The Speaking Tree Foretells Sikandar's Death
title.zh: 神語之樹預言死期

region.en: Grove of the twin tree (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 雙幹神樹林（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VI, Sikandar sec. 31

summary.en: Sikandar comes to a tree with two trunks and birds that speak. When Sol attained the apex of heaven's vault Sikandar heard aloft a cry proceeding from the leaves: why doth Sikandar roam so o'er the world, for he hath had his portion of good things, and, when he shall have reigned for twice seven years, must quit the throne of sovereignty? The female branches say: thou hast not long to live; do not thyself cloud and contract thy days. And the speaking tree said to the Shah: be speedy, and bind the baggage on; thy mother, kindred in Rum, and face-veiled ladies there will look on thee no more. Death in an alien land will come ere long.
summary.zh: 亞歷山大行至一株雙幹神樹，樹上有會說話的飛鳥。日中時分，樹葉間傳出可怕的預言：「亞歷山大啊，你已得世間應得之分；十四年之後必須讓出王座！」另一側的枝葉更道：「你命不久長，莫再自苦短日。」神樹直告：「速速收拾行裝；羅馬的母親與眷屬再也見不到你——客死異鄉之日不遠了。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the oracular trees of the sun and moon. No living community restriction.

passages.text: When Sol attained the apex of heaven's vault Sikandar heard aloft a cry proceeding from the leaves of that tall tree, an awful, boding cry. He feared and asked of the interpreter: shrewd, trusty friend! what say the talking leaves, because they bathe my heart in lymph of blood? The guide replied: the leaves upon the boughs of this tree say: why doth Sikandar roam so o'er the world, for he hath had his portion of good things, and, when he shall have reigned for twice seven years, must quit the throne of sovereignty?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 31 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當太陽到達天穹之頂，錫坎達爾聽見高處有一聲呼喊，發自那棵高樹的葉子，那是一聲可怖的、預示凶兆的呼喊。他心生畏懼，問那解語者道：精明可靠的友人啊！那會說話的葉子說些什麼，因為它們以血之液浸透我的心？那引路者回答說：這棵樹枝上的葉子說：錫坎達爾為何如此漫遊於世間，因為他已得了美物的一份，而當他統治了兩倍七年之後，就必須離開主權的寶座。

passages.text: Sikandar wept tears of blood; the guide's words wrung his heart. Thenceforth he spake to no one, but remained all sorrowful till midnight. Then the leaves upon the other trunk gave utterance. What is it that the other branches say? asked the Shah, and his informant solved the mystery: the female branches say: thou travailest in this wide world for greed and for addition. Thou hast not long to live; do not thyself cloud and contract thy days.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 31 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 錫坎達爾流下血淚；引路者的話絞痛了他的心。從那時起他不與任何人說話，只是滿懷憂傷直到午夜。隨後另一根樹幹上的葉子開口了。沙阿問道：另一邊的枝條說些什麼？他的稟報者解開了這謎：那雌性的枝條說：你在这廣闊世間為貪婪與增添而勞苦。你活不長久了；不要自己使你的日子蒙上陰雲、使之短促。

passages.text: The great king asked of the interpreter: inquire if I shall be in Rum when my dark day shall come, and if my mother see me not alive will she at last enshroud this face of mine? The speaking tree said to the Shah: be speedy, and bind the baggage on. Thy mother, kindred in Rum, and face-veiled ladies there will look on thee no more. Death in an alien land will come ere long; crown, diadem, and throne grow tired of thee.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 31 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那位偉大的君王問那解語者道：問一問，當我黑暗的日子來到時，我是否會在魯姆，若我的母親不能見我活著，她最終是否會為我這張臉裹上殮布？那會說話的樹對沙阿說：趕快，把行囊繫好。你的母親、魯姆的親族，以及那裡蒙著面紗的貴婦們，將不再見到你。死亡將不久在異鄉來臨；王冠、冕旒與寶座已對你生厭。

title.en: The Coffin of Sikandar and the Sages' Lament
title.zh: 亞歷山大之柩與智者輓歌

region.en: Iskandariya (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 亞歷山大里亞城（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VI, Sikandar secs. 37-39

summary.en: Knowing that his time was near, Sikandar bids carry his throne to the field; with failing voice he says: be devout, wise, modest, and heed all my last requests — and his life departed. They fired his palace, docked a thousand steeds, bore the golden bier out to the plain, and laved the corpse with rose-water and camphor; the wise Arastalis laid his hand on that strait coffin, saying: God-fearing Shah! where are thy prudence, knowledge, and rede that this strait coffin should become thy home? Another said: soon shall we be as thou art, thou that wast an uncut gem; another: why in this Wayside Inn laboriously didst thou employ thyself, since a narrow coffin is thine only wealth?
summary.zh: 自知大限將至，亞歷山大命人將御座抬至戰場，以微弱之聲囑託後事，隨即駕崩。全軍縞素、焚其宮殿、千馬斷鞍；金輦抬出，聖水香樟浴其遺體。賢者亞里士多德按柩而問：「敬神的王啊，你的智謀與遠見何在，竟讓這狹小棺槨成了你的居所？」群賢輓唱：「我們不久也將如此——你原是未雕之璞玉」；「你在這驛館中苦苦經營，所換得的唯有這口窄棺！」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: And knowing that his time was near, Sikandar bade carry from the palace to the field his throne. The troops bewailed his malady when they beheld the Shah's pale face. With failing voice said Caesar: be devout, wise, modest, and heed all my last requests, if ye would prosper both in soul and body. When I have gone the work is left for you, and fortune is not dealing ill with me. He spake, his life departed, and that Shah so famous, that host-shatterer, passed away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 37 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 錫坎達爾知道自己時日將近，便下令把他的寶座從宮中抬到曠野。眾軍見了沙阿蒼白的面容，都為他的病痛悲泣。愷撒以微弱的聲音說道：你們要虔誠、明智、謙遜，留心我所有的臨終囑託，若你們願在靈魂與身體上都得昌盛。我離去之後，這工便留給你們，而命運待我並不苛刻。他說完，生命便離去，那位如此著名的沙阿、那擊潰眾軍者，就此逝去。

passages.text: A cry went up from all the host and split the ears of heaven. The soldiers all strewed dust upon their heads. They fired his palace, and docked a thousand steeds, reversing all their saddles. They bore the golden bier out to the plain; a prelate laved the corpse with clear rose-water, and besprinkled thereon pure camphor. Of gold-woven brocade they made his winding-sheet, and, having shrouded thus that noble form beneath brocade of Chin, they covered it with honey to the feet and then sealed down the lid of that strait coffin: passed away that Tree so fruitful and so shadowing!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar sec. 37 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 全軍發出哀號，聲震天聽。士兵們盡皆將塵土撒於頭上。他們焚燒他的宮殿，牽來千匹駿馬，將所有馬鞍倒置。他們將金色靈柩抬至平原；一位教士以清澈的玫瑰水洗滌遺體，並在其上灑遍純淨的樟腦。他們以金線織成的錦緞製成裹屍布，如此將那高貴的身軀裹於中國錦緞之下後，從頭至腳覆以蜂蜜，然後封上那狹窄棺木的蓋子：那棵如此多果、如此蔭庇的樹就此逝去！

passages.text: They set his coffin on the plain; all earth was full of hue and cry, and above a hundred thousand flocked to Iskandariya to the coffin. The wise Arastalis stood forth and laid his hand on that strait coffin, saying: God-fearing Shah! where are thy prudence, knowledge, and rede that this strait coffin should become thy home? Another said: soon shall we be as thou art, thou that wast an uncut gem. Another said: why in this Wayside Inn laboriously didst thou employ thyself, since this is all that thou hast gained by toil? A narrow coffin is thine only wealth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Sikandar secs. 38-39 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們將他的靈柩置於平原之上；整個大地充滿了哭號之聲，十萬餘人湧向伊斯坎達里亞的靈柩。睿智的阿拉斯塔利斯挺身而出，將手放在那狹窄的棺木上，說道：敬畏真主的大王啊！你的明智、學識與謀略何在，竟使這狹窄的棺木成為你的歸宿？另一人說道：不久我們也將如你一般，你這塊未經雕琢的寶石。又一人說道：為何你在此路邊客棧中辛勤勞碌，因為這便是你勞苦所得的一切？一方狹窄的棺木便是你唯一的財富。

title.en: Bahram Gur Cancels a Hundredfold of Taxes
title.zh: 巴赫拉姆·古爾免征積欠

region.en: Istakhr of Pars (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 帕爾斯伊斯塔赫爾（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VII, Bahram Gur secs. 1-2

summary.en: Whenas Bahram Gur sat upon the throne the sun acclaimed him while the Shah adored the Maker. I give Him thanks for all His benefits; do ye too praise Him, and strive to keep His covenant unbroken. He bade Gushasp the scribe and Jawanwi the chief accountant approach, ordered them to cancel all arrears of taxes for the Iranians, and they added up the sum of the arrears and found it ninety and a hundred times three hundred thousand drachms: these he forgave, and burnt the registers, and all men rejoiced thereat, flung musk upon the Fire and blessed Bahram where New Year's Day and Sada feast were kept.
summary.zh: 巴赫拉姆·古爾登基，向造物主頌恩：「當讚美祂，謹守祂的盟約。」他命書記與稅務總管清點伊朗積欠的賦稅，共計九萬又三十萬德拉克馬——盡數豁免、焚燬稅冊；萬民歡騰，在歲首與薩達節之所向聖火撒香、祝福君王。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Bahram V (Bahram Gur), r. 420-438 CE. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Whenas Bahram Gur sat upon the throne the sun acclaimed him while the Shah adored the Maker, the all-seeing, watchful World-lord, the Lord of victory and majesty, the Lord of increase and of loss, then said: for He hath fashioned fortune, and my hopes and fears are all in Him. I give Him thanks for all His benefits; do ye too praise Him, and strive to keep His covenant unbroken.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 1 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當巴赫拉姆·古爾登上王座之時，太陽向他致敬，而沙王則崇拜造物主——那全見、警覺的世界之主，勝利與威嚴之主，增益與虧損之主——隨即說道：因祂締造了命運，我的希望與恐懼全在於祂。我為祂的一切恩惠向祂感恩；你們也當讚美祂，並努力使祂的盟約不被破壞。

passages.text: The Shah, that man of lore, then bade Gushasp, the scribe, with prudent Jawanwi, the chief accountant, approach, and ordered them to cancel all arrears of taxes for the Iranians. These two wise scribes went to their registers, added up the sum of the arrears, and found it ninety and a hundred times three hundred thousand drachms. These he forgave, and burnt the registers, and all men rejoiced thereat. Where New Year's Day and Sada feast were kept they flung musk upon the Fire and blessed Bahram the Shah.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 2 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 沙王，那位博學之人，隨即召來書記古沙斯普與精明能幹的首席會計賈萬維，命他們註銷伊朗人所有拖欠的稅款。這兩位睿智的書記前往他們的帳冊，將欠款總額相加，發現共計九十又一百個三十萬德拉克馬。他悉數免除，並焚燒了帳冊，眾人為此歡欣鼓舞。在慶祝新年與薩達節之處，他們向聖火投擲麝香，並為沙王巴赫拉姆祈福。

title.en: Bahram Gur Guest of the Water-carrier and the Jew
title.zh: 巴赫拉姆微服訪民間

region.en: Streets of the realm (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 王國街市（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VII, Bahram Gur secs. 3-5

summary.en: In disguise the Shah goes to the house of Lambak the water-carrier, who pledges his water-skins to buy a feast, and the king cuts up the meat himself and cooks it: we have been jolly in this house three days. Next night he knocks at the door of barren Baraham the Jew, who treats him scurvily — the Jew is very poor and every night reposeth, bare and hungry, on the ground — and Bahram, lodging outside, learns how the miser hoards; next day he seizes Baraham's hoards and bestows them all upon Lambak the poor host.
summary.zh: 君王微服投宿汲水人蘭巴克家中；窮漢典當水囊備宴，王親自切肉烹調：「我們在這屋裡快樂了三日！」次夜他敲響吝嗇猶太人巴拉罕的門，遭冷言拒絕——「那猶太人窮得很，夜夜露宿」——王便宿於門外窺其積藏；翌日沒其金庫，盡數賞賜好客的蘭巴克。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source. Bahram's disguise tales feed the Arabian-Nights tradition; read as folklore, not ethnography. No living community restriction.

passages.text: He took to the bazar his water-skins and tackle, which he pledged to some rich man, bought what he needed and returned in haste rejoicing to Bahram. Bahram took the meat promptly from him, cut it up, and then proceeded with the cookery. When they had eaten they took wine and goblet, and first of all drank to the king of kings. Lambak, when they had drunk, prepared for sleep, and set a candle by Bahram Gur's couch.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他將水囊與器具帶到市集，抵押給一位富人，購得所需之物，便歡喜地匆匆回到巴赫拉姆身邊。巴赫拉姆迅速從他手中接過肉，切好，然後著手烹調。他們吃罷，便取來酒與酒杯，首先為萬王之王飲酒致敬。他們飲畢，蘭巴克準備就寢，並在巴赫拉姆·古爾的床榻旁放置了一支蠟燭。

passages.text: He stole away and made toward the house of barren Baraham, knocked at the door, and said: the Shah hath come back from the chase, but I was left behind; 'tis night and I know not the way; if I may sojourn in this house to-night I will not trouble any one. The messenger departed and said: there is no shelter here for thee. The Jew is very poor and every night reposeth, bare and hungry, on the ground.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他悄悄離去，朝不孕的巴拉漢的家走去，敲了敲門，說道：沙王已從狩獵歸來，但我被落在了後面；天已黑，我不識路；若今夜能在此屋借宿，我必不麻煩任何人。信使離去後說道：此處沒有可供你棲身之所。那猶太人極為貧窮，每夜都赤身空腹地躺在地上歇息。

passages.text: Bahram replied: I will not enter but will sleep outside, and in the morning he saw how Baraham kept his hoards; he seized the wealth of Baraham, and bestowed it all upon Lambak the water-carrier who had feasted him, so that the generous host was recompensed a hundredfold and the churl went empty away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 5 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 巴赫拉姆回答說：我不進去，我要睡在外面。到了早晨，他看見巴拉罕如何守著他的財寶；他奪取了巴拉罕的財富，全都賜給了那位曾款待他的挑水夫蘭巴克，使這位慷慨的東道主得到百倍的報償，而那個吝嗇之徒則空手而去。

title.en: Bahram Gur Brings the Lute-folk from Hind
title.zh: 巴赫拉姆自印度引入樂師

region.en: Roads of Hind and Iran (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 印度至伊朗之路（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VII, Bahram Gur sec. 39

summary.en: Bahram sends letters to each archmage asking what folk are free from toil, and the answer comes: the rich wear wreaths of roses in their drinking-bouts and quaff to minstrelsy, but as for us they do not reckon us as men at all. The king of kings laughs heartily and sends a camel-post to king Shangul of Hind: select ten thousand of the Gipsy-tribe, both male and female, skilful on the harp, and send them to me. He accorded them an audience and gave each an ox and ass, for he proposed to make the Gipsies husbandmen; the Gipsies went and ate the wheat and oxen, and came at a year's end with pallid cheeks; and so the Gipsies now have for company the dog and wolf, and tramp unceasingly.
summary.zh: 巴赫拉姆問群臣：「何民不勞而享樂？」答曰：富人花間醉酒、歌舞昇平，而窮人被視如無物。王大笑，遣使印度王香古爾：「選一萬名擅彈豎琴的流浪樂師來！」他們到來後，王賜牛驢、發麥種，欲使其務農兼為窮人奏樂；誰知樂師們吃盡牛麥，一年後灰頭土臉而回。王遂命其「驢背馱琴，四海為家」——從此流浪樂人與犬狼為伴，行蹤不絕。

sensitivity.note: Epic etiology of Romani musicians in Persia (Firdausi via Bahram V); read as medieval legend. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Thereafter he sent letters to each archmage, and asked: in all the realm what folk are free from toil, and who are mendicants and destitute? An answer came from all the archimages, from all the nobles, and the men of lore: the face of earth appeareth prosperous, save that the poor complain against the ills of fortune and the Shah. The rich wear wreaths of roses in their drinking-bouts, and quaff to minstrelsy, but as for us they do not reckon us as men at all. The empty-handed drinketh with no rose or harp. The king of kings should look to it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 39 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 此後，他寫信給每一位大祭司，問道：在全國之中，哪些人免於勞苦，哪些人是乞丐和窮困之人？從所有大祭司、所有貴族和有學識的人那裡都傳來了答覆：大地的面貌顯得繁榮昌盛，只是窮人抱怨命運的災厄和國王。富人在酒宴上戴著玫瑰花冠，隨著樂師的歌聲暢飲，而至於我們，他們根本不把我們當人看待。兩手空空的人喝酒時既沒有玫瑰也沒有豎琴。萬王之王應當留意此事。

passages.text: The Shah laughed heartily at this report, and sent a camel-post to king Shangul to say thus: O thou monarch good at need! select ten thousand of the Gipsy-tribe, both male and female, skilful on the harp, and send them to me. I may gain mine end through that notorious folk. Now when the letter came to Shangul he made choice of Gipsies as bidden by the Shah who, when they came, accorded them an audience and gave each an ox and ass, for he proposed to make the Gipsies husbandmen.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 39 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 國王聽了這份報告，開懷大笑，派了一隊駱駝信使去對商古勒國王這樣說：哦，你這應急有方的君主！從吉普賽族中挑選一萬名男女，擅長彈奏豎琴的，送來給我。我也許能藉那個聲名狼藉的族群達成我的目的。當信送到商古勒那裡時，他遵照國王的吩咐挑選了吉普賽人；他們到來時，國王接見了他們，並給每人一頭牛和一頭驢，因為他打算讓吉普賽人當農夫。

passages.text: Gipsies went and ate the wheat and oxen, then at a year's end came with pallid cheeks. The Shah said: was it not your task to plough, to sow, and reap? Your asses yet remain, so load them up, prepare your harps, and stretch the silken chords. And so the Gipsies now, according to Bahram's just ordinance, have for company the dog and wolf, and tramp unceasingly.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 39 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 吉普賽人去了，吃掉了麥子和牛，然後在一年將盡時面色蒼白地回來。國王說：你們的任務不就是耕地、播種和收割嗎？你們的驢還在，那就把它們裝載起來，備好你們的豎琴，拉緊絲弦吧。於是吉普賽人如今，依照巴赫拉姆公正的敕令，與狗和狼為伴，不停地流浪。

title.en: Bahram Gur Dies on the Brocade of His Bed
title.zh: 巴赫拉姆·古爾之終

region.en: Palace of Bahram Gur (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 巴赫拉姆王宮（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VII, Bahram Gur sec. 40

summary.en: Thus passed he three score years and three, and had no equal in that age. The treasury is void, says the archmage, and the monarch answers: take no further pains, for I have passed beyond the need thereof; resign the world to its Creator. He cast away the crown, left his seat, and hasted to resign the world's affairs; at night-fall he was eager for repose, and when the sun displayed its head fear filled the archimage's heart: Yazdagird drew near his sire and spied what froze the breath upon his lips — Bahram with faded cheeks lay dead on gold brocade. Of fifty monarchs of seed royal sown who girt their loins upon the Iranian throne, Bahram Gur had no like in eminence, in justice, puissance, and excellence.
summary.zh: 他在位六十三年，舉世無雙。庫藏已空？他答：「我已無需財貨，把世界交還造物主吧。」他棄冠離座、淡出塵務；夜闌就寢，晨光初露時術士惶恐——王子趨近父王，見其唇齒凝滯：巴赫拉姆面容枯槁，僵臥於金錦之上。王族五十君王之中，論公義、威力與賢明，無出其右者。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source. Firdausi gives Bahram a bed-death; the popular mire-death is a later tradition. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Thus passed he three score years and three, and had no equal in that age. The scribe, the wise archmage, his minister, said to him: the treasury of the king of mighty men is void. The monarch answered: take no further pains, for I have passed beyond the need thereof. Resign the world to its Creator, Him who manifested forth His works. The heavens will pass away, but God abideth ever to guide both thee and me to what is good.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 40 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他就這樣度過了六十三年，在那個時代無人能與他相比。書記官、睿智的大祭司、他的大臣對他說：大力士之王的國庫空虛了。君主回答說：不必再費心了，因為我已經超越了對此的需要。把世界交還給它的造物主，就是那位顯現其作為的神。諸天將會消逝，但神永遠長存，引導你和我走向善。

passages.text: Intending to devote himself to God he cast away the crown, he left his seat, and hasted to resign the world's affairs. At night-fall he was eager for repose, and, when the sun displayed its head above the deep, fear filled his archimage's heart, who thought: the Shah ariseth not from sleep unless he hath withdrawn him from the lords. Then Yazdagird drew near his sire and spied what froze the breath upon his lips: Bahram with faded cheeks lay dead on gold brocade!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 40 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他打算獻身於神，便拋棄了王冠，離開了他的座位，急忙卸下世間的事務。夜幕降臨時，他渴望安歇；而當太陽在深淵之上露出頭來時，恐懼充滿了他大祭司的心，他心想：國王若未從貴族中抽身離去，是不會從睡夢中起身的。於是亞茲達吉爾德走近他的父親，窺見了那使他唇上氣息凝結的景象：巴赫拉姆面色蒼白，死在金線錦緞之上！

passages.text: Of fifty monarchs of seed royal sown, who girt their loins upon the Iranian throne, Bahram Gur had no like in eminence, in justice, puissance, and excellence. Thou wouldst have called king Rustam but vizir to him. Sun, moon, and Venus, Saturn, crown, and throne, a Shah, like this one, ne'er will look upon. He decked the throne and crown, from Rum and Chin took toll and tax, yet passed as he had been a starving mendicant!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Bahram Gur sec. 40 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在出身王族、束腰登上伊朗王座的五十位君主之中，巴赫拉姆·古爾在卓越、公正、權勢與德行上無人能及。你簡直會稱魯斯塔姆國王不過是他的宰相。太陽、月亮與金星，土星、王冠與寶座，再也見不到一位像他這樣的沙阿。他裝點寶座與王冠，向羅馬與中國徵收貢賦稅款，卻過得彷彿一個飢餓的乞丐！

title.en: Buzurjmihr Unravels the Game of Chess
title.zh: 布祖爾吉米赫爾解棋

region.en: Court of Nushirwan (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 努希爾萬王庭（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. VII, Nushirwan sec. 1 (Introduction of Chess)

summary.en: The Raja of Hind sends to Nushirwan a chess-board wrought with cunning workmanship: bid the questers for knowledge find out how that goodly game is played, the name of each piece and the way to move it; if they discover it I will send full tribute; but if their knowledge is no match for ours let them pay a tribute unto us, since knowledge is of all famed things the best. The chiefs and archimages examine the board and none discovers how the game is played; then Buzurjmihr comes to the Shah and says: I will discover all this goodly game, employing wisdom as my guide therein — and, retiring, he finds the powers of footman, elephant, rukh, horse, wazir, and king, and wins the wager for Iran.
summary.zh: 印度王公遣使送來一具工巧棋盤：「若伊朗智者能解此局——知各子之名、行法與方格——便奉歲貢；若不能，則爾等當向我納貢，因『知識』乃萬美之首！」群臣術士環棋而思，無人能解；賢相布祖爾吉米赫爾進言：「我憑智慧必解此局！」他退而參悟兵卒、戰象、戰車、駿馬、宰相與王的行法，替伊朗贏下這場以貢賦為注的賭局。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the Chatrang-namak legend (chess entering Persia under Nushirwan). No living community restriction.

passages.text: The envoy of the king of Hind hath come with elephants, with parasols, with horsemen of Sind and laden camels fifty score. The Raja had amassed from every hand the products of Kannuj and Mai. Then the envoy brought a letter which the Raja had written upon silk to Nushirwan, and also a chess-board wrought with cunning workmanship. The man of Hind thus gave the Raja's message: bid those much travailed in the quest for knowledge to place this board, used in the game of chess, before them and set all their wits to work to find out how that goodly game is played.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Nushirwan sec. 1 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 印度國王的使節已帶著大象、華蓋、信德的騎手以及一百乘滿載的駱駝到來。羅闍已從各方蒐集了曲女城與邁的物產。隨後使節帶來一封羅闍寫在絲帛上給努希爾萬的信，還有一副工藝精巧的棋盤。那印度人如此傳達羅闍的訊息：命那些在探求知識上歷盡辛勞的人把這副用於棋戲的棋盤擺在面前，竭盡全部才智，去弄清這美妙的遊戲該如何玩。

passages.text: If they discover all this goodly game, and prove themselves the betters of the wise, then, as the Shah commands, I will send full tribute to his court with all good will; but if the nobles of the Iranian folk have not the wit to resolve the point, since their knowledge is no match for ours, let them not seek for tax and tribute from us, but rather pay a tribute unto us, since knowledge is of all famed things the best. The envoy thus replied: 'tis all, O king! an emblem of the art of war, and thou wilt see the tactics, the plan, and order of a battlefield.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Nushirwan sec. 1 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 倘若他們能破解這美妙的遊戲，證明自己勝過智者，那麼，遵照沙阿的命令，我願滿心樂意地送全額貢賦到他的宮廷；但倘若伊朗民族的貴族們沒有才智解開此題，因為他們的學識比不上我們，那就讓他們別再向我們索取稅賦與貢品，反倒向我們納貢，因為知識是一切著名事物中最好的。使節如此答道：陛下啊！這一切皆是戰爭之術的象徵，你將看到戰場的戰術、部署與秩序。

passages.text: The chiefs and archimages that were counsellors all came before the Shah and with the chess-board in front of them considered it at large, examined it, tried every device, and played with one another in all ways; but none discovered how the game was played, and all departed louring. Buzurjmihr came to the Shah, perceived him vexed and troubled, and said: O great king, world-lord and vigilant whose word is law! I will discover all this goodly game, employing wisdom as my guide therein.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Nushirwan sec. 1 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 首領與大智者們，即那些謀臣，全都來到沙阿面前，把棋盤擺在眼前，仔細端詳，審視研究，嘗試各種方法，彼此以種種方式對弈；但無人發現這遊戲該如何玩，全都愁容滿面地離去。布祖爾吉米赫爾來到沙阿面前，見他煩惱憂愁，便說道：偉大的國王啊，世界之主，警醒而一言即法者！我將以智慧為指引，破解這美妙的遊戲。

title.en: Khusrau Parwiz and Shirin
title.zh: 霍斯勞與希琳

region.en: Hunting-grounds of Khusrau Parwiz (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 霍斯勞獵苑（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1923)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1923), vol. VIII, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 56

summary.en: Khusrau Parwiz like other paladins, while yet his father lived, was young and bold, and had for mate Shirin who was to him as his bright eyes; he cared for none beside among the fair. He parts from her when he comes to be king and has to fight Bahram Chubina, and she weeps day and night o'er his defect in love. When his mighty host rides out, seven hundred falconers, three hundred cheetah-keepers, two thousand minstrels on camel-back, and Shirin, hearing that the host hath come, puts on a yellow vest musk-scented, goes on the roof, and cries in the olden tongue: O Shah! Great Lion! where is that love of thine? Where are our loves, our troth, our bonds, our oaths?
summary.zh: 霍斯勞未登基時英武少年，唯有希琳是他的「明眸」，此外無人入心。即位後為戰巴赫拉姆·丘賓而別離，她晝夜泣血。皇家獵隊出行——七百鷹師、三百馴豹人、兩千駝背樂師——希琳聞王駕至，披灑著麝香的鵝黃羅衫登樓遠眺，以古語泣呼：「大王啊，雄獅！你的愛在哪裡？我們的山盟海誓、我們的癡情，都到哪裡去了？」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the Shahnama's version of Khusrau and Shirin (cf. Nizami's romance). No living community restriction.

passages.text: Khusrau Parwiz like other paladins, while yet his father lived, was young and bold, and had for mate Shirin who was to him as his bright eyes. He cared for none beside among the fair, but parted from her for a while when he came to be king and had to roam the world unrestingly, for all his work was then to fight Bahram Chubina, while the Fair wept day and night o'er his defect in love.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 56 (Warner 1923); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 霍斯勞·帕爾維茲與其他勇士一樣，在父親尚在世時年輕而勇敢，並以希琳為伴侶，她於他如同明亮的雙眼。在美人之中他別無所顧，但當他成為國王、不得不不停地奔走於世間時，便與她分離了一段時日，因為他當時的全部事務便是與巴赫拉姆·楚賓作戰，而那位美人則日夜為他在愛情上的疏失而哭泣。

passages.text: It was so that one day he willed to hunt, and all things were prepared as in the times of former Shahs: three hundred steeds caparisoned with gold, a thousand and eight score afoot, seven hundred falconers with royal falcons, three hundred keepers of the cheetahs, and two thousand minstrels all on camel-back, crowned with gold.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 56 (Warner 1923); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 事情是這樣的：有一天他想要出獵，一切皆如歷代沙阿在位時那般準備妥當：三百匹披掛金飾的駿馬，一千一百八十名步行隨從，七百名帶著御用獵鷹的鷹師，三百名獵豹看守，以及兩千名樂師全騎在駱駝背上，頭戴金冠。

passages.text: Now Shirin, on hearing that the host, preceded by the mighty Shah, hath come, put on a yellow vest musk-scented, and made her visage like pomegranate-blooms; she left her jocund hall, went on the roof, and waited till Khusrau Parwiz arrived, then let the tear-drops fall upon her cheeks. All tears and beauty, eagerly she cried thus in the olden tongue: O Shah! Great Lion! where is that love of thine? Where are the tears of blood once stanched by looking on Shirin? Where are our loves, our troth, our bonds, our oaths?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 56 (Warner 1923); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 如今，希琳聽聞那支由威武的沙阿率領的大軍已然到來，便穿上一件散發麝香的黃色長袍，將面容妝點得如同石榴花般嬌豔；她離開歡樂的殿堂，登上屋頂，等候庫斯勞·帕爾維茲抵達，隨後任憑淚珠落在雙頰之上。她滿是淚水與美貌，急切地用古老的語言如此呼喊：啊，沙阿！偉大的雄獅！你那愛在何處？那曾因凝望希琳而止住的泣血之淚，如今又在何處？我們的愛、我們的信誓、我們的盟約、我們的誓言，都在何處？

title.en: Barbad Sings Hidden in the Plane-Tree
title.zh: 巴爾巴德樹上獻歌

region.en: Pleasance of Khusrau Parwiz (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 霍斯勞御苑（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1923)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1923), vol. VIII, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 60

summary.en: When none fared ill at court Barbad heard tell of the minstrel Mardwi, the rival harper of the Shah, and dressed all in green and took his harp, and, when the Shah came to the pleasance, climbed into a plane-tree and sang while the monarch quaffed. None but Barbad can play so, thought the Shah; then while Barbad sang on the monarch filled the singer's mouth with jewels, and Barbad became the first of harpers. The epoch of Barbad hath past and gone: that market never failed while he could strike the strings.
summary.zh: 宮中太平無事，樂師巴爾巴德聞御前樂正馬爾德維之名，遂綠衣抱琴入御苑，攀上懸鈴木，當王獨酌時在高枝上放歌。王驚：「除巴爾巴德誰能彈得如此！」邊聽歌邊將寶石填滿歌者之口——巴爾巴德自此成為首席樂師。「巴爾巴德的時代已成過往：只要琴弦還在，那市集永不冷落。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Barbad is the famed Sasanian court musician. No living community restriction.

passages.text: When none fared ill at court, Barbad heard tell of the minstrel Mardwi, and Barbad approached Mardwi forthwith; the Shah is coming to the pleasance, said Barbad, and dressed all in green and took his harp. And thought the Shah: none but Barbad can play so. Then while Barbad sang on the monarch quaffed. He filled the singer's mouth. Barbad became the first of harpers. The epoch of Barbad hath past and gone: that market never failed while he could strike the strings.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 60 (Warner 1923); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當宮廷中無人受苦之時，巴爾巴德聽聞了樂師馬爾德維的名聲，便立刻前去接近馬爾德維；巴爾巴德說道，沙阿正前來遊樂苑，於是全身著綠，拿起他的豎琴。沙阿心想：除巴爾巴德之外，無人能彈得如此美妙。於是巴爾巴德歌唱之際，君王頻頻暢飲。他賞賜了這位歌者。巴爾巴德成了豎琴師中的第一人。巴爾巴德的時代已然過去消逝：只要他還能撥動琴弦，那市集便從未冷落。

title.en: Khusrau Parwiz Deposed and Sent to Taisafun
title.zh: 霍斯勞失位被囚泰西封

region.en: Pleasance near the river (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 河畔御苑（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1923)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1923), vol. VIII, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 65

summary.en: The Shah bode in that mead, a lofty tree overshadowing him, and when he hungered he bade his slave cut off a cantle from that costly belt, five studs of gold enriched with jewelry, and send the gardener to the bazar for bread. The jeweller cries: who will dare to buy, for this should be within the treasury of Khusrau Parwiz? Shirwi knows: 'tis Khusrau Parwiz, and sends three hundred horsemen; the astrologers had said to the king: thy death will come to thee between two heights, and by a slave's hand in a lonely spot. He mounts the elephant, crying in the ancient tongue: O treasure! if thou art my foe be not a friend to these mine enemies, for I am in the hands of Ahriman to-day — and Kubad gives orders: let trusty Galimis be made his keeper at Taisafun with a thousand horsemen.
summary.zh: 失位的霍斯勞匿身河畔樹蔭下，飢時命僕割下腰帶上五枚寶石換麵包；珠寶商驚呼：「這是霍斯勞王庫中之物！」其子希爾維遂遣三百騎尋獲。星占家曾言：他將死於「兩座高牆之間、荒僻處、奴僕之手」。他騎上大象，以古語哀呼：「寶藏啊，若你與我為敵，也莫要助我的仇人——今日我落入阿赫里曼之手！」希爾維登基，命忠僕加里米斯率千騎將他押往泰西封看管。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the deposition of Khusrau II (628 CE) as Firdausi tells it. No living community restriction.

passages.text: The Shah bode in that mead, a lofty tree overshadowing him. When half the longsome day had passed he hungered. Now within the pleasance there was a man employed who did not know the king by sight. The Sun-faced bade his slave: cut off a cantle from this costly belt. That cantle had on it five studs of gold enriched with jewelry, and the king then spake thus to the gardener: these studs will prove of use to-day; go thou to the bazar, buy meat and bread, and shun frequented paths.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 65 (Warner 1923); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 沙阿在那片草地上停留，一棵高聳的樹為他遮蔭。漫長的白晝過去一半時，他感到飢餓。此時遊樂苑中有一名受僱之人，並不認識國王的容貌。那位容顏如太陽者吩咐他的奴僕：從這條珍貴的腰帶上割下一塊。那塊腰帶上鑲有五顆以珠寶裝飾的金飾釘，國王隨即對園丁如此說道：這些飾釘今日將派上用場；你到市集去，買些肉和麵包，避開人多的道路。

passages.text: The expert, when he looked upon the studs, said: who will dare to buy, for this should be within the treasury of Khusrau Parwiz, who hath a hundred new like this each year? Whom didst thou steal these jewels from? Shirwi knew: 'tis Khusrau Parwiz, his features are the age's cynosure, and sent three hundred horsemen from the court. Meanwhile his heart was troubled at his aged fortune because astrologers had said to him: thy death will come to thee between two heights, and by a slave's hand in a lonely spot.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 65 (Warner 1923); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那識貨之人一見這些飾釘，便說道：誰敢買這東西？這本該在庫斯勞·帕爾維茲的寶庫之中，他每年都有上百件與此相同的新物。你是從誰那裡偷來這些珠寶的？希爾維心知：這正是庫斯勞·帕爾維茲，他的容貌乃當世的矚目所在，於是從宮廷派出三百名騎兵。與此同時，他心中因自己年邁的命運而憂慮不安，因為占星家曾對他說：你的死將在兩座高處之間臨到你，由一名奴僕之手，在一個偏僻之地。

passages.text: So now this armour is mine earth, my golden shield my heaven, and the heights are my two treasuries within the garden. In sooth my days are coming to an end: where is my star that used to light the world? They brought an elephant for him. His soul was dark with woe. He mounted, and the troops led him away while in the ancient tongue he cried: O treasure! if thou art my foe be not a friend to these mine enemies, for I am in the hands of Ahriman to-day. Kubad gave orders to his minister: bid them carry him to Taisafun away from court with his own counsellor; there let him bide in peace for many a day and harmed by none.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khusrau Parwiz sec. 65 (Warner 1923); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 所以如今這副甲胄便是我的大地，我的金盾便是我的蒼天，而那兩座高處便是花園中我的兩座寶庫。說來我的日子確已走到盡頭：那曾照亮世界的我的星辰如今何在？他們為他牽來一頭大象。他的靈魂因憂愁而昏暗。他騎了上去，軍隊將他帶走，而他以古老的語言呼喊：啊，寶藏！你若與我為敵，就莫要成為我這些敵人的朋友，因為今日我落在阿赫里曼的手中。庫巴德向他的大臣下令：命人將他與他自己的謀士一同帶往泰薩豐，遠離宮廷；讓他在那裡安寧地度過許多日子，不受任何人的傷害。

title.en: Angra Mainyu Tempts Zarathushtra by the Dareja
title.zh: 阿赫里曼誘惑查拉圖什特拉

region.en: River Dareja, house of Pourushaspa (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 達雷賈河畔（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded in the Avesta, c. 6th-4th century BCE (Darmesteter translation 1880)

source.work: Vendidad Fargard XIX (Zend-Avesta Part I), trans. J. Darmesteter, SBE 4 (1880)

summary.en: Zarathustra, unshaken by the evil spirit, by the hardness of his malignant riddles, swings stones in his hand, stones as big as a house, which he obtained from the Maker, Ahura Mazda, and answers: I will smite the creation of the Daeva. Again the guileful one says: thou art the son of Pourushaspa, just born of thy mother; renounce the good law of the worshippers of Mazda, and thou shalt gain such a boon as the murderer gained, the ruler of the nations. No! never will I renounce the good law of the worshippers of Mazda, though my body, my life, my soul should burst! The sacred mortar, the sacred cup, the Haoma, the Words taught by Mazda — these are my weapons, my best weapons.
summary.zh: 查拉圖什特拉立於達雷賈河畔、父親普魯沙斯帕的宅邸山上，手掄房舍般巨石（那是造物主所賜），毫不為魔王的謎語所動：「我要粉碎群魔的造物！」魔王再度誘惑：「你剛離母腹；放棄馬茲達信眾的正法吧——你將如那殺人者一樣統治萬國！」答曰：「縱使我身、我命、我魂崩裂，也絕不放棄正法！聖臼、聖杯、豪馬汁與馬茲達親授之言——這便是我的武器、我最利的武器！」

sensitivity.note: Avestan liturgical text; Darmesteter compares the riddle-contest to Oedipus and the Sphinx. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Zarathustra, unshaken by the evil spirit, by the hardness of his malignant riddles, swinging stones in his hand, stones as big as a house, which he obtained from the Maker, Ahura Mazda, he the holy Zarathustra. At what on this wide, round earth, whose ends lie afar, at what dost thou swing those stones, thou who standest by the river Dareja, upon the mountains, in the mansion of Pourushaspa?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard XIX, 4-5 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 查拉圖斯特拉，不為惡靈所動搖，不為其惡毒謎語的艱深所動搖，手中揮舞著石塊，那石塊大如房屋，是他從造物主阿胡拉·馬茲達那裡得來的，他，那神聖的查拉圖斯特拉。在這廣闊而圓的大地上，其盡頭遠在天邊，你揮舞那些石塊是為了什麼？你這站在達雷賈河畔、群山之上、普魯沙斯帕宅邸中的人啊？

passages.text: Thus Zarathustra answered Angra Mainyu: O evil-doer, Angra Mainyu! I will smite the creation of the Daeva; I will smite the Nasu, a creature of the Daeva; I will smite the Pairika Knathaiti, till the fiend-smiter Saoshyant come up to life out of the lake Kasava, from the region of the dawn.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard XIX, 5 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是瑣羅亞斯德回答安格拉·曼紐：噢，作惡者安格拉·曼紐！我將擊打眾達埃瓦的造物；我將擊打那蘇，達埃瓦的造物；我將擊打帕里卡·克納泰蒂，直到那擊殺惡魔者掃什揚特從卡薩瓦湖中、從黎明之地升起而獲得生命。

passages.text: Again to him said the guileful one, the Maker of the evil world, Angra Mainyu: do not destroy my creatures, O holy Zarathustra! Thou art the son of Pourushaspa, just born of thy mother. Renounce the good law of the worshippers of Mazda, and thou shalt gain such a boon as the murderer gained, the ruler of the nations. Thus in answer to him said Spitama Zarathustra: No! never will I renounce the good law of the worshippers of Mazda, though my body, my life, my soul should burst!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard XIX, 6-7 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那詭詐者、邪惡世界的創造者安格拉·曼紐又對他說：不要毀滅我的造物，噢，神聖的瑣羅亞斯德！你是普魯沙斯帕之子，方才由你母親所生。捨棄那崇拜馬茲達者的善法，你便將獲得如那殺人者、那統治諸民族者所獲得的恩賜。斯皮塔瑪·瑣羅亞斯德如此回答他：不！我絕不捨棄那崇拜馬茲達者的善法，縱使我的身體、我的生命、我的靈魂迸裂！

passages.text: By whose Word wilt thou strike, by whose Word wilt thou repel? asked Angra Mainyu. Thus in answer to him said Spitama Zarathustra: the sacred mortar, the sacred cup, the Haoma, the Words taught by Mazda, these are my weapons, my best weapons! By this Word will I strike, by this Word will I repel, by this weapon the good creatures will strike and repel thee, O evil-doer, Angra Mainyu! To me Spenta Mainyu gave it, he gave it to me in the boundless Time; to me the Amesha Spentas, the all-ruling, the all-beneficent, gave it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard XIX, 8-9 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你將以誰之言語擊打，以誰之言語擊退？安格拉·曼紐問道。斯皮塔瑪·瑣羅亞斯德如此回答他：神聖的研缽、神聖的杯、豪摩，以及馬茲達所教導的言語，這些便是我的武器，我最好的武器！我將以此言語擊打，以此言語擊退，以此武器，善的造物將擊打並擊退你，噢，作惡者安格拉·曼紐！是斯彭塔·曼紐把它賜予我，他在無邊的時間中把它賜予我；是眾阿梅沙·斯彭塔，那全權統治者、那全然施惠者，把它賜予我。

title.en: The Soul's Three Nights and the Bridge of Many Sides
title.zh: 亡魂三夜與多棱之橋

region.en: Peak of Judgment, Mount Alburz (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿爾布茲判決峰（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE (Pahlavi; West translation 1882)

source.work: Dadestan-i Denig chs. XX-XXI (Pahlavi), trans. E. W. West, SBE 18 (1882)

summary.en: The souls of the dead are three nights on earth: the first night satisfaction comes to them from their good thoughts and vexation from their evil thoughts, the second night pleasure from their good words and discomfort from their evil words, and the third night exaltation from their good deeds and punishment from their evil deeds. That third night, in the dawn, they go to the place of account on Alburz; the account being rendered they proceed to the bridge, and he who is righteous passes over the bridge on the ascent. The bridge is like a beam of many sides: its broad sides are so large that its width is twenty-seven reeds, and its sharp sides so contracted that in thinness it is just like the edge of a razor — it turns to that side which is suitable to the necessities of the souls arriving.
summary.zh: 亡魂在塵世停留三夜：第一夜，善念予其慰、惡念予其苦；第二夜，善言予其樂、惡言予其罰；第三夜，善行使其升揚、惡行使其受刑。第三夜黎明時分，亡魂前往阿爾布茲山上的清算之所，過秤後行至「別傳之橋」——義者拾級而升。此橋如多棱之樑：寬面廣達二十七葦之闊，利面薄如剃刀之刃——橋隨亡魂善惡而自行翻轉。

sensitivity.note: Pahlavi doctrinal Q&A rendered as myth; pairs with arda-viraf-vision and chinvat-bridge (different sources). No living community restriction.

passages.text: The reply is this, that it is thus said that the souls of those passed away and of the dead are three nights on earth; and the first night satisfaction comes to them from their good thoughts and vexation from their evil thoughts, the second night come pleasure from their good words and discomfort and punishment from their evil words, and the third night come exaltation from their good deeds and punishment from their evil deeds. And that third night, in the dawn, they go to the place of account on Alburz; the account being rendered they proceed to the bridge, and he who is righteous passes over the bridge on the ascent.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dadestan-i Denig ch. XX, 2-3 (West, SBE 18, 1882); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 答覆是這樣的，據說那些逝去者與死者的靈魂會在地上停留三夜；第一夜，滿足由他們的善念而來，煩惱由他們的惡念而來；第二夜，喜悅由他們的善言而來，不適與懲罰由他們的惡言而來；第三夜，尊榮由他們的善行而來，懲罰由他們的惡行而來。而那第三夜，在黎明時分，他們前往阿爾布爾茲山上的清算之地；清算完畢後，他們便前往那座橋，凡正直者便從橋上昇而過。

passages.text: He who is of the wicked falls from the lower end of the bridge, or from the middle of the bridge; he falls head-foremost to hell, and is precipitated unto that grade which is suitable for his wickedness. As it were that bridge is like a beam of many sides, of whose edges there are some which are broad, and there are some which are thin and sharp; its broad sides are so large that its width is twenty-seven reeds, and its sharp sides are so contracted that in thinness it is just like the edge of a razor.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dadestan-i Denig chs. XX, 4, XXI, 2-3 (West, SBE 18, 1882); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 凡邪惡者，則從橋的下端、或從橋的中段墜落；他頭朝前墜入地獄，被拋入與其邪惡相稱的那一層級。彷彿那座橋就像一根多面的樑，其邊緣有的寬闊，有的細薄而鋒利；其寬闊的一面如此之大，寬達二十七蘆葦；其鋒利的一面如此收窄，其細薄恰如剃刀之刃。

passages.text: And when the souls of the righteous and wicked arrive it turns to that side which is suitable to their necessities, through the great glory of the creator and the command of him who takes the just account. Moreover, the bridge becomes a broad bridge for the righteous, as much as the height of nine spears; and for the wicked, that they may fall from it, it becomes sharp as a needle's point, so that they slip down head-foremost into darkness.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dadestan-i Denig ch. XXI, 4-5 (West, SBE 18, 1882); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 而當正直者與邪惡者的靈魂到達時，它便轉向適合其所需的那一面，這憑藉創造者的偉大榮光，以及那主持公正清算者之命令。再者，那橋對正直者而言，變成一座寬闊的橋，寬達九矛之高；而對邪惡者而言，為使他們從橋上墜落，它變得鋒利如針尖，使他們頭朝前滑入黑暗之中。

title.en: Frashegird: Ohrmazd Answers Zarathushtra About the Resurrection
title.zh: 弗拉肖格爾德：馬茲達答復活之問

region.en: Renovated world of the future (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 未來更新之世（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE (Pahlavi; West translation 1880)

source.work: Bundahishn ch. XXX (Pahlavi), trans. E. W. West, SBE 5 (1880)

summary.en: Zarathust asks of Auharmazd: whence does a body form again, which the wind has carried and the water conveyed? And Auharmazd answers: when through me the sky arose from the substance of the ruby, without columns, on the spiritual support of far-compassed light; when by me corn was created so that, scattered about in the earth, it grew again and returned with increase; when by me a son was created and fashioned in the womb of a mother — each one of them, when created by me, was herein more difficult than causing the resurrection; observe that when that which was not was then produced, why is it not possible to produce again that which was?
summary.zh: 查拉圖什特拉問阿胡拉·馬茲達：「被風吹散、被水帶走的屍身，如何重新聚成形體？復活如何發生？」答曰：「天空由紅寶石之質憑無柱的光支柱起；五穀入土復生且結實增多；嬰兒在母腹中成形——這些創造都比復活更難！既然『無』能生『有』，為何不能讓『已有』者復生？」

sensitivity.note: Pahlavi doctrinal text rendered as myth; the Saoshyant-resurrection parallels the Osiris/Jesus resurrection cluster. No living community restriction.

passages.text: After Soshyans comes they prepare the raising of the dead, as it says, that Zarathust asked of Auharmazd thus: whence does a body form again, which the wind has carried and the water conveyed? and how does the resurrection occur? Ahharmazd answered thus: when through me the sky arose from the substance of the ruby, without columns, on the spiritual support of far-compassed light.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. XXX, 4-5 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 蘇希揚斯之後，他們便準備死者的復活，正如經上所說：瑣羅亞斯德曾如此問阿胡拉馬茲達：被風吹散、被水沖走的身體，從何處重新成形？復活又是如何發生的？阿胡拉馬茲達如此回答：當那天空藉著我，從紅寶石的本質中升起，沒有柱子，依靠著遠布之光的靈性支撐。

passages.text: When by me the sun and moon and stars are conducted in the firmament of luminous bodies; when by me corn was created so that, scattered about in the earth, it grew again and returned with increase; when by me colour of various kinds was created in plants; when by me fire was created in plants and other things without combustion.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. XXX, 5 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當日月星辰藉著我，在發光天體的蒼穹中被引導運行；當穀物藉著我而被創造，以致散播於大地之中，又生長起來，帶著增多而回歸；當各種顏色藉著我而在植物中被創造；當火藉著我而在植物及其他事物中被創造，卻不將其焚燒。

passages.text: When by me a son was created and fashioned in the womb of a mother, and the structure severally of the skin, nails, blood, feet, eyes, ears, and other things was produced; when by me legs were created for the water, so that it flows away, and the cloud was created which carries the water of the world and rains there where it has a purpose — each one of them, when created by me, was herein more difficult than causing the resurrection. Observe that when that which was not was then produced, why is it not possible to produce again that which was?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. XXX, 5-6 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當一個兒子藉著我而被創造、在母親的腹中被塑造，而皮膚、指甲、血液、雙足、眼睛、耳朵及其他各部分的結構逐一產生；當雙腿藉著我而為水被創造，使水得以流去，而雲藉著我而被創造，它承載世界之水，降落在有其目的之處——這一切，當它們藉著我被創造時，都比促成復活更為艱難。請看，既然那原本不存在的曾被產生，為何不能再產生那曾經存在的呢？

title.en: The Song of the Reed
title.zh: 蘆笛之歌

region.en: Rumi's pulpit at Konya (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 科尼亞講經台（象徵性定位）

period: Composed 13th century CE, Books I-II (Whinfield translation 1898)

source.work: Masnavi i Ma'navi, trans. E. H. Whinfield (1898), Book I, Song of the Reed

summary.en: Hearken to the reed-flute, how it discourses, complaining of the pains of separation: ever since they tore me from my osier bed my plaintive notes have moved men and women to tears; he who abides far away from his home is ever longing for the day he shall return. The flute tells the tale of love's bloodstained path; it recounts the story of Majnun's love toils. This plaint of the flute is fire, not mere air: let him who lacks this fire be accounted dead! 'Tis the fire of love that inspires the flute — love signifies the strong attraction that draws all creatures back to reunion with their Creator.
summary.zh: 請聽蘆笛的傾訴——它在低訴離別之苦：「自從被人從蘆葦叢中割下，我的嗚咽曾令多少男女落淚；離家越遠的人，越是日夜盼歸。」笛聲訴說著愛的浴血之路，講述瑪傑農的苦戀。這笛聲是火，不是風——無此火者形同死人！那是「愛」之火在吹動笛管——愛，正是將萬物拉回造物主懷抱的強力。

sensitivity.note: Sufi mystical allegory read as mythic narrative (soul separated from Source); interpretive. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Hearken to the reed-flute, how it discourses, complaining of the pains of separation: ever since they tore me from my osier bed, my plaintive notes have moved men and women to tears. I burst my breast, striving to give vent to sighs, and to express the pangs of my yearning for my home. He who abides far away from his home is ever longing for the day he shall return.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book I, Song of the Reed (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 聽那蘆笛，它如何訴說，抱怨離別之苦：自從他們將我從蘆葦叢中割下，我的哀音便使男女落淚。我撕裂胸膛，竭力吐出嘆息，表達我對故鄉的渴望之苦。遠離故鄉的人，永遠盼望著歸返之日。

passages.text: My wailing is heard in every throng, in concert with them that rejoice and them that weep; each interprets my notes in harmony with his own feelings, but not one fathoms the secrets of my heart. The flute tells the tale of love's bloodstained path; it recounts the story of Majnun's love toils.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book I, Song of the Reed (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我的哀號在每一群人中都被聽見，與歡樂者同奏，與哭泣者共鳴；各人依自己的情感解讀我的音符，卻無一人能參透我心中的秘密。蘆笛訴說愛情血染之路的故事；它講述馬杰農愛情艱辛的傳說。

passages.text: This plaint of the flute is fire, not mere air: let him who lacks this fire be accounted dead! 'Tis the fire of love that inspires the flute; 'tis the ferment of love that possesses the wine. The flute is the confidant of all unhappy lovers; yea, its strains lay bare my inmost secrets.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book I, Song of the Reed (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這蘆笛的哀訴是火，不只是空氣：讓那缺乏此火的人被視為死人！是愛之火激發了蘆笛；是愛之酵素佔據了酒。蘆笛是所有不幸戀人的知己；是的，它的曲調揭示了我內心最深處的秘密。

title.en: Four Angels and the Handful of Earth
title.zh: 四天使與一把泥土

region.en: Earth of the creation (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 創世之土（象徵性定位）

period: Composed 13th century CE, Books IV-V (Whinfield translation 1898)

source.work: Masnavi i Ma'navi, trans. E. H. Whinfield (1898), Book V, Story VII

summary.en: When the Almighty determined to create mankind to be proved by good and evil, He deputed the angel Gabriel to bring a handful of earth for the purpose of forming Adam's body. But the Earth remonstrated: the man so created would rebel against God and draw down God's curse upon her; and Gabriel returned without taking the handful. Michael was deputed next, and Israfil, and both were diverted from the execution of it. At last God sent Azrail, the angel of death, who, being of sterner disposition, resolutely shut his ears to the Earth's entreaties and brought back the required handful — and for this Azrail was made the angel of death, operating by disease and sickness, a spear in the hand of the Almighty.
summary.zh: 真主欲造人類以驗其善惡，遣加百列取土造亞當之體。大地卻哀求：「此人將叛神，致我受神咒！」加百列憫而空手而歸；米迦勒與伊斯拉菲爾亦相繼受阻。最後真主遣死神天使阿茲拉伊爾——他性剛如鐵，掩耳不聽大地哀告，毅然取土而返。真主遂命他為死亡天使，借疾病施行；他說：「我不過是全能者手中的一桿長矛。」

sensitivity.note: Sufi retelling of the Qur'anic creation of Adam (from Miskat tradition quoted by Rumi); pairs with clay-humans cluster. No living community restriction.

passages.text: When the Almighty determined to create mankind to be proved by good and evil, He deputed the angel Gabriel to bring a handful of earth for the purpose of forming Adam's body. Gabriel accordingly girded his loins and proceeded to the Earth to execute the divine commands. But the Earth, being apprehensive that the man so created would rebel against God and draw down God's curse upon her, remonstrated with Gabriel, and besought him to forbear.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book V, Story VII (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當全能者決定創造人類，使其以善惡受考驗時，祂派遣天使加百列去取一捧泥土，用以塑造亞當的身體。加百列於是束緊腰帶，前往大地執行神的命令。但大地憂慮如此造出的人類會違抗神，招致神的詛咒降於己身，便向加百列勸諫，懇求他暫緩行事。

passages.text: At last Gabriel granted her prayer, and returned to heaven without taking the handful of earth. Then God deputed Michael on the same errand, and the Earth made similar excuses to him, and he also listened to her crying, and returned to heaven without taking a handful. Then God sent the angel Israfil on the same errand, and he also was diverted from the execution of it by a divine intimation.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book V, Story VII (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 最後加百列應允了她的祈求，未取那捧泥土便返回天庭。於是神派遣米迦勒執行同一使命，大地也向他提出同樣的懇求，他也聽了她的哭訴，未取一捧泥土便返回天庭。接著神派遣天使伊斯拉菲執行同一使命，他也因神的啟示而中止了執行。

passages.text: At last God sent Azrail, the angel of death, who, being of sterner disposition than the others, resolutely shut his ears to the Earth's entreaties, and brought back the required handful of earth. The Earth pressed him with the argument that God's command to bear away a handful of her substance against her will did not override the other divine command to take pity on suppliants; but Azrail would not listen to her, remarking that he was to be regarded only as a spear in the hand of the Almighty. The moral is, that when any of God's creatures do us a harm, we ought to regard them only as instruments of God, who is the Only Real Agent.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book V, Story VII (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 最後神派遣了死亡天使亞茲拉爾，他性情比其餘諸位更為嚴厲，堅決對大地的懇求充耳不聞，帶回了所需的那捧泥土。大地以論理力勸他：神命他違背大地意願取走一捧泥土，並不能凌駕於另一條神命——憐憫懇求者；但亞茲拉爾不願聽從，只說他不過是全能者手中的一柄長矛。其寓意是：當神的任何造物加害於我們時，我們應只把他們視為神的工具，而神才是唯一真正的行動者。

title.en: Moses and the Shepherd
title.zh: 穆薩與牧羊人

region.en: Desert of Sinai (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 西奈曠野（象徵性定位）

period: Composed 13th century CE, Books I-II (Whinfield translation 1898)

source.work: Masnavi i Ma'navi, trans. E. H. Whinfield (1898), Book II, Story VII

summary.en: Moses once heard a shepherd praying as follows: O God, show me where Thou art, that I may become Thy servant; I will clean Thy shoes and comb Thy hair, and sew Thy clothes, and fetch Thee milk. When Moses heard him praying in this senseless manner he rebuked him; the shepherd was abashed, and tore his clothes and fled away into the desert. Then a voice from heaven was heard: O Moses, wherefore have you driven away my servant? Your office is to reconcile my people with me, not to drive them away from me. I regard not the words that are spoken, but the heart that offers them; I do not require fine words, but a burning heart.
summary.zh: 穆薩聽見牧羊人祈禱：「神啊，祢在哪裡？我願為祢擦鞋、梳髮、補衣、取奶！」穆薩斥其愚妄；牧羊人羞慚裂衣、遁入荒漠。天上忽有聲音：「穆薩！你為何趕走我的僕人？你奉命引人歸我，而非驅人離我。我不看言語，只看奉上言語的心；我不求華美之辭，只求一顆熾熱的心。」

sensitivity.note: Sufi parable on religious forms; read as sacred narrative. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Moses once heard a shepherd praying as follows: O God, show me where Thou art, that I may become Thy servant. I will clean Thy shoes and comb Thy hair, and sew Thy clothes, and fetch Thee milk. When Moses heard him praying in this senseless manner, he rebuked him, saying: O foolish one, God is a Spirit, and needs not such gross ministrations as, in your ignorance, you suppose.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book II, Story VII (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 摩西曾聽見一個牧人如此祈禱：神啊，請向我顯現祢在何處，好讓我成為祢的僕人。我要為祢擦鞋、為祢梳髮、為祢縫衣，還要為祢取奶。摩西聽見他這般無知地祈禱，便責備他說：愚人啊，神是靈，不需要你因無知而設想的這般粗陋的服侍。

passages.text: The shepherd was abashed at his rebuke, and tore his clothes and fled away into the desert. Then a voice from heaven was heard, saying: O Moses, wherefore have you driven away my servant? Your office is to reconcile my people with me, not to drive them away from me. I have given to each race different usages and forms of praising and adoring me; I regard not the words that are spoken, but the heart that offers them. I do not require fine words, but a burning heart.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book II, Story VII (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 牧人因他的責備而羞愧，撕裂衣裳，逃入沙漠。隨後天上傳來聲音說：摩西啊，你為何趕走我的僕人？你的職責是使我的子民與我和好，而非把他們從我身邊趕走。我賜給每個族群不同的習俗與讚美敬拜我的方式；我不看重所說的話語，而看重獻上話語的心。我不要求華美的言辭，而要求燃燒的心。

passages.text: A voice came from God to Moses: why hast thou sent my servant away? What is praiseworthy in thee is blamable in him; what is poison for thee is honey for him. I regard not the outside and the words, I regard the inside and the state of heart. The sect of lovers is distinct from all others; lovers have a religion and a faith of their own.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book II, Story VII (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 神的聲音臨到摩西：你為何趕走我的僕人？在你身上值得稱讚的，在他身上卻成了可責備的；對你是毒藥的，對他是蜂蜜。我不看重外表與言語，我看重內在與心的狀態。愛者之派別與其他一切派別有別；愛者有他們自己的宗教與信仰。

title.en: The Elephant in the Dark
title.zh: 暗室摸象

region.en: Dark room of the exhibition (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 展示暗室（象徵性定位）

period: Composed 13th century CE, Books I-III (Whinfield translation 1898)

source.work: Masnavi i Ma'navi, trans. E. H. Whinfield (1898), Book III, Story V

summary.en: Some Hindoos were exhibiting an elephant in a dark room, and many people collected to see it. But as the place was too dark to permit them to see the elephant, they all felt it with their hands: one felt its trunk and declared that the beast resembled a water-pipe; another felt its ear, and said it must be a large fan; another its leg, and thought it must be a pillar; another felt its back, and declared the beast must be like a great throne. According to the part which each felt, he gave a different description of the animal. The eye of outward sense is as the palm of a hand; the whole of the object is not grasped in the palm.
summary.zh: 印度人在暗室中展示大象，眾人湧入觀看；因光線不足，人人用手摸象：摸到鼻者說牠像水管，摸到耳者說是蒲扇，摸到腿者說是石柱，摸到背者說是禦座——各憑所觸，議論紛紜。魯米由此警醒世人：「外感官之眼不過如摸象之手掌，手掌之中豈能容下全象？莫執泡沫而忘大海；我們是海上盲人，雖在大洋卻視而不見。」

sensitivity.note: Sufi parable (blind-men-and-elephant, from the Buddhist Udana lineage); cross-tradition parable cluster. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Some Hindoos were exhibiting an elephant in a dark room, and many people collected to see it. But as the place was too dark to permit them to see the elephant, they all felt it with their hands, to gain an idea of what it was like. One felt its trunk, and declared that the beast resembled a water-pipe; another felt its ear, and said it must be a large fan; another its leg, and thought it must be a pillar; another felt its back, and declared the beast must be like a great throne.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book III, Story V (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有幾個印度人在一間暗室裡展示一頭大象，許多人聚集前來觀看。但因為那地方太暗，無法讓他們看見大象，他們便都用手去摸牠，想藉此得知牠是什麼模樣。一人摸到牠的鼻子，便宣稱這隻野獸像一根水管；另一人摸到牠的耳朵，說牠必定是一把大扇子；另一人摸到牠的腿，便以為牠必定是一根柱子；又一人摸到牠的背，便宣稱這隻野獸必定像一座大寶座。

passages.text: According to the part which each felt, he gave a different description of the animal. The eye of outward sense is as the palm of a hand; the whole of the object is not grasped in the palm. The sea itself is one thing, the foam another; neglect the foam, and regard the sea with your eyes. Waves of foam rise from the sea night and day; you look at the foam ripples and not the mighty sea.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book III, Story V (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他依各人所摸到的部位，對這動物作出不同的描述。外在感官的眼目如同手掌；對象的全貌並不能在掌中被掌握。大海本身是一回事，泡沫又是另一回事；撇開泡沫，用你的眼睛注視那大海。泡沫的波浪日夜從海中升起；你卻只看見泡沫的漣漪，而不見那浩瀚的大海。

passages.text: We, like boats, are tossed hither and thither; we are blind though we are on the bright ocean. Ah! you who are asleep in the boat of the body, you see the water; behold the Water of waters! Under the water you see there is another Water moving it; within the spirit is a Spirit that calls it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Masnavi Book III, Story V (Whinfield 1898); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 我們如同船隻，被拋來拋去；我們雖在明亮的大海之上，卻是盲目的。啊！你這在身體之船中沉睡的人，你看見了水；且去觀看那眾水之水！在水下你看見另有一水在推動它；在靈魂之內有一位神靈在呼喚它。

title.en: Astyages' Vine-Dream and the Exposed Infant Cyrus
title.zh: 阿斯杜阿該斯之夢與棄嬰居魯士

region.en: Mountains north of Agbatana (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿格巴塔納以北山地（象徵性定位）

period: Written c. 430 BCE (Macaulay translation 1890)

source.work: Herodotus, Histories Book 1, trans. G. C. Macaulay (1890), secs. 107-111

summary.en: Astyages son of Kyaxares saw a vision: it seemed to him that from his daughter a vine grew, and this vine overspread the whole of Asia. The Magian interpreters signified that the offspring of his daughter should be king in his room. So when Cyrus was born he called Harpagos, whom he trusted above all the other Medes, and bade him take the child which Mandane bore, and slay it and bury it. Not even if he shall come to be yet more out of his senses, answers Harpagos, will I agree to his will or serve him in such a murder as this; and he sends the child with a herdsman to the mountains most haunted by wild beasts — where the herdsman's wife, her own child just born, will not suffer the exposure.
summary.zh: 米底王阿斯杜阿該斯夢見女兒身上長出葡萄藤，藤蔓竟遮蔽整個亞洲；瑪術士解夢曰：其外孫將取代其王位。居魯士一降生，王便召親信哈爾帕戈斯：「把曼丹妮所生之子帶走殺掉、埋掉！」哈爾帕戈斯不敢親弑，將嬰兒交給牧人，命他拋於豺狼出沒的山中——恰好牧人之妻剛產下一子，二人便以自己的孩子換下王孫，把居魯士養大。

sensitivity.note: Greek historiography recording the Iranian Cyrus-exposure legend (cf. Oedipus/romulus types); read as legend. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Astyages saw another vision. It seemed to him that from his daughter a vine grew, and this vine overspread the whole of Asia. Having seen this vision and delivered it to the interpreters of dreams, he sent for his daughter, being then with child, to come from the land of the Persians. And when she had come he kept watch over her, desiring to destroy that which should be born of her; for the Magian interpreters of dreams signified to him that the offspring of his daughter should be king in his room.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.108 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿斯提阿格斯又看見另一個異象。在他看來，彷彿從他女兒身上長出一株葡萄藤，這葡萄藤蔓延遍及整個亞細亞。他看見這異象並將其告知解夢者之後，便召他當時正懷有身孕的女兒，從波斯人的地方前來。她來了以後，他便派人看守她，想要毀滅她將要生下的孩子；因為波斯的解夢術士向他指明，他女兒的後裔將取代他為王。

passages.text: Astyages then desiring to guard against this, when Cyrus was born, called Harpagos, a man who was of kin near him and whom he trusted above all the other Medes, and to him he said: take the child which Mandane bore, and carry it to thy house and slay it; and afterwards bury it in whatsoever manner thou thyself desirest. To this he made answer: if it is indeed thy pleasure that this should so be done, my service at least must be fitly rendered.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.108 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿斯提阿格斯為防範此事，當居魯士出生時，便召來哈爾帕戈斯——此人與他血緣相近，也是他較諸其他所有米底人更為信任的人——對他說：帶走曼丹妮所生的孩子，送到你家裡殺掉；之後隨你自己所願，用任何方式將他埋葬。他對此回答說：若這確實是你的意願，此事當如此行，那麼我的效勞至少必當妥善盡到。

passages.text: Not according as Astyages enjoined, Harpagos went weeping and told his wife: for not even if he shall come to be yet more out of his senses and more mad than he now is, will I agree to his will or serve him in such a murder as this. And for many reasons I will not slay the child; first because he is a kin to me, and then because Astyages is old and without male issue, and if after he is dead the power shall come through me, does not the greatest of dangers then await me?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.109 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 哈爾帕戈斯並未遵照阿斯提阿格斯的吩咐，而是哭著告訴他的妻子：因為即使他日後變得比現在更加神志不清、更加瘋狂，我也不會同意他的意願，也不會替他做這樣一樁謀殺。我不殺這孩子，有許多理由；首先因為他是我的親族，其次因為阿斯提阿格斯年邁且無男嗣，倘若他死後權力經由我而來，那麼最大的危險豈不就在那時等著我嗎？

passages.text: He sent a messenger to that one of the herdsmen of Astyages who fed his herds on the pastures most suitable for his purpose, and on the mountains most haunted by wild beasts: Astyages bids thee take this child and place it on the most desolate part of the mountains, so that it may perish as quickly as possible. And it came to pass that the herdsman's wife, being every day on the point of bearing a child, by a providential chance brought her child to birth just at that time.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.110-111 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他派了一名使者去見阿斯提阿格斯那些牧人之中、在最適合其目的的牧場上、在最常有野獸出沒的山上放牧畜群的那一位，說：阿斯提阿格斯命你帶走這孩子，把他放在山上最荒涼的地方，好讓他盡快死去。而事情恰巧如此：那牧人的妻子每日都臨近分娩，因著天意的安排，就在那時生下了她的孩子。

title.en: Dareios Wins the Kingdom by the Neighing of His Horse
title.zh: 大流士以馬嘶得國

region.en: Suburb of the Persian city (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 波斯城郊（象徵性定位）

period: Written c. 430 BCE (Macaulay translation 1890)

source.work: Herodotus, Histories Book 1, trans. G. C. Macaulay (1890), secs. 85-88

summary.en: After the seven conspirators had left their assembly, Dareios spoke to Oibares: we have resolved that the man whose horse first neighs at sunrise, when we are mounted upon our horses, he shall be king. Oibares, the clever horse-keeper, ties up in the suburb the mare that the horse of Dareios prefers, and lets the stallion mount her; at dawn, when the six ride past, the horse runs to the place and neighs — and just when the horse had done this there came lightning and thunder from a clear sky. Dareios made a carving in stone with the figure of a man on horseback, and wrote upon it: Dareios son of Hystaspes by the excellence of his horse, and of his horse-keeper Oibares obtained the kingdom of the Persians.
summary.zh: 七人密謀誅殺偽王者議定：翌日日出時「馬先嘶者為王」。馭手奧伊巴雷斯的詭計是：把大流士坐騎鍾愛的牝馬牽到城郊繫好，縱其交合。破曉六人騎馬路過，那馬直奔牝馬嘶鳴——恰在此刻晴空炸雷掣電！眾人認為天意如此，下馬朝拜。大流士登基後立碑刻像：「大流士憑其駿馬與馭手奧伊巴雷斯之力得波斯王位。」

sensitivity.note: Greek historiography of the Darius accession legend; read as historical legend. No living community restriction.

passages.text: When they had left their assembly, Dareios spoke these words: Oibares, we have resolved to do about the kingdom thus, namely that the man whose horse first neighs at sunrise, when we are mounted upon our horses he shall be king. Now therefore, if thou hast any cleverness, contrive that we may obtain this prize, and not any other man. Oibares replied: if, my master, it depends in truth upon this whether thou be king or no, have confidence, for none other shall be king before thee; such charms have I at my command.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.85 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他們離開集會之後，大流士說了這番話：歐伊巴瑞斯，我們已經議定關於王位之事如此辦理，即當我們騎上馬時，誰的馬最先在日出時嘶鳴，誰就作王。所以現在，你若有何機巧，就設法使我們得著這獎賞，而不讓別人得著。歐伊巴瑞斯回答說：主人啊，若此事果真取決於你是否作王，請放心，因為絕無別人能先於你作王；我自有這等法術在握。

passages.text: Oibares therefore hearing this did as follows: when night was coming on he took one of the mares, namely that one which the horse of Dareios preferred, and this he led into the suburb of the city and tied her up; then he brought to her the horse of Dareios. Now at dawn of day the six came to the place as they had agreed, riding upon their horses; and when they came near the place where the mare had been tied up on the former night, the horse of Dareios ran up to the place and neighed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.85-86 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 歐伊巴瑞斯聽了這話，便如此行：夜幕將臨時，他牽來一匹母馬，正是大流士的馬所偏愛的那一匹，把她牽到城郊並拴住；然後他把大流士的馬牽到她跟前。到了黎明時分，那六人依約騎馬來到那地方；當他們走近前夜拴母馬之處時，大流士的馬便奔到那地方嘶鳴起來。

passages.text: Just when the horse had done this, there came lightning and thunder from a clear sky; and the happening of these things to Dareios consummated his claim, for they seemed to have come to pass by some design, and the others leapt down from their horses and did obeisance to Dareios. He caused to be a carving in stone, and in it the figure of a man on horseback, writing to this effect: Dareios son of Hystaspes by the excellence of his horse, and of his horse-keeper Oibares obtained the kingdom of the Persians.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.86-88 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 就在那馬如此行之時，晴空中竟起了閃電與雷鳴；這些事臨到大流士，便成全了他的主張，因為它們彷彿是出於某種安排而發生，其餘的人便跳下馬來，向大流士行禮。他命人刻石為記，其上刻一人騎馬之像，並刻文如下：希斯塔斯佩斯之子大流士，因其馬之優異，並因其馬夫歐伊巴瑞斯之故，得波斯人之王國。

title.en: Tomyris Gives Cyrus His Fill of Blood
title.zh: 托米麗司血祭居魯士

region.en: River Araxes, land of the Massagetai (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿拉克塞斯河畔（象徵性定位）

period: Written c. 430 BCE (Macaulay translation 1890)

source.work: Herodotus, Histories Book 1, trans. G. C. Macaulay (1890), secs. 211-214

summary.en: Tomyris, queen of the Massagetai, sends a herald when her son Spargapises is taken by the wine-snare of the Persians: Cyrus, insatiable of blood, restore to me my son and depart from this land without penalty; but if thou shalt not do so, I swear to thee by the Sun, who is lord of the Massagetai, that surely I will give thee thy fill of blood, insatiable as thou art. Cyrus makes no account of her words; her son, when the wine left him, puts himself to death; Tomyris gathers all her power and joins battle, and of the army of Cyrus the greater part is destroyed and Cyrus himself falls, and Tomyris fills a skin with human blood and dips the head of Cyrus in it.
summary.zh: 瑪薩革泰女王托米麗司之子被波斯人的「酒計」所擒。她遣使警告：「嗜血的居魯士啊，還我兒子、退出此土；否則我以瑪薩革泰的主宰太陽起誓——定叫你飲血到足！」居魯士不納其言；王子醒酒後自盡。女王傾全國之兵決戰，波斯大軍盡墨、居魯士陣亡。托米麗司以人血灌滿皮囊，將居魯士之首浸入其中——「讓你飲個夠！」

sensitivity.note: Greek historiography of Cyrus' death legend; Tomyris became a Persian literary figure. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Seeing the feast that was set forth, when the Massagetai had overcome their enemies they lay down and feasted, and being satiated with food and wine they went to sleep. Then the Persians came upon them and slew many of them, and took alive many more even than they slew, and among these the son of the queen Tomyris, who was leading the army of the Massagetai; and his name was Spargapises.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.211 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 馬薩革泰人見擺設了筵席，擊敗敵人之後便躺下宴飲，飽食酒肉之後便睡去了。於是波斯人來襲，殺了他們許多人，生擒的比殺的還多，其中就有率領馬薩革泰軍的女王托米麗司之子；他的名字叫斯帕爾伽皮塞斯。

passages.text: She then sent a herald to Cyrus and said: Cyrus, insatiable of blood, be not elated with pride by this which has come to pass, because with that fruit of the vine, with which ye fill yourselves and become so mad, because setting a snare with such a drug as this thou didst overcome my son, and not by valour in fight. Now therefore receive the word which I utter: restore to me my son and depart from this land without penalty; but if thou shalt not do so, I swear to thee by the Sun, who is lord of the Massagetai, that surely I will give thee thy fill of blood, insatiable as thou art.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.212 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她便派了一名傳令官去見居魯士，說：居魯士啊，你這嗜血無厭之人，不要因這已發生之事而驕矜自傲，因為你是用那葡萄之果——你們用它灌滿自己而變得如此瘋狂——用這樣的藥物設下陷阱，才制伏了我的兒子，而不是憑戰鬥中的勇武。所以現在，請聽我所說的話：把我的兒子還給我，並不受懲罰地離開這片土地；但你若不這樣做，我便向那為馬薩革泰人之主的太陽向你起誓，我必使你這嗜血無厭之人喝血喝個飽。

passages.text: The son of the queen Tomyris, when the wine left him and he learnt in what evil case he was, entreated Cyrus that he might be loosed from his chains and gained his request, and then so soon as he was loosed and had got power over his hands he put himself to death. Tomyris, as Cyrus did not listen to her, gathered together all her power and joined battle, and of the army of Cyrus the greater part was destroyed, and Cyrus himself fell.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.213-214 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 女王托米麗斯之子在酒醒之後，得知自己身陷何等不幸的境地，便懇求居魯士讓他解開鎖鏈，並獲得了允准；於是，他一獲釋、雙手得以自由，便自盡而死。托米麗斯見居魯士不聽她的話，便召集全部兵力與之交戰，居魯士的軍隊大半被殲滅，居魯士本人也陣亡了。

title.en: The Persians' Sacrifices and the Magian Chant
title.zh: 波斯人的祭祀與瑪術士頌歌

region.en: Mountain heights of sacrifice (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 祭祀山巔（象徵性定位）

period: Written c. 430 BCE (Macaulay translation 1890)

source.work: Herodotus, Histories Book 1, trans. G. C. Macaulay (1890), secs. 131-133

summary.en: Images and temples and altars they do not account it lawful to erect; nay, they even charge with folly those who do these things, because they do not account the gods to be in the likeness of men. But it is their wont to perform sacrifices to Zeus going up to the most lofty of the mountains, and the whole circle of the heavens they call Zeus: and they sacrifice to the Sun and the Moon and the Earth, to Fire and to Water and to the Winds. When a man wishes to sacrifice, he leads the animal to an unpolluted place and calls upon the god, having his tiara wreathed with myrtle; he prays not for himself alone, but that it may be well with all the Persians and with the king; and when he has boiled the flesh, a Magian man stands by and chants over them a theogony, seeing that without a Magian it is not lawful for them to make sacrifices.
