title.en: The Igigu Rebellion and the Making of Man
title.zh: 伊吉吉叛變與人類之造

region.en: Nippur and the gods' earthworks, Iraq
region.zh: 尼普魯與眾神工程（伊拉克）

period: Old Babylonian, c. 18th c. BCE (Rogers translation 1912)

source.work: Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament, 'Ea and Atrakhasis', trans. Robert W. Rogers (1912)

summary.en: The great gods burden the Igigu with digging the rivers for centuries; at last they surround Enlil's temple and refuse the shovel. Enki and the mother goddess knead mankind from clay and the blood of a slain god: the workers who will carry the gods' labor.
summary.zh: 大神令伊吉吉掘河數百年；最後眾神圍恩利爾神殿、罷鏟不掘。恩基與母神以黏土及被誅神之血揉合成人——承擔神之勞役的工眾誕生。

sensitivity.note: Ancient myth; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: For centuries the Igigu dig the rivers, dredge canals and pile the earthworks; their strength is spent, their hands too heavy. At last they surround the house of Enlil, god of force and judgment, and refuse the shovel: who will take the burden?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Atrahasis, Tablet I (Rogers 1912); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 數世紀以來，伊吉古挖掘河流、疏濬運河、堆築土方；他們的力氣耗盡，雙手過於沉重。最終他們圍住恩利爾——力量與審判之神——的居所，拒絕鐵鏟：誰來承擔這重擔？

passages.text: Enlil's fear is calmed by wise Ea's counsel: a god must die for the new work. One of the Igigu — We-ila — is slain, and Nintu the mother goddess kneads clay with his blood; on the tenth day the seventh man is formed: mankind, made to carry the gods' baskets.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Atrahasis, Tablet I, creation scene; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 恩利爾的恐懼被睿智的埃阿之諫所平息：必須有一位神為這新工作而死。伊吉古中的一位——維伊拉——被殺，母親女神寧圖以他的血摶合泥土；第十日，第七個人被造出：人類，受造以承擔眾神的籃子。

functions: Founding myth of human labor as divine service
Etiology of the temple corvee economy
Theology of the strike: labor dispute as cosmogony

title.en: The Plague of Atrahasis
title.zh: 阿特拉哈西斯瘟疫

region.en: Nippur, Iraq
region.zh: 尼普魯（伊拉克）

period: Old Babylonian, c. 18th c. BCE (Rogers translation 1912)

source.work: Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament, 'Ea and Atrakhasis', trans. Robert W. Rogers (1912)

summary.en: Six hundred years later the land teems and the people's noise again disturbs Enlil; he sends pestilence. Atrahasis, told by Ea to stop worshipping all gods but Namtara, starves the god of death out — the plague ceases: mankind survives by giving Namtara bread and water.
summary.zh: 六百年後人丁鼎盛，喧囂再擾恩利爾；他降下瘟疫。埃亞授計阿特拉哈西斯：專祭死神納姆塔爾、斷絕他神之祭；死神因饑而求和——瘟疫止息：人類以麵包與水救了自己。

sensitivity.note: Ancient myth; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Six hundred years of teeming births later, the land roars with people like a wild ox, and Enlil, troubled by their noise, sends Namtara to destroy them: let pestilence make an end of the clamor. Ea instructs Atrahasis: worship every god but Namtara — starve the death-god out. Atrahasis gathers the people, and the offerings to Namtara alone bring him bread and water; the god, shamed, accepts the first offering in six centuries and the plague ceases.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Atrahasis, Tablet I-II (Rogers 1912); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Atrahasis, Tablet I-II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 六百年間生靈繁衍不息，此後大地如野牛般喧騰著人群的聲響，恩利爾為這喧囂所擾，遂遣納姆塔拉毀滅他們：讓瘟疫終結這片喧嘩。埃阿指示阿特拉哈西斯：敬拜諸神，唯獨不拜納姆塔拉——將這死亡之神餓斃。阿特拉哈西斯召集眾人，單單獻給納姆塔拉的供品為他送來麵包與水；這位神明羞愧難當，接受了六百年來的第一份供品，瘟疫於是止息。

functions: Myth of ritual bargaining with the god of death
Etiology of selective offering strategy
Model of the wise intercessor

title.en: Famine and Drought: The Second and Third Trials
title.zh: 饑荒與乾旱：第二三次災劫

region.en: The land of Sumer, Iraq
region.zh: 蘇美大地（伊拉克）

period: Old Babylonian, c. 18th c. BCE (Rogers translation 1912)

source.work: Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament, 'Ea and Atrakhasis', trans. Robert W. Rogers (1912)

summary.en: Enlil tries again: Adad withholds the rain, the earth's produce fails, year after year the famine eats deeper — mothers sell children — until Ea's counsel has mankind worship Adad alone, and the rain god relents.
summary.zh: 恩利爾再施毒計：阿達德收雨，地產枯竭，年復一年饑荒日深——母親賣兒——直至埃亞授計，人們獨祭阿達德；雨神心軟降雨。

sensitivity.note: Ancient myth; famine imagery belongs to the mythic register.

passages.text: Enlil tries again: Adad withholds his rain, Tiamat's fields crack, the year's produce fails; a second year brings dust, a third famine's depth — mothers barter their children for food, houses are closed, the land is a grave. Again Ea's counsel: worship Adad alone. The rain god, faced with the starving altar, relents and sends the rains — mankind, saved a second time by the wise man's management of divine needs.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Atrahasis, Tablet II (Rogers 1912); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Atrahasis, Tablet II; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 恩利爾再度出手：阿達德扣住他的雨水，提亞馬特的田野龜裂，當年收成盡毀；第二年帶來塵土，第三年則是饑荒的深淵——母親們以兒女換取食物，屋舍緊閉，大地成了一座墳墓。埃阿的勸告依舊：單單敬拜阿達德。雨神面對饑餓的祭壇，終於軟下心來，降下甘霖——人類第二次因這智者對神明需求的照料而得救。

functions: Myth of famine as divine management crisis
Escalation structure preparing the flood
Etiology of exclusive worship strategy

title.en: Barren Women and the Demon Pashittu
title.zh: 不育婦女與帕什圖魔

region.en: Birth houses of Sumer, Iraq
region.zh: 蘇美產房（伊拉克）

period: Old Babylonian, c. 18th c. BCE (Rogers translation 1912)

source.work: Cuneiform Parallels to the Old Testament, 'Ea and Atrakhasis', trans. Robert W. Rogers (1912)

summary.en: Enlil's peace is made with a regulated womb: Nintu creates the barren woman, the demoness Pashittu who snatches infants, and the classes of priestesses who may not bear — and the birth rites are instituted, so the clamor never returns.
summary.zh: 恩利爾以受控之生育締和：寧圖造不育之婦、奪嬰之魔帕什圖、不可生育的祭司階層——並定產褥之禮，喧囂自此不復。

sensitivity.note: Ancient myth; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: Enlil's peace includes a regulated womb: Nintu creates the barren woman who will not bear, and the demoness Pashittu who snatches infants from their mothers' laps. The birth rites are instituted: the mat of the birth-stool, the brick of the laboring woman, the offerings that mark the days after delivery — the poem closes with these settlements, the flood's price fixed in ritual.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Atrahasis, Tablet III end (Rogers 1912); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Atrahasis, Tablet III end; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 恩利爾的和平包含對子宮的節制：寧圖創造了不會生育的不孕女子，以及從母親膝上奪走嬰兒的女魔帕希圖。生育儀式由此訂立：產凳的席墊、產婦的磚塊、標記產後日子的供品——詩篇以這些安排作結，洪水的代價就此固定於儀式之中。

functions: Charter of birth rites and fertility regulation
Etiology of the infant-snatching demon
Social theology of sterile vocations

variants.name: Lamashtu demonology
variants.summary: The developed cult of the infant-snatching demoness.

title.en: Xisuthrus: Berossus' Flood
title.zh: 克蘇特魯斯：貝羅蘇斯洪水記

region.en: Sippar, Iraq
region.zh: 西帕爾（伊拉克）

period: Berossus' Babyloniaca, c. 290 BCE, preserved in George Smith 1876

source.work: The Chaldean Account of Genesis, George Smith (1876), ch. on Berossus

summary.en: The god Cronus warns Xisuthrus in a dream that a flood will destroy mankind, and to bury the writings at Sippar and build the boat; the flood passes, birds are sent out, and the survivor descends with his family — translating the Babylonian deluge into Greek chronicle.
summary.zh: 克羅諾斯神於夢中警告克蘇特魯斯：洪水將滅人類，命其於西帕爾埋藏典籍、建造大舟。洪水退後放鳥試探，倖存者攜家眷下舟——巴比倫洪水敘事經希臘史家之筆傳世。

sensitivity.note: Hellenistic retelling; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: The god Cronus appears to Xisuthrus in a dream and warns him: on the fifteenth day of the month Daisios mankind shall be destroyed by a flood; bury the beginnings and endings of all things at Sippar, and build the boat.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Berossus' flood account as given in George Smith, Chaldean Account of Genesis (1876); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 克洛諾斯神在夢中向西蘇特羅斯顯現，警告他：戴西俄斯月第十五日，人類將被洪水毀滅；將萬物的開端與終結埋於西帕爾，並建造船隻。

passages.text: The flood passes; birds are sent out and return without a place to rest until the third bird does not return. Xisuthrus descends with wife, daughter and pilot, pays worship to the gods, and vanishes with them; the company left in the boat searches and hears a voice from the air — go down to Babylon and dig up the writings at Sippar, and hand them to mankind.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Berossus' account (1876); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 洪水退去；放出的鳥兒飛回，找不到棲息之地，直到第三隻鳥不再歸來。西蘇特羅斯帶著妻子、女兒與舵手下船，向眾神獻上敬拜，隨即與他們一同消失；留在船上的人四處尋找，聽見空中傳來聲音——下到巴比倫，掘出西帕爾的典籍，交給人類。

functions: Late transmission of the flood myth to the classical world
Charter of the buried scriptures motif

title.en: Religious Conceptions of the Bushman
title.zh: 桑人之宗教觀念

region.en: Hantam River & Bushmanland, Northern Cape (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南非北開普省哈坦姆河與布什曼蘭（象徵定位）

period: San ethnographic summary; recorded 1870s-1880s by G. R. von Wielligh, published 1921

source.work: G. R. von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories, Deel III (1921), No. 56

summary.en: Von Wielligh's summary of Bushman belief: the old race ('Chwe-'na-ssho-'ke) could change into any animal, tree or person; the sun is a murdered man's head thrown into the sky; the moon is the Mantis's shoe that dies and revives; the hollow moon carries the newly dead, who come alive with it; death became permanent only through the Hare's quarrel; the Morning Star is Dawn's heart and the Evening Star Evening-gleam's heart; and a great star once sang all the stars their names.
summary.zh: 范威利赫之桑人信仰撮要：古族（'楚那索克）可化為任何獸、樹、人；日乃被弒者之首擲天而成；月乃螳螂之鞋，死而復生；空月承載新死者，隨月復活；死亡之恆久僅因野兔之爭；晨星為曙光之心、昏星為暮光之心；一大星曾唱出眾星之名。

sensitivity.note: Ethnographic summary written by G. R. von Wielligh from his own Bushman informants; presented as an archival record of colonial-era fieldwork.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh Deel III No. 56 (1921); not verbatim. Of a Supreme Being, of a place of Happiness or of Punishment the Bushman has no conception at all. His outgoing thought seems to be that in the beginning there existed an old race of Bushmen; to it all owe their existence. He knows the old race as 'Chwe-'na-ssho-'ke, who could change themselves into any animal, tree or person. In the beginning there was a twilight over the whole earth; the sun, moon and stars arose only later.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 56; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 馮·維利赫第三卷第五十六號（1921年）的濃縮轉述；並非逐字照錄。對於至高存在、對於幸福之地或懲罰之地，布須曼人全然沒有概念。他向外馳騁的思想似乎是：起初存在著一個古老的布須曼種族；萬物皆因它而存在。他稱這古老種族為「Chwe-'na-ssho-'ke」，他們能將自己變成任何動物、樹木或人。起初，暮光籠罩整個大地；太陽、月亮與星辰直到後來才出現。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. The sun is one of the old race, with a shining face, whom the others murdered; the children, at their mothers' command, threw the head of the sun-man into the sky, where it still is. Morning after morning the head rises on the east and seeks its body, which has become a crab, till evening, and sleeps in the west to wake again the next morning. The moon is the shoe of the 'Hotnotsgod which the whirlwind blew into the sky; the hollow of the horned moon is the receiving place of the newly dead.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 56; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同一出處的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。太陽屬於古老種族之一，有一張發光的臉，卻被其他成員殺害；孩子們奉母親之命，把太陽人的頭顱拋向天空，那頭顱至今仍留在天上。每天早晨，那頭顱從東方升起，尋找牠已化為螃蟹的身軀，直到傍晚，然後在西邊沉睡，翌晨再醒來。月亮是「Hotnotsgod」的鞋，被旋風吹上了天；帶角的月亮中空之處，是新死者安放之所。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. As the moon grows again to full moon the corpses come alive again by the power of the moonwater; and as the moon becomes full and has no more place for the revived persons, those persons descend to the earth and come alive again whenever they die — just as the moon comes alive month after month. Thus death was at first only a temporary sleep. But death — so as not to come alive again — came into the world through the Hare, who strove with the Moon and was split-lipped; hence the superstition of the piece of sinew-flesh in the hare's thigh that has remained human flesh, which Bushmen do not eat.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 56; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同一出處的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。當月亮再度盈滿，屍體便藉月亮之水之力重新活過來；而當月亮圓滿、再無餘地容納復活之人時，那些人便降回大地，每逢死去便再度復活——正如月亮月復一月地重生。因此死亡起初不過是暫時的睡眠。但死亡——為了不再復活——經由野兔進入世界，野兔曾與月亮相爭，因而裂了唇；於是有了野兔大腿上那塊仍屬人肉的筋腱肉之迷信，布須曼人不食此肉。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. The Morning Star is the heart of Daybreak and the Evening Star the heart of Evening-gleam; the other great stars are living beings, and the little stars also live. One great star gave, in a song, all the stars their names... When a notable person dies, a great heap of stones is piled over his grave, and that stone-heap is honoured for the sake of the spirit that dwells in it; when one buries someone a 'laying-down prayer' is first spoken before the funeral procession leaves the grave.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 56; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同一出處的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。晨星是破曉之心，昏星是暮光之心；其他大星皆是活物，小星亦皆有生命。有一顆大星曾以歌聲為眾星命名……當顯要之人死去，其墳上便堆起一大堆石頭，那石堆因棲居其中的神靈而受敬奉；埋葬某人時，在送葬隊伍離開墳墓之前，須先誦念一段「安放祈禱」。

title.en: Superstitions Concerning Certain Animals
title.zh: 關於特定動物之迷信

region.en: Hantam River & Bushmanland, Northern Cape (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南非北開普省哈坦姆河與布什曼蘭（象徵定位）

period: San ethnographic summary; recorded 1870s-1880s by G. R. von Wielligh, published 1921

source.work: G. R. von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories, Deel III (1921), No. 57

summary.en: Animal superstitions: the Water-Snake dries up springs before white hunters; a serpent-stone draws poison from a bite; the jackal's heart makes children cowards; ostrich lungs must be eaten raw by children for a big voice; a beheaded snake crawls home to hide in its killer's bedding; springbok possess invisible arrows; meat of slow game makes hunters' aim true; and snakes near graves bring good tidings.
summary.zh: 動物迷信：水蛇於白人獵者前涸泉；蛇石可吸毒；豺心使童懦怯；童須生食鴕肺以得巨聲；斷首之蛇爬回藏於仇者床褥；跳羚具無形之箭；食緩獸之肉使射者命中；墓旁之蛇報吉訊。

sensitivity.note: Ethnographic summary by G. R. von Wielligh; presented as an archival record.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh Deel III No. 57 (1921); not verbatim. The Great Water-Snake has a glittering stone on its head and the power to make fountains fill or dry up. He listens well to the Bushman sorcerers and follows the hunters under the ground everywhere in the waterless regions; where he is the fountains overflow, or he brings the water up to just under the surface so the hunters need only dig a shallow hole... As soon as white hunters follow the game into the desert, the Bushmen have only to speak with the Great Water-Snake, and he lets the strongest fountain dry up before the eyes of the whites.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 57; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 濃縮改述自 von Wielligh 第三卷第五十七號（1921年）；非逐字照錄。大水蛇頭上有一顆閃耀的寶石，並有使泉水湧滿或乾涸之力。牠善聽布須曼巫師之言，在無水之地隨獵人潛行於地下各處；凡牠所在之處，泉水便溢出，或牠把水帶到僅及地表之下，獵人只需挖個淺坑即可……一旦白人獵人追獵物進入荒漠，布須曼人只須與大水蛇一說，牠便在白人眼前讓最強勁的泉水乾涸。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. The heart of the jackal is never given to children to eat, for a jackal is very timid; if children eat the heart they become cowards... If a Bushman shoots an ostrich, his children must eat the lungs of the ostrich raw; for if the lungs are cooked they lose the property of giving the children a big voice — the Bushmen find the booming of an ostrich finer than the roaring of a lion.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 57; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同一出處的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。豺的心從不給孩子吃，因為豺極為膽怯；孩子若吃了心便會變成懦夫……布須曼人若射得一隻鴕鳥，其子女必須生吃鴕鳥的肺；因為肺若煮熟，便失去使孩子聲音洪亮之效——布須曼人覺得鴕鳥的轟鳴比獅子的咆哮更美妙。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. If someone wounds a snake, or even only breaks its head from the body a little way, that snake comes to the house of the person who hurt it, hides itself somewhere in a corner, in his bedding or in his veld-shoe, and lies there ready to bite the person dead. The Bushmen do not let their children play on fresh springbok skins, nor let fresh blood or flesh touch bow, arrow or quiver; for then the spirit of the springbok draws into the children or the owner of the bow and arrow, and the springboks in the veld become wild toward such people... The springbok possesses invisible arrows with which it can shoot a person unnoticed; they go inside the body and make him sick, and when he is sick he always shoots wide.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 57; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同一出處的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。若有人傷了一條蛇，甚至只是把牠的頭從身體稍稍扯斷，那條蛇便會來到傷牠之人的家中，藏身於某個角落、他的鋪蓋裡或他的草原鞋中，躺在那裡伺機咬死那人。布須曼人不讓孩子在新鮮的跳羚皮上玩耍，也不讓新鮮的血或肉觸及弓、箭或箭袋；因為如此一來，跳羚的靈便會附入孩子或弓箭主人身上，而草原上的跳羚便會對這樣的人兇猛起來……跳羚擁有無形的箭，能不知不覺地射中一個人；箭進入體內使他生病，而當他生病時，他射箭總是偏得厲害。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. When a snake is seen by a grave it must be respected and not killed, for it brings good tidings of the one buried there, or brings good tidings to the spirit of the dead person... To make rain only the maids strike with stones on the ground; the Rain-Beast hears the stamping and then lets rain come through a thunderstorm.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 57; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 節縮改述，同一出處；非逐字照錄。在墳墓旁看見蛇時，必須敬重牠，不可將牠殺死，因為牠會帶來關於葬於該處之人的好消息，或為亡者的靈魂帶來好消息……為了求雨，只有少女們會以石頭敲擊地面；雨獸聽見那跺踏聲，便透過一場雷雨讓雨水降下。

title.en: More Superstitions: Weather, Dreams and Ghosts
title.zh: 更多迷信：天氣、夢與鬼

region.en: Hantam River & Bushmanland, Northern Cape (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南非北開普省哈坦姆河與布什曼蘭（象徵定位）

period: San ethnographic summary; recorded 1870s-1880s by G. R. von Wielligh, published 1921

source.work: G. R. von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories, Deel III (1921), No. 58

summary.en: The lightning kills with stones; look straight at the flash and its eye respects yours. The Wind-bird avenges stone-throwing with a storm; toadstools are the rain's children and must be set down gently; music in a storm draws the thunderbolt; a fist-sized stone heated in the ashes burns bad dreams; and a shooting star with a long train tells of a far friend's death.
summary.zh: 雷以石殺人；直視閃光者，其電乃避其目。風鳥遭擲石則起暴風報復；傘菌乃雨之子，須輕放；雷時奏樂者引雷石；拳大之石入火灰可焚惡夢；長尾流星預告遠方友人之死。

sensitivity.note: Ethnographic summary by G. R. von Wielligh; presented as an archival record.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh Deel III No. 58 (1921); not verbatim. The Bushman has great awe of thunder, wind and storms... He believes the thunder can kill a person with stones. If the flash is sharp, one must look at the lightning, and one's eyes shine like the lightning itself, and then the ray of light will have respect for the eyes of the person who looks at it and will not strike him dead.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 58; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 節縮改述自 von Wielligh 第三卷第五十八號（1921年）；非逐字照錄。布須曼人對雷、風與暴風雨懷有極大的敬畏……他相信雷能用石頭擊殺人。若閃光銳利，人必須注視那閃電，而自己的雙眼便會如閃電本身一般發亮，如此一來，那道光線便會敬重注視牠之人的眼睛，不會將他擊斃。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. The wind is made by a bird, the Wind-bird, with its wings and blowing. If anyone throws stones, kieries or sand at the Wind-bird, or shoots arrows at him, he makes that bird angry, and the maker of the wind lets a storm arise to destroy and tear everything apart... Toadstools and other mushroom growths are the children of the rain; if anyone pulls them out he must not throw them about but set them down gently, otherwise the rain grows angry and calls up a storm that washes everything away.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 58; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 節縮改述，同一出處；非逐字照錄。風是由一隻鳥——風鳥——以其雙翼與吹氣所造成的。若有人向風鳥投擲石頭、投擲棍棒或沙土，或向牠射箭，便是惹怒了那隻鳥，而造風者便會興起一場暴風雨，將一切摧毀撕裂……毒蕈與其他菌類是雨的子女；若有人將它們拔出，不可隨意亂丟，而須輕輕放下，否則雨便會發怒，召來一場沖刷一切的暴風雨。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. To get rid of the evil consequences of dreams the Bushmen seek a stone as big as their fist, hold it in the hand, talk to it and tell the bad dreams they had in the night; then they blow their breath on the stone and quickly push it under the warm ashes and coals, so that the dreams must burn. If they do not do this, the bad dreams go with them into the field and tell everything to the game, the Bushman-rice and the veld-food, so that the dreamer finds it all bad in the field and comes home disappointed.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 58; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 節縮改述，同一出處；非逐字照錄。為了消除夢境帶來的不良後果，布須曼人會找一塊拳頭大小的石頭，握在手中，對它說話，把夜裡所做的惡夢告訴它；接著他們向石頭吹氣，迅速將它推入溫熱的灰燼與炭火之下，好讓那些夢被燒盡。若他們不這麼做，惡夢便會隨他們進入田野，把一切告訴獵物、布須曼米與野地食物，以致做夢者在田野中覺得樣樣都不順，最後失望而歸。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. The Bushman is very much afraid of ghosts; near a burial place one does not get him in the dark. If he thinks he sees a ghost, he pulls out a bush, sets it upside down with the roots up, and runs away as hard as he can; for if the ghost sees a bush standing upside down, he imagines the bush grew so, stands there marvelling how it can grow — and when a wind blows the bush over, the ghost springs away and returns to the one who planted it, seeing it is all humbug. And if a star shoots — especially with a long train of light — the Bushmen believe a friend or acquaintance has died; the star shows where the person lives, and a few days later the sad tidings come.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel III (1921), No. 58; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 節縮改述，同一出處；非逐字照錄。布須曼人非常害怕鬼魂；在墓地附近，天黑時誰也無法叫他前去。若他覺得自己看見了鬼，便會拔起一叢灌木，將它根朝上倒立起來，然後拼命逃走；因為鬼若看見一叢倒立的灌木，便會以為那灌木本是這樣生長的，站在那裡驚嘆它怎能如此生長——而當一陣風把灌木吹倒時，鬼便會跳開，回到栽種它的人那裡，看出這全是騙局。而若有星辰劃過——尤其是拖著長長光尾的——布須曼人便相信有位朋友或熟人死了；那顆星指示出那人所居之處，數日之後，悲傷的消息便傳來了。

title.en: Krappies and the Ghost in the Churchyard
title.zh: 克拉皮與墓園之靈

region.en: Cape colonial farm country (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 開普殖民地農莊（象徵定位）

period: San oral tradition; told to G. R. von Wielligh by Oom Karel and Piet M., published 1922

source.work: G. R. von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories, Deel IV (1922), No. 95

summary.en: Krappies, a superstitious Bushman servant, tends his master's grave flowers faithfully; on New Year's Eve he drinks by mistake a bottle of spirits, wakes in the churchyard, sees an owl on the grave and his dead master standing with a bottle — 'Krappies, Krappies, what is this?' — and a goat at the gate. The ghost haunts his room; he falls sick, confesses, and never touches drink again, believing the master's spirit came to set him right.
summary.zh: 迷信之桑僕克拉皮忠心照料主墓之花；除夕誤飲烈酒，醒於墓園，見墓上之鴞與手持酒瓶之亡主——「克拉皮，克拉皮，此為何物？」——門前又有山羊。亡靈夜擾其室；他病倒、吐實、滴酒不沾，深信主人之靈來懲其過。

sensitivity.note: San oral tradition recorded in Afrikaans by G. R. von Wielligh; colonial setting; presented as an archival record.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh Deel IV No. 95 (1922); not verbatim. Krappies was a particularly sly little fellow and soon became the favourite of the master's children; he was very superstitious, and that was too fine for the children, so they could play many more jokes with him. He was dead-honest in his way, but not with tobacco and strong drink — there he stole wherever a chance offered.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 95; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 節縮改述自 von Wielligh 第四卷第九十五號（1922年）；非逐字照錄。克拉皮斯是個格外狡猾的小傢伙，很快便成了主人家孩子們的寵兒；他非常迷信，而這對孩子們來說實在太妙了，因此他們能跟他開更多玩笑。就他自身的方式而言，他極為誠實，但在菸草與烈酒上卻不然——只要一有機會，他便會偷。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. Oom Willem's wife died and was buried in the family churchyard on the farm; the master called Krappies and told him the old missus had always been so good to him, and now he must see that the white flower-trees always got water... Krappies tended the churchyard and let no blade of grass grow; and when Oom Willem died soon after and was buried beside his wife, Krappies clung all the more to the churchyard, for he believed the spirits of his master and missus blessed him.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 95; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同處的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。威廉大叔的妻子去世，葬在農場上的家族墓園裡；主人叫來克拉皮斯，對他說，老太太一向待他極好，如今他得留心，讓那些白花樹時時澆到水……克拉皮斯照料墓園，不讓一根草長出來；不久威廉大叔也去世了，葬在妻子身旁，克拉皮斯便更加依戀這座墓園，因為他相信主人與老太太的亡魂都保佑著他。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. On New Year's Eve Krappies worked the whole day alone in the churchyard and got a dop of wine at noon; but under the cypress tree lay, by mistake, spirits of wine instead of brandy. 'Aha, that is the real stuff for you!' He drank, dozed off, and woke in the dark completely confused — in the churchyard. On the old missus's gravestone sat an owl; under the cypress tree stood the old master with the bottle in his hand, asking: 'Krappies, Krappies, what is this?'; and at the little gate a goat blocked his way. He burst through and ran to his room, and the old master's ghost stayed that night in his room. The next day he lay sick, and at last told the whole story; Oom Karel and Oom Piet made it clear to him that it was the spirit of the old master who had come to set him right. He believed it so firmly that he never again put his mouth to strong drink.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 95; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同處的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。除夕那天，克拉皮斯獨自在墓園裡幹了一整天活，中午得了一杯酒；可是柏樹下放著的，一時弄錯，竟是酒精而非白蘭地。「哈，這才是真正的好東西！」他喝了，打起瞌睡，醒來時天已黑透，腦子一片混亂——人還在墓園裡。老太太的墓碑上蹲著一隻貓頭鷹；柏樹下站著老主人，手裡拿著酒瓶，問道：「克拉皮斯，克拉皮斯，這是怎麼回事？」小門那兒又有一隻山羊擋住去路。他衝了出去，跑回自己的房間，那一夜老主人的鬼魂就待在他房裡。第二天他病倒了，最後把整件事都講了出來；卡雷爾大叔和皮特大叔向他講明，那是老主人的亡魂前來糾正他。他對此深信不疑，從此再沒把嘴湊近烈酒。

title.en: Bles and the Sorcerers of the Red-Stone Mine
title.zh: 布列斯與紅石礦之巫者

region.en: Agter-Hantam, Northern Cape (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南非北開普省後哈坦姆（象徵定位）

period: San oral tradition; told to G. R. von Wielligh by Ou Bles in 1882, published 1922

source.work: G. R. von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories, Deel IV (1922), No. 96

summary.en: The old race buried red ochre in a hole in the mountain-side where fierce sorcerers dwell; hunters chew kou-wood that lets them see the old sorcerers unseen, stone the holes as they dig, and club the air as they walk away. A spy-bird turns out to be a sorcerer starling, a great male baboon and his two mates the sorcerers themselves, shot dead by all three bows.
summary.zh: 古族藏紅赭石於山腹之穴，中有兇巫居住；獵者嚼口烏木，得見古巫而巫不見彼；掘時擲石鎮穴，歸途沿途擊空。偵察之鳥竟為巫者化之椋鳥；大雄狒狒與二伴即巫者化身，三弓齊射殺之。

sensitivity.note: San oral tradition recorded in Afrikaans by G. R. von Wielligh; presented as an archival record.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh Deel IV No. 96 (1922); not verbatim. Far up the slope of a mountain is a digging-place for red ochre. The Bushmen of our time always went there to fetch red ochre with which to make their bodies red, colour their knitted skins, and paint people and animals on the rocks. The man who had red ochre was a rich man, for he traded with it among far-dwelling Bushmen.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 96; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 馮·維利赫第四卷第九十六號（一九二二年）的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。高山坡上有一處挖紅赭石的地方。我們這個時代的布須曼人總到那裡去取紅赭石，用來把身體塗紅、給縫製的皮衣上色，並在岩石上畫人和動物。有紅赭石的人就是富人，因為他拿它與遠方居住的布須曼人做買賣。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. They say that in that mountain many fierce sorcerers live, and that they sometimes had to fight hard with those sorcerers over the red ochre. In the days of long ago the old race dug a hole on the slope of the mountain, made red ochre, and stored it in that hole; they hid many other things in holes too, for they lived in that mountain and could see well that others did not spoil their things.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 96; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同處的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。據說那座山裡住著許多凶惡的巫師，他們有時為了紅赭石不得不與那些巫師苦戰。很久以前，古老的一族在山坡上挖了一個洞，製出紅赭石，貯存在那洞裡；他們也在洞裡藏了許多別的東西，因為他們住在那座山裡，看得清楚，不讓別人糟蹋他們的東西。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. Our race, with understanding, can outwit the old sorcerers: before going to the ochre diggings one goes to one of our sorcerers and asks for kou-wood-chips to chew, so that we can see the old sorcerers, but they cannot see us. As they climbed they threw stones all around to frighten the sorcerers, who see the stones fall but not whence they come; the sorcerers flee into holes — a mouse-hole, a scorpion-hole, an ant-hole, the smallest hole they can crawl into. A white-tailed starling flew out of a hole and screeched; the husband shot it with the kou-chip in his mouth; it became a great male baboon with two mates, and all three bows brought them down.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 96; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同處的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。我們這一族憑著見識，能智勝那些老巫師：去赭石坑之前，先去找我們族中的一位巫師，討些嚼用的科木片，這樣我們能看見老巫師，他們卻看不見我們。他們往上爬時，向四下扔石頭，嚇唬那些巫師；巫師只見石頭落下，卻不知從何而來；巫師便逃進洞裡——鼠洞、蠍洞、蟻洞，凡是能鑽進去的最小洞。一隻白尾椋鳥從洞裡飛出，尖聲啼叫；丈夫嘴裡含著科木片，一槍打去；牠變成了一隻大公狒狒，帶著兩隻母狒狒，三張弓一齊放箭，把牠們都射倒了。

title.en: How the Leopard Made a Master of Them
title.zh: 豹之戲弄獵者

region.en: Roggeveld mountains, Northern Cape (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南非北開普省羅格山（象徵定位）

period: San oral tradition; told to G. R. von Wielligh by Ou Bles, published 1922

source.work: G. R. von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories, Deel IV (1922), No. 98

summary.en: The Bushmen trap a leopard in a poisoned-stake pit and haul him out on his tail; the leaped-up leopard scalps one man with his claws, kills another, and eats the dead — while two boys sit weaponless in trees all day. At evening the best shots lure him from tree to tree and kill him: 'so the leopard kept them all day for master.'
summary.zh: 桑人於毒樁坑困豹，曳其尾而出；躍起之豹以爪剝一人之顱、殺另一人、且食其屍——二童持弓無計，終日困於樹上。傍晚善射者誘其逐樹而斃之：「豹遂以其人為主終日。」

sensitivity.note: San oral tradition recorded in Afrikaans by G. R. von Wielligh; graphic violence; presented as an archival record.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh Deel IV No. 98 (1922); not verbatim. In those days there were many leopards in the Roggeveld and Bokveld mountains. The Bushmen knew how to snare them or catch them in trap-pits: under the pit they set long sharp wooden stakes, with points as hard and sharp as an awl, smeared with the same poison as their arrows; and over the pit they arranged the ground and grass with blood and placed the piece of bone-meat behind.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 98; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 馮·維利赫第四卷第九十八號（一九二二年）的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。那些年，羅赫費爾德和博克費爾德的山裡有許多豹子。布須曼人懂得如何設套捕捉牠們，或用陷坑捉牠們：在坑底立起長而尖的木樁，尖端像錐子一樣堅硬鋒利，塗上與他們箭上相同的毒藥；坑口用血拌過的泥土和草佈置好，再把那塊帶骨的肉放在後頭。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. One morning they found the leopard stuck fast in one of the sharp stakes, dead as a stone... They took off their karosses and laid their bows and arrow-bags on the ground, took the leopard by the tail and hind legs and dragged him out. That was too much for the male who lay there near by: he sprang up, scalped one of them with his sharp claws so that the skin of his head came off almost whole, bit another dead; and the other two fled each into a tree and sat there safe but defenceless the whole day, while the leopard ate the corpse.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 98; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同段落的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。一天早晨，他們發現那隻豹緊緊卡在一根尖樁上，僵死如石……他們脫下皮斗篷，把弓和箭袋放在地上，抓住豹的尾巴和後腿，把牠拖了出來。這對躺在近旁的那隻雄豹來說太過分了：牠一躍而起，用利爪把其中一人的頭皮剝下，使那人的頭皮幾乎整片脫落，又咬死了另一人；其餘兩人各自逃上一棵樹，整天坐在那裡，安全卻手無寸鐵，而豹則吃著那具屍體。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. In the afternoon their people came to seek them; the two best shots crept near while the leopard kept looking at the place whence he had heard the voices; the two sprang each into a tree near the others, and they teased the leopard out from tree to tree till he came to where he got his death-shot. So the leopard kept them all day for master.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 98; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同段落的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。下午，他們的族人前來尋找他們；兩名最好的射手悄悄靠近，而豹一直盯著牠聽見人聲傳來的方向；那兩人各自跳上鄰近的樹，他們把豹從一棵樹引到另一棵樹，直到牠來到被射死的地方。於是豹整整一天都把他們當作主人般困住。

title.en: The Flute-Reed and the Singing Lion Cubs
title.zh: 笛蘆與唱歌之獅子

region.en: Roggeveld, Northern Cape (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南非北開普省羅格費爾德（象徵定位）

period: San oral tradition; told to G. R. von Wielligh by Ou Bles, published 1922; the second tale told by J. M. Orpen (Cape Monthly Magazine, July 1874)

source.work: G. R. von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories, Deel IV (1922), No. 99

summary.en: An old sorcerer guards the good flute-reed; a son who takes his own arrows instead of the burning one is bitten dead, and the lion's cubs leap over the corpse singing 'He steals our flute-reed... his father knows nothing!' The father comes with the fire-arrow; the whole burning family flees. In Orpen's Maluti version 'Kaggen's son Cogaz is hung on a tree by the baboons, who sing 'Cagn thinks he is clever'; 'Kaggen, roused by his dolosse, punctures every dancer's back with sharp skewers and drives them to the mountains as baboons — then revives his son.
summary.zh: 老巫守良笛蘆；自帶己箭而不攜火箭之子被咬斃；獅子群跳屍而歌「他偷我們的笛蘆……其父毫不知情！」父攜火箭至；焚身之獅族盡逃。奧彭之馬盧蒂版：螳螂之子科加茲遭狒狒吊於樹，唱「卡恩自以為聰明」；螳螂以算籌占得噩耗，以尖籤刺眾舞者之背，逐之為狒狒——復活其子。

sensitivity.note: San oral tradition recorded in Afrikaans by G. R. von Wielligh and in English by J. M. Orpen (1874); presented as an archival record. The Orpen 'Cagn' is 'Kaggen, the Mantis.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh Deel IV No. 99 (1922); not verbatim. An old Bushman of the old race once told his son to go and fetch flute-reed to make arrows of, warning him against an old sorcerer who guarded that reed so that the old folk could not make such good arrows; and he gave the son a certain arrow with which to shoot the sorcerer, an arrow that would burn him so that he could do nothing. But the son was headstrong: he took his own arrows and left the burning arrow at home.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 99; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 馮·維利希（von Wielligh）第四卷第九十九號（1922年）的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。一位舊族的年老布須曼人曾吩咐兒子去採蘆笛蘆葦來造箭，並警告他提防一位看守那種蘆葦的老巫師，正因如此，舊時的人們才造不出那麼好的箭；他又交給兒子一支特定的箭，用來射那巫師，那箭會把巫師燒得什麼也做不成。但兒子固執任性：他帶上自己的箭，把那支燃燒之箭留在了家裡。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. When the son came where the good flute-reed grew he began at once to cut. The old sorcerer changed himself and his family into lions, and asked the son what he did there. 'Why did you not first ask me?' said the lion. 'I did not see you,' answered the son. Then the lion bit the son dead. The lion's three children sprang to and fro over the corpse and sang: 'He steals our flute-reed, He steals our flute-reed, To make arrows. Our father has beaten him, Our father has beaten him; His father knows nothing!'
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 99; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同段落的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。兒子來到生長上等蘆笛蘆葦的地方，立刻動手割取。老巫師把自己和家人變成獅子，問兒子在那裡做什麼。「你為什麼不先問我一聲？」獅子說。「我沒看見你。」兒子回答。於是獅子把兒子咬死了。獅子的三個孩子繞著屍體跳來跳去，唱道：「他偷我們的蘆笛蘆葦，他偷我們的蘆笛蘆葦，拿去造箭。我們的父親打敗了他，我們的父親打敗了他；他的父親什麼也不知道！」

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. When the son stayed away too long the father said to his wife: 'Our son is dead; I can see it in my dolosse, and I must go and look.' He found the burning arrow in the hut and went to where his son lay dead. 'Now indeed I shall also bite you dead,' said the lion; but the father shot him with the fire-arrow, the bodies of the whole family caught fire, and they all fled. In Orpen's Maluti story 'Kaggen sent his eldest son Cogaz to cut sticks for bows; the baboons hung him on the top of a tree, dancing round it and singing 'Cagn thinks he is clever'; 'Kaggen, woken by his dolosse hung over his nose, went and made every dancer stoop while he drove a sharp skewer into each one's back, chased them to the mountains to live on roots, insects and scorpions as a punishment — baboons had then no tails — and took Cogaz down and revived him.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 99, and J. M. Orpen, Cape Monthly Magazine (July 1874); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同段落的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。兒子久久不歸，父親便對妻子說：「我們的兒子死了；我從我的占卜骨中看得出來，我必須去看看。」他在茅屋裡找到那支燃燒之箭，便前往兒子陳屍之處。「這回我也要把你咬死。」獅子說；但父親用火箭射牠，獅子全家的身體都著了火，牠們全都逃走了。在奧爾彭（Orpen）的馬盧蒂故事中：「卡根（Kaggen）派他的長子科加茲（Cogaz）去砍造弓的木棍；狒狒們把他吊在一棵樹頂上，繞著樹跳舞唱歌：『卡根自以為聰明』；『卡根被他掛在鼻前的占卜骨弄醒，前去讓每個跳舞者彎下腰，把一根尖木籤刺進牠們每個人的背，把牠們趕到山裡，罰牠們以根莖、昆蟲和蠍子為食——那時狒狒還沒有尾巴——然後把科加茲放下來，使他甦醒。」

title.en: Out of the Crocodile's Mouth
title.zh: 脫鱷口而生還

region.en: Highveld, Transvaal (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南非德蘭士瓦高原（象徵定位）

period: San oral tradition; told to G. R. von Wielligh on the Highveld in 1883, published 1922

source.work: G. R. von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories, Deel IV (1922), No. 100

summary.en: A lame Bushman herder, proud that his dung-fire chimney burns like wood, tells how a crocodile dragged him under at a hippo-hole — 'if a white man and a Bushman walk through water, the crocodile never takes the white man, but the Bushman' — how he lay dead-still in the den under the bank, got a test-bite on his leg, and squeezed himself skinny through a crack of light to freedom.
summary.zh: 跛足桑牧自豪其糞火煙囪燃如柴火，述其於河馬池遭鱷曳入水底——「白人與桑人同涉水，鱷永不取白人，唯取桑人」——他在岸下穴中僵臥如屍，被試咬其腿，最後自一線之光縫中瘦身擠出而脫。

sensitivity.note: San oral tradition recorded in Afrikaans by G. R. von Wielligh; presented as an archival record.

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh Deel IV No. 100 (1922); not verbatim. 'Baas, I can see you white people and here my mate do not yet understand how to make fire with dung-balls; let me show you.' He packed the dung-balls round the fire like a chimney of eighteen inches high, and a flame leapt up in that chimney as if it were a wood fire... He pointed out the place on his leg below the knee and told his story.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 100; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 馮·維利希（von Wielligh）第四卷第一百號（1922年）的濃縮改述，非逐字照錄。「老闆，我看得見你們白人，而我的同伴在這裡還不懂怎麼用糞球生火；讓我示範給你們看。」他把糞球圍著火堆堆起來，像一座十八英寸高的煙囪，一道火焰在那煙囪裡竄起，就像木柴火一樣……他指著自己膝蓋下方腿上的那處地方，講述了他的故事。

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. 'My work was to look after the oxen. In the stream where our standing place was there were big hippo-holes; but we did not really see crocodiles there... The blood of the game that my master's people shot, and the blood-smeared things that were continually washed in the stream, lured the crocodile. One day the little baas and I walked through the shallow water; just as we were half over, a crocodile got me by the leg under my knee and dragged me into the hippo-hole... If a white man and a Bushman walk through water, the crocodile never takes the white man, but the Bushman.'
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 100; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同處摘要改述，非逐字引用。「我的工作是看牛。我們駐地所在的那條溪裡有許多大河馬洞；不過我們其實沒在那裡見到鱷魚……我主人的人所獵得的獵物之血，以及那些不斷在溪裡沖洗的沾血之物，引來了鱷魚。有一天，小老闆和我涉過淺水；就在我們走到一半時，一隻鱷魚咬住我膝下的腿，把我拖進河馬洞裡……若是白人和布須曼人一同涉水，鱷魚從不抓白人，只抓布須曼人。」

passages.text: Condensed paraphrase, same locus; not verbatim. 'The crocodile thought I was dead, for I played dead-still as he dragged me into the hole under the bank; every time he came to peep whether I still lay quiet... When my eyes had grown used to the dark and I came right, I saw a ray of light shining down through a crack; I crept softly higher and saw it was only a big crack... Just as I was ready to spring out above, the crocodile came again to peep and gave me just a sore bite on the leg — I believe to test whether I was really dead. I lay so still and breathed softly; then I took my chance and squeezed through the narrow crack, holding myself thin — and above I was out! and ran quickly away on my sore leg, clean away from his body.'
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of von Wielligh, Boesman-Stories Deel IV (1922), No. 100; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 同處摘要改述，非逐字引用。「鱷魚以為我死了，因為當牠把我拖進岸下的洞裡時，我裝得一動也不動；牠每次過來窺看是否還躺著不動……等我的眼睛習慣了黑暗、回過神來，我看見一道光從裂縫透下來；我輕輕往高處爬，發現那只是一道大裂縫……就在我準備從上方竄出去時，鱷魚又來窺看，狠狠咬了我腿上一口——我相信牠是在試我是否真的死了。我躺得一動也不動，輕輕呼吸；然後我抓住機會，把自己縮得細細的，從狹窄的裂縫擠了出去——到了上面，我出來了！我拖著受傷的腿快快跑開，徹底逃離了牠的身子。」

title.en: The Primary Clear Light at the Moment of Death
title.zh: 臨終一瞬之根本明光

region.en: Deathbed of the dying one, anywhere in Tibet (symbolic pin at the Chikhai bardo, symbolic)
region.zh: 亡者臨終之榻（以「臨終中陰」為象徵定位）

period: Bardo Thodol (Bar-do thos-grol, terma attributed to Padmasambhava, revealed as 'Liberation by Hearing on the After-Death Plane'); English translation by Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. W. Y. Evans-Wentz, 1927

source.work: The Tibetan Book of the Dead, trans. Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. W. Y. Evans-Wentz (Oxford University Press, 1927), Part I, Book I

license: Public domain (English translation published 1927; US public domain since 2023)

summary.en: At the very instant the breath ceases, the dying one is set face to face with the Primary Clear Light: all things like the void and cloudless sky, the naked spotless intellect like a transparent vacuum without circumference or centre. The lama names the symptoms of death one by one - earth sinking into water, water into fire, fire into air - enforces the resolve to win Buddhahood for all beings, presses the arteries and turns the body to the lion's posture so the vital-force passes out through the Brahmanic aperture, and repeats the address until a yellowish liquid appears at the apertures; the ordinary man endures the swoon but three and a half days, the yogi but a finger-snap.
summary.zh: 氣息將絕之際，上師令亡者直面「根本明光」：萬象如晴空無雲，赤裸無垢之心如無邊無際之澄空。上師逐一生宣死相——地入水、水入火、火入風——促其發願為一切眾生成佛，按住喉側動脈、作獅子臥，令命力自梵穴而出；反覆誦示，直至體竅滲出黃液。常人昏沉三日半，瑜伽行者僅一彈指。

canonical_translation: Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, English translation; ed. W. Y. Evans-Wentz, The Tibetan Book of the Dead, Oxford 1927 (public domain)

narrative.en:
It is best if the guru from whom the deceased received guiding instructions can be had; but if the guru cannot be obtained, then a brother of the Faith; or if the latter is also unobtainable, then a learned man of the same Faith; or, should all these be unobtainable, then a person who can read correctly and distinctly ought to read this many times over. Thereby the deceased will be put in mind of what he had previously heard of the setting-face-to-face and will at once come to recognize that Fundamental Light and undoubtedly obtain Liberation.

When the breathing is about to cease, it is best if the Transference hath been applied efficiently; if the application hath been inefficient, then address the deceased thus: 'O nobly-born, the time hath now come for thee to seek the Path in reality. Thy breathing is about to cease. Thy guru hath set thee face to face before with the Clear Light; and now thou art about to experience it in its Reality in the Bardo state, wherein all things are like the void and cloudless sky, and the naked, spotless intellect is like unto a transparent vacuum without circumference or centre. At this moment, know thou thyself; and abide in that state.' Having read this, repeat it many times in the ear of the person dying, even before the expiration hath ceased, so as to impress it on the mind of the dying one.

If the expiration is about to cease, turn the dying one over on the right side, which posture is called the Lying Posture of a Lion; the throbbing of the arteries on the right and left side of the throat is to be pressed. If the person dying be disposed to sleep, or if the deep sleep state advances, that should be arrested, and the arteries pressed gently but firmly, whereby the vital-force will not be able to return from the median-nerve and will be sure to pass out through the Brahmanic aperture. At this moment the first glimpsing of the Bardo of the Clear Light of Reality, which is the Infallible Mind of the Dharma-Kaya, is experienced by all sentient beings. The interval between the cessation of the expiration and the cessation of the inspiration is the time during which the vital-force remaineth in the median-nerve. The common people call this the state wherein the consciousness-principle hath fainted away; the duration is uncertain, depending upon constitution, good or bad, and the state of the nerves and vital-force.

In the setting-face-to-face the repetition is to be persisted in until a yellowish liquid beginneth to appear from the various apertures of the bodily organs. In those who have led an evil life and in those of unsound nerves the state endureth only so long as would take to snap a finger; in some it endureth as long as the time taken for the eating of a meal; various treatises say the swoon endureth about three and one-half days, most others for four, during all which time the setting-face-to-face with the Clear Light ought to be persevered in. The symptoms are named as they come: now the symptoms of earth sinking into water are come. When all the symptoms of death are about to be completed, the dying one is enjoined with the great resolution: by taking advantage of this death, I will so act, for the good of all sentient beings peopling the illimitable expanse of the heavens, as to obtain Perfect Buddhahood, by resolving on love and compassion and by directing my entire effort to the Sole Perfection - and even if I cannot realize it, I will serve all sentient beings, infinite in number as are the limits of the sky.
narrative.notes: Cultural function: the instruction is read aloud to the dying and, in hope, to the dead; a copy of the text - or strips of paper wound into a roll - is often tied to the corpse and burned or buried with it, as a Book of the Dead was entombed with a mummy.

functions: Liturgical technique of conscious dying: the text is read aloud, not studied silently, to a corpse or a dying person
Physiological doctrine of the death process as a reverse of the birth process, with the vital-force and median nerve mapped
Establishes the Great Perpendicular Path - instantaneous Buddhahood without further wandering - for the trained
Makes every funeral a re-enactment of the guru's teaching: whoever reads becomes the voice of the lineage

variants.name: The Ars Moriendi parallels
variants.text_tradition: European fifteenth-century death-manuals (Comper's edition, cited by Evans-Wentz)
variants.summary: Evans-Wentz compares the Tibetan reading-to-the-dying with the Christian Ars Moriendi, in which friends say prayers 'with a loud voice' before the dying - a structural parallel of both traditions' conviction that the dying moment decides the soul's fate.

variants.name: The Great Perfection (rDzogs-chen) recension
variants.summary: Those who have meditated on the Great Perfection and the Great Symbol recognize the Clear Light at the moment of death without the book being read; for all others the reading is indispensable.

primary_sources.citation: Tibetan text; English trans. Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. W. Y. Evans-Wentz, The Tibetan Book of the Dead, London: Oxford University Press, 1927, pp. 89-97

secondary_sources.work: W. Y. Evans-Wentz, The Tibetan Book of the Dead, with psychological commentary by C. G. Jung

sensitivity_guidance: The Bardo Thodol remains a living liturgy read at Tibetan deathbeds and funerals to this day; passages below are paraphrases of the 1927 public-domain translation, never verbatim ritual text, and are given for study only.

sensitivity.note: Living liturgical tradition; paraphrase of public-domain 1927 translation only, for study, not ritual use.

passages.text: O nobly-born, the time hath now come for thee to seek the Path in reality. Thy breathing is about to cease. Thy guru hath set thee face to face before with the Clear Light; and now thou art about to experience it in its Reality in the Bardo state, wherein all things are like the void and cloudless sky, and the naked, spotless intellect is like unto a transparent vacuum without circumference or centre. At this moment, know thou thyself; and abide in that state.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation, The Tibetan Book of the Dead (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 善男子，如今尋求實相之道之時已至。你的氣息即將斷絕。你的上師曾使你面見淨光；如今你將在中有境界中親證其真實本性，於此一切事物皆如虛空無雲之天，而赤裸無瑕之覺性猶如透明虛空，無邊際亦無中心。此刻，當自識自性；並安住於彼境界中。

passages.text: If the expiration is about to cease, turn the dying one over on the right side, the Lying Posture of a Lion; the throbbing of the arteries on the right and left side of the throat is to be pressed gently but firmly, whereby the vital-force will not be able to return from the median-nerve and will be sure to pass out through the Brahmanic aperture. At this moment the first glimpsing of the Bardo of the Clear Light of Reality, the Infallible Mind of the Dharma-Kaya, is experienced by all sentient beings.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 若呼氣即將斷絕，當將臨終者翻轉為右側臥，即獅子臥姿；喉部左右兩側動脈之搏動，當輕而穩地按壓，如此命力便無法從中脈回流，必能從梵穴而出。此刻，一切有情眾生皆體驗到實相淨光中有之初現，亦即法身無謬之心。

passages.text: The repetition of the address is to be persisted in until a yellowish liquid beginneth to appear from the apertures of the bodily organs; in those who have led an evil life, and in those of unsound nerves, the state endureth only so long as would take to snap a finger, and in some as long as the eating of a meal. When all the symptoms of death are about to be completed, the dying one is enjoined: by taking advantage of this death, I will so act, for the good of all sentient beings peopling the illimitable expanse of the heavens, as to obtain Perfect Buddhahood, by resolving on love and compassion - and even if I cannot realize it, I will serve all sentient beings, infinite in number as are the limits of the sky.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當持續反覆念誦此開示，直至身體諸根門開始流出黃色液體為止；對於曾造惡業者，以及神經不健全者，此境界僅持續如彈指之久，有些人則長如進一餐飯之久。當一切死亡徵象即將圓滿時，當囑咐臨終者：藉此死亡之機，我願為遍滿無邊天際之一切有情眾生之利益而行，發起慈心與悲心，誓願證得圓滿佛果——即使我不能證得，我也願服務一切有情眾生，其數無量如虛空之邊際。

title.en: The Secondary Clear Light and the Question 'Am I Dead?'
title.zh: 第二明光與「我死了嗎？」

region.en: Death-room of the deceased, Tibet (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 亡者停靈之室（象徵定位）

period: Bardo Thodol; English translation 1927

source.work: The Tibetan Book of the Dead, trans. Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. Evans-Wentz (1927), Book I

summary.en: If the Primary Clear Light is not recognized, the Secondary Clear Light dawns somewhat more than a meal-time period after the expiration has ceased; according to one's good or bad karma the vital-force flows down the right or left nerve and goes out through any of the apertures, and there comes a lucid condition of the mind. The consciousness-principle, getting outside the body, asks itself: Am I dead, or am I not dead? It cannot determine; it sees its relatives as it had been used to seeing them, and even hears the wailings - the terrifying karmic illusions have not yet dawned.
summary.zh: 若未識根本明光，則呼氣絕後約一頓飯時，第二明光顯現；依善惡業力，命力經左右脈從諸竅而出，心得清明。神識出體，自問：「我死了嗎？還沒死嗎？」無法自決；它如生前般看見親眷，甚至聽見哭聲——而可怕的業力幻象尚未現前。

sensitivity.note: Living liturgical tradition; paraphrase of public-domain 1927 translation only.

passages.text: If it be feared that the primary Clear Light hath not been recognized, then there is dawning upon the deceased that called the Secondary Clear Light, which dawneth in somewhat more than a meal-time period after that the expiration hath ceased. According to one's good or bad karma, the vital-force floweth down into either the right or left nerve and goeth out through any of the apertures of the body; then cometh a lucid condition of the mind.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 若恐未能認出初次淨光，則亡者會有稱為二次淨光者現起，此淨光在呼氣斷絕後約略超過一餐飯的時間方才現起。隨其善業或惡業，命力流入右脈或左脈，並從身體任一孔竅而出；隨後便生起心之明淨狀態。

passages.text: When the consciousness-principle getteth outside the body, it sayeth to itself: Am I dead, or am I not dead? It cannot determine. It seeth its relatives and connexions as it had been used to seeing them before; it even heareth the wailings. The terrifying karmic illusions have not yet dawned, nor have the frightful apparitions or experiences caused by the Lords of Death yet come.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當識性離體而去時，它會自問：我死了嗎，還是沒死？它無法斷定。它看見自己的親屬與眷屬，一如往昔慣常所見；它甚至聽見哀哭之聲。可怖的業力幻象尚未現起，死神所引發的駭人景象與經歷也還未到來。

title.en: The Six Bardos and the Secret of Recognition
title.zh: 六中陰與認識之祕

region.en: The Chonyid Bardo of the departed (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 亡者之「實相中陰」（象徵定位）

period: Bardo Thodol; English translation 1927

source.work: The Tibetan Book of the Dead, trans. Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. Evans-Wentz (1927), Book I

summary.en: Now that death has come to all, the departed is told not to cling; the six bardos are enumerated - the womb-bardo, the dream-bardo, the bardo of ecstatic equilibrium, the bardo of the moment of death, the bardo of Reality, and the bardo of the inverse process of sangsaric existence - and the key verses are recited: 'may I recognize whatever visions appear as the reflex of mine own consciousness... may I know the apparitions to be of the nature of apparitions; and, at this all-important moment of opportunity, may I know the emanations of the Peaceful and Wrathful Deities to be mine own thought-forms.' The body now is the thought-body of propensities: sounds, lights and rays cannot harm it, for it is incapable of dying.
summary.zh: 既死之人當知：死亡人皆有之，毋須戀棧。六中陰依次列舉——胎中、夢境、禪定、臨終、實相、受生——並誦關鍵偈：「願我認得一切顯現皆自心之影……願我知其幻化本性；於此大事因緣之際，願我知寂忿諸尊皆是自身心念之化現。」今之身乃「習氣意生身」，聲光影三相皆不能傷，以其本不能死。

sensitivity.note: Living liturgical tradition; paraphrase of public-domain 1927 translation only.

passages.text: O nobly-born, that which is called death hath now come. Thou art departing from this world, but thou art not the only one; death cometh to all. Do not cling, in fondness and weakness, to this life. Even though thou clingest out of weakness, thou hast not the power to remain here; thou wilt gain nothing more than wandering in this Sangsara. Be not attached; be not weak. Remember the Precious Trinity.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 善男子，所謂死亡如今已至。你正離開此世，但並非只有你一人；死亡臨於一切眾生。不要以貪戀與怯弱執著於此生。縱使你因怯弱而執著，你也無力留在此處；你所得的不過是在生死輪迴中漂泊。莫要貪著；莫要怯弱。當憶念三寶。

passages.text: There are six states of Bardo, namely: the natural state of Bardo while in the womb; the Bardo of the dream-state; the Bardo of ecstatic equilibrium while in deep meditation; the Bardo of the moment of death; the Bardo during the experiencing of Reality; and the Bardo of the inverse process of sangsaric existence - these are the six.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 中有共有六種狀態，即：處胎時中有之自然狀態；夢境中有；深定中狂喜平衡之中有；死時中有；體驗實相時之中有；以及生死存在逆轉過程之中有——此即六種。

passages.text: When thy body and mind were separating, thou must have experienced a glimpse of the Pure Truth, subtle, sparkling, bright, dazzling, glorious, and radiantly awesome, in appearance like a mirage moving across a landscape in spring-time; be not daunted thereby, nor terrified, nor awed - that is the radiance of thine own true nature. From the midst of that radiance the natural sound of Reality, reverberating like a thousand thunders simultaneously sounding, will come; that is the natural sound of thine own real self. The body which thou hast now is called the thought-body of propensities; since thou hast not a material body of flesh and blood, whatever may come - sounds, lights or rays - are, all three, unable to harm thee; thou art incapable of dying. It is quite sufficient for thee to know that these apparitions are thine own thought-forms.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當你的身心分離之時，你必定曾瞥見清淨真諦，微妙、閃耀、明亮、眩目、輝煌，且光明莊嚴可畏，其狀如春日原野上流動的陽焰；不要因此驚懼，不要害怕，也不要畏怯——那正是你自己真實本性的光明。從那光明之中，實相的自然之聲將響起，如千雷同時轟鳴；那正是你自己真實本我的自然之聲。你現在所有的身體稱為習氣之意生身；既然你沒有血肉之質的肉身，那麼無論出現什麼——聲音、光明或光芒——三者皆無法傷害你；你是不可能死的。你只需知道這些景象是你自心的念相，便已足夠。

title.en: The First Day: Vairochana and the Two Lights
title.zh: 中陰第一日：毗盧遮那與二光

region.en: The Central Realm, the Spreading Forth of the Seed (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 中央密聚佛國（象徵定位）

period: Bardo Thodol; English translation 1927

source.work: The Tibetan Book of the Dead, trans. Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. Evans-Wentz (1927), Book I

summary.en: Recovering from the three-and-a-half-day swoon, the departed sees the whole heavens deep blue; from the Central Realm called the Spreading Forth of the Seed the Bhagavan Vairochana, white, seated on a lion-throne, bearing an eight-spoked wheel, embraced by the Mother of the Space of Heaven, manifests. The blue light of the Wisdom of the Dharma-dhatu shoots forth from his heart - and beside it a dull white light from the devas: through the power of evil karma the glory produces fear and the dull light fondness, and the prayer is recited to be led by Vairochana across the fearful ambush of the Bardo into the state of All-Perfect Buddhahood in the Central Realm of the Densely-Packed.
summary.zh: 三日半昏沉初醒，所見長空盡作深藍；中央「遍佈種子」佛土，毗盧遮那白身獅座、手持八輻輪、與虛空佛母相擁而現。法界體性智之青光自其心間射出，耀不可視；同時一道灰白之光自天道而來。以惡業力故，青光反生怖畏，灰光反生貪戀——故誦祈請文，願毗盧遮那引度，越中陰險隘，譤於「密聚」中央佛國。

sensitivity.note: Living liturgical tradition; paraphrase of public-domain 1927 translation only.

passages.text: As soon as thou art recovered from this swoon, thou wilt have the thought, what hath happened! Act so that thou wilt recognize the Bardo. At that time all the Sangsara will be in revolution, and the phenomenal appearances that thou wilt see then will be the radiances and deities; the whole heavens will appear deep blue. Then, from the Central Realm, called the Spreading Forth of the Seed, the Bhagavan Vairochana, white in colour, seated upon a lion-throne, bearing an eight-spoked wheel in his hand, and embraced by the Mother of the Space of Heaven, will manifest himself to thee.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 你從這昏厥中甦醒過來，便會生起一念：發生了什麼事！你要讓自己認出這中有。其時整個生死輪迴都在轉動，你將看見的種種現象將是光明與諸尊；整個天空將顯現為深藍色。於是，從名為「種子廣布」的中央佛土，白色的大日如來世尊，坐於獅子座上，手持八輻法輪，為虛空界之母所擁抱，將向你顯現。

passages.text: The Wisdom of the Dharma-dhatu, blue in colour, shining, transparent, glorious, dazzling, from the heart of Vairochana as the Father-Mother will shoot forth and strike against thee with a light so radiant that thou wilt scarcely be able to look at it; and along with it there will also shine a dull white light from the devas. Because of the power of bad karma the glorious blue light will produce in thee fear and terror, and thou wilt wish to flee from it, and wilt beget a fondness for the dull white light of the devas - be not awed by the divine blue light, for that is the light of the Tathagata, and put thy whole thought earnestly upon Vairochana.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 法界智，色藍，明亮、透澈、輝煌、眩目，將從大日如來作為父母尊的心中射出，以極其燦爛的光向你照來，使你幾乎無法正視；與此同時，諸天所發的暗淡白光也將照耀。由於惡業之力，那輝煌的藍光將使你生起恐懼與驚怖，你會想要逃離它，並對諸天的暗淡白光生起喜愛——不要畏懼那神聖的藍光，因為那是如來之光，當一心至誠專注於大日如來。

title.en: The Second Day: Vajra-Sattva and the Smoke of Hell
title.zh: 中陰第二日：金剛薩埵與獄火之煙

region.en: The Eastern Realm of Pre-eminent Happiness (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 東方喜吉祥佛國（象徵定位）

period: Bardo Thodol; English translation 1927

source.work: The Tibetan Book of the Dead, trans. Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. Evans-Wentz (1927), Book I

summary.en: On the Second Day the pure form of water shines as a white light; from the Eastern Realm of Pre-eminent Happiness the Bhagavan Akshobhya as Vajra-Sattva, blue, holding a five-pronged vajra, on an elephant-throne, embraced by the Mother Mamaki, appears attended by the Bodhisattvas Kshitigarbha and Maitreya with the female Bodhisattvas Lasya and Puspa. The Mirror-like Wisdom shines as a bright radiant white light from the heart of Vajra-Sattva the Father-Mother - and a dull smoke-coloured light from Hell shines alongside: if the departed is attracted by it, he falls into the Hell-Worlds, whence there is no certain time of getting out.
summary.zh: 第二日，水大淨相現為白光；東方喜吉祥佛土，阿閦佛現金剛薩埵相——藍身、持五股杵、象座、與佛眼佛母（Mamaki）相擁，地藏與彌勒二菩薩及金剛鬘、蓮花二明妃隨侍。大圓鏡智之皎白光明自其心間射出——而地獄之暗煙色光並現：若貪之，即墮地獄，出期無定。

sensitivity.note: Living liturgical tradition; paraphrase of public-domain 1927 translation only.

passages.text: On the Second Day the pure form of water will shine as a white light; at that time, from the deep blue Eastern Realm of Pre-eminent Happiness, the Bhagavan Akshobhya as Vajra-Sattva, blue in colour, holding in his hand a five-pronged vajra, seated upon an elephant-throne, and embraced by the Mother Mamaki, will appear to thee, attended by the Bodhisattvas Kshitigarbha and Maitreya with the female Bodhisattvas Lasya and Puspa.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第二日，水的清淨形相將化現為白光；其時，從深藍色的東方「最勝喜樂」淨土，薄伽梵不動如來以金剛薩埵之相，身色深藍，手持五股金剛杵，坐於象座之上，為瑪瑪姬佛母所擁抱，將現於汝前，並有地藏菩薩與彌勒菩薩，以及拉西雅與普斯帕兩位女菩薩隨侍。

passages.text: The aggregate of thy principle of consciousness, being in its pure form - which is the Mirror-like Wisdom - will shine as a bright, radiant white light from the heart of Vajra-Sattva the Father-Mother, with such dazzling brilliancy that thou wilt scarcely be able to look at it; and a dull, smoke-coloured light from Hell will shine alongside. Through the power of anger thou wilt be startled at the dazzling white light and beget a fondness for the dull smoke-coloured light from Hell: if thou be attracted by it, thou wilt fall into the Hell-Worlds and endure unbearable misery, whence there is no certain time of getting out.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 汝意識原理之蘊，其清淨形相——即大圓鏡智——將從金剛薩埵父母之心間，化現為明亮燦爛之白光，其光耀之烈，汝幾乎不能正視；同時，地獄之昏暗煙色光亦將並現。因瞋怒之力，汝將為此耀眼白光所驚懼，而對地獄之昏暗煙色光生起喜愛：若汝為其所吸引，便將墮入地獄諸界，承受難忍之苦，且無一定出離之時。

title.en: The Third Day: Ratna-Sambhava and the Light of Equality
title.zh: 中陰第三日：寶生佛與平等性智

region.en: The Southern Realm Endowed with Glory (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 南方吉祥佛國（象徵定位）

period: Bardo Thodol; English translation 1927

source.work: The Tibetan Book of the Dead, trans. Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. Evans-Wentz (1927), Book I

summary.en: On the Third Day the primal form of the element earth shines as a yellow light; from the Southern Realm Endowed with Glory the Bhagavan Ratna-Sambhava, yellow, bearing a jewel, seated on a horse-throne and embraced by the Divine Mother Sangya-Chanmat, shines upon the departed, attended by Akasha-Garbha and Samanta-Bhadra with Mahiama and Dhupema. The Wisdom of Equality, dazzlingly yellow with satellite orbs of radiance, strikes against the departed - and beside it the dull bluish-yellow light of the human world path, of miserliness and greed.
summary.zh: 第三日，地大淨相現為黃光；南方吉祥佛土，寶生佛黃身持寶、馬座、與聖母相擁，虛空藏與普賢二菩薩及二明妃隨侍。平等性智之明黃光，帶光暈圍繞，射向亡者——旁有灰黃之倖光，即慳吝貪欲所致人道之光。

sensitivity.note: Living liturgical tradition; paraphrase of public-domain 1927 translation only.

passages.text: On the Third Day the primal form of the element earth will shine forth as a yellow light; at that time, from the Southern Realm Endowed with Glory, the Bhagavan Ratna-Sambhava, yellow in colour, bearing a jewel in his hand, seated upon a horse-throne and embraced by the Divine Mother, will shine upon thee, attended by the Bodhisattvas Akasha-Garbha and Samanta-Bhadra with the two female Bodhisattvas, all in Buddha-form, coming to shine from amidst a rainbow halo of light.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第三日，地大之根本形相將化現為黃光；其時，從南方「具榮耀」淨土，薄伽梵寶生如來，身色金黃，手持摩尼寶，坐於馬座之上，為佛母所擁抱，將照耀於汝前，並有空藏菩薩與普賢菩薩，以及兩位女菩薩隨侍，皆現佛陀之相，從彩虹光環之中前來照耀。

passages.text: The aggregate of touch in its primal form, as the yellow light of the Wisdom of Equality, dazzlingly yellow, glorified with orbs having satellite orbs of radiance, so clear and bright that the eye can scarcely look upon it, will strike against thee - and side by side with it the dull yellow light of the human world, the path of miserliness and greed, will shine.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 觸蘊之根本形相，即平等性智之黃光，耀眼金黃，以具有衛星般光暈之光球而莊嚴，其清澈明亮，幾非目所能視，將向汝迎面而來——與此同時，人間之昏暗黃光，即慳吝與貪欲之道，亦將並現。

title.en: The Blood-Drinking Herukas: The Wrathful Days
title.zh: 飲血赫魯迦：忿怒七日

region.en: The Chonyid Bardo, quarters of the departed's brain (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 實相中陰腦宮四方（象徵定位）

period: Bardo Thodol (Bar-do thos-grol, terma attributed to Padmasambhava); English translation by Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. Evans-Wentz, 1927

source.work: The Tibetan Book of the Dead, trans. Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. W. Y. Evans-Wentz (Oxford University Press, 1927), Part I, Book I: the eighth to fourteenth days

license: Public domain (English translation published 1927; US public domain since 2023)

summary.en: On the eighth to fourteenth days the fifty-eight flame-enhaloed, wrathful, blood-drinking deities dawn - only the former Peaceful Deities in changed aspect, issuing from the quarters of the departed's own brain. The Great Glorious Buddha-Heruka, dark-brown, with three faces, six hands and four feet, nine eyes in terrifying gaze, eyebrows quivering like lightning, hair of reddish-yellow standing on end, garlanded with black serpents and raw human heads, holding wheel, sword and battle-axe, bell, skull-bowl and ploughshare, embraced by the Mother Buddha-Krotishaurima who puts to his mouth a red shell filled with blood, comes forth from the departed's own brain - fear it not, for in reality it is the Bhagavan Vairochana the Father-Mother. Recognition is more difficult, but the intellect, undistractedly alert in one-pointedness under terror, is readier to be liberated - and the least of tantrika devotees will greet the blood-drinkers as tutelary deities, like human acquaintances.
summary.zh: 第八至十四日，五十八尊焰鬘熾燃、忿怒飲血之尊次第現前——彼即前七日寂靜諸尊之變相，自亡者腦宮四方而出。大悲赫魯迦深棕色，三面六臂四足，九目怒視，眉如電顫，赤黃髮豎，頸飾黑蛇與新剝人首為鬘，右手持輪、劍、斧，左手持鈴、顱器、犁鏵，佛母克羅提沙烏利瑪擁之，以盈血赤螺就其口——勿懼！其實即毗盧遮那父母雙運。此期怖畏更甚，然心因懼而專一，反易得度；最下之密乘行者亦能認彼為本尊，如遇故人。

canonical_translation: Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, English translation; ed. W. Y. Evans-Wentz, The Tibetan Book of the Dead, Oxford 1927 (public domain)

narrative.en:
In the Bardo of the Peaceful Deities there were seven stages of ambuscade, and multitudes obtain liberation by recognition at one or another stage; but the number of sentient beings being great, evil karma powerful, obscurations dense, and propensities of too long standing, the Wheel of Ignorance and Illusion becometh neither exhausted nor accelerated, and there is a vast preponderance of those who wander downwards unliberated. Therefore, after the cessation of the dawning of the Peaceful and the Knowledge-Holding Deities, who come to welcome one, the fifty-eight flame-enhaloed, wrathful, blood-drinking deities come to dawn, who are only the former Peaceful Deities in changed aspect - according to the place of the thought-body of the deceased whence they proceed; nevertheless they will not resemble them.

This is the Bardo of the Wrathful Deities; and they being influenced by fear, terror and awe, recognition becometh more difficult; the intellect, gaining not in independence, passeth from one fainting state to a round of fainting states. Yet if one but recognize a little it is easier to be liberated at this stage - because of the dawning of the radiances, which produce fear, terror and awe, the intellect is undistractedly alert in one-pointedness. If at this stage one do not meet with this kind of teaching, one's hearing of religious lore, although it be like an ocean in its vastness, is of no avail; there are even discipline-holding abbots and doctors in metaphysical discourses who err at this stage, and, not recognizing, wander into the Sangsara. As for the common worldly folk, by fleeing through fear, terror and awe, they fall over the precipices into the unhappy worlds and suffer; but the least of the devotees of the mystic doctrines, as soon as he sees these blood-drinking deities, will recognize them to be his tutelary deities, and the meeting will be like that of human acquaintances - he will trust them, and becoming merged into them, in at-one-ment, will obtain Buddhahood.

O nobly-born, the Great Glorious Buddha-Heruka, dark-brown of colour, with three heads, six hands and four feet firmly postured; the right face being white, the left red, the central dark-brown; the body emitting flames of radiance; the nine eyes widely opened in terrifying gaze; the eyebrows quivering like lightning; the protruding teeth glistening and set over one another; giving vent to sonorous utterances of 'a-la-la' and 'ha-ha' and piercing whistling sounds; the hair of a reddish-yellow colour standing on end and emitting radiance; the heads adorned with dried human skulls and the symbols of the sun and moon; black serpents and raw human heads forming a garland for the body; the first of the right hands holding a wheel, the middle one a sword, the last one a battle-axe; the first of the left hands a bell, the middle one a skull-bowl, the last one a ploughshare; his body embraced by the Mother Buddha-Krotishaurima, her right hand clinging to his neck and her left putting to his mouth a red shell filled with blood - these two deities together will come forth from within thine own brain and shine vividly upon thee. Fear that not. Be not awed. Know it to be the embodiment of thine own intellect. As it is thine own tutelary deity, be not terrified; in reality it is the Bhagavan Vairochana, the Father-Mother. Simultaneously with the recognition, liberation will be obtained.

If one flee from them, then on the Ninth Day the blood-drinking deities of the Vajra Order named the Bhagavan Vajra-Heruka, dark-blue, issue from the eastern quarter of the brain; on the Tenth Day the blood-drinking deity of the Precious-Gem Order named Ratna-Heruka, yellow, issues from the southern quarter; on the Eleventh Day the blood-drinking deity of the Lotus Order, Padma-Heruka, reddish-black, from the western quarter - in reality the Father-Mother Bhagavan Amitabha; on the Twelfth Day the blood-drinking deity of the Karmic Order, Karma-Heruka, dark green, accompanied by the Kerima, Htamenaa and Wang-chugma, from the northern quarter - in reality the Father-Mother Bhagavan Amoghasiddhi. Each time the address repeats: fear not, be not terrified, be not awed, know them to be the embodiment of thine own intellect, and Buddhahood will be obtained by merging in them in at-one-ment.
narrative.notes: Cultural function: the wrathful sequence inverts ordinary terror into liberation - the most frightful forms are the closest to home, one's own brain and one's own tutelary deities - which is why the practitioner meditates on their images while alive. The blood symbolizes sangsaric existence; 'blood-drinking' the thirsting for, and quenching of, the thirst for existence.

functions: Inverts the terror of the death-visions into the path: the more frightful the apparition, the closer to one's own mind
Grounds iconographic practice: seeing the painted likenesses and images while alive secures recognition at death
Democratizes the liberation doctrine: the least of tantrika devotees meets the blood-drinkers like old acquaintances
Explains the funeral signs - rainbow-halo and bone-reliques - as the residue of esoteric recognition

variants.name: The 58 blood-drinking deities in the mandala paintings
variants.text_tradition: The Great Mandala of the Knowledge-Holding and Wrathful Deities (folio paintings reproduced in Evans-Wentz)
variants.summary: The painted mandalas show the united manifestation of the Wrathful Deities, the three-headed Herukas of the five orders at the cruciform design's centre, and the King and Judge of the Dead, Shinje, the wrathful aspect of Avalokiteshvara, weighing the dead.

variants.name: The Great Symbol (Mahamudra) schools
variants.summary: Devotees of the Great Symbol and the Great Perfection recognize the Clear Light at the moment of death and do not need the reading of the Thodol; they may obtain the Sambhoga-Kaya in the Chonyid Bardo or the Nirmana-Kaya in the Sidpa Bardo.

sensitivity_guidance: The wrathful deities are living liturgical images, painted and meditated in Tibetan monasteries; passages below are paraphrases of the 1927 public-domain translation for study, not for ritual use, and the tradition is treated respectfully.

sensitivity.note: Living liturgical tradition; paraphrase of public-domain 1927 translation only.

passages.text: After the cessation of the dawning of the Peaceful and the Knowledge-Holding Deities, the fifty-eight flame-enhaloed, wrathful, blood-drinking deities come to dawn, who are only the former Peaceful Deities in changed aspect; this is the Bardo of the Wrathful Deities, and they being influenced by fear, terror and awe, recognition becometh more difficult - yet if one but recognize a little, it is easier to be liberated at this stage, because the intellect is undistractedly alert in one-pointedness under terror.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 寂靜尊與持明尊顯現終止之後，五十八位為火焰所環繞之忿怒飲血尊前來顯現，彼等不過是先前寂靜尊之變相；此即忿怒尊之中陰，彼等因受恐懼、驚怖與敬畏所影響，辨認遂更為困難——然而，若能稍加辨認，於此階段反而更易解脫，蓋因神識在驚怖之下專注一境而無散亂。

passages.text: The Great Glorious Buddha-Heruka, dark-brown, with three heads, six hands and four feet firmly postured, the nine eyes widely opened in terrifying gaze, the eyebrows quivering like lightning, the hair of reddish-yellow standing on end, the heads adorned with dried human skulls and the symbols of the sun and moon, black serpents and raw human heads forming a garland for the body, his body embraced by the Mother Buddha-Krotishaurima, her right hand clinging to his neck and her left putting to his mouth a red shell filled with blood - these two deities together will come forth from within thine own brain and shine vividly upon thee: fear that not, know it to be the embodiment of thine own intellect; in reality it is the Bhagavan Vairochana, the Father-Mother.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 大威德佛陀嘿嚕嘎，身色深褐，三面六臂四足，姿態穩固，九目圓睜，目光可怖，眉如閃電顫動，紅黃色頭髮豎立，頭戴乾枯人頭骨與日月標誌為飾，黑蛇與生人頭顱結成瓔珞莊嚴其身，其身為佛陀克羅提沙烏利瑪佛母所擁抱，佛母右手攀其頸，左手將盛滿鮮血之紅色顱器送至其口——此二尊將從汝自身腦中湧現，鮮明照耀於汝前：勿懼，當知此即汝自身神識之體現；其實，彼即薄伽梵毗盧遮那如來父母。

passages.text: On the Ninth Day the blood-drinking Vajra-Heruka, dark-blue, issues from the eastern quarter of thy brain - in reality the Father-Mother Bhagavan Vajra-Sattva; on the Tenth Day Ratna-Heruka, yellow, from the southern quarter; on the Eleventh Day Padma-Heruka, reddish-black, from the western quarter - in reality the Father-Mother Bhagavan Amitabha; and on the Twelfth Day Karma-Heruka, dark green, from the northern quarter - in reality the Father-Mother Bhagavan Amoghasiddhi. Each time: fear not, be not terrified, be not awed, know them to be the embodiment of thine own intellect, and Buddhahood will be obtained by merging in them in at-one-ment.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第九日，飲血金剛嘿嚕嘎，深藍色，從汝腦之東方生起——實即父母尊金剛薩埵；第十日，寶生嘿嚕嘎，黃色，從南方生起；第十一日，蓮花嘿嚕嘎，紅黑色，從西方生起——實即父母尊阿彌陀佛；第十二日，業嘿嚕嘎，深綠色，從北方生起——實即父母尊不空成就佛。每一次皆當：勿懼，勿驚，勿畏，當知彼等即汝自心之化現，融入彼中與之合一，即得佛果。

title.en: Shinje, King and Judge of the Dead
title.zh: 閻魔王（辛傑）審判

region.en: Court of the Judge of the Dead in the Bardo (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 中陰閻羅法庭（象徵定位）

period: Bardo Thodol tradition (mandala text and iconography); English ed. Evans-Wentz 1927

source.work: The Tibetan Book of the Dead, ed. W. Y. Evans-Wentz (1927), Introduction, the Judgement Scene

summary.en: Shinje - the King and Judge of the Dead, the wrathful aspect of Avalokiteshvara, monkey-headed - presides over the weighing: on one side heaped-up black pebbles, the evil deeds, on the other white pebbles, the good deeds; the Little White God empties a sack of white pebbles, the Little Black God a sack of black, and guarding the weighing stand the buffalo-headed officers; from the court issue the six paths, bearing the recently judged - a scene Evans-Wentz sets beside the judgement in the tenth book of Plato's Republic, where the just ascend by the heavenly way on the right and the unjust descend on the left, bearing the symbols of their deeds fastened to their backs.
summary.zh: 閻魔王（辛傑）——觀音之忿怒相、猴面之王——主持稱量：一側堆黑石為惡業，一側堆白石為善業；白神傾倒善石之袋，黑神傾倒惡石之袋，牛頭獄卒守秤；六道之門自法庭兩側而出，剛受審判者列隊其間——伊文思溫茲將此景與柏拉圖《理想國》第十卷之審判並觀：善者由右天路上升，惡者由左下道而降，背上縛其業跡。

sensitivity.note: Living liturgical tradition; paraphrase of public-domain 1927 edition only.

passages.text: Shinje is the King and Judge of the Dead, the wrathful aspect of Avalokiteshvara; in the Judgement Scene there is the symbolical weighing - before him, on one side, heaped-up black pebbles, the evil deeds, and on the other heaped-up white pebbles, the good deeds. On the right of Shinje stands the Little White God, emptying a sack of white pebbles; on the other side the Little Black God, emptying a sack of black pebbles; and guarding the weighing are the buffalo-headed officers.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Evans-Wentz's edition (1927), Introduction; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 閻羅（辛傑）為死者之王與判官，乃觀世音菩薩之忿怒相；於審判場景中，有象徵性之稱量——其前，一邊堆積黑色石子，即惡業，另一邊堆積白色石子，即善業。辛傑右側立小白神，傾倒一袋白石子；另一側立小黑神，傾倒一袋黑石子；守護稱量者為牛頭獄卒。

passages.text: Issuing from the Court, on either side of the Judge, are the six paths, and on them are seated twelve of the dead who have recently been judged - a scene closely resembling the Judgement described in the tenth book of Plato's Republic, where judges seated in the intermediate space commanded the just, after judgement, to ascend by the heavenly way on the right hand, and the unjust to descend by the lower way on the left, bearing the symbols of their deeds fastened to their backs.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Evans-Wentz's edition (1927) quoting Jowett's Plato; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 自法庭而出，於判官兩側，為六道，其上坐著十二位新近受判之亡者——此景與柏拉圖《理想國》第十卷所述之審判極為相似：坐於中間地帶之判官，於判決後命公正者由右手天之道路上升，命不公正者由左手下之道路下降，並背負其行為之標記。

title.en: The Sidpa Bardo: Seeking Rebirth
title.zh: 受生中陰：尋求投生

region.en: The Sidpa Bardo of the wanderer (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 受生中陰（象徵定位）

period: Bardo Thodol; English translation 1927

source.work: The Tibetan Book of the Dead, trans. Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup, ed. Evans-Wentz (1927), Book II

summary.en: In the Sidpa Bardo the wanderer, having failed recognition, undergoes visions of the Judgment of the Lords of Death - who number all deeds with the mirror and the scales of black and white pebbles - then wanders pursued by karmic winds, seeking a womb; the methods of closing the doors of the womb, the choosing of the place of birth, and the reading of omens of the sex and caste of the coming life follow, the consciousness-principle drinking of forgetfulness as it enters the door of the womb.
summary.zh: 受生中陰中，未得認識之亡者將見閻魔王之審判——以鏡與黑白石之秤算盡其業——復為業風所逐，尋求投生之胎；經中遂教以關閉胎門之法、擇生之方，以及觀察來生性別種姓之兆，神識飲忘川之水而入胎門。

sensitivity.note: Living liturgical tradition; paraphrase of public-domain 1927 translation only.

passages.text: Now henceforth thou art going to experience the other two, the Chonyid Bardo and the Sidpa Bardo. In the Sidpa Bardo, having failed to recognize the visions of the Peaceful and the Wrathful Deities as thine own thought-forms, thou wilt wander, subject to the karmic winds, until the place of rebirth is found - and the teachings, therefore, go on to the methods of closing the doors of the womb while in the Intermediate State when seeking rebirth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Lama Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translation (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 自此以後，汝將經歷其餘二者，即法性中陰與投生中陰。於投生中陰中，因未能認出寂靜尊與忿怒尊之顯現為自心之念相，汝將受業風所驅而漂泊，直至尋得投生之處——故教法繼而講述於中陰中尋求投生時關閉胎門之法。

passages.text: Drinking of the River of Forgetfulness, the consciousness-principle enters the door of the womb and is reborn direct from the desire-world called the Sidpa Bardo - the lower rebirth being unendowed, because of the lack of enlightenment of the one undergoing it, with consciousness of the process.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Evans-Wentz's edition (1927); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 飲下忘川之水，識神入胎門，直接從稱為投生中陰之欲界受生——下等投生因經歷者未得開悟，故不具對過程之意識。

title.en: Er the Pamphylian and the Ch choosing of Bodies
title.zh: 珀菲里亞人之厄爾與擇生
