passages.text: The chief, resourceless, called to Bishutan: this plight of ours is one with misery. I met the dragon's fumings like a man, but strength and manhood now avail us not. Make supplication, all of you, to God! Then Bishutan made prayer to God, while all the soldiers lifted up their hands, and offered supplications numberless. Thereon a gentle breeze arose which bare the clouds away and heaven became serene, and when the Iranians had taken heart they offered thanks to God.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 首領無計可施，呼喚比舒坦道：我們這般處境實與苦難無異。我曾以男子之姿面對巨龍的煙霧，但如今力量與勇武皆無濟於事。你們眾人一齊向神祈求吧！於是比舒坦向神祈禱，全體士兵舉起雙手，獻上無數的懇求。隨即一陣和風興起，將雲層吹散，天空恢復晴朗，伊朗人重振精神後，向神獻上感恩。

title.en: The Seventh Stage: The Deep River and Gurgsar's Head
title.zh: 七關之七：渡河與古爾格薩爾授首

region.en: Deep river before the Brazen Hold (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 銅堡前的深河（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Seven Stages sec. 8

summary.en: When he had ridden past the troops he saw a deep, unfathomed river, and a camel of the caravan had tumbled in; the chieftain seized and dragged it from the mud. Base villain, said the prince, didst thou not say here thou wilt find no water? He said: thy host's destruction would be as bright to me as sun and moon. The chieftain laughed and promised: when I return victorious from the fight thou shalt be captain of the Brazen Hold — but at the feast Gurgsar curses him: may every evil star control thy life. Roused by his words the prince smote with an Indian sword his head, and clave him, crown to midriff; to the river they flung him presently, and that malignant grew food for fishes.
summary.zh: 第七關是一條無底的深河；馱駱駝墮河，王子竟親手拽其出泥。他質問古爾格薩爾：「你不是說此處無水嗎？」答曰：「你的大軍葬身此地，在我眼中如日月光輝。」王子以王位許諾誘其指路——渡河之後設宴，古爾格薩爾卻咒他「死無葬身之地」。王子怒而揮劍，自冠至膈將其劈為兩半，拋入河中餵魚。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: When he had ridden past the troops he saw a deep, unfathomed river. Now a camel, one of the caravan whose cameleer had kept it in the front, had tumbled in; the chieftain seized and dragged it from the mud, and that malignant Turkman of Chigil quaked. Base villain, said the prince, why hast thou used this snake-like subtlety? Didst thou not say: here thou wilt find no water, and the sun will burn thee up?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他騎馬越過軍隊之後，看見一條深不可測的河流。此時，一頭駱駝——屬於那支商隊，其趕駝人一直將牠牽在前頭——跌了進去；首領抓住牠並從泥中拖出，那奇吉勒的惡毒突厥人為之顫抖。王子說道：卑鄙的惡徒，你為何施展這般如蛇般的詭計？你莫非不曾說過：此地你找不到水，太陽會將你灼燒？

passages.text: He said: thy host's destruction would be as bright to me as sun and moon. I get from thee but fetters; what should I wish but thy bale and loss? The chieftain laughed, stared, was amazed at him, but showed no wrath, and said: Gurgsar, thou man of little wit! When I return victorious from the fight thou shalt be captain of the Brazen Hold; far be from me to harm thee; all the realm is thine if thou wilt give me honest counsel.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他說道：你軍隊的覆滅於我而言，將如日月般光明。我從你處所得不過是鐐銬；除了你的災禍與損失，我還能期望什麼？首領大笑，凝視著他，為之驚異，卻未顯怒色，說道：古爾薩爾，你這愚鈍之人！當我從戰鬥中凱旋歸來，你將成為黃銅堡壘的統帥；我絕無傷害你之意；只要你肯給我忠實的建言，整個疆域都歸你所有。

passages.text: Gurgsar rejoined: no arrow plumed and pointed, when ironed thus, can find its way across; thou shalt work magic with the mighty stream if thou wilt but unfetter me. The soldiers followed him in single file, inflating at Asfandiyar's behest their water-skins forthwith, and binding them along the barrels of their beasts of burden; they all plunged in, and the host and baggage reached land.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古爾薩爾回答說：任何飾有羽毛、裝有箭頭的箭矢，若被如此束縛，都無法穿越而過；只要你解開我的鐐銬，你便能以這條巨流施展奇術。士兵們排成單列跟隨他，奉阿斯凡迪亞爾之命立即將水囊充氣，並將其綁在馱獸的桶身上；他們全都躍入水中，軍隊與輜重皆抵達岸上。

passages.text: Heart-straitened, hostile both in speech and soul, Gurgsar retorted: how long wilt thou use such converse? Be accursed and justly so; may every evil star control thy life, thy waist be cut asunder with the sword, thy gory body flung upon the dust, the earth thy bed, the grave thy winding-sheet. Roused by his words, and raging at the oaf, the prince smote with an Indian sword his head, and clave him, crown to midriff; to the river they flung him presently, and that malignant grew food for fishes.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 古爾薩爾心胸鬱結，言語與心靈皆懷敵意，反駁道：你還要這般交談多久？你該受詛咒，且理當如此；願一切凶星主宰你的性命，願你的腰身被利劍斬斷，你血淋淋的軀體被拋於塵土，大地為你的床榻，墳墓為你的裹屍布。王子被他的話語激怒，對這蠢徒勃然大怒，以印度寶劍擊其頭部，從頭頂劈至腹部；隨即將他拋入河中，那惡毒之徒遂成了魚的食物。

title.en: Asfandiyar in the Merchant's Guise at the Brazen Hold
title.zh: 商賈之計取銅堡

region.en: Brazen Hold of Arjasp (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿爾賈斯普銅堡（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Seven Stages secs. 9-12

summary.en: I shall approach the hold in merchants' guise, and none will know me for a paladin, says Asfandiyar: ten camels laden with gold, five with brocade of Chin, five with gems, a golden throne and massive crown, eighty pairs of chests with eight score mighty men hidden inside. In slippered feet and blanket, freighted with jewels, he goes toward the hold: a merchant I; my sire was Turkman and my mother Persian. That night a conflagration blazed whose burning scorched the sky; the watchman saw the flames and Bishutan assailed the hold, while within Asfandiyar undid the chest-lids and brought kabab and wine to the men inside, and went boldly to the palace of Arjasp: this merchantman will supply thee with a sword that cost dinars — and Arjasp, a mass of wounds, his huge form sank, and Asfandiyar beheaded him.
summary.zh: 強攻無望，王子改行商賈之計：十馱黃金、五馱錦緞、五馱寶石、八十口暗藏武士的大箱。他趿著便鞋、披著氈毯入城求見阿爾賈斯普：「我是商人，父突厥而母波斯。」入夜，一場大火燒紅了天；比舒坦見煙火為號、揮軍攻堡；箱中勇士破箱而出、開懷暢飲備戰。王子直入王宮，向阿爾賈斯普「獻劍」：「此劍乃魯赫拉斯普所贈，上有古什塔斯普之印——你一接劍，命便歸塵！」混戰中魔王身負重傷，被一劍梟首。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: We might assail this hold in vain for years unless indeed I take upon me to demean myself, and try a stratagem against the foe, said Asfandiyar. I shall approach the hold in merchants' guise, and none will know me for a paladin. Ten of these beasts he loaded up with gold, upon five more he put brocade of Chin, another five had various kinds of gems, a golden throne and massive crown. He brought forth eighty pairs of chests, and made choice of eight score of his mighty men, and, having hidden them within the chests, bound on the baggage and set forth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages secs. 9-10 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿斯凡迪亞爾說道：「除非我甘願自貶身分，設法對敵人施以一計，否則我們縱然攻打這座堡壘多年，也是徒勞無功。我將扮作商人接近此堡，無人會認出我是勇士。他將十頭牲口滿載黃金，另五頭馱上中國錦緞，再五頭載著各色寶石、一張金座與一頂巨冠。他取出八十對箱籠，從麾下猛士中挑選一百六十人，將他們藏於箱中，捆好行囊便啟程出發。」

passages.text: With slippered feet, a blanket thrown about him, and freighted with the jewels, gold, and silver, the chieftain went in haste toward the hold, and journeyed in the guise of chafferers. May wisdom mate with kings! a merchant I: my sire was Turkman and my mother Persian; I purchase from Turan, bear to Iran, and deal in stuffs, in clothes, and furniture, in jewels, crowns, and other valuables.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 10 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那首領腳穿軟履，身裹毛毯，滿載珠寶、金銀，匆匆朝堡壘而去，一路扮作商賈行旅。願智慧與君王為伴！我乃一介商人：家父是突厥人，家母是波斯人；我從圖蘭採買，運往伊朗，經營布帛、衣物、家具、珠寶、冠冕與其他珍貴之物。

passages.text: The night came and a conflagration blazed, whose burning scorched the sky. When from the look-out the watchman saw the flames by night he left his post and came exultingly to Bishutan, and told what he had seen of fire and fume. The army from the plain approached the hold; when news spread in the hold that a host hath come the place rang with the name Asfandiyar.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 夜幕降臨，一片大火熊熊燃起，烈焰灼燒天際。當哨望者於夜間望見火光，便離開崗位，欣喜若狂地來到比舒坦面前，訴說他所見的火焰與濃煙。平原上的軍隊逼近堡壘；當大軍來臨的消息在堡中傳開，整座堡壘迴盪著阿斯凡迪亞爾之名。

passages.text: Asfandiyar, when night was growing dark, arrayed himself again in fighting-gear, undid the chest-lids that more air might come to those inside, and brought kabab and wine with other provand. And, clutching with his hand a glittering sword, cried to Arjasp: now will this merchantman supply thee with a sword that cost dinars; I give it as a present from Luhrasp. They closed in strife outrageous, foot to foot with sword and dagger; Arjasp failed 'neath the blows; he was a mass of wounds; his huge form sank, and then Asfandiyar beheaded him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿斯凡迪亞爾趁夜色漸深，重新披上戰甲，打開箱蓋好讓裡面的人多透些氣，並取來烤肉、美酒與其他糧食。他手握一柄閃亮的劍，向阿爾賈斯普喊道：「如今這商人要贈你一柄以金幣購得的劍；我以此作為盧赫拉斯普的贈禮。」雙方展開兇猛的廝殺，短兵相接，以劍與匕首相搏；阿爾賈斯普在連番攻擊下不支，遍體鱗傷，龐大的身軀頹然倒下，阿斯凡迪亞爾隨即斬下他的首級。

title.en: The Pitfalls of Kabul and the Fall of Rakhsh
title.zh: 喀布爾陷阱與拉赫什之墜

region.en: Hunting-plain below Kabul (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 喀布爾獵場（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Rustam and Shaghad sec. 3

summary.en: The king of Kabul honeycombs the chase with pits, arranging them beneath the rides, and in them sets haft-downward hunting-spears, swords, double-headed darts, and scimitars, and masks the openings so that neither man nor eye of beast might see them. The king comes out bare-footed, dust on head, his heart all guile, and begs pardon of Rustam, who forgives him and hunts on the plain below the city. Rakhsh sniffs fresh earth, spins like a ball, and shies, suspicious of the smell, and tears the ground to pieces with his iron shoes; howbeit that fleet steed picked his steps right warily so as to make his way between two pits — but Rustam's heart is filled with wrath at Rakhsh, and he lashes him; two of his feet go through; the haunches of the mighty Rakhsh, and Rustam's legs and bosom, are impaled.
summary.zh: 喀布爾王在獵場密掘陷阱，坑中倒插獵矛、寶劍與雙頭鏢，覆以偽裝；又跣足頂塵、假意乞憐，騙得魯斯塔姆原諒而入獵。忠馬拉赫什嗅出新土、如球般後旋刨地——牠機警地想從兩坑之間踏過；魯斯塔姆卻誤怪戰馬、揚鞭催行——兩蹄落空，巨馬的後臀與英雄的腿胸一齊被坑中利刃刺穿！

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the death of Rustam by treachery. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Now when ill-starred Shaghad had left Kabul the monarch hurried to the hunting-ground, and took a hundred sappers, men of note among the troops. They honeycombed the chase with pits, arranging them beneath the rides, and in them set haft-downward hunting-spears, swords, double-headed darts, and scimitars, and made a shift to mask the openings that neither man nor eye of beast might see them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Shaghad sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 且說那命途多舛的沙加德離開喀布爾之後，國王便趕往獵場，帶了一百名工兵，皆是軍中知名之士。他們在獵場上遍挖坑洞，將坑洞佈置於馬道之下，並在坑中倒插獵矛、刀劍、雙頭標槍與彎刀，又設法遮掩洞口，使無論人或獸之眼皆不能察覺。

passages.text: Bare-footed, dust on head, his heart all guile, he went before the chief, who pardoned him his fault. There was hard by the city of Kabul a pleasant, fertile spot with wood and water, and there they willingly encamped. When thou wouldst hunt, said the king, I have a district where on plain and hill game throngeth; wild sheep, onager, gazelle fill all the waste.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Shaghad sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他赤著雙腳，頭上沾滿塵土，滿心詭詐，來到首領面前，首領赦免了他的過錯。喀布爾城附近有一處宜人肥沃之地，有林木也有水源，他們便欣然在此紮營。國王說道：「你若想打獵，我有一處地方，平原與山丘上獵物成群；野羊、野驢、瞪羚遍佈整片荒野。」

passages.text: Rakhsh sniffed fresh earth, spun like a ball, and shied, suspicious of the smell, and tore the ground to pieces with his iron shoes. Howbeit that fleet steed picked his steps right warily so as to make his way between two pits; but Rustam's heart was filled with wrath at Rakhsh, and fortune veiled discretion from his eyes. He raised his hunting-whip and lashed Rakhsh; two of his feet went through; he had no purchase; all below was spear and sword; and so the haunches of the mighty Rakhsh, and Rustam's legs and bosom, were impaled.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Shaghad sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 拉赫什嗅到新翻的泥土，像球一般打转，因疑心那气味而惊退，用铁蹄把地面踏得粉碎。然而那匹迅捷的骏马极其谨慎地择步而行，好从两坑之间穿过去；但鲁斯塔姆心中对拉赫什充满怒火，命运又使他的双眼看不见明智。他举起猎鞭抽打拉赫什；拉赫什的两只脚陷了进去，无处着力；下面尽是矛与剑；于是雄健的拉赫什的后腿，以及鲁斯塔姆的双腿与胸膛，都被刺穿了。

title.en: Rustam's Last Arrow Pins Shaghad to the Tree
title.zh: 魯斯塔姆臨終一箭釘死逆弟

region.en: Hollow plane-tree of the hunt (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 獵場空心梧桐樹（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Rustam and Shaghad sec. 4

summary.en: Since such an ill hath come on me, says dying Rustam, uncase my bow for me, and let it serve as mine interpreter: it is not fit that lions on the prowl shall see me fallen here and sorely wounded. Shaghad draws near, uncases the bow, and laughs exulting at his brother's death; the matchless hero clutches it, and Shaghad, in terror at those arrows, skulks behind a hollow plane-tree. Rustam puts forth his hands, sore wounded as he was, and looses a shaft: he pins his brother and the tree together, and gladdens in the article of death — now God be praised, that even when my soul hath reached my lips day hath not turned to night o'er my revenge. He spake, his soul departed from his body, and all the folk bewailed him bitterly.
summary.zh: 垂死的英雄命逆弟為自己解弓上弦：「莫讓巡行的獅群見我重傷倒地。」笑看兄長垂死的沙加德怕那兩支箭，閃身躲進一棵空心梧桐樹後。魯斯塔姆強提餘力放箭——一箭連人帶樹釘穿！臨終他歡然謝神：「縱然魂至唇邊，天也未在我復仇之前轉為黑夜！」言畢魂散，舉世同悲。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Warner notes Firdausi chose the treachery version over Bahman's revenge raid. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Since such an ill hath come on me uncase my bow for me, and let it serve as mine interpreter, said Rustam; string it and lay it by me with two arrows. It is not fit that lions on the prowl, and coming on the plain in quest of quarry, shall see me fallen here and sorely wounded. Shaghad drew near, uncased the bow, and strung it; he drew it once, then laid it down by Rustam, and laughed exulting at his brother's death.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Shaghad sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 鲁斯塔姆说：既然这样的灾祸已降临到我身上，就替我把弓取出来，让它作我的代言人；把弦上好，连同两支箭放在我身旁。正在潜行、来到平原上寻觅猎物的狮子们，不该看见我倒在这里、身负重伤。沙加德走近，取出弓，上了弦；他拉了一次，然后把它放在鲁斯塔姆身旁，因兄弟之死而得意地大笑。

passages.text: The matchless hero clutched it lustily, though tortured by the anguish of his wounds, what while Shaghad in terror at those arrows made haste to shield himself behind a tree, an ancient plane still boughed and leaved but hollow, and there behind it skulked the miscreant. When Rustam saw this he put forth his hands, sore wounded as he was, and loosed a shaft: he pinned his brother and the tree together, and gladdened in the article of death.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Shaghad sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那无可匹敌的英雄虽为伤痛所折磨，仍奋力抓住它；此时沙加德因惧怕那些箭，急忙躲到一棵树后藏身——那是一株古老的悬铃木，枝叶犹存，树心却已中空，那恶徒便潜伏在其后。鲁斯塔姆见此，虽身负重伤，仍伸出双手，放出一箭：他把兄弟与那棵树钉在了一起，并在临死之际感到欣慰。

passages.text: Shaghad, when he was stricken, cried out Ah! but Rustam had not left him time to suffer, and cried: now God be praised, and I have known Him through all my years, that even when my soul hath reached my lips day hath not turned to night o'er my revenge, but He hath given me strength before my death to wreak me on this traitor. He spake, his soul departed from his body, and all the folk bewailed him bitterly; within another pit Zawara died; remained no horseman high or low beside.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Rustam and Shaghad sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 沙加德中箭时大叫一声：啊！但鲁斯塔姆没有留给他受苦的时间，说道：如今赞美归于神，我一生一世都认识祂，因为即使我的灵魂已到唇边，白昼仍未因我的复仇而转为黑夜，祂反倒在我死前赐我力量，让我向这叛徒报仇。他说完，灵魂便离开了他的身体，众人都为他痛哭；在另一坑中，扎瓦拉也死了；身旁再没有留下任何骑士，无论高低。

title.en: The Three Pressers of Haoma and Their Sons
title.zh: 豪馬汁的三位榨取者及其子嗣

region.en: Fire of Zarathushtra's rite (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 查拉圖什特拉聖火前（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded in the Avesta, c. 6th-4th century BCE (Mills translation 1887)

source.work: Yasna IX, Hom Yasht (Zend-Avesta Part III), trans. L. H. Mills, SBE 31 (1887)

summary.en: At the hour of Havan, Haoma came to Zarathustra as he served the sacred fire and sang aloud the Gathas; and Zarathustra asked: who art thou, O man! who art of all the incarnate world the most beautiful in thine own body? And Haoma answers, the holy one who driveth death afar: Vivanghvant was the first of men who prepared me, and to him was born Yima the brilliant, who made from his authority both herds and people free from dying; Athwya was the second, and to him was born Thraetaona, who smote the dragon Dahaka, three-jawed and triple-headed, six-eyed; Thrita was the third, and to him were born Urvakhshaya the judge and Keresaspa, ringlet-headed and bludgeon-bearing, who smote the horny dragon and cooked his meat upon its back in iron cauldron.
summary.zh: 哈萬時分，豪馬（神聖植物之靈）來到正侍火、唱伽薩的查拉圖什特拉面前：「普世生靈之中，誰有你這般俊美？」豪馬答：「驅死之聖靈豪馬也！」第一榨取者維萬格萬之子即輝煌的伊瑪——使畜群與人類免於死亡；第二榨取者阿斯維亞之子即斬殺三頭六眼巨龍達哈卡的特賴塔歐納；第三榨取者特里塔之子凱雷薩斯帕——鬈髮持棍的英雄，曾屠巨龍、竟在其背上架鐵釜炊飯！

sensitivity.note: Avestan liturgy read as myth; the Hom Yasht condenses the Iranian hero-catalogue. No living community restriction.

passages.text: At the hour of Havan, Haoma came to Zarathustra, as he served the sacred Fire, and sanctified its flame, while he sang aloud the Gathas. And Zarathustra asked him: who art thou, O man! who art of all the incarnate world the most beautiful in thine own body? Thereupon gave Haoma answer, the holy one who driveth death afar: I am, O Zarathustra, Haoma, the holy and driving death afar; pray to me, O Spitama, prepare me for the taste.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Yasna IX, 1-2 (Mills, SBE 31, 1887); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在哈万之时，豪摩来到查拉图斯特拉面前，当时他正侍奉圣火，使火焰洁净，同时高声唱诵伽他。查拉图斯特拉问他：你是谁，啊，凡人！在一切有肉身的世界中，你以自己的身躯最为美丽？于是豪摩作答，那驱除死亡远去的圣者说：查拉图斯特拉啊，我就是豪摩，神圣而驱除死亡远去者；斯皮塔玛啊，向我祈祷吧，为我预备品尝之用。

passages.text: Vivanghvant was the first of men who prepared me for the incarnate world; this blessedness was offered him, that to him was born a son who was Yima, called the brilliant, the most glorious of those yet born, the sunlike-one of men, that he made from his authority both herds and people free from dying, both plants and waters free from drought. In the reign of Yima swift of motion was there neither cold nor heat, there was neither age nor death, nor envy demon-made.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Yasna IX, 4-5 (Mills, SBE 31, 1887); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 维万格万特是第一个为我预备、使我进入有肉身世界的人；这份福佑赐给了他，使他得生一子，名为伊玛，号称光辉者，是已生者中最荣耀的，是凡人中如太阳一般者，因为他凭自己的权威使牲畜与人民都免于死亡，使植物与水都免于干旱。在迅捷的伊玛统治期间，既无寒冷也无炎热，既无衰老也无死亡，亦无恶魔所造的嫉妒。

passages.text: Athwya was the second who prepared me for the corporeal world; to him a son was born, Thraetaona of the heroic tribe, who smote the dragon Dahaka, three-jawed and triple-headed, six-eyed, with thousand powers, and of mighty strength, a lie-demon of the Daevas, evil for our settlements, whom the evil spirit Angra Mainyu made as the most mighty Drug against the corporeal world.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Yasna IX, 7-8 (Mills, SBE 31, 1887); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿斯維亞是第二位為我預備肉身世界的人；他得了一子，即英雄部族的斯拉埃陶納，他擊殺了達哈卡巨龍——三顎三首、六眼、具千種威力、力大無窮，是達埃瓦的謊言之魔，危害我們的居所，乃惡靈安格拉·曼紐為對抗肉身世界所造最強大的德魯格。

passages.text: Thrita was the third man who prepared me for the corporeal world; to him were born Urvakhshaya and Keresaspa, the one a judge confirming order, the other a youth of great ascendant, ringlet-headed, bludgeon-bearing: he who smote the horny dragon swallowing men and swallowing horses, poisonous and green of colour, on whose back once Keresaspa cooked his meat in iron cauldron at the noon-day meal; and the dragon, scorched, upstarted, and springing off, dashed out the water as it boiled.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Yasna IX, 10-11 (Mills, SBE 31, 1887); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 斯里塔是第三位為我預備肉身世界的人；他得了烏爾瓦赫沙亞與凱雷薩斯帕二子，一為確認秩序的法官，一為氣勢極盛、捲髮、持棍棒的青年：他擊殺了吞人吞馬、有毒而色青、遍體生角的巨龍，昔日凱雷薩斯帕曾在正午進餐時於其背上以鐵釜烹煮肉食；那巨龍被灼燒，猛然躍起，騰身跳開，把沸騰的水濺了出去。

title.en: The Wicked Soul Meets Her Sin in the Shape of a Maiden
title.zh: 惡魂黎明遇「罪惡之娼女」

region.en: Bridge of judgment at dawn (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 黎明之審判橋（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE (Pahlavi; West translation 1882)

source.work: Dadestan-i Denig ch. XXV (Pahlavi), trans. E. W. West, SBE 18 (1882)

summary.en: Those three nights the soul of the wicked is upon earth, and notices the thoughts, words, and deeds of its own body; it experiences grievous fear of the account, great terror of the bridge, and perplexing fear on account of hell. The first night it is hastening away from its own evil thoughts, the second from its evil words, the third from its evil deeds — but the spirits of its good works come unto the soul and become pleasing to it. And the third night, on the fresh arrival of a dawn, its sin, in the frightful, polluted shape of a maiden who is an injurer, comes to meet it with the store of its sin; a stinking northerly wind comes out to meet it, and it comes on shudderingly and unwillingly running to the account, falls from the bridge, and is precipitated to hell.
summary.zh: 惡魂在塵世惶惶三夜：懼清算、畏天橋、恐地獄；三夜之中它逃避自己的惡念、惡言、惡行——然而畢生善行的精靈仍來相慰。第三夜黎明時分，它的罪孽化作一個玷污的可怕「娼女」，攜其罪簿前來相迎；一陣腥臭北風迎面撲來——惡魂戰慄不前、被迫赴秤，終從橋上墜落，直沉地獄。

sensitivity.note: Pahlavi doctrinal text; the personified conscience (daena) as maiden pairs with Arda Viraf's vision. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Those three nights the soul is upon earth, and notices about the thoughts, words, and deeds of its own body; it is doubtful about its own position, and experiences grievous fear of the account, great terror of the bridge, and perplexing fear on account of hell.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dadestan-i Denig ch. XXV, 2 (West, SBE 18, 1882); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那三夜之間，靈魂留在地上，察覺自己身體的所思、所言、所行；它對自己的處境感到疑惑，並經歷對清算的沉重恐懼、對橋的極大畏怖，以及因地獄而生的惶惑驚懼。

passages.text: The first night it is hastening away from its own evil thoughts, the second night from its own evil words, and the third night from its own evil deeds; but, owing to the good works which it has done in the world, the first night the spirit of its good thoughts, the second night the spirit of its good words, and the third night the spirit of its good deeds, come unto the soul, and become pleasing and commendable to it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dadestan-i Denig ch. XXV, 4 (West, SBE 18, 1882); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 第一夜它匆匆逃離自己的惡念，第二夜逃離自己的惡言，第三夜逃離自己的惡行；然而，由於它在世上所行的善業，第一夜其善念之靈、第二夜其善言之靈、第三夜其善行之靈來到靈魂跟前，使它覺得可喜可嘉。

passages.text: And the third night, on the fresh arrival of a dawn, its sin, in the frightful, polluted shape of a maiden who is an injurer, comes to meet it with the store of its sin; and a stinking northerly wind comes out to meet it, and it comes on shudderingly, quiveringly, and unwillingly running to the account. And through being deceived and deceiving, heresy, unrelenting and false accusation of constant companions, and the wide-spread sinfulness of a fiend-like existence it is ruined, falls from the bridge, and is precipitated to hell.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dadestan-i Denig ch. XXV, 5-6 (West, SBE 18, 1882); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 到了第三夜，黎明初至，它的罪以一個害人的少女那可怕而污穢的形象，帶著它罪業的積累前來相迎；一股惡臭的北風出來迎接它，它便顫抖著、哆嗦著、不情願地奔向清算。由於受欺與欺人、執迷不悟的異端與對常伴之人的虛妄指控，以及如魔般生存的普遍罪惡，它終至毀滅，從橋上墜落，被拋入地獄。

title.en: The Hedge-hog's Prickles and the Dogs of the Bridge
title.zh: 刺蝟聖獸與守橋之犬

region.en: Midnight world of the two spirits (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 子夜的善惡二靈之界（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded in the Avesta, c. 6th-4th century BCE (Darmesteter translation 1880)

source.work: Vendidad Fargard XIII (Zend-Avesta Part I), trans. J. Darmesteter, SBE 4 (1880)

summary.en: Which is the good creature among the creatures of the good spirit that from midnight till the sun is up goes and kills thousands of the creatures of the evil spirit? Ahura Mazda answers: the dog with the prickly back, with the long and thin muzzle, the dog Vanghapara, which evil-speaking people call the Dusaka — this is the good creature that from midnight till the sun is up goes and kills thousands of the creatures of the evil spirit; and whosoever shall kill it kills his own soul for nine generations, nor shall he find a way over the Chinvat bridge. And whosoever shall smite either a shepherd's dog, or a house dog, or a Vohunazga dog, his soul when passing to the other world shall fly amid louder howling and fiercer pursuing than the sheep does when the wolf rushes upon it in the lofty forest.
summary.zh: 「何為善靈造物中，自子夜至日出誅殺千萬惡靈造物者？」答曰：背生尖刺、吻長而薄的「萬哈帕拉」之犬（即刺蝟）——殺之者九代之魂無救，且不得過欽瓦特橋！擊打牧犬、家犬或聖犬者，其亡魂將在來世承受比羊遭狼逐更甚的嗥叫與追逐——守橋之犬也不會前來相助。

sensitivity.note: Avestan law-text read as myth; Darmesteter reads the hedge-hog as a myth of sunrays piercing night. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Which is the good creature among the creatures of the good spirit that from midnight till the sun is up goes and kills thousands of the creatures of the evil spirit? Ahura Mazda answered: the dog with the prickly back, with the long and thin muzzle, the dog Vanghapara, which evil-speaking people call the Dusaka; this is the good creature among the creatures of the good spirit that from midnight till the sun is up goes and kills thousands of the creatures of the evil spirit.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard XIII, 1-2 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在善靈的造物之中，哪一種是善的造物，自午夜直至日出，往來擊殺惡靈的造物以千計？阿胡拉·馬茲達回答：那背生棘刺、口鼻細長的狗，即萬哈帕拉犬，惡言之人稱之為杜薩卡；在善靈的造物之中，正是這一種善的造物，自午夜直至日出，往來擊殺惡靈的造物以千計。

passages.text: And whosoever, O Zarathustra! shall kill the dog with the prickly back, with the long and thin muzzle, the dog Vanghapara, which evil-speaking people call the Dusaka, kills his own soul for nine generations, nor shall he find a way over the Chinvat bridge, unless he has, while alive, atoned for his sin by offering up a sacrifice to Sraosha.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard XIII, 3 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 哦，查拉圖斯特拉啊！凡殺死那背上有刺、口鼻細長、名為萬加帕拉（Vanghapara）之犬——即惡言之人稱之為杜薩卡（Dusaka）者——的人，便是殺害自己的靈魂達九代之久，且不得尋得跨越欽瓦特橋（Chinvat）之路，除非他生前已藉由向斯勞沙（Sraosha）獻祭而贖其罪。

passages.text: Whosoever shall smite either a shepherd's dog, or a house dog, or a Vohunazga dog, or a trained dog, his soul when passing to the other world shall fly amid louder howling and fiercer pursuing than the sheep does when the wolf rushes upon it in the lofty forest. No soul will come and meet his departing soul and help it through the howls and pursuit in the other world; nor will the dogs that keep the Chinvat bridge help his departing soul.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard XIII, 8-9 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 凡擊打牧羊犬、家犬、沃胡納茲加犬（Vohunazga）或受訓之犬者，其靈魂前往彼世時，將在比羊於高聳森林中遭狼撲襲時更響亮的嚎叫與更猛烈的追逐中飛逃。沒有靈魂會前來迎接他離去的靈魂，助它度過彼世的嚎叫與追逐；守護欽瓦特橋的眾犬亦不會幫助他離去的靈魂。

title.en: Astyages Feeds Harpagos His Own Son
title.zh: 阿斯杜阿該斯以人子為宴

region.en: Court of Astyages, Agbatana (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 阿格巴塔納王庭（象徵性定位）

period: Written c. 430 BCE (Macaulay translation 1890)

source.work: Herodotus, Histories Book 1, trans. G. C. Macaulay (1890), secs. 117-120

summary.en: When Astyages learns that the exposed Cyrus lives, he masks his wrath with kind words: be here thyself to dine with me, for I intend to make a sacrifice of thanksgiving for the preservation of the boy. Harpagos sends his only son, of about thirteen years old, to the palace; and Astyages cuts his throat and divides him limb from limb, and having roasted some pieces of the flesh and boiled others, before Harpagos is placed the flesh of his own son, all but the head and the hands and the feet. And when Harpagos says he has been very greatly pleased, they bring to him the head of his son covered up: he is not overcome with amazement but contains himself; and this is the Harpagos who afterwards will overthrow Astyages for Cyrus.
summary.zh: 阿斯杜阿該斯得知棄嬰居魯士尚在人世，便強抑怒火、假意設宴：「為慶賀孩子平安，請你赴宴。」哈爾帕戈斯將獨子（年約十三）送入王宮——王割其喉、肢解其身，一半炙、一半煮，把這孩子的肉端到哈爾帕戈斯面前（頭與手足另藏於籃）。哈爾帕戈斯強忍悲痛說「宴席甚美」——正是這位隱忍的父親，日後將為居魯士傾覆米底王國。

sensitivity.note: Greek historiography of the Median court legend (the Thyestes motif). No living community restriction.

passages.text: Astyages ended by saying that the child was alive and that that which had come to pass was well: I was greatly troubled by that which had been done to this child; therefore consider that this is a happy change of fortune, and first send thy son to be with the boy who is newly come, and then, seeing that I intend to make a sacrifice of thanksgiving for the preservation of the boy, be here thyself to dine with me.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.118 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿斯提阿格斯（Astyages）最後說道，那孩子還活著，且所發生之事甚好：我因對這孩子所做之事而深感不安；因此你當認為這是命運的喜人轉變，首先派你的兒子去與那新來的男孩相伴，然後，鑒於我打算為這孩子的保全而獻感恩之祭，你本人也來此與我共宴。

passages.text: When Harpagos heard this, he did reverence and thought it a great matter that his offence had turned out for his profit; and so he sent forth his son, for he had one only son of about thirteen years old, bidding him go to the palace of Astyages. But Astyages, when the son of Harpagos arrived, cut his throat and divided him limb from limb, and having roasted some pieces of the flesh and boiled others he caused them to be dressed for eating and kept them ready.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.119 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 哈爾帕格斯（Harpagos）聞此言，行禮致敬，並認為自己的過失竟轉為己利，實為大事；於是他便送出他的兒子，因為他只有一個約十三歲的獨子，命他前往阿斯提阿格斯的宮殿。然而阿斯提阿格斯在哈爾帕格斯之子抵達後，割其喉嚨，將其肢解，並將部分肉烤熟、部分水煮，命人調理成可供食用之狀，備妥待用。

passages.text: Before the other guests and before Astyages himself were placed tables covered with flesh of sheep; but before Harpagos was placed the flesh of his own son, all but the head and the hands and the feet. Then when it seemed that Harpagos was satisfied with food, Astyages asked him whether he had been pleased with the banquet; and when Harpagos said that he had been very greatly pleased, they brought to him the head of his son covered up, and standing near they bade Harpagos uncover and take of them that which he desired.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.119 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在其他賓客與阿斯提阿格斯本人面前，擺放著盛滿羊肉的桌子；但在哈爾帕格斯面前，擺放的卻是他親生兒子的肉，只除去了頭、手與腳。隨後，當哈爾帕格斯看似已飽足於食物時，阿斯提阿格斯問他是否對這宴席感到滿意；當哈爾帕格斯說他極為滿意時，他們便將他兒子的頭顱蓋著呈上，並站在近旁，命哈爾帕格斯揭開，隨意取用其中他所欲之物。

passages.text: So when Harpagos obeyed and uncovered, he saw the remains of his son; and seeing them he was not overcome with amazement but contained himself; and Astyages asked him whether he perceived of what animal he had been eating the flesh: and he said that he perceived, and that whatsoever the king might do was well pleasing to him. Thus having made answer and taking up the parts of the flesh which still remained he went to his house.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Herodotus 1.119 (Macaulay 1890); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是哈爾帕格斯遵命揭開，看見了他兒子的殘骸；見此，他並未驚愕失措，而是克制住了自己；阿斯提阿格斯問他是否察覺自己吃的是何種動物的肉：他說他察覺了，且無論國王做什麼，都令他十分滿意。如此作答之後，他拿起仍剩下的那些肉塊，回到了自己家中。

title.en: Rustam on Foot Slays Ashkabus of Kashan
title.zh: 徒步的魯斯塔姆誅卡什安的阿什卡布斯

region.en: Plain before Mount Hamawan (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 哈馬萬山前平原（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Kamus sec. 28

summary.en: Ashkabus of Kashan rides out challenging the Iranians and smashes Ruhham's helm, till matchless Rustam comes on foot with bow slung and arrows in his belt: my mother called me by this name — 'Thy death!'; do lions, crocodiles, and leopards fight on horseback in thy country? Ashkabus laughs in astonishment, and Rustam shoots an arrow at the breast of his fine steed: sit by thy noble comrade and nurse its head! Then, taking his bow of Chach, he set his thumbstall to the deer-hide string; the bent bow sang; the shaft's point bussed his finger; he loosed and struck the breast of Ashkabus — the sky kissed Rustam's hand — and he of Kashan expired. The Khan's heart aged when he beheld the feathers and the point: their arrows are like spears!
summary.zh: 卡什安勇將阿什卡布斯叫陣、擊碎魯哈姆的頭盔；魯斯塔姆竟徒步出戰，肩掛弓、腰插箭：「我母親給我取名——『你的死期』！你們那裡的獅子、鱷魚也騎馬打仗嗎？」一箭射翻其戰馬，再取喬赫硬弓搭箭——弓弦輕吟、箭吻指腹——一箭貫胸！天地喝彩；卡尚人當場斃命。可汗見那箭羽箭鏃，頓時心冷：「他們的箭竟如長矛！」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: The peerless Rustam answered: hapless one! why askest thou my name among the folk? My mother called me by this name — Thy death! Fate made me for the hammer of thy helm. He of Kashan replied: without a horse thou givest up thyself to slaughtering! Then peerless Rustam: senseless challenger! Hast thou ne'er seen foot-soldiers lay proud heads beneath the stones? Do lions, crocodiles, and leopards fight on horseback in thy country?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kamus sec. 28 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 無與倫比的魯斯塔姆答道：不幸之人啊！你為何要在眾人之中問我的名字？我母親以此名喚我——你的死期！命運造我，正是為了做擊碎你頭盔的鎚。卡尚那人回答：你沒有馬，便把自己交給屠戮了！於是無與倫比的魯斯塔姆說：無知的挑戰者啊！你難道從未見過步兵把高傲的頭顱壓在石下嗎？在你們的國度裡，獅子、鱷魚和豹子會騎在馬背上爭鬥嗎？

passages.text: He marked the pride of Ashkabus in his fine steed, and shot an arrow at its breast; the charger fell headforemost. Rustam laughed and cried aloud: sit by thy noble comrade! Prithee nurse its head and rest thee from the fight awhile. Then Ashkabus, his body quivering, strung up his bow and showered shafts on Rustam, who exclaimed: in vain thou weariest thy wicked soul, thine arms, and body.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kamus sec. 28 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他看出阿什卡布斯以其駿馬為傲，便朝馬胸射出一箭；那戰馬一頭栽倒。魯斯塔姆大笑，高聲喊道：去坐在你那高貴的同伴身旁吧！請你照料牠的頭，暫且歇息，離開戰鬥吧。於是阿什卡布斯渾身顫抖，張弓搭箭，向魯斯塔姆射出一陣箭雨，魯斯塔姆喊道：你徒然耗費你那邪惡的靈魂、你的武器和身體。

passages.text: Choosing from his girdle a shaft of poplar wood he drew it forth bright-pointed, feathered with four eagle-plumes; then took his bow of Chach in hand and set his thumbstall to the deer-hide string; he straightened his left arm, curved his right; the bent bow sang; the shaft's point reached his ear; the deer-hide hummed; the shaft's point bussed his finger and its notch was at his back; he loosed and struck the breast of Ashkabus; the sky kissed Rustam's hand. He of Kashan expired, thou wouldst have said: his mother never bare him!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kamus sec. 28 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他從腰帶中選出一支白楊木箭，將它抽出，箭頭明亮，飾以四根鷹羽；隨後執起他的恰奇弓，把拇指環扣上鹿皮弓弦；他伸直左臂，彎曲右臂；彎弓歌唱；箭頭觸及他的耳際；鹿皮嗡鳴；箭頭親吻他的手指，箭尾已至他的背後；他鬆弦放箭，射中阿什卡布斯的胸膛；天空親吻了魯斯塔姆的手。卡尚那人氣絕身亡，你定會說：他母親從未生過他！

title.en: Kamus of Kashan Taken by the Sixty Coils
title.zh: 六十圈套索擒卡穆斯

region.en: Field of Mount Hamawan (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 哈馬萬戰場（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Kamus sec. 32

summary.en: The peerless Rustam let loose the twisted lasso from its straps and took his massive mace; Kamus said: bluster not so much about a thread of sixty coils. The lion roareth bravely on catching sight of game, said Rustam; now shalt thou see how tight the knots will hold. Kamus let out with his glittering glaive to sever Rustam's head; the point alighted on Rakhsh's neck and clave the battle-mail, but failed to wound. The elephantine hero coiled, whirled, and flung the lasso round his foe, then spurred away and made the leather fast beneath his thigh while Rakhsh flew eagle-like. Kamus sought by force to break the twisted thong, becoming frantic, but the raw hide held: now this illustrious warrior's helm and hauberk are his shroud, his crown is dust, and his juppon the grave.
summary.zh: 卡穆斯譏其「六十圈的線繩」；魯斯塔姆答：「獅見獵物而吼——你就知道這結有多緊！」卡穆斯的利劍劈在拉赫什頸甲上未能傷人；英雄套索飛出、纏住敵腰，一抖韁繩、驅駿馬如鷹疾馳——任憑卡穆斯如何發狂掙扎，生牛皮紋絲不斷。英雄拖其至眾將之前：「他的頭盔鎧甲成了壽衣，王冠化塵，戰袍即是墳墓！」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: The peerless Rustam let loose the twisted lasso from its straps, and took his massive mace as for a strife of chiefs; he roared like some mad elephant as he advanced with lasso on his arm and mace in hand. Kamus said: bluster not so much about a thread of sixty coils. The lion roareth bravely, Rustam said, on catching sight of game; now shalt thou see how tight the knots will hold.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kamus sec. 32 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 無與倫比的魯斯塔姆從皮帶上解開那條扭絞的套索，又取來他那沉重的狼牙棒，彷彿要與眾首領交戰；他如狂象般咆哮，臂上纏著套索、手中握著狼牙棒向前推進。卡穆斯說：不必為一根六十圈的繩子如此咆哮。魯斯塔姆說：獅子一見獵物，便會勇敢地咆哮；現在你將看到那些結會收得多緊。

passages.text: Kamus the valiant urged his dun steed on, and let out with his glittering glaive, intent to sever Rustam's head; the point alighted on Rakhsh's neck and clave the battle-mail, but failed to wound. The elephantine hero coiled, whirled, and flung the lasso round his foe, then spurred away and made the leather fast beneath his thigh while Rakhsh flew eagle-like. Kamus sought by force to break the twisted thong, becoming frantic, but the raw hide held.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kamus sec. 32 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 勇猛的卡穆斯催動他的棗紅戰馬前進，揮出閃亮的長刀，意欲斬下魯斯塔姆的首級；刀尖落在拉赫什的頸上，劈開了戰甲，卻未能傷及牠。那如象般的英雄盤旋、迴轉，把套索拋向他的敵人，隨即策馬而去，將皮索牢牢踩在大腿之下，而拉赫什如鷹般飛馳。卡穆斯拼命想掙斷那扭絞的皮索，幾近發狂，但生皮卻牢牢不放。

passages.text: The elephantine hero, checking Rakhsh, wheeled, jerked Kamus headforemost to the ground, came up, secured him in the lasso's coils, and said to him: thou art not dangerous now. In vain are all thy charms and spells; thy soul hath made a fruitless bargain with the Div. On what wise do ye purpose slaying him? Then Rustam flung Kamus upon the ground before the chiefs; the warriors left their ranks, hacked his body with their scimitars, and drenched the stones and dust beneath with blood.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kamus sec. 32 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那如象般的英雄勒住拉赫什，迴身一轉，把卡穆斯頭朝前猛拽到地上，走上前去，將他牢牢困在套索的圈中，對他說：你現在已不危險了。你所有的符咒與法術都是徒勞；你的靈魂與迪夫做了一筆無用的交易。你們打算用什麼法子殺他呢？於是魯斯塔姆把卡穆斯摔在眾首領面前的地上；戰士們離開行列，用彎刀砍他的身體，把身下的石與塵土都浸透了鮮血。

title.en: Kafur the Man-eater and the City of Bidad
title.zh: 食人者卡富爾與「不義之城」

region.en: City of Bidad in Sughd (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 粟特比達德城（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Khan of Chin sec. 20

summary.en: On marching one stage thence Rustam saw a city by name Bidad, a hold inhabited by folk whose only food was human flesh: the flesh of growing youths alone was served at the loathly king's board. The king's name was Kafur; when he heard that a host led by a famed chief approached, he armed as did his pard-like people, skilled lasso-flingers and stones and anvils in the fray. Gustaham bids Bizhan tell Rustam to come with ten score cavaliers; Kafur flung his lasso o'er the son of Zal, who ducked his head; then Rustam raised his war-cry like an angry elephant, smote his head-piece with the mace, which smashed together helmet, head, and neck: his brains ran down his nostrils, and Kafur the warrior fell.
summary.zh: 行軍途中魯斯塔姆望見「不義之城」比達德——城中人以人肉為食，少年之肉供奉暴君餐桌！食人王卡富爾率豹一般彪悍的套索手迎戰；古斯塔哈姆遣比讚求援。卡富爾擲出套索，魯斯塔姆低頭躲過，隨即如怒象般吶喊、掄錘猛擊——盔、顱、頸一齊粉碎，腦漿自鼻孔流出，食人者當場斃命！

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; man-eater episode. No living community restriction.

passages.text: On marching one stage thence he saw a city by name Bidad, a hold inhabited by folk whose only food was human flesh. The lovely there were ever perishing, while at the table of a king so loathly the flesh of growing youths alone was served. Those slaves that were the goodliest supplied the provand for the monarch's board; such was his food. The king's name was Kafur; he held the city by patent.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khan of Chin sec. 20 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他從那裡行進一站，便看見一座名為比達德的城市，那是一座由以人肉為唯一食物之民所居的堡壘。那裡可愛的人不斷死去，而在如此可憎的國王餐桌上，只供奉成長中青年的肉。那些最俊美的奴隸供作君王餐桌的食糧；這便是他的食物。國王名叫卡富爾；他憑敕令佔有這座城市。

passages.text: When he heard that from Iran a host, led by a famed and warlike chief, approached, he armed as did his pard-like people, who were skilled lasso-flingers, cavaliers, and stones and anvils in the fray. Gustaham said to Bizhan in haste: ride hence; tell Rustam: pause not, but come with ten score cavaliers.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khan of Chin sec. 20 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他聽說從伊朗來了一支軍隊，由一位著名且好戰的首領率領，正逼近時，他便武裝起來，他那些如豹般的子民也同樣武裝，他們擅長擲套索、是騎手，在戰鬥中如石與鐵砧。古斯塔哈姆急忙對比詹說：從此騎行而去；告訴魯斯塔姆：不要停留，帶兩百名騎手前來。

passages.text: Kafur came rushing with a furious charge against the royal and fruit-bearing Tree, and hurled his sword, as though it were an arrow, but Rustam received it on his shield and took no harm. Kafur next flung his lasso o'er the son of Zal, who ducked his head; then Rustam raised his war-cry like an angry elephant, whereat Kafur stood still in blank amaze, and Rustam smote his head-piece with the mace, which smashed together helmet, head, and neck: his brains ran down his nostrils, and Kafur the warrior fell.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khan of Chin sec. 20 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 卡富爾怒氣沖沖地衝向那株王者且結果的樹，並像箭一般擲出他的劍，但魯斯塔姆用盾牌接住，未受傷害。卡富爾接著把套索拋過扎爾之子，他低頭閃避；隨後魯斯塔姆像一頭憤怒的大象般發出戰吼，卡富爾當場愕然站住，魯斯塔姆用狼牙棒擊打他的頭盔，將頭盔、頭顱和脖子一同砸碎：他的腦漿從鼻孔流下，戰士卡富爾倒下了。

title.en: Rustam Uproots Puladwand Like a Plane-tree
title.zh: 魯斯塔姆如拔山楊般揪起普拉達萬德

region.en: Plain of Machin and Chin (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 馬秦與秦地平原（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. III, Khan of Chin secs. 24-25

summary.en: Afrasiyab summons the warrior-div Puladwand to his aid, and Tus, Giv, Ruhham, and Bizhan are all unhorsed. Rustam challenges the ill-conditioned div, and elephantine Rustam with his mace strikes his foe's head: all present heard the crash. When the mace fails, Puladwand says: wrestling is the test 'twixt man and man; take we each other by the leathern belt. Afrasiyab, breaking troth, urges him on: if thou gett'st him down in wrestling rip him open with thy dagger. Then, like a lion, reaching out he clutched the chest and neck of that fierce Crocodile, and, straining hard, uprooted Puladwand, as though he were a plane-tree, from his place, raised him aloft, dashed him upon the ground, and uttered praises to Almighty God.
summary.zh: 阿弗拉西亞卜召來魔王戰將普拉達萬德，圖斯、吉夫、魯哈姆、比讚接連墜馬。魯斯塔姆出陣，一錘擊其頭顱——全場聽得巨響！魔王懼其虎皮鎧甲，提議角力定勝負；暴君卻背信喝令「摔倒便以匕首剖之」。然而獅爪般的英雄抓住那兇鱷的胸頸，奮力一拔——如拔山楊樹般將魔王連根揪起、高舉過頂、狠狠摜地，並讚頌全能之神！

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; pairs with the Sohrab and Human wrestling duels. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Then closing with the div he threw his lasso, but Puladwand, brave horseman though he was, ducked in alarm, he had had fight enough. Consider now the fire of mine attack, my lasso, courage, might, and enterprise, said the div; thou shalt behold no traces of thy Shah, his nobles, or his mighty men henceforth, for I will give thine army to Afrasiyab.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khan of Chin sec. 24 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 然後他與迪夫扭打，擲出套索，但普拉德萬德雖是勇敢的騎手，卻驚慌地低頭閃避，他已經打夠了。現在想想我攻擊的火焰、我的套索、勇氣、力量和進取心吧，迪夫說；從今以後你將看不到你的沙阿、他的貴族或他的勇士的任何蹤跡，因為我要把你的軍隊交給阿弗拉西亞布。

passages.text: Then both the warriors wheeled till Puladwand, whose massive mace fell but without effect on Rustam's tiger-skin and coat of steel, said: wrestling is the test 'twixt man and man; take we each other by the leathern belt, that we may know which one the will of fate dismisseth worsted from the battlefield.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khan of Chin sec. 24 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 然後兩位戰士轉動身軀，直到普拉德萬德——他那巨大的狼牙棒落在魯斯塔姆的虎皮和鋼甲上卻毫無效果——說道：摔跤是人與人之間的考驗；讓我們各抓住對方的皮帶，好讓我們知道命運的意旨會把誰作為敗者逐出戰場。

passages.text: Giv marked the king's wild words: observe Afrasiyab, his eagerness, and wild words! He hath come forth to inflame the heart of thine antagonist and prompt him to use his dagger in a wrestling-bout. Then, like a lion, reaching out Rustam clutched the chest and neck of that fierce Crocodile, and, straining hard, uprooted Puladwand, as though he were a plane-tree, from his place, raised him aloft, dashed him upon the ground, and uttered praises to Almighty God.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Khan of Chin secs. 24-25 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 吉夫注意到國王的狂言：看看阿弗拉西亞布，他的急切和狂言！他出來是要煽動你對手的心，促使他在摔跤中用匕首。然後，魯斯塔姆像獅子一樣伸出手，抓住那兇猛鱷魚的胸和頸，用力一拉，把普拉德萬德像梧桐樹一樣從原地連根拔起，高高舉起，猛摔在地上，並讚美全能的神。

title.en: Kai Khusrau Crosses the Jihun
title.zh: 卡伊霍斯勞渡烏滸水

region.en: Fords of the Jihun (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 烏滸水渡口（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. IV, Great War sec. 14

summary.en: As soon as Kai Khusrau had passed the river he banished banqueting, repose, and sleep, and sent this proclamation forth: let no man be in terror at our coming, but offer prayer for us to holy God. He gave great largess to the mendicants, thence departed to the march of Sughd, and saw a novel world, the home of owls, lavishing treasure in eagerness for its prosperity. He harangued his host: as for the Turkmans who submit themselves, and in their hearts repent of making war, fight not against them, and shed not their blood — but if any whose vengeful heart remaineth recusant shall strive against you, then bloodshed and harrying are permitted you. He traversed in this way a hundred leagues, depopulating stronghold, hill, and plain.
summary.zh: 大軍一渡烏滸水，霍斯勞即戒宴樂、戒酣眠，並傳諭：「我軍所至，爾等勿懼；請向聖神為我們祈禱。」他厚賜貧者，兵發粟特——那「貓頭鷹的國度」；並告誡全軍：「凡棄戰歸順、真心悔過的突厥人，不得加害；唯有負隅頑抗者，方可誅討。」於是大軍橫掃百驛之地，堡壘丘陵悉數平毀。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the avenger-king's conquest of Turan. No living community restriction.

passages.text: As soon as Kai Khusrau had passed the river he banished banqueting, repose, and sleep, and, when he had transported all his troops across, he sent this proclamation forth: let no man be in terror at our coming, but offer prayer for us to holy God. He gave great largess to the mendicants, especially to those who welcomed him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 凱霍斯魯一渡過河，便戒絕了宴飲、安歇與睡眠；待他將全軍盡數渡過之後，便頒下這道詔令：凡我軍所至，任何人皆不得驚懼，反當為我們向聖神祈禱。他對乞者施以厚賜，尤其厚待那些前來迎接他的人。

passages.text: He thence departed to the march of Sughd, and saw a novel world, the home of owls; upon that country too he lavished treasure in eagerness for its prosperity, and, whereso'er he halted, cavaliers came seeking quarter. Anon the Shah harangued his host and said: in that our task is different to-day, as for the Turkmans who submit themselves, and in their hearts repent of making war, fight not against them, and shed not their blood. Lead none the way to evil, but if any, whose vengeful heart remaineth recusant, shall seek to strive against you with a host, then bloodshed, harrying, and combating in any quarter are permitted you. He traversed in this way a hundred leagues, depopulating stronghold, hill, and plain.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他從此處啟程前往粟特邊境，見到一個新奇的世界，那是貓頭鷹的居所；他對那片土地也慷慨傾注財寶，急切盼望其繁榮；凡他駐足之處，皆有騎士前來求宿。不久，沙阿向全軍訓話道：今日我等任務有別，至於那些歸順、心中悔於興戰的突厥人，不可與之交戰，不可流其血。勿引任何人走上邪路；但若有人心懷報復、執意不從，率軍來與你們相爭，那麼在任何地方流血、劫掠與交戰，皆准許你們為之。他就這樣行過百里之地，所過之處，堡壘、山丘與平原盡皆荒廢。

title.en: Afrasiyab Shuts Himself in Gang-bihisht, His Earthly Paradise
title.zh: 阿弗拉西亞卜退守「地上天堂」剛比希什特

region.en: Gang-bihisht beyond Chin (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 秦地之外的剛比希什特（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. IV, Great War secs. 16-18

summary.en: Gang is eight leagues in length and four in breadth; men, women, children, and troops are there; no eagles soar above its battlements, none dreameth of such heights! There are provisions, palace, treasure, crown, and majesty; the country round about is called Bihisht — i.e. Paradise — where all is pleasure, peace, and happiness. Relying on his fortune Afrasiyab entered Gang-bihisht exultingly with all his arms and implements of war; he bade magicians bring up mighty stones upon the walls, stationed troops upon the ramparts, and kept a troop of smiths at work to fashion claws of steel on every side and bind them to long spears to grapple any that adventured nigh.
summary.zh: 阿弗拉西亞卜退入他自建的「地上天堂」——剛比希什特：八里縱橫、泉池棋布、寶庫王宮俱全，「鷹隼不越其雉堞，凡人難夢其高峻」！他命術士以法力運巨石築牆，塔樓遍佈甲士，又令鐵匠打造長桿鋼鉤——凡近城者，非被鉤住即被嚇退。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the fortified paradise of the Turanian king. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Gang is eight leagues in length and four in breadth; men, women, children, and troops are there; thou wilt have wealth, the foe will still toil on. No eagles soar above its battlements, none dreameth of such heights! There are provisions, palace, treasure, crown, and majesty, command, and throne and host. The country round about is called Bihisht, where all is pleasure, peace, and happiness.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 16 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 岡城長八里，寬四里；其中有男、有女、有孩童，亦有軍隊；你將得財富，敵人仍將徒然勞苦。沒有鷹隼翱翔於其城垛之上，無人敢夢想這般高峻！那裡有糧秣、宮殿、寶藏、王冠與威嚴，有號令、寶座與大軍。四周之地名為比希什特，那裡盡是歡愉、安寧與幸福。

passages.text: Whenas Afrasiyab had heard these words they pleased him and, relying on his fortune, he entered Gang-bihisht exultingly with all his arms and implements of war. He went about the city and beheld not e'en a hand-breadth of waste ground therein; there was a palace lifted to the sky, built by himself, a king whose word was law.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 16 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿弗拉西亞布聽聞此言，甚為喜悅，遂倚仗自己的運勢，帶著全副兵器與戰具，歡欣鼓舞地進入岡比希什特。他巡行城中，竟不見其中有一掌之寬的荒地；那裡有一座高聳入雲的宮殿，乃是他親手所建，他是一位言出法隨的君王。

passages.text: Afrasiyab for his own part at Gang abandoned quiet, banqueting, and sleep, arranged his catapults upon the walls, and fitted up the towers to stand a siege. He bade magicians bring up mighty stones upon the walls, and he kept a troop of smiths at work to fashion claws of steel on every side and bind them to long spears to grapple any that adventured nigh, or, if not that, to make him shun the hold.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 17 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿弗拉西亞布本人則在岡城捨棄了安寧、宴飲與睡眠，將他的投石機架設於城牆之上，並整備塔樓以備守城。他命術士將巨石運上城牆，又令一隊鐵匠不停勞作，在各處打造鋼爪，縛於長矛之上，以鉤抓任何膽敢靠近之人；若非如此，也要令其不敢接近此堡。

title.en: The Secret Souterrain of Gang-bihisht
title.zh: 剛比希什特的密道

region.en: Palace of Gang-bihisht (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 剛比希什特王宮（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. IV, Great War sec. 22

summary.en: Afrasiyab, beholding such terror and defeat — no Jahn, no brother, no land, no throne, no realm, no gems, no treasure — farewells his throne of sovereignty: when shall I ever look on thee again upon a day of pleasure, ease, and joy? Now when he built the palace in the hold he had made a secret passage underground, and not a soldier of the army wotted that there was such a by-way underneath the castle: he made choice of ten score chiefs, and vanished by that secret souterrain, emerging he betook him to the waste, while all his kingdom wondered after him, none knowing where he was. Khusrau approached the palace, trod down his foe's star, and assumed the throne.
summary.zh: 堡破之際，阿弗拉西亞卜登樓一望——戰士死傷殆盡、兄弟俱失、江山財寶成空——他泣別御座：「幾時才能再享歡愉之日？」原來他築宮時預留了一條地下密道，全軍無一人知曉；他率兩百名酋長自密道遁入荒野，舉國驚疑、莫知所蹤。霍斯勞入城、踏碎敵星，登上那空置的王座。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Afrasiyab, beholding matters thus, such terror and defeat, no Jahn, no brother, no land, no throne, no realm, no gems, no treasure, cried out in very earnest, seared and sore: how wantonly heaven's vault hath dealt with us! He came down woeful from the palace-roof, farewelled his throne of sovereignty, and said: when shall I ever look on thee again upon a day of pleasure, ease, and joy?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 22 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿弗拉西亞布見情勢如此，驚恐萬分、潰敗至此，既無雅恩，亦無兄弟，無土地，無王座，無疆域，無寶石，無財寶，遂痛徹心扉、聲嘶力竭地喊道：天穹待我們何其恣意無常！他滿懷悲傷地從宮殿屋頂下來，告別了他的主權寶座，說道：我何時才能再於歡愉、安逸與喜樂之日見到你？

passages.text: Now when he built the palace in the hold he made a secret passage underground, and not a soldier of the army wotted that there was such a by-way underneath the castle. He made choice of ten score chiefs, and vanished by that secret souterrain; emerging he betook him to the waste, while all his kingdom wondered after him, none knowing where he was because he vanished so suddenly.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 22 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當他在堡壘中建造宮殿時，便在地下開鑿了一條秘密通道，軍中沒有一名士兵知道城堡底下有這樣一條暗道。他挑選了兩百名首領，經由那條秘密地道消失無蹤；出來之後，他前往荒野，而他的整個王國都在追尋他的下落，卻無人知道他身在何處，因為他消失得如此突然。

passages.text: Khusrau approached the palace, trod down his foe's star, and assumed the throne amid the paladins with golden helms. They made abundant quest, but failed to trace that chief of nobles; then the Shah inquired of Jahn and Garsiwaz about their king: how did he go and whither hath he gone? The conquering Shah said: now that my foe hath vanished from the throne his name and purpose matter not a jot.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 22 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 霍斯勞逼近宮殿，踏碎敵人的星辰，在金盔武士之間登上王座。他們大肆搜尋，卻未能追查到那位貴族之首；於是沙阿向賈恩與加爾西瓦茲詢問他們的君王：他是如何離去，又往何處去了？征服者沙阿說道：既然我的敵人已從王座上消失，他的名字與意圖便無關緊要了。

title.en: Hum's Lasso: Afrasiyab and Garsiwaz Slain
title.zh: 胡姆的套索：阿弗拉西亞卜與加爾西瓦茲授首

region.en: Lake of the wanderers (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 流浪者之湖（象徵性定位）

period: Composed c. 1010 CE (Warner translation 1905)

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. IV, Great War sec. 44

summary.en: While these two princes were exchanging words the mind of Hum, the devotee, devised a scheme: he went upon a spit of land, and, when he saw Afrasiyab anear, undid the royal lasso from his waist and flung it, and took the monarch's head within the noose; he dragged him forth from lake to land and resigned him to the Shahs. First I allege the murder of thy brother, says Kai Khusrau; next of Naudar, that world-lord and memorial of Iraj; and thirdly that of Siyawush, whose head thou didst cut off as 'twere a sheep's. With Indian sword he smote Afrasiyab upon the neck, and flung upon the dust the swarthy form whose ears and hoary beard were red with blood; they dragged Garsiwaz shamefully in heavy bonds, and clave the chief asunder at the waist, and flung those two like mountains side by side.
summary.zh: 隱士胡姆設計擒龍：一記套索將阿弗拉西亞卜自湖畔拖上陸地，獻於王前。霍斯勞歷數其三罪：「弑叔伊拉吉、誅瑙達爾、斬西亞瓦什如屠羊！」言畢揮劍斬其頸，那黑面白鬚的軀體轟然倒地；其弟加爾西瓦茲被縛至帳前，自腰斬為兩段——如兩座山嶽並陳於野。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the end of the Turanian arch-foe. No living community restriction.

passages.text: While these two princes were exchanging words the mind of Hum, the devotee, devised a scheme; he went upon a spit of land, and, when he saw Afrasiyab anear, undid the royal lasso from his waist, and came on stalking like a savage lion, then flung the lasso that was ready coiled, and took the monarch's head within the noose. Hum dragged him forth in miserable plight, and loathing life itself, from lake to land, resigned him to the Shahs and went his way.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 44 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 當這兩位王子交談之際，虔誠者胡姆心中生出一計；他走到一處伸入水中的陸地上，當他看見阿弗拉西亞布靠近時，便從腰間解下王家的套索，像一頭兇猛的獅子般潛行而來，隨即拋出早已盤好的套索，將君王的頭顱套入繩圈之中。胡姆將他悽慘地拖了出來，令他厭棄自己的生命，從湖中拖到岸上，將他交給諸位沙阿，便自顧離去。

passages.text: O evil-doer, answered Kai Khusrau, well worthy of reproach and infamy! First I allege the murder of thy brother, who never sought to injure noble men; next of Naudar, that famous sovereign, that world-lord and memorial of Iraj, whose neck thou clav'st with thy sharp scimitar; and thirdly that of Siyawush, like whom none seeth any horseman to recall him, whose head thou didst cut off as 'twere a sheep's. How was it possible to slay my sire and not expect an evil day like this?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 44 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「哦，作惡之人，」凱霍斯勞答道，「你實在該受譴責與惡名！首先我指控你殺害你的兄弟，他從未圖謀傷害高貴之人；其次是瑙達爾，那位著名的君主，那位世界之主、伊拉吉的紀念，你曾用鋒利的彎刀砍斷他的頸項；第三是西亞武什，無人能見到像他這樣的騎士可與之相比，你卻像宰羊一般砍下他的頭顱。你怎能殺害我的父親，卻不預期會有這樣一個凶日呢？」

passages.text: With Indian sword he smote Afrasiyab upon the neck, then flung upon the dust the swarthy form, whose ears and hoary beard were red with blood, while Garsiwaz his brother lost all hope; Afrasiyab's imperial throne was void; the day of his good fortune reached its close. They dragged him from the jailors shamefully in heavy bonds, on that his evil day; when in sad plight he came before Khusrau the Shah called an executioner who came with trenchant sword unsheathed, and clave the chief asunder at the waist, and they flung those two like mountains side by side.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Great War sec. 44 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 他以印度之劍擊中阿弗拉西亞布的頸項，隨即將那黝黑的身軀拋落塵埃，他的雙耳與花白鬍鬚都染滿了鮮血，而他的兄弟加爾西瓦茲則徹底絕望；阿弗拉西亞布的帝座已然空虛；他好運的日子已到了盡頭。他們在那凶日將他從獄卒手中以沉重的鎖鏈羞辱地拖出；當他悽慘地來到霍斯勞面前時，沙阿召來一名劊子手，那人拔出鋒利的劍走來，將那位首領攔腰劈成兩半，他們便將那兩人如兩座山般並排拋下。

title.en: The Five Joys and the Five Griefs of the Earth
title.zh: 大地的五喜與五悲

region.en: Neck of Arezura, gate of hell (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 地獄之門阿雷祖拉山頸（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded in the Avesta, c. 6th-4th century BCE (Darmesteter translation 1880)

source.work: Vendidad Fargard III (Zend-Avesta Part I), trans. J. Darmesteter, SBE 4 (1880)

summary.en: Which is the first place where the Earth feels most happy? It is the place whereon one of the faithful steps forward with the holy wood in his hand, the baresma in his hand, the holy meat in his hand, the holy mortar in his hand, fulfilling the law with love. Which is the first place where the Earth feels sorest grief? It is the neck of Arezura, whereon the hosts of fiends rush forth from the burrow of the Drug — the mount at the gate of hell. The second grief is the place wherein most corpses of dogs and of men lie buried; the third, the place whereon stand most of those Dakhmas on which corpses of men are deposited; the fourth, the place wherein are most burrows of the creatures of Angra Mainyu; and the fifth, the place whereon the wife and children of one of the faithful are driven along the way of captivity, the dry, the dusty way, and lift up a voice of wailing.
summary.zh: 大地何處最喜？——信徒手持聖薪、聖枝、聖肉與聖臼行禮之處！大地何處最悲？——阿雷祖拉山頸：群魔自地獄洞穴湧出之門！其後四悲：犬與人的屍骨密集之地、屍體高疊的寂靜塔、惡靈洞穴遍布之地，以及信徒妻兒被驅上塵土俘虜之路、一路哀哭之處。

sensitivity.note: Avestan law-text read as sacred geography; Dakhma and Arezura lore. No living community restriction.

passages.text: O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! Which is the first place where the Earth feels most happy? Ahura Mazda answered: it is the place whereon one of the faithful steps forward, O Spitama Zarathustra! with the holy wood in his hand, the baresma in his hand, the holy meat in his hand, the holy mortar in his hand, fulfilling the law with love.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard III, 1 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 哦，物質世界的創造者，聖者啊！大地在哪一處最先感到最快樂？阿胡拉·馬茲達回答說：就是那忠信者向前邁步的地方，哦，斯皮塔馬·瑣羅亞斯德！他手中持著聖木，手中持著巴雷斯瑪，手中持著聖肉，手中持著聖臼，以愛心履行律法。

passages.text: O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! Which is the first place where the Earth feels sorest grief? Ahura Mazda answered: it is the neck of Arezura, whereon the hosts of fiends rush forth from the burrow of the Drug.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard III, 7 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「啊，物質世界的創造者，聖者啊！大地最先在哪一處感到最深的悲痛？」阿胡拉·馬茲達回答：「是在阿雷祖拉的頸項上，成群的惡魔從毒品之獸的巢穴中衝出之處。」

passages.text: It is the place wherein most corpses of dogs and of men lie buried; it is the place whereon stand most of those Dakhmas on which corpses of men are deposited; it is the place wherein are most burrows of the creatures of Angra Mainyu; and it is the place whereon the wife and children of one of the faithful, O Spitama Zarathustra! are driven along the way of captivity, the dry, the dusty way, and lift up a voice of wailing.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard III, 8-11 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「那是最多狗與人的屍體被埋葬之處；那是大多數停放著人屍的達赫瑪矗立之處；那是安格拉·曼紐所造之物巢穴最多之處；啊，斯皮塔瑪·瑣羅亞斯德！那也是信士之一的妻兒被驅趕上俘虜之路——那乾燥、塵土飛揚之路——並高聲哀號之處。」

title.en: He Who Sows Corn Sows Holiness
title.zh: 播種五穀者播撒聖潔

region.en: Barley-fields of the faithful (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 信徒的大麥田（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded in the Avesta, c. 6th-4th century BCE (Darmesteter translation 1880)

source.work: Vendidad Fargard III (Zend-Avesta Part I), trans. J. Darmesteter, SBE 4 (1880)

summary.en: Who is the first that rejoices the Earth with greatest joy? It is he who digs out most of those corpses of dogs and men; the second is he who pulls down most of those Dakhmas. But it is he who sows corn, sows holiness: he makes the law of Mazda grow higher and higher, he makes the law of Mazda as fat as he can with a hundred acts of adoration, a thousand oblations, ten thousand sacrifices. When barley is coming forth, the Daevas start up; when the corn is growing rank, then faint the Daevas' hearts; when the corn is being ground, the Daevas groan; when wheat is coming forth, the Daevas are destroyed. In that house they can no longer stay; it is as though red hot iron were turned about in their throats, when there is plenty of corn.
summary.zh: 誰最能使大地歡喜？——掘淨犬屍人屍者、拆毀寂靜塔者；但真正的至喜乃是「播種五穀者即播撒聖潔」——他使馬茲達之法茁壯高升！大麥抽芽，群魔跳起；禾苗繁茂，魔心衰竭；磨麥之聲起，群魔呻吟；麥浪湧現，群魔滅亡——屋裡麥香彌漫之處，惡魔如遭烙鐵燒喉，再也待不下去！

sensitivity.note: Avestan law-text; the husbandry-as-holiness digression. No living community restriction.

passages.text: O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! Who is the first that rejoices the Earth with greatest joy? Ahura Mazda answered: it is he who digs out most of those corpses of dogs and men. The second is he who pulls down most of those Dakhmas on which corpses of men are deposited.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard III, 12-13 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「啊，物質世界的創造者，聖者啊！誰最先以最大的喜悅使大地歡欣？」阿胡拉·馬茲達回答：「是那挖出最多狗與人屍體的人。其次是那拆毀最多停放人屍的達赫瑪的人。」

passages.text: He who sows corn, sows holiness: he makes the law of Mazda grow higher and higher; he makes the law of Mazda as fat as he can with a hundred acts of adoration, a thousand oblations, ten thousand sacrifices. When barley is coming forth, the Daevas start up; when the corn is growing rank, then faint the Daevas' hearts.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard III, 31-32 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「播種穀物者，即播種聖潔：他使馬茲達的律法日益高漲；他以百次崇拜、千次獻祭、萬次犧牲，盡其所能地使馬茲達的律法肥壯。當大麥萌發時，達埃瓦們便躍起；當穀物茂盛生長時，達埃瓦們的心便衰弱。」

passages.text: When the corn is being ground, the Daevas groan; when wheat is coming forth, the Daevas are destroyed. In that house they can no longer stay, from that house they are beaten away, wherein wheat is thus coming forth. It is as though red hot iron were turned about in their throats, when there is plenty of corn.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard III, 32 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「當穀物被磨碎時，達埃瓦們呻吟；當小麥萌發時，達埃瓦們被消滅。在小麥如此萌發的那戶人家裡，他們再也無法停留，他們被逐出那戶人家。當穀物豐足時，就好像燒紅的鐵在他們喉嚨裡轉動一般。」

title.en: The Corpse Carried Alone and the Thirty Paces
title.zh: 獨自負屍者與三十步之罰

region.en: Barren place of banishment (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 荒涼的放逐地（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded in the Avesta, c. 6th-4th century BCE (Darmesteter translation 1880)

source.work: Vendidad Fargard III (Zend-Avesta Part I), trans. J. Darmesteter, SBE 4 (1880)

summary.en: Let no man alone by himself carry a corpse: if a man alone by himself carry a corpse, the Nasu rushes upon him, to defile him, from the nose of the dead, from the eye, from the tongue, from the jaws, from the sexual organ, from the hinder parts; this Drug, this Nasu, falls upon him, stains him even to the end of the nails, and he is unclean, thenceforth, for ever and ever. What shall be the place of that man who has carried a corpse alone? Thirty paces from the fire, thirty paces from the water, thirty paces from the consecrated bundles of baresma, three paces from the faithful: there shall they erect an enclosure, and therein shall they establish him with the coarsest food and with the most worn-out clothes.
summary.zh: 任何人不得獨自負屍！若獨負屍體，「屍毒」惡靈便從死者之鼻、眼、舌、口、私處與後竅撲來，沾染他直至指甲之端——他從此永世不潔！其罰所為：離聖火三十步、離聖水三十步、離聖枝束三十步、離信徒三步——眾人在彼築一圍屋，以最粗劣的食物與最破舊的衣衫供其度日。

sensitivity.note: Avestan purity law read as mythic boundary-drawing; corpse-pollution lore. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Let no man alone by himself carry a corpse. If a man alone by himself carry a corpse, the Nasu rushes upon him, to defile him, from the nose of the dead, from the eye, from the tongue, from the jaws, from the sexual organ, from the hinder parts. This Drug, this Nasu, falls upon him, stains him even to the end of the nails, and he is unclean, thenceforth, for ever and ever.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard III, 14 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「不可讓任何人獨自搬運屍體。若有人獨自搬運屍體，納蘇便從死者的鼻、眼、舌、顎、生殖器、臀部向他撲來，要玷污他。這毒品，這納蘇，落在他身上，將他玷污直至指甲末端，從此以後，他永遠不潔。」

passages.text: O Maker of the material world, thou Holy One! What shall be the place of that man who has carried a corpse alone? Ahura Mazda answered: thirty paces from the fire, thirty paces from the water, thirty paces from the consecrated bundles of baresma, three paces from the faithful.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard III, 15-17 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「物質世界的創造者啊，聖者！那獨自搬運屍體的人，其居處當在何處？」阿胡拉·馬茲達回答：「距火三十步，距水三十步，距聖化的巴瑞斯瑪束三十步，距信徒三步。」

passages.text: There, on that place, shall the worshippers of Mazda erect an enclosure, and therein shall they establish him with food, therein shall they establish him with clothes, with the coarsest food and with the most worn-out clothes. That food he shall live on, those clothes he shall wear, and thus shall they let him live, until he has grown to the age of a Hana, or of a Zaurura.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vendidad Fargard III, 18-19 (Darmesteter, SBE 4, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 就在那地方，馬茲達的崇拜者當立一道圍欄，在其中安置他，供以食物，在其中安置他，供以衣物，以最粗劣的食物與最破舊的衣物。他當賴那食物為生，他當穿那些衣物，他們當如此讓他活著，直到他長到哈納或扎烏魯拉的年歲。

title.en: The Twelve Thousand Years and the Zodiac of Kings
title.zh: 一萬二千年與黃道諸王朝

region.en: Wheel of the constellations (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 星座之輪（象徵性定位）

period: Recorded 9th century CE (Pahlavi; West translation 1880)

source.work: Bundahishn ch. XXXIV (Pahlavi), trans. E. W. West, SBE 5 (1880)

summary.en: Time was for twelve thousand years; three thousand years was the duration of the spiritual state, where the creatures were unthinking, unmoving, and intangible; and three thousand years was the duration of Gayomart, with the ox, in the world. As this was six thousand years the series of millennium reigns of Cancer, Leo, and Virgo had elapsed, and when the millennium reign came to Libra the adversary rushed in, and Gayomart lived thirty years in tribulation. After the millennium reign came to Scorpio, Dahak ruled a thousand years; after it came to Sagittarius, Fretun reigned five hundred years; and so the reigns run from constellation to constellation down to Ardashir son of Papak and the Sasanians, four hundred and sixty years, and then it went to the Arabs.
summary.zh: 宇宙之壽一萬二千年：前三千年為「無形無思」的靈界之世；其後三千年伽堯馬特與原牛居於世界。黃道三千年的王朝依次輪轉——巨蟹、獅子、室女座之後，輪至天秤時惡靈破界而入，伽堯馬特苦難三十年！天蠍座千年是扎哈克的暴政；人馬座五百屬法里東……歷數至阿爾達希爾與薩珊王朝四百六十年，而後天下歸於阿拉伯人。

sensitivity.note: Pahlavi cosmological chronology; the zodiac-millennium scheme. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Time was for twelve thousand years; and it says in revelation, that three thousand years was the duration of the spiritual state, where the creatures were unthinking, unmoving, and intangible; and three thousand years was the duration of Gayomart, with the ox, in the world.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. XXXIV, 1 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 時間共為一萬二千年；啟示中說，三千年為靈性狀態之期，其時造物無思、無動、不可觸及；三千年為伽約馬特與牛在世間之期。

passages.text: As this was six thousand years the series of millennium reigns of Cancer, Leo, and Virgo had elapsed, because it was six thousand years when the millennium reign came to Libra, the adversary rushed in, and Gayomart lived thirty years in tribulation. After the millennium reign came to Scorpio, Dahak ruled a thousand years; after the millennium reign came to Sagittarius, Fretun reigned five hundred years.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. XXXIV, 2-6 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 如此已過六千年，巨蟹、獅子、處女三個千年之治的序列已然流逝，因為當千年之治臨到天秤時，正值六千年，敵人衝入，伽約馬特在苦難中活了三十年。當千年之治臨到天蠍時，達哈克統治了一千年；當千年之治臨到人馬時，弗雷通統治了五百年。

passages.text: Ardashir son of Papak and the number of the Sasanians four hundred and sixty years, and then it went to the Arabs. The Adamians bore the title in an uninterrupted sovereignty two hundred and eighty-four years, and Darai son of Darai fourteen years; Alexander the Ruman fourteen years.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. XXXIV, 8-9 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 帕帕克之子阿爾達希爾與薩珊諸王共四百六十年，然後歸於阿拉伯人。亞當族人以不間斷的主權保有稱號二百八十四年，達賴之子達賴十四年；羅馬人亞歷山大十四年。

title.en: The Two Friends Who Set Off to Travel Round the World
title.zh: 兩友環遊世界記

region.en: Smith Sound, Polar Eskimo country, Northwest Greenland
region.zh: 西北格陵蘭史密斯海峽極地因紐特之地

period: Inuit oral tradition (Polar Eskimo, Smith Sound); collected by Knud Rasmussen, published 1921

source.work: Knud Rasmussen (collector), Eskimo Folk-Tales, ed. and rendered into English by W. J. Alexander Worster (Gyldendal, 1921), 'The Two Friends who set off to travel round the world', eBook #28932

summary.en: Two newly married men set out in opposite directions to travel round the world, so they might tell others what it is like. They live, have children, and grow old on the way; only in extreme age do they meet again, their drinking horns worn to stubs by the many fills along the road. 'The world is great indeed.'
summary.zh: 兩名新婚男子相背而行，分頭環繞世界，好向族人述說天下之貌。旅途遙遠，二人成家生子、白髮蒼蒼，直到垂暮方重逢，獸角杯已被沿途取水磨得只剩柄底。二人相語：『世界真是大啊。』

sensitivity.note: Polar Eskimo (Inughuit) oral tale recorded by Rasmussen, 1910s, published 1921. Colonial-era mediation acknowledged; no living-community consent claimed.

passages.text: Two men desired to travel round the world, that they might tell others what was the manner of it. This was in the days when men were still many on the earth and there were people in all the lands — the teller adds that now men grow fewer and fewer, evil and sickness having come upon them. The two had each newly taken a wife and had no children yet. They made themselves cups of musk-ox horn, each cutting his cup from one side of the same beast's head, and they set out, each going away from the other by different ways, agreeing to meet again some day. They travelled with sledges and settled each summer on whatever land they reached.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Knud Rasmussen, Eskimo Folk-Tales (Worster 1921), 'The Two Friends who set off to travel round the world'; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有兩個人想要環遊世界，好告訴別人世界是何模樣。那時世上的人還很多，各地都有人——講述者補充說，如今人越來越少，邪惡與疾病已臨到他們身上。這兩人各自新娶了妻，尚無子女。他們用麝牛角為自己做了杯子，各從同一頭牛頭的一側切下自己的杯子，然後出發，各自取不同的路彼此相離而去，約定他日再相見。他們帶著雪橇旅行，每到夏天便在所到之地安頓下來。

passages.text: The journey took a whole life. On the road the two men had children, the children grew old, and the travellers became so old they could no longer walk but were led by their children. At last they met — and of their drinking horns there was but the handle left, so many times had they filled them by scraping the horn against the ground as they drank. 'The world is great indeed,' they said when they met. Young when they started, old when they found each other again, led by their children. Truly the world is great, the teller concludes.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Knud Rasmussen, Eskimo Folk-Tales (Worster 1921), 'The Two Friends who set off to travel round the world'; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 這段旅程耗盡了一生。途中，這兩名男子有了孩子，孩子們長大變老，而旅人自己也老得再也走不動，只能由孩子們攙扶著前行。他們終於相會——而他們的飲角只剩下把手，因為他們飲水時總是把角抵著地面刮磨，不知反覆裝了多少回。「世界著實廣大啊。」他們相會時說道。出發時年少，重逢時已老，由孩子們攙扶著。世界著實廣大，講述者如此作結。

title.en: Nukunguasik, Who Escaped from the Tupilak
title.zh: 努孔瓜西克逃出圖皮拉克之手

region.en: South-East Greenland (Ammassalik district)
region.zh: 東南格陵蘭（阿馬薩利克一帶）

period: Inuit oral tradition (South-East Greenland); collected by Knud Rasmussen, published 1921

source.work: Knud Rasmussen (collector), Eskimo Folk-Tales, ed. and rendered into English by W. J. Alexander Worster (Gyldendal, 1921), 'Nukunguasik, who escaped from the Tupilak', eBook #28932

summary.en: Nukunguasik stumbles on a brother of his neighbours secretly fashioning a tupilak monster to bite him to death. Creeping close, he slaps the maker's side and asks 'But where is this Nukunguasik?' — frightening the sorcerer dead at his own unfinished weapon. The reawakened tupilak later gnaws its maker's corpse, and the victim of the plot lives to be the oldest man of his place.
summary.zh: 努孔瓜西克偶然撞見鄰家兄弟暗中捏製圖皮拉克怪物，欲令其咬死自己。他悄近拍了那術士一掌，問道：『可努孔瓜西克在哪裡？』術士竟被自己未竟的咒物嚇死。復活的圖皮拉克其後啃食造主屍身，而陰謀所害之人卻壽終為故里最長者。

sensitivity.note: South-East Greenland (Ammassalik) oral tale recorded by Rasmussen, 1910s. Tupilak-making is a documented historical shamanic practice; tale presented as archival record, not as representation of living Ammassalik belief.

passages.text: Nukunguasik lived in a place with many brothers, a wifeless man to whom the brothers gave meat for the pot when they made a catch. One day he rowed northward in his kayak and, on a whim, crossed to a big island he had never visited. Going up to look at the beautiful land, he came upon the middle one of many brothers busy in a hollow, whispering all the time. Crawling stealthily nearer, he heard the whisper: 'You are to bite Nukunguasik to death; you are to bite Nukunguasik to death.' The man was making a Tupilak and stood telling it what to do.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Knud Rasmussen, Eskimo Folk-Tales (Worster 1921), 'Nukunguasik, who escaped from the Tupilak'; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 努孔瓜西克住在一個有許多兄弟的地方，他是個沒有妻子的人，兄弟們捕到獵物時，會分些肉給他下鍋。有一天，他划著皮艇向北行，一時興起，便渡到一座他從未造訪過的大島。他上岸察看這片美麗的土地，卻撞見眾多兄弟中的居中那一個，正忙於一個窪坑之中，口中不停低聲細語。他悄悄爬近，聽見那低語道：「你要把努孔瓜西克咬死；你要把努孔瓜西克咬死。」那人正在製作一個圖皮拉克，站在那裡吩咐它該做什麼。

passages.text: Suddenly Nukunguasik slapped the maker's side and said: 'But where is this Nukunguasik?' The man was so frightened that he fell down dead. Nukunguasik saw that the sorcerer had let the Tupilak sniff at his body — it was now alive and lay there sniffing — and being afraid of it, he went away without harming it. He rowed home, and the brothers waited in vain for the middle one to return. When they prepared to search for him, Nukunguasik suggested the island where no one ever goes, and sent the searchers to its southern side.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Knud Rasmussen, Eskimo Folk-Tales (Worster 1921), 'Nukunguasik, who escaped from the Tupilak'; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 努孔瓜西克突然拍了那製作者的身側一下，說道：「可這個努孔瓜西克在哪兒呢？」那人驚嚇過度，當場倒地而死。努孔瓜西克看見巫師曾讓圖皮拉克嗅過自己的身體——它此刻已活了過來，躺在那裡嗅著——他心生畏懼，便離去，沒有傷害它。他划船回家，兄弟們卻苦等居中那一個不歸。當他們準備去尋找他時，努孔瓜西克提議去那座從無人前往的島，並把搜尋的人派往島的南側。

passages.text: The brothers found the dead man and cried out over him — and there lay the Tupilak, still alive, nibbling at the body of its maker. The brothers buried him under a mound of stones and went home. Nukunguasik lived on as the oldest man of the place and died at last after many years. 'Here I end this story: I know no more,' the storyteller says. The tale teaches the old Greenlandic belief that a tupilak made to kill another may turn on its maker, and that the sorcerer who dies at his own creature dies doubly shamed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Knud Rasmussen, Eskimo Folk-Tales (Worster 1921), 'Nukunguasik, who escaped from the Tupilak'; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 兄弟們找到了那死者，為他放聲哀哭——而圖皮拉克就躺在那裡，仍然活著，正啃咬著它製作者的身體。兄弟們將他葬在一堆石塚之下，然後回家。努孔瓜西克繼續活著，成了當地最年長的人，許多年之後終於死去。「我的故事到此為止：我再也不知道更多了。」講述者說道。這則故事教導了古老的格陵蘭信仰：為殺害他人而製作的圖皮拉克，可能會反噬其製作者；而巫師若死於自己造出的東西之手，便是雙重地蒙羞而死。

title.en: Qujavarssuk: The Strong Man Protected by the Old Wizard
title.zh: 古亞瓦舒克：受老巫護佑的強者

region.en: Ikerssuaq (Godthaab district), West Greenland
region.zh: 西格陵蘭伊克舒阿峽（努克一帶）

period: Inuit oral tradition (Godthaab, West Greenland); collected by Knud Rasmussen, published 1921

source.work: Knud Rasmussen (collector), Eskimo Folk-Tales, ed. and rendered into English by W. J. Alexander Worster (Gyldendal, 1921), 'Qujavarssuk', eBook #28932

summary.en: A childless strong man arranges with an old fisherman-wizard to beget a son on his wife; the boy Qujavarssuk grows to be a matchless hunter, harpooning two seals daily. When two jealous kinsmen raise a tupilak against him, the boy seems to vanish from its sight and lures it to destroy its own maker; his wife later banishes the sea-ice by magic. Named after a man who died of hunger, Qujavarssuk finally out-hunts the champion of Amerdloq and takes a whale.
summary.zh: 無子的強者與老漁巫立約，令其子嗣托生己妻；所生古亞瓦舒克日獵雙豹，技冠群倫。兩名嫉妒親戚以圖皮拉克加害，少年隱身使其撲空，誘其吞噬造主；其妻更以巫術破海冰。少年承亡者之名，終勝阿默德洛克第一獵手，獵得一鯨。

sensitivity.note: Godthaab (Nuuk) district oral tale recorded by Rasmussen, 1910s. Includes a ritual-wife arrangement described as the teller's community custom of its era; recorded as archival material without endorsement.

passages.text: A strong man lived at Ikerssuaq with one other resident, an old man who lived on nothing but devil-fish and traded the fish for the strong man's surplus catch. The hunter, who never failed to catch seal, fell silent as time went on, because he could get no children. The old one was a wizard, and one day the strong man bargained with him: go to my wife when she comes down to the shore, and each day I will give you something of my catch. The wife, finely dressed, went down twice before the old wizard came in to her; that day he caught scarcely any fish, and the strong man, hearing his confession, gave him a seal and sealed their bargain. The wizard then prescribed a cormorant skeleton from a bird cliff and an unsunned stone for a lamp, and told the couple the woman was with child.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Knud Rasmussen, Eskimo Folk-Tales (Worster 1921), 'Qujavarssuk'; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 有個強壯的男子住在伊克蘇阿克，那裡還有一位居民，是個老人，他單靠魔鬼魚過活，並用魚換取那強壯男子多餘的漁獲。那獵人捕海豹從不失手，卻隨著時日推移而沉默寡言，因為他始終得不到孩子。那老人是個巫師，有一天，強壯的男子與他講定條件：當我妻子下到岸邊時，你便去找她，而我每天會分些漁獲給你。那妻子盛裝打扮，下到岸邊兩回，老巫師才進到她那裡；那天他幾乎沒捕到什麼魚，強壯的男子聽了他的告解，便給了他一頭海豹，雙方就此立約。巫師於是開出方子：要一隻來自鳥崖的鸕鶿骨架，以及一塊未經日曬的石頭作燈，並告訴這對夫妻，那女人已有身孕。

passages.text: The wife bore a son, whom the strong man gave to the old one to name after a dead man — for it was believed the qualities of the dead passed to the living namesake. 'Let him be named after him who died of hunger in the north, at Amerdloq,' said the wizard, and the boy was called Qujavarssuk. When the wizard tested the finished kayak by holding the boy in it, seals rose all around the water, a sign he would be a chief among hunters. Rowing out for the first time, he harpooned a black seal at his first cast, and every day thereafter he brought home a catch, two seals a day even when the ice pressed the open water into a narrow lead.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Knud Rasmussen, Eskimo Folk-Tales (Worster 1921), 'Qujavarssuk'; not verbatim.
passages.zh: 妻子生下一個兒子，強壯的男子把他交給老人，要他以一個死者的名字命名——因為人們相信死者的稟性會傳給同名的生者。「就讓他以那個在北方阿梅德洛克餓死的人命名吧。」巫師說道，於是男孩便叫作夸瓦爾蘇克。當巫師把男孩放進造好的皮艇裡試艇時，海豹從水面四周紛紛浮起，這是他將成為獵人首領的徵兆。他第一次划船出海，第一擲便以魚叉刺中一頭黑海豹，此後他天天帶回漁獲，即使冰層把開闊的水面擠壓成一條狹窄的水道，他也一天捕得兩頭海豹。

passages.text: In a time of hunger, visitors heard of Qujavarssuk and came to his land. Among them were two old wizards, his mother's kinsmen, who were fed on the best of the catch — but one of them took offence at being told he had begun eating from the wrong side of the seal, lest the hunter's luck cease. Laden with gifts on the road home, the angry kinsman resolved to make a Tupilak to eat Qujavarssuk.
