passages.text: That morning the Buddha sent Moggallana to overmaster the treasurer without impairing his faith or his riches. Poised in the air at the window, the elder walked, sat cross-legged, and stood on the sill while the miser snarled that none of it would get him anything; then the elder belched smoke until the whole mansion was one mass of it, and the treasurer, eyes stinging, bade his wife cook one little cake to get rid of him. The dough swelled past the pot; every cake exceeded the last; and when the wife tried to take one from the basket, all the cakes stuck together. Husband and wife pulled with might and main, sweat poured from him, and his craving vanished. The elder preached almsgiving to them, took the couple and the basket in hand, left the head of their staircase in Jaggery and set its foot at the battlemented gate of Jetavana, and in less time than walking downstairs the two stood before the Buddha.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 4, story 5 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那天早晨佛陀派目犍連去降伏庫藏官，卻不可損害他的信心或財富。長老凌空立於窗前，行走、結跏趺坐、立在窗檻上，慳吝者咆哮說這些都討不到什麼；長老便打嗝噴煙，直到整座樓閣煙霧瀰漫；庫藏官雙眼刺痛，命妻子做一小塊餅打發他走。麵糰脹出了缽；每一塊餅都比上一塊大；妻子去籃裏拿一塊，所有的餅粘成了一團。夫妻使盡力氣拉扯，他汗如雨下，貪念卻消失了。長老向他們說布施之法，手提夫妻二人與籃子，把他們樓梯的頭留在糖城，把梯腳立在祇園的城堞門口；不到下一層樓梯的工夫，兩人已站在佛陀面前。

passages.text: The Teacher and five hundred monks ate their fill, the couple ate their fill, and still the cakes suffered no diminution until the leftovers were thrown into a cave near the gate, which is called the Cake-cave to this day. At the words of thanksgiving both husband and wife were established in stream-entry, and mounting the staircase at the gate they found themselves at home, free to spend eighty crores solely in the religion of the Buddha. When the monks praised Moggallana in the Hall of Truth, the Buddha declared that a monk must approach a household as a bee approaches a flower, gathering honey without hurting the bloom, its color, or its scent, and praised the elder in the stanza: even so should a sage go about a village.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 4, story 5 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 導師與五百僧人吃飽了，夫妻倆吃飽了，餅卻不見減少，直到把剩下的扔進城門附近的一個洞裏——那洞至今被稱為「餅洞」。謝恩偈誦罷，夫妻二人證入預流果；登上城門的樓梯，他們發現自己已在家中，可以自由地把八十俱胝全都用在佛陀的教法上。僧眾在真諦殿稱讚目犍連時，佛陀說，比丘接近施主之家，當如蜜蜂接近花朵：採蜜而不傷花色、不傷其香；並以偈讚歎長老：智者入村，亦當如是。

title.en: Visakha's Marriage and the Building of Pubbarama
title.zh: 毘舍佉成婚與東園鹿母講堂

region.en: Savatthi and Saketa
region.zh: 舍衛城與沙柯多城

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: Crowned with the garland of the Five Beauties at a riverside festival, the merchant's daughter Visakha married into the heretic household of Migara, answered ten riddling admonitions from her father before the assembled householders, and converted her father-in-law, who took her breast in his mouth and adopted her as his mother. Her jeweled parure, touched by Ananda, was sold for nine crores and spent on the eastern monastery Pubbarama; at its festival she sang that her hundred-thousand-cycle wish was fulfilled.
summary.zh: 毘舍佉於河畔節慶中因五妙相被擲花鬘，嫁入外道米加拉家。公公無故逐她，她於眾長者前一一解釋父親的十條隱語訓誡，自證清白。米加拉聞法證果，以口含媳之乳認她為母。阿難尊者觸過的金蔓花鬘以九億金售予自己，建東園精舍（鹿母講堂）。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: At the Saketa festival called Public Day, Visakha, daughter of the treasurer Dhananjaya, walked unhurried through a sudden storm while her five hundred maidens ran; the Brahmans sent to find a wife for Migara's son reproached her as slothful, and she answered that a king, a state elephant, a monk, and a woman appear to no advantage running, and that a girl is a good for sale whose limbs must be kept whole. Observing her teeth, the Brahmans threw over her the golden garland worth a hundred thousand. Married to Punnavaddhana, she was accused by her father-in-law Migara, a patron of the Naked Ascetics, and bidden to prove herself before the assembled householders by explaining the Ten Admonitions her father had given with hidden meanings: the fire not to be carried out means never tell of a fault you find in husband or father-in-law; the fire not to be brought in means never repeat what neighbors say against them. Cleared of every charge, she won her one condition: that the congregation of monks might be fed in that house.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 4, story 8 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 在娑祇多城名為「公共日」的節慶上，庫藏官財護的女兒維莎訶在突起的風暴中不慌不忙地走著，她的五百位侍女卻奔跑起來；為彌迦羅之子尋訪新娘的婆羅門們斥她懶惰，她答道：國王、御象、僧人與女子奔跑皆有失體面，而女孩是件要完好保存才好出售的商品。婆羅門們觀察她的牙齒，把價值十萬的金花環擲在她的頭上。她嫁給了福增，卻被公公彌迦羅——裸形苦行者的施主——控告，命她當著聚集的居士們解釋父親授以隱義的十條訓誡方證清白：火不可攜出，意思是絕不向人說丈夫或公婆的過失；火不可攜入，意思是絕不把鄰里對他們的非議帶回家中。每一條控告都被洗清，她贏得了唯一的條件：僧團可以在那個家裏受供。

passages.text: When the Naked Ascetics surrounded the house and forbade Migara to come, he sat behind a curtain; but the Buddha declared that beyond curtain, wall, or mountain he could make his voice heard, and as Migara listened, his mind ripened, and he was established in stream-entry. Lifting the curtain, he went to his daughter-in-law and, taking her breast in his mouth, adopted her as his mother, 'To-day henceforth you are my mother'; and thenceforth she was called Mother of Migara. Later the parure worth nine crores that her grandfather's smiths had made was forgotten by her slave-girl and hung by Ananda beside the staircase; Visakha, who would wear nothing her master's hand had touched, could find no buyer rich enough, so she paid its price herself, nine crores more for the building, and nine crores of alms, and raised a thousand-roomed dwelling for the monks at the eastern gate, Pubbarama, with Moggallana fetching whole trees a hundred leagues.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 4, story 8 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 裸形苦行僧們圍住宅邸，禁止彌迦羅前來，他只好坐在帷幕後面；但佛陀宣說，帷幕、牆壁與山嶺之外，他都能讓自己的聲音抵達；彌迦羅聽著聽著，心成熟了，證入預流果。他掀開帷幕走向兒媳，含住她的乳房收她為母：「從今日起，你就是我的母親」；從此她被稱為彌迦羅之母。後來她祖父的工匠們打造的一套價值九俱胝的首飾被婢女遺忘，被阿難掛在樓梯旁；維莎訶不願佩戴師長的手碰過的東西，卻找不到出得起價的買主，便自己付了九俱胝的首飾之價、九俱胝的營建之資、九俱胝的布施，在東門建起千室之居——東園精舍，目犍連自一百由旬外整棵整棵地運來樹木。

passages.text: On the day the monastery was opened, Visakha walked the rounds with children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, singing five stanzas: when shall I give the gift of a monastery? Fulfilled is my desire. The monks wondered if her bile was out of order or if she had gone mad, but the Teacher said she was breathing forth a solemn utterance, and told them her wish made a hundred thousand cycles ago under the Buddha Padumuttara, when she saw his chief benefactress standing as mother to him and asked how a woman might become thus beloved; seven days of alms, a prophecy, and lives of merit had brought her to this hour. Even so, said the Buddha, from a heap of flowers of many kinds a garland-maker makes many garlands: so a mortal should perform many good deeds.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 4, story 8 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 僧院落成之日，維莎訶帶著兒女、孫兒與曾孫巡行，唱出五偈：我何時才能行布施僧院之施？我的心願已成。僧眾疑惑她是不是膽汁失調、是不是瘋了；導師說她正誦出莊嚴的宣言，並告訴他們，這心願是她十萬劫前在無憂佛座下發的：那時她見佛陀的第一女施主如母一般侍奉佛陀，便問一個女子怎樣才能得此殊榮；七日的布施、一段預言與累世功德，把她帶到了這一刻。佛陀又說：如同花鬘師以種種的花堆積成許多花環，世人應當廣行眾善。

title.en: Pandita, the Seven-Year-Old Novice Who Watched the Ditch-Diggers
title.zh: 般達聰穎沙彌——觀掘溝引水而悟

region.en: Savatthi, Jetavana monastery
region.zh: 舍衛城祇園精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: In a former life the poor man Mahaduggata worked all day to feed one monk, and the Buddha himself accepted his bowl while Sakka cooked, so that a rain of seven jewels filled his house; reborn as the merchant's son Pandita, he was ordained at seven and, on the road, watched ditch-diggers lead water, arrow-makers straighten reeds, and carpenters bend wood, and asked to turn back to strive for arahatship. Sakka stilled sun, moon, and birds for him, and while the Buddha questioned Sariputta about food the novice won arahatship in his preceptor's cell.
summary.zh: 窮人摩訶達嘎夫婦打工一天只為供一位比丘齋飯，佛陀親往應供，帝釋化作幫傭下廚，供畢天降七寶盈屋。其後生為般達（智慧之子），七歲出家。路上見掘溝引水、製箭者烤竹弄直、木匠彎木作輪，遂向和尚求回寺修行。帝釋令日月停空、四天王守衛，佛以四問絆住舍利弗，沙彌於房中證阿羅漢。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: At Benares, when the Buddha Kassapa visited with twenty thousand monks, a solicitor of alms urged even the pauper Mahaduggata to pledge food for one monk. The poor man and his wife hired themselves out, he splitting wood, she pounding rice as if she were dancing, and earned five measures of rice; gathering curry leaves by the river, singing for joy, he earned four redfish from a fisherman besides. Sakka, whose throne grew hot, came disguised as a man-of-all-work and cooked the meal, and the Buddha, tender to the poor, placed his own bowl in Mahaduggata's hands while kings begged for it in vain. Sakka's porridge perfumed the whole city, and at a sign from him a rain of the seven kinds of jewels filled the house till the children had to be carried out; the king made Mahaduggata treasurer. Dying at last full of merit, he was reborn in the heaven world, and in the present dispensation was conceived in the house of a merchant of Savatthi.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 6, story 5 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 波羅奈，迦葉佛與兩萬僧眾前來之時，一位乞食勸募者竟連窮人摩訶杜伽多也被勸為一位僧人認捐齋食。窮人與妻子出賣勞力，他劈柴，她搗米如跳舞一般，掙得五斗米；在河邊掬 curry 葉時歡唱，又從漁夫那裏得了四尾紅魚。帝釋寶座發熱，化作雜役為他們做飯；佛陀憐憫窮人，把缽親自放在摩訶杜伽多手中，國王求缽而不可得。帝釋的粥香滿全城，他一示意，七寶之雨灌滿屋宇，孩子們只得抱出去；國王立摩訶杜伽多為庫藏官。壽終之時功德圓滿，他轉生天界，並在今日的教法中入胎於舍衛城一位商人之家。

passages.text: From the day the child was conceived the household's dull and deaf grew wise, and he was named Pandita, Youth Wiseman. At seven he was ordained under the Elder Sariputta, and on the eighth day, walking with his preceptor, he saw by the road a ditch by which men lead water to their fields, arrow-makers heating reeds to straighten them, and carpenters fashioning spokes and rims from senseless logs. 'If they can lead and straighten things that have no reason, surely we who have reason can bring our minds under our own control and strive for arahatship.' He gave back bowl and robe to the amazed elder, asked that only the choicest redfish be brought him, and shut himself in his preceptor's cell. Sakka's throne grew hot again; he commanded the Four Great Kings to guard the four quarters, the moon-deity to hold back the moon, the sun-deity the sun, and stood himself at the door-rope, while the Buddha detained Sariputta on the steps with four questions about food, sensation, form, and contact.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 6, story 5 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 自孩子入胎之日起，家中愚魯的、失聰的都變得聰明，他取名般提達，「少年智者」。七歲在舍利弗長老門下出家；第八天，隨親教師經行時，他看見路邊引水灌田的水溝、燒直箭桿的造箭匠、以無知的圓木製作輻條與車輞的木匠。「無心的東西尚且能引、能直，我們有心之人定能調伏自心，努力證得阿羅漢。」他把缽與衣還給驚訝的長老，請人只送最好的紅魚來，閉門坐於親教師的僧房之中。帝釋的寶座又發熱了；他命四大天王守護四方，月神握住月亮，日神按住太陽，自己執著門繩，而佛陀以食、受、色、觸四問留住了舍利弗。

passages.text: While those four questions were being answered the seven-year-old attained arahatship. Sariputta knocked, the novice came out, took the bowl, and fanned his teacher before eating his own breakfast 'like a freshly blossomed water-lily'; then the moon and sun were released, the Four Kings went home, and the sun vanished strangely from mid-heaven, to the monks' alarm. The Teacher told them what had passed: even a Buddha had left his place to stand guard over his son. Ditch-diggers lead the water, arrow-makers straighten their shafts, carpenters straighten the wood, and the wise control themselves.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 6, story 5 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 就在這四問解答之間，七歲的孩子證得阿羅漢。舍利弗敲門，沙彌出來接缽，先為老師打扇，然後才吃自己的早餐，「如一朵初開的睡蓮」；隨後月亮與太陽獲釋，四大天王歸位，太陽卻怪異地在半空中消失，僧眾大驚。導師告訴他們方才發生的事：連佛陀也離座為自己的兒子守門。掘溝者引水，造箭者直桿，木匠正木，智者調伏自心。

title.en: Patacara Bereft of All Her Family
title.zh: 波吒左囉痛失全家

region.en: Savatthi, Jetavana monastery
region.zh: 舍衛城祇園精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: The beautiful daughter of a Savatthi merchant eloped with her page; in childbirth on the road her husband died of a snakebite, a hawk carried off one son, the river swept away the other, and a storm destroyed her parents' house so that all burned on one pyre. Naked and mad she roared her grief through the city until the Buddha restored her mind and taught that the tears shed through the round of existences outweigh the four oceans; meditating on spilled water she saw rise and fall and won arahatship.
summary.zh: 舍衛城富商之女私奔，途中產子時丈夫被毒蛇咬死；鷹抓走一子，河沖走另一子，風暴摧毀娘家，父母兄弟同日焚於一炬。她赤身瘋癲流浪街頭，佛陀令其復明心志，教以輪迴中流的淚多過四大海水；後以潑水觀生滅，證阿羅漢。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: Patacara, daughter of a merchant worth four hundred millions, was kept on the top floor of a seven-storied palace and loved her own page. When her wedding day with a man of her own rank drew near she smeared her body with red powder, disheveled her hair, and slipped out among the slave-maidens with a water-pot, fleeing to her lover. They lived in a distant village where she pounded rice and drew water, reaping the fruit of her own sin. Twice pregnant, she set out for her parents' house against her husband's will; the first child was born in a clump of bushes by the road. On the second journey a storm burst out of season, and as her birth-pains began her husband climbed an ant-hill for brushwood; a poisonous snake slid out and bit him, and he fell dead where he stood.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 8, story 12 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 缽左左羅，家財四億的商人之女，被關在七層樓閣的頂層，卻愛上了自己的侍從。與門當戶對者的婚期臨近時，她在身上塗滿硃砂，披散頭髮，提著水罐混在婢女中溜出去，奔向情人。他們住在遙遠的村子，她舂米汲水，自食其罪之果。兩度懷孕後，她違著丈夫的心願回娘家去；第一個孩子生在路旁的灌木叢中。第二趟路上，一場不合時節的風暴襲來，產痛開始時丈夫爬上蟻丘拾柴；一條毒蛇滑出咬了他，他當場倒斃。

passages.text: Through wind and rain she bore her second son crouched on the ground, and at dawn took the newborn on her hip, giving the elder boy her finger, and followed her husband's path. At the ant-hill she found his rigid purple body; at the river, swollen knee-deep by the night's rain, she left the older boy on the near bank and carried the younger across on a branch, then turned back for the first. Midstream a hawk, mistaking the child for meat, swooped; three times she screamed, too far to be heard, and the bird flew up with him. The older boy, thinking his mother called, fell into the water and was swept away. Coming on a man from Savatthi she asked after her family, and learned that the storm had leveled her father's seven-storied house, crushing merchant, wife, and son, whose bodies even now burned on one pyre, their smoke in sight.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 8, story 12 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 冒著風雨她蹲在地上生下第二個兒子，黎明時抱起新生兒，把手指給長子牽著，循丈夫的路走去。在蟻丘她看見他僵硬的青紫色屍體；到了河邊——夜雨使水漲到膝深——她把大孩子留在近岸，抱著小的攀枝渡河，再回頭去接大的。半渡之中一隻鷹把孩子誤當肉食撲下；她三次尖叫，太遠了聽不見，鳥把他叼走了。大孩子以為母親在喚他，跌入水中被沖走。遇見一個舍衛城來的人，她打聽家人，得知風暴掀倒了父親的七層樓閣，商人、妻子與兒子全被壓死，屍身此刻正焚在同一堆柴上，煙就在眼前。

passages.text: Instantly she went mad; her clothes fell off unheeded, and naked as at her birth she wandered the roads wailing that both sons were dead, her husband on the road, her mother, father, and brother burning on one pyre, while people yelled 'Crazy fool!' and pelted her with rubbish and clods. The Buddha, seeing one who a hundred thousand cycles ago had wished before the Buddha Padumuttara for preeminence among nuns versed in the Canon, said none but he could be her refuge, and bade her return to her right mind; modesty and shame returned at once, a man threw her his cloak, and she cast herself at the Teacher's feet. He told her she had wept over the loss of sons and dear ones more than the waters of the four oceans, that to one going to the world beyond neither sons nor kith can be a refuge, and she entered the Order. One day, watching water she spilled run a little way and vanish, once farther, once farther yet, she meditated on those who die in youth, in the prime of life, and in old age, and at the Buddha's word won arahatship with the supernormal powers.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 8, story 12 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她當即瘋了；衣裳掉落也不理會，赤身如出生之時一般在大路上遊走，哭喊兩個兒子死了、丈夫死在路上、母親父親與兄弟焚在一堆柴上，人們喊「瘋婆娘！」朝她扔垃圾與土塊。佛陀見她正是十萬劫前在無憂佛座下求作「持經尼中第一」的那人，說唯有他能作她的庇護，便命她恢復心智；慚愧之心即刻回復，一個男人拋來自己的外套，她拜倒在導師腳前。他告訴她，她為失去兒子與親人所流的眼淚，比四大海洋的水還多；走向彼岸的人，兒子與親人都不能作庇護；她便入了僧團。一天，她看見自己潑出的水流出一小段便消失，一次更遠，一次又更遠，便觀察死於幼年、盛年與老年的人，依佛陀之言證得阿羅漢與神通。

title.en: The Novice Sankicca and the Five Hundred Thieves
title.zh: 僧伽羯吒沙彌與五百大盜

region.en: Forest hermitage, Savatthi region
region.zh: 舍衛城郊森林精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: Thirty monks who had vowed never to sleep two together were betrayed to five hundred forest thieves, who demanded a victim for their sacrifice to the wood-spirit. Each monk in turn, senior first, offered his life, but the novice Sankicca insisted on going; the ringleader's sword bent double and split like a palm-leaf on his shoulder, and the whole band begged to be ordained by the child they could not kill.
summary.zh: 三十位比丘曾互約不二人同處，卻被指認給五百林盜，盜賊欲殺一僧祭樹神。從上座起人人爭先赴死，最後沙彌僧伽羯吒執意前往。盜魁一刀劈下，刀彎如馬蹄葉、再劈裂如棕櫚葉，遂棄刀懺悔，五百盜眾求此七歲沙彌為其剃度。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: Thirty monks under the Elder Sankicca's instruction had promised never to stand or sit two together, that each might tend his own meditation, assembling only at the bell. A traitor who had lived two months among them, planning to steal their robes, told a band of five hundred forest thieves where the monks lodged and that a human offering would speed their vow to the forest-spirit. Striking the bell, the ringleader asked for one monk for the sacrifice. The Chief Elder said the decision lay with the senior and offered his life first; the Junior Elder claimed the duty belonged to the junior; and so every one of the thirty, though not brothers of one mother, rose in order saying 'Let none but me go,' until the novice Sankicca silenced them: 'You remain here; I alone will go,' for he was Sariputta's novice and the monks would not bear the reproach of yielding him up.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 8, story 9 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 僧基叉長老座下的三十位僧人約定絕不兩人同起同坐，各修自己的禪觀，只在鈴響時聚集。一個混入兩個月、打算偷僧衣的叛徒，告訴五百人的林中盜匪僧人們的住處，並說以人祭可速成他們對林神的誓願。匪首敲響鈴，索要一位僧人作祭。首席長老說決定權在上座，先獻出自己；次座長老說這職責屬於下座；就這樣三十位僧人——雖非同母兄弟——依次起身說「除我之外誰也不許去」，直到沙彌僧基叉止住他們：「你們留在這裏；我獨自去。」他是舍利弗的沙彌，僧眾不忍背負把他交出的罵名。

passages.text: While the thieves whetted stakes and spread leaves the novice sat apart and entered a trance. The ringleader swung his sword on the boy's shoulder, but the blade bent double, edge striking edge; a second blow split it from hilt to tip like a palm-leaf. No one, the Commentary says, could have killed him then even by piling Mount Sineru on him. Flinging down the useless sword, the chief prostrated himself: men a thousand strong tremble at his band afar off, yet this boy's face shone bright as gold in a crucible. Rising from trance the novice preached that one rid of the corruptions regards existence as a burden laid on the head, whose fall brings joy, not fear, and recited that he who has destroyed the Eye of Existence puts death down like a burden. The chief resolved to become a monk under the boy, and all five hundred bowed and asked the same; with the blades of their own swords and arrows he shaved them, dyed their clothes with yellow earth, and led the five hundred new monks back to the Thirty, whose tears had kept them from their meditations.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 8, story 9 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 盜匪們磨著尖樁、鋪著樹葉時，沙彌獨坐一邊入了定。匪首把劍劈在孩子的肩上，劍卻彎成了兩折，刃口互碰；第二擊把劍從柄到尖劈開如一片棕櫚葉。註釋說，那時即便把須彌山壓在他身上也殺不了他。匪首擲下無用的劍，拜倒在地：千人的隊伍遠遠聽見他的名號都發抖，而這孩子的面容在坩堝裏一般金光燦燦。沙彌出定說法：斷盡煩惱的人視存在如頂在頭上的重擔，擔子落下帶來歡喜而非恐懼，並誦出「滅除存在之眼者，卸下死亡如卸重擔」。匪首決意在這孩子門下出家，五百人一齊頂禮作同樣的請求；他以他們自己的刀劍之刃為他們剃度，以黃土染衣，帶著五百新僧回到那三十人中間——他們的眼淚一直耽誤著他們的禪修。

title.en: The Enchanted Hunter Kukkutamitta
title.zh: 被咒術定身的獵戶鳩鳩陀彌多羅

region.en: Rajagaha, Veluvana monastery
region.zh: 王舍城竹林精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: The hunter Kukkutamitta, finding no deer in his nets but the Buddha's footprint, drew his bow to kill the man he thought had freed his catch, and found himself rooted to the spot; his seven sons, drawn by the same bow, were frozen too, until their mother ran out crying, 'Do not kill my father.' Father-in-law and grandsons alike begged pardon, all fifteen were converted, and the Buddha taught that the hand without a wound may carry poison unharmed.
summary.zh: 獵戶鳩鳩陀彌多羅見網中無獸而有佛足印，誤以為有人放走獵物，張弓欲殺佛陀，卻被定在原地；七個兒子持弓趕來也一一被定。其妻趕到高喊「別殺我父親」，眾人方知是岳父，齊來懺悔。十五人皆得初果。無傷之手可以執毒而不受其害。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: A rich man's daughter at Rajagaha saw from her window the hunter Kukkutamitta driving in a cartload of venison and followed him out of the city in soiled clothes till he took her on his cart; her parents held a funeral feast for her as one dead. She bore him seven sons and married them off. One day the Buddha, seeing that the hunter, his seven sons, and their wives were ready for conversion, went to the place where the nets were spread, and left his footprint on a net before sitting down in the shade. Kukkutamitta, finding not one animal in five hundred snares and five hundred spears, reasoned that someone was freeing his catch, and when he came upon the Teacher, drew his bow to kill him. The Buddha let him draw but did not let him shoot: the hunter stood as if his ribs were shattered, arrow drawn, unable to loose or lower it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 9, story 8 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 王舍城一位富商之女從窗中看見獵人鳩鳩多彌陀趕著一車鹿肉，便穿著弄髒的衣服跟出城去，直到他把她抱上車；父母為她辦了葬宴，當作死了。她為他生了七個兒子並為他們娶妻。一天，佛陀見獵人、他的七個兒子與兒媳們時機已熟，便去網羅布設之處，在網上留下足印，然後在樹蔭下坐下。鳩鳩多彌陀見五百處陷阱與五百支矛竟一無所獲，推想有人在放他的獵物；遇見導師時，他拉弓要殺。佛陀讓他拉弓卻不許他放箭：獵人立在那裏，如同肋骨碎裂，箭已拉滿，既放不出也放不下。

passages.text: When the sons came seeking their father and saw him standing enchanted, they took him for an enemy and drew their bows, and were likewise rooted to the spot. The mother, going out with the daughters-in-law, saw beyond the bows the Teacher, and screamed, 'Do not kill my father; do not kill my father!' Husband and sons understood at once what a wicked deed they had about to do, their hearts softened, and at the Teacher's permission they lowered their bows and begged pardon; all fifteen were established in the Fruit of Conversion, and the hunter gave up the taking of life. The monks wondered how a stream-enterer could have handed her husband bow and arrows all those years; the Buddha answered that she acted only to obey her husband's command, never thinking he would take life, for if a man's hand be free from wounds he may carry poison and it cannot harm him; no evil befalls him who does no evil. Their past merits as builders of the Buddha Kassapa's shrine, given not in coin but with their very selves, ripened now into this conversion.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 9, story 8 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 兒子們來尋父親，見他站著被懾住，以為是敵人，拉弓便射，也同樣定在原地。母親帶著兒媳們出來，越過滿弓看見了導師，尖叫道：「不要殺我的父親！不要殺我的父親！」丈夫與兒子們頓時明白自己正要行多大的惡，心軟了下來；得導師之允，他們放下弓箭求饒；十五人全部證入預流果，獵人放棄了殺生。僧眾疑惑一位預流者怎麼多年來一直替丈夫遞弓遞箭；佛陀答道，她只是遵從丈夫的命令，從不曾想他會殺生，因為手上無傷的人即便捧著毒藥也傷不到自己；不行惡者不遭惡。他們前世為迦葉佛的塔廟捐資——不是以錢財，而是以自身——的功德，如今成熟為這次度化。

title.en: Anathapindika and the Goddess of the Fourth Gate
title.zh: 給孤獨長者與第四門的守護神

region.en: Savatthi, house of Anathapindika
region.zh: 舍衛城給孤獨長者宅

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: The gate-goddess of Anathapindika's house could not endure the radiance of the Buddha and his monks and, finding her patron now poor, urged him to abandon his giving and rebuild his fortune. Driven from the house with her children, she found no shelter anywhere, and by Sakka's advice recovered fifty-four crores of the merchant's scattered wealth to atone; then the Teacher forgave her, teaching that the evildoer sees happiness until his deed ripens, and the good man sees evil until his does.
summary.zh: 給孤獨長者家第四門的守護神不堪佛陀僧眾威德，趁長者家道中落，夜半現身勸他停止布施、重理家業。被長者驅逐後無處棲身，依帝釋之計尋回五十四億失散之財贖罪，懺悔後蒙佛赦宥。惡人未熟果時見樂，善人未熟果時見苦。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: Anathapindika, who had spent fifty-four crores on Jetavana alone, went three times a day to wait on the Teacher, never empty-handed: porridge in the morning, medicines after breakfast, perfumes and garments at evening. But eighteen crores lent to traders went unpaid, and eighteen crores buried by the river were swept into the sea, so that he grew gradually poor, giving as before but with bird-feed and sour gruel. The Teacher told him not to be disturbed: pure intention cannot give the Buddhas coarse food, and once, in the time of Velama, he had stirred all India with rich offerings and won not a single person to the Three Refuges. When the Teacher and his disciples entered the house, the goddess who dwelt above the fourth gate could not endure the intensity of their goodness, and resolved, now that the merchant was poor and would listen, to detach him from his allegiance.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 9, story 4 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 給孤獨長者——單在祇園便花費五十四俱胝——每日三次前往侍奉導師，從不空手：清晨是粥，早餐後是藥，傍晚是香料與衣物。但借給商人的十八俱胝未獲償還，藏於河邊的十八俱胝被沖入大海，他漸漸貧窮，布施如舊，卻只能以鳥食與酸粥供養。導師告訴他不要憂擾：清淨的心念獻不出佛陀眼中的粗食；往昔韋羅摩的時代，他以豐盛供養震動全印度，卻不曾度一人皈依三寶。導師與弟子入宅之時，住在第四道門上空的天女受不了那善的光強，決意趁商人貧窮、肯聽話之時，讓他脫離忠誠。

passages.text: By night she stood poised in the air in his chamber and warned him that he would soon lack food and clothing if he went on feeding 'the monk Gotama'; he must give up lavish giving and mind his business. 'Begone,' said the merchant; 'though a hundred thousand like you should try, you could not move me from my course.' Unable to withstand the word of a Noble Disciple, she left with her children, but found lodging nowhere; the city's tutelary deity and the Four Great Kings refused to plead for her, and Sakka, though he would not speak to the merchant, told her the way: recover the eighteen crores lent to the traders, the eighteen swept into the ocean, and a third eighteen without an owner, and fill the empty storerooms. She did all this, then stood radiant in the chamber, begging pardon as the blind, stupid goddess of the fourth gate. Anathapindika led her to the Teacher, where she fell upon her face, and the Buddha forgave her: even an evildoer sees happiness while his deed is unripe, and even a good man sees evil while his is unripe; when they ripen, each sees his own fruit.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 9, story 4 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 夜裏她凌空立於他的寢室警告他：若繼續供養「喬達摩僧人」，他將衣食無著；他必須停止豪奢的布施，打理自己的生意。「走開，」商人說；「縱使一萬個你這樣的來試，也動搖不了我的道。」她敵不過聖弟子的言語，帶著孩子離開了，卻無處容身；城的護法神與四大天王都不肯替她說情；帝釋雖不肯與商人說話，卻給她指了路：討回借給商人的十八俱胝，沖入大海的十八俱胝，以及無主的第三個十八俱胝，把空倉填滿。她一一照辦，然後光彩煥發地立在寢室中，自認是第四門那個又盲又蠢的天女，請求饒恕。給孤獨帶她去見導師，她俯伏在地；佛陀饒恕了她：作惡者在其業未熟時仍見安樂，行善者在其業未熟時亦見苦；業熟之時，各見其果。

title.en: Kundadhana, the Monk Followed by a Phantom Woman
title.zh: 摳那達那——被幻影女子跟隨的比丘

region.en: Savatthi, Jetavana monastery
region.zh: 舍衛城祇園精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: From the day Kundadhana ordained, a female form followed him whom he alone could not see: villagers fed 'our female friend,' the king staked out his cell and saw her vanish upstairs, and the monks cried 'corrupt monk!' The Buddha traced it to a goddess who, in the dispensation of Kassapa, took a woman's form behind a monk and ruined his good name, and paid for it in Avici; he bade Kundadhana keep silence like a broken gong, for by silence he would win Nibbana.
summary.zh: 摳那達那尊者出家之日起，身後即有一女子身影隨行，唯他本人看不見：村人連他的「女朋友」也供養，國王埋伏其房前忽見忽失，僧眾罵他「破戒」。佛陀追溯：過去迦葉佛時，一位天神化作女身跟在比丘身後毀其名譽，因此墮阿鼻地獄一劫。佛令其如破鑼般默然，以寂靜證涅槃。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: From the day Elder Kundadhana became a monk a female form accompanied him wherever he went; he himself never saw her, but everybody else did, so that on his alms-round the villagers gave him one portion saying 'Reverend Sir, this is for you,' and another saying 'And this is for our female friend.' Long before, in the dispensation of Kassapa, the same being, then a goddess of the Thirty-three, had seen two companion-monks as close as brothers going together to the Hall of Discipline, and thought in her folly to part them. When one stepped into a thicket, she assumed the form of a woman and followed him out, arranging her hair and undergarment; the waiting monk saw, though the elder did not, and accused him. Though the goddess later confessed the trick to the accuser, the pair's friendship was broken, and for that deed the goddess was reborn in Avici and suffered through an interval between two Buddhas.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 10, story 4 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 自軍達長老出家之日起，一個女性的身影無論他去哪裏都跟隨著他；他自己看不見，別人卻都看得見，以至於他乞食時村民們給他一份說「長老，這是給您的」，再給一份說「這是給我們的女朋友的」。很久以前，在迦葉佛的教法中，同一個生靈——那時是三十三天的天女——看見兩位如兄弟般親密的同行僧人一同走向律堂，愚癡地想把二人拆開。當其中一人走進樹叢時，她化作女人之形跟在他身後，整理頭髮與內衣；在外面等候的僧人看見了——長老卻沒有——便指控他。雖然天女後來向告發者承認了詭計，兩人的友誼卻破裂了；因那一業，天女墮入阿鼻地獄，在兩佛之間的空劫裏受盡了苦。

passages.text: Reborn at last as a man of Savatthi, he ordained, and the phantom woman came with him, so that the monks asked Anathapindika and Visakha to expel the unchaste monk, then appealed to the king, who went by night to surround the elder's lodging. When Kundadhana stepped out, the king saw the woman behind him; upstairs, she was gone. Twice more the king made the elder step out and saw her appear and vanish, and concluded it must be a phantom; instead of expelling him he invited him to take his Four Requisites from the palace alone, to the monks' fury. Stung, Kundadhana retorted that they were the corrupt ones, consorting with women, and the monks reported him. The Teacher asked why he answered slander with slander when he had seen nothing, told him the whole past story, and bade him never again hold converse with the monks: make no sound, even as a brass plate shattered at the rim, for so you will attain Nibbana. Speak not harshly to anyone, for angry words bring trouble; silent as a broken gong, you have already reached Nibbana.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 10, story 4 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 她最後轉生為舍衛城的一個男子，出家之後幽靈的女人也跟著來了；僧眾請給孤獨與維莎訶逐出這個行不淨者，又向國王申告，國王夜裏前去圍住長老的住處。軍達一跨出門，國王便看見他身後的女人；上樓去看，她不見了。國王又兩次讓長老跨出門，都看見她現身又消失，便斷定這必是幽靈；他不但不逐他，還邀他只從王宮領取四事供養——僧眾大怒。受了刺激的軍達反唇相譏，說他們才是行不淨的、與女人廝混的；僧眾便告到導師那裏。導師問他為何以誹謗回敬誹謗，既然他什麼也沒看見；把整個往事告訴他，命他從此不要再與僧眾交談：不出一聲，如邊緣破損的銅盤一般，如此你將證得涅槃。莫向任何人說粗暴的話，粗暴之言招禍患；寂靜如破鑼，你已經抵達涅槃。

title.en: The Death of Moggallana the Great
title.zh: 大目犍連之死

region.en: Black Rock forest, Rajagaha; Veluvana
region.zh: 王舍城黑岩林、竹林精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: Heretics hired thieves to kill Moggallana, whose preaching of the fate of the dead in heaven and hell drew away their patrons. Twice he slipped through a keyhole and soared through the roof, but in the third month the force of an old deed held him: beaten and pounded to grains of rice, he gathered himself by meditation, flew to the Buddha to announce his Nibbana, and passed away at Black Rock. The Buddha told how, to please a faithless wife, he had once lured his own parents into a forest and beaten them to death.
summary.zh: 外道僱盜賊殺害目犍連，因其宣說天獄果報令信施流向佛門。尊者兩度穿鎖孔、破屋頂飛脫，第三個月宿業現前而受擒，被肢解捶骨至米粒。他以禪定裹身飛回向佛辭行，於黑岩林入滅。佛陀說其過去生為取悅妻子，誘父母入林而擊殺之。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely. Contains the violent death of a disciple and parricide.

passages.text: The heretics met together and agreed that all the rich offerings to the monk Gotama had come about through Moggallana the Great, who visited heaven and hell and told men on earth what deeds win such glory and what deeds win such torment. 'If we kill him, the gifts will fall to us.' They hired thieves with a thousand pieces of money and sent them to Black Rock. The elder, knowing his abode was surrounded, slipped out through the keyhole; the next day he broke through the circular peak of the house and soared into the air; month after month the thieves failed. But when the third month came the elder felt the compelling force of the evil deed he had done in a former existence, and made no attempt to escape. Caught at last, he was torn limb from limb and his bones pounded to grains of rice; then, swathing himself in meditation as with a cloth, he flew through the air to the Buddha, announced that he was about to pass into Nibbana, preached a last discourse, performed such miracles as Sariputta had shown, and passed away in Black Rock forest.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 10, story 7 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 外道們聚在一起商定：僧人喬達摩得到的豐厚供養，全靠大目犍連——他下地獄上天堂，把什麼業得榮耀、什麼業得苦刑講給世人聽。「殺了他，供養便歸我們。」他們以千金僱了盜賊，送往黑岩。長老自知住處被圍，從鑰匙孔中遁出；次日他破開屋頂的圓頂凌空而去；一個月又一個月，盜賊無功。但到了第三個月，長老感到前世所造惡業的牽引之力，便不再逃避。他終於被擒，被活活拆散肢體，骨頭搗成米粒；然後他以禪定裹身如以布裹身，凌空飛到佛陀那裏，說自己即將入涅槃，作了最後的開示，現出如舍利弗所現的神變，在黑岩林中寂滅。

passages.text: The thieves, boasting over drink, betrayed themselves, and King Ajatasattu had five hundred heretics and five hundred thieves buried waist-deep in pits, burned, and plowed to bits. In the Hall of Truth the monks said Moggallana had met a death he did not deserve, but the Buddha answered that only in this life did it look undeserved: in exact conformity with his former deed. Once, a devoted son who served his parents with his own hands married a wife who could not bear the old people, and scattered clay and scum about the house to make them seem filthy. At last he told his blind parents there were kinsfolk who wished to see them, handed his father the reins in the deep forest, and, yelling like thieves, beat his mother and father to death. For that monstrous sin he burned in hell for numberless hundreds of thousands of years, and in a hundred successive existences was beaten and pounded to pieces in the same manner. Whosoever visits punishment on the offenseless, said the Teacher, quickly comes to one of ten evil states, and at the dissolution of the body goes to hell.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 10, story 7 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 盜賊們飲酒自誇，露出馬腳；阿闍世王把五百外道與五百盜賊埋入齊腰的坑中焚燒，又用犁犁碎。真諦殿中僧眾說目犍連死得不應如此，佛陀答道，唯有此生看來不應如此；那與他前世之業嚴絲合縫。往昔，一位親手奉養父母的孝子娶了容不下老人的妻子，便把黏土與污穢撒滿房屋，讓老人顯得骯髒。最後他告訴失明的父母，有親戚想見他們，把韁繩交給父親，在幽深的森林裏如盜賊般呼喊，把父母活活打死。因這滔天之罪，他在地獄中焚燒了無數十萬年，並在一百個連續的生存裏被同樣地毆打搗碎。導師說：凡對無過者施以刑罰的，速入十惡趣之一，身壞命終墮入地獄。

title.en: Santati, the Adorned Minister Who Passed into Nibbana in the Air
title.zh: 珊達帝大臣——嚴飾而於空中入滅

region.en: Savatthi, Jetavana monastery
region.zh: 舍衛城祇園精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: Santati, given a week of royal pleasures and a dancing woman after pacifying the frontier, was drunk on the seventh day when the dancer died mid-performance before his eyes; his week of liquor vanished like a drop of water on a hot potsherd, he went to the Teacher, and at a single stanza won arahatship. Rising to seven palm-trees' height he rehearsed his merit as a dharma-crier under the Buddha Vipassi, then self-cremated in the air, and the Buddha declared even the adorned man a Brahman, a hermit, a monk.
summary.zh: 珊達帝大臣平亂凱旋，王賜七日之樂與舞伎。第七日酒醉觀舞，舞伎絕食七日炫技，忽然倒斃。他七日酒意如水滴落紅熱瓦上瞬間消失，向佛求皈，一偈之下證阿羅漢，升至七棵棕櫚之高處自述前世弘法功德，於空中自焚入滅，捨利如茉莉花落下。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: Santati returned from suppressing disorder on the frontier of King Pasenadi Kosala, and the delighted king gave him his kingdom for seven days and a woman who danced and sang. For seven days Santati steeped himself in liquor, and on the seventh rode the state elephant to the baths, adorned with every adornment, nodding a salute to the Teacher as they passed. The Buddha smiled and told Ananda that this very day the drunken sot, so adorned, would hear one stanza and attain arahatship, then pass into Nibbana seated seven palm-trees above the earth. Heretics and believers marked the words, the one to catch him in a lie, the other to see his glory. At the bathing-place the dancer, who had fasted seven days to show her grace, was cut through by knife-like pains in her belly as she performed, and died before his eyes with open mouth and open eyes.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 10, story 9 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 善帝平定了憍薩羅國邊疆的叛亂回朝，大喜的國王把王國贈他七日，還賜一位歌舞女子。善帝七日沉醉酒鄉，第七日乘御象前往浴場，盛裝打扮，經過導師時點頭致意。佛陀微笑，告訴阿難：今日這醉漢盛裝聽一首偈便證阿羅漢，然後離地七棵棕櫚之高，於空中結跏入滅。外道與信眾都記下了這句話，一個要抓他的把柄，一個要看他的榮耀。浴場上，那為顯身段禁食七日的舞女表演之際，腹部如刀絞的劇痛襲來，當著他的面張著嘴、瞪著眼死去。

passages.text: 'Look to the lady!' cried Santati. 'She is dead, master.' At those words the liquor of the whole week vanished like a drop of water on a red-hot potsherd, and overwhelmed with sorrow he went in the evening to the one man he knew could extinguish it. The Teacher told him that on countless occasions this woman had died in this very manner and he had wept tears more abundant than the four great oceans, and spoke of what is past, letting nothing lie before, and nothing between be grasped. At the stanza's end Santati attained arahatship with the supernormal powers; and since heretics stood ready to mock, the Teacher bade him rehearse his past merit, not on the ground but poised in the air. Santati rose palm-tree by palm-tree to the height of seven and, seated cross-legged, told how under the Buddha Vipassi, ninety-one cycles ago, he had gone about proclaiming the Three Jewels on foot, then on a horse, then a chariot, then on an elephant decked in jewels, for eighty thousand years, sandal fragrance diffusing from his body and lotus fragrance from his mouth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 10, story 9 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「看住那位女士！」善帝喊道。「大王，她死了。」這句話一出口，一整週的酒如一滴水落在燒紅的瓦片上般消失；他被憂傷壓倒，傍晚去見那唯一能熄滅它的人。導師告訴他，這個女子已經無數次以這樣的方式死去，他為她流的淚比四大海洋還多，並說起已逝的過去，無物存於之前，無物可執於其間。偈頌結束，善帝證得阿羅漢與神通；因外道們正等著嘲弄，導師命他不立於地，凌空複述自己宿世的功德。善帝一棵棕櫚接一棵棕櫚地升起，到第七棵的高度結跏趺坐，講述九十一劫前毗婆尸佛的時代，他曾徒步、騎馬、乘車、乘寶象宣揚三寶達八萬年，身放檀香，口出蓮香。

passages.text: As he finished, seated cross-legged in the air, he applied himself to meditation on the element of fire, entered trance, and passed straightway into Nibbana: flames burst from his body and consumed flesh and blood, and his relics floated down like jasmine flowers into a white cloth the Teacher spread. They were enshrined at a crossing of four highways, that reverence there might yield the populace much merit. When the monks debated whether one who died adorned and in state should be called hermit or Brahman, the Teacher declared he was both, and spoke the stanza: even though a man be richly adorned, if he walk in peace, quiet, subdued, restrained, and chaste, and injure no living being, that man is a Brahman, that man is a hermit, that man is a monk.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 10, story 9 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 講述完畢，他凌空結跏趺坐，觀火界而入定，當即入滅：火焰從他身中迸出，燒盡血肉，舍利如茉莉花瓣飄落，落入導師展開的白布之中。舍利被供養在四衢路口，使前往禮敬的民眾廣積功德。僧眾議論盛裝而死、於莊嚴之中入滅的人該稱沙門還是婆羅門，導師宣說他兩者都是，並說偈：縱然盛裝嚴飾，若行於寂靜、調伏、收攝、淨持梵行而不害一眾生者，彼是婆羅門，彼是沙門，彼是比丘。

title.en: Angulimala, the Robber with the Garland of Fingers
title.zh: 指鬘外道安古利馬拉

region.en: Highway near Savatthi; Jetavana
region.zh: 舍衛城郊大道、祇園精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: The robber Angulimala, who had worn a garland of his victims' fingers, stalked the Buddha walking alone down the haunted road, yet could not catch him, and at the riddle 'I stand still' he threw his sword into the chasm and was ordained. King Pasenadi came out with five hundred horse to hunt him and found him a yellow-robed elder. later, pelted with clods and stones on his alms-round, he bore the first installment of karma that might have burned him in hell for thousands of years.
summary.zh: 戴人指鬘的劫匪安古利馬拉在凶路上追趕獨行的佛陀，卻怎麼也追不上；在「我已止息」之謎前棄劍懺悔出家。波斯匿王率五百騎出城緝捕，見到的卻是披黃衣的尊者。後來他托缽時被擲石塊土坷，血流破缽，佛陀教他安忍：此是地獄數千年苦報的先付。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely. Contains a serial killer's conversion.

passages.text: In the realm of Pasenadi Kosala lived the robber Finger-Garland, Angulimala, so merciless that villages he harried were villages no more and towns towns no more, and he slew man after man and wore their fingers as a garland. Herdsmen and farmers ran three times to warn the Buddha walking alone into that road, and three times he went on in silence. Angulimala saw him coming and thought to deprive this single unaccompanied monk of life; but though he ran with all his might while the Buddha walked at his usual gait, he could not close the distance. 'Stand still, monk!' he cried. 'I stand still, Angulimala; do you also stand still.' Asked how a walking man could claim to stand still, the Buddha answered that he stood steadfast forever, merciful to all living beings, while Angulimala was merciless to living beings.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 13, story 6 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 憍薩羅的波斯匿王境內住著強盜「指鬘」阿闍世那人——兇殘至極，被他劫掠的村落不再是村落，城鎮不再是城鎮，他殺人無數，以他們的手指作鬘佩在身上。牧人與農夫三次跑去警告獨行於那條路上的佛陀，三次佛陀默默前行。指鬘望見他來，想奪取這獨身僧人的性命；但他全力奔跑，佛陀卻以平常的步幅行走，他就是追不上。「站住，僧人！」他喊道。「我已站住了，指鬘；你也站住吧。」被問及走路的人怎能自稱站住，佛陀答道：我永遠站定，慈念一切眾生；而你對眾生無慈。

passages.text: The robber flung sword and weapons over the precipice, prostrated himself, and begged for ordination; the word 'Come, monk!' sufficed. Soon a hue and cry rose at King Pasenadi's palace gate, and the king set out with five hundred horses to subdue the outlaw. At the grove the Buddha asked what he would do if he saw such a man shaven, yellow-robed, abstaining from killing, stealing, and lying. 'We would salute him, seat him, provide for him,' said the king, 'but how could one so wicked be so restrained?' Then the Teacher stretched forth his hand: 'This, mighty king, is Angulimala!' The king's hair stood on end, but on the Buddha's reassurance he honored the elder, marveling that he who could not subdue the robber with rod or sword had been tamed without either.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 13, story 6 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 強盜把劍與武器拋下山崖，俯伏在地，乞求出家；一句「來吧，比丘！」便足夠了。不久波斯匿王的宮門前響起緝拿的呼聲，國王率五百騎出城征討大盜。在林園佛陀問他：若見這樣一個人——剃除鬚髮、披黃衣、離殺離盜離妄語——你們當如何？「我們當向他行禮、讓座、供養，」國王說，「可這樣兇惡的人怎麼可能如此調伏？」導師便伸出手：「大王，這就是指鬘！」國王毛髮倒豎；得佛陀的寬慰後，他恭敬長老，驚異不以刑杖與刀劍竟能如此馴服強盜。

passages.text: On his alms-round the new elder saw a woman in the agonies of childbirth and pitied how living beings suffer; sent back with a solemn utterance, he spoke over her, 'Since I was born of the Noble Birth I am not conscious of having deliberately deprived any living being of life; if this be true, may health come to you,' and she was delivered in health. In time he won arahatship. But one morning, as he made his unbroken round of Savatthi, one man threw a clod of earth that struck his body, another a stick, another a stone, till he came to the Buddha with broken head, streaming blood, broken bowl, and rent mantle. 'Endure, Brahman, endure!' said the Teacher; 'you are suffering here and now the fruit of deeds for which you might have been tormented in hell for many thousands of years.' Whose past misdeeds are covered by good deeds, he later said of him, illumines this world as the moon freed from a cloud.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 13, story 6 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 乞食途中，新戒的長老遇見一位產難的婦人，憐憫眾生之苦；奉導師莊嚴之語而回，為她誦道：「自我受聖生以來，我不曾故意奪取任何眾生的性命；若此為真，願你得安產」，她果然平安分娩。不久他證得阿羅漢。但一天早晨，他在舍衛城次第乞食之時，一人擲來土塊擊中其身，另一人擲來棍棒，又一人擲來石頭，直到他頭破血流、缽破衣裂地來到佛陀面前。「忍受吧，婆羅門，忍受吧！」導師說；「你此刻正受的，本該是你在地獄裏受幾萬年的業報。」凡以善行覆蓋宿惡之人，他後來這樣說他，如脫雲之月，光照此世。

title.en: The Twin Miracle at the Foot of Ganda's Mango-Tree
title.zh: 健陀芒果樹下之雙神變

region.en: Savatthi, foot of Ganda's mango-tree
region.zh: 舍衛城健陀芒果樹下

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: When Pindola won a suspended sandalwood bowl by flying with a mountain under his foot and was rebuked, the heretics challenged the Buddha to out-miracle them; he named the full-moon day, four months off at Savatthi, and they pursued him the whole way. There he sprang a mango-tree from a seed at the gardener's hand, refused the miracle-offers of his mightiest disciples, and walking a jeweled walk in the sky sent fire and water streaming from every pore of his body before ascending in three strides to preach the Abhidhamma to his mother.
summary.zh: 賓度羅跋羅墮阇飛空取缽遭佛訶責，外道遂向佛陀挑戰神變。佛約定四個月後在舍衛城。屆時他以園丁所供芒果一粒種出大樹，謝絕目犍連、蓮花色等弟子請求代現神變，於寶徑上經行，全身毛孔同時出火出水，展現雙神變，隨後三步跨越雪山至三十三天為母說阿毘達磨三個月。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: A treasurer of Rajagaha suspended a red-sandalwood bowl sixty cubits in the air and proclaimed that whoever flew up to take it should make a disciple of him. Six rival teachers strove in vain for six days; on the seventh the Elder Pindolabharadvaja, urged by Moggallana, encircled the flat rock three leagues wide with the tip of his foot, raised it like a silk-cotton tuft, and walked seven times about Rajagaha with it, till the terrified citizens hid under winnowing-baskets. He took the bowl filled with sweet foods; the Teacher rebuked him, had the bowl ground to sandal-paste, and forbade his disciples to work wonders for trifles. The heretics proclaimed that Gotama had banned miracles, and would now perform them with him; the Buddha answered that as a king alone may eat the fruit of his own garden, so the precept bound his disciples but not himself, and named the full-moon of Asalhi, four months hence, near Savatthi.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 14, story 2 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 王舍城一位庫藏官把一隻紅檀木缽懸在六十肘高的空中，宣告誰能飛上去取缽，便拜誰為師。六派外道苦鬥六日而無功；第七日，受目犍連慫恿的賓度羅跋羅墮闍長老，以腳尖挑起三由旬寬的平巖，如舉絲棉絮一般，繞王舍城七匝，嚇得市民躲進簸箕之下。他取了盛著甜食的缽；導師斥責他，命人把缽磨成檀香粉，並禁止弟子們為瑣屑之事顯神通。外道們宣揚喬達摩禁了神通，要與他鬥法；佛陀答道，如同唯有國王能吃自家園林的果子，戒律約束弟子卻不約束他本人，並定下四個月後舍衛城附近的頞沙月望日。

passages.text: The heretics pursued him town by town the whole four months, crying that he was running away, and a multitude followed to see. At Savatthi on the appointed day the gardener Ganda offered the Teacher a ripe mango meant for the king; the Buddha drank its sherbet, had the seed planted, washed his hands over it, and instantly a mango-tree fifty cubits high stood there with fruit on one branch, known ever after as Ganda's Mango-tree, while Sakka's winds tore up the heretics' pavilion, scorched and drenched them, and drove the heretic leader Purana to drown himself. Before the miracle, disciples begged to perform it: Gharami would turn the earth to water, Culla Anathapindika would thunder as Maha Brahma, the novice Cira would carry Mount Sineru, Moggallana would crunch Sineru between his teeth and walk the air holding the earth like an umbrella; the nun Uppalavanna would approach as a Universal Monarch. 'I know your power,' said the Teacher to each; 'but this basket of flowers was not prepared for you. My burden is like none other's.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 14, story 2 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 外道們整整四個月鎮接鎮地追著他，喊他落荒而逃，群眾也跟著去看。舍衛城約定之日，園丁甘陀把本要獻給國王的熟芒果供給導師；佛陀喝下它的甜汁，命人埋下果核，在上面洗手，剎那間一株五十肘高的芒果樹立在眼前，一枝上結著果——後世稱之為甘陀的芒果樹——而帝釋的風撕碎了外道的亭閣，灼燒澆淋他們，外道首領普蘭那投河自盡。神變之前，弟子們請求由他們來行：伽羅彌要使大地化為水，小給孤獨要如大梵天作獅子吼，沙彌吉祥要扛起須彌山，目犍連要以齒嚼碎須彌山、如撐傘般提著大地行於空中，比丘尼蓮花色要以轉輪王之姿現身。「我知道你們的能力，」導師對每人說；「但這籃花不是為你們備下的。我的擔子沒有別人的像它。」

passages.text: Then before a company thirty-six leagues wide the Teacher performed the Twin Miracle: flames of fire streamed from the upper part of his body and water from the lower, then the reverse; fire and water poured from right and left eyes, ears, nostrils, shoulders, hands, sides, feet, and every pore of his body, in six colors, arching each world-system, while a counterpart of himself walked, stood, sat, or lay opposite him as he moved. Preaching between wonders, he read the heart of everyone in the multitude. Then, as past Buddhas had done, he rose in three strides, mountains huddling under his feet, sixty-eight hundred thousand leagues, to the Yellowstone Throne in the World of the Thirty-three, and for the three months of the rains expounded the Abhidhamma Pitaka to his mother, come down from the Palace of the Tusita gods, while the multitude camped below and Moggallana preached and Culla Anathapindika fed them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 14, story 2 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 於是在寬三十六由旬的大眾面前，導師行雙神變：火從上身流出，水從下身流出，繼而反轉；火與水從雙眼、雙耳、雙鼻孔、肩、手、脅、足與全身毛孔中流出，作六色，環繞每一世界系，而他移動時，一個與他相對應的分身同樣行走、站立、端坐或臥。他在神變之間說法，讀出大眾中每個人的心。然後，如過去諸佛所行，他三步跨出——群山在腳下縮聚，六萬八千由旬——升至三十三天的黃石寶座，在三個月的雨安居中為自兜率天宮下來的母親講說阿毗達磨藏，民眾在下面紮營，目犍連說法，小給孤獨供養飲食。

title.en: Mara Possesses the Villagers and the Buddha Feasts on Joy
title.zh: 魔附村民，佛以法喜為食

region.en: Brahman village of Pancasala
region.zh: 五沙門婆羅門村

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: Mara took possession of every body in the Brahman village of Pancasala, so that the Buddha's bowl came out clean as if washed, without a spoonful of rice. Mocked at the gate and told to enter the village again, the Teacher answered that though he received nothing today he would spend the day in the bliss of joy, like the Bright Gods, and spoke the stanza on living happily possessing nothing.
summary.zh: 魔王附身五沙門村全村之人，佛陀托缽一勺飯也未得，缽空如洗。魔羅在村口譏嘲並勸他再入村，欲令村人拍手訕笑。佛陀答：今日雖無所得，我仍將住於法喜之樂，如光音天人般自在，並誦出「無所有而快樂住」一偈。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: The Teacher, perceiving that five hundred maidens of the Brahman village of Pancasala had the faculties for conversion, took up his residence nearby. On a festival day the maidens bathed in the river, adorned themselves with rich apparel and jewels, and set out for the village, and the Teacher entered it on his alms-round. But Mara took possession of the bodies of all the inhabitants, with the result that the Teacher received not so much as a spoonful of boiled rice. As he left with his bowl clean as if just washed, Mara stood at the gate and asked, 'Monk, you received no alms?' 'Embodiment of evil, why have you so wrought that I should receive no alms?' 'Very well, Reverend Sir, enter the village again,' said Mara, planning to make the possessed villagers clap their hands, laugh in his face, and mock him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 15, story 2 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 導師見般闍薩羅婆羅門村的五百位少女具有可度之根，便在近處住了下來。節日那天，少女們在河中沐浴，盛裝佩寶，結伴回村；導師入村乞食。魔羅卻附上了全體村民的身，以致導師連一勺熟飯也沒乞到。他帶著乾淨得如同剛洗過的缽離村時，魔羅站在村口問：「僧人，你沒乞到齋飯吧？」「惡魔之身啊，你為何這樣做，使我乞不到齋飯？」「很好，長老，請再進村一次吧，」魔羅說，打算讓被附身的村民拍手、當面大笑、嘲弄他。

passages.text: At that moment the five hundred maidens reached the gate, saluted the Teacher, and stood respectfully on one side. Mara pressed his point: seeing that he had not received a morsel, he must be oppressed with the pangs of hunger. The Teacher answered that embodiment of evil that though today they received nothing, they would spend the day in the bliss of joy, like the Great Brahma in the Heaven of the Bright Gods, and spoke the stanza: Oh, happily let us live, we who possess nothing; let us feed on joy, like the Bright Gods. To possess nothing, and to feast on joy, is the wealth Mara cannot touch.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 15, story 2 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 那一刻五百位少女來到村口，向導師行禮，恭恭敬敬地立在一旁。魔羅窮追不捨：既然一點食物也沒乞到，他必定被飢餓之苦壓迫著。導師回答惡魔之身：雖然今天沒有乞得食物，我們卻要在喜悅的快樂中度過這一天，如光音天的大梵天，並說偈：我們無所有而快樂地活著；如光音諸天，以喜悅為食。無所有而以喜悅為饗宴，是魔羅觸不到的財富。

title.en: The King of Kosala Thrice Defeated by His Nephew
title.zh: 憍薩羅王三敗於其甥

region.en: Village of Kasika, Kosala; Jetavana
region.zh: 憍薩羅國迦西迦村、祇園精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: King Pasenadi of Kosala fought his nephew Ajatasattu near the village of Kasika and was defeated three times, until he took to his bed refusing food, saying there was no use living if he could not subdue that milk-faced youth. The monks reported it, and the Buddha declared that victory breeds hatred and defeat brings suffering, and spoke the stanza on the man who renounces both victory and defeat and lives in tranquillity.
summary.zh: 憍薩羅國波斯匿王在迦西迦村三次敗於其甥阿闍世王，第三敗後不食臥床，嘆不能降此乳色青年便無生趣。比丘們禀告佛陀，佛說勝者生怨恨、敗者受苦惱，捨勝與敗者安樂寂靜。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: The king of Kosala fought against his nephew Ajatasattu near the village of Kasika and suffered defeat three times. Returning from the third defeat he reasoned that since he had not been able to subdue this milk-faced youth, there was no use in his living any longer; so he refused food and took to his bed. The news spread through city and monastery, and the monks told the Teacher that the king, thrice defeated near Kasika, had refused to eat and taken to his bed in despair.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 15, story 3 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 憍薩羅王在迦悉迦村附近與侄兒阿闍世交戰，三戰皆敗。第三次敗歸，他思量：既然制服不了這個乳白麵皮的少年，自己再活著也無益了；便拒絕進食，臥床不起。消息傳遍都城與僧院，僧眾告訴導師：國王在迦悉迦附近三戰三敗，絕望之中不肯進食，臥床不起。

passages.text: The Buddha answered that by winning a victory a man produces hatred, and he that is defeated is afflicted with suffering; only he that renounces both victory and defeat lives in tranquillity and happiness, and spoke the stanza. Hatred need not wait for the battlefield: every victory plants it, and every defeat feeds it; the king's cure lay not in a fourth battle but in laying both aside.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 15, story 3 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 佛陀答道：戰勝的人生出仇恨，戰敗者受苦惱之煎；唯有捨棄勝負二者的人住於寂靜與安樂，並說偈。仇恨不必等著戰場：每一場勝利都種下它，每一場失敗都餵養它；國王的藥方不在第四場戰役，而在把勝負兩者一併放下。

title.en: How Anger Marred the Maiden Rohini's Looks
title.zh: 瞋心毀容的少女羅希尼

region.en: Kapilavatthu, Banyan Grove
region.zh: 迦毘羅衛城榕樹園

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: Rohini, sister of the Elder Anuruddha, hid her eruption-covered face behind a cloth until the elder made her spend her jewels on an assembly-hall for the monks; as she swept it her skin cleared. The Buddha traced the eruption to a past life when she, a jealous queen, had powdered scabs secretly into a dancing-girl's bed; anger or jealousy, however slight, is always unbecoming, and Rohini, converted, took on a golden hue and after death was reborn a nymph at whose beauty four deities quarreled.
summary.zh: 阿那律尊者之妹羅希尼因皮膚病以布蒙面，尊者命她傾首飾為僧建講堂；她日日灑掃，瘡疤漸癒。佛陀說其病因：過去為妒后，將瘡痂粉末偷偷撒入舞女的床鋪衣衾，令其潰爛。嫉妒與瞋怒再小也不可取。羅希尼證初果，身現金色，死後生三十三天，四天王為她爭執。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: When the Elder Anuruddha came to Kapilavatthu with five hundred monks, every kinsman paid him respect except his sister Rohini, who stayed at home, ashamed of an eruption of the skin. Summoned, she came with a cloth bound over her face, and the elder asked whether she ought not to perform some work of merit. Told to spend her set of jewels worth ten thousand on building an assembly-hall, she asked who would build it; 'This shall be your duty,' he said to the kinsfolk standing near, 'and I shall stay right here.' So a hall two stories high was raised, and Rohini, standing below as soon as the planks were laid, swept it constantly, filled the water-vessels, and saw the monks seated there from day to day. Even as she swept, the eruption subsided.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 17, story 1 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 阿那律長老率五百僧人回到迦毗羅衛，每位親人都向他致敬，唯有妹妹羅希尼留在家中，羞於皮膚上的疹疾。被召來時，她以布裹著臉面，長老問她是否該行一些功德。得知要她以價值一萬的整套首飾建一座講堂，她問誰來建造；「這就是你們的職責，」他對站在近旁的親人們說，「我就住在這裏。」於是一座兩層的講堂建了起來；木板一鋪好，羅希尼便站在下面，不停地灑掃，把水瓶盛滿，看著僧人們日日坐在那裏。掃著掃著，疹疾便消退了。

passages.text: At the opening feast she was summoned before the Teacher and asked whether she knew why the eruption had broken out. 'Because of anger,' said the Buddha, and told the story: long ago the chief consort of the king of Benares, hating one of the dancing-girls, powdered large ripe scabs and contrived to place the powder in her bed, cloak, and coverlet, sprinkling some on her body as if in fun; the girl's flesh broke out in boils and she went about scratching, suffering harsher pain on her very bed. That chief consort was Rohini. 'Anger or jealousy, however slight, is always unbecoming.' One should put away anger, utterly renounce pride, and overcome every attachment; whoever clings not to name and form is not beset with pain. At the stanza's close Rohini was established in stream-entry, and her body took on a golden hue. Dying, she was reborn at the meeting-point of four deities' boundaries in the Heaven of the Thirty-three, so fair that the four quarreled over her until Sakka claimed her as his darling.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 17, story 1 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 落成之宴上她被召到導師面前，被問是否知道自己為何生疹。「因為憤怒，」佛陀說，並講述往事：很久以前，波羅奈王的正妃憎恨一位舞女，把大塊成熟的瘡痂磨成粉，設法撒在她的床上、斗篷與被褥裏，還假裝嬉戲般撒在她身上；那女孩滿身生瘡，邊抓邊走，在自己的床上受著更重的痛苦。那位正妃就是羅希尼。「憤怒或嫉妒，無論多麼微小，總是不相稱的。」應當息滅憤怒，徹底捨棄我慢，超越一切執著；不執著名色的人，不為苦所困。偈頌結束，羅希尼證入預流果，身體呈現金色。命終之時，她轉生在三十三天四位天王轄界的交界之處，美得讓四神為她相爭，直到帝釋認她為自己的愛侶。

title.en: The Tree-Spirit Who Spared the Monk Who Cut Her Home
title.zh: 饒恕砍樹比丘的樹神

region.en: Alavi; Jetavana, Savatthi
region.zh: 阿羅鞞、舍衛城祇園精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: A monk of Alavi set out to fell a tree tenanted by a spirit with an infant child; she begged him to spare her home, placed the baby on a branch, and saw him strike off its arm. About to kill him, she remembered that a righteous man's death would damn her and be copied by other spirits, and went weeping to the Buddha instead. He praised her as a charioteer who reins in anger like a speeding chariot, gave her a vacant tree by the Perfumed Chamber, and laid down the precept against injuring plants.
summary.zh: 阿羅鞞比丘欲砍一神樹建舍，樹神抱子哀求，將幼兒放上枝頭，比丘卻失手砍斷其臂。神怒欲殺之，旋念若殺有德者必墮地獄，且群神效仿則僧眾受害，遂泣告佛陀。佛讚其如馭疾馳戰車者善勒怒馬，並賜祇園香室旁空樹為居，製定不傷草木之戒。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: When the Teacher permitted the monks to lodge outside the monastery walls, a certain monk of Alavi decided to build himself a lodging, and seeing a tree that suited him began to cut it down. A spirit reborn in that tree, carrying her infant child on her hip, appeared before him and begged him not to cut down her home, for she could not wander homeless with her child. 'I shall not be able to find another tree like this,' said the monk, and paid no further heed. The spirit thought that if he only saw the child he would desist, and placed the baby on a branch; but the monk's axe had already swung and could not be checked, and he cut off the child's arm. Furious, the tree-spirit raised both her hands, crying that she would strike him dead.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 17, story 2 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 導師允許僧人在僧院牆外住宿之後，阿羅維的一位僧人決定為自己蓋一間住處，看中了一棵合意的樹便動手砍伐。轉生在那棵樹裏的樹神——懷裏還抱著嬰孩——現身在他面前，求他不要砍倒她的家，因為她無法抱著孩子四處流浪無家可歸。「我找不到另一棵這樣的樹了，」僧人說，不再理會。樹神心想，若他看見孩子，或許會住手，便把嬰兒放在樹枝上；但僧人的斧頭已經掄起，收不住了，砍斷了孩子的手臂。樹神大怒，舉起雙手，喊著要把他打死。

passages.text: In an instant another thought came to her: this monk is a righteous man; if she killed him she would go to hell, and if other tree-spirits saw monks cutting down their trees they would imitate her and kill other monks; moreover this monk has a master. Lowering her hands, she went weeping to the Teacher and told him all. 'Well done, well done, spirit!' said the Buddha; 'you have done well in holding in, like a swift-speeding chariot, your anger when it was thus aroused,' and spoke the stanza: whoever controls his anger when it is aroused, like a speeding chariot, him I call a charioteer; other folk merely hold the reins. Though she had won the Fruit of Conversion she stood weeping for her destroyed home, and the Teacher pointed out a tree near the Perfumed Chamber at Jetavana from which a spirit had just departed, telling her to enter it; thereafter no powerful spirit could shake that tree, for its tenant held her abode as a gift from the Buddha. On this occasion the Teacher laid down the observance of the precept regarding the injuring of plants and trees.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 17, story 2 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 一瞬間另一個念頭來到她心裏：這僧人是位正法之人；殺了他自己要下地獄，別的樹神若看見僧人砍樹也會效法她殺別的僧人；況且這僧人有一位導師。她放下雙手，哭著去見導師，把一切告訴了他。「善哉，善哉，樹神！」佛陀說；「你如疾馳的戰車一般勒住了被這樣激起的憤怒，做得好，」並說偈：凡能如勒住疾馳戰車一般制伏已起之憤怒者，我稱之為御者；其他人只是握著韁繩而已。雖已證得預流果，她仍為毀掉的家哭泣，導師便指出祇園香室近旁一棵樹神剛剛遷走的樹，叫她進住；從此再無大威力的樹神能撼動那棵樹，因為住客視其居所為佛陀所賜。這一次，導師制定了關於傷害草木的戒條。

title.en: Pothila the Empty-Head and the Seven-Year-Old Teacher
title.zh: 波吒拉「空頭」與七歲小老師

region.en: Jetavana; forest hermitage a hundred leagues away
region.zh: 祇園精舍、百里外森林精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: Pothila, 'Versed in the Tipitaka' through the dispensations of seven Buddhas, was stung when the Teacher always called him Tucchapothila, the empty-head, and set out to meditate. In a hermitage of thirty arahats the monks passed him down from senior to junior until he stood before a seven-year-old novice, who made him plunge robes and all into a pool to prove his tractability, then taught him to stop five of the six sense-doors and watch the mind's door, whereby the Buddha's image from a hundred leagues away brought him to arahatship.
summary.zh: 經七佛之世皆稱「通三藏」的波吒拉，被佛陀屢喚「空頭波吒拉」所激，前往禪修。三十位阿羅漢將他從上座一路推向最年幼的七歲沙彌。沙彌命他連衣入池以試其受教，再教他關閉五根門、專注意門。佛陀從一百二十由旬外放光照拂，以「從禪定生智慧」一偈令其證阿羅漢。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: Elder Pothila bore the title Versed in the Tipitaka through the dispensations of all Seven Buddhas and recited the Law to five hundred monks. The Teacher, thinking it had not even occurred to him to seek escape from suffering, stirred him by calling him always Tucchapothila, empty-head: come, empty-head; sit, empty-head; empty-head has gone. Pothila reasoned that the Teacher slighted him because he had never developed the trances, and resolved that very evening to enter the forest and meditate. He walked a hundred and twenty leagues to a hermitage where thirty monks dwelt, and asked each to be his refuge; each, knowing himself an arahat and him a proud scholar, sent him to his junior, until at last the whole chain of monks set him before the youngest of all, a seven-year-old novice doing needlework in his day-quarters.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 20, story 7 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 缽帝沙拉長老頭頂「通曉七佛三藏」的名號，向五百僧人講說經法。導師想到他連從苦中解脫的念頭都還不曾生起，便以「空頭缽帝沙拉」相稱來激他：來吧，空頭；坐吧，空頭；空頭走了。缽帝沙拉推想導師輕視他，是因為他從未修習禪定，便決定當晚入林修行。他走了一百二十由旬，來到三十位僧人居住的草庵，一一請求作他們的弟子；每一位都知道自己是阿羅漢而他是傲慢的學者，都把他介紹給自己的下座，最後整條僧鏈把他送到最年幼的一位面前——一個七歲的沙彌，正在日間住處做針線。

passages.text: His pride humbled, Pothila raised clasped hands to the child: 'Good sir, be my refuge.' The novice answered that one of mature age and great learning should rather teach him, but agreed on one condition, that Pothila endure admonition; the monk vowed he would enter fire if told to. So the novice pointed to a pool and bade him plunge in, robes and all, testing whether the owner of costly double robes was tractable; no sooner were the words spoken than Pothila plunged. Then the novice gave him the lizard simile: in an ant-hill with six holes, he who would catch the lizard stops five and watches the sixth. So should you deal with the six doors of the senses: close five, and give your whole attention to the door of the mind. Pothila concentrated on the material body and began to meditate; the Teacher, a hundred and twenty leagues away, surveyed him and sent forth a luminous image that spoke with him, and by the stanza, from meditation springs wisdom and without it wisdom dwindles away, Pothila attained arahatship.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 20, story 7 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 傲慢被折服的缽帝沙拉合掌向孩子行禮：「賢者，請作我的老師。」沙彌答道，年長而博學的人應該來教他才是，但答應有一個條件：缽帝沙拉必須忍受訓誡；僧人發誓若被吩咐入火，他便入火。沙彌指著一個水池，命他穿著僧衣跳進去，試探這穿著昂貴雙層僧衣的主人是否馴順；話音一落，缽帝沙拉便跳了下去。沙彌便給他蜥蜴的比喻：要在有六個洞的蟻丘裏捉住蜥蜴，先封住五個洞，只盯住第六個。你也當這樣對待六根之門：封住五門，全心守護意門。缽帝沙拉繫念於色身，開始禪修；一百二十由旬外的導師觀察著他，放出一個放光的分身與他說話，以偈——從禪定中生智慧，無禪定則智慧枯萎——缽帝沙拉證得阿羅漢。

title.en: Thou Shalt Surely Die: the Merchant Who Planned a Year of Trade
title.zh: 你必定要死——盤算全年買賣的商人

region.en: River bank near Savatthi
region.zh: 舍衛城郊河岸

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: The merchant Mahadhana of Benares, flooding-delayed on the far bank with five hundred cartloads of safflower-dyed cloth, resolved to stay the whole rainy season, winter, and summer selling his goods. The Buddha, seeing he had only seven days to live, sent Ananda to warn him; warned, the merchant fed the Congregation for seven days and at the Teacher's thanksgiving attained stream-entry, then died quietly on his bed and was reborn in the Tusita heaven.
summary.zh: 波羅奈商人摩訶檀那載五百車胭脂紅衣布，因河水氾濫滯留對岸，決意留住雨季、冬季、夏季售完貨物再走。佛陀見其壽僅餘七日，遣阿難告知。商人驚懼供僧七日，於佛隨喜時證初果，隨後安臥而逝，生兜率天。愚者盤算久住，不知死期將至。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: Merchant Great-Wealth, Mahadhana of Benares, loaded five hundred carts with cloth dyed with safflower and set out to trade. Returning toward Savatthi he reached the river bank and thought to cross the morrow; that night a storm burst, and for seven days the river was at flood while the citizens kept holiday, so that he found no chance to sell his crimson cloths. He reasoned that to go back would mean delay, and resolved to dwell right there through the rainy season, the winter, and the summer, doing his work and selling his goods. As the Teacher made his alms-pilgrimage through the city he became aware of the intention and smiled, telling Ananda that not realizing the end of his life was near, the merchant had made up his mind to stay a whole year.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 20, story 10 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 波羅奈的富商大財主摩訶達那，裝了五百車紅花染的布匹外出經商。返回舍衛城途中抵達河岸，想著明日再渡；當夜風暴襲來，河水一連七天氾濫，市民們過著節日，他便沒有機會賣出紅色的布匹。他盤算回去必耽誤行程，便決定就地住下雨季、冬季與夏季，一面做工一面賣貨。導師入城乞食時察知此意而微笑，告訴阿難：不曾覺知死期已近，商人竟決定住上整整一年。

passages.text: 'Only seven days longer will he live,' said the Buddha, and bade Ananda warn him. The elder made his alms-round at the cart-enclosure, was fed, and asked how long the merchant meant to stay; told a whole year, he answered that though the end of life be near, it is hard to realize, and that only seven days more remained. Overcome, the merchant invited the Congregation with the Buddha, gave alms seven days, and on the last took the Teacher's bowl to receive the words of thanksgiving. 'A wise man,' said the Teacher, 'should never allow himself to think, Right here will I dwell during the rain, during the winter and summer; I will do this work and that. Here will I dwell through the rains, the simpleton imagines, knowing not that he must die.' At the lesson's close the merchant was established in the Fruit of Conversion. He walked a little way with the Teacher, complained of a trouble in his head, lay down on his bed, and no sooner had he lain down than he died, and was reborn in the World of the Tusita gods.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 20, story 10 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「他只剩七天壽命了，」佛陀說，命阿難去提醒他。長老到車隊圍欄處乞食，受供之後問商人打算住多久；聽說整整一年，他答道，雖然死期已近，人卻難以體會，而他只剩七天了。商人如遭雷擊，請佛陀率僧團應供，布施七日，最後一天捧著導師的缽聽受謝恩之偈。「智者，」導師說，「決不該想：我要在這裏度過雨季、冬夏；我要做這事做那事。我要在雨季中住在此處——愚人如此盤算，不知自己必死。」開示結束，商人證入預流果。他陪導師走了一小段，說頭有點疼，躺到床上，剛一躺下便死了，轉生兜率天界。

title.en: The Ascent of the Ganges and the Jewel Sutta
title.zh: 恆河上遊之行與寶經

region.en: Vesali and the river Ganges
region.zh: 毗舍離與恆河

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: Vesali, stricken by famine, evil spirits, and pestilence, sent for the Buddha; he crossed the Ganges on a jeweled float while Bimbisara waded neck-deep behind it, and at the city gate Ananda recited the Jewel Sutta, drops of silver water falling on the sick and curing them as the spirits fled through walls. Naga kings, deities, and kings covered the river with parasols and lotuses, and the Buddha explained it all as the fruit of one slight offering of grass, sand, and flowers he once made at a Private Buddha's shrine.
summary.zh: 毗舍離遭飢荒、惡鬼、疫病三災，遣使請佛。頻毘娑羅王鋪路五由旬送佛至河，以珠寶浮舟渡河；佛陀一登岸大雨傾盆，屍骸盡沖入河，大地清淨。阿難持缽誦《寶經》繞城三匝，水珠如銀丸落於病者身上，疫病隨愈，惡鬼破牆而逃。天、龍、王傘蓋蓮花滿河；佛說此皆過去於辟支佛塔前拔草、鋪沙、撒花之小施所感。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: When Vesali's crops failed, corpses drew evil spirits, the spirits brought intestinal disease, and three plagues wasted the city, the Licchavi assembly, finding no fault in their king, resolved to send for the Buddha. Mahali obtained Bimbisara's leave, and the king smoothed a five-league road to the Ganges with rest-houses each league and flowers knee-deep, conducting the Teacher in five days. On a jeweled float the Buddha crossed the boundary of Vesali's territory, the king wading behind the float to his neck in promise, 'Until the Exalted One returns, I shall remain right here on the bank of the Ganges.' The Licchavi princes, meeting him in the water, doubled the king's honors; the moment the Teacher set foot ashore a storm burst, washing every corpse into the Ganges and leaving the region pure and sweet.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 21, story 1 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 毗舍離的莊稼歉收之後，屍體引來惡鬼，惡鬼帶來腸疫，三重瘟疫摧殘著都城；離車族的議會在國王身上找不到過錯，決定迎請佛陀。摩訶利徵得頻毗娑羅王的准許；國王平整了通往恒河的五由旬大道，每一由旬設涼亭，鮮花鋪得齊膝，五天之內恭迎導師。佛陀乘寶石浮舟渡過毗舍離的國界，國王在舟後蹚水，水至其頸，許諾道：「直到世尊歸來，我都留在恒河岸上。」離車的王子們在水中迎駕，把國王的禮敬加了一倍；導師的腳一上岸，風暴驟起，把每一具屍體都沖入恒河，全境潔淨芬芳。

passages.text: Sakka drew near with his deities and most of the evil spirits fled. At the gate of the city the Teacher gave Ananda the Jewel Sutta to recite as a protection within the three walls, making the rounds with the Licchavi princes. When Ananda uttered the word 'Whatsoever' and threw water upward from the stone bowl, it fell upon the sick and cured them where they stood, while drops like balls of silver fell upon the evil spirits, who strove to escape by every door and, finding not room enough in a thousand doors, broke down the walls and fled. In the town-hall the Teacher recited the Jewel Sutta again, and eighty-four thousand beings obtained comprehension of the Law; for seven days the plague abated, and he departed, honored on the river by Naga kings with boats of gold and silver and by deities from earth to the Brahma world with parasol after parasol, while he created a counterfeit Buddha in each boat, one festival within the whole circle of the Cakkavala.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 21, story 1 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 帝釋率領天眾趕到，大部分惡鬼逃散。在城門口導師把《寶經》交給阿難，命他繞三重城牆之內誦持以作守護，與離車王子們一同巡行。當阿念誦出「一切」一詞、從石缽向上潑水時，水落在病人身上，他們當場痊癒；如銀丸般的水滴落在惡鬼身上，他們奪門而逃，一千扇門不夠逃的，便破牆而遁。在議政廳導師再次誦《寶經》，八萬四千眾生領悟了法；瘟疫七日平息，他啟程離去，龍王們以金銀之舟在河上致敬，從大地到梵天的諸神以一重又一重的傘蓋相送，他在每條船上化出一尊分佛——在整個輪圍界內唯一的一場慶典。

passages.text: The monks marveled that such honor had come from Buddha-power or from nagas, deities, and Brahma; the Buddha corrected them: it came from a slight offering made in a previous existence. Long ago the Brahman Sankha of Takshashila, seeking his son Susima, found that the youth had become a Private Buddha at Isipatana, passed into Nibbana quickly, and been enshrined at the gate of Benares. The father wept, then tore up the grass in the shrine's enclosure, brought sand in his outer garment and spread it, sprinkled the ground with water from his pot, scattered wild flowers, raised his robe as a banner, and planted his own parasol over the mound. 'It was I who uprooted that grass,' said the Buddha; 'as its fruit these princes cleared a road eight leagues long. I spread the sand, and they spread sand; I scattered flowers, and lotuses of five colors covered the Ganges a league; I sprinkled water, and a shower fell on Vesali; I raised a banner and planted a parasol, and parasols rose as far as the highest heaven.' If by renouncing some trifling pleasure one may obtain pleasure abounding, a wise man renounces the trifling pleasure.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 21, story 1 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 僧眾驚嘆這樣的榮耀究竟出自佛力還是龍神梵天之力；佛陀糾正他們：它來自前世一件微小的供養。很久以前，呾叉始羅的婆羅門商迦去尋找兒子蘇悉摩，發現這少年已在仙人墮處證得獨覺佛，很快入滅，被供養在波羅奈城門。父親哭泣之後，把塔園裏的草連根拔起，以外衣運來細沙鋪撒，以罐中的水灑灑地面，散上野花，舉起僧衣作為旗幟，把自己的陽傘撐在塔上。「是我拔掉了那些草，」佛陀說；「作為它的果報，這些王子平整了八由旬長的路。我鋪了沙，他們便鋪沙；我散了花，五色的蓮花便舖滿恒河一由旬；我灑了水，毗舍離便落了雨；我舉旗撐傘，傘蓋便一直升到最高的天界。」若捨棄微小的欲樂便能獲得無量的安樂，智者便捨棄那微小的欲樂。

title.en: Young Archer the Wise and the Wife Who Bartered Husbands
title.zh: 智箭少年與換夫之妻

region.en: Forest road to Benares
region.zh: 往波羅奈的林間道路

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: A young monk grown yellow with longing for a householder's wife was told by the Buddha of his own past life as Young Archer the Wise, who slew fifty bandits with fifty arrows and yet was killed by the bandit his wife had fallen for; the bandit himself abandoned her by a river, and Sakka, as a jackal that lost both fish and flesh, shamed her. Doubt agitated and passion swaying him strengthen the bond; meditating on the unlovely cleaves it.
summary.zh: 年輕比丘因思念施主之女而面黃肌瘦。佛陀說過去世他為智箭少年，五十箭射殺五十盜，其妻卻瞬間愛上倖存盜首、遞劍害夫；盜首懼她移情，渡河棄她而去。帝釋化為失魚失肉的胡狼譏其更慘，她自慚形穢。佛陀教他：疑惱與貪愛只會加固魔縛。

sensitivity.note: Canonical commentary of a living tradition; retold freely.

passages.text: A young monk who went for drinking-water to a certain house fell in love with the young woman there; she fed him rice-gruel, then boiled rice, and talked to him of how lonely the house was, until he grew yellow with discontent. Taken to the Teacher, he confessed the cause, and the Buddha told him it was no strange thing for such a woman to act so: in a previous existence she forsook Dhanuggaha, the wisest man in all India, conceived a sudden passion for a bandit, and slew her husband. In times past Young Archer the Wise, trained at Takshashila and married to his teacher's daughter, was set on at the forest's entrance by fifty bandits and slew them all with fifty arrows; when the arrows were gone he seized the leader, and 'Wife, bring me my sword!' But the moment she saw the bandit she conceived a passion for him, and set the sword's hilt in the bandit's hand, and he slew Young Archer the Wise and took her away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 24, story 7 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 一位年輕僧人到某戶人家取飲水，愛上了那家的少女；她先後供他米粥、熟飯，對他說家裏多麼冷清，直到他因不滿而面黃肌瘦。被帶到導師那裏，他坦白了緣由；佛陀告訴他，這樣的女人行徑並不稀奇：前世她曾拋棄過全印度最智慧的男子檀奴迦哈，忽然對一個強盜動了情，殺了自己的丈夫。往昔「智者」青年射師在呾叉始羅受業，娶了老師的女兒；在森林入口，五十個強盜圍攻他，他以五十支箭把他們全部射殺；箭用盡了，他抓住強盜頭子喊道：「妻子，把我的劍拿來！」可她一看見強盜便動了情，把劍柄塞進強盜手裏，強盜殺了智者青年射師，把她帶走了。

passages.text: Going on his way, the bandit reasoned that a woman who could betray one husband would kill him too, and at a river left her on the near bank, 'Remain until I carry your ornaments across,' and crossed alone, taking everything. 'You have taken all my ornaments and crossed,' she cried; 'return speedily, now take me too.' 'Woman,' he answered, 'you bartered a husband long known for one unknown; you may barter me for another man. Therefore I will go far from hence.' Then Sakka came to put her to shame, as a jackal with a piece of meat, his charioteer a fish, his musician a bird: the jackal sprang at the leaping fish, dropped the meat, and the bird snatched it into the air, so the jackal lost both fish and flesh and mourned like a pauper. The woman laughed; the jackal retorted that easy to see are the faults of others, hard to see one's own: she had lost both husband and lover, and would do evil again. The wisest man in India was Young Archer; the jackal was the Buddha himself.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 24, story 7 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 強盜上路後想到：能背叛一個丈夫的女人也會殺了我；到一條河邊，他把留在近岸，說「等我把你們的飾物帶過去」，便獨自渡河，把一切都帶走了。「你拿走了我所有的飾物渡過去了，」她喊道，「快回來，把我們倆也帶過去。」「女人，」他答道，「你把相知的丈夫換成了一個陌生的；你也會把我換成另一個男人。所以我遠走高飛。」於是帝釋前來羞辱她：化作一隻叼著肉塊的豺，御者是魚，樂師是鳥；豺撲向跳起來的魚，丟了肉，鳥把肉叼上天空，豺便魚肉兩失，如乞丐一般哀嚎。女人大笑；豺反駁道：他人之過易見，己身之過難見；你已失去丈夫與情人，日後還要作惡。全印度最智慧的男子就是青年射師；那隻豺就是佛陀本人。

passages.text: 'Monk, uproot and destroy the desire which has sprung up within you for this woman,' said the Teacher, and expounded the two stanzas: if a man be agitated by doubt, swayed by strong passion, seeking only what is pleasing, craving increases the more, and he strengthens the bond that holds him; but whoever delights in suppressing doubt and meditates with mindfulness on what is not pleasing will destroy and cleave the bond of Mara. The monk uprooted his desire, and the wife's fickleness stood revealed as the very shape of craving.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Dhammapada Commentary, Book 24, story 7 (Burlingame 1921); not verbatim.
passages.zh: 「僧人啊，連根拔除並毀滅你心中對這女人生起的欲望吧，」導師說，並講解兩首偈頌：若人為疑惑所擾、為強烈的情欲所動、只尋可意之事，渴愛便愈增，束縛他的枷鎖也愈緊；而以正念欣然制伏疑惑、觀察不可意之事的人，必摧斷魔羅之縛。那僧人拔除了欲望；妻子的善變，正是渴愛之形。

title.en: Uggasena the Tumbler Converts on the Tip of the Pole
title.zh: 烏迦西那——竿頂當下轉法

region.en: Rajagaha, Veluvana monastery
region.zh: 王舍城竹林精舍

period: Pali commentary, c. 5th c. CE (Buddhaghosa-tradition); Burlingame translation 1921

source.work: Buddhist Legends (Dhammapada Commentary), trans. E. W. Burlingame, HOS 28/29/30

summary.en: A treasurer's son fell in love with a tumbler's daughter and followed her troupe as a cart-driver, enduring his wife's contempt until he mastered tumbling himself.
